**Deployment flexibility for regulated industries.** The option to run private cloud or on-premise, plus what WotNot describes as enterprise-grade encryption and an InfoSec/legal review step on the Enterprise plan, is aimed at healthcare, insurance, and financial services customers who can't put customer data through a fully multi-tenant SaaS pipeline.

**Voicebot and outbound bot options.** Beyond inbound chat, WotNot offers outbound bot campaigns and voicebot capability, positioning it as a broader conversational-automation platform rather than a pure inbound support widget.

## Who WotNot is actually for

- **Solo creators and very small businesses:** WotNot is a mismatch here. The $29/month entry tier and 1,000-chat cap are still more than a solo operator typically needs, and there's no free-forever plan to fall back on. A lighter tool built for small teams — see our [Tidio review](/blog/tidio-review) — fits this segment better.
- **Small support/sales teams (10-50 agents):** The Starter or Premium tier is the realistic entry point, particularly for teams already running WhatsApp as a primary customer channel and wanting AI Studio's multi-model training without building a custom LLM pipeline themselves.
- **Regulated mid-market and enterprise (healthcare, insurance, financial services, real estate):** This is where WotNot's pitch is strongest — private cloud/on-premise deployment, InfoSec review, SSO, and custom integrations on the Enterprise tier are built specifically for teams that can't use a generic multi-tenant chatbot SaaS product.
- **Agencies managing bots for multiple clients:** The white-label option (hide branding, custom widget styling) on Premium and up makes WotNot workable for agencies reselling chatbot deployments, though per-client chat/credit limits need to be budgeted carefully.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Native WhatsApp Business API support alongside Instagram, Messenger, SMS, and voice | No permanent free plan — 14-day trial only |
| Choice of underlying LLM (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Mistral) rather than a single locked-in model | Entry-tier chat/credit caps (1,000/month) are tight for anything beyond a small pilot |
| Live Chat human handoff available from the Premium tier | Live Chat and white-labeling are gated behind the $299/month plan, not included lower down |
| On-premise/private cloud deployment options for regulated industries | Pricing scales by both chats and AI credits simultaneously, which can make cost forecasting harder than a flat per-seat model |
| Broad CRM/helpdesk integration list (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Zoho) | Enterprise-grade security and compliance features require a custom quote, not published pricing |

## Integrations and ecosystem

WotNot connects to Salesforce, HubSpot, and Zoho CRM for lead and contact sync; Zendesk and Freshdesk for ticketing; and Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, and Calendly for scheduling. On the automation side, it supports Zapier and Make, plus raw HTTP requests and an API for custom integrations, along with direct Google Sheets and Airtable connections. Messaging coverage spans WhatsApp Business API, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, Slack, and voice, alongside the standard web widget and native Android/iOS apps. Businesses needing something not on that list can request a custom integration, according to WotNot's site — though turnaround time for custom requests isn't published and should be confirmed directly with sales.

## Where WotNot is a strong fit

WotNot works well for teams that live in WhatsApp as a customer channel rather than treating it as a nice-to-have, and for regulated businesses that need deployment control (private cloud/on-premise) that most SaaS chatbot tools simply don't offer. It's also a reasonable fit for teams that want to try more than one LLM behind their support agent without switching platforms, since AI Studio's model choice is baked into the Starter tier and up.

## Where to think twice

WotNot isn't the right call if a business needs a fully free tool to start — there's no permanent free plan, only a 14-day trial, so budget-conscious solo founders and very early-stage startups should look elsewhere first. It's also not the best fit for teams that mainly need a simple website chat widget with minimal setup; WotNot's flow builder and AI Studio are more capable than that use case requires, and a lighter tool will get a basic widget live faster and cheaper. Teams with unpredictable or spiky conversation volume should also be cautious: because pricing scales on both chats and AI credits together, a busy month can burn through both caps at once and force an unplanned upgrade. And if strict published pricing matters more than "contact sales," note that InfoSec/legal review and SSO sit behind a custom Enterprise quote, not a fixed listed price.

## Bottom line

WotNot earns its place in the WhatsApp-first, mid-market-to-enterprise segment of the chatbot market rather than as a general-purpose small-business widget. The combination of native WhatsApp Business API support, a choice of underlying LLMs, and on-premise deployment options is a real differentiator for healthcare, insurance, and financial-services teams that can't use a typical multi-tenant SaaS bot. For a smaller team or solo creator just wanting a website chat widget with a free tier to start on, the entry price and lack of a permanent free plan make WotNot overkill — that audience will usually be better served by a lighter tool.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does WotNot have a free plan?**
No. WotNot offers a 14-day free trial on its Lite, Starter, and Premium plans, but there's no permanent free tier — after the trial, a paid plan starting at $29/month is required to keep using the platform.

**What LLMs does WotNot's AI Studio support?**
WotNot states that AI Studio (available on Starter and above) supports OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, and Mistral models, letting a business choose which one powers its agent rather than being locked into a single vendor.

**Can WotNot run on WhatsApp?**
Yes — WhatsApp Business API is one of WotNot's primary supported channels, alongside Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, voice, and a standard web widget.

**Is WotNot good for a small business or solo creator?**
Not really. The lowest tier is $29/month with a 1,000-chat cap and no free-forever option, which is more overhead than most solo operators or very small businesses need. A widget-first tool with a free plan, like Tidio, is usually a better starting point.

**Does WotNot support on-premise or private cloud deployment?**
Yes, according to WotNot's own site, the platform can be deployed on public cloud, private cloud, or fully on-premise — a feature aimed at healthcare, insurance, and other regulated industries with data-residency requirements. Enterprise-tier specifics should be confirmed directly with WotNot's sales team.

**What integrations does WotNot support?**
WotNot integrates with CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho), helpdesks (Zendesk, Freshdesk), scheduling tools (Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, Calendly), automation platforms (Zapier, Make), and messaging channels including WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, and Slack, plus a general API and HTTP request support for custom setups.

**How does WotNot's pricing scale?**
Plans scale by two combined limits — monthly chats and AI credits — rather than by number of bots or agent seats. Lite covers 1,000 of each, Starter 5,000, Premium 10,000, and Enterprise is unlimited on a custom quote.

**How does WotNot compare to Tidio or Lyro AI?**
WotNot targets WhatsApp-first, mid-market, and regulated-industry deployments with multi-LLM choice and on-premise options, while Tidio and its Lyro AI add-on target smaller teams wanting a website widget with a free starting tier. See our [Tidio review](/blog/tidio-review) and [Lyro AI review](/blog/lyro-ai-review) for that comparison.

For broader software discounts, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) page.

title: Paperguide Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is Paperguide worth it for literature reviews and research writing? A look at its research agent, pricing, and where it genuinely falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Paperguide worth it for academic research and writing?

Paperguide is worth it if you're managing a literature review, systematic review, or thesis and want one tool that searches papers, chats with PDFs, drafts citation-grounded text, and manages references. It's less useful if you just need a simple citation formatter or a general-purpose AI writing tool — for that, a lighter tool is a better fit.

## At a glance

| | Details |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (2,000 AI credits/month); paid plans from $12/seat/month |
| Free tier / trial | Yes — free plan with limited AI searches, 10-paper data extraction, 4,000-word plagiarism checks |
| Best for | Literature reviews, systematic reviews, thesis/dissertation writing |
| Standout feature | Research Agent that runs multi-step searches across 200M+ papers and cites sources inline |

Paperguide bills itself as an AI-native platform for scientific research, literature reviews, systematic reviews, and evidence synthesis. According to the company's own site, it's used by roughly 974,000 researchers across universities and research institutions. Unlike a general chatbot bolted onto a citation manager, Paperguide is built around a reference library first — everything else (chat, writing, extraction) reads from and writes back to that library.

The company doesn't publish which underlying AI models power its features, so treat any output quality as something to verify yourself rather than take on faith. That's a fair ask for a tool aimed at researchers who are, by training, supposed to check sources anyway.

## Pricing (as of publication)

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability below were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI research tools update pricing and quotas often, so confirm current numbers on Paperguide's own [pricing page](https://paperguide.ai/pricing) before you commit to a plan.

| Plan | Price | AI credits/month | Systematic review cap | Notable limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 2,000 | Not supported | 10 papers for extraction, 4,000 words/month plagiarism check, 10 search API requests/month |
| Plus | $12/seat/month (billed annually gets a discount the site lists as 37% off) | 12,500 | Up to 1,000 papers | 50 columns / 100 papers for extraction, 20,000 words/month plagiarism check |
| Pro | $29/seat/month (annual billing discount listed as 41% off) | 50,000 | Up to 5,000 papers | Same extraction cap as Plus, 100,000 words/month plagiarism check, 500 search API requests/month |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Up to 20,000 papers | Dual-reviewer PRISMA screening, dedicated support |

Paperguide also advertises a 30% student discount with a valid university email address — worth checking at signup if you're on a .edu account. The exact dollar figure for annual billing isn't broken out on the pricing page beyond the percentage-off claim, so confirm the actual annual total at checkout before assuming the discounted rate.

## Features walkthrough

**Research Agent.** This is the feature Paperguide leads with: point it at a research question and it runs a multi-step search across a claimed 200 million+ papers, pulling in comparative findings across studies rather than returning a flat list of abstracts. For a literature review's early scoping stage, this can save real time versus manually running the same search five different ways.

**Chat with papers.** You can query a single PDF or a whole folder of them at once, and Paperguide grounds its answers in the actual text rather than general knowledge — useful for pulling specific findings, methodology details, or numbers out of a stack of PDFs without re-reading each one.

**Citation-grounded writing assistant.** The writing tool drafts text with citations pulled from your library or external databases as it goes, rather than generating prose first and asking you to source it after. Paperguide's site states support for 1,000+ citation styles, which covers essentially any journal or institutional format you're likely to be asked for.

**Systematic review tooling.** This is the feature that separates Paperguide from most general AI writing assistants. Dual-reviewer screening with conflict resolution, evidence-linked extraction, and PRISMA-style reporting are aimed squarely at people running formal systematic reviews or meta-analyses — a workflow that tools like Grammarly, Jasper, or general chat assistants simply don't address.

**Reference manager as the backbone.** Rather than treating citations as an add-on, Paperguide positions its reference manager as the foundation every other feature builds on. It imports from Zotero and Mendeley or lets you add papers by DOI, and the site says it auto-fetches metadata and open-access PDFs where available.

## Who it's actually for

- **Grad students and PhD candidates** running a literature review or writing a thesis will likely get the most value from the Plus or Pro tier, where the systematic-review caps (1,000–5,000 papers) and higher AI credit allowances matter.
- **Solo researchers doing occasional lit reviews** can likely get by on the Free tier for a while, though the 10-paper extraction cap and limited AI searches will bite quickly once a project gets serious.
- **Research teams running formal systematic reviews or meta-analyses** (the kind that need PRISMA reporting) are the target audience for Pro or Enterprise — the dual-reviewer screening and higher paper caps aren't relevant to casual users.
- **Anyone just wanting a citation formatter** for a single paper is better served by a free, dedicated citation tool — Paperguide's pricing and feature depth are overkill for that narrow job.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Reference manager, chat, and writing assistant share one library — no re-uploading papers between tools | AI models used aren't disclosed, so output quality is harder to independently benchmark |
| Systematic review / PRISMA tooling is a real differentiator most AI writing tools don't offer | Free tier's 10-paper extraction cap is tight for anything beyond a quick test |
| Supports 1,000+ citation styles and imports directly from Zotero/Mendeley | Per-seat pricing on Plus and Pro adds up quickly for a multi-person research team |
| Student discount lowers the entry cost for the audience most likely to need it | Annual-billing savings are advertised as percentages, not flat dollar amounts, on the public pricing page |
| Free plan exists with no credit card required for basic use | AI credit systems (rather than flat "unlimited" tiers) mean heavy users can hit ceilings mid-month |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Paperguide's main integration story is on the reference-management side: it imports libraries from **Zotero** and **Mendeley**, and lets you add sources directly by **DOI**. The paid tiers add a **search API** with a monthly request cap (10 on Free, up to 500 on Pro, custom on Enterprise), which suggests some programmatic/automation use is possible for teams that want to pull search results into other tooling. The site doesn't list a Word or Google Docs plugin, a Slack integration, or a public marketplace of third-party plugins as of this writing — if a live-in-your-word-processor citation plugin is a must-have for your workflow, confirm that's supported (or find a workaround) before switching your whole reference library over.

## Where it's a strong fit

Paperguide earns its subscription fee for anyone doing structured literature work at scale: systematic reviews, evidence synthesis for a lab, or a thesis that needs to survive a committee's scrutiny on sourcing. The combination of a real reference manager, grounded paper chat, and PRISMA-aware review tooling under one login is genuinely rare — most competitors pick one of those three and bolt on the others as an afterthought.

It's also a reasonable pick for someone early in a research project who wants to scope the literature quickly. The Research Agent's multi-step search can surface papers and angles a single keyword search would miss, which matters most in the exploratory phase before you've settled on a thesis question.

## Where to think twice

Skip Paperguide, or at least stay on the free tier a while longer, if you only need to format citations for one or two papers — you're paying for infrastructure (systematic review screening, high-volume AI credits) you won't touch. If your institution requires a specific compliance certification (SOC 2, HIPAA, or similar) for handling unpublished or sensitive research data, Paperguide's public materials don't spell out a security/compliance posture, so check directly with their team before uploading anything sensitive.

Teams billing per seat should do the math carefully: at $29/seat/month on Pro, a five-person review team adds up fast, and Enterprise custom pricing becomes the more realistic path past two or three seats.

## How Paperguide compares to other AI academic writing tools

Paperguide isn't the only AI tool aimed at students and researchers — our [Litero AI review](/blog/litero-ai-review) covers a tool that leans harder into citation search and AI drafting for essay-style writing, with a narrower feature set than Paperguide's systematic-review tooling. If your work is closer to essay drafting than formal evidence synthesis, read both before picking one — Litero is closer to a drafting assistant, Paperguide closer to a research operations platform built around a reference library.

## Bottom line

Paperguide is a genuinely differentiated tool in a crowded AI-writing-assistant space because it's built for the parts of academic work that most competitors skip: systematic review screening, evidence traceability, and a reference manager that's the backbone rather than an afterthought. It's not the cheapest way to format a citation, and the undisclosed model details mean you should verify important outputs rather than trust them outright, but for anyone running a structured literature review or systematic review, the Plus or Pro plan is likely to pay for itself in time saved during the screening and extraction phase alone.

## FAQ

**Is Paperguide free?**
There's a free plan with 2,000 AI credits per month, limited AI searches, and data extraction capped at 10 papers. It doesn't support systematic reviews, which are gated to paid plans.

**How much does Paperguide cost?**
Paid plans start at $12/seat/month on the Plus tier and $29/seat/month on Pro, both with a percentage discount for annual billing according to the pricing page. Enterprise pricing is custom.

**Does Paperguide offer a student discount?**
Yes — Paperguide's site lists a 30% discount for users with a valid university email address.

**What citation styles does Paperguide support?**
The company states support for more than 1,000 citation styles, which should cover virtually any journal or institutional formatting requirement.

**Can Paperguide import my existing Zotero or Mendeley library?**
Yes, Paperguide supports importing from both Zotero and Mendeley, or adding sources directly by DOI.

**Is Paperguide suitable for a systematic review or meta-analysis?**
Yes — this is one of its core differentiators. Paid plans include dual-reviewer screening with conflict resolution and PRISMA-style reporting, scaling from 1,000 papers on Plus up to 20,000 on Enterprise.

**What AI models does Paperguide use?**
The company doesn't publicly disclose which underlying AI models power its search, chat, and writing features. If that matters for your institution's disclosure requirements, contact Paperguide's support directly.

**How does Paperguide compare to a general AI writing assistant like Litero AI?**
Paperguide is built around a reference manager and systematic-review tooling, making it a better fit for structured literature reviews, while general academic writing tools like the one covered in our [Litero AI review](/blog/litero-ai-review) lean more toward drafting individual essays or papers. Read both if you're deciding between research-operations depth and lighter drafting help.

title: Captitles Review 2026: Theatre Surtitles, Pricing, Verdict
excerpt: Captitles brings AI-assisted surtitles to live theatre and translation, not social video. Full pricing, features, and who it's actually for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Captitles Review 2026: Theatre Surtitles, Not Social Video Captions

Captitles is good if you run live theatre or festival performances and need AI-assisted surtitle creation, translation, and real-time syncing across screens and phones. It's not a fit if you're captioning TikToks or YouTube Shorts — that's a different category of tool entirely, and Captitles doesn't compete there.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (limited); €75/month Subscription; €4.99/day rental |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — permanent free plan for 2 shows, no card required |
| Best for | Theatres, opera houses, and touring productions needing live surtitles |
| Standout feature | Script-to-surtitle AI conversion plus real-time live sync during performances |

## What Captitles actually is

Here's the thing worth clearing up before anything else: if you searched for Captitles expecting another Submagic or CapCut-style tool for burning animated subtitles onto short-form video, you've landed on something different. Captitles is built for theatre and live-performance surtitling — the practice of projecting or streaming translated dialogue above a stage, or onto audience members' phones, in sync with a live show.

The company markets it to resident theatres, opera houses, festivals, and touring productions that need to caption performances in multiple languages without hiring a dedicated surtitle operator for every single show. Instead of transcribing spoken audio after the fact (the job most "AI captioning" tools do), Captitles works from the show's actual script: you import the text, and its AI parses it into discrete surtitle lines, distinguishing spoken dialogue from stage directions and splitting long lines into shorter, screen-friendly chunks automatically.

Captitles doesn't publish which specific language model or speech-recognition engine powers this parsing and its live-sync detection — like most vendors in this space, it treats that as proprietary, so any accuracy claim here should be read as what the company states rather than an independently verified benchmark.

If you're specifically after a tool that auto-captions short-form video for TikTok, Reels, or YouTube Shorts, [Submagic](/blog/submagic-review) is the more relevant review on this site — it covers that exact use case, including its credit-based pricing and B-roll automation. The two tools solve genuinely different problems and shouldn't be compared head-to-head.

## Pricing

| Plan | Price | Shows | Translations per show | Team members | Screens | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | €0/month | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 external screen | Speech detection & captions-to-audio are trial-only |
| Subscription | €75/month | Unlimited | 10 | 4 | 3 external screens, 3 languages each | Full speech detection and captions-to-audio access |
| Daily Rental | €4.99/day | Unlimited (that day) | 10 | 4 | 3 external screens | Same feature set as Subscription, billed per day used |

Captitles' free plan isn't a time-limited trial in the usual SaaS sense — it's a permanent tier capped at 2 shows and 1 translation each, positioned explicitly for amateur and community theatres running a single production rather than as a taste of the paid plan. The two paid options share the same feature set; the difference is simply whether you pay monthly for year-round use or by the day for a short run, festival slot, or tour stop where a full monthly subscription wouldn't be worth it.

There's no visible enterprise or multi-venue custom tier on the pricing page — festival circuits running several venues at once would likely need separate Subscription plans per venue or a direct conversation with Captitles.

Pricing, plan limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — confirm current figures on [Captitles' pricing page](https://www.captitles.com/pricing) before committing to a plan.

## Features walkthrough

**Script-to-surtitle AI conversion.** Rather than transcribing audio, Captitles reads an imported script and automatically identifies which lines are spoken dialogue versus stage directions, then breaks longer lines into shorter surtitle-length segments. This is the feature that separates it from generic subtitle software — it's built around how surtitling actually works in a theatre, where the source text exists before the performance does.

**AI-assisted translation with style preservation.** Captitles states its translation engine works across the full script for context, aiming to preserve tone and writing style rather than translating line-by-line in isolation — a meaningful distinction for theatre, where dialogue often carries rhythm and register that a literal translation would flatten.

**Live sync and automatic detection during performances.** During an actual show, Captitles can automatically detect where the live performance is in the script and advance the correct surtitle line in real time, reducing (though the company doesn't claim eliminating) the need for a dedicated human surtitle operator clicking through cues manually.

**Mobile screening to audience devices.** Beyond an overhead screen, Captitles can push captions directly to spectators' phones, letting individual audience members follow along in their own language without a shared physical screen — useful for smaller venues or productions running several language options simultaneously.

**Cloud collaboration and line flagging.** Dramaturgs, directors, and translators can work on the same script and translation set simultaneously, similar to a shared document, and flag specific lines needing revision without interrupting a live screening in progress.

## Who it's actually for

- **Community and amateur theatres running a single show**: The free plan's 2-show, 1-translation cap is genuinely usable here, not just a stripped-down trial — though speech detection and captions-to-audio remain trial-only until you upgrade.
- **Resident theatres and opera houses programming year-round**: The €75/month Subscription plan's unlimited shows and 10 translations per show fit a venue running a rotating season rather than a single production.
- **Festivals and touring productions**: The €4.99/day rental plan is built for exactly this — full feature access without paying for months you're not using, which matters for a two-week festival run or a touring show that only visits a venue occasionally.
- **Short-form video creators, podcasters, or YouTubers**: Not the right tool. Captitles has no audio transcription-first workflow, no vertical-video export, and nothing resembling the animated caption styles that drive engagement on TikTok or Reels — look at [Submagic](/blog/submagic-review) instead.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely useful free tier for single-production community theatres | Niche product — irrelevant if you need social/YouTube video captions |
| Daily rental pricing fits festivals and short runs well | No published enterprise/multi-venue tier visible on the pricing page |
| Script-first workflow matches how surtitling actually works in theatre | Underlying AI models/tech not disclosed |
| Real-time live sync reduces (not eliminates) need for a manual operator | Full speech detection and captions-to-audio gated behind paid plans |
| Cloud collaboration lets translators and directors work simultaneously | Limited independent reviews available to cross-check accuracy claims |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Captitles is a closed, purpose-built web platform rather than a tool designed to plug into a broader stack. It doesn't advertise a public API, Zapier connector, or Slack integration — its "integration" story is really about the venue side: pushing output to external screens (projectors, TVs) and to audience members' own mobile devices during a live show. If your workflow needs programmatic access to caption data, confirm directly with the company.

## Where it's a strong fit

Captitles makes the most sense for theatres and performance venues that currently rely on a manually operated surtitle system (someone clicking through cues live) or outsource translation and surtitling to a third party per production. The script-first AI parsing genuinely automates a task that's traditionally manual and error-prone, and the daily-rental option removes the awkwardness of paying for a full month when you only need coverage for a festival week or a single touring stop.

## Where to think twice

If you're looking for a tool to caption short-form social video, skip Captitles entirely — it has no relevant features for that use case, and reviewing it as if it competes with TikTok/Reels captioning tools would be comparing apples to a completely different fruit. It's also not the right choice if your venue needs a documented public API or enterprise SSO/compliance features, since none of that is advertised on the pricing or feature pages. And because Captitles doesn't publish independent accuracy benchmarks for its script-parsing or live-sync detection, larger venues running high-stakes, multi-language premieres may want to pilot it on a lower-stakes show first before trusting it for opening night.

## The bottom line

Captitles fills a specific, underserved niche well: AI-assisted surtitling for live theatre, built around how a script actually becomes a live performance rather than around transcribing audio after the fact. For amateur and community theatres, the free plan is a real option, not just a teaser. For resident venues and touring productions, the Subscription and Daily Rental plans map sensibly onto how theatres actually operate — a season versus a single run. Just don't confuse it with the crowded field of AI video-captioning tools built for creators; if that's what you need, look elsewhere on this site instead.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Captitles free to use?**
Yes, there's a permanent free plan covering 2 shows and 1 translation per show, with speech detection and captions-to-audio available only as a trial. It's aimed at amateur and community theatres rather than being a time-limited trial of the paid plan.

**How much does Captitles cost for a festival run?**
The Daily Rental plan is €4.99/day and includes the same feature set as the €75/month Subscription plan (unlimited shows, 10 translations per show, 4 team members, 3 external screens), making it the more cost-effective choice for short festival runs or tour stops.

**Does Captitles work from audio or from a script?**
Primarily from a script. Captitles' AI parses an imported script into surtitle lines and detects dialogue versus stage directions, then uses live detection to sync those pre-written lines to the actual performance in real time — it isn't a live audio-transcription tool.

**Can audience members see captions on their own phones?**
Yes, Captitles supports mobile screening, letting spectators follow surtitles on personal devices rather than only via an overhead or side-stage screen.

**Is Captitles the same kind of tool as Submagic or CapCut?**
No. Submagic and similar tools auto-caption short-form video for social platforms from spoken audio. Captitles is built for live theatre surtitling from a script. They don't overlap in use case despite both involving "captions." See our [Submagic review](/blog/submagic-review) if you're after the short-form video use case.

**Does Captitles disclose what AI model powers its transcription and translation?**
No — the company doesn't publish the specific models or engines behind its script parsing, translation, or live-sync detection. Treat any accuracy claim as a vendor statement rather than an independently verified figure.

**Is there an API for Captitles?**
Not one that's publicly advertised on its pricing or feature pages as of this review. If API access matters for your production pipeline, confirm directly with Captitles.

**Who is Captitles NOT a good fit for?**
Anyone captioning social media video, podcasts, or YouTube content, and any venue needing a documented enterprise API or multi-venue custom contract not currently listed on the public pricing page.

title: HeadshotPro Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is HeadshotPro worth it for LinkedIn photos? A detailed look at its pricing tiers, features, team tools and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is HeadshotPro worth it for professional headshots?

HeadshotPro is a solid pick if you need LinkedIn- or corporate-ready headshots without booking a photographer — it turns a handful of selfies into 30-70 polished portraits in as little as 15-30 minutes, starting at $29 one-time with no subscription. It's best for individuals and teams who need fast, consistent results; it's a weaker fit if you need guaranteed studio-grade realism for print or a fully free option.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $29 one-time (Basic, 30 headshots) |
| Free tier/trial | No free tier; money-back guarantee if the result "doesn't look like you" |
| Best for | Individuals, teams and enterprises needing fast, professional headshots without a photo shoot |
| Standout feature | 30-minute-or-less turnaround with team admin dashboard and API for bulk/whitelabel use |

## What HeadshotPro actually is

HeadshotPro is an AI headshot generator founded in 2023 that converts a set of uploaded selfies into studio-style professional portraits — no camera, lighting kit or photographer required. You upload roughly 6-20 photos of yourself taken on a phone, pick a gender-appropriate outfit and backdrop combination (or let the tool auto-pair one for you), and the model generates dozens of finished headshots in a range of styles: corporate blazer against a gray backdrop, casual blouse against a bookshelf, scrubs for healthcare workers, and so on.

HeadshotPro doesn't publicly name the underlying image-generation model on its marketing pages, so treat "which diffusion model powers this" as an open question best confirmed directly with the company if it matters to your evaluation. What the company does state clearly is its data-handling policy: uploaded photos are not used to train its models, and source photos are automatically deleted after 30 days, with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS in transit during that window.

No SmartFares store entry currently exists for HeadshotPro, so pricing and feature details below are sourced directly from the company's own pricing and product pages.

## Pricing

HeadshotPro sells one-time credit packs rather than a recurring subscription for individuals — unusual in the AI-tool space and worth knowing if you're comparing it against subscription-based competitors.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $29 one-time | 30 headshots, ~2 hour turnaround, 6 photo credits for edits, no free redo |
| Professional | $39 one-time | 50 headshots, ~30 minute turnaround, 26 photo credits, 1 free redo within 14 days |
| Executive | $59 one-time | 70 headshots, ~15 minute turnaround, 46 photo credits, 4K downloads, portrait + landscape formats, 1 free redo within 14 days |
| Team | From $25.35 per person (per "shoot" credit) | 40 headshots + 1 free retry per person, admin dashboard, bulk management, volume discounts up to 50% off at scale, credits never expire |
| Enterprise | Custom pricing | Everything in Team, plus SSO/SCIM, signed MSA, dedicated support |

There's no ongoing free tier — you pay per shoot rather than per month. Every package carries a "money back if it doesn't look like you" guarantee, and Professional/Executive throw in one free regeneration within 14 days. Team credits are pooled and don't expire, which matters if you're rolling out headshots gradually rather than all at once.

Pricing and features above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — confirm current numbers on [HeadshotPro's official pricing page](https://www.headshotpro.com/pricing) before buying.

## Core features walkthrough

**Speed tiers you actually pay for.** Unlike most AI photo tools that treat turnaround as an afterthought, HeadshotPro prices it directly — Basic takes about 2 hours, Executive claims 15 minutes. Pay for speed if you need a LinkedIn photo before a same-day interview; otherwise Basic saves money for the same output count.

**Backdrop and outfit combinations.** The company advertises "thousands" of backdrop/outfit pairings split by gender, covering corporate (suits, blazers), medical (scrubs), casual and creative-industry looks. A "choose for me" auto-pairing option is a genuinely useful shortcut when you just want a fast, reasonable batch without fiddling with style pickers.

**4K upscaling and format flexibility.** The Executive tier adds 4K downloads plus portrait and landscape crops — useful when the same headshot needs to work as a LinkedIn photo, a website team-page portrait, and a print bio at once.

**Built-in profile picture editor.** Rather than exporting a raw image and cropping it in a separate app, HeadshotPro includes an editor for logo overlays, text, and platform-specific crops (LinkedIn, Slack, email signature sizing).

**Team rollout tools.** For companies buying headshots for a whole staff, admins can pre-select approved styles centrally while employees self-upload their own photos via a passwordless magic-link — no shared logins or manual photo-collection spreadsheets. Combined with pooled, non-expiring credits, this is built for the "50 new hires need consistent headshots by next quarter" scenario that individual AI photo apps aren't designed for.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo professionals and job seekers** updating a LinkedIn photo or resume headshot on a budget — the $29-39 one-time packs cover this without a recurring cost.
- **Freelancers and consultants** who need a handful of polished portrait variations for a website, pitch deck, or speaker bio — the Executive tier's 4K output and landscape crops fit here.
- **HR and People teams** onboarding new hires who need consistent company-wide headshots without scheduling a photographer visit for every new employee — the Team plan's admin dashboard and magic-link self-upload flow are built for this.
- **Larger organizations** with SSO/compliance requirements — the Enterprise tier adds SCIM provisioning and a signed MSA, which smaller plans don't include.
- **Developers building on top of it** — the documented API lets you manage teams, retrieve generated photos, check credit balances, and whitelabel the whole workflow inside your own app, though HeadshotPro doesn't publish API pricing separately from the standard plans.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| No subscription — pay once per shoot, credits don't expire on Team plans | No ongoing free tier to test before paying |
| Fast turnaround, with a paid option for 15-minute delivery | Underlying AI model isn't publicly named, which limits transparency for technical buyers |
| Wide style/backdrop selection with a "choose for me" shortcut | Results depend heavily on source-photo quality; poor selfies produce weaker output |
| Money-back guarantee plus free redo on higher tiers | Redo policy is limited to Professional/Executive tiers and a 14-day window |
| Team dashboard and API for bulk/whitelabel rollout | API pricing isn't published separately — worth confirming directly before building on it |
| SOC 2 Type II compliance and 30-day photo auto-deletion | Enterprise pricing is fully custom, requiring a sales conversation for larger teams |

## Integrations and ecosystem

HeadshotPro publishes a documented API (currently V2, with V1 kept for legacy support) that lets developers programmatically invite team members, create and organize teams, pull generated photos and favorites, and monitor credit balances. The stated use case is whitelabeling — embedding HeadshotPro's headshot generation inside another product or internal HR tool rather than sending employees to HeadshotPro's own site. Authentication uses bearer tokens issued from your organization settings.

Beyond the API, HeadshotPro doesn't market a Zapier connector or a broad third-party integration marketplace — its ecosystem is narrower and aimed more at the API/whitelabel path than plug-and-play integrations with tools like Slack or HR platforms. Confirm any specific integration is supported, or buildable via the API, before committing budget.

## Where it's a strong fit

HeadshotPro is a strong fit if you need a batch of consistent, professional-looking headshots fast, without booking a photographer, and you're comfortable with a one-time payment instead of a subscription. It's particularly well suited to company-wide rollouts — the admin dashboard, self-upload magic links and pooled non-expiring credits solve a real coordination problem that individual photo-editing apps don't address at all. Job seekers and freelancers on a tight budget also get real value from the $29-39 entry tiers if a couple dozen output variations is genuinely all they need.

## Where to think twice

Skip HeadshotPro, or temper expectations, if any of the following apply to you:

- **You need a fully free tool.** There's no free tier — every credit pack costs money up front.
- **You need guaranteed print-grade or studio-verified realism.** AI headshots can occasionally show subtle artifacts (odd hands, slightly off ears, mismatched accessory lighting) that a trained eye catches faster than a screen will. The money-back guarantee helps, but it's a refund, not a fix.
- **You require documented model provenance for a compliance review.** HeadshotPro doesn't name its underlying AI model publicly, so confirm those details directly with the company before an enterprise contract.
- **You need offline or on-prem generation.** This is cloud-only SaaS; there's no self-hosted option.
- **Your source photos are low quality.** Blurry, poorly lit, or heavily filtered selfies drag down output regardless of tier.

## The bottom line

HeadshotPro earns its "professional headshot without a photographer" pitch reasonably well: one-time pricing avoids subscription fatigue, the turnaround tiers mean something real (paying more genuinely buys speed), and the team-rollout tooling solves a real HR pain point rather than being bolted on. It's not a fully free tool, it won't replace a studio shoot for people needing airtight print-grade realism, and the model's specifics stay undisclosed. For most individuals and teams who just need a good professional photo fast, it's a reasonable $29-59 bet — start with a single Professional-tier purchase before committing a whole team's budget to it.

## Frequently asked questions

**How much does HeadshotPro cost?**
Individual one-time packs run from $29 (Basic, 30 headshots) to $59 (Executive, 70 headshots, 4K output). Team plans start around $25.35 per person per shoot with volume discounts, and Enterprise is custom-priced. Confirm current figures on HeadshotPro's own pricing page, since they can change.

**Is there a free trial or free tier?**
No. HeadshotPro doesn't offer an ongoing free tier — instead it backs every purchase with a money-back guarantee if the results don't look like you, and Professional/Executive buyers get one free redo within 14 days.

**What happens to my uploaded photos?**
HeadshotPro states that uploaded selfies aren't used to train its AI models and are auto-deleted after 30 days, with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS in transit. It also states SOC 2 Type II compliance and offers a DPA for business customers on request.

**How long does it take to get results?**
Turnaround is tied to the plan: about 2 hours on Basic, roughly 30 minutes on Professional, and as fast as 15 minutes on Executive.

**Is HeadshotPro good for teams, not just individuals?**
Yes — that's arguably its strongest differentiator versus single-user AI photo apps. The Team plan includes an admin dashboard, passwordless self-upload for employees, pooled non-expiring credits, and volume discounts that scale up to 50% off at higher credit counts.

**What are the alternatives to HeadshotPro?**
Other AI headshot generators exist with similar selfie-to-portrait workflows and comparable one-time or credit-based pricing. Compare turnaround speed, team/admin tooling, data-retention policy and refund terms side by side rather than price alone, since that's where offerings genuinely differ.

**Do I need any special photography skills or equipment?**
No. You upload existing phone selfies with a reasonable variety of angles and lighting, and the AI handles the rest. Better source photos produce better results, so a few minutes taking clear, well-lit selfies before uploading is worth it.

**Does HeadshotPro offer an API for developers?**
Yes. A documented V2 API (with legacy V1 support) lets developers manage teams, retrieve generated photos, check credit balances, and whitelabel the workflow inside another product, authenticated via bearer tokens. API-specific pricing isn't published separately, so confirm costs directly with HeadshotPro if building on it.
