title: Parakeet AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Parakeet AI gives live interview answer suggestions and invisible screen-share overlays. Here's what it costs and who it's actually for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Parakeet AI worth it for interview prep?

Parakeet AI is a real-time AI copilot that listens to your interview or sales call and feeds you live answer suggestions, code, and talking points while you talk. It works well as a coding-interview crutch and mock-interview trainer, but the $100+/month Unlimited plan and the ethics of using a hidden assistant during a live interview are real considerations before you buy.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Prepare Only plan from roughly $12/month billed annually (question bank, resume tools, headshots — no live call sessions) |
| **Free tier/trial** | Free trial, no credit card required, per the official pricing page |
| **Best for** | Software engineering interview candidates needing live coding/behavioral answer support |
| **Standout feature** | "Invisible" overlay that stays undetectable during screen share on Zoom, Teams, Meet, Webex, HackerRank, LeetCode, and CoderPad |

## What Parakeet AI actually is

Parakeet AI is a browser- and desktop-based assistant built by ParakeetAI d.o.o. that transcribes a live conversation — a job interview, a sales call, a client meeting — and generates suggested responses in real time, based on the audio it hears through your microphone or system audio. It positions itself less as a general chatbot and more as a purpose-built "call copilot": it detects when someone asks you a question, decides what kind of question it is (behavioral, technical, coding), and pushes a suggested answer or code snippet to a small overlay window only you can see.

The company doesn't publish which specific LLMs power the tool; its marketing copy says it "selects between top available LLMs" and pairs that with a "state-of-the-art transcription model." Neither claim is independently documented, so treat "100% Accurate Responses" — a phrase used on the marketing site — as a vendor claim rather than a verified benchmark; no interview-copilot tool can guarantee correctness on live, unscripted technical questions.

The product actually bundles three distinct uses under one subscription:

- **Live call assistance** — the real-time overlay during actual interviews or sales calls.
- **Interview preparation tools** — a "Question Bank" of interview questions by role/company, a resume builder, and an AI-generated LinkedIn headshot tool.
- **Mock interview practice** — a simulated interview with an AI interviewer, meant to be used before the real thing rather than during it.

## Pricing

Parakeet AI's pricing page geo-detects and displays rates in local currency (it showed Indian rupees when we checked); the approximate USD figures below are converted from that listing and should be re-confirmed in your own currency on the [official pricing page](https://www.parakeet-ai.com/pricing), since exact tiers can shift.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Prepare Only | ~$12/month billed annually (~$35/month billed monthly) | Question Bank, resume builder, up to 20 resume PDF downloads and 30 headshots per day — no live call sessions |
| Unlimited | ~$38/month billed annually (~$114/month billed monthly) | Unlimited live call sessions, unlimited mock interviews, full "privacy/invisible" mode, all Prepare Only tools |
| Credit packs | ~$28–$45 per pack depending on bundle size | Pay-as-you-go: 0.5 credit = one 30-minute call session or mock interview; 0.5 credit = one resume download or headshot; 1 credit = one Question Bank unlock |

A free trial is offered with no credit card required, and the company advertises no lock-in contracts, with cancellation available anytime. Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tools in this category iterate fast, so verify current numbers before subscribing.

There's no matching store entry for Parakeet AI on this site yet, so the figures above come directly from the vendor's pricing page rather than a verified coupon listing.

## Features walkthrough

**Real-time answer generation.** As someone speaks, Parakeet transcribes it and — per the vendor — responds in as little as 124 milliseconds with a suggested answer, walking through a technical approach or drafting a behavioral talking point. That speed claim is Parakeet's own figure, unverified independently, though it's consistent with how streaming-transcription-plus-LLM pipelines are typically architected.

**"Invisible" operation.** The feature the product is really built around. Parakeet says its overlay has no dock icon, no visible process name in Activity Monitor, and doesn't register as a shared window when you screen-share — verified, per the company, against Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, Lark/Feishu, Amazon Chime, CoderPad, and HackerRank specifically. That specificity is more concrete than most competitors offer, and it's the main reason candidates pick this tool over a general-purpose AI chat window.

**Coding interview mode.** Beyond conversational Q&A, Parakeet handles live coding rounds — reading a problem off a shared screen (LeetCode, CoderPad, HackerRank) and generating suggested code with explanations for technical phone screens.

**Document upload and context.** You can upload a resume, job description, or project notes so answers get tailored to your actual background instead of generic advice.

**Mock interview + prep suite.** Outside live-call mode, the Question Bank, AI mock interviewer, resume builder, and headshot generator function as a standalone prep kit even if you never touch the live overlay.

## Who it's actually for

- **Job seekers doing high-volume technical interview loops** (new grads, career-switchers into engineering) are the core audience for the Unlimited plan — frequent live coding rounds are where the invisibility and coding-support features earn their keep.
- **Occasional interviewees** doing one or two interviews a quarter are better served by the Credits plan than a recurring Unlimited subscription, since the per-session cost works out lower than a month of Unlimited if you're not interviewing constantly.
- **People who just want prep tools** — question banks, a resume rewrite, a professional headshot, mock practice — without ever running the live overlay should look at Prepare Only, which is meaningfully cheaper.
- **Sales and customer-success reps** doing live client calls are a secondary use case the vendor markets to, though most of the site's own marketing and the Question Bank/resume features are clearly interview-first.
- **Teams needing procurement-grade compliance** (SOC 2 reports, enterprise data agreements) won't find that documentation published on the marketing site as of this review — enterprise buyers should ask directly before committing budget.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Real-time overlay purpose-built for live interviews, not a generic chatbot retrofitted for the job | Unlimited plan is genuinely expensive at ~$114/month billed monthly (~$38/month annually is far more reasonable, but requires an upfront year commitment) |
| Invisibility tested against named platforms (Zoom, Teams, Meet, Webex, HackerRank, CoderPad, etc.), not just a vague "works everywhere" claim | Underlying LLM(s) and transcription model aren't disclosed, so accuracy claims can't be independently verified |
| Credits option for infrequent users avoids paying for a full month of access for one interview | Using it live during an actual interview raises real integrity questions many employers would object to if discovered |
| Bundled prep tools (question bank, resume builder, mock interviews, headshots) add value beyond the live-call feature | No published SOC 2/enterprise compliance documentation on the public site |
| Free trial with no credit card required lowers the barrier to test it | Pricing page geo-detects currency, making cross-region comparison harder without manual conversion |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Parakeet AI isn't an API-first developer tool — it's a consumer-facing desktop/browser app, so there's no public API, Zapier connector, or Slack integration. Its "integrations" are really platform compatibility: it runs invisibly alongside Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, Lark/Feishu, Amazon Chime, CoderPad, HackerRank, and LeetCode rather than connecting with other software in your stack. If you need programmatic access or workflow automation, this isn't that category of tool.

## Where it's a strong fit

Parakeet AI is a strong fit if you're actively interviewing for software engineering roles and keep getting stuck on live coding rounds or freezing on behavioral questions under pressure — a coding-aware live assistant plus a mock-interview trainer covers both failure modes in one subscription. It's also reasonable for candidates who want the prep tools (question bank, resume rewriting, a headshot) even if they never turn on the live overlay during an actual call.

## Where to think twice

Skip the live-assistance feature if you interview for companies that explicitly prohibit AI assistance and conduct proctored or in-person interviews — being caught using a hidden overlay can get an offer rescinded, and some employers have changed interview formats specifically because of tools like this. If you need a fully free solution, Parakeet's trial is limited rather than a permanent free tier, so budget-constrained candidates may prefer free mock-interview resources and pay only for a short credits burst right before a real loop. Enterprise teams needing SOC 2 or data-residency documentation won't find it published here and should contact the vendor directly. And if you want a transparent, disclosed model stack, Parakeet's "top available LLMs" phrasing is vaguer than competitors that name their underlying model explicitly.

## The bottom line

Parakeet AI does what it says: it gives you a genuinely hard-to-detect live overlay with coding-aware answer suggestions, on top of a reasonably complete interview-prep toolkit. The Unlimited plan is pricey month-to-month, so anyone who isn't interviewing constantly should default to the Credits plan or the cheaper Prepare Only tier for the non-live tools. The bigger question isn't whether the software works — it's whether using AI assistance covertly during a live interview is something you're comfortable doing given your specific employer's policies, since that risk sits with the candidate, not the vendor.

## FAQ

**Is Parakeet AI free?**
There's a free trial with no credit card required, but no permanent free tier — ongoing use requires a Credits pack or a Prepare Only/Unlimited subscription.

**How much does Parakeet AI cost?**
Plans run from roughly $12/month (Prepare Only, annual) up to about $114/month (Unlimited, monthly), with a cheaper ~$38/month rate on annual Unlimited. Credit packs suit occasional use. Confirm exact pricing on the [official pricing page](https://www.parakeet-ai.com/pricing), since it geo-detects currency.

**Does Parakeet AI actually stay invisible during screen sharing?**
The vendor states it's verified undetectable across platforms including Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, Webex, HackerRank, and CoderPad. That's a vendor claim we haven't independently tested, and detection methods can change as platforms update.

**Is it ethical or allowed to use during a real interview?**
That depends on the employer's stated policy. Many companies explicitly prohibit AI assistance, and some have moved to proctored formats specifically because of tools like this. Using it against stated rules risks disqualification or a rescinded offer.

**What data does Parakeet AI collect from my calls?**
The marketing pages don't publish detailed data-handling documentation beyond a general privacy policy link; anyone concerned about audio/transcript retention should read the current privacy policy before using it on a real call.

**Does Parakeet AI work for coding interviews specifically?**
Yes — it's built for LeetCode, HackerRank, and CoderPad, offering live code suggestions and explanations, one of its more differentiated features versus generic AI chat assistants.

**What's the difference between Unlimited, Prepare Only, and Credits?**
Unlimited includes unlimited live sessions plus all prep tools; Prepare Only covers the question bank, resume builder, and headshots but excludes live sessions; Credits is pay-as-you-go for individual sessions, downloads, or unlocks.

**Are there alternatives to Parakeet AI?**
Yes — the live-interview-copilot category includes similar tools such as Final Round AI and Interview Coder, each with different pricing and platform-invisibility claims; compare based on which video platforms and coding sites you'll actually be tested on.

For more AI tool coverage, see the [AI & software deals](/category/software) category.

title: Quidget Review 2026: AI Support Chatbot Pricing, Verdict
excerpt: Quidget review: how this pay-per-resolution AI support agent from SupportYourApp prices, its features, and where it's a strong or weak fit.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Quidget worth it for automating customer support?

Quidget is worth a look if you want an AI support agent that resolves chat, email, and voice tickets and only charges you when it closes a ticket. Built by SupportYourApp, a 15-year support outsourcing company, it shows in the hybrid AI-plus-human handoff design. It's less appealing if you want a flat, forecastable monthly bill, since pay-per-resolution costs scale with volume.

### At a glance

| | Quidget |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $0.20 per AI resolution (Native Quidget plan) |
| Free tier/trial | "Start for Free" signup, no credit card required; no explicit free resolution allowance published |
| Best for | Support teams that want AI to only get billed when it actually closes a ticket |
| Standout feature | Pay-per-resolution billing — failed answers, handoffs, and test chats are free |

## What Quidget actually is

Quidget is an AI customer support agent built by [SupportYourApp](https://supportyourapp.com), a company that has run outsourced customer service operations for other businesses for more than 15 years. That parentage matters more here than it does for most AI chatbot startups: Quidget wasn't built by a pure AI lab bolting a support use case onto a language model — it's designed around a hybrid model where the AI handles repetitive work and humans stay in the loop for anything needing judgment.

The pitch is straightforward. Quidget trains on your existing help content — docs, FAQs, past tickets — and then handles incoming chat, email, and voice conversations across your website and messaging channels. According to Quidget, the agent "resolves 80% of tickets across chat, email, and voice," though that figure is the vendor's own stated claim rather than an independently audited benchmark, and actual resolution rates will depend heavily on how well-documented your product is and how open-ended the incoming questions are.

Quidget doesn't publish which specific large language model powers the agent — the site emphasizes the training and orchestration layer rather than naming an underlying LLM vendor. If model provenance matters for your evaluation, confirm it directly with Quidget's sales team rather than assume.

## Pricing: pay-per-resolution instead of per-seat

Most AI support chatbots price on conversation volume, message credits, or seats. Quidget instead prices per **resolution** — defined on its own pricing page as a conversation the AI closed without a human stepping in. Handoffs to a human agent, abandoned chats, failed answers, negative customer feedback, and test conversations are explicitly free. You only pay when the AI actually solves the customer's problem end to end.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native Quidget | $0.20 per AI resolution | Website widget, live chat, conversation inbox, AI summaries, flows, templates, multi-channel support |
| Helpdesk Integration | $0.20 per AI resolution + $249/month | Everything in Native Quidget, plus handoff setup, integration maintenance, and connections to Zendesk, Freshdesk, Freshchat and similar helpdesks |
| Enterprise | Custom pricing | Volume discounts, custom seat pricing, custom helpdesk terms, tailored onboarding, dedicated account manager |

Quidget's site advertises a "Start for Free" signup with no credit card required, but it doesn't spell out a specific number of free resolutions included before billing kicks in — worth confirming directly with Quidget before you commit, since it affects how cheaply you can actually pilot the tool. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly in the AI tools space, so double-check current numbers on Quidget's own pricing page before signing up.

The pay-per-resolution model is genuinely different from most competitors. Tools like Tidio's Lyro agent or SiteSpeakAI charge per conversation or credit regardless of outcome, meaning you pay even when the bot fails and a human steps in anyway. Quidget removes that frustration — but its bill is variable and harder to forecast, especially once the $249/month helpdesk fee is added.

## Core features that actually matter

**Multi-channel coverage.** Quidget handles website chat widgets, email, and voice in one system, plus messaging channels including WhatsApp, Telegram, and Viber. Most competitors in this price range stop at website chat and maybe email — voice support is unusual at this end of the market.

**Language coverage.** Quidget supports 45+ languages with auto-detection, which matters if your customer base isn't English-only. This is one of the more concrete, checkable claims on the site rather than a vague marketing figure.

**Human handoff with full context.** When the AI can't resolve something, it escalates to a human agent along with the full conversation history, so customers don't have to repeat themselves. Given SupportYourApp's outsourcing background, this handoff flow appears to be a genuine focus area rather than an afterthought.

**Continuous learning.** Quidget says the agent improves from ongoing interactions rather than staying static after initial training. As with the 80% resolution figure, treat this as a vendor claim rather than an independently verified metric.

**No-code setup.** Setup is built around uploading existing content (docs, FAQs, help center articles) rather than building conversation flows from scratch, which shortens time-to-launch for teams without a dedicated support-ops engineer.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo founders and small e-commerce shops** get the most value from the Native Quidget plan — pay-per-resolution billing means no fixed monthly fee for support automation you're barely using yet, though map out expected ticket volume before assuming the math beats a flat competitor plan.
- **Mid-size support teams already on Zendesk or Freshdesk** are the target for the Helpdesk Integration tier. The $249/month base fee plus per-resolution charges only pays off once the AI is meaningfully offloading work from paid human agents.
- **Enterprises with compliance or custom-seat requirements** should go straight to the custom-priced Enterprise tier and get data handling, SLA, and account-management specifics in writing.
- **Teams that want voice support automated**, not just chat and email, are better served here than by most website-widget-only competitors, since voice handling is a genuine differentiator.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Pay only for resolved tickets, not failed attempts or handoffs | Variable billing makes monthly cost harder to forecast than flat-fee competitors |
| Voice channel support alongside chat and email is rare at this price point | No specific LLM/model disclosed, limiting transparency for technical evaluators |
| 45+ language support with auto-detection | No published free-resolution allowance — real trial cost is unclear upfront |
| Built by a 15-year customer support operations company, with handoff design to match | Helpdesk integration tier adds a flat $249/month fee on top of per-resolution pricing |
| No-code setup trained on existing docs/FAQs | Independently reported resolution-rate benchmarks aren't available to verify the 80% claim |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Quidget connects to Zendesk, Freshdesk, and Freshchat for helpdesk routing (Helpdesk Integration plan and above), plus messaging channels including Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, and Viber, and Calendly for scheduling handoffs. There's no mention of a public API or Zapier app on the site, so confirm with sales if you need a broader stack.

## Where it's a strong fit

Quidget makes sense if your support volume is high enough that per-resolution pricing beats a flat per-seat SaaS bill, and if you specifically want a system that doesn't charge you for the AI's failures. It's also a solid pick if voice support automation matters, since that's rarer than chat-only bots at this price tier, and if you run support across several languages without hiring native speakers for each one.

## Where to think twice

Skip Quidget if you need predictable, flat monthly costs for budgeting — pay-per-resolution pricing moves with your support volume and success rate, which can be uncomfortable for finance teams used to fixed SaaS pricing. It's also not the right pick if you need airtight guarantees about which LLM answers your customers, since that isn't published, and regulated industries with strict model-provenance requirements should get that in writing first.

If you want a completely free, unlimited chatbot with no usage-based cost, look elsewhere — Quidget's free option is a no-credit-card signup, not a permanent free tier with a fixed allowance. And if your support volume is very low, a fixed-seat helpdesk plan with a built-in AI add-on might work out cheaper in absolute dollars, even if the per-unit economics look worse on paper.

## The bottom line

Quidget's pay-per-resolution billing is a genuinely different, customer-friendly way to price an AI support agent — you're not stuck paying for a bot that fails, unlike flatter per-conversation pricing elsewhere in this category. Voice channel support and 45-language coverage add real differentiation against website-widget-only competitors. The tradeoffs are transparency (no disclosed model, no published free-resolution allowance) and predictability (variable billing instead of a flat monthly number). If your ticket volume makes the math work and you're comfortable confirming specifics — free-tier limits, model details, SLA terms — directly with Quidget first, it's a solid contender for automating routine support without over-hiring.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Quidget free to use?**
Quidget offers a "Start for Free" signup with no credit card required, but it doesn't publish a specific number of free AI resolutions included before paid billing applies. Confirm the exact free allowance with Quidget directly before assuming it covers a meaningful trial.

**How much does Quidget cost?**
The Native Quidget plan charges $0.20 per AI resolution with no separate monthly fee. The Helpdesk Integration plan adds a $249/month base fee on top of the same per-resolution charge for connecting to tools like Zendesk and Freshdesk. Enterprise pricing is custom.

**What counts as an "AI resolution" on Quidget?**
A resolution is a conversation the AI closed without a human agent stepping in. Handoffs to humans, abandoned chats, failed answers, and test conversations are not billed.

**What channels does Quidget support?**
Website live chat, email, and voice, plus messaging integrations with WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber, and Slack.

**Which languages does Quidget support?**
Quidget states it supports 45+ languages with automatic detection, so it can respond to customers in their own language without manual per-market setup.

**Does Quidget disclose which AI model it uses?**
No. Quidget's public site describes its training and orchestration approach but doesn't name a specific underlying language model. Ask sales directly if this matters for compliance.

**Is Quidget good for small businesses or only enterprise teams?**
Both. Small businesses can use the Native Quidget plan without a flat monthly fee, paying only per resolution. Larger teams needing helpdesk integrations or custom terms have the Helpdesk Integration and Enterprise tiers.

**What are the best alternatives to Quidget?**
[Lyro AI by Tidio](/blog/lyro-ai-review) is a Claude-powered alternative with a free 50-conversation allowance and per-conversation pricing rather than per-resolution. [CoSupport AI](/blog/cosupport-ai-review) targets larger Zendesk/Freshdesk/Salesforce teams with a resolution guarantee. [SiteSpeakAI](/blog/sitespeakai-review) leans toward website-content-trained chatbots with credit-based pricing. Compare based on your actual channel mix and expected ticket volume.

For more AI and software coverage, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: FreJun Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: FreJun is an AI-powered CRM calling platform for sales and support teams. Here is what it costs, what it does well, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is FreJun worth it for a sales or support team?

FreJun is a cloud calling platform for sales, support and recruiting teams that need CRM-synced calling, recordings and AI call insights without building telecom infrastructure themselves. It suits small-to-mid teams already using HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho or Pipedrive; it's a weaker fit for a solo user wanting a free calling app.

### At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $16.99/user/month (Standard, monthly billing) |
| Free tier / trial | Free trial on signup; FreJun Teler offers 25,000 promotional calling credits for new developer signups |
| Best for | Sales, support and recruiting teams calling out of a CRM |
| Standout feature | Native two-way CRM sync (HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Freshworks, Pipedrive, Dynamics 365) plus AI call insights |

## What FreJun actually is

FreJun is an India-founded cloud telephony company that sells two related products under one umbrella. **FreJun Dialer** is the business-facing product — a browser and mobile calling app that plugs into a CRM so sales and support reps can click to call a lead, have the call auto-logged, and get a recording, transcript and AI-generated summary attached to that contact's record afterward. **FreJun Teler** is the developer-facing side — programmable voice infrastructure (SIP trunking, virtual numbers in 50+ countries, low-latency streaming) for teams building their own AI voice agents rather than using FreJun's dialer interface.

This review focuses on FreJun Dialer, since that's the product most businesses evaluating "an AI calling tool" compare against competitors like JustCall or Ozonetel.

FreJun doesn't publish which underlying speech or language models power its AI transcription and insights features — like most calling platforms in this price range, it likely licenses third-party speech-to-text and summarization models rather than building its own. That's a reasonable approach for a company this size, but FreJun's marketing doesn't claim a proprietary in-house model, and neither should this review.

## Pricing

FreJun's pricing splits between a per-seat dialer plan, a mandatory virtual number fee, and a list of optional add-ons — so the advertised "$16.99/user/month" headline isn't the whole story.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | $16.99/user/month ($14.49/user/month billed annually) | 1 virtual number, $5 starter calling credits, call logs, call recordings, mobile app, click-to-call browser extension |
| Professional | $19.99/user/month ($16.99/user/month billed annually) | Everything in Standard, plus IVR, incoming call routing, custom reports, call transfer, post-call surveys |

Expect these recurring add-on costs on top of a plan:

| Add-on | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Extra virtual number | $6/number/month |
| CNAM (caller ID name) | $2/number/month |
| Autodial | $7/user/month |
| AI Insights (sentiment, talk-ratio, call summaries) | $0.009/minute |
| WhatsApp Business messaging | $9.99/user/month |

Outbound and inbound call minutes are billed on top of the subscription at carrier rates that vary by destination country — FreJun doesn't publish a flat per-minute rate, so budget for a usage-based line item rather than assuming the seat price is all-in. The AI Insights add-on is easy to miss in that math: a 20-person team making heavy daily calls can rack up a meaningful minutes-based bill on top of the per-seat license.

Pricing, free-tier limits and add-on availability above are accurate as of this post's publish date and can change fast — always confirm current numbers on FreJun's own pricing page before budgeting, especially carrier call rates, which FreJun doesn't lock in publicly.

## Features walkthrough

**CRM-native calling.** FreJun's core pitch is that reps never leave their CRM to make a call. Click-to-call from a HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Freshworks, Pipedrive or Microsoft Dynamics 365 record starts the call, and the outcome — duration, recording, notes — syncs back automatically. This two-way sync is the biggest reason teams choose FreJun over a generic softphone: it removes the manual logging step reps skip when they're busy.

**AI call insights and summaries.** Every recorded call can run through the AI Insights add-on to generate a transcript, automatic summary, and metrics like talk-to-listen ratio and sentiment. FreJun says this helps managers review call quality without listening to every recording — a reasonable claim, though as with any automated sentiment scoring, treat the label as a rough signal to spot-check rather than a definitive read.

**IVR and call routing (Professional plan).** For inbound-heavy teams, Professional adds an interactive voice response menu and rule-based routing, so incoming calls land with the right rep without a human dispatcher. It's genuinely absent from Standard, so teams needing any inbound routing should budget for Professional from day one.

**Auto-dialer for outbound volume.** The Autodial add-on lets reps queue a list of numbers and dial through them sequentially without manually re-dialing after every hang-up — useful for cold-calling sprints, at an extra $7/user/month.

**Virtual numbers across 50+ countries.** Because FreJun handles the underlying telecom layer, teams can get local-presence numbers in dozens of countries instead of always calling out on one home-country number, at $6/month per additional number.

## Who it's actually for

**Solo users or freelancers** are a poor fit — there's no meaningful free-forever tier, and the per-seat-plus-add-ons pricing model is built around teams, not a single person making occasional calls.

**Small sales or support teams (5–20 reps) already on a supported CRM** are FreJun's clearest audience. Standard covers basic click-to-call and recording; teams handling any inbound volume should go straight to Professional for IVR and routing.

**Recruiting and outreach-heavy teams** benefit from the Autodial add-on and multi-country virtual numbers, since recruiters and BDRs often call across regions and burn through call lists quickly.

**Developers building their own voice AI product** should look at FreJun Teler instead of Dialer — it's a genuinely different product (programmable SIP/API infrastructure vs. a ready-made dialer UI), and evaluating it means checking Teler's own docs and pricing.

**Larger enterprises with strict compliance requirements** should confirm SSO/SAML and role-based access claims directly with sales and get data residency/retention specifics in writing — the site states these features exist but doesn't publish a compliance-certification page (e.g. SOC 2) we could independently verify.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Native two-way sync with major CRMs (HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, Freshworks, Dynamics 365) | No free-forever plan; billing is per-seat plus multiple stacking add-ons |
| AI call summaries and sentiment tracking reduce manual call review | AI Insights, autodial, CNAM and WhatsApp are all separate paid add-ons, not included in either base plan |
| IVR and inbound routing available on Professional | IVR/routing locked out of the cheaper Standard plan entirely |
| Virtual numbers in 50+ countries suit international outbound teams | Per-minute carrier call rates aren't published upfront — real total cost is hard to estimate before talking to sales |
| Separate developer product (Teler) for teams building custom voice AI | Two distinct products (Dialer vs. Teler) under one brand can be confusing when researching pricing |

## Integrations and ecosystem

FreJun's integration story centers on CRMs rather than a broad app marketplace: native connections to HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho CRM, Freshworks, Pipedrive and Microsoft Dynamics 365, with click-to-call and automatic activity logging built into each. FreJun also offers API access and webhooks for custom workflows, and the WhatsApp Business add-on brings messaging into the same activity timeline as calls. There's no public Zapier listing at the time of writing, so confirm no-code automation is possible via the API before assuming it works out of the box.

## Where it's a strong fit

- Teams already standardized on one of FreJun's supported CRMs who want calling activity logged automatically instead of relying on reps to type notes.
- Outbound sales or recruiting teams that need multi-country virtual numbers and an auto-dialer to move through call lists faster.
- Support teams that need IVR-based call routing without building custom telecom infrastructure — provided they budget for the Professional tier.
- Teams that want AI-generated call summaries as a first-pass review tool for coaching reps, understanding this is a review aid, not a replacement for listening to calls that actually matter.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a genuinely free tool.** There's no free-forever plan — every seat, virtual number and most useful features beyond basic dialing carry a recurring cost.
- **If your team doesn't use one of FreJun's supported CRMs.** The core value proposition is CRM sync; without a supported CRM, a competitor built specifically for standalone use may serve you better.
- **If you need airtight, published compliance certifications up front** (e.g. SOC 2, HIPAA) for a regulated industry — get compliance specifics in writing from FreJun's sales team rather than assuming coverage from marketing copy.
- **If predictable, all-in pricing matters more than feature depth.** Between per-seat cost, per-number fees, and stacking add-ons (AI Insights, autodial, WhatsApp, CNAM), the real monthly bill can land well above the advertised $16.99–$19.99 headline, and carrier call-minute rates aren't published to fully model that in advance.
- **If you actually need the developer infrastructure product.** Anyone wanting to build a custom voice AI product should look at Teler's own pricing and docs, not this review.

## Bottom line

FreJun Dialer earns its keep for sales, support and recruiting teams that live inside a CRM and are tired of reps manually logging calls — the two-way sync into HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, Freshworks and Dynamics 365 is genuinely useful, and the AI call summaries are a decent first-pass coaching aid. Where it's harder to love is the pricing structure: the seat price is only the entry point, and IVR, autodial, AI insights, CNAM and WhatsApp are all separate line items that add up fast beyond a small, low-volume team. If your team runs on a supported CRM and needs inbound routing, budget for Professional plus the add-ons you'll actually use, and get a real per-minute call-rate quote before assuming the advertised price is your final bill.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is FreJun free to use?**
No. There's a free trial to test the product, but no permanent free tier — you'll need a paid Standard or Professional seat plus at least one virtual number to run it day to day.

**What's the difference between FreJun Dialer and FreJun Teler?**
Dialer is the ready-made calling app for sales and support teams, with a CRM-synced interface. Teler is a separate developer product for building custom voice AI applications on programmable infrastructure rather than using FreJun's dialer UI.

**Does FreJun record and transcribe calls?**
Yes, call recording is included from Standard, and AI-powered transcription, summaries and sentiment tracking are available through the AI Insights add-on at $0.009/minute.

**Which CRMs does FreJun integrate with?**
HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho CRM, Freshworks, Pipedrive and Microsoft Dynamics 365, all with native two-way sync.

**Does FreJun support international calling and numbers?**
Yes, virtual numbers across 50+ countries, at an extra $6/month per additional number.

**Is FreJun suitable for a solo user or freelancer?**
Not really — the pricing model and features (CRM sync, team routing, IVR) are built around teams, and a solo caller with light volume will find the per-seat-plus-add-ons cost hard to justify.

**How accurate is FreJun's AI sentiment scoring?**
FreJun doesn't publish independent accuracy figures, and no third-party benchmarking is publicly available — treat AI-generated sentiment as a directional signal for spot-checking calls, not a definitive score.

**Are there cheaper alternatives to FreJun?**
Yes — general VoIP/dialer platforms vary widely in price. If you only need basic click-to-call without IVR, autodial or AI insights, compare FreJun's Standard plan against simpler competitors before committing to Professional and its add-ons.

title: Rosie AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Rosie AI answers business calls 24/7, books appointments, and transfers urgent calls starting at $49/month. Here's the honest breakdown.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Rosie AI worth it for answering your business phones?

Rosie (heyrosie.com) is an AI phone receptionist built for small businesses that miss calls when the team is busy, on a job site, or closed for the night. It answers calls 24/7, books appointments, transfers urgent calls, and texts callers back — starting at $49/month for 250 minutes. It's a solid pick if your main pain point is missed calls, less so if you need a full omnichannel support platform.

Note upfront: "Rosie" is a common product name. This review covers **Rosie AI, the AI call-answering and receptionist service at heyrosie.com** — not any unrelated grocery, robotics, or personal-assistant app that also uses the name. If you landed here looking for a different "Rosie," this isn't it.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $49/month (Professional, 250 minutes) |
| Free trial | 7 days, all features, cancel anytime |
| Best for | Small businesses/solo operators missing calls (trades, clinics, salons, law firms) |
| Standout feature | Live and warm call transfers with team briefing, not just voicemail-style messaging |

No AI tool store profile exists yet for Rosie on this site, so pricing and feature details below come directly from heyrosie.com's homepage and pricing page, cross-checked against each other for consistency.

## What Rosie actually is

Rosie is a phone-answering service where an AI voice agent — not a human — picks up your business line, has a real-time conversation with the caller, and takes action based on rules you set. It's built for small businesses that can't staff a receptionist around the clock: contractors, med spas, law firms, salons, and similar appointment-driven businesses.

The setup pitch is that Rosie trains itself automatically from your website and Google Business Profile, so you're not manually feeding it a script from scratch. You still refine it — adjusting FAQs, hours, and call-handling scenarios — but the starting point is meant to require no developer or technical setup.

The company doesn't publish detailed founder or founding-date information on its site, and it's a newer entrant in a category that also includes Smith.ai, Ruby Receptionists, Numa, and My AI Front Desk. If verified company background matters for your vendor-vetting process, ask Rosie's sales team directly before signing an annual contract.

## Pricing

Rosie runs three monthly plans, all metered by minutes of AI call-handling time:

| Plan | Price | Minutes/month | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Professional | $49/mo | 250 | 2 custom message-taking scenarios, appointment links by text, spam filtering, free website chat widget |
| Scale | $149/mo | 1,000 | 5 custom scenarios, direct calendar booking, warm transfers with team briefing, live call transfers, mid-call texting |
| Growth | $299/mo | 2,000 | Unlimited custom scenarios, waterfall transfers across multiple numbers, custom agent training, white-glove onboarding, priority support |

All three tiers include 24/7 availability, simultaneous call handling (so no caller gets a busy signal), automatic spam/sales-call detection, call recordings, transcripts and summaries, and bilingual English/Spanish support.

There's also a website texting add-on at $50/month for 25 conversations, with a per-conversation overage charge beyond that. Website chat itself is bundled free into every plan.

Rosie offers a 7-day free trial with full feature access and no stated credit-card requirement, plus an annual billing option that Rosie says works out to two months free compared to paying monthly.

Pricing, minute allowances, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) based on heyrosie.com's own pricing page — AI receptionist products iterate fast, so confirm current numbers on their site before buying, especially if you're near a plan's minute ceiling and want to know the overage rate, which Rosie doesn't post publicly.

## Features walkthrough

**Real-time call handling and answering.** Rosie picks up the phone, has a live spoken conversation with the caller, answers common questions from a knowledge base trained on your site, and takes messages or books appointments based on what the caller needs.

**Warm and live call transfers.** On Scale and Growth, Rosie can transfer a call to a real person and brief them on what the caller needs before handing off — closer to how a trained human receptionist screens calls than a basic "press 1 for sales" IVR tree.

**Calendar booking built into the call.** Instead of taking a message and asking the caller to book online later, Rosie can check your calendar and book directly during the call on Scale and above — useful when the caller wants the slot locked in immediately.

**Spam and sales-call filtering.** Every plan detects spam and unsolicited sales calls automatically, so those don't eat into paid minutes or your team's attention the way a plain call-forwarding setup would.

**Website chat and texting.** Rosie extends past the phone line with a free website chat widget on every plan and an optional SMS layer for callers who'd rather text a quick question than wait on hold.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo operators and small trade businesses** (plumbers, electricians, cleaners) losing jobs to competitors who pick up faster — Professional's 250 minutes can suffice for low call volume, but track actual usage during the trial before committing.
- **Appointment-based service businesses** (salons, med spas, clinics, law firm intake) that need direct calendar booking during the call — this pushes you toward Scale, since Professional only sends booking links by text.
- **Growing teams with multiple staff to route calls to** — Growth's waterfall transfers across several numbers and unlimited custom scenarios fit a business that's outgrown a single-line setup.
- **Businesses replacing a human answering service** and testing whether AI matches it at a lower price — worth trialing, but expect an AI voice, not a human-indistinguishable one, and test with your own real caller scenarios rather than the vendor's demo script.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| 24/7 answering with no staffing cost or scheduling gaps | Minute-based pricing means costs scale with call volume, and Rosie doesn't publish its overage rate |
| Live/warm transfers instead of just voicemail-style messaging (Scale and up) | Direct calendar booking and unlimited scenarios are gated behind the two higher tiers |
| Automatic training from your website and Google Business Profile lowers setup effort | An AI voice will still occasionally misread accents, background noise, or unusual requests — no phone AI is immune to this |
| Bundled free website chat widget on every plan | Company transparency is thin — no public founder/team info or third-party audited review volume at time of writing |
| 7-day free trial with full features, cancel anytime | Bilingual support currently covers English and Spanish only, not a broader language set |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Rosie connects to calendar platforms for direct appointment booking (Scale plan and up) and lists Zapier connectivity, which in principle opens the door to 1,000+ apps for passing call data, messages, and bookings into a CRM or spreadsheet. Native iOS and Android apps are included so business owners can review call transcripts, summaries, and recordings from a phone rather than a desktop dashboard only.

What's less clear is a documented, developer-facing API or a list of specific CRM integrations (HubSpot, Salesforce, Jobber, etc.) by name — if a particular CRM connection is a dealbreaker, confirm it with Rosie's sales team during the trial rather than assuming Zapier alone covers it.

## Where it's a strong fit

Rosie makes the most sense for a small, appointment-driven business that is currently missing calls outright — voicemail, no answer, or an overwhelmed front desk — and needs something better than nothing, fast, without hiring a full-time receptionist or paying a traditional answering service's per-minute rates. It's also a fit for businesses that want transfers to stay "warm," with the AI briefing the human first, rather than a bare transfer that leaves the customer re-explaining themselves.

## Where to think twice

Skip Rosie, or trial it very carefully, if any of the following apply:

- **You need a fully free tool.** There's a 7-day trial but no permanent free tier; every plan is a paid subscription with a minute cap.
- **Your call volume is unpredictable or spiky.** Since pricing is minute-metered and the overage cost isn't published, a spike in calls could push your bill higher than expected without a clear rate to plan around.
- **You need enterprise-grade compliance documentation.** Rosie's site doesn't publish SOC 2, HIPAA, or similar certifications; healthcare or legal practices should get written confirmation directly from Rosie before signing.
- **Multilingual support beyond English/Spanish is a requirement.**
- **You want deep, named CRM integrations out of the box.** Zapier bridges a lot, but verify any specific native integration exists before buying.

## Bottom line

Rosie is a reasonably priced answer to a specific, expensive problem: small businesses losing revenue to missed phone calls. Professional is an affordable way to stop that bleeding for a low-volume operation, and Scale's direct calendar booking and warm transfers make it genuinely useful for busier, appointment-heavy businesses. It's not trying to be a full contact-center platform, and shouldn't be judged as one — the honest comparison is against a human answering service or a missed-call voicemail box. Against that bar, Rosie looks like a fair deal, provided you test it on your own real call patterns during the free trial rather than assuming it handles every edge case a trained human would.

## FAQ

**Is Rosie AI free?**
No. There's a 7-day free trial with full feature access, but after that every plan is a paid monthly (or discounted annual) subscription starting at $49/month.

**How many minutes do I get on the cheapest plan?**
The Professional plan includes 250 minutes of AI call-handling per month for $49. Going over that allotment isn't priced publicly on Rosie's site, so confirm the overage rate with their sales team before you're likely to exceed it.

**Does Rosie book appointments directly, or just take messages?**
Direct, on-call calendar booking is available starting on the Scale plan ($149/month). The Professional plan sends appointment links by text rather than booking directly during the call.

**Can Rosie transfer calls to a real person?**
Yes, on the Scale and Growth plans. Rosie can do warm transfers (briefing your team on the caller's need first) and live transfers, and Growth adds waterfall transfers across multiple numbers.

**What languages does Rosie support?**
English and Spanish, across all plans, as of this writing.

**How does Rosie handle my business's data and calls?**
Rosie records, transcribes, and summarizes calls to generate reports and notifications. It doesn't publish third-party compliance certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA) on its site, so regulated businesses should request written confirmation of data handling before signing up.

**What are the alternatives to Rosie?**
Other AI/human-hybrid answering services include Smith.ai, Ruby Receptionists, Numa, and My AI Front Desk. If your need is closer to a website chat widget than phone answering, [Tidio](/blog/tidio-review) or [Lyro AI](/blog/lyro-ai-review) are built for that and are worth comparing against Rosie's bundled free chat widget.

**Is Rosie beginner-friendly to set up?**
Rosie trains itself from your existing website and Google Business Profile with no technical setup required, though you'll still want to spend trial time refining scenarios, FAQs, and transfer rules to match how your business actually operates.

Explore more [AI & software deals](/category/software) for other AI tools covered on this site.

title: Luthor Review 2026: AI Marketing Compliance, Pricing
excerpt: Luthor review: is this AI marketing compliance platform for regulated financial firms worth a demo? Features, security, and honest pricing gaps.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Luthor Worth It for Marketing Compliance Review?

Luthor is an AI platform that scans marketing content — ads, social posts, emails, SMS, video, and websites — for regulatory and policy violations before it goes live. It's built for regulated industries like financial services, banks, and lenders, sold as an enterprise deal with no public self-serve pricing, so it's a strong fit for compliance teams drowning in manual review but a poor fit for solo marketers or small businesses on a budget.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Not published — custom enterprise quote via demo |
| **Free tier/trial** | None advertised; sales-led "Get a demo" only |
| **Best for** | Compliance and marketing teams at regulated financial firms |
| **Standout feature** | Automated policy engine covering SEC disclosures, testimonials, and PII across every content format |

### What Luthor actually is

Luthor, Inc. positions itself as an "enterprise marketing compliance platform" rather than a general writing or legal-drafting tool. Instead of generating content, it reviews content other people or tools already wrote — text, images, video, audio, SMS, social posts, and URLs — flagging language that could violate SEC rules, state advertising regulations, or a company's internal brand and disclosure policies before publication.

It sits in an odd middle ground between legal tech and martech: legal and compliance teams use it to enforce rules, but the workflow lives inside marketing's publishing pipeline. Luthor doesn't disclose which specific AI models power its detection engine, so that's worth asking directly if model transparency matters to your procurement process.

The company's published customer list leans heavily on wealth management and financial advisory firms — names like PCM Encore, Barrett Financial Group, Vertical Wealth Management, Finance Advisors, and Matson Money appear as case studies on Luthor's site. That's a useful signal: this is a tool built and proven for RIAs, broker-dealers, banks, credit unions, and lenders first, not a horizontal tool for e-commerce or SaaS marketing teams.

### Pricing: no public numbers, and that itself is a signal

Luthor does not publish pricing tiers, a free trial, or a self-serve signup anywhere on its marketing site. Every call to action reads "Get a demo." That's consistent with how most compliance software aimed at regulated financial institutions is sold — deals typically involve custom contracts scoped to content volume, number of brands/advisors covered, and which regulatory frameworks apply (SEC, FINRA, state-level rules), so a flat price sheet wouldn't mean much anyway.

| What you'd expect to negotiate | Why it varies |
|---|---|
| Per-seat or per-brand licensing | Financial advisory networks often need coverage across dozens or hundreds of individual advisor accounts |
| Content volume/API call limits | Pricing likely scales with how much content (ads, social, SMS) gets scanned per month |
| Compliance framework scope | SEC-specific rule packs cost differently than general advertising-standards coverage |
| Implementation/onboarding | Enterprise compliance tools typically bundle a setup and policy-configuration phase |

Because none of this is published, treat any pricing figure from a reseller or third-party listing with caution — get it in writing from Luthor directly. Pricing, free-tier availability, and feature scope described here reflect what was publicly verifiable as of this post's date and can change; confirm current details with Luthor before signing anything.

### Features walkthrough

**Content review across formats.** Luthor scans text, images, video, audio, SMS, social media posts, and URLs rather than being limited to plain copy — useful for compliance teams signing off on everything from a landing page to a TikTok script to a text-message campaign.

**Policy engine.** The core differentiator: a rules layer checking content against specific regulatory categories the company lists publicly — SEC violations, required disclosures, forward-looking projections, testimonials, fee disclosures, citations, and PII exposure. For a bank or RIA, this maps directly onto the violations that trigger real regulatory fines, a narrower and more defensible use case than a generic "AI compliance checker."

**Fact-checking against approved sources.** Luthor says it validates specific claims against a company's own approved knowledge base and product specs, catching cases where copy overstates a return, a rate, or a feature relative to what's actually been approved internally.

**Brand and voice alignment.** Separate from regulatory compliance, the platform also checks content against brand voice guidelines and tone matrices — a useful bundled add-on rather than the main selling point.

**Audit trail.** Every compliance decision is logged, which matters for regulated firms that need to show a regulator or auditor exactly why content was approved, flagged, or rejected — and when.

Luthor's own marketing claims 100% content coverage, a 90% reduction in manual review time, "3x faster" approvals, and a 98.4% detection rate. These are the vendor's own reported outcomes, not independently audited figures — treat them as directional and ask for a proof-of-concept on your own content before committing to a contract.

### Who it's actually for

- **Compliance officers at RIAs, broker-dealers, and wealth management firms** — the clearest fit, matching Luthor's published case studies and its SEC/FINRA-flavored policy categories.
- **Banks, credit unions, and consumer lenders** — Luthor explicitly lists these as target industries, likely because lending and deposit marketing carries its own dense disclosure requirements (APR disclosures, Reg Z, UDAAP-adjacent claims).
- **Marketing teams inside regulated companies** who need faster sign-off cycles without waiting days for a human legal review on every social post or ad variant.
- **Not a fit for** small businesses, solo marketers, or unregulated-industry content teams — there's no visible entry-level plan, and the entire product is architected around enterprise compliance workflows, not lightweight content checks.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Purpose-built policy categories (SEC, disclosures, testimonials, PII) vs. generic AI moderation | No public pricing, free tier, or trial — every evaluation starts with a sales call |
| Covers text, image, video, audio, SMS, social, and URL content in one workflow | Detection-engine model/tech stack isn't disclosed publicly |
| Built-in audit trail supports regulatory documentation requirements | Vendor-reported accuracy stats (98.4% detection, 100% coverage) aren't independently verified |
| SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and SEC 17a-4-ready infrastructure with zero-retention on submitted content | Narrow focus on regulated financial marketing is overkill for general content teams |
| Verifiable customer base in wealth management and financial advisory | No self-serve signup, so smaller teams can't just try it |

### Integrations and ecosystem

Luthor's public site doesn't list specific integrations — no Slack, Zapier, or named CMS connectors are advertised as of this writing. What is documented is its security architecture: SSO via OAuth or SAML, role-based access control with multi-factor authentication, and infrastructure described as SOC 2 Type II audited, GDPR compliant, and "SEC 17a-4 ready" for audit-log retention. Encryption is AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, with keys managed through a dedicated KMS. If your workflow depends on a specific integration, confirm it directly with Luthor's sales team during the demo.

### Where it's a strong fit

Luthor makes the most sense for compliance and marketing teams at financial services firms that currently rely on slow, manual legal review for every piece of outbound content — advisor social posts, email campaigns, website copy, SMS drips. If your firm already deals with SEC marketing-rule requirements for investment advisers and reviews hundreds of content pieces a month by hand, a tool purpose-built around those exact policy categories beats adapting a generic AI content checker.

### Where to think twice

Skip Luthor if you need a fully free or low-cost tool — there's no published free tier, and the entire go-to-market motion is enterprise sales, so budget-constrained teams and solo creators will likely find the sales process itself a mismatch. Skip it too if your content isn't in a regulated financial or lending category; the policy library is tuned for SEC/FINRA-style disclosure rules, and a generic e-commerce or SaaS marketing team won't get much value from testimonial and fee-disclosure checks that don't apply to them. And if you need independently verified accuracy numbers before signing, be aware the detection-rate and coverage figures available today are vendor-reported, not third-party audited — push for a pilot on your own content first.

### Bottom line

Luthor is a credible, narrowly-focused compliance tool for regulated financial marketing, not a general-purpose AI writing or legal assistant. Its policy categories map closely to real SEC and lending disclosure requirements, its security posture (SOC 2 Type II, zero data retention, SEC 17a-4-ready logging) is built for institutions that actually get audited, and its published customer base is entirely financial-services firms. The tradeoff is opacity everywhere else: no pricing, no trial, no disclosed model architecture, and accuracy claims that come only from Luthor itself. If you're a compliance leader at a bank, lender, or RIA buried in manual review, it's worth booking a demo and pushing for a pilot. Outside that lane, this isn't the tool for you.

### FAQ

**Is Luthor free to use?**
No. Luthor doesn't publish a free tier or self-serve trial; access starts with a "Get a demo" request and moves into a custom enterprise contract.

**How much does Luthor cost?**
Luthor doesn't publish pricing. Enterprise compliance software in this category is typically priced around content volume, number of brands or advisors covered, and which regulatory frameworks (SEC, FINRA, state rules) need to be enforced — get a written quote directly from Luthor rather than relying on third-party estimates.

**What kind of content can Luthor review?**
Text, images, video, audio, SMS, social media posts, and URLs, according to Luthor's own product pages.

**Is Luthor only for financial services companies?**
Its published policy categories (SEC violations, disclosures, testimonials, fee language) and customer case studies are all financial-services and lending focused, so that's clearly its primary market.

**How does Luthor handle data privacy?**
Luthor states it follows a zero-retention policy where submitted content isn't retained by model providers or used for training, and that its infrastructure is SOC 2 Type II audited, GDPR compliant, and built to support SEC 17a-4 audit-log retention. Confirm specifics in your contract's data-processing terms.

**Are Luthor's accuracy claims (like 98.4% detection) independently verified?**
No — those figures come from Luthor's own marketing materials, not a third-party audit. Ask for a proof-of-concept review against your own content before treating them as guaranteed performance.

**What are the alternatives to Luthor?**
Compliance review in regulated marketing is a narrow niche; alternatives are mostly in-house legal review, broader GRC platforms, or point solutions from other financial-services compliance vendors. For general AI-assisted legal work rather than marketing compliance specifically, see our [Referent review](/blog/referent-review), which covers an AI platform built for law firms.

**Does Luthor integrate with marketing tools like Slack or a CMS?**
No specific integrations are listed on Luthor's public site as of this writing; ask directly during a demo if a particular platform connection is a requirement for your team.

For more AI and software coverage, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Hexabot Review 2026: Self-Hosted AI Chatbot Pricing
excerpt: Hexabot lets you self-host an AI chatbot and workflow builder with YAML config. Here is a hands-on look at its pricing, features, and limits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Hexabot a good AI chatbot builder?

Hexabot is a self-hostable platform for building AI chatbots, agentic workflows, and business automations with YAML-based configuration and full control over the codebase. It suits developers and teams who want to own their data and infrastructure rather than rent a closed SaaS chatbot, and it charges for license activations, not message volume.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (Community, self-hosted) |
| Cheapest paid plan | $19/month (Starter) |
| Free tier | Yes — 1 user, 10 workflows, self-hosted, no license key |
| Best for | Developers and agencies wanting a self-hosted, code-owned chatbot/automation platform |
| Standout feature | YAML-based workflow definitions with schema-validated inputs/outputs, plus MCP support |

Hexabot has no matching store entry on this site yet, so there's no coupon page below — pricing and plan details come directly from Hexabot's own site and public GitHub repository.

## What Hexabot actually is

Hexabot is built by Hexastack and positions itself less as a "chatbot builder" in the Intercom/Drift sense and more as an **AI workflow automation platform** — you build agents and multi-step automations triggered by chat messages, forms, schedules, or external events, then wire in LLM calls, memory, RAG, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool connections.

The core is a Node.js application (v3 requires Node ^24.17.0) using TypeORM for data access and Zod for schema validation, managed as a Turbo/PNPM monorepo. Local development defaults to SQLite; production is expected to run on PostgreSQL. Docker is available for supporting services, though Hexabot doesn't force a particular hosting stack on you — that's the point of a self-hosted tool.

Licensing is worth flagging: Hexabot ships under the **Fair Core License (FCL-1.0-ALv2)**, a source-available license rather than a permissive OSI license like MIT or Apache 2.0. The code is inspectable and self-hostable, and Hexastack has committed to an eventual Apache 2.0 transition, but read the license terms yourself before building a commercial product on top of it.

## Pricing

| Plan | Price | Users | Workflows | Activations | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Community | Free | 1 | 10 | No license key needed | Self-hosted, aimed at students/prototypes |
| Starter | $19/month | 3 | 25 | 3 | Freelancers, indie developers |
| Pro | $59/month | 10 | 150 | 10 | Most popular; priority support, longer history retention |
| Unlimited | $149/month | 25 | Unlimited (fair use) | 25 | Agencies; dedicated success channel |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom | SLA, 24/7 support, compliance assistance |

A detail that distinguishes Hexabot from most hosted chatbot SaaS products: it doesn't bill by conversation volume, message count, or workflow executions. Quotas apply only to users, workflows, and license activations (roughly, how many separate deployments your key can run). Paid plans carry a 14-day money-back guarantee; annual invoicing is available on Unlimited and Enterprise.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability described here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — confirm current numbers on [Hexabot's pricing page](https://hexabot.ai/pricing) before committing, since AI tooling pricing shifts often.

## Core features walkthrough

**YAML-based workflow definitions with typed contracts.** Rather than a purely drag-and-drop canvas (Hexabot does support visual workflow modeling too), you can define conversation flows in YAML with schema-validated inputs, outputs, and settings — workflows live in version control and go through code review like any other infrastructure change, unlike most no-code chatbot builders.

**Multi-trigger conversation entry points.** Conversations and workflows can be kicked off not just by an incoming chat message but by form submissions, scheduled jobs, or external events — useful for automations beyond "customer types a question," like a scheduled follow-up sequence or a webhook-triggered escalation.

**Memory, RAG, and MCP support.** Hexabot lets you attach explicit memory definitions to conversations, plug in retrieval-augmented generation so responses stay grounded in your own documents, and connect to external tools via the Model Context Protocol — the same interoperability standard increasingly used to connect LLMs to tools and data across the industry.

**Human review points and conditional logic.** Workflows can include explicit checkpoints where a human approves an action before it proceeds, plus branching conditional logic — relevant for automations touching money, customer data, or anything you don't want a model acting on unsupervised.

**Reusable capability bindings.** Actions and their underlying integrations are kept separate from the task logic that uses them, so a single integration (an LLM connection, a CRM lookup, etc.) can be reused across multiple workflows without duplicating configuration.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo developers and freelancers** building a chatbot for a client can start on the free Community tier to prototype, then move to Starter ($19/month) once they need more than one user or 10 workflows.
- **Small agencies and dev shops** running builds for multiple clients will likely land on Pro ($59/month) or Unlimited ($149/month), where activation counts stop being a constant concern and priority support kicks in.
- **Regulated or compliance-sensitive organizations** (healthcare, finance, government-adjacent) that can't send customer data to a third-party SaaS vendor are a strong match — you own the infrastructure, so data residency and access control stay entirely in your hands. Enterprise adds SLA and compliance assistance.
- **Non-technical teams** wanting a point-and-click chatbot with zero DevOps involvement are probably not the target audience — Hexabot expects you to run a Node.js/PostgreSQL stack, a very different commitment than signing up for hosted SaaS.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Self-hosted — full control over data, infrastructure, and customization | Requires real DevOps capability (Node.js, PostgreSQL, optional Docker) to run well |
| Pricing based on users/workflows/activations, not message volume | Source-available (Fair Core License), not a fully permissive open-source license from day one |
| YAML-based workflows are version-controllable and code-review-friendly | No drag-and-drop-only path for fully non-technical users who don't want to touch config |
| MCP and RAG support built in for grounding responses in your own data | Specific third-party channel integrations (WhatsApp, Slack, etc.) aren't clearly documented on the public site/README |
| Free Community tier has no license key requirement, good for real prototyping | 14-day money-back guarantee is short compared to some competitors' 30-day windows |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Hexabot's site describes "multi-channel" deployment across web, messaging, and social channels, and the platform is built for MCP-based tool interoperability, letting it call out to external tools and context providers in a standardized way. That said, the public documentation and README don't spell out an exhaustive list of named channel integrations — teams evaluating Hexabot for a specific channel (WhatsApp Business API, Microsoft Teams) should confirm current coverage directly with Hexastack rather than assuming parity with closed SaaS vendors that publish long integration marketplaces.

There's no public app marketplace or Zapier-style connector library, which tracks with Hexabot's positioning as infrastructure-level, code-first software rather than plug-and-play SaaS with dozens of one-click integrations.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You want a chatbot/automation platform you can audit, modify, and self-host rather than trust to a vendor's servers.
- Your team is comfortable running (or paying for help running) a Node.js/PostgreSQL stack.
- You need workflows defined as code — in YAML, under version control — rather than trapped in a proprietary visual builder.
- You're mixing chat-triggered and non-chat-triggered logic (scheduled jobs, webhook events) in one system.
- Cost predictability matters more than message-volume flexibility, since pricing doesn't scale with conversation count.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a fully permissive open-source license** for a commercial derivative product, the Fair Core License's terms may not fit — read them before assuming MIT/Apache-style freedom.
- **If your team has zero backend/DevOps capacity**, self-hosting Node.js and PostgreSQL is real ongoing overhead a fully hosted SaaS chatbot avoids entirely.
- **If you need a specific, well-documented pre-built channel integration today**, verify it's actually supported before committing — the public documentation doesn't itemize every channel connector.
- **If you want guaranteed SLA and 24/7 support without a custom quote**, that only exists on Enterprise; self-serve tiers don't include SLA guarantees.
- **If you're a non-technical solo founder** who just wants a website widget live in ten minutes with no config file in sight, a fully hosted, no-code chatbot SaaS will get you there faster.

## Bottom line

Hexabot is a genuinely different kind of chatbot product: infrastructure you run yourself, priced by seats and workflow count rather than message volume, with workflows defined in YAML rather than locked inside a closed visual builder. That's a real advantage for developers, agencies, and compliance-conscious teams who want to own their stack — and a drawback for anyone hoping to avoid touching a terminal. If you have the technical capacity to self-host and value data ownership over turnkey convenience, Hexabot is worth evaluating seriously. If you just want a chatbot widget live today with no DevOps involved, look at a hosted SaaS alternative instead.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Hexabot free to use?**
Yes — the Community tier is free, self-hosted, and requires no license key, though it's capped at 1 user and 10 workflows: fine for prototyping, tight for production.

**How does Hexabot pricing work?**
Paid plans ($19 Starter, $59 Pro, $149 Unlimited monthly, plus custom Enterprise) are based on users, workflows, and license activations — not message volume, which is unusual for chatbot platforms.

**Do I need to self-host Hexabot, or is there a managed cloud option?**
Community and paid license tiers are described as self-hosted deployments; Enterprise customers get dedicated support that may include deployment help, but confirm current managed-hosting options directly with Hexastack, since it isn't spelled out in detail on the public pricing page.

**What license does Hexabot use, and is it truly open source?**
It's released under the Fair Core License (FCL-1.0-ALv2), a source-available license — inspectable and self-hostable, with a planned future transition to Apache 2.0, but not fully permissive open source from the outset. Check the license text before building a derivative product.

**What can Hexabot connect to?**
It supports MCP-based tool and context connections, plus multi-channel deployment across web, messaging, and social channels. Specific named third-party integrations aren't exhaustively documented publicly, so verify support for the exact channel you need first.

**Is Hexabot beginner-friendly for non-developers?**
Not particularly. It supports visual workflow modeling, but assumes comfort with self-hosting a Node.js/PostgreSQL app, and its YAML-based configuration favors developers over non-technical users.

**What are the main alternatives to Hexabot?**
Hosted, no-code chatbot builders like Tidio's Lyro AI or Droxy AI trade self-hosting control for zero-DevOps convenience and message-based pricing. Read our [Lyro AI review](/blog/lyro-ai-review) or [Droxy AI review](/blog/droxy-ai-review) for that comparison point.

**Does Hexabot offer a money-back guarantee?**
Yes, paid plans other than Enterprise come with a 14-day money-back guarantee, and annual invoicing is available on Unlimited and Enterprise.
