title: Undetectable AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features, Ethics
excerpt: Does Undetectable AI really beat GPTZero and Turnitin? An honest look at pricing, features, and the disclosure risks involved.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Does Undetectable AI actually get past GPTZero, Turnitin, and Originality AI?

Undetectable AI is a paraphrasing tool that rewrites AI-generated text so it scores as human-written on detectors like GPTZero, Turnitin, Originality.ai, and Copyleaks. It works reasonably well against most consumer-grade detectors in the short term, but detection and evasion are locked in an arms race, and using it to disguise AI writing where disclosure is required is a policy violation, not a gray area.

### At a glance

| | Undetectable AI |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $9.99/month (Starter, monthly billing); from $5/month billed yearly |
| Free tier/trial | Very limited — about 250 words to test, then a paid plan is required for further use |
| Best for | Rewriting AI-assisted drafts to sound more natural, or checking how "AI-flaggable" a draft reads before submitting it somewhere disclosure is optional |
| Standout feature | Built-in AI detector that highlights the specific sentences most likely to get flagged, before you rewrite anything |

## What Undetectable AI actually is

Undetectable AI is a web-based platform, not a browser extension or desktop app, that pairs two functions: an **AI detector** that scores text and flags which sentences read as machine-generated, and a **humanizer** that rewrites those sentences to reduce that score. The company doesn't publish a paper on its rewriting model's architecture — like most tools in this space, the exact method is a trade secret, partly because publishing it would make it easier for detector vendors to patch around. What the site does disclose is that it works by varying sentence structure, swapping vocabulary, and adjusting tone and rhythm to shift the text's statistical fingerprint away from patterns detectors associate with GPT-family, Claude, Gemini, and other model output.

The tool supports more than 50 languages, though the company notes English gets the most reliable results — a common caveat across detector and de-detector tools alike, since both directions of this technology train overwhelmingly on English text.

It's marketed broadly to students, content writers, marketers, and businesses producing AI-assisted copy at volume, and the company has publicized a user base in the tens of millions — a figure that comes from the company itself and isn't independently auditable, though plausible given the tool's visibility in searches for "bypass AI detector."

## Pricing

Undetectable AI runs on a monthly word-quota model, and yearly billing roughly halves the effective monthly price across every tier.

Pricing and word limits below were accurate as of this post's date (September 2026) and can change quickly — detector-evasion tools iterate pricing often as detector vendors adjust their own models.

| Plan | Monthly price | Yearly (per month) | Words/month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free trial | $0 | — | ~250 words |
| Starter | $9.99 | $5.00 ($60/yr) | 10,000 |
| Professional | $19.00 | $9.50 ($114/yr) | 20,000 |
| Advanced | $31.00 | $15.75 ($189/yr) | 35,000 |
| Premium | $42.50 | — | 50,000 (expandable to 380,000) |
| Business | Custom | Custom | Non-expiring credits, white-label, priority support |

Every individual plan gets the same feature set — the only differentiator is monthly word quota. That ceiling matters in practice: detection and rewrite passes draw from the same quota, so heavy back-and-forth editing burns through an allotment faster than a single pass would suggest.

## Core features walkthrough

**AI detector with sentence-level highlighting.** Rather than a single pass/fail score, the tool marks up a document sentence by sentence, showing which lines are most likely to trip a detector — more useful than a blunt percentage score because it lets you target the rewrite instead of resubmitting the whole document.

**Humanizer with adjustable aggressiveness.** Settings control how heavily the engine alters source text — lighter passes preserve more of the original phrasing and meaning; heavier passes rewrite more freely and drift further from the original.

**Writing-level and tone matching.** The tool markets matching a target reading/writing level, aimed at making output sound consistent with a given writer's typical style rather than uniformly "smoothed."

**Browser extension and API access.** A Chrome extension runs detection and rewriting without leaving the page you're working in; API access on paid plans lets teams build the rewrite step into their own content pipeline.

**Bundled adjacent tools.** The platform also includes an AI image detector, a plagiarism checker, and a general paraphrasing/SEO-writing tool — though the humanizer is clearly what the product is built and marketed around.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo users testing a single draft** fit the Starter plan or free trial, since 10,000 words/month covers a few essays or articles without paying for unused capacity.
- **Agencies producing AI-assisted copy at volume** likely need Professional or Advanced, since detection and rewrite passes on longer pieces add up fast against a monthly cap.
- **Businesses with an existing content pipeline** are the intended audience for the API and Business tier's non-expiring credits and white-labeling.
- **Students** are a named audience in the company's marketing, but this is the use case where the ethical stakes are highest — see below.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Combines a detector and a rewriter in one tool, so you can target specific flagged sentences | Free trial is very small (~250 words), not enough to test on a real assignment or article |
| Same full feature set across every paid tier — no artificial feature-gating | Heavier rewrite settings can noticeably change meaning, tone, or factual nuance |
| Supports 50+ languages | Company acknowledges English gets the most reliable results, so non-English output quality is less certain |
| API and browser extension for workflow integration | No independent, ongoing audit of bypass rates against specific detector versions |
| Word-based quota scales with plan, with expandable capacity on the top tier | Detector vendors update their models regularly, so results that pass today aren't guaranteed to pass after a detector update |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Undetectable AI offers a documented API for developers who want to call the detector and humanizer programmatically, plus a Chrome extension for in-browser use. It doesn't publish native Zapier, Slack, or Google Docs integrations, so anything beyond the API or extension means manual copy-paste or custom glue code.

## Where it's a strong fit

- Writers and marketers who use an LLM for a first draft, substantially edit it themselves, and want a final pass that smooths over the stiffer, repetitive phrasing that makes AI-assisted writing read a little flat.
- Teams that already disclose AI involvement in their content process but want output that reads more naturally, independent of any detector concerns.
- Developers who want an automated "does this read like AI, and can we soften it" check inside a larger publishing pipeline via the API.

## Where to think twice

- **If you're bound by an academic integrity policy, employer disclosure rule, or platform authenticity terms**, using this to get flagged AI writing past a required check is a policy violation, full stop — getting caught later carries consequences it can't protect you from.
- **If you need guaranteed, permanent evasion**, there isn't one — detector vendors retrain against known humanizer output.
- **If accuracy matters more than tone**, aggressive rewriting can subtly change claims or drop qualifying language.
- **If you need a free tool**, the ~250-word trial won't get you through a real assignment.
- **If your organization needs SOC 2 or a documented compliance trail**, that documentation isn't published, so this isn't built for regulated environments.

## Ethical and practical considerations

This section carries more weight here than in most tool reviews, because bypassing AI detection is the product, not a side effect of it.

- **It changes what a detector reports, not what actually happened.** Rewriting AI output so it scores as human doesn't make the underlying research or argument more accurate or original — it removes the signal a detector uses to flag machine authorship. A hallucinated fact in the original draft survives the rewrite exactly as wrong, just harder to trace.

- **The most direct use case is misrepresentation.** A student submitting AI-written work as their own against an honor code, a freelancer claiming fully original writing to a client paying for human work, or a journalist passing off AI-drafted copy as personally written — these dishonesty problems existed before this tool, and its whole function is removing the one signal that might catch them.

- **Platform and contract terms increasingly require disclosure.** Publishers, marketplaces, and employers with explicit AI-use clauses treat evading a check meant to enforce one as a breach of the agreement, independent of the content's quality.

- **The legitimate use case is real but narrower than the marketing suggests.** Someone who drafted with an LLM, substantially edited it, and takes ownership of the final piece running a pass to smooth stiff phrasing is materially different from handing in a finished AI submission as unaided work. The tool can't tell which situation you're in — only you can, and only you're accountable for it.

- **This is an arms race with no permanent winner.** Detector vendors retrain on known humanizer output, and humanizer vendors adjust in response. Treat any "beats GPTZero" claim, including the vendor's own, as a snapshot in time, not a permanent guarantee.

## Bottom line

Undetectable AI does what it says: it rewrites AI-flagged text into something that reads more naturally and scores lower on major detectors, and its paired detector-plus-humanizer workflow beats rewrite tools that skip straight to rewriting without showing what's actually triggering a flag. It's not free, its trial is too small to evaluate on a real document, and its bypass results are inherently temporary given how often detector vendors update their models. Whether it's right for you depends less on whether it works and more on what you're using it for — smoothing a draft you're allowed to submit is defensible; dodging a disclosure requirement isn't, regardless of how well the rewrite reads.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Undetectable AI actually beat Turnitin and GPTZero?** It's built to reduce scores on major detectors including Turnitin, GPTZero, Originality.ai, and Copyleaks, and generally succeeds against consumer-grade checks at any given moment. But detector vendors update models regularly and there's no independent benchmark confirming a fixed bypass rate — treat any specific claim, including the vendor's own, as a snapshot rather than a guarantee.

**Is there a free version?** A free trial capped at roughly 250 words — enough to test the interface, not to rewrite a real essay. Continued use requires a paid plan starting at $9.99/month (about $5/month billed yearly).

**Will rewriting change the meaning of my text?** It can, especially at more aggressive settings, which trade fidelity to the original meaning for a lower detection score. Lighter settings are safer for accuracy-sensitive text.

**Is using this to submit AI-written schoolwork as my own considered cheating?** If your school's policy requires disclosed or unaided human work and you use this to bypass a check enforcing that, yes — that's a violation regardless of the writing quality that results. See "Ethical and practical considerations" above.

**How does it handle my data and privacy?** The company doesn't publish detailed third-party certifications like SOC 2, so confirm current data-retention and privacy practices on the official site before uploading sensitive documents.

**Does it work in languages other than English?** It claims 50+ languages, but the company states English gets the most reliable results, so treat non-English output as less certain.

**What's the difference between the pricing tiers?** All paid tiers share the same features — the difference is monthly word quota, from 10,000 on Starter to 50,000 (expandable to 380,000) on Premium, plus custom non-expiring credits on Business.

**Are there alternatives?** Yes — a competitive category with tools like Un AI My Text, AI Image Humanizer (for images), and various paraphrasing tools. If your priority is disclosure-compliant editing rather than evasion, a standard style editor without a "bypass AI detection" framing may be a better, less fraught fit.

For deals on AI writing and detection tools, see the [AI & software deals](/category/software) category page.

title: Lutra AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Lutra AI automates data extraction, CRM enrichment and outreach by running real code. Here's what it costs, does well, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Lutra AI worth using for workflow automation?

Lutra AI is an agent-style automation tool that writes and runs real code to pull data from sites and PDFs, enrich CRM records, and send outreach emails, instead of just chatting about the task. It suits sales, marketing, and ops teams doing repetitive data work, though its credit-based pricing isn't published with fixed dollar figures, so budget-conscious users should confirm costs before committing.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free tier available; paid plans are credit-based (exact monthly prices not published — confirm on site) |
| Free tier/trial | Yes, a free tier with a limited monthly credit allowance |
| Best for | Sales, marketing, finance and ops teams automating data extraction, enrichment and outreach |
| Standout feature | "Playbooks" — reusable, schedulable automations that execute real code rather than just generating text |

Lutra AI doesn't have a matching store entry on this site yet, so there's no coupon page to link below. Everything here comes from Lutra's own site, its public help center, and cross-checking both against each other.

## What Lutra AI actually is

Lutra AI is built by Lutra AI, Inc., and positions itself less as a chatbot and more as a task-executing agent. When you ask it to do something — say, "pull every contact from this list of company websites and add them to my CRM" — it doesn't just describe the steps or generate a one-off text response. It writes and runs actual code against your connected apps, which the company argues cuts down on the hallucinated or half-finished output you get from a pure chat interface.

Lutra doesn't commit to a single underlying model on its marketing pages; it describes itself as an orchestration layer that calls AI functions for text generation, document classification, and data extraction, alongside deterministic code execution for parts of a workflow that don't need a model at all (reading a spreadsheet, calling an API, writing to Slack). That split — AI where it helps, code where it's more reliable — is the main technical differentiator from tools that route everything through a single model call.

It connects to Google Workspace (Gmail, Sheets, Docs), Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive), Slack, GitHub, HubSpot, Airtable, LinkedIn, and Supabase, with custom integrations via REST APIs, OpenAPI specs, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

## Pricing

Lutra uses what it calls a hybrid model: a flat monthly subscription for platform access and core features, plus usage-based credits for AI-intensive actions on top. Per Lutra's help documentation, credits are consumed by things like web search (3 credits), website retrieval (roughly 1 credit per page), and person or company profile lookups (3 credits each), while basic read/write actions inside connected apps — writing to a Slack channel, updating a Google Sheet — don't cost credits at all. AI functions like text generation and document analysis carry variable costs based on input size and complexity.

The catch for anyone budgeting in advance: Lutra's pricing page renders its plan table dynamically and doesn't expose fixed dollar amounts for the Free, Professional, and Custom tiers, and its help center says allowances vary "by plan" without listing numbers. That's unusual — most competitors publish at least a starting price — so treat any specific dollar figure quoted elsewhere online as unverified until you check the live pricing page yourself.

| Plan | What's included | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Platform access, limited monthly credits | Good for testing Playbooks before paying |
| Professional | Higher credit allowance, plus discounted credits on demand | For individuals and small teams |
| Custom | Negotiated allowance and credit discounts, team/enterprise features | Requires talking to sales |

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly for AI tools — always confirm current numbers on [Lutra's official pricing page](https://www.lutra.ai/pricing) before subscribing.

## Core features walkthrough

**Playbooks.** Lutra's name for a saved, repeatable workflow. Once you've built and tested a task — say, a weekly competitor-pricing scrape into a Sheet — save it as a Playbook, schedule it to run automatically, and share it with teammates instead of rebuilding the automation from scratch. This is what turns Lutra from a one-off task runner into a lightweight internal automation platform.

**Data extraction from websites and PDFs.** Point Lutra at a list of URLs or uploaded documents and ask it to pull structured fields — names, prices, contract terms, whatever you define — into a spreadsheet or database. Because it executes code rather than just summarizing text, it handles larger batches more consistently than asking a chatbot to paste in page after page.

**Contact and company enrichment.** Person and company profile lookups are built in as first-class actions (each costs credits), letting sales and ops teams fill in missing CRM fields — job titles, company size, LinkedIn profiles — without searching each contact manually.

**Email automation at scale.** Lutra can draft and send personalized outreach based on enriched data, aimed at sales and growth teams doing list-based outreach rather than one-off email drafting.

**MCP and API extensibility.** Beyond built-in connectors, Lutra supports the Model Context Protocol plus REST/OpenAPI integrations, so technical teams can wire in internal tools or newer MCP-compatible services without waiting for an official connector.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo operators and freelancers** doing repetitive research can start free and test whether the credit system fits their workload before paying.
- **Sales and RevOps teams** get the most obvious value — contact enrichment, CRM updates, and personalized outreach are exactly what Playbooks are built for.
- **Marketing teams** can use it for scraping competitor data or automating recurring reports into Sheets or Docs.
- **Engineering-adjacent ops teams** wanting more than the built-in connectors can lean on MCP and API access.
- **Enterprises with compliance needs** get some reassurance from SOC 2 certification, though HIPAA or on-prem hosting should be verified directly with sales.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Executes real code instead of only generating text, reducing hallucinated "task completion" | No published fixed dollar amounts, making cost comparison harder upfront |
| Playbooks make recurring workflows reusable and shareable across a team | Credit-based pricing on top of a subscription adds complexity vs. flat-fee competitors |
| Broad integration list (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, HubSpot, Airtable, GitHub) plus MCP/API | No single named underlying model, so language-task output is harder to benchmark |
| SOC 2 certified with OAuth-based app connections | Value is concentrated in sales/ops use cases, less compelling as a general chat assistant |
| Free tier lets you test before paying | Smaller, newer company than Zapier, so third-party reviews are thinner |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Lutra's built-in connector list covers the tools most sales and ops teams use day to day: Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Outlook, OneDrive, Slack, GitHub, HubSpot, Airtable, LinkedIn, and Supabase. For anything outside that list, it supports MCP — an increasingly standard way for AI agents to talk to arbitrary tools — plus general REST and OpenAPI-based custom integrations. There's no public app marketplace or Zapier-style catalog of thousands of pre-built connectors here — if you need extremely long-tail app support out of the box, [Zapier](/blog/zapier-review) may still cover more ground natively, even though its AI agent features work differently from Lutra's code-executing approach.

## Where it's a strong fit

Lutra is a strong fit if your team spends real hours each week on manual data collection, contact enrichment, or outreach personalization, and you'd rather hand that off to a workflow that runs and re-runs itself than re-prompt a chatbot every time. The Playbook model rewards teams with a handful of recurring, well-defined tasks — pulling competitor prices weekly, enriching new leads daily — rather than one-off requests. Because it executes code, it also handles larger, structured batches (hundreds of URLs or PDFs) more reliably than a chat tool asked to process the same volume by pasting text back and forth.

## Where to think twice

Skip Lutra, or at least test thoroughly on the free tier first, if any of the following apply to you:

- **You need to know your exact monthly cost before signing up.** The credit system layered on a subscription makes budgeting harder than with flat-fee tools.
- **You want a fully free, ongoing tool.** The free tier is designed for evaluation and light use, not indefinite production workflows.
- **You need heavy enterprise compliance guarantees (HIPAA, on-prem/self-hosted deployment).** SOC 2 is confirmed, but anything beyond that should be verified directly with Lutra.
- **Your main need is a general-purpose writing or chat assistant.** Lutra is built for structured, repeatable tasks, not open-ended conversation — [ChatGPT](/blog/chatgpt-review) or [Claude AI](/blog/claude-ai-review) fit that better.
- **You need an enormous pre-built connector catalog.** A broader automation platform may already cover more niche SaaS tools natively.

## Bottom line

Lutra AI earns its keep as an automation agent for teams with concrete, repeatable data tasks — lead enrichment, outreach personalization, structured extraction from messy sources — where "run this reliably every week" matters more than "have a conversation." The code-execution approach is a genuinely different angle from agent tools that just chain prompts together, and the integration list covers what most revenue and ops teams already rely on. The friction point is pricing transparency: it's hard to know what you'll pay monthly until you dig into the app and your own usage, and that's worth weighing against more clearly priced alternatives before committing a team to it.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Lutra AI free to use?**
Lutra offers a free tier with a limited monthly credit allowance — enough to test Playbooks and integrations, but production use will likely need a paid plan once you exceed those credits.

**How much does Lutra AI cost per month?**
Lutra uses a flat subscription plus usage-based credits rather than one flat price, and its pricing page doesn't display fixed dollar figures for its Professional or Custom tiers — check [Lutra's pricing page](https://www.lutra.ai/pricing) directly for current numbers.

**What counts as a "credit" in Lutra?**
Credits are spent on AI-intensive actions like web search, website retrieval, and person/company profile lookups, while basic read/write actions inside connected apps (like writing to Slack) don't consume credits.

**Does Lutra AI use my data to train its models?**
Lutra states it's SOC 2 certified and uses OAuth authentication for connecting to your apps, but data-training and retention policies should be confirmed in its own privacy policy rather than assumed from marketing copy.

**Is Lutra AI good for beginners with no coding background?**
Yes — non-technical users can describe a task in plain language and let Lutra generate and run the underlying code, though power users can go further with MCP and API access.

**How is Lutra different from Zapier or Make?**
Zapier and Make are trigger-and-action builders connecting apps through pre-built steps; Lutra leans more on AI to interpret an instruction and write the connecting logic itself. See our [Zapier review](/blog/zapier-review) for more on that comparison.

**What are the best alternatives to Lutra AI?**
Zapier and Make for classic app-to-app automation, or Claude AI and ChatGPT if you want a more general-purpose assistant that also handles structured tasks.

**Does Lutra AI have an API?**
Yes — beyond built-in connectors, Lutra supports REST APIs, OpenAPI specs, and MCP for custom integrations.

title: Prompt Mixer Review 2026: Free Open-Source Prompt IDE
excerpt: Prompt Mixer is a free, open-source desktop app for chaining and comparing AI prompts across 20+ LLM providers. Here's the full review.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Prompt Mixer worth using in 2026?

Yes, if you want a free, open-source desktop workspace for building and comparing prompts across multiple LLM providers without a subscription. Prompt Mixer trades polished onboarding for full data ownership and zero cost — a good fit for developers and teams comfortable installing a desktop app and wiring up their own API keys.

**At a glance**

| | Prompt Mixer |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (MIT-licensed, open source) |
| Free tier | Yes — the entire app is free; no paid tier exists |
| Best for | Developers and prompt engineers comparing models/chains before shipping |
| Standout feature | Side-by-side multi-model testing with an open connector system for 20+ LLM providers |

Prompt Mixer is a desktop application, built by a small team publishing under the PromptMixerDev organization on GitHub, for testing, chaining, and managing AI prompts before they go into production. Unlike most tools here, it isn't a hosted SaaS product with a login wall — it's an open-source desktop app you download and run locally, and every "connector" that talks to an LLM provider is its own small, inspectable code module rather than a black box.

The project describes itself as a place where "managers, engineers, and data experts" can jointly develop AI features — prompt chaining, workflow building, version tracking, and cross-model testing, all inside one local app. It isn't tied to a single model family; it ships with (or supports adding) connectors for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Cohere, Perplexity, Groq, DeepInfra, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Aleph Alpha, AI21, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and Stable Diffusion — plus function-calling connectors that hook OpenAI models up to SQL, MongoDB, SERP APIs, and web search via LangChain.

## Pricing: there isn't any

This is what differentiates Prompt Mixer from almost everything else covered on this site: no pricing page, no tiered plans, no paywalled feature. The desktop app (Prompt Mixer CE, "Community Edition") is MIT-licensed and free to download for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows, and Linux. The project accepts optional Stripe-based donations, but that's separate from using the app — nothing is gated behind it.

The catch: Prompt Mixer doesn't include API access to any model provider. You bring your own keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or whichever connector you install, and pay those providers directly at their metered rates. Prompt Mixer's own cost is $0; your actual LLM usage cost depends on which models you call and how much you test.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt Mixer CE (desktop app) | Free | Full app: chaining, workflows, version history, multi-model testing, connectors |
| LLM provider usage | Pay-as-you-go | You supply your own API keys; billed by that provider, not Prompt Mixer |
| Optional sponsorship | Whatever you choose | Stripe donation link on GitHub; supports development, doesn't unlock features |

Pricing and connector coverage were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly for an actively developed open-source project — check the [Prompt Mixer GitHub repository](https://github.com/PromptMixerDev/prompt-mixer-app-ce) and [official docs](https://docs.promptmixer.dev/) before building a workflow around a specific connector.

## Features walkthrough

**Prompt chaining.** You can construct sequences of prompts that pass context and outputs forward, so a later step in a chain can reference what an earlier step produced. This is the core mechanic that separates Prompt Mixer from a plain "type a prompt, get a response" playground — it's built for multi-step logic, not one-shot testing.

**Workflows.** A form-based interface lets you assemble multi-step prompt workflows without hand-writing orchestration code for every experiment, aimed at people who want to iterate on prompt logic visually before formalizing it into an application.

**Side-by-side model comparison.** Because connectors are modular, you can run the same prompt against multiple providers in one session and compare outputs directly — useful for deciding whether a task needs a frontier model or whether a cheaper one performs close enough for production.

**Connector extensibility.** Anyone can write a new connector (the repo includes a sample-connector template) to wire in a custom model, internal API, or specialized tool. Several existing connectors go beyond plain chat completions — function-calling connectors let OpenAI models query a SQL database, hit a SERP API, or run a MongoDB query mid-prompt, plus LangChain-based connectors for web search.

**Version tracking.** Prompt and workflow changes are tracked so you can experiment freely and roll back if a change makes outputs worse — useful once a prompt has gone through a dozen edits and you've lost track of which version worked best.

## Who it's actually for

**Solo developers and prompt engineers** get the most direct value: a local, free environment to iterate on prompts and compare model outputs before wiring them into an app, with no subscription to justify and no lock-in on which model you ship with.

**Small technical teams** can use the collaboration framing (shared prompt libraries, version history) if everyone is comfortable running a desktop app locally and doesn't need real-time cloud collaboration — "collaboration" here means sharing files or a synced repo, not simultaneous multi-user editing in one session.

**Non-technical marketers or writers** looking for a simple prompt-generation tool are not the target audience. Installing connectors and managing API keys assumes a comfort with APIs that a general business user typically won't have out of the box.

**Enterprises needing formal compliance guarantees** (SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, a support contract) won't find any of that here — it's a community-maintained open-source project, not an enterprise vendor with a sales and compliance team.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Completely free and open source (MIT license) | No hosted/cloud version — desktop-only, local setup required |
| Wide connector ecosystem: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Bedrock, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, more | You manage your own API keys and pay providers directly |
| Full prompt-chaining and workflow support, not just single-turn testing | No official enterprise support tier, SLA, or certifications |
| Inspectable code — audit exactly what a connector sends/receives | Smaller community, slower cadence than funded SaaS competitors |
| Works with local models via Ollama, useful for privacy-sensitive testing | UI and docs less polished than paid competitors |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Prompt Mixer's "integration" model is its connector system rather than a traditional app marketplace. The GitHub organization hosts dozens of connector repos, covering major hosted LLM APIs, local inference via Ollama, image generation via Stable Diffusion and DALL-E, and function-calling connectors that give OpenAI models access to SQL databases, MongoDB, SERP APIs, GitHub, and LangChain-powered web search.

There's also a separate `mix-tools-sdk` Python package pointing to `mix.tools`, suggesting the team is building adjacent tooling — worth checking directly if you need a programmatic API rather than the desktop GUI, since that project sits outside the core app and isn't documented in the same place.

Because every connector is open source, you can also write your own using the published sample-connector template if you need to hit an internal or unlisted API nobody has built a connector for yet.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You want to A/B test prompts across several LLM providers without paying for another SaaS subscription on top of your model API bills.
- You're building an AI feature and need a fast way to iterate on multi-step prompt chains before hardcoding them into your app.
- You value reading the actual code that talks to each model provider, rather than trusting a closed-source vendor's claims about what data it sends where.
- You already run Ollama locally and want to test prompts against local models alongside hosted ones in the same interface.

## Where to think twice

- If you need a browser-based tool with zero installation — Prompt Mixer is a native desktop download, a worse fit if your team is fully cloud-based or locked to managed devices where installing software is restricted.
- If you need enterprise guarantees like SSO, audit logging, or a signed SOC 2 report — none of that exists here; this is a community project, not a vendor with a compliance program.
- If you want model access bundled into the price — you still pay your own OpenAI/Anthropic/Google API bills, so it isn't a "free unlimited AI" tool the way some all-in-one apps market themselves.
- If you want a large, fast-shipping community — development continues (commits as recent as late 2025) but at the pace of a small open-source team, not a funded company.
- If real-time, in-browser multi-user collaboration on the same session matters — Prompt Mixer's collaboration story is version tracking and shared files, not simultaneous cloud editing.

## The bottom line

Prompt Mixer earns its place by doing one thing honestly: it's a genuinely free, open-source, multi-model prompt-testing desktop app with a real connector ecosystem, not a freemium funnel dressed up as one. If you're a developer who wants to compare GPT, Claude, Gemini, and a local Ollama model side by side, chain prompts together, and keep full control of your API keys and code path, it's a low-risk download — the worst case is you uninstall it and you're out nothing but setup time. It's a poor fit if you need turnkey cloud collaboration, enterprise compliance, or bundled model access without an API key. For technical users, it fills a gap that paid "prompt management" SaaS products often charge $20–$100+/month for.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Prompt Mixer really free, with no hidden paid tier?**
Yes. Prompt Mixer CE is released under the MIT license and is free to download and use on macOS, Windows, and Linux. There's an optional Stripe sponsorship link for anyone who wants to support development, but it doesn't unlock any feature.

**Do I need my own API keys to use it?**
Yes. Prompt Mixer doesn't bundle or resell access to any LLM provider. You add your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or other provider API key inside the app, and usage is billed by that provider at its normal rates.

**What models and providers does Prompt Mixer support?**
Through its connector system it supports OpenAI (including DALL-E), Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Cohere, Perplexity, Groq, DeepInfra, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Aleph Alpha, AI21, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and Stable Diffusion, plus function-calling and LangChain-based connectors. Since connectors are community-maintained, confirm current status on the [PromptMixerDev GitHub organization](https://github.com/PromptMixerDev) first.

**Is Prompt Mixer good for beginners with no coding background?**
Not especially. Installing the app is simple, but getting real value means understanding API keys and provider settings — non-technical users looking for a simple prompt-writing helper will likely find a hosted, no-setup tool easier.

**How does Prompt Mixer handle my data and API keys?**
Because it's a local, open-source desktop app, your prompts and keys stay on your machine and go directly to whichever provider you've connected — there's no Prompt Mixer server in the middle. Review the source on GitHub if you need to verify this for a security review, since there's no formal third-party audit published.

**Is Prompt Mixer actively maintained?**
The GitHub organization has had commits as recently as late 2025 across its main app and connector repos, so it's active but run at the pace of a small open-source team.

**What are the main alternatives to Prompt Mixer?**
For general-purpose AI assistants rather than a prompt-testing IDE, see our [ChatGPT review](/blog/chatgpt-review), [Claude AI review](/blog/claude-ai-review), and [Google Gemini review](/blog/google-gemini-review) — Prompt Mixer can actually compare all three side by side. Developers may also want our [Cursor AI review](/blog/cursor-ai-review) or [GitHub Copilot review](/blog/github-copilot-review).

**Does Prompt Mixer offer a cloud or team plan?**
Not as a formal product. Collaboration is built around shared prompt files, version history, and connectors rather than a hosted multi-user cloud workspace — check the [official docs](https://docs.promptmixer.dev/) directly if this changes.

For more AI and software tool coverage, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Luma AI by Serviceaide Review 2026: Pricing & Features
excerpt: Luma AI is Serviceaide's agentic IT service-desk assistant. Here's a look at its real pricing, features, integrations, and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Luma AI by Serviceaide a good IT service desk assistant?

Luma AI is Serviceaide's agentic AI engine for IT and enterprise service desks, built to deflect tickets, answer employee questions, and automate routing and knowledge-base upkeep inside Serviceaide's own ITSM platform. It's a solid fit for mid-size-to-large IT and shared-services teams already using or considering Serviceaide's ChangeGear/ESM suite, but not a self-serve tool you can sign up for and try in an afternoon.

Note: this review covers **Luma AI by Serviceaide**, the IT-service-desk virtual agent — not the unrelated video-generation company "Luma AI" (Luma Labs).

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Not published — sold as part of Serviceaide's platform (contact sales) |
| Free tier/trial | No public free tier; demos/consultations only |
| Best for | Enterprise IT and shared-services teams already on or evaluating Serviceaide's ESM/ChangeGear platform |
| Standout feature | Agentic ticket deflection paired with knowledge-base cleanup (dedup, gap detection) built into the same workflow |

Luma AI has no matching store entry on this site, so there's no coupon page below. Pricing, feature, and integration claims come from Serviceaide's own public pages as of this post's date and should be confirmed directly with Serviceaide, since enterprise vendors often gate specifics behind a sales call.

## What Luma AI actually is

Serviceaide is an enterprise digital service management vendor whose flagship products are ChangeGear (ITSM), DSM (Digital Service Management), and AISM (AI-driven service integration for managed service providers). Luma AI sits across all of them as Serviceaide's "agentic AI engine for service automation and user support" — a virtual employee living inside the ticketing and knowledge layer rather than a standalone chatbot bolted onto a website.

Serviceaide states that Luma AI's virtual agent is built on OpenAI/ChatGPT-family models, layered with the company's own retrieval and workflow logic rather than a purely off-the-shelf wrapper. That's a meaningful distinction from many "AI helpdesk" add-ons: Luma isn't a widget that only answers FAQs, it's meant to read tickets, search the internal knowledge base, route or resolve requests, and flag emerging incident patterns as part of the same system IT analysts already work in.

The company targets Fortune 100 and other large regulated enterprises, and cites Gartner recognition for its broader service management portfolio. That positioning matters for anyone evaluating Luma AI — this isn't a $20/month SaaS tool for a five-person startup; it's licensed and deployed the way most enterprise ITSM software is, with an implementation timeline measured in weeks.

## Pricing

Serviceaide doesn't publish a standalone price for Luma AI. Pricing sits at the platform level, and Luma AI's virtual agent capabilities are delivered as part of (or an add-on to) these tiers:

| Plan | Published price | Minimum commitment | What it includes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Knowledge Management | $1,800/month | 1,000 end-user seats | Self-service answers across IT and business teams, aimed at reducing ticket volume |
| Change Management | $2,800/month | 10 analyst seats | Policy-driven approvals, automated testing/rollback safeguards for change requests |
| ITSM – ESM (Enterprise Service Management) | Contact for pricing | 500 end-user seats | Full enterprise service management suite, volume discounts available |

There's no self-serve free trial listed on Serviceaide's pricing page — the calls to action are "Schedule a Call" or "Get Started," routing to a sales conversation and demo rather than an instant sign-up. Implementation timelines Serviceaide quotes run 4–12 weeks depending on tier, typical for enterprise ITSM but very different from the "install and go" experience of consumer AI tools.

Pricing, minimum seat counts, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's date (September 2026) based on Serviceaide's public pricing page, but enterprise vendors renegotiate deal structures constantly — treat these figures as a starting reference, not a locked-in quote.

## Core features walkthrough

**Agentic virtual agent for ticket deflection.** Luma AI's headline capability is handling employee requests conversationally — answering IT and HR-style questions, guiding password resets or access requests, and only escalating to a human analyst when needed. Serviceaide frames this as "round-the-clock assistance," meant to absorb the repetitive first-tier volume that otherwise clogs an IT queue.

**Natural language query (NLQ) across the knowledge base.** Rather than keyword search, Luma AI is built to interpret intent and pull from (and summarize) existing knowledge articles. This determines whether the tool actually reduces ticket volume in practice — an agentic layer is only as good as the knowledge base underneath it, so organizations with thin or outdated documentation should expect a heavier setup lift before deflection rates look good.

**Automated ticket categorization and routing.** Incoming requests get classified and routed to the right team automatically, which Serviceaide positions as reducing manual triage work.

**Incident pattern detection.** Luma AI is designed to spot clusters of related tickets — a signal of a major outage rather than isolated issues — and surface that to IT operations faster than manual review would.

**Knowledge-base hygiene: deduplication and gap detection.** Worth calling out because it's less common in competing helpdesk-AI tools: Luma AI includes tooling to identify duplicate knowledge articles and flag gaps where no article exists for a recurring question. That closes the loop between "the bot couldn't answer this" and "someone needs to write an article," often the missing piece in AI-deflection rollouts elsewhere.

## Who it's actually for

- **Enterprise IT/shared-services teams already on Serviceaide's platform**: Luma AI's value is clearest here, layered directly onto the ticketing and knowledge system you already run rather than a separate integration project.
- **Organizations evaluating a full ITSM replacement, not just a chatbot**: Serviceaide's minimum seat counts (500–1,000+ end users depending on tier) target mid-size-to-large deployments, not a team wanting a lightweight AI FAQ bot bolted onto Zendesk or Freshservice.
- **Regulated industries and Fortune 100-style enterprises**: Serviceaide explicitly markets to this segment, and the sales-led, multi-week implementation reflects procurement norms in healthcare, finance, and government IT more than fast-moving SMB teams.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Deep integration with Serviceaide's own ITSM/knowledge stack rather than a bolt-on widget | No public self-serve pricing or free trial — everything routes through sales |
| Built-in knowledge-base dedup and gap detection, not just a Q&A bot | High minimum seat/commitment thresholds shut out small teams |
| Incident pattern detection adds proactive value beyond simple deflection | 4–12 week implementation timelines mean no quick evaluation |
| Vendor cites hundreds of integrations with enterprise ITSM/CRM systems | Specific integration list and API documentation aren't fully public, so due diligence requires a sales conversation |
| Backed by an established ITSM vendor with Fortune 100 customers, reducing platform-risk concerns | Underlying model is OpenAI/ChatGPT-based per Serviceaide's own claim, not a proprietary differentiator |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Serviceaide states Luma AI connects to "hundreds of integrations" spanning ITSM platforms and CRM systems, and that it plugs into "leading business applications and communication channels." The company's own product page doesn't spell out, in public-facing text, whether that explicitly covers Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, or voice channels. Anyone evaluating this for a specific stack (say, a Teams-first organization, or one running ServiceNow alongside Serviceaide) should ask for the current integration and API list directly, since this is exactly the kind of detail that changes between marketing copy and what a sales engineer confirms on a call.

## Where it's a strong fit

Luma AI makes the most sense for organizations that already have (or are actively buying) a broader Serviceaide deployment and want the AI layer to sit natively on top of tickets and knowledge articles they already manage, rather than syncing a third-party chatbot against their ITSM data via API. It's also reasonable for enterprises that specifically want the knowledge-hygiene angle — flagging duplicate or missing articles — a workflow gap many pure-chatbot competitors leave to a separate tool.

## Where to think twice

Skip Luma AI if you need a fully free or low-cost tool to test before committing — there's no self-serve trial, and published tiers start at $1,800–$2,800/month with four-figure minimum seat counts, pricing out small IT teams and solo admins entirely. It's also not the right choice if you want to move fast: a 4–12 week implementation is standard for the category but a poor match for anyone hoping to have an AI assistant live within days. And because Serviceaide's public materials don't spell out granular data-handling or compliance certifications for Luma specifically, teams with strict data-residency or SOC 2/HIPAA requirements should get that confirmed in writing during procurement rather than assumed from general "Responsible AI" language on the marketing site.

## Bottom line

Luma AI is a credible, enterprise-grade agentic assistant for IT service desks, and its knowledge-base cleanup and incident-pattern features go a step beyond the basic "answer FAQs and open a ticket" pattern most AI helpdesk add-ons stop at. But it's priced, packaged, and sold like the enterprise ITSM software it's part of — no transparent pricing, no free trial, and seat minimums that put it out of reach for smaller teams. If you're already shopping for a full service management platform, it's worth a serious look; if you just want a cheap, fast AI chatbot for a small support queue, look elsewhere first.

## FAQ

**Is Luma AI the same as Luma Labs' video-generation AI?**
No. Luma AI by Serviceaide is an enterprise IT service-desk virtual agent. "Luma AI" from Luma Labs is a separate company that makes text-to-video and 3D-generation AI tools — the name overlap is coincidental.

**How much does Luma AI cost?**
No standalone price is published. It's delivered as part of platform tiers starting around $1,800/month for Knowledge Management (1,000-seat minimum) up to custom enterprise pricing for full ITSM-ESM deployments. Contact Serviceaide sales for a quote.

**Is there a free trial?**
No public self-serve free trial is listed. Serviceaide's pricing page routes prospects to a demo or sales call instead.

**What AI model powers Luma AI?**
Serviceaide states its virtual agent is built using OpenAI/ChatGPT technology, combined with the company's own retrieval, routing, and workflow logic layered on top.

**How long does implementation take?**
Serviceaide quotes 4–8 weeks for Knowledge Management and 8–12 weeks for Change Management or full ITSM-ESM deployments, depending on scope.

**Does Luma AI integrate with tools like Slack, Teams, or ServiceNow?**
Serviceaide says it supports "hundreds of integrations" across ITSM and CRM systems and "leading" communication channels, but doesn't publish a specific list — confirm your stack during a sales conversation.

**Who is Luma AI built for?**
Mid-size to large enterprises, particularly regulated industries and Fortune 100-style organizations already using or evaluating Serviceaide's ChangeGear/ESM platform — not small teams or solo IT admins looking for a lightweight, self-serve chatbot. If you just need a standalone AI chatbot for a smaller support queue without an enterprise ITSM commitment, a lighter-weight, self-serve tool will likely be a faster and cheaper fit. For more options across categories, see the [AI & software deals](/category/software) roundup on this site.

title: HairstyleAI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: HairstyleAI turns your selfies into 120 AI hairstyle previews for $9. Here's what it costs, how it works, and who it's actually worth it for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is HairstyleAI worth $9 for trying out new haircuts?

HairstyleAI (hairstyleai.com) is a one-time-payment tool that generates AI renderings of you wearing 30 different haircuts across 4 poses, so you can preview a style before booking a salon appointment. At $9 for 120 photos with roughly an hour turnaround, it's cheap and low-commitment, but the results are AI approximations, not a guarantee of how a cut will actually look on your real hair and face.

Note: "AI Hairstyle" isn't a single trademarked product name — several tools use similar branding. This review covers **HairstyleAI** (hairstyleai.com), built by the team behind [HeadshotPro](/blog/headshotpro-review), since it's the most prominent, currently live product that matches the "AI hairstyle try-on/generator" description. If you landed here looking for a different app with the same generic name, the core mechanics (upload a selfie, get AI-generated hairstyle variations) are similar across most competitors, but pricing and photo counts will differ.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $9 one-time payment (no subscription) |
| Free tier/trial | None published — every generation requires payment |
| Best for | Anyone deciding on a haircut before a salon visit, or just curious what a different style would look like |
| Standout feature | 120 HD photos across 30 hairstyles and 4 poses from a single upload batch, delivered in about an hour |

## What HairstyleAI actually is

HairstyleAI is made by HeadshotPro, a company based in Holland that also runs a well-known AI headshot generator (which we've reviewed separately — see the [HeadshotPro review](/blog/headshotpro-review)). HairstyleAI is a narrower, purpose-built spinoff: instead of generating professional headshots, it trains a model on a handful of your uploaded photos and then renders that same "you" wearing dozens of different haircuts and hair colors, male or female, so you can compare options side by side.

The company doesn't publish which underlying image model powers the generations, which is common among consumer AI photo tools. What's public is the output: HairstyleAI says it has generated over 155,000 hairstyles for more than 1,200 customers as of this writing, though that figure comes from the vendor's own site and isn't independently auditable.

There's no matching store entry for HairstyleAI in this site's coupon catalog at the time of writing, so there's no discount code to check here — the $9 price appears flat and non-negotiable.

## Pricing

HairstyleAI keeps pricing simple: there's exactly one package, not a tiered plan structure like most SaaS tools.

| Package | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Standard hairstyle pack | $9 one-time | 30 unique AI hairstyles, 4 poses, 120 total HD photos, roughly 1-hour turnaround |

There's no monthly subscription, no credit top-ups, and no free tier — you pay $9 before the AI starts generating anything. That's a meaningfully different model from most AI image tools on this site, which usually offer at least a handful of free credits. It also means there's less room to "try before you buy": you're committing the full $9 up front based on sample images and marketing claims alone.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — always double-check the current price and package details directly on [hairstyleai.com](https://hairstyleai.com) before paying, since AI tool pricing shifts often.

The site's FAQ lists a "Can I get a refund?" question, but the specific refund terms weren't fully accessible during our research — confirm the refund policy on the official site before purchasing if that matters to your decision.

## Features walkthrough

**Multi-pose, multi-style batch generation.** Rather than generating one hairstyle at a time, HairstyleAI processes your uploaded photos once and returns 30 different hairstyles across 4 poses in a single $9 batch — 120 images total. That's the core value proposition: volume, so you can compare a buzz cut against a fade against a longer style without paying per-render.

**Gender-inclusive style library.** The tool supports both male and female hairstyle libraries, covering a range from short cuts to longer styles, and different hair colors within those styles, rather than being scoped to one style category.

**Selfie-based training.** You upload a set of your own photos (the exact number required wasn't specified in accessible marketing copy — check the upload requirements on-site), and the AI trains on those to produce a consistent likeness across all 120 output images, rather than generating a generic face wearing each hairstyle.

**Fast turnaround.** HeadshotPro's own claim is about a 1-hour delivery window, which is fast relative to booking and sitting through an actual haircut consultation — useful if you're deciding same-day whether to book a specific style at a salon.

**Downloadable, owned output.** The site states that generated images belong to the user after download, which matters if you want to save specific results to show a stylist.

## Who it's actually for

- **Anyone about to get a haircut and undecided on style** — the main intended use case: preview options before committing scissors to hair.
- **People with hair-loss or texture concerns** who want to see how a shorter or different style might look before a permanent change.
- **Casual/curious users** who just want to see themselves with a different look for social media or fun, without any salon intent at all.
- **Stylists or salons** wanting to show clients a range of options — though HairstyleAI isn't built or priced as a B2B/multi-client tool, so a salon doing this repeatedly for many customers would be paying $9 per person, which adds up compared to enterprise-style avatar tools.

It's not built for anyone who needs pixel-accurate simulation of a specific cut on their specific hair texture — it's a visualization aid, not a virtual stylist with real cutting/color technique modeling.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Cheap flat fee ($9), no subscription trap | No free tier at all — you pay before seeing your specific results |
| Large output volume (120 photos, 30 styles) for the price | Refund terms aren't clearly published; confirm before buying |
| Fast ~1-hour turnaround | AI renderings are approximations, not guaranteed likenesses of a real haircut outcome |
| Works for both male and female style libraries | No published detail on the underlying AI model or accuracy testing |
| Made by an established company (HeadshotPro) rather than an anonymous app | Single, non-customizable package — can't buy fewer styles for less, or many more for a bulk discount |

## Integrations and ecosystem

HairstyleAI is a standalone web tool — there's no public API, no Zapier/Slack integration, and no browser extension. You upload photos through the website and download the resulting images directly; there's no built-in way to push results into a salon booking system, a photo-editing suite, or a social scheduler. If you want the hairstyle renders inside another workflow (for example, sending them straight to a stylist via a booking app), you'll be doing that manually by downloading and re-uploading images yourself.

The only real "ecosystem" tie-in is the connection to HeadshotPro — same company, but the two tools are sold and billed separately, and buying one doesn't get you credit on the other.

## Where it's a strong fit

HairstyleAI earns its keep in the narrow but common moment of "I'm not sure what haircut to get." Paying $9 for 120 rendered options is cheaper than a bad haircut, and faster than scrolling Pinterest boards hoping to find a photo of someone with your face shape. It's also a reasonable low-stakes way to experiment with color or a bolder cut you're nervous about committing to in real life.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a free tool** — there's no free tier here, so if budget is the blocker rather than curiosity, look at general-purpose AI image editors with free credits instead, understanding you'll get less specialized results.
- **If you want a guarantee the AI render matches a real-world outcome** — this is a preview/inspiration tool, not a simulation with any warranty of matching what a stylist can actually achieve with your hair type, thickness, or growth pattern. Bring the AI images to a consultation as a reference point, not a contract.
- **If you need enterprise or bulk features** — there's no team plan, no bulk-client pricing, and no API, so salons or apps wanting to embed this at scale for many customers would need to look elsewhere or negotiate directly with HeadshotPro.
- **If refund clarity matters before you buy** — since the refund policy text wasn't fully visible in our research, anyone risk-averse about a non-refundable purchase should read the FAQ in full and possibly reach out to support before paying.
- **If privacy of your photos is a hard requirement** — HairstyleAI's FAQ addresses data storage and photo deletion, but read those answers directly on-site rather than assuming; uploading face photos to any third-party AI service carries some inherent privacy trade-off.

## The bottom line

HairstyleAI does one thing — batch-generate AI hairstyle previews from your photos — and it does it at a low, predictable flat price rather than nickel-and-diming you per render. For the specific job of "help me decide on a haircut before I commit," $9 for 120 images across 30 styles is a fair trade, especially compared to the cost of an actual bad haircut. Just go in treating the results as inspiration and rough visualization rather than a photorealistic promise of your next salon outcome, and read the refund and privacy FAQ before you pay if either is a dealbreaker for you.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is HairstyleAI free?**
No. There's no published free tier — the only offer is a single $9 one-time package that includes 120 photos across 30 hairstyles and 4 poses.

**Does HairstyleAI have a subscription plan?**
No. It's sold as a flat one-time payment rather than a monthly or annual subscription, which is unusual compared to most AI SaaS tools.

**How long does it take to get results?**
The vendor states roughly a 1-hour turnaround after you upload your photos and pay, though actual times can vary with demand.

**Who makes HairstyleAI?**
It's built by the team behind HeadshotPro, an AI headshot generator based in Holland. You can read our full [HeadshotPro review](/blog/headshotpro-review) if you're also considering that product for professional photos.

**Can I get a refund if I don't like my results?**
The site has a refund FAQ entry, but the specific terms weren't fully accessible during our research — check the current refund policy directly on hairstyleai.com before purchasing.

**Will the AI-generated hairstyle look exactly like the real haircut?**
No — treat it as a visualization aid. The AI renders an approximation based on your uploaded photos and a chosen style; actual results from a real haircut depend on your stylist, hair texture, growth pattern, and other factors the AI can't fully model.

**Does HairstyleAI work for both men and women?**
Yes, the platform's style library covers both male and female hairstyle and hair-color options.

**What happens to my uploaded photos?**
HairstyleAI's FAQ addresses photo storage, ownership, and deletion, but read the specific answers on their site directly, since exact retention and deletion timelines weren't confirmable from the marketing pages alone.

**Are there cheaper or free alternatives?**
Yes — several general AI photo-editing apps offer basic hairstyle-filter features for free or as part of broader free credits, though usually with far fewer style options and less consistency than a purpose-built tool like HairstyleAI. title: Vidnoz AI Clothes Changer Review 2026: Free Outfit Swap
excerpt: Vidnoz AI Clothes Changer lets you swap outfits in a photo free online. Here is real pricing, features, limits, and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is the Vidnoz AI Clothes Changer worth using?

Vidnoz's AI Clothes Changer is a free browser-based tool for swapping outfits in a photo — pick a top, bottom, or full look from its wardrobe (or upload your own garment image) and it generates a new version of the picture. It's genuinely useful for quick e-commerce mockups and casual outfit try-ons, but daily free generations are capped, downloads need a free account, and there's no dedicated pricing page just for this tool.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free to use online; paid credits unlock HD/no-watermark exports and Vidnoz's other 12+ AI tools |
| Free tier/trial | Unlimited visits, but a limited number of free generations per day; login required only to download results |
| Best for | Sellers making quick product-photo variations, and casual users trying on outfit ideas |
| Standout feature | No-login editing with 2000x2000px output sized for Amazon, Shopify, eBay and Etsy listings |

## What it actually is

"AI Clothes Changer" isn't a trademarked product name on its own — several photo-editing sites ship a tool under that label. The one that matches this description most closely, and that shows up as a dedicated, currently-live feature page rather than a buried menu item, is **Vidnoz's AI Clothes Changer**, part of the broader Vidnoz AI suite. Vidnoz is an online AI content platform (also known for its AI avatar and text-to-video tools) that has built out a set of photo-editing utilities — background removal, photo restoration, AI photo editing, and this clothes-swapping tool among them.

The clothes changer works entirely in the browser: you upload a photo of a person, choose which part of the outfit to change (top, shorts, pants, short skirt, long skirt, or the full outfit), then either pick from a built-in wardrobe of styles or upload a reference clothing image. Vidnoz's own generation pipeline then renders a new photo with the swapped garment while trying to preserve the person's pose and body shape. The company doesn't publish which underlying image-generation model powers this specifically, so treat "AI-generated" here as the vendor's own description rather than a named, verifiable model.

## Pricing

Vidnoz doesn't sell the Clothes Changer as its own subscription product — it sits inside Vidnoz's shared credit system alongside the company's other AI tools (avatars, text-to-video, voice cloning, background removal, and more). On the clothes-changer page itself, Vidnoz states you get "free unlimited access to visit" the editor every day, but only "limited free times to use" the actual generation feature daily, and that downloading a finished image requires creating a free account. Beyond that, the page doesn't break out a credit cost per clothes-changer generation.

For a fuller picture of what upgrading buys you, Vidnoz's general pricing page lists platform-wide plans:

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0/month | Daily free-tool access, standard processing, limited exports |
| Starter | From around $2/month (promotional first-month rate) | 15 credits/month plus daily free credits, 1080p export, no watermark, faster processing |
| Business | From around $2/month (promotional first-month rate) | Everything in Starter plus unlimited photo generations, brand kit, team collaboration |
| Enterprise | Custom | Dedicated support, custom credit volumes, SSO |

Those introductory Starter/Business prices are promotional first-month rates rather than the ongoing renewal price, and Vidnoz doesn't clearly state how many credits a single clothes-changer generation consumes versus, say, an avatar video render. If the exact renewal price or per-generation credit cost matters for your decision, confirm it on Vidnoz's own pricing page before buying credits — platform-wide bundles like this tend to reallocate credit costs across tools over time.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tool pricing and credit allowances move fast, especially on multi-tool platforms like this one.

## Features walkthrough

**Outfit swapping by clothing region.** Rather than replacing an entire outfit, you can target just the top, just the bottom (shorts, pants, or a skirt of either length), or the whole look. That granularity matters if you only want to test a new jacket on an otherwise-unchanged photo.

**Custom garment upload.** Instead of picking from Vidnoz's built-in style wardrobe, you can upload a photo of an actual product — useful for sellers who want to show their own inventory on a model photo rather than a generic stock look.

**E-commerce-sized output.** Generated images come out at 2000x2000px, and Vidnoz specifically calls out compatibility with Amazon, Shopify, eBay, and Etsy listing requirements. That's a deliberate nod to the sell-more-with-less-photography use case rather than pure entertainment.

**No-login editing.** You can run the tool and see the generated result without creating an account — the login wall only appears when you try to download. That's a lower-friction trial experience than most AI photo tools that gate the entire preview behind a signup.

**Bundled into a wider AI toolkit.** Once you're inside a Vidnoz account, the same credits and login carry over to its other tools — background remover, photo restoration, avatar generator, and video tools — so heavier users get more value out of a single subscription than a one-off clothes-changer tool would offer on its own.

## Who it's actually for

- **Small online sellers and dropshippers** who need quick outfit variations of an existing product photo without a full photoshoot — the output size and marketplace framing make this the clearest fit.
- **Social content creators** testing outfit concepts for thumbnails or mockups before committing to a real photoshoot or purchase.
- **Casual users** curious about how an outfit might look on them, without expecting studio-grade realism.
- **Not a great fit** for brands needing pixel-perfect, on-model product photography for a catalog — this is a fast mockup tool, not a replacement for real photography or a dedicated fashion-retouching service.
- **Not a great fit** for teams that need guaranteed unlimited daily generations without hitting Vidnoz's free-tier cap, or that need enterprise data-handling guarantees for photos of real people — that's a conversation to have directly with Vidnoz's sales team, since none of it is detailed on the public feature page.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Free to try, no account needed to preview a result | Daily free generations are capped and not clearly quantified |
| Fast three-step workflow (upload, select, generate) | Downloading requires creating an account |
| Output sized for major marketplace listings | No clothes-changer-specific pricing page; credit costs are folded into Vidnoz's broader plans |
| Can target a specific garment or the whole outfit | No published info on the underlying model or training data |
| Works from a front-facing photo without special equipment | Needs a clear, front-facing, unobstructed photo — side angles or poor lighting degrade results |

## Integrations and ecosystem

There's no public API, Zapier connector, or Slack/plugin integration for the Clothes Changer specifically. It's a standalone web tool inside the Vidnoz platform, and any automation would have to go through Vidnoz's broader account/credit system rather than a documented developer API. If programmatic, bulk, or workflow-embedded outfit-swapping is what you need, this isn't built for that — it's a manual, one-photo-at-a-time editor.

## Where it's a strong fit

Vidnoz's Clothes Changer earns its keep when you have a single decent photo and want to quickly test how a different top, bottom, or full outfit looks on it — without booking a photographer or firing up Photoshop. For small sellers wanting quick marketplace-ready variations, or anyone testing outfit ideas casually, the no-login preview and simple three-step flow remove most of the friction.

## Where to think twice

Skip it if you need a tool with a fully transparent, dedicated pricing page — the credit system here is shared across a dozen-plus Vidnoz tools, and the vendor doesn't spell out exactly what a clothes-changer generation costs once you're past the free daily limit. Skip it too if your team needs enterprise-grade data handling commitments for photos containing real people's faces; that information simply isn't published anywhere on the feature page, and you'd need to get it in writing from Vidnoz directly. And if you need fully automated, bulk, or API-driven outfit swapping for a large product catalog, this manual one-photo tool won't scale to that without significant hands-on time.

Accuracy is also worth tempering expectations on: like most AI image-editing tools, results depend heavily on photo quality, and Vidnoz's own guidance (avoid profile angles, dim lighting, and obstructed poses) is effectively an admission that the model struggles outside a fairly narrow set of "good" input photos.

## Bottom line

For what it's clearly built for — quick, no-cost outfit mockups on a single well-lit, front-facing photo — Vidnoz's AI Clothes Changer does the job without much friction, and the marketplace-sized output is a genuinely useful touch for small sellers. It's not a professional photography replacement, its pricing structure is more opaque than most single-purpose AI tools, and heavier or bulk use will bump into the shared-credit system fast. Try the free version first on a clean, front-facing photo before deciding whether Vidnoz's paid credits are worth it for your volume of use.

## FAQ

**Is the Vidnoz AI Clothes Changer free?**
Yes, you can use the editor and preview a generated result without an account. You'll need a free Vidnoz account to download the finished image, and there's a daily cap on how many free generations you get — Vidnoz doesn't publish the exact number.

**Do I need to pay to download my result?**
You don't need to pay, but you do need to create a free account to unlock the download. Paid credits remove the watermark, unlock HD output, and raise your daily usage limits.

**What kind of photo works best?**
A clear, front-facing, well-lit photo of someone standing without obstructions. Profile shots, dim lighting, or objects blocking the body noticeably hurt the result quality.

**Can I upload my own clothing image instead of using the built-in wardrobe?**
Yes — you can upload a photo of an actual garment and Vidnoz will attempt to place it on the person in your uploaded photo, which is the main use case for sellers wanting to show their own inventory.

**What resolution does it output, and is it usable for marketplace listings?**
Vidnoz outputs images at 2000x2000px and specifically markets this as compatible with Amazon, Shopify, eBay, and Etsy listing requirements.

**Is there an API for bulk or automated use?**
No. There's no public API or documented bulk-processing option for this tool — it's a manual, single-photo web editor.

**How does pricing actually work if I want more generations?**
Vidnoz doesn't sell a standalone clothes-changer subscription. Extra usage draws from Vidnoz's shared credit plans (Starter, Business, Enterprise), which also cover its avatar, video, and other photo tools — so the effective cost per clothes-changer generation isn't published as a standalone number.

**Are there alternatives worth comparing?**
Yes — several general AI photo-editing platforms offer similar virtual outfit-swap features as one tool among many, often with the same free-preview-then-paywall-download pattern. If you're evaluating several, compare daily free limits, output resolution, and whether downloads need an account before settling on one.
