title: Odown Review 2026: Uptime Monitoring Pricing & Features
excerpt: Odown bundles uptime, API, and SSL monitoring with status pages and incident alerts. Here is real pricing, features, and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Odown a good uptime monitoring tool?

Odown is a website, API, and SSL monitoring platform aimed at small engineering teams that want uptime checks, status pages, and incident alerting in one dashboard instead of stitching together separate tools. It's a solid, affordably priced pick for startups and small SaaS teams, though its "AI-assisted" incident tooling is thinner in public documentation than the marketing framing suggests, and larger teams may outgrow its monitor caps.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $12/month (Basic plan) |
| Free tier/trial | 14-day free trial, full feature access, no credit card required |
| Best for | Solo developers and small-to-mid engineering teams monitoring websites, APIs, and SSL certs |
| Standout feature | 17-location global check network with unified status pages and incident escalation in one plan |

Odown has no matching store entry on this site, so there's no coupon page for it below — pricing and feature details here come directly from Odown's own pricing and homepage pages as of this post's date, and are worth double-checking on [odown.com](https://www.odown.com) before you buy, since monitoring vendors adjust monitor caps and check intervals fairly often.

## What Odown actually is

Odown is built by a small independent team (not backed by a major cloud vendor) as a consolidated alternative to running separate uptime, SSL, and status-page tools. According to Odown's own homepage, the platform serves roughly 500+ customers running 2,000+ monitors and processing around 600,000 checks a day — modest numbers next to category giants like UptimeRobot or Pingdom, which suggests a smaller, earlier-stage operation rather than an enterprise-scale one.

The pitch is straightforward: instead of paying for a separate uptime checker, a separate SSL expiry tracker, a separate status-page tool, and a separate incident/on-call system, Odown bundles all four into one subscription. That bundling is really the product's core value proposition, more than any single standout technical capability.

On the "AI-assisted incident analysis" framing specifically: Odown's public pricing and marketing pages describe incident management, alerting, and escalation (Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, SMS, etc.) but don't prominently document a named AI/root-cause-analysis feature the way some newer monitoring tools do. If AI-powered incident summarization matters to your decision, confirm directly with Odown's team before signing up rather than assuming it from general marketing framing.

## Pricing

Odown's pricing is unusually low for the category, especially for teams that don't need hundreds of monitors:

| Plan | Price | Monitors | Check interval | Status pages | Notable inclusions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | $12/month | 10 | Down to 1 minute | 1 status page | 17 data-center locations, 50 SMS credits, email/Slack/webhook/Telegram/Discord alerts |
| Pro | $29/month | 40 | Down to 1 minute | Unlimited, up to 1,000 subscribers | Everything in Basic plus incident management tools, Vonage SMS, 60 SMS credits |
| Advanced | $249/month | 300 | Down to 1 minute | Unlimited, up to 5,000 subscribers | All alert integrations, full incident management, 300 SMS credits |

All plans include the same 1-minute-to-24-hour check interval range and access to the same 17 global data-center locations — the differentiator between tiers is monitor count, status-page subscriber limits, and SMS credit allowances, not check frequency. Odown offers a 14-day free trial with full feature access and no credit card required, which is a genuinely low-friction way to test whether the check network catches the outages you care about before committing.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's date (September 2026) per Odown's public pricing page, but monitoring vendors revise monitor caps and plan structures often enough that it's worth reconfirming on their site before purchasing.

## Features walkthrough

**Website and API monitoring.** Odown checks HTTP(S) endpoints from its 17 worldwide data centers, supporting standard uptime pings as well as more detailed API checks (methods, headers, and response validation). For teams monitoring a handful of REST endpoints alongside a marketing site, this covers the common case without needing a separate synthetic-monitoring tool.

**SSL certificate monitoring.** Odown tracks certificate expiry dates across your monitored domains and alerts before a cert lapses — a genuinely useful feature since expired-SSL outages are one of the most common and most avoidable causes of downtime, yet easy to forget about until it's too late.

**Status pages.** Every paid plan includes at least one branded, customer-facing status page; Pro and Advanced unlock unlimited status pages and thousands of subscriber slots. This matters for any team that fields "is your service down?" support tickets during incidents — a public status page with subscriber notifications cuts down on that repetitive support load.

**Incident management and escalation.** Odown routes alerts through email, SMS, Slack, Discord, Telegram, webhooks, and (on Pro/Advanced) integrates with PagerDuty and Opsgenie for on-call escalation. This is the piece that turns "we got an email" into an actual incident-response workflow with acknowledgment and escalation paths.

**Global check network.** The 17-location spread (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America per Odown's own description) helps distinguish a real outage from a regional network blip.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo developers and indie SaaS builders** — the Basic plan's 10 monitors and single status page are enough for a side project or an early-stage product, and $12/month is inexpensive insurance against silent downtime.
- **Small engineering teams (2–15 people)** — the Pro plan's 40 monitors, unlimited status pages, and PagerDuty/Opsgenie integration cover a small team running several services with a lightweight on-call rotation.
- **Growing companies with dozens of services** — the Advanced plan's 300 monitors and 5,000 status-page subscribers can support a mid-size infrastructure footprint, though at $249/month it's worth comparing against enterprise-grade competitors that may offer more mature incident tooling at similar cost.
- **Not ideal for** — large enterprises needing SOC 2/enterprise compliance documentation, multi-region private network monitoring, or teams that specifically need a mature, named AI root-cause-analysis feature today rather than standard alerting and escalation.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Low entry price ($12/month) relative to bundled feature set | Public AI-incident-analysis capability isn't clearly documented — confirm before relying on it |
| 14-day free trial with full features, no credit card | Advanced plan's $249/month jump is steep relative to Pro's $29/month |
| SSL, uptime, API, and status pages bundled in one subscription | Smaller customer base (500+) than category leaders, so fewer public reviews to cross-check |
| 17-location global check network on every plan | 1-minute minimum check interval — no sub-minute checks for teams needing tighter SLAs |
| Native PagerDuty and Opsgenie integration on paid plans | Basic plan limited to a single status page |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Odown connects to the incident-response tools most small teams already use: Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, email, SMS (including Vonage on higher tiers), and generic webhooks. PagerDuty and Opsgenie support on Pro and Advanced plans lets Odown plug into an existing on-call rotation rather than replacing it. Odown's docs also describe API access for programmatic monitor management, useful for provisioning monitors as part of infrastructure-as-code.

## Where it's a strong fit

Odown makes sense if you want one subscription that replaces three or four point tools — an uptime checker, an SSL expiry tracker, a status page, and basic incident escalation — without enterprise pricing. The 14-day no-card trial is a low-risk way to validate the check network against your actual services before paying anything, and the Basic and Pro tiers are priced well below what teams often end up paying when they stack Better Uptime, a separate SSL checker, and a separate status-page tool.

## Where to think twice

Skip Odown, or at least dig deeper first, if:

- You need a fully free tier for ongoing production use — Odown's trial is generous but time-limited, with no permanent free plan.
- Your team requires SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar enterprise compliance documentation for a vendor handling uptime data — that level of paperwork isn't prominently published on Odown's public site.
- You specifically need a named, documented AI incident-analysis or automated root-cause feature today — the public pricing and feature pages reviewed here describe standard alerting/escalation, not a distinct AI-analysis product surface, so verify this directly with their team before assuming it's included.
- You're monitoring at a scale beyond a few hundred endpoints — the jump from Pro ($29/month, 40 monitors) to Advanced ($249/month, 300 monitors) is a big price step, and even Advanced may not scale as cost-effectively as usage-based competitors for very large monitor counts.

## Bottom line

Odown is a reasonably priced, competently built uptime-and-incident bundle that's well suited to solo developers and small teams who want website, API, and SSL monitoring plus a status page without juggling four separate vendors. It earns its place at the budget end of the category on price and feature bundling alone. Where it's less clear-cut is the AI-incident-analysis angle some buyers may be expecting — that capability isn't spelled out in Odown's own public pricing or feature pages as of this review, so anyone choosing Odown specifically for AI-driven root-cause analysis should confirm the details with Odown directly rather than assume it from general monitoring-tool marketing. For everyone else who just needs solid, affordable uptime and incident coverage, it's worth the 14-day trial.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Odown free?**
No permanent free plan exists, but Odown offers a 14-day free trial with full feature access and no credit card required, so you can fully test it before paying.

**How much does Odown cost?**
Plans start at $12/month (Basic, 10 monitors), $29/month (Pro, 40 monitors), and $249/month (Advanced, 300 monitors), per Odown's public pricing page as of this review.

**Does Odown have AI-powered incident analysis?**
Odown's public pricing and feature pages describe standard incident management, alerting, and escalation (including PagerDuty and Opsgenie integration) rather than a distinctly branded AI root-cause-analysis feature. If that capability matters to your decision, confirm directly with Odown before subscribing.

**What check interval does Odown use?**
All plans support check intervals from 1 minute up to 24 hours, checked from 17 global data-center locations, according to Odown's pricing page.

**Does Odown monitor SSL certificates?**
Yes — SSL certificate expiry monitoring is included so you get alerted before a certificate lapses, rather than discovering it during an outage.

**Can I get a branded status page with Odown?**
Yes. Basic includes one status page; Pro and Advanced include unlimited status pages with up to 1,000 and 5,000 subscribers respectively.

**What are the main alternatives to Odown?**
Common alternatives in the uptime-monitoring category include UptimeRobot, Better Stack (formerly Better Uptime), Pingdom, and StatusCake — each with different pricing structures and monitor caps worth comparing against Odown's tiers for your specific monitor count.

**Is Odown beginner-friendly?**
Yes — setup is dashboard-driven with no infrastructure to deploy, and the free trial lets new users test monitors, status pages, and alert integrations before committing to a paid plan.

title: SMMRY Review 2026: Free AI Article Summarizer Tested
excerpt: SMMRY offers a free AI text summarizer plus paid tiers with YouTube, podcast and mind-map tools. Here's an honest look at what you actually get.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is SMMRY worth using in 2026?

Yes, for quick article summaries — SMMRY's free plan gives you 10 AI summaries with no account hassle, and the paid tiers add YouTube, podcast and book summarization plus mind maps. It's a heavier, more feature-rich tool than a bare-bones text condenser, but the free allowance is limited and most of the interesting features sit behind a subscription.

**At a glance**

| | SMMRY |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (10 summaries), then $14/month or $7/month billed yearly for Essential |
| Free tier | Yes — 10 AI summaries on the Standard plan, no stated character cap on input |
| Best for | Students and researchers who also want YouTube/podcast summaries and a saved library |
| Standout feature | "AI Summarizer 2.0" with mind-map generation and podcast/video extraction on higher tiers |

## What SMMRY actually is

SMMRY started life as one of the older, more recognizable names in web-based text summarization — a simple tool you'd paste an article or URL into and get back a shortened, sentence-extracted version. The product has since been rebuilt around what it calls "AI Summarizer 2.0," moving from a purely extractive algorithm (picking and keeping the most relevant existing sentences) toward AI-generated condensed output, alongside newer additions like YouTube video insights, podcast extraction, and mind-map generation on paid tiers.

SMMRY doesn't publish which specific large language model powers its newer AI modes, so treat any claim about "AI-driven" summaries as the vendor's own description rather than a benchmarked fact. What is documented is the API, which is credit-based: one credit processes roughly 750,000 input tokens for about $1, with no expiry on unused credits and volume discounts above 250 credits — aimed at developers who want to bake summarization into their own product rather than end users browsing the web app.

## Pricing

SMMRY's consumer-facing pricing has three tiers, plus a separate developer API priced on its own credit system.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Standard AI Summarizer, 10 summaries total, works on text, articles and web pages |
| Essential | $14/mo (or $7/mo billed yearly) | AI Summarizer 2.0, 20 summaries/day, personal library, books and websites, YouTube video insights |
| Advanced | $25/mo (or $13/mo billed yearly) | Everything in Essential, unlimited daily summaries, podcast extraction, mind map generation |
| API (developer) | ~$1 per credit (≈750,000 input tokens), no subscription, credits don't expire | Custom sentence count, 20+ languages, content filters, batch processing, text/URL/PDF input |

A few things worth flagging before you commit a card number: the free plan's "10 summaries" reads as a lifetime allowance on the Standard tier, not a recurring daily or monthly quota — a meaningfully thinner free tier than tools like Resoomer that cap nothing. See our [Resoomer review](/blog/resoomer-review) if unlimited free use matters more than SMMRY's extra features. Annual pricing is also billed once a year at that monthly-equivalent rate (Essential is $84/year, not $7 charged monthly), which is standard but easy to misread.

Pricing, free-tier limits and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI summarization tools update their plans often, so confirm current numbers on SMMRY's own pricing page before subscribing.

## Core features

**AI Summarizer 2.0.** The rebuilt summarization engine is the headline change from SMMRY's older extractive-only tool. Paid tiers let you summarize not just pasted text but full articles, web pages and entire books, with the option to save results to a personal library instead of losing them when you close the tab.

**YouTube and podcast extraction.** Essential and Advanced respectively add the ability to pull a summary out of a YouTube video or a podcast episode — useful if your actual bottleneck is long-form audio/video content rather than text, which most competing summarizers (including Resoomer) don't attempt at all.

**Mind map generation.** Available on the Advanced tier, this turns a summarized document into a visual node map rather than a block of text — a genuinely different output format from the bullet-point or paragraph summaries most tools default to, and useful for anyone studying material rather than just skimming it.

**Developer API with granular controls.** The API's `num_of_sentences`, `avoid_questions`, `avoid_exclamations` and `avoid_quotations` parameters give programmatic users real control over summary shape, and support for 20+ languages with auto-detection means it isn't limited to English input. Batch processing across multiple documents at once is aimed squarely at teams building summarization into their own workflow rather than casual one-off use.

**Personal library.** Once you're on a paid plan, summaries get saved rather than disappearing — a small but practical difference if you're regularly re-referencing material you've already condensed, instead of re-pasting the same article every time you need it.

## Who it's actually for

- **Students on a budget:** the free 10-summary allowance is enough to try the tool, but if you're summarizing dozens of readings a week, you'll hit the ceiling fast and need to weigh Essential's $7/month annual rate against free alternatives.
- **Researchers and lifelong learners:** Essential's personal library and YouTube support fit people doing ongoing reading and video research who want results to persist across sessions.
- **Podcast-heavy content consumers:** Advanced's podcast extraction and unlimited daily summaries are the only reason to pay the higher tier over Essential — if you don't listen to podcasts, Advanced's extra $11–18/month buys you mostly unlimited volume and mind maps.
- **Developers:** the credit-based API is built for embedding summarization into another product, not for a person who just wants to paste one article a day.
- **Casual one-off users:** if you need to summarize a single article occasionally, the free tier or a genuinely unlimited free tool will cover it without a subscription.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Wider input support than most summarizers — text, URLs, PDFs, YouTube, podcasts | Free tier caps out at 10 summaries total, not a recurring allowance |
| Mind-map output is a genuinely different, study-friendly format | Underlying AI model isn't publicly named, so output quality claims are unverified |
| Developer API with real parameter control and no credit expiry | Meaningful features (YouTube, podcasts, mind maps, unlimited use) are locked behind $14–25/month |
| Personal library keeps past summaries instead of losing them | Annual pricing framing ($7/mo billed yearly) can read cheaper than the actual yearly charge at a glance |

## Integrations and ecosystem

SMMRY's main integration point is its own REST-style API, which accepts text, URLs and PDF files and returns summaries with configurable sentence counts and language handling — suited to developers wiring summarization into an internal tool, a CMS, or a research pipeline. There's no publicly documented native Zapier connector, Slack app, or browser extension in the way some competing summarizers offer (Resoomer, for one, ships extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi), so check SMMRY's current site before assuming parity there.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You regularly need to summarize a mix of content types — articles, PDFs, YouTube videos and podcasts — in one place rather than juggling separate tools for each.
- You want summaries to persist in a searchable personal library instead of re-running the same text through a tool repeatedly.
- You're a developer who wants a pay-as-you-go, credit-based summarization API without committing to a monthly subscription.
- You find mind-map style output more useful for studying than plain bullet-point or paragraph summaries.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a fully free, unlimited tool,** SMMRY's free plan tops out at 10 summaries total — look at Resoomer or similar no-signup tools instead if budget is the deciding factor.
- **If accuracy verification matters to you,** SMMRY doesn't publish which model powers its AI summaries, so there's no public benchmark to check output quality against; treat any "AI-driven" marketing language as a vendor claim, not an independent finding.
- **If you need enterprise compliance documentation (SOC 2, GDPR data processing agreements, etc.),** SMMRY's public pages don't detail this — confirm directly with their team before using it on sensitive or regulated content.
- **If you only ever summarize plain text occasionally,** the YouTube, podcast and mind-map features you'd be paying for on Essential or Advanced go unused, making the subscription poor value relative to a simpler free tool.
- **If you need offline or on-premise summarization,** SMMRY is a cloud web app and API only — there's no self-hosted or offline option documented.

## Bottom line

SMMRY has grown from a bare-bones extractive summarizer into a broader research and content tool, and the YouTube/podcast/mind-map additions genuinely differentiate it from simpler competitors. But that breadth comes at a real cost: the free plan's 10-summary lifetime cap is thin, the useful features sit behind $14–25/month, and the vendor doesn't disclose what's under the hood well enough to independently verify quality claims. If you specifically want video or podcast summarization alongside text and are willing to pay for it, SMMRY is one of the few tools that covers all three. If you just need to condense the occasional article for free with no strings attached, a simpler unlimited tool will likely serve you better.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is SMMRY completely free?** The Standard plan is free but limited to 10 summaries in total, not a recurring daily or monthly allowance. Ongoing use requires the $14/month Essential or $25/month Advanced plan (both cheaper billed yearly).

**Does SMMRY have a browser extension?** SMMRY's publicly documented tools center on its web app and API; check its current site for any extension availability, since this isn't detailed the way it is for some competing summarizers.

**What AI model does SMMRY use?** SMMRY doesn't publicly name the model behind its "AI Summarizer 2.0." Treat specific quality or accuracy claims as the vendor's own description rather than an independently verified fact.

**Can SMMRY summarize YouTube videos and podcasts?** Yes — YouTube video insights are included from the Essential plan up, and podcast extraction is available on the Advanced plan.

**Is there a free trial of the paid plans?** SMMRY's public pricing page lists a free Standard tier rather than a time-limited trial of Essential or Advanced; confirm current trial availability directly on their pricing page before subscribing.

**How does SMMRY's API pricing work?** The API uses a credit-based model, roughly $1 per credit, with each credit covering about 750,000 input tokens. Credits don't expire, and volume discounts apply above 250 credits. There's no listed free API tier.

**Is SMMRY good for beginners?** The web app itself is simple to use — paste text or a URL and get a summary — but understanding which plan you actually need (Essential vs. Advanced) requires reading the feature breakdown carefully, since the difference is mainly unlimited use, podcasts and mind maps rather than summary quality.

**What's a free alternative to SMMRY if I don't need YouTube or podcast support?** Our [Resoomer review](/blog/resoomer-review) covers a tool with no summary cap and no sign-up requirement, which may suit lighter, text-only summarization needs better than SMMRY's capped free tier.

For more free-tool comparisons and software savings, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub.

title: Mistral AI Review 2026: Le Chat Pricing and Verdict
excerpt: Is Mistral AI worth using in 2026? A look at Le Chat and La Plateforme pricing, open-weight models, and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Mistral AI worth using in 2026?

Mistral AI is a French lab that ships two related products: Le Chat, a free-to-start consumer chatbot with coding and image-generation modes, and La Plateforme, a developer API for its open-weight and proprietary models. It's a solid pick if you want strong open-weight models, EU-hosted data, and cheap API pricing, but it still trails ChatGPT and Claude on raw reasoning benchmarks and plugin depth.

### At a glance

| | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | Free (Le Chat), API from $0.1 per 1M tokens (Ministral 3) |
| Paid plans | Le Chat Pro $14.99/mo, Team $24.99/user/mo, Enterprise custom |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — free Le Chat plan with limited messages, $10/mo in API credits included |
| Best for | Developers wanting open-weight models, EU/privacy-focused users, budget API use |
| Standout feature | Open-weight model family (Mistral Large/Medium/Small) usable both via API and self-hosted |

## What Mistral AI actually is

Mistral AI is a Paris-based lab founded in April 2023 by Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix — three researchers who previously worked on large language models at Google DeepMind and Meta AI. It became one of Europe's fastest-funded AI startups, and as of its most recent funding round in September 2026 the company was valued above €21 billion after a €3 billion Series D. That scale matters for a French/EU company specifically, because it positions Mistral as the closest thing Europe has to a sovereign counterweight to US-based labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, and Chinese labs like Moonshot AI (Kimi) or DeepSeek.

The company ships two distinct products under one roof:

- **Le Chat** — the consumer-facing chatbot, comparable to ChatGPT or [Kimi](/blog/kimi-ai-review), with chat, coding, image generation, web search and an agentic coding mode called Vibe.
- **La Plateforme** — the developer API, where you pay per token to call Mistral's models programmatically, either hosted by Mistral or, for the open-weight releases, downloaded and run on your own infrastructure.

Mistral's biggest differentiator from day one has been releasing many of its flagship model weights openly, rather than keeping everything closed like OpenAI and Anthropic do. The current lineup, per Mistral's own model pages, includes Mistral Large 3, Mistral Medium 3.5, Mistral Small 4, the lightweight Ministral 3 family (3B/8B/14B parameters), Codestral for code generation, Voxtral for speech, and Mistral OCR for document intelligence. Several of these are open-weight; others (like the newest Medium releases) are API-only.

## Pricing

Mistral's pricing was accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — like most AI products, both the consumer plans and the per-token API rates move often, so confirm current numbers on Mistral's own pricing pages before budgeting around them.

### Le Chat (consumer)

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Limited chat messages and web searches, limited coding sessions, image generation, $10/month in API credits |
| Pro | $14.99/mo ($5.99/mo for verified students) | Expanded message and search limits, all-day coding access, more image generations, $15/month in API credits, chat/email support |
| Team | $24.99 per user/month | Everything in Pro, plus up to 30GB storage per user, domain verification, data export, shared workspace features |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom models/agents, custom workflows, audit logs, SAML SSO, white-label deployment options |

### La Plateforme (API)

API pricing is charged per million tokens, split between input and output, with steep price gaps between model tiers:

| Model | Input ($/1M tokens) | Output ($/1M tokens) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ministral 3 (3B) | $0.10 | $0.10 | Cheapest, lightweight tasks |
| Ministral 3 (8B) | $0.15 | $0.15 | Small-scale agents, classification |
| Mistral Small 4 | $0.15 | $0.60 | Open-weight, general use |
| Codestral | $0.30 | $0.90 | Code generation/completion |
| Mistral Large 3 | $0.50 | $1.50 | Open-weight flagship |
| Mistral Medium 3.5 | $1.50 | $7.50 | Powers Vibe's remote coding agents |
| Mistral Embed | $0.10 | — (input only) | Embeddings for search/RAG |
| Mistral OCR 4.1 | $4 per 1,000 pages | — | Document parsing/extraction |

Mistral also offers batch processing at roughly 50% off standard rates for non-real-time workloads, and prompt caching that Mistral states can cut input costs by up to 90% on repeated context. Mistral's open-weight tiers (Small, Large) are consistently cheaper per token than comparable GPT or Claude API tiers — that gap is the main reason cost-sensitive builders (high-volume classification, RAG pipelines, internal tools) look at Mistral first.

## Core features walkthrough

**Open-weight model access.** Unlike ChatGPT or Claude, several Mistral models can be downloaded and run on your own hardware or private cloud, not just called through an API — useful for teams with strict data-residency requirements or anyone who wants to fine-tune a base model rather than only prompt-engineer around a closed one.

**Le Chat's coding agent (Vibe).** Le Chat's Pro and Team tiers include "all-day coding" access through Vibe, an agentic coding mode with Work and Code modes and a VS Code extension launched in mid-2026. It's positioned against GitHub Copilot and Cursor, though newer with a shorter track record.

**Multilingual strength.** As a European company, Mistral has invested in non-English language quality — French, German, Spanish and Italian in particular — with several independent multilingual benchmarks ranking it above GPT and Claude's non-English output, though English nuance still tends to favor the larger US labs' flagship models.

**Document intelligence (OCR).** Mistral OCR is a dedicated model for parsing scanned documents, PDFs and forms into structured text, priced per page rather than per token, aimed at document-heavy enterprise workflows rather than general chat.

**Agentic Search and MCP connectors.** Le Chat added Agentic Search for more reliable document navigation and citation verification, plus support for custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors — the same open standard Anthropic introduced — letting Le Chat pull live data from external tools rather than working from a static knowledge cutoff alone.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo developers and indie builders** get the most obvious win: cheap per-token API pricing on Ministral and Small-tier models for cost-sensitive apps (chat widgets, classifiers, summarizers) where a frontier-model price tag doesn't make sense.
- **EU-based teams and privacy-conscious businesses** benefit from Mistral being a French company subject to EU data-protection law by default, plus the option to self-host open-weight models — a real advantage for anyone with GDPR or data-sovereignty requirements in procurement.
- **Individual Le Chat users** who want a free daily-driver chatbot with image generation and basic coding help will find the free tier usable, though message caps push moderate users toward the $14.99 Pro plan quickly.
- **Enterprises** needing custom models, SSO, audit logs and white-labeling have a real Enterprise tier to negotiate into, though actual cost and SLA terms need confirming directly with Mistral's sales team.
- **Teams already standardized on Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT or Claude** have less reason to switch outright; Vibe and Le Chat are competitive but newer, with a smaller integration ecosystem than either incumbent.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Genuinely open-weight models you can self-host | Consumer app free tier is limited on messages/searches |
| Cheaper per-token API pricing than most frontier-model competitors | Trails GPT/Claude on some general reasoning benchmarks |
| EU-based, GDPR-native data handling by default | Vibe coding agent is newer with a shorter track record |
| Strong multilingual output, especially European languages | Smaller third-party plugin/integration ecosystem than ChatGPT |
| Batch discounts and prompt caching cut real API costs | Enterprise pricing isn't public — requires a sales conversation |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Mistral offers a standard REST API through La Plateforme, official SDKs for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and hosting through major cloud marketplaces including AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry and Google Cloud Vertex AI — useful if your infrastructure is already committed to one of those clouds. Le Chat supports custom MCP connectors for pulling in external tools and data sources, and Mistral has a distribution partnership with Mozilla to bring private, multilingual AI features into Firefox. There's no large third-party plugin marketplace comparable to the GPT Store, so most integrations happen at the API level through your own code rather than a one-click app ecosystem.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You need to self-host or fine-tune an open-weight model rather than only call a hosted API.
- Your organization has EU data-residency or GDPR requirements that make a US-hosted provider a harder sell to legal/procurement.
- You're building a high-volume, cost-sensitive app (classification, RAG, summarization) where per-token API cost matters more than squeezing out the last few benchmark points.
- You work primarily in French, German, Spanish or another European language and want a model tuned with that in mind.

## Where to think twice

- If you need the single best general-reasoning model regardless of cost, GPT and Claude's flagship tiers still generally edge out Mistral's on several independent benchmarks.
- If you rely on a large third-party plugin ecosystem (GPT Store-style extensions), Mistral's is thinner.
- If you need a mature, battle-tested agentic coding tool, Vibe is new enough that GitHub Copilot or Cursor may be the safer near-term bet.
- If you want a fully free tool with no message caps, Le Chat's free tier has real limits that push regular users toward Pro.
- If you need enterprise compliance certifications already documented publicly rather than discussed on a sales call, some competitors publish more of that detail upfront.

## Bottom line

Mistral AI earns its spot less on raw chatbot polish and more on what it represents structurally: a credible, well-funded European alternative that actually opens its model weights and charges less per token than the biggest US labs. If you're optimizing for API cost, need EU-based data handling, or want to self-host rather than depend on someone else's API uptime, Mistral is worth setting up today. If you just want the single sharpest chatbot regardless of cost or data residency, ChatGPT and Claude still have a benchmark edge — though the gap has narrowed with each new Mistral release.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Mistral AI free to use?**
Yes — Le Chat has a free plan with limited messages, web searches and coding sessions, plus $10/month in included API credits. Heavier use requires the $14.99/month Pro plan.

**How does Mistral's API pricing compare to OpenAI and Anthropic?**
Mistral's open-weight tiers (Ministral, Small, Large) are generally cheaper per million tokens than equivalent GPT or Claude tiers, though Mistral Medium 3.5 (its highest-capability model) is priced closer to competitors' mid-tier offerings. Always check current rates on each provider's pricing page, since these numbers change often.

**Can I run Mistral's models on my own servers?**
Yes, for the open-weight releases (including Mistral Large 3 and Small 4) — you can download the weights and self-host, which is one of Mistral's core differentiators versus fully closed competitors.

**Is Mistral good for coding?**
Codestral is Mistral's dedicated coding model, and Le Chat's Pro/Team tiers include Vibe, an agentic coding assistant with a VS Code extension. It's newer than GitHub Copilot or Cursor, so track record and third-party tooling are thinner.

**Where is Mistral's data hosted, and is it GDPR-compliant?**
As a French company, Mistral operates under EU data-protection law by default, which is a meaningful factor for European businesses with data-residency requirements. Enterprise customers should confirm specific hosting-region guarantees directly with Mistral, since exact infrastructure details can change.

**What's the difference between Le Chat and La Plateforme?**
Le Chat is the consumer chatbot app (like ChatGPT); La Plateforme is the developer API for calling Mistral's models programmatically or integrating them into your own products.

**Is Mistral AI good for non-English languages?**
Mistral has specifically invested in European-language quality (French, German, Spanish, Italian), and several multilingual benchmarks rank it strongly there, though this should be tested against your specific use case rather than assumed.

**What are the main alternatives to Mistral AI?**
ChatGPT and Claude are the closest general-purpose competitors; [Kimi AI](/blog/kimi-ai-review) is a comparable open-weight-friendly alternative with a much larger context window. Explore more options on [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Video Background Remover Review 2026: Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Video Background Remover was Unscreen — now folded into Canva's Pro plan. Here's what it costs, how well it works, and who it's worth it for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Video Background Remover (Unscreen) still a good way to remove video backgrounds?

"Video Background Remover" and "Unscreen" are the same underlying AI tool — Unscreen.com now redirects straight to Canva's video background remover feature, since Canva acquired its parent company, Kaleido AI, in 2021. It's a genuinely useful, fast background-removal engine for casual clips and social content, but it's no longer a free standalone site — it's a Canva Pro feature wrapped inside a full design and video editor.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free with limited/one-off use; full unlimited access requires Canva Pro (subscription, billed monthly or annually) |
| Free tier/trial | Canva's free plan allows some background-removal use with restrictions; Canva Pro typically includes a free trial period |
| Best for | Creators, marketers, and small teams already using Canva for video, who need quick green-screen-free background removal |
| Standout feature | One-click AI background removal on ordinary video clips, no green screen or manual masking required |

## What Video Background Remover actually is

If you searched "video background remover" expecting a dedicated site, you likely had Unscreen in mind — for years the best-known browser-based tool for stripping backgrounds out of video clips and GIFs using AI, without a green screen. Unscreen was built by Kaleido AI GmbH, a Vienna-based computer-vision company that also created the well-known image tool remove.bg.

That's no longer a separate destination. Canva acquired Kaleido AI in March 2021, and by 2026 unscreen.com redirects directly to canva.com's video background remover feature page. The frame-by-frame AI subject-detection technology Unscreen pioneered — working on ordinary footage instead of requiring a physical green screen — now powers the "Background Remover" tool inside Canva's video editor. There's no meaningfully-maintained standalone competitor still operating under the old Unscreen brand.

Canva doesn't publish deep technical detail on which model runs the video background remover today (described only as an in-house AI/ML segmentation model), so treat model-specific claims as unverified.

## Pricing

Canva's pricing structure applies to the background remover the same way it applies to Canva's other AI-assisted design tools: a limited allotment on the free plan, full/unlimited use gated behind Canva Pro.

| Plan | Price (typical) | Background remover access |
|---|---|---|
| Canva Free | $0 | Some background-removal use is available, but Canva has historically limited free, unlimited use of premium AI tools like this one — expect either a capped number of uses or reduced quality/resolution |
| Canva Pro | Paid monthly or annual subscription (commonly quoted around $12–15/month billed annually, higher month-to-month) | Full, repeated use of the video background remover plus Canva's other premium AI features (Magic Studio tools, Brand Kit, more storage) |
| Canva Teams | Per-seat pricing on top of Pro-level features | Same AI feature access, extended to shared team workspaces and approval workflows |
| Canva Enterprise | Custom/contact sales | Adds admin controls, SSO, and compliance features on top of the same core AI toolset |

Because Canva changes plan names, trial lengths, and exact price points fairly often, treat the numbers above as directional rather than exact, and confirm the current figures on Canva's own pricing page before you commit. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability here were accurate as of this post's date (2026-09-18) and can change without much notice.

Canva has no matching store entry on this site as of this writing, so there's no dedicated coupon page to link to for it — check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for other current AI-tool offers instead.

## Features walkthrough

**Automatic subject detection on ordinary footage.** The core trick, inherited from Unscreen, is that it doesn't need a green screen or a static camera — it analyzes each frame and separates the moving subject from the background using AI segmentation, then lets you drop in a new background, a solid color, or full transparency.

**Works inside a full video editor, not a one-trick uploader.** Where standalone Unscreen was a single-purpose upload-and-download tool, the Canva version sits inside Canva's timeline-based video editor, so once the background is removed you can layer text, transitions, stock footage, or your brand kit on the same canvas instead of exporting and reimporting into a separate app.

**Export flexibility.** Canva exports processed clips as standard MP4, or as a layer composited directly onto other Canva elements — useful for talking-head overlays and product demos where you want a subject floating over a different scene.

**Bundled with Canva's broader AI suite.** Because it lives inside Canva Pro, the same subscription unlocks Magic Studio features like Magic Eraser, Magic Resize, and text-to-image generation, which matters if you'd use those tools anyway.

**No coding, no manual rotoscoping.** A clip that would take an editor several minutes of manual masking per shot can be processed automatically — though edges aren't always frame-perfect on complex footage; hair, motion blur, and busy backgrounds remain the classic failure points for any AI matting tool, and this one is not immune.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and social-media managers** making short-form video (Reels, TikToks, Shorts) who want to swap backgrounds without a physical studio setup — Canva Pro's monthly cost is easy to justify if you're publishing regularly.
- **Small marketing teams** already using Canva for graphics who want background removal in the same tool instead of adding a separate app — Canva Teams adds shared brand assets and approval flows.
- **Freelance video editors on a budget** doing quick client turnarounds without a green screen — a real time-saver for talking-head clips and quick promos, though not a substitute for professional chroma-key work on demanding footage.
- **Anyone hoping for a free, no-account, no-subscription tool** the way the old Unscreen site briefly offered — that version doesn't exist anymore. Free-plan users get limited access at best.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| No green screen or manual masking needed for most clips | No longer a dedicated free-standing tool — it's now bundled inside Canva Pro |
| Sits inside a full editor, so you can build the rest of the video in the same place | Edge quality on hair, fast motion, and busy backgrounds can still be inconsistent, like most AI matting tools |
| Bundled subscription unlocks Canva's other AI design/video tools, not just this one feature | Exact free-tier limits and pricing aren't always clearly documented and change over time |
| Backed by Kaleido AI's segmentation technology, the same team behind remove.bg | Not built for professional VFX-grade chroma-key work on complex footage |
| Works on ordinary phone-shot footage, not just studio setups | Requires a Canva account and, for full use, a paid subscription |

## Integrations and ecosystem

The video background remover doesn't have its own standalone API — it's a feature inside the Canva app, not a developer product. Canva as a platform does offer broader integrations worth knowing about if you're evaluating the whole subscription:

- Canva's Content Planner can schedule and publish finished videos directly to social platforms (Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn) from inside the app.
- Cloud-storage integration (Google Drive, Dropbox) for importing raw footage and exporting finished clips.
- Canva Enterprise/Teams plans add SSO and brand-control integrations for larger organizations, though these aren't specific to this feature.
- There is no Zapier-style automation trigger tied to the background remover — if you need batch-processing many clips programmatically, this tool isn't built for that.

## Where it's a strong fit

- Quick social-media edits where you need a subject cut out of a background without a green-screen setup.
- Teams already paying for Canva Pro for graphics work, where adding video background removal costs nothing extra.
- Product demo or talking-head videos shot on a phone or webcam, where "good enough" edge quality is fine and speed matters more than pixel-perfect matting.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a genuinely free tool with no subscription.** The free Unscreen experience has been folded into Canva Pro; if budget is the deciding factor, expect more manual work with a free/open-source alternative in exchange.
- **If you need broadcast- or VFX-grade keying.** This is an AI convenience tool for social and marketing content, not a substitute for professional chroma-key software on footage with fine detail (flyaway hair, transparent objects, fast pans).
- **If you need programmatic/batch processing via an API.** There's no developer-facing endpoint; it's a manual, one-clip-at-a-time workflow inside the editor.
- **If your organization needs strict data-residency or on-prem processing.** Clips are processed on Canva's servers — confirm compliance requirements directly with Canva's enterprise team rather than assuming either way.

## The bottom line

Video Background Remover, in the form most people are actually looking for today, is Canva's in-editor AI background-removal feature — the direct successor to Unscreen after Canva's 2021 acquisition of Kaleido AI. It's fast, needs no green screen, and is genuinely convenient for everyday social and marketing video, especially if you're already inside Canva for graphics. The catch: it's no longer free-standing — full use requires Canva Pro — and edge-case footage (hair, motion blur, cluttered backgrounds) can still trip up the AI. Good pick for quick, decent removal bundled with a broader toolkit; less so if you wanted the old free Unscreen experience or professional-grade keying.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Unscreen still a separate tool from Canva?**
No. Unscreen's domain redirects to Canva's video background remover feature page. Canva acquired Kaleido AI, Unscreen's parent, in 2021, and there's no independently operating Unscreen product left — the technology lives inside Canva.

**Is Video Background Remover free?**
Canva's free plan allows some limited use of AI features like this one, but full, repeated use is generally reserved for Canva Pro subscribers. Confirm the exact free-tier cap on Canva's current pricing/help pages, since limits change.

**Do I need a green screen to use it?**
No — that's the core advantage of the AI segmentation technology. It detects and separates a subject from an ordinary background without a physical green screen, though results are cleaner with good lighting and a distinct subject.

**How good is the edge quality compared to manual masking?**
Good enough for most social and marketing content, but not flawless. Like other AI matting tools, it can struggle with flyaway hair, fast motion, or backgrounds similar to the subject. For demanding professional work, manual chroma-key/rotoscoping still generally out-performs automatic AI removal.

**Can I use it outside of Canva's editor?**
No — it's a feature inside the Canva platform, not a standalone uploader or API. If you need a dedicated utility outside a full design suite, look at other AI video tools.

**What happens to my video footage during processing?**
Video is uploaded to Canva's servers for AI processing, as with any cloud-based editing feature. If you have strict data-handling requirements, confirm Canva's current retention/privacy practices before uploading sensitive footage.

**Are there good alternatives if this doesn't fit my budget or use case?**
Yes — [Runway AI](/blog/runway-review) covers more advanced AI video generation/editing, and [Submagic](/blog/submagic-review) covers AI-assisted short-form video captioning. Neither is a direct swap for background removal, but both are worth comparing if you're evaluating your broader video-tool stack.

**Is this tool beginner-friendly?**
Yes, relative to manual video editing. It's built into Canva's drag-and-drop interface, so there's little learning curve for the removal step itself — the bigger curve, if any, is getting comfortable with Canva's editor overall.

For other current AI software offers, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: My AskAI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is My AskAI worth it for helpdesk automation? We break down its per-ticket pricing, Zendesk/Intercom integrations, and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is My AskAI worth it for automating customer support?

My AskAI is a solid pick if you already run a helpdesk (Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, Gorgias, HubSpot) and want an AI agent that drafts or auto-resolves tickets inside that existing system rather than replacing it. It's less useful if you just want a simple website chat widget with no helpdesk behind it, or if a flat per-ticket bill of $199+/month is too steep for your support volume.

### At a glance

| | My AskAI |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $199/month (Pro plan, 1,000 tickets included) |
| Free tier/trial | 30-day free trial, no credit card required |
| Best for | Support teams already on Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, Gorgias, Freshchat or HubSpot |
| Standout feature | Trains on your help center, docs, and historic tickets, then drafts or auto-sends replies inside your current helpdesk |

## What My AskAI actually is

My AskAI is a customer-support AI agent (running under the My AskAI name since 2023, originally a simpler "ask questions about my content" chatbot builder before pivoting into helpdesk automation). Instead of ripping out your existing support stack, it installs as an approved app inside Zendesk, Intercom, Gorgias, Freshdesk, Freshchat, or HubSpot and works from there — reading incoming tickets, drafting or sending replies, and tagging conversations using your existing taxonomy.

The company doesn't publish which underlying language model does the reasoning. What it does publish clearly is the training pipeline: it ingests help center articles, website content, PDFs and other docs, plus — critically — your historic support tickets, so answers reflect how your team has actually resolved issues before, not just what's written in a knowledge base.

Worth flagging: My AskAI starts every new install in what it calls "internal-notes mode." The AI drafts replies privately for a human agent to review before anything goes live, and only moves to auto-sending once a team trusts the accuracy. That staged rollout differs from tools that go live in customer-facing chat from day one.

## My AskAI pricing

My AskAI prices per ticket resolved rather than per seat or per message credit, which is a different mental model from most AI chatbot tools and worth understanding before you commit.

| Plan | Price | Tickets included | Notable inclusions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pro | $199/month | 1,000/month (~$0.12/extra ticket up to 5,000) | 5 seats, up to 3 websites, historic-ticket training, AI self-learning, basic AI task automation, 95+ language support |
| Scale | $499/month | 2,000/month ($0.10/extra ticket, 15% cheaper than Pro) | Unlimited seats, up to 10 websites, multi-agent setup, SOC 2 Type II, branding removed, API/Slack/Teams access |
| Enterprise | From $999/month | Volume-based | Everything in Scale plus dedicated success manager, white-glove onboarding, <3-hour priority support, whitelabel/API access |

There's a 30-day free trial with no credit card required, a useful window to test resolution quality on your own ticket backlog before committing. My AskAI's pricing page frames its per-ticket cost as "5–8x cheaper" than native AI add-ons from Zendesk or Intercom's Fin — that's a vendor comparison against named competitors, so treat it as a starting point rather than a guaranteed multiple, since actual savings depend on your ticket volume and how many the AI fully resolves versus just drafts.

Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability described here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current tiers on My AskAI's official pricing page before buying.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Native helpdesk integration, not a bolt-on widget.** My AskAI installs inside Zendesk, Intercom, Gorgias, Freshdesk, Freshchat, and HubSpot as an approved marketplace app. Agents keep working in the tool they already know; the AI operates as another "agent" in the queue rather than a separate widget bolted onto your site.

**Training on historic tickets, not just docs.** Most competitors train exclusively on help-center articles and website content. My AskAI also ingests your resolved-ticket history, so it can pick up on how your team phrases refund policies, escalation language, and edge-case answers that never made it into official documentation.

**AI Copilot Chrome extension.** For teams that want a human in the loop everywhere, not just on AI-handled tickets, the Chrome extension surfaces draft replies and relevant context across every ticket an agent opens — including ones the AI isn't automatically resolving.

**Task automation beyond answering questions.** Beyond drafting replies, My AskAI advertises performing actions like order lookups, refunds, and cancellations when connected to live account/order data — moving it from a pure Q&A tool into a limited support-automation layer.

**Resolution-rate reporting.** My AskAI states an average AI resolution rate of 75% across its customer base, with some accounts exceeding 85%; it cites named customers (Edel Optics at 79%, TravelJoy improving from 24% on Zendesk's native AI to 80%). These are vendor-published case-study figures, not independently audited numbers, so treat them as directional for your own ticket mix.

## Who it's actually for

**Small support teams on a mainstream helpdesk.** If you already run Zendesk, Intercom, Gorgias, Freshdesk, Freshchat, or HubSpot and get a steady volume of repetitive tickets, the Pro plan's 1,000 tickets/month and 5 seats is a reasonable entry point to test AI resolution without a big commitment.

**Growing e-commerce or SaaS support operations.** The Scale plan's multi-agent setup, 10-website allowance, and API/Slack/Teams access suit teams juggling several brands or product lines under one support umbrella, where ticket volume is already past a few thousand a month.

**Larger or compliance-sensitive organizations.** Enterprise unlocks SOC 2 Type II (available from Scale up), white-label options, and a dedicated success manager — relevant for companies that need to show auditors their AI vendor meets a specific security bar, or that want the tool fully invisible to end customers.

**Not a fit for teams without a helpdesk already.** If you don't use one of My AskAI's supported platforms, or just want a lightweight chat widget for a small marketing site, a standalone website widget (see our [SiteSpeakAI review](/blog/sitespeakai-review)) is a more natural starting point.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Works inside your existing helpdesk instead of replacing it | Only supports six specific helpdesk platforms — no generic embed for arbitrary CMS/site setups |
| Trains on historic tickets for more on-brand answers | Per-ticket pricing can climb quickly for high-volume support teams |
| "Internal-notes mode" lets you validate accuracy before going live to customers | $199/month entry price is high next to lightweight website-chatbot tools |
| Task automation (refunds, order lookups) beyond just answering questions | Underlying AI model isn't publicly disclosed |
| SOC 2 Type II certification available from the Scale tier up | SOC 2 and branding removal are gated behind the $499/month plan, not Pro |
| 30-day free trial with no credit card required | Resolution-rate stats are self-reported vendor case studies, not third-party audited |

## Integrations and ecosystem

My AskAI's integration story is narrow and deep rather than broad and shallow. It plugs directly into six named helpdesk platforms — Zendesk, Intercom, Gorgias, Freshdesk, Freshchat, and HubSpot — via approved marketplace apps, so the AI shows up as a native part of the ticket workflow your agents already use, complete with existing macros, tags, and routing rules, rather than a separate inbox to check.

Scale and Enterprise plans add API access plus Slack and Microsoft Teams connectivity, useful for routing escalations wherever your team already communicates. There's no general-purpose Zapier connector documented publicly, so if your stack includes a helpdesk My AskAI doesn't support, verify direct compatibility before signing up.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You already run one of the six supported helpdesks and have a real backlog of tickets to train on
- You want a staged rollout — AI drafts first, full automation once trust is established — rather than going live in customer chat immediately
- Your support volume justifies per-ticket pricing (a few thousand tickets a month or more) rather than a flat per-seat SaaS fee
- You need actions taken (refunds, cancellations, lookups), not just answers drafted

## Where to think twice

- If you need a fully free tool for basic Q&A, My AskAI isn't it — pricing starts at $199/month after the trial, with no permanent free tier
- If your website doesn't sit behind one of the six supported helpdesks, look at a standalone chatbot-widget product instead
- If your ticket volume is small and sporadic, the flat $199 floor may cost more per resolved ticket than a lower-volume, seat-based competitor
- If you need the underlying AI model named explicitly for a compliance review, My AskAI's public materials don't specify it — you'd need to ask their sales team directly
- If you're evaluating resolution-rate claims for a board presentation, treat the published 75%/85% figures as vendor case studies to validate with your own pilot, not as guaranteed outcomes

## Bottom line

My AskAI earns its price by doing one thing well: sitting inside a helpdesk you already use and getting measurably better at answering tickets as it learns from your history, rather than asking your team to learn a new inbox. The per-ticket pricing is honest about what you're paying for, but it also scales with support volume in a way flat-fee tools don't, so run the 30-day trial against a real month of tickets before committing to Pro or Scale. Teams outside its six supported helpdesks, or wanting a bargain generic chatbot, should look elsewhere.

## FAQ

**Is My AskAI free?**
No. There's a 30-day free trial with no credit card required, but after that the cheapest plan is Pro at $199/month for 1,000 tickets.

**What helpdesks does My AskAI work with?**
Zendesk, Intercom, Gorgias, Freshdesk, Freshchat, and HubSpot, via approved marketplace apps. There's no generic widget for arbitrary websites without one of these platforms.

**Does My AskAI reply to customers automatically, or just draft replies?**
Both, depending on how you configure it. New installs typically start in "internal-notes mode," where the AI drafts replies for a human to review, and can be switched to sending replies automatically once you're confident in accuracy.

**What data does My AskAI train on?**
Help center articles, website content, uploaded documents, and — distinctively — your historic support tickets, so it can match how your team has actually resolved similar issues before.

**Is My AskAI SOC 2 compliant?**
SOC 2 Type II certification is listed as included from the Scale plan ($499/month) upward; it isn't included on the base Pro tier.

**How is pricing calculated?**
Per ticket resolved rather than per seat: $199/month covers 1,000 tickets on Pro, with extra tickets billed at roughly $0.12 each up to 5,000; Scale drops the overage rate to about $0.10 per ticket.

**What's a good alternative if I don't use a supported helpdesk?**
A standalone website chatbot builder that doesn't require an existing helpdesk, such as the tool covered in our [SiteSpeakAI review](/blog/sitespeakai-review), is a closer fit if you want an embeddable widget rather than helpdesk-integrated automation.

**Are the resolution-rate numbers (75%, 85%) verified?**
No — they're figures My AskAI publishes from its own customer base and named case studies. They're a reasonable benchmark to ask about during a trial, but not an independently audited statistic.
