title: Pixlr Review 2026: AI Photo Editor Pricing and Verdict
excerpt: Pixlr pairs a free browser photo editor with credit-based AI tools for background removal, generative fill, and image generation. Here's if it's worth it.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Pixlr worth it for AI photo editing?

Pixlr is a browser-based photo editor that pairs classic tools (crop, layers, adjustments) with a credit-metered set of AI features — background removal, generative fill, object removal, upscaling, and text-to-image generation. It's a reasonable pick if you want AI editing without installing Photoshop, but the free tier is thin and heavier AI use pushes you into a subscription fast.

### At a glance

| | Pixlr |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Plus plan from $1.99/month billed yearly ($2.49 month-to-month) |
| Free tier | Free access to core editing tools; AI features run on a limited free credit allowance and are ad-supported |
| Best for | Casual editors, small e-commerce sellers, and social content creators who need quick background removal or touch-ups without a design background |
| Standout feature | A full credit-based AI toolkit (background/object removal, generative fill/expand, upscaling, face swap) bolted onto a free-to-start browser editor |

## What Pixlr actually is

Pixlr is a browser, mobile, and desktop photo-editing suite made by Pixlr Pte Ltd., and the company has been running the product for more than 15 years — long enough that a lot of people still remember it as a lightweight Photoshop alternative before "AI editing" was a category. That history is part of the pitch: Pixlr isn't a new AI startup racing to ship features, it's an established editor that has layered AI tools on top of tools it already had.

The suite is split across a few products. Pixlr X (also marketed as Pixlr Express) is the quick, one-click editor for fast crops, filters, and background removal. Pixlr E (Pixlr Editor) is the deeper, desktop-style editor with layers and more granular controls, positioned as its "advanced online photo editor." There's also a newer AI-agent-style surface for prompt-driven generation and editing. Pixlr doesn't publicly document which image-generation models power its text-to-image and generative-fill features — the pricing page just references "leading models" — so if the underlying model matters to your workflow, confirm that directly with Pixlr support before committing to a paid tier.

## Pricing

Pixlr sells access to its AI features through a credits system layered on top of a free base editor. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability below were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tool subscriptions move fast, so double-check the current numbers on Pixlr's own pricing page before buying.

| Plan | Monthly price | Annual price (per month) | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | $0 | Core editing tools (crop, adjustments, filters, layers in Pixlr E); a limited allotment of AI credits; ads shown in the interface |
| Plus | $2.49 | $1.99 | Ad-free editing, unlimited saves, 80 monthly AI credits, 1 concurrent AI generation |
| Premium | $9.99 | $7.99 | Everything in Plus, plus 1,000 monthly credits, 4 concurrent generations, access to all image/video/audio AI models, private mode, and the full font/template library |
| Ultra | $24.99 | $19.99 | Everything in Premium, plus up to 10,000 monthly credits, 8 concurrent generations, priority queue, and extended exports; Pixlr also advertises "unlimited fast image generations" on this tier, subject to a fair-use policy |
| Ultra MAX | $49.99 | $39.99 | Everything in Ultra with roughly double the monthly credits |

The credit system is the thing to actually pay attention to, not the sticker price. Pixlr's own estimates put Plus at around 80 "fast" AI images or 16 higher-quality ("pro") images per month — that's a low ceiling if you're doing more than the occasional background swap. Premium's 1,000 credits (roughly 200 pro-quality images) is where the plan starts to feel usable for regular content work, which also explains why Pixlr markets it as the "popular" tier rather than the cheaper Plus plan.

## Core features walkthrough

**AI background and object removal.** One-click background removal and object erasing are the features most casual users reach for first, and they're available even on lower tiers since they're comparatively cheap in credits. This is the feature set that competes most directly with dedicated tools like remove.bg or the background-removal features baked into Canva.

**Generative fill and expand.** Pixlr lets you select a region of an image and either replace it, add new content, or extend the canvas beyond its original borders (outpainting). This is the same category of feature Adobe popularized in Photoshop's Generative Fill, and it's credit-metered here rather than gated behind a separate paywall.

**Text-to-image generation.** Pixlr includes a prompt-driven image generator alongside the editing tools, so you can create a base image and then immediately touch it up in the same interface — a genuine convenience over juggling a separate generator and editor, though the output quality and prompt adherence will depend on whichever underlying model Pixlr routes your request to.

**Upscaling and enhancement.** Pixlr's "Super Scale" upscaler and noise/skin enhancement tools target the common case of taking a low-resolution or noisy photo (old product shots, phone photos in poor light) and cleaning it up for reuse — useful for sellers repurposing existing catalog images rather than generating new ones from scratch.

**Face swap and video/audio generation.** Newer additions extend the credit system into face-swapping and short-form AI video and audio generation, putting Pixlr in competition with more specialized generation tools for those specific tasks, though photo editing remains its core strength.

## Who it's actually for

- **Casual users and hobbyists** doing occasional touch-ups, cropping, or background swaps will likely get by on the free tier or Plus, since those tasks burn few credits.
- **Small e-commerce sellers** cleaning up product photos (background removal, upscaling, minor retouching) are a good fit for Premium, where the credit allowance covers a realistic monthly batch of listing images.
- **Social content creators and small agencies** producing a steady stream of generated or heavily edited visuals will want Premium or Ultra — the free and Plus tiers run out of credits quickly under that kind of volume.
- **Design teams needing brand consistency, approval workflows, or seat-based collaboration** are better served by a dedicated design platform like Canva or Adobe's suite; Pixlr is built around a single-user editing session, not team collaboration.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Runs entirely in the browser — no install, works cross-platform | AI features are credit-metered, and lower tiers run out fast under real use |
| Combines classic editing (layers, adjustments) with AI tools in one interface | Free tier is ad-supported and capped on AI credits |
| Broad AI toolkit: background/object removal, generative fill/expand, upscaling, face swap | Underlying AI models aren't publicly disclosed, making output quality hard to predict in advance |
| Long operating history (15+ years) versus AI-only startups | No visible team/seat-based collaboration features for agencies |
| Free-to-start pricing with a genuinely usable free editor for non-AI tasks | Jump from Plus to Premium (roughly 4x the price) is the point where AI use actually becomes practical for most people |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Pixlr is primarily a standalone web app, not a platform with a deep third-party integration ecosystem. It ships desktop and mobile apps alongside the browser editor and exports in standard image formats. It doesn't publicly document a general-purpose developer API, and there's no native Zapier or Slack integration listed on its site — confirm directly with Pixlr if API access or workflow automation is a requirement.

## Where it's a strong fit

Pixlr earns its place when the job is "edit a photo I already have" rather than "generate something from nothing." Background removal, cleanup, upscaling, and quick generative fixes on existing images are exactly what the free-to-cheap tiers are built for, and running in the browser means there's no software to install or update. For sellers managing a modest catalog of product photos, or creators doing occasional social graphics, the combination of a real editor plus AI shortcuts in one tab is genuinely convenient.

## Where to think twice

The credit system is the main thing to weigh before buying in. If you need more than light, occasional AI use, budget for Premium rather than Plus — the cheaper tier's 80 monthly credits disappear quickly once you're generating or heavily editing images regularly. Pixlr also isn't the right pick if you need a fully free AI editor with no caps; the free tier's AI allowance is limited and ad-supported. Teams that need seat management, shared brand libraries, or approval workflows should look at Canva or Adobe Express instead, since Pixlr is built for single-user sessions. And if the specific AI model behind a feature matters (for consistent style, for example), Pixlr's lack of public model disclosure makes results harder to predict than tools that name their model outright, such as Midjourney.

## The bottom line

Pixlr is a capable, browser-based photo editor that's genuinely useful for background removal, touch-ups, and light generative editing, backed by a company that's been doing this long enough to have ironed out the basics of a real editing interface. The free and Plus tiers are fine for occasional use, but anyone doing regular AI-assisted editing should plan on Premium to get a workable credit allowance. It's not a fit for teams needing collaboration features or developers needing API access, and the lack of disclosed underlying AI models means you're trusting Pixlr's routing rather than picking a model yourself. For solo creators and small sellers who want AI editing without a subscription to a heavyweight design suite, though, it's a sensible, low-commitment starting point.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Pixlr actually free to use?**
The base editor (Pixlr X and Pixlr E) is free to use for standard editing tasks like cropping, filters, and adjustments. AI features such as background removal, generative fill, and image generation run on a limited free credit allowance, and the free experience includes ads.

**How does Pixlr's credit system work?**
Each AI action consumes a set number of credits, with "fast" generations costing fewer credits than higher-quality "pro" generations. Paid plans include a monthly credit allowance (from 80 credits on Plus up to 10,000 on Ultra MAX) that resets each billing cycle.

**What's the cheapest way to get Pixlr's AI features?**
The Plus plan, at $1.99/month billed yearly, unlocks AI credits and removes ads, but its 80 monthly credits are only enough for light, occasional use — heavier users will find Premium's 1,000 credits more practical.

**Does Pixlr disclose which AI models it uses?**
No. Pixlr's marketing references "leading models" for image, video, and audio generation without naming them specifically. If model provenance matters for your use case, confirm details directly with Pixlr before subscribing.

**Is Pixlr good for beginners?**
Yes. Pixlr X's one-click tools (background removal, filters, quick adjustments) are built for users with no editing background, while Pixlr E offers more advanced, Photoshop-style controls for users who want them.

**Does Pixlr have a mobile app?**
Yes, alongside the browser editor, Pixlr offers mobile and desktop apps so editing isn't limited to a single device.

**What are the main alternatives to Pixlr?**
For pure background removal, tools like remove.bg are more narrowly focused. For AI image generation specifically, Midjourney and Leonardo AI are dedicated generation platforms rather than editors. For teams needing collaboration and brand kits alongside light AI editing, Canva is a common alternative.

**Does Pixlr offer a free trial of its paid plans?**
Pixlr's pricing page doesn't list a traditional free trial of paid tiers; instead, it offers an ongoing free tier with capped AI credits. Confirm current trial or credit-bonus promotions directly on Pixlr's pricing page, since these details change.

For more AI editing and creative tools, see our [Leonardo AI review](/blog/leonardo-ai-review) and [video background remover review](/blog/video-background-remover-review), or browse current [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: MagicSchool AI Review 2026: Pricing, Tools and Verdict

author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is MagicSchool AI worth it for teachers?

MagicSchool AI is worth it for most K-12 teachers who want AI help with lesson planning, feedback, and admin busywork — the free plan alone covers 80+ tools and a classroom chatbot, and the $8.33/month Plus tier removes generation limits. It's less compelling for districts needing deep LMS integration without an enterprise contract.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (Plus from $8.33/month billed annually) |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — 80+ tools, no credit card, permanent free plan |
| **Best for** | Individual K-12 teachers and school districts |
| **Standout feature** | Purpose-built library of 80+ education-specific AI tools |

MagicSchool positions itself as an "AI operating system for schools" rather than a general chatbot wrapper, and that framing matters — it's built around the actual paperwork and planning tasks teachers do every week, not a blank prompt box.

## What MagicSchool AI actually is

MagicSchool is a web platform built by Magic School, Inc. specifically for educators, students, and school administrators. Instead of handing teachers a generic chat interface and expecting them to write good prompts, it packages AI into single-purpose tools: pick "Lesson Plan Generator," fill in a short form (grade level, subject, standard, duration), and get a structured output back. The same pattern repeats across more than 80 teacher-facing tools and 50-plus student-facing ones on paid plans.

The company doesn't publish which underlying language model(s) power the platform on its marketing pages — it's most likely orchestrating calls to one or more third-party foundation models behind the scenes rather than running its own — so if the specific model matters to your workflow (for example, for citation or accuracy reasons), that's worth confirming directly with MagicSchool's support team rather than assuming.

MagicSchool has grown quickly in the K-12 space, positioning itself against general-purpose tools like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot by leaning on education context: FERPA-oriented data handling, student-safe outputs, and tools mapped to actual curriculum tasks.

## Pricing

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| **Free** | $0 forever | 80+ teacher tools, Raina chatbot, quiz generator, class writing feedback, basic support |
| **Plus** | $8.33/month billed annually ($12.99/month billed monthly) | Everything in Free, plus unlimited generations, unlimited output history, unlimited AI-output editing, 50+ student tools, student learning insights, early access to MagicSchool Labs |
| **Enterprise (district)** | Custom quote | Everything in Plus, plus SSO, SIS/LMS integrations (Clever, ClassLink, Canvas, Schoology), custom data privacy agreement, tool guardrails, admin dashboards, dedicated customer success manager, white-glove onboarding |

There's no store entry for MagicSchool AI on SmartFare at the time of writing, so these figures come directly from MagicSchool's own pricing page rather than a verified coupon listing — confirm current rates before buying, since AI-tool pricing and feature availability shift often. This information was accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026).

Individual teachers face effectively no financial barrier to trying it — the free tier isn't a crippled trial, it's a real permanent plan with dozens of usable tools. Plus mainly removes caps rather than unlocking hidden capability.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**A tool library instead of a prompt box.** The biggest practical difference between MagicSchool and using ChatGPT directly is that MagicSchool has already done the prompt engineering. The Lesson Plan Generator, Rubric Generator, IEP Generator, and Report Card Comment tool each ask for the specific inputs a teacher would naturally have on hand (grade, subject, standard, student name/goals) and return output formatted the way schools expect. That removes the "figure out the right prompt" step entirely.

**Raina, the education-scoped chatbot.** Rather than a general-purpose assistant, Raina is tuned to answer teaching and classroom-management questions and is available even on the free plan. It functions as a lighter-weight complement to the structured tools when a teacher has a one-off question that doesn't fit a specific generator.

**Student-facing tools with teacher oversight.** On the Plus and Enterprise tiers, MagicSchool extends into 50+ student tools (tutoring support, writing feedback, study aids) that teachers can assign, alongside "student learning insights" so educators can see how students are using the tools rather than handing them an unmonitored chatbot.

**IEP and differentiation support.** The IEP Generator and related differentiation tools address a genuinely time-consuming, high-stakes part of special education work. This is a niche that general AI tools don't address well out of the box, since IEP language has to follow specific legal and pedagogical conventions.

**District-grade guardrails on Enterprise.** For administrators, the Enterprise tier adds SSO, SIS/LMS integrations, and tool-level content guardrails — meaning a district can control which of the 80+ tools are available to which grade bands or departments, rather than giving every classroom unrestricted access.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo classroom teachers:** the Free plan is genuinely usable long-term for lesson planning, quizzes, and feedback — Plus is only necessary once you're generating frequently enough to hit output limits.
- **Small schools or single departments:** Plus at roughly $8–13/month per teacher is cheap enough for a department head to expense without going through procurement, especially compared to a full Copilot or ChatGPT Plus seat.
- **School districts and IT/curriculum leaders:** Enterprise is the realistic tier once you need SSO, Clever/ClassLink rostering, data privacy agreements, or the ability to restrict specific tools — this is not something to bolt on later informally.
- **Special education teams:** the IEP generator and differentiation tools make MagicSchool worth evaluating even for staff who otherwise wouldn't touch a general AI tool.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Real, permanent free tier with 80+ tools — not a time-limited trial | Underlying AI model(s) aren't disclosed, limiting transparency on quality/accuracy |
| Education-specific tools (IEPs, rubrics, standards-aligned lesson plans) save real prompt-engineering time | Some advanced/student tools are gated behind Plus or Enterprise |
| Plus tier is priced well below general AI subscriptions | District-level integrations (SSO, SIS/LMS) require an Enterprise quote, not self-serve |
| Purpose-built for classroom workflows, not repurposed general AI | Output still needs teacher review — AI-generated IEP or grading language carries real accuracy/compliance risk if used unedited |
| Data-privacy framing aimed at FERPA-conscious schools | No published on-prem or fully offline option |

## Integrations and ecosystem

MagicSchool's integration story is concentrated at the top of its plan structure. The Enterprise tier connects with common K-12 systems — Google Classroom and Google Docs, Canvas, Schoology, Clever, and ClassLink — plus Microsoft tooling and single sign-on. That means individual free or Plus users are mostly working inside MagicSchool's own interface rather than pushing content directly into their school's LMS; exporting to Google Docs/Slides format is the more accessible path for solo teachers.

There's no public general-purpose API documented on MagicSchool's marketing site, so this isn't a platform to build custom classroom software on top of — it's meant to be used directly by teachers and administrators.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You're a K-12 teacher who wants AI help with lesson plans, quizzes, rubrics, or feedback without building your own prompts from scratch.
- Your school or district needs education-specific data privacy handling rather than a general consumer AI subscription.
- You work in special education and need faster first drafts of IEP language or differentiated materials.
- You want to introduce students to AI tools under teacher oversight rather than an open, unmonitored chatbot.

## Where to think twice

- If your workflow depends on knowing exactly which foundation model is generating your content (for compliance, citation, or quality-control reasons), the lack of public model disclosure is a real gap — ask MagicSchool directly before committing at the district level.
- If you need deep LMS/SIS integration (Clever, ClassLink, Canvas, Schoology, SSO), that functionality sits behind a custom Enterprise quote, not a self-serve upgrade — budget time for a sales conversation, not just a credit card.
- If your district requires a signed, custom data privacy agreement as a hard requirement (common in larger or more litigation-conscious districts), that's also an Enterprise-only conversation, not something available on Plus.
- If you need a fully offline or self-hosted tool for network-restricted environments, MagicSchool is cloud-only.
- Skip it if you're looking for a general-purpose AI assistant for tasks outside the classroom — MagicSchool is deliberately narrow, and a broader tool like ChatGPT or Claude will serve non-teaching use cases better.

## The bottom line

MagicSchool AI earns its niche by turning AI into classroom-shaped tools instead of asking teachers to become prompt engineers. The free plan is generous enough that most teachers can justify trying it at zero cost, and Plus is priced well below general AI subscriptions for what it removes (usage caps, output history limits). Where it gets more complicated — and more expensive — is at the district level, where the integrations and privacy guarantees that matter for a large rollout live behind a custom Enterprise quote rather than a published price. Teachers evaluating this alone should treat Free and Plus as low-risk; administrators evaluating it district-wide should expect a sales process, not a self-serve checkout.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is MagicSchool AI free for teachers?**
Yes. MagicSchool offers a permanent free plan with 80+ teacher tools, the Raina chatbot, quizzes, and class writing feedback — it's not a time-limited trial, though it does cap output generation compared to the paid Plus tier.

**How much does MagicSchool AI Plus cost?**
Plus is listed at $8.33/month when billed annually, or $12.99/month billed monthly, as of this post's publish date. Confirm current pricing on MagicSchool's official pricing page, since AI tool pricing changes frequently.

**Does MagicSchool AI have a free tier limit?**
The free plan includes the full library of 80+ teacher tools but limits total generations and output history; Plus removes those caps entirely.

**Is MagicSchool AI safe for student data?**
MagicSchool markets itself around FERPA-conscious data handling and, at Enterprise, offers a custom data privacy agreement plus SOC 2-certified security. Districts with strict compliance needs should request specific data-handling documentation directly rather than relying on marketing claims.

**What AI model does MagicSchool AI use?**
MagicSchool doesn't publicly disclose the underlying language model(s). Ask MagicSchool's team directly if model transparency matters for your use case.

**What are the best alternatives to MagicSchool AI?**
General AI assistants like ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot can do similar tasks with manual prompting but lack MagicSchool's education-specific tool structure and IEP support. Other education-focused AI platforms exist too, so compare feature lists and pricing directly since this space evolves quickly.

**Is MagicSchool AI beginner-friendly for teachers with no AI experience?**
Yes — the form-based tools (fill in grade/subject/standard rather than write a prompt) are built for teachers with zero prior AI experience.

**Can students use MagicSchool AI directly?**
On Plus and Enterprise plans, teachers can assign 50+ student-facing tools, with learning insights so teachers can monitor usage — not available on the free plan.

title: Dippy AI Review 2026: Free Character Chat, Pricing
excerpt: Dippy AI offers free, unlimited AI character chat and image generation. Here's what it does, who makes it, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Dippy AI worth trying in 2026?

Dippy AI is a free character-chat and roleplay app from Impel Intelligence, Inc. that lets you talk to AI companions, build your own custom characters, and generate unlimited images inside the conversation. It's a solid pick if you want unrestricted chat and character creation at zero cost; it's a weaker fit if you need proven safety moderation, desktop access, or a company track record longer than a couple of years.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | Free (no paid tier currently offered) |
| Free tier/trial | Unlimited messages and unlimited image generation at no cost, per the developer |
| Best for | Solo users wanting AI companion chat, character creation, or casual roleplay on mobile |
| Standout feature | Fully open character creation plus unrestricted (17+) roleplay themes |

## What Dippy AI actually is

Dippy AI is a mobile-first AI companion and character-chat app made by Impel Intelligence, Inc., available on the App Store as "Dippy: Chat with AI characters" and through a companion web app at dippy.ai. It sits in the same category as Character.AI, Chai, Sakura AI, and Swerve — apps built around chatting with AI-generated personas rather than a general-purpose assistant like ChatGPT.

The pitch is simple: create or pick a character, and Dippy remembers your preferences, interests, and past conversation details over time. The app leans into "immersive" roleplay rather than productivity — its own App Store listing describes it as letting you "be unhinged or wholesome," and it carries a 17+ age rating from Apple alongside advisories for mild profanity, fantasy/realistic violence, and mature/suggestive themes. That combination (open-ended roleplay, no explicit content warnings excluded, mature rating) is worth noting upfront if you're evaluating this for a teenager or a shared device.

Dippy doesn't publish which underlying language model or models power its characters. Unlike Character.AI (its own in-house model) or apps that openly say they route to GPT or Claude, Dippy's public pages, app store listing, and terms of service don't name a specific LLM provider. Treat any claim about "the most advanced AI" in Dippy's own marketing as a vendor claim rather than a verified technical spec — if the underlying model matters to your decision (for instance, because you care about a specific provider's safety filtering), confirm directly with Dippy's support team before relying on it.

## Pricing — and why "free" needs a caveat

Dippy's own Terms of Service, current as of writing, state plainly: "As of the date of these Terms and for a limited period afterward, we currently offer a complimentary membership to access our Services." That's a meaningfully different promise than "this app is free forever." The same terms also reserve the right to change that membership-fee policy, with users notified if and when it happens.

In practice, as of this review, the app has no visible in-app purchase or subscription tier — no "Dippy Gold," no message caps, no paywalled image generation. That puts it in an unusual position: most rivals in this category (Character.AI, Chai, Sakura AI) already gate faster responses, extra image generation, or ad-free chat behind a paid tier, typically somewhere in the $5–$15/month range. Dippy currently doesn't, which is either a genuine differentiator or a sign the business model isn't finalized yet — both are true simultaneously.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free (current, only tier) | $0 | Unlimited messages, unlimited image generation, character creation, community character browsing |

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (2026-09-18) and can change quickly in this category — confirm current terms directly in the app or at dippy.ai before assuming today's free-for-everyone model still applies.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

- **Open character creation.** Anyone can build a character from scratch — name, personality, backstory, appearance — and choose to keep it private or publish it for the community to interact with. This is table stakes for the category now, but Dippy doesn't gate it behind a paywall the way some competitors do for advanced customization fields.
- **Persistent memory claims.** Dippy's listing says characters "actively learn more about you and have perfect memory" of prior conversations. This is a vendor claim about memory persistence, not an independently verified benchmark — treat it as directional rather than a guaranteed spec, since "perfect memory" is a strong claim for any consumer chat app.
- **Unlimited in-chat image generation.** Users can prompt for illustrations inside a conversation with no stated cap, which is generous compared to apps that ration image credits even on paid tiers.
- **Mood-reactive illustrations.** The app generates "cool illustrations that showcase their mood based on what they're thinking," a lightweight visual layer most text-only competitors skip.
- **Fifteen customization colors and full character naming**, letting you personalize the chat UI itself rather than just the character.

## Who it's actually for

- **Casual companion-chat users** who want a free way to talk to an AI persona without hitting a message wall — Dippy's unlimited free messaging is a real advantage over apps that throttle free users after a daily cap.
- **Hobbyist character creators** who want to build and share personas without paying for advanced customization — this is open to everyone on the free tier right now.
- **Adults comfortable with unmoderated-leaning roleplay** — the 17+ rating and lack of a published content-moderation policy in its privacy notice suggest looser guardrails than, say, Character.AI's more heavily filtered chat.
- **Not a fit** for anyone needing a desktop app (it's mobile/web-first), enterprise or team use, verified data-handling certifications, or a paid tier with guaranteed feature stability — since Dippy's own terms flag that free access is time-limited, not permanent.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Currently free with no message or image caps | No published content-moderation or NSFW policy in its privacy notice |
| Fast, open character creation for all users | Underlying AI model(s) not disclosed publicly |
| 4.3-star rating across roughly 2,378 App Store reviews | Its own terms state free access is temporary, not guaranteed long-term |
| Active development (multiple 2026 releases, bug-fix updates) | No desktop app; web version is limited compared to mobile |
| Community character browsing adds variety without paying | Young company (Impel Intelligence, Inc.) with a shorter track record than category leaders |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Dippy is largely a closed, standalone experience — there's no public API, no Zapier/Slack integration, and no third-party plugin ecosystem to speak of, which is typical for consumer companion-chat apps in this category (Character.AI and Chai are similarly closed). Support is handled directly by email (support@dippy.ai) rather than a help center or live chat, and the company runs a presence on the App Store and Google Play rather than offering a browser extension or API tier for developers. If you need programmatic access to build on top of a character-chat model, this isn't the tool — look toward a general LLM provider's API instead.

## Where it's a strong fit

Dippy earns its download if you specifically want free-form character roleplay without hitting a paywall on day one. The unlimited free messaging and image generation are genuinely rare in this category at zero cost, and the character-creation tools are open to everyone rather than reserved for paying users. If your main use case is casual companion chat, worldbuilding with a custom character, or exploring roleplay scenarios on your phone, Dippy delivers that without asking for a credit card.

## Where to think twice

Skip Dippy if you need documented content-safety guardrails for a younger user or a shared/managed device — the 17+ rating, mature-theme advisories, and absence of a published moderation policy mean you're trusting the app's default settings rather than a transparent, audited system. Also think twice if you want assurance the free tier survives long-term: Dippy's own terms explicitly reserve the right to introduce fees, so budgeting on "this stays free forever" isn't safe. And if data-handling certifications (SOC 2, GDPR-specific tooling) matter for your use case, Dippy's privacy policy doesn't detail that level of compliance infrastructure — confirm directly with support if it's a requirement. Finally, if you want a named, verifiable underlying model (for trust or capability reasons), Dippy isn't transparent about that the way some competitors are.

## Bottom line

Dippy AI is a capable, currently-free entrant in the AI companion/character-chat space, built by a small team (Impel Intelligence, Inc.) rather than a category giant like Character.AI. Its unlimited free messaging and image generation, combined with open character creation, make it worth trying if that's the kind of app you're after — but go in aware that "free" here is explicitly framed as temporary in its own terms, and that neither its underlying AI model nor its content-moderation approach is disclosed in detail. Treat it as a fun, low-commitment app to test rather than one to build a paid workflow or long-term expectation of unlimited access around.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Dippy AI actually free?**
Yes, as of this review there's no paid tier, message cap, or image-generation limit. However, Dippy's own Terms of Service describe this as a "complimentary membership" offered "for a limited period," and the company reserves the right to introduce fees later, so don't assume it stays free indefinitely.

**Who makes Dippy AI?**
Dippy is developed by Impel Intelligence, Inc., listed as the seller on both the App Store and in Dippy's privacy policy.

**What AI model does Dippy use?**
Dippy doesn't publicly name the language model(s) powering its characters in its marketing, app store listing, or terms of service. If the specific model matters to you, ask Dippy support directly rather than assuming a particular provider.

**Is Dippy AI safe for teenagers?**
No — the app carries a 17+ rating on the App Store with advisories for mild profanity, fantasy and realistic violence, and mature/suggestive themes. Its privacy policy also states the service isn't directed at users under 16. It isn't designed or positioned as a teen-safe product.

**Does Dippy AI have a website version?**
Yes, dippy.ai offers a web-based version alongside the iOS and Android apps, though the mobile app is the more actively marketed experience.

**How does Dippy AI compare to Character.AI or Chai?**
All three let you chat with and create AI characters. Character.AI uses more heavily filtered, in-house models and has a much larger user base; Chai leans into character variety with voice options. Dippy's main differentiator right now is that it has no paywall at all, while Character.AI and Chai both gate some features behind subscriptions.

**Can I create my own character on Dippy?**
Yes, character creation is open to all users, whether you keep the character private or publish it for the community to interact with.

**Does Dippy AI have a data privacy policy?**
Yes, Dippy publishes a privacy policy and terms of service (linked from dippy.ai) that describe what data is collected and how long it's retained, but they don't detail specific compliance certifications like SOC 2 or a formal content-moderation framework — confirm directly with the company if that level of detail matters for your use case.

title: Freed AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Freed AI turns patient visits into clinical notes. Here's a hands-on look at pricing tiers, EHR integration, and who it's actually built for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Freed AI worth it for clinicians?

Freed is an AI medical scribe that listens to patient visits and drafts clinical notes. It's a solid pick for a solo clinician or small practice drowning in charting: HIPAA-compliant, works across 30+ specialties, and starts at $39/month. It doesn't store recordings or replace clinical judgment — every note still needs review before it goes in the chart.

### At a glance

| | Freed AI |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $39/month (Starter, billed annually) |
| Free tier / trial | 7-day free trial, no credit card required |
| Best for | Solo clinicians and small clinics wanting ambient note-taking |
| Standout feature | One-click push of finished notes into browser-based EHRs |

## What Freed AI actually is

Freed is an ambient AI scribe built specifically for outpatient medicine. You open the app (web or mobile) before a visit, hit record, talk to your patient like normal, and Freed turns the conversation into a structured clinical note formatted the way you already chart — SOAP, H&P, or a custom template. It was founded by Erez Druk, a software engineer, alongside Dr. Gabriella Meckler, a practicing physician, which explains why the product leans hard into templates for specific specialties rather than a generic "meeting notes" format.

The company doesn't publish which underlying language model powers its transcription and note generation. What Freed does state clearly is scale: more than 26,000 clinicians across 1,300+ clinics used the platform to document over 32 million patient visits in 2025, returning an estimated 5.9 million hours to clinicians annually. Those are Freed's own reported figures, not independently audited, so treat them as a scale claim rather than a verified statistic.

Freed covers family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, psychiatry and mental health, OB/GYN, functional medicine, and nurse practitioners by name, with 30+ specialties total according to the company.

## Pricing

Freed uses four tiers, and — like a lot of SaaS pricing pages — the sticker price depends on whether you pay monthly or commit to a year upfront. Here's what the current pricing page shows:

| Plan | Monthly billing | Annual billing (per month) | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $59/month | $39/month | Up to 40 notes/month, AI scribe, specialty templates, live support |
| Core | $79/month | $59/month | Unlimited notes, instant template builder, cited clinical-evidence answers |
| Premier | $119/month | $104/month | Everything in Core, plus visit summaries, patient instructions/letters, one-click EHR integration, dictation, ICD-10/CPT coding |
| Groups | Custom | Custom | Everything in Premier, plus medical assistant seats, note sharing, SSO, admin dashboards, dedicated account manager |

A few things to flag before picking a tier. The jump from Starter to Core isn't just "unlimited notes" — Core also unlocks the clinical-evidence lookup tool, arguably the bigger upgrade for some clinicians. EHR integration and coding assistance (ICD-10/CPT/E&M) are gated behind Premier, so if push-to-EHR is why you're evaluating an AI scribe, budget for the top individual tier. Freed also offers free access to residents, students, and trainees through a pilot program, plus a 50% discount for students who apply directly.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI scribe pricing has moved more than once in the past year as competitors like Abridge, Nabla, and Heidi Health have entered the same market, so confirm current numbers on [Freed's own pricing page](https://www.getfreed.ai/pricing) before committing to an annual plan.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Ambient transcription that doesn't require a wake word or a pause.** You start the recording, talk to the patient normally — tangents included — and Freed's note generation filters out the small talk. This is table stakes for the category now, but Freed's templates are noticeably tuned per specialty rather than one generic SOAP format stretched across every visit type.

**Clinical Evidence tool.** Available from Core up, this surfaces cited answers pulled from what Freed describes as 50+ trusted medical sources, directly inside the charting workflow. It's positioned as a quick reference, not a diagnostic tool — Freed doesn't market it as a substitute for UpToDate or formal clinical decision support.

**One-click EHR push.** On Premier and above, finished notes push directly into browser-based EHR systems instead of requiring copy-paste. This matters more than it sounds — copy-paste between a scribe app and an EHR is where a lot of ambient-scribe time savings quietly evaporate, so gating this behind the top tier is a real cost consideration.

**Automated coding suggestions.** Premier also adds ICD-10, CPT, and E/M code suggestions generated from the visit note — useful for solo practitioners without a dedicated coder, but it's a suggestion engine, not a compliance guarantee. Codes still need sign-off from whoever is accountable for your billing.

**Front Desk AI (separate add-on).** Freed also sells a front-desk product handling inbound calls, appointment requests, and message triage, with multilingual support mentioned for that product. It's a separate line of business from the core scribe and isn't included in the scribe tiers above.

## Who Freed AI is actually for

- **Solo clinicians and small independent practices** — Starter and Core are priced and scoped for one clinician, and Starter's 40-notes-a-month cap is realistic for a part-time or lower-volume practice.
- **High-volume outpatient clinicians** — Core's unlimited notes plus Premier's EHR push and coding assistant suit clinicians seeing a full patient panel daily who need the administrative time back.
- **Small group practices** — the custom Groups tier adds admin dashboards, SSO, and note sharing across medical assistants and clinicians, useful once you're managing more than one or two users.
- **Residents, students, and trainees** — free pilot access and a 50% student discount make this one of the few AI scribes with a genuine student-friendly path.
- **Not a fit for hospitals or large health systems** needing deep, bidirectional EHR integrations beyond browser-based note push, formal enterprise procurement, or a scribe embedded in existing hospital IT infrastructure — those buyers should talk to Freed's sales team directly.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Fast note turnaround from ambient recording | EHR integration and coding assistant locked behind the top tier |
| Specialty-specific templates, not one generic format | No published detail on which AI model powers transcription |
| HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified, no stored recordings | Groups pricing is fully custom, no self-serve number above 1 seat |
| Free access program for residents/students/trainees | Every note still requires clinician review, not autopilot |
| 7-day free trial, no credit card | Verified independent review data is harder to find than for established EHR vendors |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Freed's main integration story is the one-click push into browser-based EHR systems on Premier and above — Freed doesn't publish a full public list of which specific EHR platforms are supported at that level, so if you're on a specific EHR (Epic, athenahealth, DrChrono, etc.), confirm compatibility before upgrading for that feature alone. There's no public API for third-party developers and no Zapier or Slack connector — this is a purpose-built clinical tool, not a general-purpose automation platform.

## Where it's a strong fit

Freed is a strong fit if you're a clinician spending evenings finishing charts, and your visits follow a fairly standard structure — annual exams, follow-ups, medication management, therapy sessions — where a specialty template can absorb most of the note structure. It's also a reasonable pick for a small practice trying to reduce documentation burnout without hiring a scribe or medical assistant, and for residents/students who can access it free or heavily discounted while building their charting speed.

## Where to think twice

Skip Freed, or at least trial it carefully first, if any of these apply to you:

- **You need a fully free, ongoing tool** — the 7-day trial is generous for evaluation, but there's no free tier for continued use outside the resident/student program.
- **Your organization needs deep, contract-backed EHR integration** at a hospital-system scale, formal enterprise SLAs, or a vendor security review beyond published SOC 2/HIPAA statements — Freed's public tiers target individual clinicians and small groups, not enterprise procurement.
- **You practice in a setting with unusual documentation requirements** — specialized procedural notes, forensic documentation, or workflows that don't map to Freed's templates may need more manual editing than the time savings justify.
- **You're uncomfortable with any ambient recording in the room** — even with no-recording-storage and HIPAA compliance, some practice settings require additional consent workflows Freed doesn't solve on its own.
- **You want visibility into the underlying AI model** for internal risk-assessment reasons — Freed doesn't publish this, and it's unlikely to change given how vendors in this space typically treat it as proprietary.

## Bottom line

Freed does what it says: it takes the conversation you'd already have with a patient and turns it into a note you'd otherwise have typed yourself, and it does that well enough that clinicians pay a recurring monthly fee for it rather than treating it as a novelty. The pricing rewards commitment — annual billing and the Premier tier are where the real value (EHR push, coding help, unlimited notes) lives — so a trial run is a fair way to judge fit before deciding whether Premier is worth it for your workflow. It isn't a substitute for clinical judgment, coding sign-off, or a full security review if you're buying for a larger organization, and Freed doesn't claim otherwise.

## FAQ

**Is Freed AI HIPAA-compliant?**
Yes. Freed states it's HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, and says it doesn't store patient audio recordings after a note is generated. For your own compliance sign-off, request Freed's current security documentation directly.

**Does Freed AI have a free plan?**
Not an ongoing free plan for general use. There's a 7-day free trial with no credit card required, plus a separate free-access pilot program for residents, students, and trainees, with a 50% discount for students who apply directly.

**How much does Freed AI cost?**
Individual plans run from $39/month (Starter, billed annually) up to $104–119/month (Premier, depending on billing cycle). Groups pricing for multi-clinician practices is custom.

**Which specialties does Freed AI support?**
Freed lists templates for family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, psychiatry/mental health, OB/GYN, functional medicine, nurse practitioners, and 30+ additional specialties, according to the company.

**Does Freed AI integrate with my EHR?**
On Premier and above, Freed offers one-click push of finished notes into browser-based EHR systems. It doesn't publish a full list of supported platforms, so confirm compatibility with your specific EHR before upgrading for that feature.

**Can Freed AI suggest billing codes?**
Yes, on the Premier tier — it suggests ICD-10, CPT, and E/M codes based on the visit note. These are suggestions for review, not a substitute for coding sign-off from whoever is accountable for your billing.

**What are the alternatives to Freed AI?**
Abridge, Nabla, Heidi Health, and DAX Copilot are the most commonly cited competitors in ambient clinical documentation. Each targets slightly different buyers — some lean more toward hospital-system deployments than solo-practice pricing — so compare EHR integration depth and per-seat pricing against your own practice size.

**Is Freed AI easy to learn for a non-technical clinician?**
Most onboarding materials describe a short learning curve — record a visit, review the drafted note, adjust templates as needed. The bigger adjustment is trusting the note enough to spend less time re-typing it, which typically takes a few visits.

title: Brainly Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
