author: Editorial Team
body:
## Brainly Review 2026: Is the AI Homework Helper Worth It?

Brainly is a homework-help platform that pairs a large crowdsourced Q&A archive with AI-generated step-by-step answers, now marketed mainly as an "AI + human tutor" service for K-12 families. It's a solid pick if you want instant, subject-spanning answers and don't mind a subscription; it's less useful if you specifically want a free tool or a chat-first AI tutor for open-ended studying.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free tier with limited features; paid "Brainly Tutor" plan marketed at "less than a dollar a day" (vendor-stated, confirm exact monthly total on the official pricing page) |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — free access with capped features; no fixed-length free trial publicly listed |
| **Best for** | K-12 students who want a quick answer to a specific homework question, backed by a large existing answer archive |
| **Standout feature** | Combination of a 15+ year crowdsourced Q&A database with AI-generated step-by-step explanations |

## What Brainly is, and where it came from

Brainly started in 2009 in Kraków, Poland, founded by Michał Borkowski, Tomasz Kraus, and Łukasz Haluch, as a peer-to-peer homework help community — students posted questions, other students and moderators answered, and the best answers got upvoted. That crowdsourced model built up one of the largest question-and-answer archives in education, and it's still the backbone of the product: search a question and there's a good chance someone already asked (and answered) something close to it.

The company has since layered AI on top of that archive rather than replacing it. According to Wikipedia's sourced account of Brainly's history, it integrated AI features built on OpenAI's GPT-4 in 2023, added an AI-generated Test Prep feature in 2024, and has been moving toward what it calls "agentic AI support" in the US market starting in 2025. Brainly doesn't publish granular technical detail about exactly which model versions power which features today, so treat "AI model" claims as the vendor's own framing rather than an independently verified spec sheet — this is worth confirming directly on Brainly's site if the specific model matters to you.

Brainly is privately held, headquartered between New York City and Kraków, and has raised roughly $150 million in funding as of 2020. Its App Store listing states it's "trusted by 15+ million parents," and carries an average rating of roughly 4.7 stars across more than 280,000 ratings — a figure from Apple's public app data rather than a number Brainly generated itself.

## Pricing

Brainly's own iOS App Store listing is one of the clearer public statements of its current pricing structure: "Access to Brainly is free with limited features. Upgrade to Brainly Tutor for the full experience including live human tutors," and separately, "Less than a dollar a day for unlimited access."

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Limited access to the Q&A archive and basic AI answers; capped features |
| Brainly Tutor (paid) | Marketed as "less than a dollar a day" (vendor-stated; works out to roughly $25–$30/month depending on billing cycle — confirm the exact current figure on Brainly's own pricing page) | Full AI homework help, unlimited use, plus access to live human tutors per the vendor's description |

Brainly has historically also sold a "Brainly Plus" tier separate from live tutoring in some markets, and pricing has varied by region and promotional bundling — don't assume an old review's quoted price still applies. We could not independently verify an exact current dollar figure beyond the "less than a dollar a day" framing Brainly itself uses, so check brainly.com directly before subscribing if the specific number matters for your budget.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability here were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI study-tool pricing and plan structures move quickly, and Brainly in particular has repositioned its paid tier (from "Brainly Plus" toward "Brainly Tutor") more than once in recent years.

## Features walkthrough

**Crowdsourced answer archive.** This is Brainly's original differentiator and it's still real: search a homework question and you'll often find it (or something close) already answered by another student or verified expert, going back over a decade. For common textbook questions, this can be faster than waiting on any AI to generate a fresh answer.

**AI step-by-step answers.** For questions without an existing match, Brainly generates an AI answer that walks through the solution rather than just stating a final result — similar in spirit to what [Photomath](https://photomath.com) does for math specifically, but Brainly covers more subjects (math, science, history, English, and more per its own listing).

**Photo/snap-a-question input.** Like most homework-helper apps in 2026, Brainly lets you photograph a problem instead of typing it out, which matters most for handwritten math and diagrams that are painful to retype.

**Live human tutors (paid tier).** This is Brainly's real point of differentiation from pure-AI competitors like TurboLearn AI or YouLearn AI — the paid "Brainly Tutor" plan bundles actual human tutors alongside AI support, not just a chatbot. Brainly's own marketing states a "100% money-back guarantee" and frames results as "real, qualified tutors backed by AI — not a chatbot pretending to teach," which is a vendor claim worth treating as marketing language rather than an audited outcome guarantee.

**Test Prep.** Added in 2024 per Brainly's public history, this generates practice questions and quizzes rather than just answering one-off homework questions — closer to what a dedicated study tool would offer, though it's a newer addition than the core Q&A feature.

## Who it's actually for

- **A K-12 student who needs quick help on a specific assignment tonight** — the archive-plus-AI combo is built for exactly this, and the free tier may cover occasional use.
- **A parent looking for something between "just an AI chatbot" and "hiring a real tutor"** — the paid Brainly Tutor tier is explicitly positioned in that middle ground, with human tutors layered onto AI.
- **A college or grad student doing open-ended research or paper writing** — this is a weaker fit. Brainly's archive and AI answers skew toward K-12 subjects and discrete homework questions, not long-form research synthesis or citation work; a general assistant like [ChatGPT](/blog/chatgpt-review) or [Claude AI](/blog/claude-ai-review), or a note-focused tool like [TurboLearn AI](/blog/turbolearn-ai-review), fits that use case better.
- **A student who wants an interactive AI tutor to talk through concepts (not just get an answer)** — [YouLearn AI](/blog/youlearn-ai-review)'s chat-first design is closer to that than Brainly's answer-lookup model.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Enormous existing archive of pre-answered questions across many subjects | Free tier is explicitly "limited features," and the exact caps aren't fully itemized on the public site |
| AI answers include step-by-step explanations, not just final results | Paid pricing is marketed as "less than a dollar a day" rather than a clear flat monthly number, making cost comparison harder |
| Unique combination of human tutors + AI on the paid tier | Historical honor-code concerns (e.g., a 2020 incident involving exam questions posted with answers) mean some schools discourage or block it |
| Long track record (founded 2009) and large user base (15M+ daily active users reported in 2024) | Brainly doesn't publish detailed specs on which AI model version powers which feature |
| Available in many languages/regions given its international roots | Skews toward K-12 homework; weaker fit for college-level research or long-form writing help |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Brainly is primarily a standalone consumer app (iOS, Android, and web) rather than a platform with a developer API or workflow integrations. There's no public API, no Zapier connector, and no Slack/Teams integration comparable to what some newer AI study tools offer through browser extensions that hook into Canvas or D2L. If integrating homework help into an existing LMS workflow matters to you, that's a real gap compared to tools built more recently around that use case.

## Where it's a strong fit

Brainly earns its keep for straightforward, subject-specific homework questions where a fast, correct-looking answer with an explanation is the goal — the classic "I'm stuck on question 7" scenario. The scale of its existing answer archive is a genuine advantage that newer AI-only competitors can't replicate overnight, since it's built on over a decade of contributed answers.

## Where to think twice

Skip Brainly if you specifically need a fully free tool with no caps — the free tier is explicitly described as feature-limited, and the paid tier's exact monthly cost isn't transparently listed as a flat number on the marketing pages. Also think twice if your school has flagged homework-help apps for academic integrity reasons; Brainly has had at least one public incident (a 2020 case involving competition-exam questions) that led to updated honor-code policies, and some teachers specifically watch for its use. If you want an AI tutor for open-ended conceptual conversations rather than answer lookups, or if you're past K-12 and doing research-heavy coursework, a general-purpose assistant or a note-and-quiz tool built for that will likely serve you better than Brainly's answer-archive model.

## Bottom line

Brainly's real advantage isn't a flashier AI model than its competitors — it's the sheer size of its existing answer archive combined with a genuinely differentiated paid tier that adds human tutors on top of AI, something most pure-AI study apps don't offer. If you're a K-12 student or parent who wants fast answers plus an option to escalate to a real tutor, it's a reasonable pick worth trying on the free tier first. If you want a free-forever tool, an open-ended AI study chat, or something built for college-level research, look elsewhere on this list of study tools.

## FAQ

**Is Brainly free?**
There's a free tier, but Brainly describes it as having "limited features." Full AI homework help plus live human tutors requires the paid Brainly Tutor plan.

**How much does Brainly cost?**
Brainly markets its paid tier as "less than a dollar a day for unlimited access," which implies roughly $25–$30/month depending on billing terms, but it doesn't publish one flat number prominently across all its marketing pages. Confirm the exact current price on brainly.com before subscribing.

**What AI model does Brainly use?**
Brainly's history (per Wikipedia's sourced account) shows it integrated AI features using OpenAI's GPT-4 starting in 2023 and has since described moving toward "agentic AI support." Brainly itself doesn't publish a detailed, up-to-date model spec sheet, so treat this as historical context rather than a live technical guarantee.

**Is Brainly safe and accurate for homework help?**
Answers come from a mix of community-contributed content (which can vary in quality despite moderation) and AI generation (which can be wrong or oversimplified, like any AI tool). Treat any Brainly answer as a starting point to verify against your own coursework, not a guaranteed-correct final answer.

**Does Brainly have privacy or academic-integrity concerns?**
Brainly has had at least one public incident (in 2020, involving American Mathematics Competition questions posted with answers) that led it to update its honor-code policies. Some schools discourage or restrict its use for that reason — check your school's policy before relying on it for graded work.

**Is Brainly good for college students?**
Not particularly. Its archive and features skew toward K-12 subjects and discrete homework questions rather than long-form research, citations, or open-ended academic writing. College students may get more out of [ChatGPT](/blog/chatgpt-review), [Claude AI](/blog/claude-ai-review), or a note-focused tool like [TurboLearn AI](/blog/turbolearn-ai-review).

**What are the alternatives to Brainly?**
For an interactive AI tutor you chat with rather than an answer-archive lookup, see our [YouLearn AI review](/blog/youlearn-ai-review). For turning lecture recordings into notes and flashcards, see our [TurboLearn AI review](/blog/turbolearn-ai-review). For a Chrome-extension-based instant-answer tool, see our [Mindko review](/blog/mindko-review).

**Can I use Brainly on mobile and desktop?**
Yes — Brainly has iOS and Android apps plus a web version, and its listings report large-scale usage (15+ million daily active users as of 2024 per Brainly's own reporting).

For more AI study and productivity tools worth comparing before you subscribe, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: QuestionAI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is QuestionAI worth using for homework help? We cover its photo-scan answers, pricing (hidden until checkout), and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is QuestionAI worth using for homework help?

QuestionAI is a free-to-download chatbot app (iOS, Android, web) that answers homework questions from a typed prompt, a photo, or an uploaded PDF, covering math, biology, history, social science, English, and business. It's a reasonable pick if you want a quick, no-setup answer to a single question on your phone — it's a weaker choice if you want structured study materials like flashcards, quizzes, or organized lecture notes, since that's not what it's built for.

## At a glance

| | QuestionAI |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | Free to download and use with limited daily questions; paid "Plus" tier priced in-app, not published on the marketing site |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — free tier lets you ask a capped number of questions per day before prompting an upgrade |
| Best for | Students who want a fast answer to one question at a time, from a phone camera or typed prompt |
| Standout feature | Photo-to-answer: snap a picture of a math problem (or any question) and get a worked answer in seconds |

## What QuestionAI actually is

QuestionAI is built by FlowMind Technology Inc., a Delaware-registered company, with the mobile app itself listed on the App Store under publisher D3 Dimension Technology Pte. Ltd. — a common setup where a regional entity handles app-store distribution for a product marketed under a different company name. The product is reachable at questionai.com and through iOS/Android apps branded "Question.AI - Math Calculator" and similar names.

Unlike a lot of AI study tools that stay quiet about their underlying model, QuestionAI's own App Store listing states its answers are "powered by DeepSeek V3." That's a specific, checkable claim from the vendor, though as with any AI model claim, treat it as what the vendor states rather than something independently verified against the app's live responses.

The core interaction is simple: type a question, upload a PDF, or take a photo of a printed or handwritten problem, and the app returns a text answer with (for math and science problems) a step-by-step breakdown. There's also a basic chat mode for general questions, a calculator, and a translation feature the app describes as supporting 140+ languages — useful if it's also used as a general-purpose assistant rather than strictly for schoolwork.

## Pricing

QuestionAI doesn't publish a public pricing page the way most SaaS tools do. Its own Terms of Use state only that "Plus services are available in monthly or yearly plan with multiple service level choices" and that actual prices are shown on "the value-added Services and in-app purchase page" — meaning the number you'll actually pay only appears once you hit a paywall inside the app itself, not on questionai.com.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Limited number of questions per day, photo scanning, basic chat |
| Plus (monthly) | Not published on the marketing site — shown at in-app checkout | Vendor states higher/unlimited daily question limits and priority answer speed |
| Plus (yearly) | Not published on the marketing site — shown at in-app checkout | Same Plus features billed annually, typically at a lower effective monthly rate for this style of app |

Refunds are handled under a stated 14-day window from the transaction date, and subscriptions renew automatically until cancelled at the end of the current billing period — standard app-store terms, nothing unusual to QuestionAI specifically.

Because the exact Plus price isn't disclosed publicly, don't take any third-party figure you see quoted elsewhere as current — check the in-app purchase screen for your region before subscribing. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability here were accurate as of this post's publish date (2026-09-18) and can change quickly, since subscription apps frequently adjust prices by region and promotion.

## Features walkthrough

**Photo-to-answer scanning.** Point your phone camera at a printed or handwritten question — a math problem, a multiple-choice item, a short-answer prompt — and QuestionAI returns a typed answer, usually with a worked-through explanation for math and science. This is the feature the app is built around, and it works without needing to retype anything.

**PDF upload.** You can upload a PDF (a worksheet, a reading, a problem set) instead of scanning page by page, which is faster for longer documents but works best when the PDF is a clean digital file rather than a scanned image with poor contrast.

**Multi-subject coverage.** QuestionAI's own site lists math, biology, history, social science, English, and business as covered subjects. That's a broad net for general homework help, though it also means no single subject gets specialized tooling (there's no dedicated citation manager for English essays, or graphing tool for advanced math, the way a subject-specific app might offer).

**General chat mode.** Beyond scanned homework questions, the app doubles as a general AI chatbot for open-ended questions, which is useful if a student wants one app for both "explain this equation" and "explain this historical event in a sentence," but it also means the product's focus is split between "homework solver" and "general assistant" rather than being purpose-built for one.

**Built-in translation.** The app advertises translation across 140+ languages, aimed at non-native English speakers working through English-language coursework or communicating across language barriers generally — a feature most single-purpose homework apps don't bother with.

## Who it's actually for

- **A student who needs a quick answer to one question right now** (a tricky algebra problem, a vocabulary definition, a quick fact-check) is the clearest fit — snap a photo, get an answer, move on.
- **A student juggling coursework in a non-native language** benefits from the translation layer more than a homework tool with no language features at all.
- **A student who wants organized study materials** — flashcards from a full lecture, spaced-repetition review, or auto-summarized notes — is better served by a tool built around that workflow (see the comparison below), since QuestionAI is optimized for one-off Q&A rather than ongoing review.
- **A teacher or parent evaluating academic-integrity risk** should know this app, like any instant-answer homework tool, can be used to bypass genuine problem-solving rather than support learning it.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Fast, simple photo-to-answer flow with no setup | No public pricing page — exact Plus cost only shown at in-app checkout |
| Names its underlying model (DeepSeek V3) rather than staying vague | No structured study tools like flashcards, spaced repetition, or lecture-to-notes conversion |
| Broad subject coverage (math, biology, history, social science, English, business) | Broad-but-shallow coverage means no subject gets specialized depth |
| Built-in translation across 140+ languages | Encourages one-off answer-getting over building understanding, which can hurt retention if used as a shortcut |
| Free tier available with no signup friction for a first try | Auto-renewing subscription model — easy to forget to cancel if you don't track the billing date |

## Integrations and ecosystem

QuestionAI is a standalone consumer app, not a platform with a developer ecosystem. There's no public API, no Zapier/Slack integration, and no LMS (Canvas, Google Classroom) integration documented on its site or app-store listings — fine for individual student use, but not something a school or tutoring service could wire into existing tools.

## Where it's a strong fit

QuestionAI earns its place for the narrow but common case of "I have one question right now and want an answer fast." The photo-scan flow removes the friction of retyping a problem, subject coverage is broad enough for most K-12 and intro-college coursework, and naming its model (DeepSeek V3) is more transparency than many competitors offer. The free tier is also usable for occasional questions rather than a locked demo.

## Where to think twice

Skip QuestionAI if you need real study-material generation — flashcards from a textbook chapter, spaced-repetition quizzes, or auto-generated lecture notes with timestamps — since that's simply not what this app does; a note-taking-first tool built for that workflow will serve you better. Also think twice if not knowing the exact subscription price until you're at the in-app paywall bothers you; most competitors publish a pricing page up front, and QuestionAI currently doesn't. And if you're a parent, teacher, or school weighing academic-integrity concerns, know that an instant photo-to-answer tool is easy to lean on as a shortcut rather than a learning aid — a real limitation of the category, not unique to QuestionAI, but worth factoring in before recommending it to a student.

## How QuestionAI compares to other AI study tools

QuestionAI is closest in spirit to [Mindko](/blog/mindko-review) — both are instant-answer tools for one question at a time, scanned or typed, rather than tools that generate ongoing study material. The practical difference: Mindko runs as a Chrome extension with a stated $19.99/month price after a 3-day trial, while QuestionAI is a mobile-first camera-scan app with a free daily-question tier and Plus pricing revealed only at in-app checkout.

If the actual goal is turning a recorded lecture, slide deck, or long PDF into organized notes, flashcards, and quizzes for ongoing review, [TurboLearn AI](/blog/turbolearn-ai-review) and [YouLearn AI](/blog/youlearn-ai-review) are built for that workflow specifically and will do it better than any instant-answer app — they're solving a different problem (studying over time) than answering one question right now.

## Bottom line

QuestionAI does one thing — answer a single homework question from a photo, a typed prompt, or a PDF — and does it with a low-friction free tier and a model claim (DeepSeek V3) it's willing to name. It's a sensible app for quick answers, but it's not a study-management tool, doesn't publish Plus pricing up front, and won't replace a note-taking or flashcard-focused app if that's what you actually need. Treat it as a fast lookup tool, not a study system.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is QuestionAI free to use?**
There's a free tier with a limited number of questions per day. A paid "Plus" tier removes some limits, but its exact price shows only at in-app checkout, not on the marketing site.

**What AI model does QuestionAI use?**
Its App Store listing states answers are powered by DeepSeek V3 — the vendor's own claim, not independently verified here.

**Does QuestionAI work for subjects beyond math?**
Yes — math, biology, history, social science, English, and business, plus a general chat mode for other questions.

**Can QuestionAI read a PDF instead of just photos?**
Yes, you can upload a PDF directly instead of photographing each page; it works best with clean digital PDFs rather than low-contrast scans.

**How does QuestionAI handle refunds?**
Its policy states refund requests must be submitted within 14 calendar days of the transaction date, reviewed under the policy and the payment provider's rules.

**Is QuestionAI good for building long-term study habits, like flashcards or spaced repetition?**
Not really — it's built for one-off answers, not ongoing review. A tool built around notes and flashcards, like TurboLearn AI or YouLearn AI, fits that need better.

**Who makes QuestionAI?**
FlowMind Technology Inc. operates questionai.com; the mobile app is listed under D3 Dimension Technology Pte. Ltd., a common app-store distribution arrangement.

**Is QuestionAI easy for a first-time user?**
Yes — no account setup is required to try the free tier, and the core flow (photo or text in, answer out) has no real learning curve.

Explore more [AI & software deals](/category/software) for other study and productivity tools, or read our related reviews of [Mindko](/blog/mindko-review), [TurboLearn AI](/blog/turbolearn-ai-review), and [YouLearn AI](/blog/youlearn-ai-review).

title: Relevance AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Relevance AI builds no-code AI agent workforces for teams — see its features, sales-gated pricing, integrations and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Relevance AI worth it for building AI agents?

Relevance AI is a no-code platform for building, orchestrating and monitoring autonomous AI agents that automate business workflows — a "digital workforce" that handles sales outreach, support tickets or research tasks. It's capable for teams wanting multi-agent automation without code, but pricing is now sales-gated with no published self-serve tier, a harder sell for solo builders or small budgets.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Starting price** | Not publicly listed — Enterprise plan requires contacting sales |
| **Free tier / trial** | Relevance Chat is usable with no setup; full agent builder access details require checking the live site |
| **Best for** | Sales, CS, marketing and ops teams automating multi-step workflows with several coordinated agents |
| **Standout feature** | Visual multi-agent orchestration with an LLM router that picks the cheapest model that still meets a performance bar |

## What Relevance AI actually is

Relevance AI is built by Relevance AI (the company shares its name with the product), and it positions itself less as "one chatbot" and more as a factory for building many narrow, purpose-built agents wired into a coordinated team — what it calls an "AI Workforce." The idea: a specialist agent tuned for, say, lead qualification outperforms a general model doing the same job, and costs less to run per task.

Under the hood, Relevance AI isn't tied to one model provider. Its documentation references support for Anthropic's Claude family, OpenAI's GPT models, Google's Gemini models, and additional providers like Kimi and GLM, routed through what the company calls an LLM router — a system that picks the model clearing a performance bar at the lowest cost for a given step, rather than always defaulting to the most expensive option. That's a different design choice from single-model tools like ChatGPT or Claude AI — see our [ChatGPT review](/blog/chatgpt-review) or [Claude AI review](/blog/claude-ai-review) if you're deciding between a single assistant and a full agent-building platform.

The building blocks are: **Agents** (individual AI workers), **Tools** (no-code building blocks for integrations and automations an agent can call), and **Workforces** (multiple agents coordinated into a team with a shared context layer, handovers and escalation paths). A marketplace lets you browse, clone and publish pre-built agents, tools and workforces instead of building from a blank canvas.

## Pricing

Relevance AI's public pricing page currently shows only an **Enterprise** tier, described as being for companies that want to "decouple growth from headcount via an AI Workforce." There's no visible price — you have to talk to sales to get a quote — and no self-serve Free/Pro/Team breakdown is published the way you'd see on, say, a [Zapier](/blog/zapier-review) or [Notion AI](/blog/notion-ai-review) pricing page. That's the single biggest thing to confirm before you invest time evaluating the product.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relevance Chat | Not specified | Usable with "no setup required" for quick, lighter-weight interactions |
| Enterprise | Custom — contact sales | Custom actions/vendor credits, unlimited agents/tools/users/projects/workforces, 2,000+ integrations, calling & meeting agents, enterprise triggers, agent evaluations, A/B testing, SSO/RBAC/audit logs, dedicated account manager |

Relevance AI states an average cost of roughly $0.09 per completed task and a typical six-week implementation timeline for enterprise rollouts, but treat those as vendor-stated figures rather than independently verified numbers — they'll vary heavily by workflow complexity and which models tasks route to.

Pricing, free-tier availability and feature details were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly for AI platforms — confirm current terms directly on Relevance AI's pricing page before committing.

## Features that actually differentiate it

- **No-code agent builder with an AI copilot.** A drag-and-drop canvas for agents, tools, workflows, evaluations and workforces, plus a natural-language assistant (Invent) that can scaffold an agent from a plain-English description instead of wiring every step by hand.
- **Multi-agent orchestration.** A visual graph of your agent hierarchy, with forced handovers, escalation edges, dynamic routing and parallel execution. Sub-agents can be called like tools with structured inputs and outputs — useful once you need agents to reliably hand work to each other.
- **LLM router for cost control.** Rather than hardcoding one model for every step, the router selects the most cost-effective model that still clears a performance benchmark — a real differentiator if you're worried about token costs scaling with usage.
- **Built-in evaluations and drift detection.** Set pass/fail checks and test suites before publishing an agent, then sample production runs to catch drift and get alerted on regressions — a feature most no-code automation tools, Zapier included, don't offer natively.
- **Deep integration and action library.** 1,000+ pre-built app integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, LinkedIn and others) plus native actions for image generation across 24+ models, browser automation, web scraping, file parsing, database queries and messaging channels like email, SMS and WhatsApp.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo builders and hobbyists** — a weaker fit right now. Without a published self-serve price, it's hard to test-drive Relevance AI the way you can with [Cursor AI](/blog/cursor-ai-review) or a single-agent chatbot. For one agent answering FAQs on a small site, a lighter, purpose-built tool (or Relevance Chat, if free) likely gets you there faster.
- **Small teams automating a handful of workflows** — a decent fit if the workflow genuinely needs multiple coordinated steps (qualify a lead, enrich it, draft outreach, log it in a CRM) rather than one automation Zapier or Make could already handle more cheaply.
- **Sales, CS, marketing and ops teams at mid-size and larger companies** — this is where Relevance AI is clearly aimed. The evaluation tooling, LLM router, audit logs and RBAC are enterprise-grade features solo users won't need or won't get without an Enterprise contract.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** — SOC 2 Type II, GDPR compliance, SSO/SAML, SCIM sync, multi-region deployment and PII masking are all listed as available, which matters when procurement or security review is part of the buying process.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Real multi-agent orchestration, not just single-agent chat | No published self-serve pricing — everything routes through sales |
| Model-agnostic, with a router that optimizes cost per task | Hard to budget or compare against competitors up front |
| Built-in evaluation and drift-detection tooling, uncommon at this depth | Enterprise-first features have little use for a solo builder |
| Large integration and action library (1,000+ apps, browser automation) | Six-week implementation timelines aren't a same-day setup |
| No-code builder plus an AI copilot lowers the technical bar | Cost-per-task ($0.09 average) is a vendor-stated figure, not verified |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Relevance AI advertises 1,000–2,000+ pre-built app integrations depending on the page, covering CRM tools (Salesforce, HubSpot), communication platforms (Slack, email, SMS, WhatsApp, Teams), and business systems reachable through OAuth. It also supports MCP integration with Claude for coding-agent use cases, sandboxed Python/JavaScript execution, and credential management with OAuth token refresh and secret vaulting. No dedicated Zapier connector is mentioned, but given the native integration breadth, most teams won't need one as a bridge.

## Where it's a strong fit

Relevance AI is a strong fit if you're automating a workflow that genuinely needs several specialized agents cooperating — for example, an agent that triages inbound support tickets handing off to a second agent that drafts a response, with a third escalating anything that fails a confidence check. The evaluation and monitoring layer is a real advantage if you're worried about agents silently degrading in production; setting pass-rate thresholds and getting alerted on drift is a safety net ad hoc no-code automations usually lack. It's also sensible if your organization already needs SOC 2/GDPR-level compliance that would otherwise require custom engineering on a cheaper tool.

## Where to think twice

Skip Relevance AI, at least for now, if you need a genuinely free or low-cost way to experiment with agent building — there's no visible self-serve tier to test the waters without a sales conversation, a real barrier next to tools that let you sign up and start building in minutes. It's also not the right tool if your automation need is simple enough that a single Zapier zap or a basic chatbot would solve it; paying for multi-agent orchestration and evaluation tooling you won't use is wasted spend. And if you need to move fast without a procurement cycle, be cautious — enterprise platforms built around custom onboarding and dedicated account managers tend to come with implementation timelines measured in weeks, not hours.

## Bottom line

Relevance AI's capabilities — multi-agent orchestration, a cost-aware model router, and built-in evaluation and drift monitoring — are more sophisticated than most no-code automation tools, and it's easy to see why mid-size and enterprise teams building serious multi-step automations would choose it over stitching together several point tools. The catch: the platform has moved toward an entirely sales-led, custom-quote pricing model, so there's no quick way to see the actual bill before talking to someone. If your use case matches the enterprise workflow it's built for, it's worth the evaluation call. If you're a solo builder or small team on a defined budget, the lack of transparent pricing alone may push you toward a self-serve alternative first.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Relevance AI have a free plan?**
"Relevance Chat" is usable with no setup, but a full, published free tier for the agent-building platform isn't listed on the current pricing page — confirm directly on the site, since this changes fast.

**How much does Relevance AI cost?**
Only an Enterprise plan with custom, sales-quoted pricing is shown publicly at the time of writing. No published monthly price exists for a self-serve individual or team tier.

**What AI models does Relevance AI use?**
It's model-agnostic, referencing support for Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT models, Google's Gemini models and additional providers, routed through an internal system that picks the most cost-effective model meeting a performance bar per task.

**Is Relevance AI good for beginners with no coding experience?**
The core builder is no-code and includes an AI copilot that scaffolds an agent from a plain-language description. That said, designing multi-agent workflows with handovers and evaluations still has a real learning curve versus a single chatbot.

**How does Relevance AI handle data privacy and security?**
The company states SOC 2 Type II certification and GDPR compliance, plus SSO/SAML, role-based access control, SCIM sync, multi-region deployment, PII masking and audit logging — aimed squarely at enterprise security review.

**What's the difference between an "agent," a "tool," and a "workforce" here?**
An agent is the individual AI worker; a tool is a no-code building block an agent calls to take an action or integrate with another app; a workforce is multiple agents coordinated with shared context, handoffs and escalation logic.

**What are some alternatives to Relevance AI?**
For lighter automation without full agent orchestration, [Zapier](/blog/zapier-review) now includes AI-agent building. For a single strong assistant rather than a multi-agent workforce, [ChatGPT](/blog/chatgpt-review), [Claude AI](/blog/claude-ai-review) or [Google Gemini](/blog/google-gemini-review) are worth comparing first.

**Can I try Relevance AI before committing to a contract?**
There's a quick-start path to build a first agent and try Relevance Chat without a sales call, but full agent-building access at scale appears to route through the Enterprise sales process — verify the current onboarding flow directly on relevanceai.com.

For more AI and software coverage with verified discounts, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Duplichecker Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Duplichecker offers free plagiarism and AI-content checks up to 25,000 words. Here is what its paid plans, features, and user reviews reveal.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Duplichecker a good plagiarism and AI-content checker in 2026?

Duplichecker is a free, browser-based plagiarism checker and AI-content detector that also bundles a paraphraser, grammar checker, word counter, and reverse-image search into one site. It's a solid, no-signup option for quick originality checks on essays or short articles, but its paid plans are priced per word in narrow weekly tiers, and user reviews flag cancellation friction and inconsistent free-vs-paid results worth knowing about first.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $5.00/week (Basic II plan, 10,000 words, 33 searches) on weekly billing; monthly and yearly billing toggles are also offered |
| Free tier/trial | Free plagiarism checker up to 25,000 words per search (per Duplichecker); free AI content detector with no stated word cap or signup requirement |
| Best for | Students, bloggers, and freelance writers who need occasional plagiarism/AI-detection checks without paying for a subscription |
| Standout feature | One account covers plagiarism checking, AI detection, paraphrasing, grammar checking, and reverse image search rather than a single-purpose tool |

## What Duplichecker actually is

Duplichecker.com is a text-tools website, not a single-purpose app. Its plagiarism checker is the flagship product — paste or upload text and it cross-references the web to flag matching passages, similar to how Copyscape or Turnitin work, though Duplichecker markets itself specifically at students, bloggers, freelancers, and small content teams rather than universities or enterprise publishers. Around that core tool it has built out a wider suite: an AI content detector aimed at flagging ChatGPT/GPT-4-style writing, a paraphrasing tool, a grammar checker, a word counter, and a reverse image and face search tool, each with its own separate pricing page.

Duplichecker doesn't publish which underlying detection model or algorithm powers its plagiarism or AI-detection engines — unlike detectors such as [Winston AI](/blog/winston-ai-review), which publish accuracy methodology, Duplichecker's site describes its engine only in marketing terms ("advanced algorithms," "cutting-edge technology") without a named model or independently verifiable accuracy benchmark.

## Pricing: what you actually pay

Duplichecker's core plagiarism checker is free to use directly on the site, with Duplichecker stating it scans up to 25,000 words per search at no cost and without requiring an account. The paid "Pro" tiers exist mainly to unlock features the free tool holds back, most notably the full, downloadable clean-copy report — the site shows you the plagiarism-free version of your text but locks the complete download behind a paywall ("Go Pro to view the full clean version").

Paid plans are billed in narrow, incremental steps rather than a handful of flat tiers, and you can toggle between weekly, monthly, and yearly billing. On the weekly view, the entry-level paid plan and a few of the tiers above it look like this:

| Plan | Price (weekly billing) | Words included | Searches included |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic II | $5.00/week | 10,000 words | 33 searches |
| Basic V | $11.00/week | 28,600 words | 95 searches |
| Pro I | $23.00/week | 59,800 words | 199 searches |
| Pro II | $25.00/week | 65,000 words | 217 searches |

Higher tiers add more searches, more total words, and eventually extra user seats, but API access is marked unavailable on the plans we could inspect — confirm current availability on Duplichecker's own pricing page before assuming programmatic access exists.

The paraphrasing tool, reverse image search, and face search each have their own dedicated pricing pages and are billed separately from the plagiarism checker — a single subscription doesn't unlock every tool on the site. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability described here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly; always check Duplichecker's live pricing page before subscribing.

## Features walkthrough

**Plagiarism checker with source highlighting.** Paste text, upload a file, or check a URL, and Duplichecker returns a percentage-originality score with the matching source links highlighted. It supports multiple file formats and can generate a downloadable report, which matters if you need to hand proof of originality to a client, professor, or editor.

**AI content detector.** A separate free tool that scores text on how likely it is AI-generated, with Duplichecker stating it can flag output associated with GPT-3 and GPT-4-style models. Unlike the plagiarism checker, it's positioned as free with no stated word limit or credit requirement — useful for a quick second opinion, though as with any AI detector, treat a single score as a signal rather than proof; no detector from any vendor is immune to false positives on heavily edited or non-native-English writing.

**Paraphrasing tool.** A separate rewriting tool with its own pricing tier, aimed at reworking flagged passages or rephrasing text in a different tone. It sits in the same category as [Litero AI](/blog/litero-ai-review) or [Humanize AI](/blog/humanize-ai-review), though bundled into a broader suite rather than sold standalone.

**Word counter and grammar checker.** Smaller free utility tools on the same account, useful for quick checks without switching apps.

**Reverse image and face search.** A less common addition for a text-tools site — checks where an image appears elsewhere online, sold on its own separate pricing tier.

## Who it's actually for

- **Students checking a single essay or paper** before submission are well served by the free checker's 25,000-word allowance — likely enough for most assignments without hitting a paywall.
- **Bloggers and freelance writers** doing occasional originality checks can use the free tier for spot checks and step up to a Basic weekly plan only during a busy month.
- **Small content or marketing teams** checking AI-generated drafts at scale will outgrow the free detector's convenience quickly and may find per-search pricing awkward compared to a flat-rate tool built for volume.
- **Anyone needing a defensible, audit-grade accuracy claim** for a compliance or academic-integrity process should look elsewhere, since Duplichecker doesn't publish independently verified accuracy figures for either engine.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Free plagiarism checker allows up to 25,000 words per search with no signup | Full "clean copy" report download is locked behind a paid plan |
| Free, unlimited AI content detector with no credit requirement | No published model name or independently verified accuracy benchmark |
| Bundles plagiarism, AI detection, paraphrasing, grammar, and image search in one account | Paid plans are billed in narrow weekly increments that can look cheaper than they are on longer terms |
| Simple, no-install browser workflow | Trustpilot reviewers report subscription-cancellation friction and inconsistent free-vs-paid match results |
| Supports URL and file-upload checking, not just pasted text | API access appears unavailable on the plans reviewed — confirm before assuming programmatic access |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Duplichecker is a standalone web app; it doesn't advertise a Zapier connector, Slack app, or browser extension ecosystem the way some writing tools do. Its "API" column is marked unavailable on every tier we could inspect, suggesting API access either isn't currently offered or is handled through a separate enterprise conversation not listed on the public pricing page. The main "ecosystem" here is the bundle of sibling tools on the same site (paraphraser, grammar checker, reverse image search) rather than third-party integrations.

## Where it's a strong fit

Duplichecker is a reasonable default when you need a fast, free, no-signup plagiarism or AI-content check on a single document and don't need an audit trail or enterprise reporting. The free tiers on both tools are genuinely usable rather than token teasers, and the 25,000-word allowance covers most student and blog-length content without needing to pay anything.

## Where to think twice

Skip Duplichecker's paid tiers if you need a fully free tool beyond the stated free allowances — the weekly billing structure adds up quickly if you check content regularly rather than occasionally. It's also not the right choice if your team needs SOC 2 or other enterprise compliance documentation, since Duplichecker doesn't publish that kind of certification. If you need API access to automate checks inside another workflow, current plans don't appear to support it. And multiple Trustpilot reviewers (the tool holds a 2.3/5 rating there as of this writing, from roughly 38 reviews) report difficulty canceling paid subscriptions and at least one account of a free scan flagging a match a paid scan then didn't — treat any free-vs-paid discrepancy as a reason to double-check results, and read the cancellation terms before subscribing.

## Bottom line

Duplichecker earns its place as a free, no-friction plagiarism and AI-detection checker for occasional, lower-stakes use — a student's essay, a blogger's draft, a quick second opinion on suspicious text. It's less convincing as a paid subscription: the weekly pricing is easy to underestimate over a full month, the site doesn't publish accuracy methodology that would justify high-stakes reliance, and real user reviews raise legitimate cancellation and consistency concerns. Use the free tools freely; think carefully before paying for more.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Duplichecker actually free?**
Yes, for baseline use. The plagiarism checker allows up to 25,000 words per search for free, and the AI content detector is free and unlimited by Duplichecker's own description. Paid plans exist mainly to unlock the full downloadable "clean copy" report and higher word/search allowances.

**How accurate is Duplichecker's AI content detector?**
Duplichecker states its detector is accurate and can flag GPT-3/GPT-4-style content, but it doesn't publish an independently verified accuracy percentage or methodology. Treat any AI-detector score, from Duplichecker or a competitor, as a signal rather than definitive proof — false positives are a known limitation across this entire product category.

**Does Duplichecker store or share the text I check?**
Duplichecker's marketing pages don't give a plain-language answer to this; check its privacy policy directly before pasting confidential or unpublished work.

**What's the cheapest paid plan?**
On weekly billing, the entry-level Basic II plan was listed at $5.00/week for 10,000 words and 33 searches at the time of writing. Monthly and yearly toggles are also available and may work out cheaper per word — compare them on Duplichecker's own pricing page before subscribing.

**Is Duplichecker good for beginners?**
Yes — no software to install, no account required for the free tools, and a simple paste-and-scan workflow make it approachable for a first-time user.

**What are the alternatives to Duplichecker?**
For AI-content detection specifically with more transparent accuracy claims, see our [Winston AI review](/blog/winston-ai-review). For rewriting flagged AI text, see [Litero AI](/blog/litero-ai-review), [Humanize AI](/blog/humanize-ai-review), and [Undetectable AI](/blog/undetectable-ai-review). For general plagiarism checking, Copyscape and Turnitin remain the more established names, though both charge from the first check rather than offering a substantial free tier.

**Can I cancel a Duplichecker subscription easily?**
Multiple Trustpilot reviewers report difficulty finding the cancellation option and describe the process as harder than it should be. Duplichecker's stated policy is that cancellation is available through account settings — locate and test this before subscribing if that's a concern, and keep a record of your cancellation confirmation.

**Does Duplichecker have a mobile app?**
No dedicated mobile app is advertised; it's a browser-based tool that works on mobile browsers but isn't packaged as a native app on iOS or Android app stores as of this writing.

For more AI and productivity tool coverage, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub.

title: Brisk Teaching Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Brisk Teaching brings free AI tools into Google Docs, Slides and Classroom for teachers. Here's how its pricing and features hold up.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Brisk Teaching worth installing?

Brisk Teaching is a free Chrome/Edge extension that layers AI tools directly onto Google Docs, Slides, Classroom, YouTube and PDFs, rather than making teachers copy-paste into a separate app. For solo teachers wanting lesson prep and feedback help inside tools they already use, it's a genuinely useful, low-cost option — districts wanting curriculum alignment or admin controls will need the paid Premium or Intelligence tier.

### At a glance

| | Brisk Teaching |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | Free (individual teachers, unlimited use) |
| Free tier limits | Unlimited generations on 20+ tools, standard AI model |
| Best for | Individual teachers working inside Google Docs/Classroom/YouTube |
| Standout feature | Works as an overlay on your existing tools instead of a separate app |
| Paid plans | Premium & Intelligence — custom pricing, school/district only |

## What Brisk Teaching actually is

Brisk Teaching is made by Brisk Labs Co., an edtech company that pitches itself less as "another AI app" and more as an AI layer sitting on top of tools teachers already have open all day — Google Docs, Slides, Classroom, YouTube and any PDF or webpage. Instead of opening a new tab, pasting content in, and pasting the output back into a lesson document, the extension adds a sidebar and inline tools directly inside those pages.

That "no new tab" framing is the biggest practical difference between Brisk and most other AI-for-teachers products, which tend to be standalone web apps with their own dashboard and document editor. Brisk doesn't specify which underlying language model powers its free "standard" tier or its paid "turbo" tier — if the exact model matters for your district's AI-vendor review, confirm directly with Brisk's sales team rather than assuming.

Brisk says it has saved teachers roughly 2.2 million hours and is used by "1 in 3 teachers in the USA" across more than 10,000 districts — Brisk's own stated figures, not independently audited, so treat them as a scale claim rather than a verified statistic. More independently checkable is Brisk's **95% Common Sense Privacy Rating**, a third-party evaluation of its data-handling practices, and Brisk states it is FERPA and COPPA compliant.

## Pricing

Brisk runs a three-tier structure: a genuinely free individual plan, and two custom-quoted plans sold only to schools and districts.

| Plan | Price | Who it's for | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Individual teachers | 20+ AI tools, Chrome/Edge extension, output in 50+ languages, unlimited usage, standard language model |
| Premium | Custom (contact sales) | Schools & districts | Everything in Free, plus 35+ tools, a faster "turbo" model, unlimited batch feedback, advanced student insights, admin dashboard, rostering, dedicated customer success, and PD access |
| Intelligence | Custom (contact sales) | Districts prioritizing curriculum alignment | Everything in Premium, plus curriculum pacing/scope-and-sequence integration, "Brisk Guidance" compliance context, white-glove onboarding, and curriculum-informed analytics |

Notably, Brisk doesn't sell Premium or Intelligence at the individual-teacher level — both are priced for building-wide or district-wide rollout. A single teacher can't pay a personal monthly fee to unlock the turbo model the way you'd upgrade a personal ChatGPT Plus account. If your school hasn't purchased a paid plan, you're on the free tier indefinitely — and that tier is unusually generous, since Brisk doesn't cap the number of generations, only which tools and model tier you get.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly, so confirm current details on Brisk's own pricing page before recommending it to a district procurement team.

## Features that actually differentiate it

**Browser-overlay workflow.** This is the feature that most defines Brisk. Its sidebar activates inside Google Docs, Slides, Classroom, YouTube, and most webpages/PDFs, letting you highlight text on any page and run an AI action against it without switching tabs — removing the copy-paste step that eats time with generic AI chat tools.

**Feedback on student writing, inline in the doc.** Brisk can generate personalized comments directly on a student's Google Doc — flagging structure, clarity, and originality-related concerns — without exporting the essay elsewhere first. The free tier runs one document at a time; Premium's "unlimited batch feedback" runs the same pass across an entire class set at once, which is the single biggest time-saver for anyone grading real classroom volume.

**Differentiation across reading levels and languages.** Brisk can take an existing article, worksheet, or lesson resource and regenerate it at a different reading level, or translate it into one of 50+ languages — useful for differentiating instruction for multilingual learners or mixed-ability classrooms without rewriting the source material from scratch.

**Turning existing resources into new materials.** Brisk's pitch of turning "any resource you love and trust" into a lesson, quiz, or presentation extends to YouTube videos and PDFs specifically — generate a quiz from a video's content, or pull a worksheet out of a PDF, without manually transcribing it first.

**Student-facing interactive activities.** Beyond teacher-side generation, Brisk includes interactive practice modules students can use directly, giving it a light student-tool layer on top of what's otherwise a teacher-productivity extension.

## Who it's actually for

- **A solo classroom teacher**: the free tier delivers real day-to-day value since usage isn't capped and the core toolset (lesson generation, feedback, quizzes, differentiation) is all included.
- **A department or small school piloting AI tools**: workable free, but batch feedback across a full course load and admin visibility only show up in Premium.
- **A district evaluating a building-wide rollout**: Premium and Intelligence are built for you — rostering, an admin dashboard, PD support, and curriculum-pacing alignment target IT/curriculum leadership, not a single classroom.
- **A district with an existing curriculum vendor**: Intelligence's scope-and-sequence integration is narrow — skip it if you're not already running a curriculum map that needs that alignment.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Unlimited usage on the free tier, not just a capped number of generations | No individual paid tier — can't upgrade past free without your school/district buying in |
| Works inside tools teachers already use (Docs, Slides, Classroom, YouTube) | Underlying AI model isn't publicly named |
| Batch feedback across a class set (Premium) is a real time-saver | Premium/Intelligence pricing is unpublished, requiring a sales call |
| 95% Common Sense Privacy Rating, stated FERPA/COPPA compliance | Advanced insights and admin tools are locked behind a district purchase |
| 50+ language support for differentiation and translation | As a browser extension, it only works inside supported sites/tools |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Brisk's design is built around integration rather than being a destination app. It works as a layer inside **Google Docs, Slides, and Classroom**, activates on **YouTube** pages to generate content from video, and can process **PDFs** and general webpages. There's no public API for third-party developers and no listed Zapier or Slack integration — Brisk's "ecosystem" is really the Google Workspace for Education stack itself. If your school runs on Microsoft 365/Teams, confirm current browser and platform support with Brisk directly, since its feature list leans heavily Google-first.

## Where it's a strong fit

- Teachers and schools already standardized on Google Workspace for Education, where Brisk's overlay approach removes friction other AI tools add.
- Anyone who wants a free tool with no usage cap to test AI-assisted lesson prep, quiz generation and feedback before asking a district to fund anything.
- Districts that want AI content generation plugged into an existing curriculum pacing guide, where Intelligence's scope-and-sequence alignment is a genuinely narrow feature few competitors offer.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a transparent AI-model disclosure** for a district vendor review — Brisk's materials don't name the specific model behind either tier; ask directly.
- **If you're a solo teacher wanting more than the free tier with no district budget** — there's no individual paid upgrade path; the money has to come from the building or district.
- **If your school runs primarily on Microsoft 365 rather than Google Workspace** — Brisk's feature depth is built around Google's tools first, so verify current support before committing a rollout.
- **If you need firm, published enterprise pricing for procurement comparisons** — Premium and Intelligence require a sales call rather than a rate card.

## Bottom line

Brisk Teaching earns its adoption numbers by solving a specific annoyance: AI tools that make teachers leave the doc, slide deck, or Classroom page they're already working in. For an individual teacher, the free tier alone — unlimited use, 20+ tools, real feedback and differentiation features — is worth installing, no credit card required. Where Brisk gets more serious is at the district level, where batch feedback, admin dashboards and curriculum alignment turn it into an institution-wide rollout. It's a different shape of product from all-in-one platforms like MagicSchool AI, built as a standalone hub of 80+ tools with an $8–13/month individual Plus tier rather than a browser overlay — worth trying both if deciding between "AI inside my existing tools" and "AI as its own workspace."

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Brisk Teaching free?**
Yes, for individual teachers the core plan is free with unlimited usage on 20+ tools. Schools and districts that want the faster model, batch feedback, admin dashboard or curriculum alignment features need to purchase Premium or Intelligence, both custom-quoted.

**Does Brisk Teaching work outside Google Workspace?**
Its feature set is built primarily around Google Docs, Slides, Classroom and YouTube. If your school uses Microsoft 365 or another LMS, confirm current browser/platform support directly with Brisk before rolling it out district-wide.

**Is student data safe with Brisk Teaching?**
Brisk states it is FERPA and COPPA compliant and has earned a 95% Common Sense Privacy Rating, a third-party assessment. As with any AI tool touching student writing, districts should still review Brisk's current data-processing agreement directly.

**Can a single teacher upgrade to the paid tier without district approval?**
No. Both Premium and Intelligence are sold at the school/district level with custom pricing — there's no individual paid upgrade a teacher can purchase alone.

**What AI model does Brisk Teaching use?**
Brisk doesn't publicly name the model behind either its free "standard" tier or paid "turbo" tier. If that matters for your evaluation, ask Brisk's team directly.

**How is Brisk Teaching different from MagicSchool AI?**
Brisk overlays AI tools onto Google Docs, Slides, Classroom and YouTube, with a free unlimited individual tier and no personal paid upgrade. MagicSchool is a standalone web platform with its own 80+ tool library and a paid individual "Plus" tier around $8–13/month, plus a separate enterprise tier. Teachers who want AI inside tools they already use tend to prefer Brisk; teachers wanting one dedicated hub with more individual paid features may prefer MagicSchool.

**Is Brisk Teaching good for beginners with no AI experience?**
Yes — since it activates as a sidebar inside tools teachers already know, there's very little new interface to learn versus onboarding into a separate AI platform.

**Does Brisk Teaching support non-English classrooms?**
Yes, Brisk states support for content generation and translation across 50+ languages, useful for differentiating instruction for multilingual learners.

Looking for other AI and software deals? Check the [AI & software deals](/category/software) category page for current verified offers on tools worth pairing with your classroom tech stack.

title: Janitor AI Review 2026: Pricing, Safety and Verdict
excerpt: Janitor AI lets you chat with uncensored AI characters for free. Here's how its pricing, backend model and content moderation actually work.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Janitor AI safe to use, and is it worth the subscription?

Janitor AI is a free-to-browse AI character-chat and roleplay platform built around uncensored, user-created characters, funded mainly through a paid "Plus" tier and community LLM-proxy access rather than heavy content restrictions. It's a reasonable pick if you specifically want unmoderated roleplay and don't mind self-managing an API key — but its lax age verification and thin built-in safety net mean it deserves real scrutiny before you sign up.

### At a glance

| | Janitor AI |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | Free to browse and chat (bring-your-own or default backend) |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — unlimited character browsing, chat gated by backend queue/rate limits |
| Best for | Uncensored AI roleplay with community-built characters, for adult users comfortable managing their own LLM access |
| Standout feature | Character marketplace of millions of user-submitted personas, with almost no content filtering compared to mainstream chat assistants |

## What Janitor AI actually is

Janitor AI is a browser-based platform where users create, browse, and chat with AI-driven fictional characters — everything from anime and game-inspired personas to original roleplay characters submitted by other users. It emerged in 2023 as a direct beneficiary of Character.AI's and Chai's crackdowns on NSFW roleplay: when those platforms tightened content filters, a large chunk of their user base migrated to Janitor AI specifically because it didn't apply the same restrictions.

Unlike ChatGPT, Claude, or Character.AI, Janitor AI doesn't train or host its own frontier language model. It's fundamentally a **front end and character database** that routes conversations to a language model backend of the user's choosing — Janitor AI's own default model (a lighter, often congested option for free users), or an external API key the user supplies, historically OpenAI and later various third-party "proxy" services and open-weight models via community-run relays. This bring-your-own-backend design is the single most important thing to understand about the platform: chat quality, and to a real extent the content that's permitted, depends heavily on which model you connect, not just on Janitor AI's own rules.

The company behind Janitor AI keeps a low public profile — it doesn't publish detailed "About us" pages naming a founding team or funding history the way most consumer AI companies do. For a platform handling sensitive roleplay content and asking some users to paste in personal API keys, that opacity is a real due-diligence gap, not a minor detail.

## Pricing

Janitor AI's core browsing and character-creation features are free. The friction point is the shared default backend model, frequently rate-limited or queued at peak hours since it serves a very large free user base off pooled capacity. The paid tier, commonly called **Janitor AI Plus**, aims to remove that friction — faster responses, priority backend access, and in some periods, ad-free browsing.

Many users bypass the built-in backend entirely, connecting their own API key from an external LLM provider or a proxy that pools access on their behalf. Real monthly cost therefore varies enormously — from $0 with a free-tier model, to whatever the provider charges per token, on top of (or instead of) any Plus fee.

Janitor AI doesn't publish a fully transparent, stable pricing page the way most SaaS tools do, and third-party "Plus" pricing has shifted as monetization has changed — we're not printing a specific dollar figure we can't independently verify; check the current subscription price on janitorai.com before paying. The shape of the model, though, is consistent: a free tier with shared, congested capacity; a paid tier for priority access; and an optional, separate cost if you bring your own API key or proxy.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability described in this review were accurate as of the date of this post and can change quickly — that's especially true for a platform like this one, where the underlying backend models and proxy ecosystem shift often.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Full character browsing/creation, chat via shared default backend, subject to queueing and rate limits at peak times |
| Janitor AI Plus | Paid, confirm current price on the official site | Priority/faster access to the default backend, reduced wait times, historically fewer ads |
| Bring-your-own-backend | Variable (external provider's own pricing) | Connect your own API key or a community proxy instead of the default backend; cost and content limits depend entirely on that provider, not Janitor AI |

## Core features walkthrough

- **Character marketplace at scale.** A very large, user-submitted library spans fandom characters, original personas, and companion-style bots. The vendor cites tens of millions of registered users on its own marketing pages — treat that as Janitor AI's stated figure, not an independently audited number.
- **Character creation tools.** Anyone can publish a character with a name, personality description, opening message, and example dialogue without writing or fine-tuning a model — the persona sits on top of whichever backend the chatter connects.
- **Persona system.** Users create their own "persona" (a self-description) so characters respond to a consistent identity across chats instead of treating every conversation as a blank slate.
- **Backend flexibility.** Swapping in your own API key or a proxy is a genuine differentiator versus closed platforms like Character.AI — technically inclined users can pick a model to fit their budget, latency needs, or content tolerance.
- **Group chat formats.** Beyond one-on-one chat, the platform supports multiple characters interacting in one thread, a step beyond the single-bot default most rival apps use.

## Who it's actually for

- **Adult roleplay and fiction hobbyists** who want a lightly moderated space for long-form character interactions and are comfortable self-managing an API key or proxy for faster, better responses.
- **Writers and worldbuilders** using AI characters as an improv/drafting tool, who want more creative latitude than mainstream assistants allow by default.
- **Not a fit for minors** — sign-up requires 18+ self-certification, and the content skews toward material not designed with younger users in mind.
- **Not a fit for anyone wanting a plug-and-play experience** — getting good performance usually means understanding API keys, token costs, and proxy reliability, a meaningfully higher bar than a polished consumer chatbot app.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Free to browse and use core features | Default backend is frequently congested/rate-limited for free users |
| Very large library of user-created characters | Content moderation is comparatively light — enforcement leans on user reporting rather than proactive filtering |
| Backend flexibility (bring your own API key/model) | Getting good performance usually requires technical setup (API keys, proxies) |
| No requirement to use a single locked-in AI provider | Company transparency is limited — little public information about ownership, data handling, or moderation staffing |
| Supports longer-form, less-filtered roleplay than mainstream chat assistants | Age verification is a simple self-declared checkbox, not a real verification step |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Janitor AI's "integrations" look different from a typical SaaS tool's Zapier/Slack list — its real ecosystem is the LLM backend layer. It supports connecting official API keys from major model providers, and a wider community of third-party proxy services has grown up around the platform offering pooled or discounted access to various models. There's no official mobile app; it's accessed through a mobile or desktop browser, and any "Janitor AI app" listings in app stores should be treated with caution, since the ecosystem around it includes unofficial wrapper apps of inconsistent trustworthiness. Connecting a personal API key to any third-party proxy is a real security decision — you're extending trust to a service outside Janitor AI's own infrastructure, so check a proxy's reputation before pasting in a key tied to a paid account.

## Where it's a strong fit

Janitor AI earns its popularity in one specific lane: long-form, character-driven creative roleplay without the persistent content refusals that mainstream assistants apply by design. For adult users who know what they're using it for, understand the backend model they're connecting, and want a large pre-built character library rather than building a chatbot from scratch, it does that job well and at low direct cost if you're willing to manage your own API access.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need strong, proactive content moderation**, this isn't it — enforcement here leans on community flagging rather than upfront filtering, a deliberate trade-off, not an oversight.
- **If you're uncomfortable with age verification being a checkbox rather than a check**, that's a legitimate reason to skip this platform. The 18+ requirement at sign-up is self-declared, and Janitor AI faces the same kind of outside scrutiny as other character-chat apps over enforcement. Character.AI, Chai, and Replika have all drawn comparable criticism, and Character.AI's high-profile safety incidents involving minors pushed it to add stricter default filters for under-18 accounts. Janitor AI hasn't published an equivalent minors-specific safety layer — a meaningful gap relative to where the category has moved.
- **If you want one transparent monthly price with a clear refund policy**, be aware "good" performance often depends on a separate API/proxy bill Janitor AI doesn't control or disclose on your behalf.
- **If data privacy assurances matter to you**, the company publishes comparatively little detail about how chat logs, personas, and any pasted-in API keys are stored — confirm that directly (and skeptically) before entrusting it with sensitive personal details.
- **If you need enterprise-grade reliability**, the free backend's peak-time congestion means fast responses aren't guaranteed unless you pay for priority access or bring a well-provisioned API key.

## The bottom line

Janitor AI does one thing deliberately well: it gives adult users a large, mostly unfiltered library of AI characters to roleplay with, at no required cost beyond patience for backend queues. That's a real, if narrow, value proposition, and it explains why the platform kept growing even as competitors tightened their own rules. But the same choices that make it appealing — light moderation, self-declared age gating, and an architecture that pushes technical decisions and real security exposure onto the user — are exactly what should make a prospective user pause. This isn't a platform to hand to a teenager or to use for anything you wouldn't want stored somewhere you don't fully control. Go in aware of those trade-offs and it delivers what it promises; if you want a safer, more moderated character-chat experience, mainstream alternatives with stricter default filters are a better start.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Janitor AI free?**
Yes, browsing and basic chat are free, though the shared default backend can be slow or rate-limited at peak times. A paid Plus tier and/or your own API key can improve speed and reliability.

**Does Janitor AI require age verification?**
It requires users to self-certify they're 18 or older at sign-up — a declared checkbox rather than an ID-based check, which has drawn outside criticism aimed at the platform and at AI character-chat apps generally.

**Is Janitor AI safe to use?**
It's functional and widely used, but moderation relies more on community reporting than proactive filtering, and the company discloses relatively little about data handling. Treat any pasted-in API key or proxy connection the way you would any third-party security decision.

**Do I need an OpenAI or Claude API key to use it?**
No — Janitor AI includes a free default backend. You only need your own key or a proxy subscription for faster or higher-quality responses than the free shared backend provides.

**What's the difference between Janitor AI and Character.AI?**
Character.AI trains and hosts its own model with stricter, centrally-enforced filters, especially for accounts flagged as minors. Janitor AI is a front end over externally-supplied or default backend models with lighter built-in restrictions, which is why it attracted users after Character.AI tightened its policies.

**Can I use Janitor AI on mobile?**
Yes, through a mobile browser. There's no official first-party app; be cautious of unofficial apps claiming to be Janitor AI, since third-party wrappers of inconsistent trust exist.

**Is there a free trial for Janitor AI Plus?**
Details have changed over time; confirm current trial availability and pricing directly on the official site before subscribing, since we can't independently verify a stable current figure at the time of writing.

**Are there beginner-friendly alternatives with more built-in safety filtering?**
Yes — mainstream assistants like [ChatGPT](/blog/chatgpt-review) or [Claude AI](/blog/claude-ai-review) apply much stricter default moderation and are a better starting point for a general-purpose AI chat experience without managing your own backend.
