**API and storefront widget.** Beyond batch generation, Hautech.ai exposes an API for pulling generation into existing PIM/DAM or e-commerce systems, and a widget that runs generation live on a storefront, letting a shopper preview an item on a body type closer to their own.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo sellers and small apparel brands** testing whether AI product imagery can replace occasional photoshoots will find the Starter or Growth bundle enough to experiment on a handful of SKUs before committing further spend.
- **Growing DTC and fashion brands** running regular catalog refreshes are the platform's core audience — the Scale and Catalog tiers suit needing dozens to hundreds of new product images a month without scaling an in-house photo studio.
- **Larger retailers, marketplaces, and agencies** producing imagery for multiple brand clients fit the Enterprise tier and are the likeliest users of the API and Liana workflow builder rather than the plain Studio interface.
- **Teams needing real-time on-site personalization**, like a try-on widget for shoppers, are pointed at the Widget integration specifically, a different use case from bulk catalog generation.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Credits never expire, unlike most subscription AI tools | No published free tier or trial — you commit real money to test output quality |
| Full commercial rights on every plan, including the cheapest bundle | Pricing isn't transparent about exactly what drives per-image credit cost until you generate |
| Multiple integration surfaces (Studio, API, Liana, Widget) for different technical needs | Underlying model/tech stack isn't publicly disclosed, making it hard to compare output quality claims against named competitors |
| Volume discounts reward brands that commit to larger bundles | Smallest bundle (5 credits, ~13 photos) is expensive per image relative to bulk tiers |
| Backed by major cloud/AI accelerator programs, suggesting infrastructure maturity | Aimed squarely at commerce/fashion use cases — not a general-purpose image generator |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Hautech.ai's main integration path is its **API**, intended for connecting generation directly into a brand's product information management (PIM), digital asset management (DAM), or e-commerce backend so new SKUs can be processed without manual upload/download through Studio. **Liana** functions as an internal workflow layer for scripting repeatable generation sequences rather than a third-party integration. The **Widget** is the closest thing to a plug-and-play storefront integration, embedded on product pages for live, on-demand visual generation such as a try-on preview. The site doesn't list native Shopify, WooCommerce, or Zapier app-store integrations at this time — brands on those platforms would likely route generated assets through the API or manual export/import, so confirm current integration options directly with Hautech.ai before assuming plug-and-play compatibility with a specific storefront platform.

## Where it's a strong fit

- Apparel and fashion brands that need a steady stream of on-model product photography without booking recurring photoshoots.
- Brands wanting to show the same garment on a wider range of body types or in more settings than a single photoshoot could realistically cover.
- Teams that need short video content for social commerce but lack in-house video production.
- Larger catalogs where per-image cost drops meaningfully at higher credit tiers, making bulk generation cheaper than photography at scale.

## Where to think twice

- If you need a genuinely **free tool to test with zero spend**, Hautech.ai isn't it — there's no free tier, so you're paying for your first batch of test images before knowing if the output style fits your brand.
- If your product category isn't apparel or a similarly visual, wearable/physical good, the try-on and model-swap focus won't be as useful as a general-purpose image generator.
- If you need precise control over facial features, brand-specific model likenesses, or exact art direction, review sample outputs carefully first — AI-generated models can still show artifacts a real photoshoot wouldn't.
- If your team needs enterprise compliance documentation (SOC 2, GDPR data processing agreements) before adopting a vendor, that isn't published on the marketing site and would need to be requested directly from sales.
- If you want transparent, itemized feature differences between plan tiers rather than just credit volume and discounts, the current pricing page doesn't spell that out — clarify with sales before a large Enterprise commitment.

## Bottom line

Hautech.ai is a purpose-built alternative to traditional product photography for brands selling physical, wearable goods — its virtual try-on, model-swap, and video-from-stills tools solve a real, expensive problem (photoshoot cost and turnaround time) rather than acting as a generic image generator with an e-commerce label attached. The credit system is fairer than a flat subscription for lumpy production needs since unused credits don't expire, but the lack of a free tier means you're betting on output quality with your first purchase. For fashion and DTC brands doing regular catalog refreshes, it's worth testing at the Starter or Growth level before scaling into Catalog or Enterprise bundles.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Hautech.ai have a free trial?**
There's no published free credit tier — Studio can be explored without cost, but generating images requires a credit bundle starting at $10 for 5 credits. Confirm current trial availability directly on hautech.ai before assuming otherwise.

**How much does Hautech.ai cost per image?**
Effective cost ranges from about $2.00 per credit on Starter down to $1.20 per credit on Enterprise, with each photo typically costing less than one full credit — the site estimates roughly 13 photos from a $10, 5-credit Starter pack. Exact costs depend on output complexity and are shown before you generate.

**Do credits expire?**
No — Hautech.ai states purchased credits don't expire and carry over across its tools (photo, video, model swap).

**Can I use Hautech.ai images commercially?**
Yes, all plans include full commercial usage rights on generated output, though it's worth double-checking against your specific use case in the terms of service before large campaigns.

**What's the difference between Studio, Liana, API, and Widget?**
Studio is the self-serve app for manual generation; Liana is a node-based workflow builder for bulk needs; the API integrates generation into your own systems; and the Widget is embeddable for live, on-storefront generation like try-on previews.

**Is Hautech.ai beginner-friendly?**
Studio is a self-serve entry point that doesn't require coding. Liana and the API assume more technical comfort and target teams building repeatable or integrated workflows.

**What alternatives should I compare it against?**
SmartFare's [Unrealshot AI review](/blog/unrealshot-ai-review) and [Remaker AI review](/blog/remaker-ai-review) cover two other AI image tools with overlapping use cases worth weighing against Hautech.ai's credit pricing and feature set.

**Does Hautech.ai disclose which AI models it uses?**
No — the underlying generation technology is described as proprietary, and specific models behind the image or video pipeline aren't publicly named.

For more AI and software deals and reviews, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Diffutoon Review 2026: Open-Source Anime Video Toon Shader
excerpt: Diffutoon turns real video into anime-style footage using diffusion models. Here is what this free, open-source research tool actually does and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Diffutoon Review 2026: Is This Open-Source Toon Shader Worth Running?

Diffutoon is a free, open-source diffusion-model pipeline that converts real video into anime-style "toon shaded" footage at high resolution, and it's genuinely good at what it does if you're comfortable running Python code on a GPU. It's not a SaaS app with a sign-up form — there's no dashboard, no subscription, and no hosted version to click into.

That distinction matters more than usual here, so before going further: this is a research project, not a commercial product. There's no pricing plan to quote, no free-trial email gate, and no company behind a support inbox. What follows treats it accordingly — as a tool overview rather than a pricing-and-plans review.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Open-source research tool (diffusion model pipeline), not a SaaS product |
| **Cost** | Free — Apache-2.0 licensed, self-hosted only |
| **Best for** | Developers, ML researchers, and animators comfortable with Python/GPU setup |
| **Standout feature** | Renders high-resolution, temporally consistent anime-style video from live-action footage |
| **Requires** | A CUDA-capable GPU and local (or cloud) Python environment — no web app exists |

## What Diffutoon actually is

Diffutoon comes out of East China Normal University's research lab (the paper credits Zhongjie Duan, Chengyu Wang, Cen Chen, Weining Qian, and Jun Huang) and was published as "DiffuToon: High-Resolution Editable Toon Shading via Diffusion Models," arXiv:2401.16224, presented at IJCAI 2024. The code ships inside [DiffSynth-Studio](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio), a broader open-source diffusion toolkit under the ModelScope/Alibaba ecosystem, released under Apache-2.0.

The core problem is "toon shading" — taking photorealistic video and re-rendering it so it looks hand-drawn or anime-style, while keeping motion smooth and details sharp across frames. That's harder than it sounds: run a single-image diffusion style transfer on every frame independently and you get flickering, inconsistent line work, and warped structure from one frame to the next. Diffutoon's paper breaks the problem into four sub-tasks — stylization, consistency enhancement, structure guidance, and colorization — and solves each with a dedicated component rather than throwing one model at the whole thing.

According to the paper, this decomposed approach outperformed both open-source and proprietary baseline methods in the authors' quantitative benchmarks and human evaluation, though those results reflect the authors' own test setup rather than an independently audited benchmark — worth keeping in mind if comparing Diffutoon against a different toon-shading pipeline.

## How it works, at a high level

Diffutoon builds on a video diffusion backbone and layers on:

- **Stylization** — the actual anime/toon-style rendering pass, driven by diffusion model conditioning.
- **Consistency enhancement** — techniques aimed at keeping character shapes, colors, and line work stable frame-to-frame instead of flickering, which is the classic failure mode of naive per-frame stylization.
- **Structure guidance** — using signals from the source footage (motion, edges, depth-like cues) to keep the stylized output anatomically and spatially faithful to what was actually filmed.
- **Colorization** — a dedicated step for applying anime-appropriate color grading and shading rather than leaving colors to whatever the stylization pass produces by default.

The project page also describes an editable branch that lets users steer the output with text prompts, so you're not limited to a single fixed "anime look" — you can push the style in a particular direction through prompting, similar to how text-to-image diffusion models are steered.

Because it's a research codebase rather than a polished app, there's no built-in UI beyond what DiffSynth-Studio's examples provide. You clone the repository, install the Python dependencies, and run the provided scripts against your own source video. The GitHub repo and project page (ecnu-cilab.github.io/DiffutoonProjectPage) include example input/output pairs so you can gauge the pipeline before investing time in setup.

## Core capabilities that differentiate it

- **High-resolution output** — the paper's stated goal, and its main differentiator from earlier toon-shading diffusion demos, is detailed, high-resolution anime-style video rather than low-res proof-of-concept clips.
- **Extended-duration consistency** — the four-part decomposition specifically targets keeping longer clips visually stable, not just short bursts of frames.
- **Fast-motion handling** — the project page highlights that the method copes with rapid motion, a scenario that tends to break naive per-frame stylization.
- **Text-prompt editability** — an additional processing branch lets you adjust the stylistic direction through prompts rather than being locked to one fixed look.
- **Open weights and code** — Apache-2.0 licensed and bundled inside DiffSynth-Studio, so you can inspect, modify, and fine-tune the pipeline yourself, which a closed commercial anime-filter app won't allow.

Pricing, feature availability, and license terms referenced here reflect the project's public GitHub repository and project page as of this article's publication date below; open-source projects can change licensing or fold features into newer releases, so it's worth checking the current DiffSynth-Studio repository before building anything on top of it.

## Who it's actually for

- **ML researchers and diffusion-model tinkerers** — aimed at people who want to study or extend a published toon-shading method, not casual users looking for a one-click filter.
- **Developers building a video-stylization feature** — the code is open and Apache-2.0 licensed, so a team could integrate or fine-tune the approach into their own product rather than paying for a black-box API.
- **Animators and VFX hobbyists with GPU access** — comfortable in a terminal and own (or can rent) a capable GPU, you can experiment with converting your own footage without paying per-clip.
- **Not for casual creators** — if you just want to upload a phone video and get an anime filter back in a browser, this isn't that; a consumer video-styling app with a hosted interface serves that need better.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Completely free and open source (Apache-2.0) | No hosted app — requires local/cloud GPU setup |
| Published, peer-reviewed method (IJCAI 2024) | No customer support, SLA, or company backing it |
| Targets high resolution and longer clips specifically | Setup requires Python/ML environment familiarity |
| Editable via text prompts, not a fixed single style | Rendering time and GPU cost fall entirely on the user |
| Part of the actively maintained DiffSynth-Studio project | Benchmarks are self-reported by the paper's authors |

## Integrations and ecosystem

There's no plugin marketplace, Zapier connector, or Slack app here — Diffutoon is a Python-based pipeline, not a SaaS integration hub. Its practical "ecosystem" is DiffSynth-Studio itself, which bundles other diffusion-based tools (image editing, video synthesis, and more) sharing the same infrastructure, so an existing DiffSynth-Studio setup makes adding Diffutoon-style toon shading a smaller lift than starting from scratch. Since the code is open source, it can be wrapped in your own API layer or web front end — community demo spaces on platforms like Hugging Face have done this for similar DiffSynth-Studio components — but that wrapper work is on you, not something Diffutoon ships out of the box.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You need a documented, benchmarked method for anime-style video conversion and want to build on published research rather than reverse-engineer a closed product.
- You already run GPU-backed ML infrastructure and want a free component to slot into a video pipeline.
- You want to fine-tune or modify the stylization behavior yourself, which a closed commercial tool won't allow.
- You're prototyping or researching video style transfer and need something citable and reproducible.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a point-and-click hosted tool**, skip this — there's no web app or upload-and-download interface; you're working directly with code.
- **If you don't have GPU access or ML setup experience**, expect to spend real time on environment setup (CUDA drivers, dependencies, model weight downloads) before rendering a single clip.
- **If you need commercial support or an SLA**, there is none — this is a research project maintained by academic authors and open-source contributors, not a vendor with a support team.
- **If your use case needs guaranteed licensing clarity for commercial output**, Apache-2.0 covers the code, but verify how any underlying pretrained model weights are licensed for your specific commercial use before shipping a product on top of it.
- **If you want a fixed, predictable per-clip cost**, there isn't one — your cost is whatever GPU compute you spend, which can add up on long or high-resolution renders even though the software is free.

## Bottom line

Diffutoon delivers on a specific, well-defined research goal — high-resolution, temporally consistent anime-style rendering of real video — and does so as free, open, peer-reviewed code rather than a locked-down product. For developers and researchers with GPU access and Python comfort, that's a genuinely useful starting point: no subscription, no paywall, and a documented method behind it. For anyone hoping for a simple upload-and-download anime filter, the lack of a hosted interface makes this the wrong tool — a consumer-facing video-to-anime app trading some technical depth for a browser-based workflow would serve better.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Diffutoon free to use?**
Yes. It's released under the Apache-2.0 open-source license as part of the DiffSynth-Studio project, so there's no subscription fee or per-clip charge — your only cost is the GPU compute needed to run it.

**Do I need coding skills to use Diffutoon?**
Yes, in practice. There's no hosted web app; you run it by cloning the DiffSynth-Studio repository and executing Python scripts against your own footage.

**What hardware do I need to run Diffutoon?**
A CUDA-capable GPU is effectively required for reasonable render times. The project doesn't publish a strict minimum VRAM figure publicly, so check the current DiffSynth-Studio repository's requirements before committing hardware or cloud spend.

**Is Diffutoon the same as a commercial anime-filter app?**
No. Commercial anime-style video apps are typically hosted, subscription-based products with a simple upload interface. Diffutoon is the underlying research method and open-source code, not a consumer product.

**Can I use Diffutoon's output commercially?**
The code is Apache-2.0 licensed, which is permissive, but commercial use of output also depends on the licensing of whatever pretrained model weights you use with it. Confirm those terms against the current repository before commercial use.

**Where can I find example outputs before setting it up?**
The project page (ecnu-cilab.github.io/DiffutoonProjectPage) and the DiffSynth-Studio GitHub repository both include sample input/output comparisons, the fastest way to gauge quality before installing anything.

**How is Diffutoon different from running Stable Diffusion style-transfer on each frame?**
Naive frame-by-frame stylization tends to flicker and drift because each frame is generated somewhat independently. Diffutoon's paper specifically targets that with dedicated consistency-enhancement and structure-guidance components, the main technical contribution over simpler per-frame approaches.

**Is there a simpler alternative if I don't want to run code?**
For anime- or cartoon-style video conversion without touching a terminal, look for a hosted consumer video-editing tool with a built-in style filter — you'll trade some technical control and cost-free licensing for a browser-based, no-setup workflow. See [AI & software deals](/category/software) for hosted AI video tool coverage as it's added.

title: Plus AI Review 2026: AI PowerPoint Maker Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Plus AI generates decks right inside PowerPoint and Google Slides. Here's what its pricing, credits, and features mean for your team.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Plus AI Review 2026: The AI PowerPoint Maker Pricing and Verdict

Plus AI (by Plus Docs, Inc.) is an AI PowerPoint and Google Slides add-in that generates and edits full decks from a prompt or an uploaded document without leaving PowerPoint. It's a strong pick if your team already lives in PowerPoint or Slides and wants AI drafting inside that app; it's less appealing if you want a standalone web-based deck builder.

## At a glance

| | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $10/user/month (Basic, billed annually) |
| Free tier / trial | 7-day free trial, 1,000 AI credits, new customers only |
| Best for | Teams that create decks inside PowerPoint or Google Slides |
| Standout feature | Native PowerPoint add-in with an Open XML renderer, not a separate web app |

Plus AI's positioning answers a specific search intent most people typing "AI PowerPoint maker" actually have: they don't want another browser tab that exports a clunky .pptx file, they want AI help inside the PowerPoint (or Google Slides) file they already work in. That's the gap Plus AI fills, and it's worth understanding before comparing it to browser-first tools.

## What Plus AI actually is

Plus AI installs as an add-in inside Microsoft PowerPoint and as an add-on inside Google Slides. Rather than generating a deck on a separate web canvas and forcing you to export or re-import it, it builds and edits slides directly in the file format you're already using. You can type a topic or one-line prompt, upload a PDF, Word document, or existing .pptx/.txt file, and have it draft a full outline and slide set using your existing template or a library template.

The company doesn't publicly name which underlying language or image model powers generation, so treat any claims about output quality as Plus AI's own positioning rather than a documented benchmark. What is documented is the mechanism: PowerPoint decks are built with what Plus AI describes as a custom Open XML renderer, which is why formatting tends to survive edits better than tools that generate a deck externally and then convert it.

## Pricing

Plus AI prices per user, per month, with a meaningful jump in AI credit allowances between tiers. Annual billing is materially cheaper than month-to-month across every paid plan.

| Plan | Price (annual billing) | Price (monthly billing) | AI credits/month | Who it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free trial | $0 for 7 days | $0 for 7 days | 1,000 (one-time) | Testing before you commit, new customers only |
| Basic | $10/user/month | $15/user/month | 1,500 | Solo users creating and remixing decks |
| Pro | $20/user/month | $25/user/month | 3,000 | Individuals/teams needing document uploads and AI image generation |
| Team | $30/user/month | $40/user/month | 6,000 | Teams needing custom branding and shared presets |
| Max | $200/user/month | $240/user/month | Unlimited | Heavy users who don't want to think about credit limits |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Orgs needing SSO and centralized user management |

There is no permanently free plan — Plus AI's only no-cost access is the 7-day trial, and it's restricted to new customers, which is worth knowing if you were hoping to use it occasionally at zero cost the way you might with a browser-based generator that has an ongoing free tier.

Pricing, credit allowances, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current figures on Plus AI's own pricing page before buying, since AI tool pricing moves fast.

## Features that actually differentiate it

**Native PowerPoint and Google Slides integration.** This is the core differentiator. Most AI deck generators build a presentation on their own web canvas and then let you export a .pptx or push to Slides — a lossy step that often breaks fonts, spacing, or animations. Plus AI skips that step entirely by rendering inside the file format itself.

**Document-to-deck conversion.** On Pro and above, you can upload a PDF, Word doc, .pptx, or plain text file and have Plus AI turn it into a structured slide outline. This is genuinely useful for turning a long report or proposal into a client-ready deck without manually re-keying content.

**Remix.** Rather than regenerating a slide from scratch, Remix takes an existing slide and reformats it into a different layout while keeping the content — handy when a generated slide has the right words but the wrong visual structure.

**Custom instructions and preset libraries (Team plan).** Teams can save brand guidelines, tone instructions, and slide layout presets so that everyone generating decks produces output that's roughly on-brand without a design pass every time.

**Multilingual generation.** Plus AI can read, write, and translate across multiple languages, which matters for global teams building the same deck for different regions rather than manually translating slide by slide.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo consultants and freelancers** who build decks occasionally will likely find the Basic plan ($10/month annual) sufficient — 1,500 credits per month covers a handful of full-deck generations plus edits, though heavy remixing can burn through that faster than expected.
- **Individual power users** who need to convert long documents into decks regularly should look at Pro, since document upload is gated behind that tier.
- **Marketing, sales, and consulting teams** that need consistent branding across everyone's decks are the target for the Team plan — custom branding and shared presets solve the "every rep's deck looks different" problem.
- **Agencies or high-volume teams** generating dozens of decks a week may find even 6,000 monthly credits tight and should budget for Max or negotiate Enterprise.
- **Large organizations** with SSO and compliance requirements should go straight to Enterprise and get IT involved before rollout, since Plus AI states SOC 2 Type II compliance but a formal security review is still worth doing for regulated industries.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Generates directly inside PowerPoint/Slides, not a separate export step | No ongoing free plan — only a 7-day trial for new users |
| Document upload turns reports/PDFs into decks (Pro+) | Underlying AI model isn't publicly disclosed |
| Credit-based pricing scales with actual usage instead of flat seats | Entry-tier credit allowance (1,500) is easy to exhaust with a few full decks |
| Team presets and custom branding keep multi-user output consistent | Jump from Team to Max ($30 to $200/user/month) is steep if you outgrow 6,000 credits |
| SOC 2 Type II compliance and enterprise integrations (Salesforce, Airtable, Zapier) | Best features (uploads, image gen, custom instructions) require Pro or Team, not Basic |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Plus AI connects to Zapier, Notion, Asana, Atlassian, Airtable, and Salesforce, and offers a Presentation Agent API, an MCP server, and a PowerPoint API for developers who want to trigger deck generation programmatically rather than through the add-in UI. That's a wider integration surface than most presentation-generator competitors, which tend to stop at basic export options.

## Where it's a strong fit

If your organization has standardized on PowerPoint or Google Slides and the friction is "our team spends hours formatting decks that already have the right content," Plus AI addresses that directly. It's also a reasonable fit for teams that already use Salesforce, Notion, or Airtable as a source of truth and want deck generation wired into that workflow via the API or Zapier, rather than manually copying data into a prompt box.

## Where to think twice

Skip Plus AI if you need a genuinely free, ongoing tool — the 7-day trial is a taste, not a long-term free tier, and competitors like Gamma offer a persistent (if limited) free plan. It's also not the right pick if you want a standalone web app you can access from anywhere without PowerPoint or Google Slides installed or licensed; Plus AI is built as an add-in, so you need the host application. Teams that need heavy AI image generation as a primary feature rather than a supporting one should evaluate dedicated image tools, since Plus AI's image generation is a feature within the deck workflow rather than the product's focus. And because the underlying model isn't disclosed, teams with strict AI-vendor-disclosure requirements should ask Plus AI directly before procurement.

## The bottom line

Plus AI solves a real, specific problem: getting AI-generated slide content into PowerPoint or Google Slides without the export-and-fix-formatting step that plagues browser-first generators. The pricing is usage-based rather than flat, which is fair for light users but can get expensive fast for teams that generate a lot of decks and blow through the Team plan's 6,000 monthly credits into Max's $200/user/month tier. If you're evaluating it against a browser-based tool like [Gamma](/blog/gamma-review), the decision mostly comes down to whether you want to stay inside PowerPoint/Slides (Plus AI) or you're fine working in a new web canvas and exporting when you're done (Gamma).

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Plus AI free?**
No, not on an ongoing basis. Plus AI offers a 7-day free trial with 1,000 AI credits for new customers, but there's no permanent free plan — after the trial you need a paid subscription starting at $10/user/month billed annually.

**Does Plus AI work with both PowerPoint and Google Slides?**
Yes. It installs as a native add-in in Microsoft PowerPoint and as an add-on in Google Slides, and the trial and paid plans cover both.

**What happens if I run out of AI credits?**
Once your monthly credit allowance is used, you'd need to upgrade to a higher tier (or wait for the next billing cycle's refresh) to keep generating and editing with AI. The exact behavior when credits run out should be confirmed on Plus AI's own site, since specifics can change.

**Can Plus AI turn an existing document into a slide deck?**
Yes, on the Pro plan and above you can upload PDFs, Word documents, existing PowerPoint files, or plain text and have Plus AI convert them into a structured slide outline.

**Which AI model does Plus AI use?**
Plus AI doesn't publicly disclose the specific underlying model on its marketing pages. If model provenance matters for your procurement process, ask their sales team directly before subscribing.

**Is Plus AI good for teams, or just individuals?**
Both, but the Team plan (custom branding, shared presets, unlimited team members) is specifically built for keeping multiple people's decks consistent, which the Basic and Pro tiers don't offer.

**How does Plus AI compare to Gamma or other AI deck generators?**
The core difference is delivery: Plus AI generates and edits inside the PowerPoint or Google Slides file itself, while tools like [Gamma](/blog/gamma-review) generate on their own web canvas first and export or share from there. Choose based on whether your workflow is PowerPoint-native or you're comfortable starting in a new app.

**Does Plus AI have enterprise security features?**
Plus AI states it is SOC 2 Type II compliant and offers an Enterprise plan with SSO and centralized user management. Organizations with strict compliance requirements should still run their own security review before rollout.

For more AI and productivity software coverage, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: FLUX.1 [dev] Review 2026: License, Pricing, Where to Run It
excerpt: FLUX.1 [dev] review: what Black Forest Labs' open-weight model does, its non-commercial license, pricing, and how it differs from pro and schnell.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is FLUX.1 [dev] worth using?

Yes, if you want near-flagship image quality without paying per-image API fees and you're working on personal, research, or non-revenue projects — it's free to download, runs on a single high-VRAM consumer GPU, and produces output close to FLUX.1 [pro]. It's the wrong pick the moment a project generates revenue, since the weights themselves are licensed non-commercial only.

**At a glance**

| | FLUX.1 [dev] |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free to download and self-host; usage-based when run through an API host |
| Free tier | Yes — full model weights, no account or subscription required from Black Forest Labs |
| Best for | Hobbyists, researchers, and technical teams who want pro-tier quality on their own hardware |
| Standout feature | Guidance-distilled 12B transformer that runs in far fewer steps than a typical diffusion model, under a license that explicitly allows commercial use of the images it produces |

FLUX.1 [dev] is one of three image-generation models Black Forest Labs released together in mid-2024 under the FLUX.1 name — the team founded by several of the researchers behind Stable Diffusion. It's a 12-billion-parameter rectified-flow transformer, and Black Forest Labs' own materials describe it as "second only to" the flagship FLUX.1 [pro] in output quality, while being open-weight and runnable outside their own API.

That's the whole pitch: dev is the version you can download, inspect, fine-tune, and run locally, trading a bit of quality and some usage rights for that freedom. It's not a hosted app with a dashboard — it's a model file plus a license agreement, and how you use it depends entirely on where you run it.

### What it actually is, and how it's built

The model uses a flow-matching architecture rather than the classic denoising-diffusion approach older Stable Diffusion versions used, part of why it needs noticeably fewer sampling steps to converge on a clean image. Black Forest Labs trained FLUX.1 [dev] with **guidance distillation** — a technique that bakes classifier-free guidance behavior into the model weights themselves, so it doesn't need a separate negative-prompt pass at inference time the way many earlier text-to-image models did.

In practice, FLUX.1 [dev] typically needs around 20–50 inference steps at a guidance scale near 3.5 to produce a finished image — fewer than a comparable non-distilled diffusion model, though still more than its faster sibling. The weights are published on Hugging Face and support the standard `diffusers` library, plus community tooling like ComfyUI, so most of the open-source image-gen ecosystem (LoRAs, ControlNet adapters, inpainting workflows) already works with it.

### License terms — the part that actually matters here

This is the section to read carefully, because it's the whole reason dev exists as a separate release from pro. FLUX.1 [dev] ships under Black Forest Labs' **Non-Commercial License**, and the key terms are:

- **The weights are non-commercial only.** Personal projects, hobby work, academic research, and non-production R&D testing are fine. Explicitly excluded: any "revenue-generating activity," any use that directly interacts with or affects end users (a paid app, a client-facing SaaS feature), and using the model's outputs to train a competing commercial model.
- **Generated images are treated differently from the model itself.** Black Forest Labs states it claims no ownership over the images FLUX.1 [dev] produces, and that outputs can be used "for any purpose (including for commercial purposes)" — with the exception of using them to train a rival model. That's a useful carve-out: a freelancer can, in principle, generate art with a locally-run dev model and sell the resulting image, even though running dev itself as a paid generation service would violate the license.
- **Redistribution comes with obligations.** Sharing the model or a fine-tuned derivative requires including the license text, attributing Black Forest Labs, and disclosing modifications — you can't repackage it as an official release.

If any of that reads as more nuance than you want to manage, that's the exact gap FLUX.1 [pro] is built to close — it's Black Forest Labs' commercially licensed, API-only tier, accessed through their own endpoint or partners like Replicate. **FLUX.1 [schnell]**, the third sibling, takes the opposite trade-off from dev: it's distilled even further for speed (Black Forest Labs' own materials point to single-digit step counts) and ships under a permissive Apache 2.0 license that allows commercial use of the weights themselves, at some cost to peak image fidelity compared to dev or pro.

So the three-way split is genuinely about different jobs: **schnell** for fast, commercially-clear iteration; **dev** for the best quality you can self-host, with commercial use of the model restricted; **pro** for commercial production use, paid per image through an API.

### Running FLUX.1 [dev] — where and how

There's no single "FLUX.1 [dev] app" — you pick a runtime that fits your setup:

- **Hugging Face + Diffusers** — the reference way to run it in Python, with the model card walking through the `diffusers` pipeline setup.
- **ComfyUI** — the most common way hobbyists run it locally with a node-based visual workflow, plus community LoRAs and ControlNet models built specifically for FLUX.
- **Local desktop apps** — tools like Draw Things (macOS/iOS) and DiffusionBee package FLUX.1 [dev] behind a simpler UI for people who don't want to touch Python.
- **API hosts** — Replicate, fal.ai, and a handful of other inference providers offer FLUX.1 [dev] as a pay-per-image API, a practical middle ground if you don't own a GPU with enough VRAM but still want the non-commercial dev model rather than paying pro rates. Exact per-image pricing varies by host and output resolution — check the provider's pricing page before committing.

Running it yourself needs real hardware: expect a GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM for comfortable full-precision inference, though quantized and lower-precision community builds have brought that requirement down for consumer cards. Pricing and hosting-provider rates mentioned here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can shift quickly — confirm current figures before budgeting a project around them.

### Core capabilities that actually differentiate it

- **Strong prompt adherence** — handles multi-subject and compositionally complex prompts noticeably better than many earlier open-weight diffusion models.
- **Text rendering inside images** — meaningfully better than older Stable Diffusion checkpoints at legible in-image text (signage, labels, short phrases), though still not flawless.
- **Fine-tunability** — because the weights are open, the community has produced LoRAs, ControlNet variants, and fine-tuned checkpoints built on FLUX.1 [dev], which don't exist for the closed pro tier.
- **Fewer steps than classic diffusion** — the guidance-distilled architecture means faster local generation than a non-distilled model of similar size, though still slower than schnell.
- **Full pipeline control** — resolution, sampler, LoRA stacking, and inpainting workflows are all configurable, versus the fixed parameters an API-only model like pro gives you.

### Who it's actually for

- **Hobbyists and artists** experimenting on their own machine — dev is effectively the best open-weight image quality available to run locally, and the commercial-use carve-out for generated images means a personal art project or portfolio piece isn't off-limits.
- **Researchers and ML engineers** — open weights, published architecture details, and Hugging Face integration make it a realistic base for academic work or model comparisons without an API budget.
- **Technical teams prototyping internal tools** — as long as the use stays non-production (internal demos, R&D evaluation), dev is a reasonable way to test a FLUX-quality pipeline before licensing pro for the real product.
- **Anyone building a paid product, client-facing app, or commercial API around image generation** should skip dev entirely and go straight to FLUX.1 [pro] or a properly licensed hosting arrangement — running dev in that context breaks the license regardless of how the outputs are used.

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Free to download, no account required | Non-commercial license restricts how the model itself can be used |
| Near-pro-tier image quality in an open-weight release | Needs a high-VRAM GPU for comfortable local inference |
| Broad ecosystem support (Diffusers, ComfyUI, LoRAs, ControlNet) | No official hosted app or dashboard — you assemble your own workflow |
| Generated outputs can be used commercially with no BFL royalty | Slower per-image than FLUX.1 [schnell] |
| Fine-tunable — community checkpoints and LoRAs already exist | License terms require careful reading before any team/business use |

### Integrations and ecosystem

FLUX.1 [dev] isn't a platform with a plugin marketplace, but it slots into tools most people running open-weight image models already use: the Hugging Face `diffusers` library for scripted pipelines, ComfyUI for node-based local workflows, and community-maintained LoRA and ControlNet checkpoints built for the FLUX architecture. On the hosted side, Replicate and fal.ai both expose it as an API endpoint — useful for testing without managing GPU infrastructure, though a host's own API access doesn't override Black Forest Labs' underlying non-commercial license on the weights.

### Where it's a strong fit

FLUX.1 [dev] earns its place for anyone who wants the best image quality they can run outside a paid API and doesn't need to monetize the output pipeline itself — students, researchers, digital artists building a personal portfolio, and technical teams evaluating FLUX before committing budget to the pro tier. Strong prompt adherence, decent text rendering, and a genuinely permissive stance on commercial use of *outputs* (not the model) cover a surprising amount of real-world use without ever touching an API bill.

### Where to think twice

Skip FLUX.1 [dev] if you need to run the model itself as part of a revenue-generating product — a paid app, a client deliverable built on your own hosted instance, or any service with direct end-user impact — that's exactly what the non-commercial license prohibits. It's also not the right pick without access to a capable GPU or budget for a hosting provider's per-image rate, or if your team needs a vendor relationship with support, SLAs, or indemnification, none of which come with a self-hosted download. If turnaround speed matters more than peak quality, FLUX.1 [schnell] will generally get you to a usable image faster.

### Bottom line

FLUX.1 [dev] is best understood as Black Forest Labs' answer to "give us the good model, but let us run it ourselves" — and it delivers on that fairly directly, at the cost of a license that keeps the model itself out of anything commercial. For research, hobby projects, and evaluating whether FLUX-quality output is worth paying for at all, it's hard to beat for the price of zero dollars and a GPU. The moment a project needs to make money from what dev generates through your own hosted instance, it's time to move to FLUX.1 [pro] or a licensed commercial host instead.

### FAQ

**Is FLUX.1 [dev] free to use?**
Yes — the model weights are free to download from Hugging Face after accepting the non-commercial license. Running it costs whatever compute you use, whether that's your own GPU or a pay-per-image API host.

**Can I use images I generate with FLUX.1 [dev] commercially?**
Generally yes — Black Forest Labs states it claims no ownership of outputs and permits their use for any purpose, including commercial ones, with the exception of using those outputs to train a competing model. The restriction is on running the *model* commercially, not on what you do with the images it produces. Read the current license text on Hugging Face before relying on this for a business decision, since terms can be updated.

**What's the difference between FLUX.1 [dev], [pro], and [schnell]?**
Schnell is the fastest and most permissively licensed (Apache 2.0, commercial use of the model itself allowed) but trades some peak quality for speed. Dev sits in the middle — near-pro image quality, open weights, non-commercial licensing on the model. Pro is Black Forest Labs' commercially licensed, API-only flagship, priced per image through their own endpoint or hosting partners.

**Do I need a powerful GPU to run FLUX.1 [dev]?**
For comfortable full-precision local inference, plan on a GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM. Quantized and lower-precision community builds have made it runnable on smaller cards, with some trade-off in speed or quality.

**Where can I run FLUX.1 [dev] without owning a GPU?**
API hosts including Replicate and fal.ai offer it as a pay-per-image endpoint, avoiding the hardware requirement while keeping the non-commercial licensing terms in force. Confirm current per-image pricing directly with the host.

**Is FLUX.1 [dev] the same as Stable Diffusion?**
No. Black Forest Labs was founded by several former Stability AI researchers, and FLUX.1 uses a different flow-matching transformer architecture rather than the classic diffusion approach behind Stable Diffusion — separate models from separate companies.

**Does FLUX.1 [dev] support fine-tuning and LoRAs?**
Yes — because the weights are openly published, the community has built LoRA adapters, ControlNet models, and fine-tuned checkpoints specifically for FLUX.1 [dev], one of its main advantages over the closed pro tier.

**Is there a hosted, no-code way to try FLUX.1 [dev]?**
Yes — several API hosts and community demo spaces on Hugging Face let you try prompts without setting up a local environment, though a demo space's usage limits and a production API's terms are worth checking separately.

For more open-weight and commercial AI image models, see our coverage in the [AI & software deals](/category/software) section.

title: Free Face Swap Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: FaceSwapper.ai review: is this no-signup, no-credit AI face swap tool for photos, video and GIFs actually free and worth using?
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Free Face Swap (FaceSwapper.ai) Actually Free, and Is It Any Good?

FaceSwapper.ai is a browser-based face-swap tool that lets anyone swap faces in photos, videos, GIFs and group shots without creating an account or paying for credits. It's a solid pick for quick, casual swaps and memes, but it's a single-purpose novelty tool, not a photo-editing suite, and its output quality can't be independently verified beyond the vendor's own claims.

### At a glance

| | Details |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $0 — no paid plan currently listed |
| **Free tier/trial** | Fully free; no sign-up, no credits, no watermark |
| **Best for** | Quick photo/video/GIF face swaps, memes, group photos |
| **Standout feature** | Video and multi-face batch swapping with no account required |

A quick note on naming: "Free Face Swap" isn't a single trademarked product name — several tools use similar generic branding. This review covers **FaceSwapper.ai**, which markets itself explicitly as "a completely free face swap experience" with no credits, no paywall, and no sign-up wall, the closest real match to that description. It's a different product from [Remaker AI](/blog/remaker-ai-review), the credit-based face-swap-plus-photo-editing toolkit already covered on this site — more on that difference below.

## What FaceSwapper.ai Actually Is

FaceSwapper.ai is a single-purpose web app built around one job: taking a source face and mapping it onto a target photo, video, or GIF. There's no desktop client and no mobile app listed on the site — everything runs in the browser at faceswapper.ai. The company doesn't publish which underlying face-swap or diffusion model powers the tool, so treat any "natural, vivid, and realistic" quality claims as the vendor's own marketing language rather than a benchmarked fact.

The site bundles a cluster of related tools under the same free-access model:

- Photo face swap (single face, one-to-one)
- Video face swap (replace a face throughout a video clip)
- Multi-face swap (swap multiple faces in a group photo at once)
- GIF face swap (swap a face across an animated GIF)
- Batch face swap (apply the same source face across multiple photos in one pass)
- A clothes swapper, gender swap, and AI face/AI girl generator listed as adjacent tools

That last group signals what kind of product this is: a fast, free, meme-and-novelty-oriented utility, not a professional retouching or VFX tool. If you need production-grade compositing for film, marketing, or brand work, this isn't the tier of tool for that job.

## Pricing

There isn't much to say here because there isn't a pricing tier to compare. As of this review's publish date, FaceSwapper.ai's own pricing page returns a message saying pricing isn't available and that the site's functions "can still be used for free." No credit packs, subscription, or paid upgrade path were found anywhere on the site.

| Plan | Price | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Free (only option) | $0 | Unlimited stated face swaps across photo, video, GIF, multi-face and batch tools, no sign-up, no watermark |

That's unusual in this category — most comparable tools (including Remaker AI) meter usage through credits or cap free-tier swaps per day. Whether FaceSwapper.ai stays fully free long-term or eventually introduces paid tiers, as many "free forever" AI tools do once traffic scales, isn't predictable from the current site alone — confirm current terms on the official site before relying on it for repeated or commercial use. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability noted here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly in the AI tools space.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**No sign-up, no credit meter.** The biggest practical difference between this tool and most competitors is that there's genuinely no account wall. You land on the page, upload a source face and a target image, and get a result — no email capture, no "sign up to unlock your first 3 swaps" gate that so many free AI tools use as a lead-generation trick.

**Video and GIF face swap, not just static photos.** A lot of "free face swap" tools online only handle still images and push video swapping behind a paywall. FaceSwapper.ai lists video and GIF swapping as part of the same free toolset — useful for short clips, reaction GIFs, and social content — though very long or high-resolution videos will likely hit practical processing-time ceilings even without a formal paywall (the site doesn't publish exact limits, so test with your actual file before relying on it).

**Batch and multi-face swapping.** If you've got a folder of group photos and want the same face swapped into all of them, the batch tool avoids repeating the manual upload-and-swap cycle for every image. Multi-face swap does the group-photo version of the same idea in a single pass.

**Fast turnaround.** The vendor states results generate "within seconds," consistent with how most consumer face-swap tools operate, though actual speed will vary with file size and server load — this wasn't independently timed for this review.

**Adjacent generator tools.** Beyond swapping, the site also lists a clothes swapper, gender swap, and an AI face/AI girl generator, rounding out the "have fun with a photo" use case the tool is built around.

## Who It's Actually For

- **Casual users and meme-makers** — anyone who wants to swap a face into a photo for a laugh, a group chat, or a social post gets full functionality with zero friction and zero cost.
- **Content creators making quick social clips** — the free video and GIF swap tools can speed up short-form content without needing a paid subscription just to test the idea.
- **Anyone who's already tried a credit-metered competitor and hit a wall** — if a tool like Remaker AI has burned through your free credits, FaceSwapper.ai is a reasonable free fallback for occasional use.
- **Not a fit for professional/commercial production work** — there's no published API, no team seats, no commercial licensing terms, and no stated quality guarantee. Studios, agencies, or anyone needing consistent, licensable, production-grade output should look elsewhere.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Completely free — no sign-up, no credits, no watermark | No published paid tier means no guaranteed support, SLA, or roadmap commitment |
| Covers photo, video, GIF, multi-face and batch swapping in one place | Underlying AI model isn't disclosed, so output quality can't be independently benchmarked |
| No account wall or email-gated "free trial" | No API, mobile app, or team/enterprise features |
| Fast, simple interface aimed at quick tasks | Pricing page currently shows a placeholder message rather than real terms, which is a mild reliability flag |
| Uploads are stated to be deleted after processing | No published limits on video length/resolution — could hit practical ceilings without warning |

## Integrations and Ecosystem

There's no meaningful integration ecosystem here. No API for developers, no Zapier connector, no Slack or Discord bot, and no browser extension were found on the site. This is a standalone consumer web tool you use directly in a browser tab, not something you'd wire into a larger workflow or app. If integration into an automated pipeline matters to you, this isn't the right category of tool — look at API-first alternatives instead.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

- You want to swap a face into a photo, video, or GIF right now, for free, without registering anywhere
- You're doing a one-off task (a meme, a party photo, a quick social clip) rather than an ongoing production workflow
- You've already used up free credits on a metered competitor and just need an occasional free swap

## Where to Think Twice

- **If you need guaranteed data handling for sensitive or professional work** — the site states uploads are deleted after processing, but there's no independently verifiable SOC 2 or enterprise-grade compliance documentation published, so treat it as consumer-grade privacy, not enterprise-grade.
- **If you need an API or need to integrate face swapping into an app or automated pipeline** — there's none available here.
- **If you're producing anything commercial that needs a stable roadmap and support channel** — a tool with an unpublished, "not available now" pricing page is a signal the business model may still be in flux, which isn't ideal if you're depending on it long-term.
- **If you need consistently high-fidelity output for professional use** — without a disclosed model or third-party benchmarks, quality is inherently unverified; test it yourself with a non-critical image before trusting it for anything that matters.
- **If accuracy on complex faces matters** — side angles, glasses, or unusual lighting can trip up any consumer face-swap tool; expect occasional artifacts, and verify with your own images before relying on it.

## Bottom Line

FaceSwapper.ai delivers on the "free face swap" promise better than most of the category — no account, no credits, no paywall for photo, video, GIF, or batch swapping. For casual, one-off use it's hard to beat on price. But the lack of a published pricing model, disclosed AI backend, or any integration options means it's not a tool to build a workflow around — it's a fast, free utility for a fun result, not a professional or dependable production tool. If you need more structure — credit packs, a broader photo-editing toolkit, or mobile apps — a tool like [Remaker AI](/blog/remaker-ai-review) is worth comparing before you commit either way.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is FaceSwapper.ai actually free, or is there a hidden paywall?**
Based on the current site, yes — there's no credit system, no subscription, and no sign-up wall for its photo, video, GIF, multi-face, or batch face-swap tools. The pricing page itself states no paid plan is currently available and that the site's functions can still be used for free.

**Do I need to create an account to use it?**
No. The tool is usable directly without registration, which is unusual in this category — most competitors gate at least some features behind a free account.

**What happens to the photos or videos I upload?**
The site states uploaded files "are fully protected and only visible to you," and that files are not stored on their servers and are deleted after your result is generated. Confirm the current privacy policy directly on the site before uploading anything sensitive, since these terms can change.

**Does it work on video, or just photos?**
Both. Video face swap and GIF face swap are listed as free tools alongside photo swapping, along with multi-face and batch swap options.

**Is there a mobile app?**
No dedicated mobile app was found on the site as of this review — it runs entirely in the browser, which also means it works on mobile browsers without installing anything.

**How does it compare to Remaker AI?**
Remaker AI is a broader, credit-metered toolkit that bundles face swap with AI photo editing, upscaling, and background removal, and it does have paid credit packs. FaceSwapper.ai is narrower and fully free but doesn't offer that wider editing toolkit or a published account/subscription tier. Read the full [Remaker AI review](/blog/remaker-ai-review) for the credit-pricing breakdown.

**Is the output quality good enough for professional use?**
Treat it as consumer-grade. The vendor doesn't disclose the underlying model, and there's no independent benchmark available, so test it yourself on a non-critical image before relying on it for client or commercial work.

**Are there usage limits on video length or file size?**
The site doesn't publish specific limits for video length, resolution, or file size. Assume very large or long files may hit practical processing ceilings even without a formal paid tier, and check the site directly if you're planning a larger batch job.

For more free and paid AI tools worth checking before you commit to one, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Midday Review 2026: Why the AI Finance Tool Is Shutting Down
excerpt: Midday was an AI finance OS for freelancers — now it's winding down into Ramp. Here's what happened and what to use instead.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Midday Review 2026: Why It's Shutting Down and What to Use Instead

Midday was a well-regarded all-in-one finance OS for freelancers and small businesses — invoicing, bank sync, receipt matching, time tracking and an AI assistant in one dashboard. As of this review, Midday is being acquired by Ramp and winding down over 90 days, so new signups aren't a sensible bet; existing users get data export and migration paths, and anyone shopping for this category should look at Ramp or an active alternative instead.

### At a glance

| | Midday |
| --- | --- |
| Status as of this review | Winding down — acquired by Ramp, ~90-day shutdown window |
| Starting price | No longer publicly listed (pricing page replaced by the wind-down notice) |
| Free tier/trial | Historically offered a free trial; not confirmed still active |
| Best for | Freelancers and small teams who previously used it for invoicing + bookkeeping |
| Standout feature | Automatic receipt-to-transaction matching pulled from email and connected accounts |

## What Midday actually was

Midday (midday.ai) was built by founders Pontus and Viktor as a bootstrapped side project that grew into a full product used by, in their own words, "thousands of founders and freelancers." The pitch: instead of juggling a separate invoicing tool, a spreadsheet for expenses, a time tracker and a folder of scanned receipts, Midday put the financial back-office of a small business or solo operation into one connected dashboard.

Core to the product was bank account syncing, invoicing with online payment collection, automatic reconciliation that matched receipts and invoices pulled from email against transactions, time tracking tied to projects and clients, and an accounting export designed to hand off cleanly to a bookkeeper. Midday also added AI-assistant integrations, supporting connections to tools like Claude and ChatGPT alongside various automation platforms, positioning itself as an "AI-powered" operations layer rather than a plain bookkeeping app.

## The news that changes this review: Midday is joining Ramp

This is the part of the review that matters most if you're evaluating Midday today. Midday's own site no longer shows a pricing page — visiting `midday.ai/pricing` now redirects to an announcement titled "Midday is Joining Ramp." Midday is being acquired by Ramp, the corporate-card and spend-management company, and the standalone product will wind down over the following three months.

The founders describe the move as driven by shared values with Ramp around "craft, speed, and building software that feels like someone gave a damn," framing Midday's experience handling "real money, real workflows, real edge cases" as the reason the team is folding into what the announcement calls Ramp's "category-leading AI platform for finance." For existing customers, the stated terms are:

- Direct email notification sent to all customers about the transition
- Refunds offered on annual subscription plans that were paid in advance
- Full data export available before the shutdown completes
- Accounts remain active for roughly 90 days with continued export access during that window
- Eligible customers are offered a personalized migration path into Ramp
- The founders explicitly state customer data "is yours" throughout the transition

What isn't stated publicly is an exact calendar date for when access ends, or what specific Ramp product tier absorbed users will land on. If you're a current Midday user, the safest move is to export everything (transactions, invoices, receipts, time entries) well before the 90-day window closes, and to confirm any annual-plan refund directly with Midday support rather than assuming it happens automatically.

## Pricing — what's known and what isn't

Midday historically ran as a subscription SaaS product aimed at freelancers and small teams, with the usual freemium-to-paid structure common in this category (a limited free tier or trial, then monthly/annual paid plans scaled by usage or seats). At the time of writing, however, the specific tier names and dollar amounts are no longer published anywhere on midday.ai — the pricing page has been fully replaced by the acquisition announcement, and no other official page currently lists plan pricing.

This review won't quote specific dollar amounts for Midday's plans, since that information can no longer be checked against a live source and should be treated as unverifiable. If you're an existing customer trying to confirm what you were charged or whether you qualify for a refund, contact Midday support directly through your account rather than relying on a cached pricing page.

Pricing, free-tier limits and feature availability described here reflect what was verifiable as of this post's publish date and can change quickly, especially for a product actively in wind-down — treat this as a snapshot, not a live quote, and confirm current status on midday.ai before acting on it.

## Core features walkthrough (as the product existed)

**Bank sync and transaction feed.** Midday connected to business bank accounts and payment platforms and pulled transactions in automatically, which was the backbone the rest of the product built on — invoices, expenses and reports were all anchored to this live feed rather than manual entry.

**Invoicing with built-in payment collection.** Users could send invoices directly from the platform, with customers able to pay online rather than being redirected to a separate checkout flow. This kept the "send invoice → get paid → reconcile" loop inside one tool instead of three.

**Automatic receipt matching.** Midday's stated differentiator was pulling receipts and invoices out of connected email accounts and automatically matching them against bank transactions for reconciliation — the manual step most small-business owners dread was meant to happen in the background.

**Time tracking tied to projects and clients.** Freelancers and small agencies could log hours against specific projects, which fed back into invoicing and gave a picture of which clients or projects were actually profitable.

**AI assistant and integrations.** Midday positioned an AI layer on top of the financial data, with support for connecting external AI tools (the vendor names Claude and ChatGPT specifically) and various automation platforms, aimed at surfacing insights rather than just storing data.

## Who it was actually for

- **Solo freelancers** who wanted one dashboard instead of separate invoicing, expense-tracking and time-tracking tools were the core audience — the product's design leaned toward reducing app-switching for a one-person operation.
- **Small agencies and two-to-five person teams** could use the client/project structure to track time and invoicing per client, though team-tier specifics are no longer verifiable.
- **Businesses needing enterprise compliance or on-prem deployment** were never the target — Midday's positioning (and its SOC 2 certification reportedly still "in progress" at the time of the acquisition announcement) fit small, fast-moving operations rather than regulated enterprises.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Combined invoicing, bank sync, receipts and time tracking in one product | No longer a going concern for new customers — wind-down in progress |
| Automatic receipt-to-transaction matching cut down manual reconciliation work | Pricing and full feature set are no longer publicly documented |
| Built by founders who developed it publicly and iterated with user feedback | SOC 2 certification was reportedly still in progress, not yet complete |
| Clean data-export and refund terms for existing users during the transition | Migration into Ramp's product may mean a materially different tool, not a like-for-like continuation |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Midday's own AI integrations reportedly supported connecting external assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT, plus unspecified "various automation platforms" — likely covering common workflow tools rather than a deep, documented API ecosystem. No public developer API documentation was independently verifiable at the time of this review, and given the wind-down, building new integrations against Midday today isn't a sound investment of engineering time.

## Where it was a strong fit

If you were a freelancer or very small team drowning in disconnected tools — an invoicing app here, a spreadsheet for expenses there, a separate time tracker somewhere else — Midday's pitch of one connected dashboard solved a real, common pain point. The automatic receipt matching in particular addressed a task most solo operators do badly or skip entirely, and doing it from email rather than manual upload was a meaningful convenience.

## Where to think twice

The overriding reason to think twice is timing: Midday is shutting down as a standalone product within roughly 90 days of its acquisition announcement, so signing up today means planning a migration almost immediately. Skip it if:

- **You need a tool you can commit to for the next year or more** — Midday isn't that right now, regardless of how good the product was.
- **You need current, verifiable pricing before you can get budget approval** — that information isn't published anywhere on the official site anymore.
- **You need SOC 2-certified compliance today** — the certification was reportedly still in progress, not finished, as of the acquisition announcement.
- **You're an existing user who hasn't exported your data yet** — this should be a priority regardless of how this review is used, since account access is time-limited.

## Bottom line

Midday was a genuinely useful finance dashboard for freelancers and small businesses, and its acquisition by Ramp is framed by its founders as a natural extension rather than a failure — but for anyone deciding whether to sign up today, the practical answer is: don't, at least not for the standalone product. Existing customers should export their data and confirm migration or refund status with Midday support well before the 90-day window closes. Anyone new to this category should look at Ramp directly, or compare other active invoicing-and-bookkeeping tools.

For other current AI and software tools worth comparing, see the [AI & software deals](/category/software) category.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Midday still available to sign up for?**
Midday's official pricing page has been replaced by its acquisition announcement, and the product is winding down over roughly 90 days from that announcement — treat any pricing or signup information you find elsewhere as potentially outdated and confirm directly on midday.ai.

**What happens to my data if I was already a Midday customer?**
Existing customers get full data export, continued account access for about 90 days, refunds on prepaid annual plans, and a personalized migration path to Ramp for eligible accounts, per the official announcement. Contact Midday support to confirm specifics for your account.

**Why did Midday shut down instead of continuing independently?**
The founders describe it as joining Ramp rather than failing — citing shared values around product craft and Ramp's position as a "category-leading AI platform for finance." It's presented as an acquisition and team integration, not a collapse.

**Is Ramp a direct replacement for Midday?**
Ramp is a different, larger product built primarily around corporate cards and spend management, with Midday's team and technology folding into it — not necessarily a feature-for-feature continuation of Midday's freelancer-focused tools. Confirm which Ramp tier and features apply to your use case.

**What should freelancers use instead of Midday right now?**
Compare active, currently-supported invoicing and bookkeeping tools alongside Ramp itself, and prioritize tools with clear, currently published pricing pages rather than a product mid-wind-down.

**Did Midday have a free plan, and was it SOC 2 certified?**
Midday historically offered some form of free trial or entry tier, standard for this SaaS category, but exact terms are no longer published. SOC 2 certification was reportedly still in progress, not complete, as of the acquisition announcement, alongside stated GDPR compliance.

**Is my financial data safe during the Midday-to-Ramp transition?**
The founders state customer data remains customer-owned throughout the transition and full export is available, but verify specific security or compliance requirements directly with Midday or Ramp support.

title: Fotor AI Anime Generator Review 2026: Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Fotor's AI Anime Generator turns photos and prompts into anime art free, watermark-free. Here's the pricing, features, and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Fotor's AI Anime Generator worth using?

Fotor's AI Anime Generator turns text prompts or uploaded photos into anime-style art in seconds, with a decent range of styles (chibi, shonen, cyberpunk, Ghibli-esque filters) and no watermark on exports. It's a good free-to-cheap option for anime avatars and fan art, but it's a feature bolted onto a broader photo-editing suite, not a dedicated anime platform, and Fotor's own billing draws recurring complaints worth knowing first.

Note: "AI Anime Generator" isn't a single trademarked product — dozens of apps use nearly identical generic names. This review covers the **AI Anime Generator built into Fotor** (fotor.com), made by Everimaging, one of the most established tools matching that description. If you landed here looking for a different app with the same label, the mechanics — prompt or photo in, style picked, image out — are similar across competitors, but credit systems and pricing differ.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (credit-based); paid plans start around the Fotor Pro tier |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — new accounts get starter credits, plus more via daily check-ins or community sharing |
| Best for | Quick anime avatars, chibi/fan-art style portraits, photo-to-anime conversions |
| Standout feature | Watermark-free exports even on the free tier, with both text-to-anime and photo-to-anime modes |

## What Fotor's AI Anime Generator actually is

Fotor is a browser- and app-based design and photo-editing platform originally built around collage-making and photo touch-ups; it's been around for over a decade and has since bolted on a wide AI toolkit — background removal, AI headshots, image upscaling, and, relevant here, an AI Anime Generator. It isn't a standalone anime app; it's one generator inside a much larger suite that includes general text-to-image generation, photo editing, and design templates.

The generator supports two input modes: text-to-anime (type a description, get anime art) and photo-to-anime (upload a photo and the tool restyles it while keeping the general composition). Fotor's own materials say the feature draws on multiple underlying AI models — naming Flux AI, GPT Image, and Gemini among them, depending on the style or mode picked — rather than a single proprietary anime model. That's worth being upfront about: this isn't a specialist anime diffusion model fine-tuned exclusively on anime datasets the way dedicated tools like Anifusion or SoulGen are; it's a general-purpose AI art pipeline with anime-specific style presets layered on top.

Style options include shonen and shojo looks, chibi (the small, big-eyed "cute" style popular for stickers), cyberpunk, fantasy, a Studio Ghibli-inspired filter, and 3D anime variants. Users can also type extra style cues into the prompt for finer control beyond the preset buttons.

## Pricing

Fotor runs on a freemium, credit-based model. Every generation — anime or otherwise — consumes credits, and the free Basic tier hands out a limited starting allotment, replenished slowly through daily check-ins or by sharing creations to Fotor's community. Paid tiers unlock larger monthly credit pools, more simultaneous ("concurrent") generations, and additional storage/editing tools.

| Plan | What's included | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic (Free)** | Starter credits, 1 concurrent generation, 50 AI chats, basic editing tools, 512MB storage | Anime generator is watermark-free even here |
| **Pro** | Monthly credits, 10 concurrent generations, 2,000 AI chats, 100+ editing tools, 2GB storage, HD PNG exports | Entry paid tier; exact price is set dynamically on Fotor's pricing page, not consistently retrievable at review time |
| **Pro+** | Larger credit pool, 30 concurrent generations, 4,000 AI chats, batch editing, 100GB storage, brand kits | Aimed at teams doing higher-volume work |
| **Max** | 50 concurrent generations, 10,000 AI chats, 500GB storage | Top tier for heavy/professional use across the suite |

Fotor also states unused credits roll over for up to five months while the subscription stays active, softening the sting of a slow month.

A caution worth flagging plainly: Fotor's pricing page renders plan prices dynamically (likely geo- or promo-adjusted), which made exact dollar figures hard to pin down independently at review time — and a meaningful number of Trustpilot reviews describe unexpected annual renewal charges and refund difficulty. Neither is unique to the anime feature, but both matter before handing over a card number. **Confirm the live price and cancellation terms directly on Fotor's pricing page before subscribing** — don't rely on any third-party figure, including this one. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability here were accurate as of September 19, 2026, and AI tool pricing changes often.

## Features walkthrough

**Text-to-anime and photo-to-anime in one tool.** Most competitors force a choice — generate from scratch or restyle an existing photo. Fotor does both from the same interface: type a prompt, or upload a photo and let the model reinterpret it in an anime style while roughly preserving pose and composition.

**Style presets plus prompt-level control.** The named presets (chibi, shonen, shojo, cyberpunk, fantasy, Ghibli-style, 3D anime) cover common requests without prompt-engineering skill, while power users can type extra style language for finer results.

**Watermark-free exports.** Anime generations export without a watermark, more generous than many free tiers that gate clean exports behind a paid plan.

**Multi-model backend.** Because the feature can call on more than one image model (Fotor names Flux AI, GPT Image, and Gemini), output can vary run to run — useful for variety, less predictable for a consistent batch.

**Bundled editing suite.** Once generated, an anime image is one click from Fotor's broader editor — background removal, retouching, resizing — convenient for a finished asset rather than a raw generation.

## Who it's actually for

**Casual users** wanting a quick anime avatar are well served by the free Basic tier — a handful of generations, no watermark, no pushy signup wall.

**Fan-art hobbyists and content creators** producing anime images regularly will likely outgrow the free credit allotment and should budget for Pro, factoring in the concurrent-generation limit for batch work.

**Small teams already using Fotor** for other design work get the most value, since the anime generator is one tool among many included in a Pro/Pro+ subscription rather than a standalone cost.

**Professional illustrators needing a consistent, trained style** are better served by a specialist anime-tuned model or a human illustrator — Fotor's multi-model approach trades consistency for accessibility.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Free tier, no forced watermark on anime exports | Plan pricing renders dynamically, not listed as static text — harder to comparison-shop |
| Both text-to-anime and photo-to-anime in one tool | Not a dedicated anime-specialist model — output style varies between generations |
| Bundled into a full photo-editing suite | Multiple Trustpilot reviews report renewal charges and refund friction |
| Decent range of named anime style presets | Concurrent-generation limits on lower tiers can slow batch work |
| Cross-platform: web, iOS, Android, Windows, Mac | Underlying model per generation isn't user-selectable |

## Integrations & ecosystem

Fotor publishes developer resources — an API and SDK at developers.fotor.com — for teams integrating its image tools, though the anime generator isn't marketed as a headline API use case the way its background-removal or upscaling APIs are. There's no Zapier or Slack integration listed. The tool spans Fotor's own apps — web, iOS, Android, Windows, Mac — so generations sync to the same account regardless of device.

## Where it's a strong fit

- A free or low-cost way to turn a photo or idea into anime-style art without installing anything or learning a complex prompt syntax.
- You're already a Fotor user for other design/photo-editing tasks and want anime generation as a bonus rather than a separate subscription.
- You need watermark-free output on a budget.
- You want quick variety across several anime sub-styles (chibi, cyberpunk, Ghibli-style) without hunting for separate specialist tools for each.

## Where to think twice
