- **If you need pixel-consistent character design across many images** (e.g., a recurring webcomic character), a general multi-model pipeline like Fotor's tends to drift in style — a dedicated, fine-tuned anime model holds a look better.
- **If transparent, fixed pricing matters**, the dynamically rendered pricing page and the volume of Trustpilot complaints about auto-renewal and refunds are worth weighing before an annual plan.
- **If you need commercial licensing clarity for client work**, confirm Fotor's usage rights directly with its terms of service — this review isn't a substitute for that legal check.
- **If you want a fully free, unlimited tool**, Fotor's credit system means heavy use will eventually require a subscription or repeated daily check-ins.

## Bottom line

Fotor's AI Anime Generator does what it promises — fast, watermark-free anime art from a prompt or photo, with enough style variety to cover common requests — and the free tier is genuinely usable, not just a demo. It won't replace a specialist anime model for anyone chasing a tightly consistent character design, and the billing friction some subscribers report is worth weighing before upgrading. For casual avatars, fan art, and quick photo-to-anime conversions, it's a reasonable, low-risk starting point — just read the cancellation terms first.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Fotor's AI Anime Generator free?**
Yes, a free Basic tier includes starter credits and lets you generate watermark-free anime images. Credits are limited and replenish slowly (daily check-ins, community sharing) unless you upgrade for a larger monthly allotment.

**Does Fotor's anime generator use a specific AI model?**
Fotor states it can draw on multiple underlying models, including Flux AI, GPT Image, and Gemini, depending on mode and style, rather than a single named proprietary model.

**Can I convert a real photo into anime style, or only generate from text?**
Both — text-to-anime and photo-to-anime, a genuinely useful edge over text-only competitors.

**Are the anime images watermarked?**
No — Fotor states anime generations export without a watermark, including on lower tiers, more generous than many freemium competitors.

**How much does Fotor Pro cost?**
Fotor's pricing page renders figures dynamically and appeared to vary by promotion or region at review time — check the live [Fotor pricing page](https://www.fotor.com/pricing/) rather than relying on any third-party figure.

**Is Fotor's billing trustworthy?**
Some Trustpilot reviewers report unexpected annual renewal charges and difficulty securing refunds. Not specific to the anime generator, but relevant to any paid signup — read cancellation terms before subscribing.

**What's the difference between Fotor's anime generator and a dedicated anime AI app?**
Dedicated anime-specialist tools are typically fine-tuned on anime datasets and hold a more consistent character style across generations. Fotor's version is a general-purpose, multi-model generator with anime presets layered on — more versatile for one-off images, less consistent for a recurring character.

There's no matching store entry for Fotor in this site's coupon catalog at the time of writing, so there's no verified discount code here. For other AI tool deals, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) category, and for an AI image generator with clearer model transparency, see our [Dzine AI review](/blog/dzine-ai-review).

title: Chatim Review 2026: Live Chat + AI Chatbot Pricing
excerpt: Chatim review covering live chat and AI chatbot pricing, free plan limits, features, and who this small-business support tool fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Chatim worth it?

Chatim is worth trying if you want a live chat widget with a built-in AI chatbot that doesn't require a developer to set up, and its free plan is usable enough to test on a real site before paying anything. It's less compelling if you need high-volume AI automation, since the AI conversation caps on paid plans (200–500/month) are tight for busy support teams.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $9/month (Starter plan, billed monthly) |
| Free tier | Yes — live chat, basic chatbot flow, contact button, single user |
| Best for | Small businesses and solo site owners wanting live chat plus light AI automation |
| Standout feature | AI chatbot trained on your own knowledge base, paired with unlimited live chat seats on paid plans |

## What Chatim actually is

Chatim is a live chat and chatbot platform built for website owners who want to talk to visitors in real time and automate the repetitive parts of that conversation with AI. It sits in the same broad category as Tidio, Crisp, and Tawk.to — a chat widget you drop onto a site, plus a dashboard where a support team manages conversations, and a chatbot builder for handling the questions a human doesn't need to answer personally.

The company doesn't publicly disclose which underlying language model powers "Chatim AI," and there's no model name (like GPT-4 or Claude) listed on its marketing pages as of this writing. If the specific model matters for your evaluation — for compliance, output quality benchmarking, or vendor risk assessment — that's a detail worth confirming directly with Chatim's team rather than assuming.

Chatim positions itself around fast setup: install a JavaScript snippet, or use a dedicated plugin for WordPress, Shopify, or Wix, and the widget is live in a few minutes according to the vendor. It then offers three parallel ways to engage visitors — live chat with a human agent, a drag-and-drop chatbot flow builder for scripted logic, and an AI layer that can answer questions using content pulled from a connected knowledge base.

## Chatim pricing

Chatim uses a flat-rate structure where the core chat and chatbot infrastructure — unlimited conversations, unlimited team seats on paid tiers — is included at every paid level, and the thing that scales with price is AI conversation volume plus advanced features like white-labeling and API access.

| Plan | Price | AI conversations/month | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Not included | Live chat, basic chatbot flow, contact button, single user only |
| Starter | $9/month | Not included | Team access, email notifications, custom branding, unlimited live chat |
| Pro | $29/month | Up to 200 | Chatim AI, Slack integration, premium chatbot blocks, JavaScript SDK, integrations |
| Ultimate | $59/month | Up to 500 | Advanced reporting, white label, API access, dedicated support, account manager |

Chatim also offers a 14-day free trial on paid plans with no credit card required, and reseller pricing for agencies managing multiple client sites, available on request. The vendor notes that AI conversation capacity within a plan's cap depends on knowledge base size and conversation length, so a business with a large help center may burn through its monthly allotment faster than the raw number suggests.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI tool pricing and feature sets move quickly, so confirm current numbers on Chatim's own pricing page before committing to a plan.

## Core features walkthrough

**Live chat with human handoff.** The base of the product is a real-time chat widget where a support agent can respond to visitors directly. Even on the free plan, this works without any AI involvement, which makes Chatim usable for a solo operator who just wants a chat bubble on their site.

**Chatim AI trained on your content.** On Pro and Ultimate, the AI layer can be pointed at a business's existing documentation, FAQ pages, or other knowledge sources and answer visitor questions in that context rather than giving generic responses. This is the feature that differentiates Chatim from a plain live-chat tool — it's meant to deflect repetitive questions before they reach a human agent.

**Drag-and-drop chatbot builder.** Separate from the AI layer, Chatim includes a rule-based flow builder for scripted conversations — think lead-qualification sequences or appointment booking flows that don't need AI reasoning, just branching logic. This gives teams a fallback for predictable interactions where AI unpredictability isn't worth the risk.

**Multi-channel contact buttons.** Chatim can surface WhatsApp, Telegram, and Facebook Messenger as additional contact options alongside the on-site widget, so visitors aren't locked into one channel to reach support.

**Analytics dashboard.** Paid plans include visitor trend tracking and performance reporting, with the Ultimate tier adding more advanced reporting for teams that need to justify chat ROI internally.

## Who Chatim is actually for

**Solo site owners and very small businesses** get real value from the free plan — a working chat widget and basic chatbot flow with no credit card required is enough to validate whether live chat helps conversion before spending anything.

**Small teams needing multiple agents** are the target for the $9/month Starter plan, since that's where team access and custom branding unlock, even though AI automation is still off the table at that tier.

**Support-heavy small businesses** that want to reduce repetitive tickets are the clearest fit for Pro at $29/month — 200 AI conversations a month is workable for a site with moderate traffic, plus Slack notifications keep a small team looped in without living in a separate dashboard.

**Agencies and higher-volume teams** managing several client sites, or businesses needing white-label chat widgets and API access to build custom integrations, are better served by Ultimate at $59/month — though even its 500-conversation AI cap is modest next to enterprise-grade AI support platforms.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Usable free plan with no credit card required | AI conversation caps (200–500/month) are tight for busy sites |
| Flat-rate pricing — unlimited live chat and team seats on paid plans | Underlying AI model isn't publicly disclosed |
| Fast setup via JS snippet or WordPress/Shopify/Wix plugins | AI automation only unlocks starting at the $29/month Pro tier |
| Multi-channel contact buttons (WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger) | No published enterprise/SOC 2 compliance details on the marketing site |
| 14-day free trial on paid plans, no card required | Advanced reporting and API access are locked to the top $59/month tier |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Chatim connects to Slack for team notifications starting on the Pro plan, and offers a JavaScript SDK for developers who want to customize widget behavior beyond the drag-and-drop builder. The Ultimate plan adds full API access, which is the tier to look at if you need to pipe chat data into a CRM or internal tool rather than relying on Chatim's own dashboard. Platform-specific installation plugins exist for WordPress, Shopify, and Wix, which cuts setup time for businesses already running on one of those platforms. There's no public Zapier listing as of this writing, so teams wanting broader no-code automation across hundreds of apps should verify that directly with Chatim before assuming it's supported.

## Where Chatim is a strong fit

Chatim works well for a small business or solo operator that wants a single tool covering live chat, a scripted chatbot, and light AI automation without juggling three separate vendors. The free-to-paid path is gentle — start free, upgrade to Starter for team seats, and only pay for AI once you actually need it on Pro. The flat unlimited-seat pricing on paid tiers also means a growing team doesn't get penalized per-agent the way some competitors charge, which keeps costs predictable as headcount increases.

## Where to think twice

Skip Chatim if your support volume is high enough that a few hundred AI conversations a month won't cover it — at that point, a platform with usage-based AI pricing or a much higher included cap will end up cheaper and less limiting. It's also not the right choice if you need documented enterprise compliance (SOC 2, HIPAA, etc.) since Chatim's public pages don't list that kind of certification, so regulated industries should confirm compliance status directly with the vendor before rolling it out. And if knowing exactly which language model is answering your customers' questions matters to you — for accuracy benchmarking or vendor risk reasons — the lack of a disclosed model name is worth raising with Chatim's team before you commit, since you're trusting an unnamed model with real customer conversations.

## Bottom line

Chatim is a reasonably priced live chat and AI chatbot combo that's easy to get running and doesn't punish small teams with per-seat fees. The free plan is a genuine way to test the waters, and the $9 Starter tier is cheap for teams that just want multi-agent live chat without AI. Where it gets more of a judgment call is the AI layer itself — the conversation caps are modest, the underlying model isn't disclosed, and businesses with real support volume will likely outgrow the Pro or even Ultimate allotment faster than expected. For a small business easing into AI-assisted support without a big commitment, it's a sensible starting point; for a team that already knows it needs high-volume AI automation, it's worth comparing against platforms built specifically around that use case, like [Chatbase](/blog/chatbase-review).

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Chatim free to use?**
Yes. Chatim has a free plan that includes basic live chat, a basic chatbot flow, and a contact button for a single user, with no credit card required to sign up.

**Does the free plan include AI features?**
No. AI-powered conversations (Chatim AI) are only available on the Pro plan ($29/month) and above, with monthly conversation caps of 200 on Pro and 500 on Ultimate.

**What happens if I exceed my AI conversation limit?**
Chatim's public pricing page doesn't specify exact overage terms, so confirm current behavior — whether conversations are paused, throttled, or billed extra — directly with Chatim support before relying on it for high-volume periods.

**Which platforms does Chatim integrate with?**
Chatim offers dedicated plugins for WordPress, Shopify, and Wix, a JavaScript SDK for custom sites, Slack notifications on Pro and above, and API access on the Ultimate plan.

**Is there a free trial for paid plans?**
Yes, Chatim offers a 14-day free trial on paid plans with no credit card required, so you can test AI features and team access before paying.

**Can agencies get discounted pricing for multiple client sites?**
Chatim lists reseller pricing available on request for agencies and web studios managing chat for multiple clients — contact Chatim directly for those terms.

**What underlying AI model does Chatim use?**
Chatim doesn't publicly name the language model behind Chatim AI on its marketing site. If that matters for your evaluation, ask the vendor directly before rolling it out for customer-facing use.

**How does Chatim compare to Chatbase or Tidio?**
Chatim leans toward affordable, flat-rate live chat with light AI automation, while tools like [Chatbase](/blog/chatbase-review) are built more specifically around training and deploying a dedicated AI support agent across multiple channels. If your primary need is a trainable AI agent rather than a live chat widget with AI added on, it's worth comparing both directly against your expected conversation volume and budget.

Chatim doesn't have a matching store entry on SmartFare yet, so there's no coupon page to link here — check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers on AI tools that do.

title: AI Content Detector by Leap AI Review 2026: Worth It?
excerpt: A hands-on look at Leap AI's sentence-level content detector — pricing, features, accuracy claims, and who it actually suits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Leap AI's Content Detector Worth Using?

Leap AI's detector (found at tryleap.ai) scores text sentence-by-sentence for likely AI origin instead of giving one blanket percentage, and it's free to try with 500 lifetime words. It's a solid quick-check tool for editors and teachers, but its paid tiers are capped by word count, and like every detector on the market, it isn't immune to false positives.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (500 lifetime words); paid plans from $9.99/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | 500 lifetime words free, or 3-day trial at $1.99 |
| **Best for** | Editors, teachers, and content managers spot-checking text in small batches |
| **Standout feature** | Sentence-level AI scoring with per-sentence highlighting instead of one overall number |

Note: Leap AI's own marketing groups this under "AI Detector + Humanizer" branding, and a companion AI Humanizer product on the same site handles the rewriting/paraphrasing side. This review covers the detection product specifically.

## What Leap AI's Content Detector Actually Is

Leap AI is a text-analysis product built by the team behind tryleap.ai, offered alongside a companion AI Humanizer tool on the same site. You paste text into an editor, and rather than returning a single "78% AI" verdict the way many detectors do, it scores each sentence individually on a 0-100 scale and color-codes the output so you can see exactly which lines triggered the flag.

The vendor doesn't publish which underlying detection model or architecture powers the scoring — no transformer version, training corpus, or benchmark is named on the site. That's typical of AI detectors generally, most of which treat their classifier as proprietary, but it means you're trusting the vendor's own accuracy claims rather than an independently published methodology.

Leap AI states its detector aims to catch text from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, Anthropic's Claude models (Sonnet, Opus, Haiku), Google's Gemini family, and open models like Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, and xAI's Grok. Whether it catches all of those with equal reliability isn't independently verifiable, and the vendor itself is upfront that no detector is 100% accurate.

## Pricing

Leap AI's detector uses a word-allowance model rather than a flat monthly fee for unlimited use, which matters if you're checking long documents regularly.

| Plan | Price | Monthly allowance | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 500 words (lifetime, not monthly) | AI detection, sentence-level scoring, confidence highlighting, no signup required for basic checks |
| Starter | $9.99/month (3-day trial for $1.99) | 10,000 words/month (~20 essays) | Everything in Free, plus saved scan history and no preview caps |
| Pro | $19/month (3-day trial for $1.99) | 20,000 words/month (~40 essays) | Everything in Starter, plus a larger monthly allowance for higher-volume use |
| One-Time Document Pass | $5.99 | Up to 5,000 words, valid 72 hours | No subscription, single document check |

Annual billing is available and Leap AI advertises roughly 50% savings over paying monthly, though you should confirm the exact discounted rate at checkout since annual pricing isn't itemized on the public pricing page. Starter and Pro subscriptions also carry a 7-day money-back guarantee per the vendor's pricing page.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on [Leap AI's pricing page](https://www.tryleap.ai/pricing) before subscribing, since AI tool pricing shifts frequently.

There's no matching store entry for Leap AI on this site yet, so there's no coupon page to link to here — check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers on other AI tools in the meantime.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Sentence-level scoring instead of one number.** This is the detector's main differentiator. Rather than a single "62% likely AI" verdict for an entire document, each sentence gets its own score and color, so you can see exactly which paragraphs need a human rewrite rather than re-writing an entire piece because of one flagged section.

**Model fingerprinting.** Leap AI's detector attempts to identify which specific model likely generated a flagged passage (say, GPT-4 style phrasing versus Claude style phrasing). Treat this as a rough signal rather than a confirmed source — the vendor doesn't publish accuracy figures broken out by model.

**Pattern explanations.** Flagged sentences come with notes on what triggered the score — things like repetitive hedging language ("it's important to note," "in conclusion") or unusually uniform sentence structure. This is more actionable than a bare percentage because it tells an editor what to actually change.

**Low-confidence flagging.** Instead of forcing a verdict on short or ambiguous inputs, the tool is designed to flag when it doesn't have enough signal to make a call — the vendor notes that inputs under roughly 50 words don't give it enough to work with.

**One-time document pass.** For anyone who only needs to check a handful of documents (a single thesis chapter, one freelance submission), the $5.99 one-time pass avoids a subscription entirely, which most competing detectors don't offer as cleanly.

## Who It's Actually For

- **Teachers and academic staff checking individual submissions** get real value from the Free tier's 500 lifetime words for the occasional spot-check, though that allowance is small — it'll run out fast if you're screening a whole class of essays regularly, at which point Starter's 10,000 monthly words becomes the more realistic option.
- **Freelance editors and content managers reviewing a steady stream of client work** are the clearest fit for Pro, since 20,000 words/month covers roughly 40 essay-length documents without hitting a wall mid-month.
- **One-off users** — someone checking a single document before submission, without wanting a subscription — are well served by the $5.99 one-time pass.
- **Agencies or teams screening high volumes of AI-assisted content daily** will likely find even the Pro tier's word cap limiting; Leap AI doesn't publish an enterprise/unlimited tier, so heavy daily users should confirm scalability directly with the vendor before committing.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Sentence-level scoring is more actionable than a single overall percentage | Free tier is a lifetime 500-word cap, not a recurring monthly allowance |
| Free tier requires no signup for basic detection | No published accuracy benchmarks or third-party audits of detection rates |
| One-time document pass avoids a subscription for occasional users | Paid tiers are word-capped rather than unlimited-use |
| Trial is low-cost ($1.99 for 3 days) to test paid features | Same vendor also sells a humanizing tool, which is a built-in conflict of interest worth being aware of |
| Claims coverage across most major model families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Grok) | Vendor doesn't disclose the underlying detection model or methodology |

## Integrations and Ecosystem

Leap AI's detector is a standalone web tool — paste text into the editor and get a score back. As of this review, the tryleap.ai site doesn't advertise a public API for the detector, a browser extension, or native integrations with Zapier, Slack, Google Docs, or LMS platforms like Canvas or Turnitin. If your workflow depends on checking text programmatically or inside another platform, confirm current integration options directly with Leap AI before subscribing, since this is exactly the kind of feature that gets added without much announcement.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

- Spot-checking individual pieces of writing (essays, blog drafts, freelance submissions) where a sentence-level breakdown helps you decide what to actually edit rather than reject outright.
- Budget-conscious occasional use, thanks to the free tier and the $5.99 one-time pass.
- Situations where you want a rough signal plus a plain-language explanation of what triggered it, rather than a black-box score.

## Where to Think Twice

- **If you need volume-based unlimited scanning** — the word-cap structure on every paid tier means heavy daily use (agencies, large classrooms) will hit ceilings that a flat-fee unlimited detector wouldn't.
- **If you need a fully free tool for ongoing use** — 500 words is a one-time lifetime allowance, not a monthly reset, so free use runs out quickly.
- **If you need independently audited accuracy figures** — Leap AI, like most detectors, publishes its own accuracy claims without a named third-party benchmark, so treat any single score as one data point rather than proof.
- **If your use case is high-stakes (academic discipline, employment decisions)** — the vendor's own FAQ content cautions against treating flags as a verdict, particularly for non-native English writers, who carry elevated false-positive risk on most detectors including this one. Corroborate any flagged result with additional review before acting on it.
- **If you need enterprise compliance features** — no SOC 2, HIPAA, or enterprise-tier language is published on the site, so teams with formal compliance requirements should confirm directly with Leap AI rather than assume coverage.

## Bottom Line

Leap AI's detector does one thing reasonably well: it breaks a single blanket "AI or not" verdict into sentence-level scores you can actually act on, and it backs that with reasonable free and low-cost entry points. It's a sensible pick for individual editors, teachers, or freelancers checking documents in small-to-moderate volume. It's a weaker fit for anyone who needs unlimited high-volume scanning, a documented detection methodology, or enterprise compliance guarantees — none of which the vendor currently publishes. As with any AI detector, treat its output as a signal to investigate rather than a final verdict, especially in situations with real consequences attached to the result.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Leap AI's detector free to use?**
Yes, there's a free tier that includes 500 lifetime words of detection with no signup required for basic checks. Paid plans start at $9.99/month for higher monthly word allowances.

**How accurate is Leap AI at detecting AI-generated text?**
The vendor states it aims for a low false-positive rate across major AI models but doesn't publish independent benchmark data. It also explicitly acknowledges that no AI detector is 100% accurate, and that short inputs (under roughly 50 words) and non-native English writing carry a higher risk of misclassification.

**Does Leap AI store or share the text I submit?**
The site doesn't publish detailed data-handling specifics in an easily citable location as of this review, so if you're submitting sensitive or confidential documents, confirm Leap AI's current data retention and privacy policy directly on tryleap.ai before uploading anything you wouldn't want retained.

**What AI models can Leap AI detect?**
Leap AI states it targets output from OpenAI's GPT-3.5/GPT-4/GPT-4o/GPT-5, Anthropic's Claude models, Google's Gemini family, and open models including Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, and Grok.

**Is Leap AI beginner-friendly?**
Yes — it's a paste-and-go web editor with no setup required, and the free tier lets you try it without creating an account.

**What are the alternatives to Leap AI's detector?**
Other detection-focused tools worth comparing include [Winston AI](/blog/winston-ai-review) and [Undetectable AI](/blog/undetectable-ai-review), both of which take somewhat different approaches to scoring and reporting. Compare free-tier limits and pricing structure against your actual usage volume before choosing.

**Can I check a document once without subscribing?**
Yes — the $5.99 one-time document pass covers up to 5,000 words for 72 hours without requiring a subscription.

**Does Leap AI offer an annual plan?**
Yes, annual billing is available and the vendor advertises roughly 50% savings versus paying monthly, though the exact discounted rate should be confirmed at checkout since it isn't broken out on the public pricing page.

title: AiFaceSwap Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: AiFaceSwap review: is this credit-based face swap and video tool worth paying for over free alternatives like FaceSwapper.ai?
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is AiFaceSwap Worth Paying For, or Should You Stick With a Free Tool?

AiFaceSwap is a browser-based face-swapping platform for photos, videos, and GIFs that pairs a genuinely free tier with paid credit subscriptions for longer videos, batch jobs, and API access. It's worth paying for if you need bulk or video-heavy swapping with queue priority; casual, occasional swappers can likely stay on the free tier indefinitely.

### At a glance

| | Details |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $0 free tier; paid plans start at $29.90/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | No sign-up required; unlimited single/multi-face photo swaps, 3 video or GIF swaps every 12 hours |
| **Best for** | Bulk photo batches, longer video face swaps, developers wanting API access |
| **Standout feature** | Batch processing plus a documented face-swap API for automated workflows |

A quick disambiguation first: this review covers **AiFaceSwap** (aifaceswap.io), a credit-based subscription tool with a paid API tier. It's a different product from [Remaker AI](/blog/remaker-ai-review), the broader credit-based photo-editing-plus-face-swap toolkit already reviewed on this site, and different again from [FaceSwapper.ai](/blog/free-face-swap-review), which stays entirely free with no paid plans at all. If your priority is "never pay a cent," FaceSwapper.ai is the simpler pick. If you need higher-volume or longer-video swapping with a subscription and an API, AiFaceSwap is built for that instead.

## What AiFaceSwap Actually Is

AiFaceSwap is a single-purpose web app: you upload a source face and a target photo, video, or GIF, and its facial-recognition model maps the source face onto the target. Beyond the basic one-to-one swap, it offers multiple-face swapping (for group photos), gender-swap transformations, and batch mode for running dozens of photos through the same source face at once. There's no desktop app — everything runs in the browser, and it supports JPG, PNG, and WebP inputs.

The company doesn't publish which underlying face-mapping model or architecture powers the tool, so there's no independently verifiable claim to make here about the tech stack beyond "a proprietary facial-recognition pipeline," which is how the vendor describes it.

## Pricing

AiFaceSwap runs on a credit system: every swap consumes credits, and you can either buy a monthly subscription that refills credits automatically or buy one-time credit packs.

| Plan | Price | Credits/month | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | N/A | Unlimited single/multi-face photo swaps, 3 video/GIF swaps every 12 hours, no watermark, files auto-deleted after 1 day |
| Basic | $29.90/mo | 5,000 | ~83 minutes of video/GIF swapping or 5,000 batch photos, VIP queue priority, permanent history, 1080p output, API access |
| Plus | $59.90/mo | 11,000 | ~183 minutes of video/GIF swapping or 11,000 batch photos, same feature set as Basic |
| Pro | $99.90/mo | 21,000 | ~350 minutes of video/GIF swapping or 21,000 batch photos, same feature set as Basic |

One-time credit packs are also available outside a subscription, ranging from 500 credits for $6.99 up to 32,000 credits for $168.35, with the per-credit rate improving at higher pack sizes — useful if you need a short burst of video credits without committing to a monthly plan.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI tools update pricing frequently, so confirm current figures on [AiFaceSwap's pricing page](https://aifaceswap.io/pricing/) before subscribing.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Free, no-login photo swapping.** Unlike most credit-gated AI tools, AiFaceSwap's single and multi-face photo swaps are unlimited on the free tier with no account required — you land on the site, upload two images, and get a result. That's a meaningfully more generous free tier than most competitors offer for photo swaps specifically.

**Video and GIF face swapping.** This is where the paid tiers earn their keep. The free tier caps you at 3 video or GIF swaps every 12 hours; paid plans convert credits into video-swap minutes (roughly 60 credits per minute of footage based on the published figures), with the Basic plan covering about 83 minutes a month.

**Batch processing.** Rather than running one swap at a time, batch mode lets you queue multiple photos against the same source face in one pass — useful for things like swapping a mascot or presenter face across a set of marketing images.

**Multiple-face and gender-swap modes.** Group photos with several faces can be swapped individually rather than only supporting a single face per image, and there's a dedicated gender-swap transformation mode as a separate feature from the standard face swap.

**API access.** Paid subscribers get access to a documented face-swap API, which is the feature that separates AiFaceSwap from purely consumer-facing tools like FaceSwapper.ai — it's the more realistic option if you want to build face-swapping into an app or automated pipeline rather than using the web UI by hand.

## Who It's Actually For

- **Casual users and meme-makers** — the free tier's unlimited photo swaps cover this use case completely; there's little reason to ever upgrade if you're not touching video.
- **Content creators doing occasional video swaps** — the free tier's 3-per-12-hours video allowance may be enough for light, sporadic use; anything more regular will hit the wall quickly.
- **Marketers and small teams running batch campaigns** — the Basic or Plus plan's batch photo allowance and queue priority make sense once you're processing dozens of images regularly.
- **Developers integrating face-swap into a product** — the API access bundled into every paid tier is the main reason to pick AiFaceSwap over a purely browser-based competitor.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely unlimited free photo swaps, no account needed | Video allowance on the free tier is thin (3 swaps/12 hours) |
| API access included on all paid tiers | No published information on the underlying face-mapping model |
| Batch processing scales well for bulk jobs | Files are auto-deleted after 1 day, so there's no built-in long-term storage on the free tier |
| Multiple one-time credit pack sizes if you don't want a subscription | Credit-to-minute video math (roughly 60 credits/minute) can burn through a plan fast on longer clips |
| No watermarks on free-tier output | Output quality claims can't be independently verified beyond what the vendor states |

## Integrations & Ecosystem

AiFaceSwap's main integration point is its own **API**, documented separately from the consumer web app, aimed at developers who want to send swap requests programmatically rather than through the browser UI. There's no native Zapier, Slack, or Adobe plugin listed on the site, and no desktop or mobile app beyond a mobile-compatible web interface — so integration options are narrower than a full creative suite, but sufficient if all you need is a swap endpoint to call from your own code.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

AiFaceSwap works well if you need face swapping that scales past casual use — batch photo jobs, longer videos, or programmatic access via API — without wanting to build or train your own model. The free tier is also genuinely useful on its own for anyone who just needs the occasional swapped photo and doesn't want to hand over payment details.

## Where to Think Twice

Skip AiFaceSwap, or at least the paid tiers, if you need a **fully free tool with no video cap at all** — FaceSwapper.ai's no-credit model may fit that better, even though it lacks an API. Skip it if your organization needs **enterprise-grade compliance documentation** (SOC 2, formal DPAs) — none is advertised on the public site, and you'd need to contact the company directly to confirm anything beyond the stated 1-day auto-delete privacy policy. And skip it if you need **on-premise or offline processing** — this is a cloud-only web tool with no local/on-prem deployment option mentioned anywhere in its documentation.

More broadly, as with any face-swap tool, treat the output as a fun or productivity tool rather than something with guaranteed photorealism on every input — result quality depends heavily on the source and target image angle, lighting, and resolution, and AiFaceSwap doesn't publish independently audited accuracy benchmarks.

## The Bottom Line

AiFaceSwap earns its place as a step up from purely free, casual face-swap tools rather than a replacement for them. Its free tier alone is competitive for photo swapping, and the paid plans make sense specifically once you need video volume, batch throughput, or an API — not because the free tier is crippled. If your use case never touches video or automation, you may never need to pay. If it does, the Basic plan at $29.90/month is the natural starting point before stepping up to Plus or Pro.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is AiFaceSwap actually free to use?**
Yes, for photos. Single and multiple-face photo swaps are unlimited with no sign-up or payment required. Video and GIF swaps are capped at 3 every 12 hours on the free tier; higher volume requires a paid plan.

**Does AiFaceSwap require an account?**
No — the free tier works without creating an account or logging in. An account is only needed to manage a paid subscription or track permanent history.

**How does the credit system work?**
Paid plans allocate a monthly credit pool (5,000 to 21,000 credits depending on tier) that's consumed per photo or per minute of video/GIF processed. One-time credit packs are also available if you'd rather not subscribe monthly.

**What happens to my uploaded photos and videos?**
According to AiFaceSwap's privacy policy, uploaded content is automatically deleted after 1 day, and usage data is stated to be kept private. Confirm the current policy details directly on the site's privacy policy page before uploading anything sensitive.

**Is there an API?**
Yes. All paid subscription tiers include access to a documented face-swap API, aimed at developers who want to integrate face swapping into their own applications rather than using the web interface manually.

**How does AiFaceSwap compare to Remaker AI?**
[Remaker AI](/blog/remaker-ai-review) is a broader credit-based toolkit that bundles face swapping alongside other photo-editing AI features. AiFaceSwap is narrower and more focused specifically on face, video, and GIF swapping, but adds a documented API that Remaker doesn't emphasize as heavily.

**How does AiFaceSwap compare to a fully free tool like FaceSwapper.ai?**
[FaceSwapper.ai](/blog/free-face-swap-review) has no paid plans at all — everything is free, including video swaps, but there's no subscription tier for higher volume, no batch queue priority, and no API. AiFaceSwap trades that simplicity for scalability once you outgrow casual use.

**Is AiFaceSwap beginner-friendly?**
Yes. The core workflow — upload a source face, upload a target, generate — doesn't require any editing skill. The API and batch features add complexity only if you choose to use them.
