title: June Review: What the Analytics Tool Was, and What Happened
excerpt: June (june.so) was B2B SaaS product analytics that joined Amplitude in August 2025. Here's what it offered and what to use instead.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is June still available as a standalone product?

No — June (june.so) is a discontinued standalone product. The B2B SaaS product analytics platform, built by former Intercom employees and backed by Y Combinator, announced on August 8, 2025 that it had joined Amplitude, folding its product and team into Amplitude's platform rather than continuing to sell or support June on its own.

**At a glance**

| | June |
|---|---|
| What it was | Product & customer analytics software for B2B SaaS |
| Founded | Around 2020, per Y Combinator's Winter 2021 batch and the founders' "~5 years" 2025 timeline |
| Founders | Enzo Avigo and Ferruccio Cinquemani (both ex-Intercom) |
| Key integrations | Salesforce, HubSpot, Attio |
| What happened | Joined Amplitude, announced August 8, 2025 |
| Current status | Not sold or onboarded as a standalone product; existing customers migrated to Amplitude |
| What to use instead | Amplitude directly, or another product-analytics tool (Mixpanel, PostHog, Heap) |

If you landed here after searching for June's pricing or a signup link, there isn't one anymore — the rest of this article covers what June actually was, why it joined Amplitude, and where to look instead if you need product analytics for a B2B SaaS company today.

## What June actually was

June was a product analytics platform built specifically for B2B SaaS companies, not general web or mobile analytics. Its own pitch described software that generated "auto-generated reports for customer analysis focused on how companies use your product" — it turned raw product-usage events into account-level and user-level reports without requiring a team to hand-build dashboards or write SQL first.

The company was founded by Enzo Avigo and Ferruccio Cinquemani, who left Intercom to start it. June went through Y Combinator's Winter 2021 batch, with earliest institutional backing from Speedinvest (partner Frederik Hagenauer, later a board observer) and a seed round led by Point Nine Capital's Louis Coppey at the end of the YC batch. By the company's own account, June reached profitability over its roughly five years of operation and personally onboarded more than 1,000 startups over its lifetime — consistent with its positioning as a tool for earlier-stage SaaS teams that wanted account-level product insight without hiring a dedicated analytics engineer.

## The core idea behind the product

June's stated ambition, in the founders' own words, was "to build a product analytics tool that can take you from idea to IPO." Its day-to-day value proposition centered on a few things: **auto-generated reports** rather than requiring users to build every chart or funnel from scratch, **account-level analysis for B2B SaaS specifically** — tracking how whole customer accounts (companies) engaged with a product, not just individual users, a distinction that matters where the buyer, the admin, and the end users inside one account are often different people — and **CRM integrations** with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Attio that let usage data flow into records sales and customer-success teams already used, useful for spotting expansion or churn-risk accounts. The founders also emphasized **a more approachable design and onboarding**, saying they wanted June to be "warm and welcoming, in a space that's often cold and intimidating."

Because June is no longer a live product, none of its dashboards, report templates, or UI can be verified hands-on anymore — this description reflects the company's own public positioning rather than a first-hand walkthrough.

## Pricing history (no longer applicable)

June's site no longer carries a pricing page — the page that replaced its marketing site after the Amplitude announcement is a farewell letter, not a pricing archive. Like most self-serve B2B SaaS analytics tools, June is understood to have run a tiered model gated by event volume or tracked users, with an entry tier for early-stage startups and paid tiers scaling toward larger companies, consistent with its 1,000-plus-startup customer base. Because that page is gone, this article can't verify exact historical tier names or dollar amounts through any current source — treat any June pricing figures you find elsewhere online as unverified.

Pricing and availability noted here are accurate as of this post's date. June itself won't change further since it's retired, but Amplitude's own pricing for anyone migrating or evaluating fresh can and does move — confirm current details directly on Amplitude's site.

## The announcement: what actually happened, and when

On August 8, 2025, June published a post titled "A new chapter for June" announcing the company had joined Amplitude. The founders framed the decision candidly: after roughly five years, June had gone "from zero to profitable," but growing further as an independent product analytics company would have required either moving upmarket toward enterprise customers (away from June's original vision) or cutting costs aggressively to stay profitable at the low end — neither of which felt right to them.

They cited a specific comparable case: Command AI, a company they describe as friends with, had joined Amplitude and had its product integrated within a few weeks. That outcome reportedly convinced the June team there was a third path beyond "go upmarket" or "stay small": joining Amplitude, a public company with, in their words, "all the resources to provide great service for both big and small businesses." The founders also noted Amplitude had launched an "Amplitude Made Easy" initiative about a year earlier, which they say was partly inspired by June's approach.

For existing customers, the message was a migration path, not an abrupt shutdown: the founders wrote that "hundreds" of June customers had already decided to join them at Amplitude, where the team would keep supporting them. The announcement doesn't state a hard cutoff date or data-export deadline — if you were a June customer and haven't migrated, contacting Amplitude directly is the way to get current guidance.

## What made June different, historically

**Built specifically for B2B SaaS, not general analytics.** Many product analytics tools are broad enough to cover consumer apps, e-commerce, and B2B software at once. June's account-level reporting and CRM integration were a narrower, more opinionated bet, shaped by founders who came from Intercom — a company deeply embedded in the B2B SaaS customer-communication space.

**CRM-native integrations as a first-class feature.** Salesforce and HubSpot support is common among analytics tools broadly, but the inclusion of Attio — a newer, smaller CRM more popular with early-stage startups — suggests June was tracking where its actual customer base lived, not just the two biggest incumbents.

**A design/onboarding emphasis unusual for the category.** Analytics tools are frequently built analyst-first. June's founders explicitly positioned ease of use as a differentiator, targeting the same non-technical or lightly-technical SaaS operators who made up much of its customer base.

## Who June was actually for (historically)

June made the most sense for early- to growth-stage B2B SaaS founders and operators who wanted account-level usage insight without hiring a dedicated analytics engineer, especially teams already on Salesforce, HubSpot, or Attio who wanted usage signals to flag expansion-ready or at-risk accounts alongside their CRM data. It was also a fit for companies that found tools like Amplitude or Mixpanel intimidating or overbuilt for their stage — June's stated design philosophy aimed to be the friendlier, faster-to-configure alternative. None of that maps onto a current buying decision, since June itself isn't purchasable, but it's a useful filter for evaluating what to replace it with.

## Pros and cons, as the product stood historically

| Pros (historical) | Cons (historical, and now) |
|---|---|
| Purpose-built for B2B SaaS account-level analysis | No longer available — nothing to sign up for |
| CRM-native integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Attio) | Never independently benchmarked here vs. Amplitude/Mixpanel/PostHog |
| Profitable over ~5 years, 1,000+ startups onboarded, per the company | Historical pricing isn't verifiable through any current source |
| Founder-market fit from Intercom | Couldn't scale upmarket without more funding or a strategy shift |
| Migration path into Amplitude, not an abrupt shutdown | No stated data-retention timeline beyond the announcement |

## Integrations and ecosystem (historical)

June's most-cited integrations were Salesforce, HubSpot, and Attio, connecting product-usage data to the CRM systems sales and customer-success teams already used. Beyond CRM connections, as a product analytics platform it relied on standard event-tracking ingestion to capture usage data — but specific SDK names or a public API reference aren't things this article can confirm now that the product's documentation is no longer live. That level of detail isn't recoverable from June's current public presence, which is limited to a single retirement-announcement page.

## Where to think twice — and what to use instead now

There's nothing to evaluate hands-on anymore, but a few things matter for anyone researching June today:

- **If you were an existing June customer**, the direct next step is Amplitude — a migration path already exists, and "hundreds" of June customers had moved over as of the August 2025 announcement.
- **If you need a B2B-SaaS-specific analytics tool with CRM integrations today**, Amplitude's "Amplitude Made Easy" initiative is the closest continuation of June's ideas, since June's founders say it partly inspired their decision to join. Confirm current features and pricing on [amplitude.com](https://amplitude.com) directly.
- **If you want an alternative to Amplitude itself**, Mixpanel, PostHog, and Heap are established competitors worth comparing, each with different pricing and CRM-integration depth. If you need a free or open-source option, PostHog offers a self-hosted tier — none of the others do. Skip researching June for a current buying decision otherwise; any "June vs. X" comparison you find elsewhere compares a discontinued product's old marketing claims to a competitor's current one.

## The bottom line

June was a genuine, profitable, purpose-built product analytics tool for B2B SaaS companies that ran for about five years, onboarded more than 1,000 startups, and built real integrations into the CRMs its customers actually used. This isn't a story about a broken product or an outraged customer base — by the founders' own account, June hit a familiar SaaS ceiling: profitable at a smaller scale, but unable to grow upmarket without either raising significantly more money or compromising the vision that made it distinct. Joining Amplitude in August 2025 was a considered exit, not a collapse. If you're researching June today, the takeaway is simple: there's no product left to buy, and Amplitude — not a resurrected June — is where its ideas and its migrated customers now live.

Browse more [AI & software deals](/category/software) for tools you can actually use today.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is June (june.so) still available to sign up for?**
No. June joined Amplitude, announced August 8, 2025, and its website no longer offers signup, pricing, or a live product — only the retirement announcement.

**Was June acquired by Amplitude, or did it merge?**
June's own announcement frames it as "joining" Amplitude rather than using the word "acquisition" explicitly. Exact deal terms weren't disclosed publicly.

**What did June actually do as a product?**
It was product and customer analytics software built for B2B SaaS companies, generating auto-generated, account-level usage reports and integrating with CRMs including Salesforce, HubSpot, and Attio.

**Who founded June, and when?**
Enzo Avigo and Ferruccio Cinquemani, both formerly of Intercom, founded June and went through Y Combinator's Winter 2021 batch, with early backing from Speedinvest and a seed round led by Point Nine Capital.

**What should I use instead of June now?**
Amplitude is the direct continuation, since June's team and ideas moved there. Mixpanel, PostHog, and Heap are independent alternatives worth comparing if you're evaluating product analytics tools fresh, rather than migrating specifically from June.

**Why did June join Amplitude instead of continuing independently?**
Per the founders, after reaching profitability at a smaller scale over about five years, growing further would have required either moving upmarket toward enterprise customers or cutting costs aggressively to stay profitable at the low end. They concluded joining a larger, resourced platform was the better path.

title: WriteText.ai for Magento Review 2026: Pricing & Fit
excerpt: WriteText.ai's Magento extension auto-generates product, category and meta content inside your admin. Here's install, pricing and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is WriteText.ai good for Magento stores?

WriteText.ai's Magento extension generates product descriptions, meta tags, Open Graph text, and category-page copy directly inside the Magento or Adobe Commerce admin, then publishes it without a separate export/import step. It's built for merchants running Magento 2.4.4+ with catalogs too large to write by hand — not a tool a five-SKU store needs.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $90 pay-as-you-go Starter plan or $149/month Pro plan |
| **Free tier/trial** | Free trial with full Pro-feature access, no credit card required |
| **Best for** | Magento/Adobe Commerce stores with a large or frequently changing catalog |
| **Standout feature** | Native admin-panel integration that writes directly into Magento's product, category, and meta fields |

WriteText.ai already has a WooCommerce plugin and a Shopify app on the same content engine (see our [WriteText.ai for WooCommerce review](/blog/writetext-ai-woocommerce-review) if that's your platform). The Magento extension runs the same generation logic but is a different piece of software, with its own install path and platform-specific quirks — cron jobs, multi-store views, and split short/long description fields chief among them. This review sticks to what's specific to Magento.

## What the Magento extension actually is

WriteText.ai is a content-generation platform aimed at ecommerce catalogs, run by 1902 Software as "a service" under that company. It ships separate native integrations for WooCommerce, Shopify, and Magento/Adobe Commerce, plus an API for headless setups, PIM systems, and ERPs. It describes itself as independent — not affiliated with or endorsed by Adobe, Magento, or any platform it plugs into.

The Magento extension installs into the admin panel and supports Magento 2.4.4 or newer (tested up to 2.4.8), requiring PHP 8.1+. As with the WooCommerce plugin, generation happens on WriteText.ai's backend — the extension is a bridge that pulls catalog data out, sends it for generation, and writes the result back into Magento's native fields.

WriteText.ai's knowledge base flags that the extension needs Magento cron jobs enabled to work correctly — automation, scheduled bulk generation, and new-product detection all depend on it. If your hosting has cron disabled or throttled (not uncommon on some managed Magento hosts), automation won't fire reliably, so check with your host before buying a plan built around it.

## Installation and setup on Magento

The extension is listed on the Adobe Commerce Marketplace as a native extension rather than a theme-level plugin, so it installs the way most Magento extensions do — via Composer or the Marketplace's direct-download flow, followed by the standard `bin/magento module:enable`, `setup:upgrade`, and cache-flush sequence. WriteText.ai's knowledge base has a dedicated "How to install in Magento" article, though the exact package name and manual steps weren't fully visible in what's publicly indexed — budget developer time rather than expecting a one-click install like a WordPress plugin.

Once installed, connect the extension to your WriteText.ai account, then map which Magento fields each content type should populate — the step where this integration differs most from WooCommerce and Shopify.

## Field mapping — the Magento-specific part

Magento's catalog structure splits product copy differently than WooCommerce or Shopify do, and WriteText.ai's knowledge base documents "how to map product and category text fields" as a separate Magento topic — a sign the mapping isn't fully automatic. In practice, that means matching generated outputs to:

- **Short and full description** — Magento's two separate fields (short on category/listing pages, full on the product page), which WooCommerce doesn't split the same way.
- **Meta title and meta description** — standard SEO fields, generated per product.
- **Open Graph text** — a dedicated knowledge base article covers how OG text is handled in Magento specifically, worth reading before assuming social-share previews populate as expected.
- **Category pages** — generated separately via the extension's own category-content generator.
- **Image alt text** — version 4.5 release notes list "expanded alt text coverage," implying earlier versions had narrower support here than elsewhere.
- **FAQ/Q&A blocks** — newer content type for answer-engine visibility, not a default Magento field, so it likely renders through a custom block depending on theme.

For multi-store-view or multilingual setups, WriteText.ai states 25+ language support, generating separate localized copy per store view rather than one description you'd duplicate and translate manually.

## Pricing

Pricing runs on the same credit-based system as WriteText.ai's WooCommerce and Shopify integrations — there's no separate Magento-only tier. Figures below were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change; confirm current numbers on WriteText.ai's pricing page before buying, since AI tool pricing moves fast.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| **Starter (flexible)** | From $90, no monthly commitment | 1,000–20,000 pay-as-you-go credits (~$0.09/credit); core generation, custom templates, brand voice, unlimited sites |
| **Pro** | $149/month (annual option available) | 2,000 credits/month (~$0.075/credit); adds full automation, advanced SEO/AEO tools, keyword tracking, internal linking, API access |
| **Managed Setup** | $999 | 6,000 credits, everything in Pro plus guided onboarding, dedicated account manager, 1:1 training, optional private cloud |

Starter-plan credits expire after one year; Pro-plan monthly credits don't roll over. Prices shown are exclusive of applicable taxes. WriteText.ai doesn't publish an exact words-per-credit ratio, and a product with description, meta fields, OG text, and alt text generated together will burn more credits than a bare description — confirm the current credit math directly before committing to a larger block on a thousands-of-SKUs catalog.

A free trial gives full access to Pro-tier features, no credit card required — a reasonable way to test field mapping against your own theme before paying.

## Core features that differentiate it on Magento

**Admin-panel-native generation.** Content is generated and mapped from inside the Magento admin rather than a separate dashboard you copy-paste from — relevant given how many Magento merchants work through an agency's admin workflow rather than touching code directly.

**Automation tied to Magento cron.** Full automation — keyword analysis, generation, and publishing as one sequence — depends on Magento's cron jobs. A misconfigured or paused cron will silently break scheduled automation without an obvious error in the interface, so flag this with your host or dev team.

**New-product email alerts and category generation.** The extension detects newly added products and sends email notifications, useful for stores bulk-importing SKUs via ERP/PIM feeds. It also has a dedicated generator for category pages, and states it can pull supplementary product info from the web when catalog data is thin.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo merchants or small agencies** with a modest catalog can get by on Starter's pay-as-you-go credits.
- **Growing catalogs with regular new-SKU intake** are the clearest fit for Pro, where automation and alerts save recurring work.
- **Multi-store-view / multilingual setups** benefit from 25+ language support per store view.
- **Agencies managing several Magento clients** may prefer Managed Setup's dedicated onboarding, though $999 up front is a bigger commitment.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Writes directly into Magento's native fields, including split short/long descriptions | Requires reliable Magento cron for automation to work as advertised |
| Dedicated category-page content generator, not just product-level | Install steps aren't fully documented publicly — budget dev time |
| Multi-language, multi-store-view support built in | Credit-to-content ratio isn't published; costs are hard to estimate |
| Free trial with full Pro-tier access, no card required | Same pricing plans as WooCommerce/Shopify regardless of complexity |
| New-product email alerts for ERP/PIM-fed catalogs | Field mapping needs manual configuration, not fully automatic |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Beyond the native extension, WriteText.ai offers an API for PIM systems, ERPs, and headless storefronts, included from the Pro plan up. There's no native Zapier or Slack integration for the Magento extension specifically — automation runs through WriteText.ai's own workflow engine instead.

## Where it's a strong fit, and where to think twice

Magento stores with catalogs in the hundreds or thousands of SKUs, frequent new-product intake from suppliers, and a need for consistent meta/OG/alt-text coverage are where this extension earns its subscription. The category-page generator and multi-store-view language support are genuinely Magento-relevant features a generic AI writing tool wouldn't replicate without significant manual setup.

It's a weaker fit if you need a fully free tool — even Starter begins at $90 in credits. If your hosting can't guarantee cron jobs run reliably, the automation and new-product-alert features you'd be paying the Pro premium for may not work as described, so ask your host first. If your catalog is small enough to write by hand, or you already have in-house copywriters, the ongoing credit cost probably isn't worth it. If you need exact, guaranteed per-product credit costs to plan a fixed budget, the vendor's materials don't spell out the credit-to-word ratio precisely enough without asking directly.

## Bottom line

WriteText.ai's Magento extension is a purpose-built tool for a common Magento pain point — keeping product and category copy consistent, SEO-formatted, and current across a catalog too large to write by hand. It's not a general AI writing assistant repurposed for Magento; the field mapping into short/long descriptions, category pages, and store views shows real platform-specific engineering. The catch: its stronger features lean on Magento's cron working correctly, and credit-based pricing takes trial-and-error to budget precisely. For a mid-to-large Magento store with a real content backlog, the free trial is worth running against your own theme before choosing between Starter and Pro.

## FAQ

**Is WriteText.ai for Magento different from the WooCommerce plugin?**
Yes. Both share the same content engine and pricing, but they're separate integrations with different install processes and field mappings — Magento's version targets its admin panel and catalog structure (split descriptions, store views, category pages), while WooCommerce's targets WordPress's product post type. See our [WriteText.ai for WooCommerce review](/blog/writetext-ai-woocommerce-review).

**Which Magento versions does it support?**
Magento 2.4.4 or newer, tested up to 2.4.8, requiring PHP 8.1 or higher. Confirm compatibility with your specific version before installing.

**Does it work with Adobe Commerce, not just Magento Open Source?**
Yes, it's marketed for both.

**How is pricing calculated for a large catalog?**
Credits — pay-as-you-go (Starter, from $90) or monthly (Pro, $149 for 2,000 credits). No exact cost-per-product is published, so estimate conservatively and confirm the ratio with the vendor.

**Do I need Magento cron jobs enabled?**
Yes, for automation and new-product detection — check with your host that cron runs reliably first.

**Is there a free trial?**
Yes, with full access to Pro-tier features and no credit card required to start.

**Does WriteText.ai store or reuse my product data to train its models?**
That isn't spelled out in the marketing pages reviewed here — check the current privacy policy or ask support before connecting a catalog with sensitive data.

**Is it beginner-friendly to install?**
Less so than the WooCommerce plugin. It's installed via Composer/Marketplace and the standard Magento CLI upgrade sequence, not a one-click install — plan for developer involvement.

Looking for the underlying deal? Check the [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub for current software offers, or read our [WriteText.ai for WooCommerce review](/blog/writetext-ai-woocommerce-review) if you're comparing platforms.

title: SendShort Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: SendShort auto-clips long video into shorts with captions and B-roll built in. Full pricing, features, and honest verdict for creators.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## SendShort Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict

SendShort is an AI-powered short-form video tool that turns long recordings into TikTok, Reels and Shorts-ready clips, and can also generate faceless videos from scripts or AI avatars. It's a solid pick for creators who want automated clipping plus caption styling, though its plan-based clip caps mean high-volume publishers will likely land on the Business tier.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $19/month (Starter, billed monthly; $15/month billed yearly) |
| Free tier/trial | 3 free videos, no credit card required |
| Best for | Solo creators and small teams repurposing long video into shorts |
| Standout feature | Auto-extraction of "key moments" from long-form video into multiple short clips |

## What SendShort actually is

SendShort is built by PXCH Holding I, LLC and sold as a browser-based platform rather than desktop software. The pitch is simple: upload a long video (a podcast, webinar, livestream, or YouTube link) and let the AI find the moments worth clipping, then auto-caption, auto-B-roll, and reframe them for vertical platforms. It also has a second mode — faceless video generation — where you type or paste a script and the tool assembles a video around it using stock or AI-generated footage, background music, and an AI voiceover, without you needing to appear on camera.

SendShort doesn't publish which specific AI models it runs on for transcription, moment-detection, or voice synthesis; the site markets the underlying AI as proprietary "auto-editing" logic rather than naming a model provider. That's fairly typical among tools in this category — worth knowing if model transparency matters to your workflow, but not unusual for a consumer-facing SaaS product.

## Pricing

SendShort runs three paid tiers, all billed monthly or yearly (yearly saves roughly 20%). There's no permanent free plan, but new accounts get three free video credits to test the editor before paying.

| Plan | Monthly price | Yearly price (per mo) | Shorts per month | Max clip length | Exports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $19 | $15 | 20 | 1 min 30 sec | 1080p @ 30 FPS |
| Professional | $29 | $23 | 50 | 3 min | 1080p & 2K |
| Business | $59 | $47 | Unlimited | 10 min | 1080p, 2K & 4K @ 60 FPS |

Starter includes no watermark, auto captions, basic B-roll, and 3 faceless videos per week. Professional adds 3 custom caption themes, an AI hook-title generator, 10 weekly faceless videos, noise reduction, and auto-translated captions. Business removes the clip-count cap entirely, adds unlimited faceless videos and custom themes, unlimited long-video-to-shorts conversion, content analytics, and a dedicated account manager.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI video tools iterate quickly, so confirm current numbers on SendShort's own pricing page before subscribing.

## Core features that actually matter

**Long-video-to-shorts auto-clipping.** This is the tool's main draw. You feed it a long recording (uploaded file or a link) and it identifies segments it judges worth publishing as standalone clips, then reframes them to 9:16 with auto-generated captions. How well "key moment" detection performs depends heavily on your source material — a structured interview or podcast with clear talking points tends to clip more usefully than a rambling livestream.

**Faceless video generation.** Rather than clipping existing footage, this mode builds a video from a text script, pairing it with stock/AI visuals, an AI voiceover (SendShort states 6+ voices across 48+ languages), and background music. It's aimed at niche/UGC-style channels that publish without a presenter on camera.

**Auto-captioning with style presets.** Captions come with over 37 font/style options and emoji-overlay support, plus auto-translation into 30+ languages on Professional and above — useful if you're repurposing the same clip for multiple language audiences rather than re-editing from scratch each time.

**Auto B-roll and zoom effects.** The editor inserts stock B-roll automatically based on spoken content and adds pacing effects like zooms, which is the kind of manual polish work that otherwise eats the most editing time on short-form content.

**Multi-platform scheduling.** SendShort states it can publish or schedule directly to 10+ platforms including TikTok and YouTube Shorts, which removes a step compared to editors that only export a file for you to upload manually.

## Who it's actually for

**Solo creators and podcasters repurposing long content** are the clearest fit — the Starter plan's 20 shorts and 90-second cap covers a modest weekly clipping cadence for someone turning one long-form episode into a handful of shorts.

**Small agencies or multi-show creators** publishing more frequently, or wanting 3-minute clips and translated captions for international audiences, are better matched to the Professional tier.

**High-volume publishers, agencies managing multiple client accounts, or anyone hitting monthly clip caps** should expect to land on Business, where the unlimited clip count, 4K export, and account manager make the $47–59/month price easier to justify against the alternative of manually editing dozens of clips a week.

**Anyone who mainly needs original video generation from a blank prompt** (not repurposing existing footage) is a weaker fit — SendShort's strength is clipping and captioning, not generative video creation from scratch the way dedicated text-to-video models are.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Automates the most time-consuming parts of short-form editing (clipping, captions, B-roll) | No permanent free plan — only 3 trial videos |
| Faceless video mode covers creators who don't want to appear on camera | Clip counts and max length are capped by plan; heavy users need Business |
| Auto-translation into 30+ languages on paid tiers | AI model/provider details aren't publicly disclosed |
| Direct scheduling to 10+ platforms | Automated "key moment" detection quality varies by source material |
| No watermark on any paid plan | No offline/desktop version; browser-based only |

## Integrations and ecosystem

SendShort's own marketing focuses on direct publishing integrations with major short-form platforms (it names TikTok and YouTube Shorts specifically, with "10+ platforms" total) rather than a broader developer ecosystem. There's no publicly documented Zapier connector or public API on the pricing page at the time of writing, so if your workflow depends on programmatic access or third-party automation chains, that's a detail to confirm directly with SendShort before committing to a plan — don't assume API access exists just because other tools in the category offer it.

## Where it's a strong fit

- You already have long-form source video (podcasts, webinars, interviews, livestream VODs) and want it turned into multiple shorts without manually scrubbing through hours of footage.
- You publish across several short-form platforms and want scheduling handled from one place instead of exporting and re-uploading manually.
- You need captions translated into multiple languages to repurpose the same clip for different regional audiences.
- You want a faceless-video option without separately subscribing to a text-to-video generator and a voice-cloning tool.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a fully free tool** — SendShort's trial is capped at 3 videos, and every ongoing plan is paid; tools with a genuinely free forever tier (even if limited) exist elsewhere in this category.
- **If your team needs enterprise compliance documentation** (SOC 2, detailed data-processing agreements) — SendShort doesn't publish this on its marketing pages, so enterprise buyers should request it directly before assuming it's available.
- **If you need offline or on-prem editing** — this is a cloud/browser tool only; there's no downloadable desktop app or local-processing option.
- **If your primary need is generating entirely new video from a text prompt** rather than repurposing existing footage, a dedicated generative-video tool will likely serve you better than SendShort's clipping-first design.
- **If AI-detected "key moments" consistently miss what you'd choose manually** — like most auto-clipping tools, it's a starting point to review and adjust, not a fully hands-off replacement for editorial judgment.

## The bottom line

SendShort does what it says: it takes the grunt work out of turning long video into short-form clips, with captioning, B-roll, and scheduling bundled in rather than sold as separate tools. The pricing is reasonable at the entry tier for occasional creators, but the plan-based clip caps mean anyone publishing daily or managing multiple channels should budget for Business from the start rather than upgrading reactively. It's not a generative-video replacement and it doesn't publish deep technical specifics about its AI stack, but for the specific job of repurposing existing footage into platform-ready shorts, it covers the core workflow well.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is SendShort free?**
No. There's no permanent free plan — new accounts get 3 free videos to test the platform, after which you need a paid plan starting at $19/month (or $15/month billed yearly).

**What's the cheapest SendShort plan?**
Starter, at $19/month billed monthly or $15/month billed yearly, includes 20 shorts per month with a 90-second max clip length and 1080p export.

**Does SendShort watermark videos on the free trial?**
SendShort states no watermark applies on any paid plan; check directly with SendShort on trial-specific watermarking, since that detail isn't explicitly broken out on the pricing page.

**Can SendShort publish directly to TikTok and YouTube Shorts?**
Yes — SendShort advertises scheduling and direct publishing to 10+ platforms, including TikTok and YouTube Shorts.

**Does SendShort offer an API?**
There's no publicly documented API or Zapier integration listed on SendShort's pricing/marketing pages as of this review; confirm directly with SendShort if programmatic access is a requirement.

**How does SendShort compare to other short-form editing tools?**
It sits in the same category as tools like [Submagic](/blog/submagic-review), which focuses more narrowly on caption styling and editing rather than auto-clipping from long-form source video. SendShort's differentiator is the automated long-to-short extraction and faceless-video generation bundled into one subscription.

**Is SendShort good for beginners?**
The core workflow (upload, let AI clip and caption, review, export or schedule) doesn't require video-editing experience, which makes it approachable for creators without an editing background.

**What languages does SendShort support for captions?**
SendShort states auto-caption translation into 30+ languages on Professional and Business plans, alongside AI voiceover in 48+ languages for faceless videos.

For more AI and software deals, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Databar.ai Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Databar.ai enriches company and contact data across 160+ sources with an AI fallback agent. Here's pricing, features and who it's actually for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Databar.ai good for finding and enriching business data?

Databar.ai is a credit-based data enrichment platform that pulls firmographic, contact, funding, hiring, and tech-stack data from 160-plus live sources into a spreadsheet-style workspace, then fills gaps with an AI research agent that reads the open web. It's built for sales, marketing, and RevOps teams doing list-building at scale — not a fit if you only need to look up a handful of companies by hand.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $99/month (Build plan) |
| **Free tier/trial** | 100 free trial credits per workspace, no paid plan required to start |
| **Best for** | GTM teams building and enriching prospect lists at volume |
| **Standout feature** | Waterfall enrichment across 160+ providers, plus an AI agent that fills in what the databases can't find |

Databar, Inc. positions the product as a workspace for go-to-market teams and, increasingly, AI agents — the pitch is "find, research, enrich, and monitor" companies and people from one interface instead of stitching together Clearbit, Hunter, People Data Labs, and a dozen other point tools. It runs as a spreadsheet-like grid where each column can be wired to a data source, an API, or a natural-language AI instruction, and each row is a company or contact record.

## What Databar.ai actually is

Under the hood, Databar isn't a single data vendor — it's an aggregation and orchestration layer sitting on top of many. When you ask it to fill in, say, a company's employee count or a contact's verified email, it runs a **waterfall**: it queries one provider, and if that provider returns nothing or an unverified result, it automatically tries the next one until it gets a confident answer or exhausts its sources. Databar states that failed attempts don't consume credits, so in theory you're only billed for enrichment that actually resolves.

When none of the connected providers have an answer — a company too small or too new to be indexed anywhere, for instance — Databar's AI research agent steps in, crawls the live web, and returns a structured value with a citation you can click through to verify. That's a meaningfully different approach from a static database lookup tool: it's closer to a research assistant that happens to output spreadsheet cells.

The product isn't tied to one underlying language model in its public marketing; it's described as an AI agent layered over its own enrichment pipeline rather than a wrapper around a single named foundation model.

## Databar.ai pricing

Databar runs three paid tiers plus a starting allotment of free trial credits. Pricing below reflects monthly billing as published on Databar's own pricing page; annual/quarterly billing reportedly front-loads the full credit allotment instead of rolling credits over.

| Plan | Price | Credits/month | Included |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Build** | $99/mo | 5,000 | CRM/email integrations, bring-your-own API keys, up to 5 custom HTTP APIs, batch enrichment up to 10k rows, 3 workspace editors |
| **Scale** | $495/mo | 50,000 | Everything in Build, plus unlimited HTTP APIs, custom rate limits, turbo queue, dedicated infrastructure, 10 workspace editors, batch enrichment up to 100k rows |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom | Everything in Scale, plus personal support, scheduled runs (minute/hour/day), Databar SDK access, unlimited workspace editors |

Every new workspace starts with 100 free trial credits to test enrichments and API calls before committing to a paid plan. Databar's stated model is that only successful, verified API requests draw down credits — a failed lookup costs nothing, which matters a lot for a tool priced on consumption rather than seats.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability shown here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — Databar, like most credit-metered AI tools, adjusts tiers and credit costs periodically, so confirm current numbers on its pricing page before buying.

## Core features that actually matter

**Waterfall enrichment across 160+ sources.** Rather than picking one data provider and living with its blind spots, Databar chains providers — Hunter.io, Clearbit-style firmographic databases, People Data Labs, and others — so a lookup that fails in one source gets retried in the next. This is the biggest differentiator versus buying a standalone enrichment API directly: you're not stuck with one vendor's coverage gaps.

**AI research agent with citations.** When structured databases come up empty, the agent reads live web pages and returns an answer plus a link to where it found it. That auditability is a meaningful trust signal for a category (AI-generated data) where hallucinated facts silently corrupting a CRM is a real risk.

**Flows (workflow automation).** Users can build branching logic that triggers enrichment, lead scoring, and routing automatically — for example, enrich a new inbound lead, score it against ideal-customer-profile criteria, and push it to the right rep's queue in HubSpot without manual steps. This pushes Databar from "enrichment tool" toward "lightweight RevOps automation layer."

**Advanced filtered search.** Databar supports compound filters — funding stage, specific investor backing, hiring velocity by function, technology adoption — as a single search rather than requiring several separate queries stitched together manually.

**Multi-surface access.** The same enrichment engine is reachable through the spreadsheet UI, a REST API, a CLI, and an MCP server, which matters if your team wants to call Databar from an internal tool or an AI agent pipeline rather than only the web app.

## Who Databar.ai is actually for

- **Small sales/growth teams (Build, $99/mo):** enough credits and row limits for a lean team running outbound list-building and basic CRM enrichment without custom rate limits or dedicated infrastructure.
- **Agencies and scaling GTM teams (Scale, $495/mo):** 50,000 credits, 100k-row batches, and unlimited team members fit agencies enriching lists for multiple clients or in-house teams running high-volume campaigns.
- **Larger orgs with compliance/support needs (Enterprise):** custom credit volumes, scheduled runs, and SDK access suit companies embedding Databar into internal systems.
- **Solo founders or very small lists:** the 100 free trial credits are enough to test the workflow, but there's no permanent free tier — once they run out, $99/month is the floor, which is steep for a few dozen leads a month.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Waterfall across 160+ sources reduces single-provider blind spots | No perpetual free plan — only one-time trial credits |
| AI agent provides citations, making fallback answers auditable | Entry price ($99/mo) is high next to single-purpose enrichment tools |
| Two-way CRM sync (HubSpot, Pipedrive, Attio) plus push to Salesforce | Credit consumption can be hard to predict until you've run real volume |
| API, CLI, and MCP server access for building enrichment into other workflows | Advanced automation (Flows, scheduling) is gated to higher tiers |
| Failed lookups reportedly don't consume credits | Enterprise features (SDK, scheduling, dedicated infra) require a custom quote, not transparent pricing |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Databar's stated integration list centers on GTM tooling: two-way sync with **HubSpot**, **Pipedrive**, and **Attio**, plus one-way push to **Salesforce** and outreach platforms. Beyond native CRM connectors, it exposes a **REST API**, a **CLI**, and an **MCP server** — the last of which lets AI agent frameworks call Databar's enrichment functions directly, positioning it for teams building agentic workflows rather than only manual spreadsheet work. Custom HTTP API connections (5 on Build, unlimited on Scale/Enterprise) let teams wire in internal or niche data sources Databar doesn't natively support.

## Where it's a strong fit

Databar makes the most sense for teams that are currently paying for, or manually cross-referencing, several separate enrichment tools — a Clearbit subscription here, a Hunter.io plan there, a manual LinkedIn Sales Navigator search to fill gaps. Consolidating that into one credit pool with automatic provider fallback is a genuine time and cost saver if your list-building volume is high enough to justify the $99+/month floor. Agencies running enrichment for multiple clients, and RevOps teams building lead-scoring automations, are the clearest fits.

## Where to think twice

If you need a completely free tool, or only enrich a handful of records a month, Databar's pricing doesn't work in your favor — the cheapest paid tier assumes real volume. Teams with strict data-provenance requirements should scrutinize the AI research agent's web-sourced answers carefully; a citation is helpful, but it's not a guarantee like a verified database record, and customer-facing data pulled this way should be spot-checked before it drives outbound messaging. If you only need one narrow data type — say, email verification — a single-purpose tool built for that one job will likely be cheaper than a multi-source aggregation platform. And if you need on-premise or offline data processing for regulatory reasons, Databar's cloud/API-first architecture won't fit; confirm compliance questions directly with their sales team rather than assuming.

## The bottom line

Databar.ai earns its place for teams that have outgrown single-vendor enrichment tools and are tired of coverage gaps forcing manual lookups. The waterfall-across-160-sources model plus an AI agent that fills remaining gaps with cited web research is a genuinely useful combination, and the credit-only-on-success pricing logic is fairer than flat per-seat SaaS pricing for a usage-driven category. The catch is the entry price: at $99/month with no ongoing free tier, this is a tool for teams already committed to volume list-building, not a casual add-on for occasional lookups. If that's your team, it's worth a trial run on the free credits before committing to a monthly plan.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Databar.ai free?**
There's no permanent free plan. Every new workspace gets 100 free trial credits to test enrichment and API calls, but ongoing use requires a paid plan starting at $99/month.

**How does Databar's credit system work?**
Credits are consumed only by successful, verified enrichment results — a failed lookup (no verified data found) is stated not to cost credits. Monthly plans roll unused credits over for one additional month; annual and quarterly plans provide the full credit allotment upfront.

**What data sources does Databar pull from?**
Databar aggregates 160+ live sources covering firmographics, funding history, tech stacks, hiring signals, and contact details, drawing on providers such as Hunter.io and People Data Labs, tried in sequence via its waterfall system until a verified answer is found.

**Does Databar integrate with my CRM?**
It offers two-way sync with HubSpot, Pipedrive, and Attio, and one-way push to Salesforce and outreach tools, alongside a REST API, CLI, and MCP server for custom integrations.

**Is Databar's AI research agent accurate?**
Databar states the agent returns structured answers with citations to the source page so you can audit them yourself. Treat AI-agent-sourced fields as a helpful starting point rather than a verified database record, especially for anything customer-facing.

**What's the difference between the Build and Scale plans?**
Build ($99/mo) gives 5,000 credits, 5 custom HTTP APIs, batch enrichment up to 10k rows, and 3 editors. Scale ($495/mo) raises that to 50,000 credits, unlimited HTTP APIs, 100k-row batches, dedicated infrastructure, and unlimited team members.

**Is Databar.ai beginner-friendly?**
The spreadsheet-style interface is approachable for anyone who's used Excel or Google Sheets, but getting real value from Flows, custom APIs, and advanced filtering has a learning curve typical of B2B data tools — budget time to set up your first enrichment workflow properly.

**What are the alternatives to Databar.ai?**
Alternatives range from single-purpose tools (Hunter.io for email finding, Clearbit for firmographics) to broader RevOps platforms with their own enrichment layers. If your needs are simple, a single-source tool may be cheaper; Databar's value is specifically in aggregating many sources plus AI fallback into one workspace. Teams already using [Zapier](/blog/zapier-review) for cross-app automation may want to compare how much of Databar's Flows overlaps with what they could build with existing tooling.

For more AI and software deals, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Creatify Review 2026: AI Video Ad Generator Pricing
excerpt: Creatify turns product URLs into AI avatar video ads for Meta, TikTok and YouTube. Here's real pricing, features, and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Creatify worth it for video ads?

Creatify is worth it if you're running paid social ads and need a steady stream of UGC-style or avatar-led video variations without booking a production shoot every time. It converts product URLs into finished ad scripts and clips, offers 300+ AI actors, and pushes exports straight to Meta, TikTok, YouTube, and Amazon ad specs — but the free plan is watermarked and thin, so real use means paying at least $39/month.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $39/month (Starter), $99/month (Pro) |
| **Free tier/trial** | Free plan with 10 credits/month, up to 2 video ads or 20 image ads, watermarked exports |
| **Best for** | Performance-marketing teams and DTC brands producing high volumes of video ad variations |
| **Standout feature** | URL-to-Video — turns a product page into a scripted, avatar-narrated ad in minutes |

Pricing, free-tier limits and feature availability noted here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on [Creatify's pricing page](https://creatify.ai/pricing) before buying.

## What Creatify actually is

Creatify is an AI advertising platform built specifically for video and image ad production at scale, not a general-purpose video editor. The pitch is narrow and practical: feed it a product URL, a script, or a brief, and it outputs ad creative — UGC-style talking-head clips, cinematic product shots, or static image ads — ready to run on Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, and Amazon.

Creatify states it has processed data from 30M+ analyzed ads and generated more than 15M ads for over 18,000 brands and agencies, with $24M raised from investors including WndrCo and Comcast Ventures. It also states it holds SOC 2 Type II compliance, which matters for a vendor security review. These are vendor-reported figures without independent third-party audits, so treat them as company-reported scale rather than verified benchmarks.

Under the hood, Creatify doesn't build its own foundation models for avatars or video generation. It orchestrates a mix of AI models (the "Model Playground" lets you pick between several) for scripting, voice, and avatar rendering, plus its own workflow layer — the node-based Ad Flow editor, batch generation, and the ad-platform export pipeline.

## Pricing

Creatify runs a credit-based system rather than flat per-seat pricing, which takes some getting used to if you're coming from a tool like Canva or CapCut where a subscription just unlocks features outright.

| Plan | Price | Monthly credits | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 10 credits | Up to 2 video ads or 20 image ads, 300 AI actors, 10 premium models, 40 templates, watermarked exports |
| Starter | $39/month | 100 credits | Watermark removed, all creation tools, 300 AI actors, 200+ ad templates, 50+ premium models, 75+ languages, videos up to 2 minutes, 5GB asset storage, 1 generation at a time |
| Pro | $99/month | 300–5,000 credits | Everything in Starter, plus 1,500 AI actors, 3 custom avatars, 500+ templates, 100+ premium models, up to 5 parallel generations, Creatify MCP integration, competitor ad tracker, performance agent, ad cloning, videos up to 10 minutes, 10GB storage, up to 5 team seats (2 included), up to 5 brand spaces (2 included) |
| Enterprise | Custom | 1,200 credits/year baseline, custom limits | Done-for-you studio service, model fine-tuning, white-label support, enterprise SLA, IP assignment, dedicated account manager |

The credit system is the thing to model out before you commit. A single finished video ad can burn several credits depending on length, avatar count, and whether you're regenerating variations for A/B testing — so a team doing serious batch testing (the whole point of the tool) will likely outgrow Starter's 100 monthly credits fast and land on Pro by default. Budget for Pro if "batch create 20 ad variations" is actually your use case, not the entry Starter tier.

The Pro plan's credit range (300–5,000) is wide — Creatify doesn't spell out on its public pricing page what unlocks the higher end, so confirm the specific allotment with sales or in-app before assuming you'll get the top figure.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**URL-to-Video.** Paste a product page link and Creatify scrapes the images, copy, and pricing to draft a script and matching visuals automatically. This is the single biggest time-saver versus a general AI video tool — you skip the blank-page script problem entirely for straightforward product ads.

**AI avatars and UGC-style actors.** With 300+ stock AI actors on the free/Starter tiers (1,500+ on Pro) speaking 75+ languages, Creatify leans hard into the "looks like a real customer testimonial" aesthetic that performs well on TikTok and Reels feeds, as an alternative to hiring real UGC creators per campaign. Pro adds custom avatars — you can train the platform on your own spokesperson or team member.

**Ad Cloner and competitor tracking.** Pro-tier users get a competitor ad tracker plus an "ad cloner" that can recreate the structure of a high-performing ad you've spotted elsewhere, restyled with your own product and script. This is squarely aimed at performance marketers who iterate off what's already working in a niche rather than starting from a blank template.

**Batch generation and Ad Flow.** Instead of producing one ad at a time, Creatify supports generating multiple variations in parallel (up to 5 simultaneous on Pro) and a node-based "Ad Flow" editor for teams that want more granular control over how script, voice, visuals, and CTA combine — useful for structured A/B testing across hooks or offers.

**Direct platform publishing.** Exports are pre-formatted to spec for Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, and Amazon, and Creatify states ads can be pushed to these platforms directly from the app rather than manually re-exporting for each aspect ratio and file-size limit.

## Who Creatify is actually for

- **Solo founders and small DTC brands**: Starter at $39/month covers watermark-free exports and the core toolkit, but 100 credits a month means rationing.
- **Performance-marketing teams and agencies**: Pro's parallel generation, competitor tracking, ad cloning, and multi-seat/multi-brand support map onto managing several client accounts at once.
- **Enterprise advertisers with compliance requirements**: SOC 2 Type II, IP assignment, and a dedicated account manager target brands that need contractual guarantees.
- **Anyone wanting a free, casual tool**: skip it. The watermark and 10-credit cap make the free plan a sandbox, not a production tool.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| URL-to-Video removes the blank-page script problem for product ads | Credit system makes real usage cost hard to predict up front |
| Large avatar/language library (300+ actors, 75+ languages) | Free plan is too limited to actually ship ads with (watermarked, 10 credits) |
| Direct export to Meta/TikTok/YouTube/Amazon ad specs | Custom avatars are Pro-only, and limited to 3 even then |
| Competitor ad tracking and ad cloning built in on Pro | No published flat monthly-unlimited plan for high-volume shops |
| SOC 2 Type II compliance for security-conscious teams | Enterprise pricing is opaque — requires a sales call |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Creatify's main integration story is outbound: direct publishing to Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, and Amazon ad accounts, formatted to each platform's spec. Pro adds "Creatify MCP integration," letting the platform connect into an AI-agent workflow via the Model Context Protocol rather than only through its own web UI — useful for teams already building agentic marketing workflows. There's no public Zapier app or broad third-party plugin marketplace at the time of writing, so if your stack depends on no-code automation across dozens of tools, verify Creatify's current integration list directly first.

## Where it's a strong fit

Creatify earns its price for teams that need volume: brands testing five, ten, or twenty ad-hook variations a week to find what converts, agencies juggling multiple client accounts, or DTC stores that want that UGC aesthetic without a constant stream of real creators. The URL-to-Video workflow genuinely shortens the path from "product page exists" to "ad is running."

## Where to think twice

Skip Creatify if you need a fully free tool — the watermarked 10-credit plan isn't enough to run real campaigns, and there's no unlimited free tier behind a "contact sales" wall. Skip it too if your ads depend on real customer footage or a specific brand voice AI avatars can't replicate credibly; avatar-led ads read as synthetic to some audiences, and platforms increasingly label AI-generated content, which can affect performance in some niches. Teams needing offline/on-prem generation or a flat unlimited-usage plan should also look elsewhere, since Creatify is credit-metered SaaS only. And if you need granular manual editing (fine-cut timing, custom motion graphics), Creatify is faster but shallower than a dedicated editor for frame-level work — see our [Movavi AI review](/blog/movavi-ai-review) or [Wondershare Virbo review](/blog/wondershare-virbo-review) for alternatives.

## The bottom line

Creatify does one job well: turning a product URL or script into a batch of ready-to-run ad video variations, formatted for the platforms that actually matter for paid social. The Starter plan is a reasonable entry point for a solo operator testing the waters, but the credit ceiling means most teams that stick with it end up on the $99/month Pro plan once they're producing at the volume the tool is actually built for. If your ad strategy already runs on constant creative testing, that's a fair trade; if you only need the occasional ad, the credit math may not favor you over hiring a freelancer per project.

## FAQ

**Is Creatify free?**
There's a free plan with 10 credits a month (roughly 2 video ads or 20 image ads) and watermarked exports. It's usable for testing the platform, not for running live campaigns, since paid ads with a visible watermark aren't something most brands want to ship.

**How much does Creatify cost?**
Paid plans start at $39/month for Starter (100 credits, watermark-free, 2-minute videos) and $99/month for Pro (300–5,000 credits, custom avatars, batch generation, competitor tracking). Enterprise pricing is custom via sales.

**What are Creatify's credits actually spent on?**
Credits are consumed per generation — cost varies by video length, avatar count, and regenerations. Creatify doesn't publish a fixed per-video credit cost publicly, so check current per-action costs inside the app before budgeting.

**Does Creatify support real human actors, or only AI avatars?**
Its core library is AI-generated actors, with custom avatar training on Pro (up to 3). It isn't a marketplace for booking real freelance UGC creators.

**Which ad platforms can Creatify export to?**
Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, and Amazon, pre-formatted to each platform's ad specs.

**Is Creatify secure enough for enterprise use?**
Creatify states SOC 2 Type II compliance, and Enterprise adds IP assignment and a dedicated account manager. Confirm current documentation with sales for your procurement requirements.

**Is Creatify beginner-friendly?**
The URL-to-Video and template flows are straightforward for non-editors — pick a product, pick an avatar, generate. The Ad Flow editor and Model Playground add optional depth for advanced control.

**What are the main alternatives to Creatify?**
See our [Wondershare Virbo review](/blog/wondershare-virbo-review) and [Movavi AI review](/blog/movavi-ai-review) for avatar-video alternatives with different pricing and editing depth — none specialize as tightly in ad-platform export formatting as Creatify.

title: Webscrape AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Webscrape AI turns plain-language requests into scraped data with no code. Here's what it costs, what it does well, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Webscrape AI worth it for no-code data extraction?

Webscrape AI is a no-code, AI-assisted scraping tool that turns a plain-language description of what you want ("product name, price, rating") plus a URL into a structured schema, then pulls that data out automatically. It's a solid fit for solo operators and small teams who need occasional structured data without writing scraper code, but its documentation is thin on limits, refunds, and data handling, so treat it as a lightweight utility rather than an enterprise scraping platform.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $27/month (WebScrapeAI plan, 250 URLs/month) |
| **Free tier/trial** | Free trial advertised on the homepage; exact duration and URL cap aren't published — confirm at checkout |
| **Best for** | Solo founders, marketers, and small teams doing periodic product/price/lead extraction without hiring a developer |
| **Standout feature** | Describe the data you want in plain English; the AI builds the extraction schema instead of you writing selectors |

No matching store entry exists in this site's coupon catalog for Webscrape AI, so there's no coupon-page link to offer here — pricing below comes directly from the vendor's own pricing and documentation pages.

## What Webscrape AI actually is

Webscrape AI is built around a simple loop: you paste a target URL, describe in plain language what you want pulled from it ("scrape every product title, price, and review count"), and the AI scraper generates a field schema, which you can review and adjust before running the job. There's no selector-writing, no XPath, and — per the vendor — no programming knowledge required.

Under the hood, the product exposes a REST API at `api.webscrapeai.com/scrapeWebSite`, which takes your API key, the target URL, a plain-language extraction command, and a schema defining the fields you want back, plus optional parameters like page count and custom headers. That API is the backbone of the product — the dashboard is a front end over the same endpoint. If you're comfortable calling an API directly, you can skip the UI and wire extraction into your own scripts.

The company behind Webscrape AI doesn't publish detailed "about us" information — no named founders, funding history, or registration details are surfaced on the pages this review checked. That's worth knowing going in: this isn't backed by the kind of public track record you'd get from an established player like Bright Data or Apify.

## Pricing

Webscrape AI runs three monthly-billed tiers, priced by number of URLs processed per month rather than by scrape volume or bandwidth:

| Plan | Price | URLs/month | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| WebScrapeAI | $27/month | 250 | No-code AI scraping, live support |
| WebScrapeAI Pro | $47/month | 500 | Everything in the base plan, plus proxy support and JavaScript-wait handling for dynamic pages |
| WebScrapeAI Bulk | $87/month | 1,000 | Everything in Pro, plus bulk multi-URL scraping and pagination support |

There's no published annual-billing discount, and no free-forever tier — the vendor advertises a free trial from its homepage, but the trial length and URL allowance aren't spelled out on the pricing or documentation pages, so confirm that detail before you sign up expecting a specific number of test runs. There's also no visible refund policy published on the site, which is worth asking support about directly if you're paying annually or committing to the Bulk tier upfront.

Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI scraping tools iterate quickly, so verify current numbers on Webscrape AI's own pricing page before you buy.

One flag for budget planning: none of the three tiers publish a bandwidth or storage cap, only a URL-count ceiling. If your jobs hit pages with heavy pagination, "1,000 URLs" on the Bulk plan can mean fewer effective scraping runs than it sounds, since pagination can burn through multiple URL credits per job.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Plain-language schema generation.** Instead of pointing at CSS selectors or building an XPath map, you describe the fields you want in normal sentences and the AI infers a schema, which you can then edit before running. This is the main thing separating it from classic no-code scrapers like Octoparse or ParseHub, which still require click-selecting elements on a rendered page.

**JavaScript-aware scraping on paid tiers.** Pro and Bulk plans support browsing instructions — clicking elements, waiting for content to load, scrolling, filling form fields — before extraction runs. That matters for single-page apps and infinite-scroll listings a basic HTTP-fetch scraper would return empty-handed on. The base $27 plan doesn't get this, so if your targets are JavaScript-heavy (most modern ecommerce sites are), plan on needing Pro at minimum.

**Built-in proxy support.** Pro and Bulk plans include proxy handling, reducing the odds of getting IP-blocked on rate-limiting sites. The vendor doesn't publish proxy pool size, geographic coverage, or rotation frequency, so if proxy quality is mission-critical (e.g., geo-specific pricing checks), confirm that detail with support rather than assume.

**Bulk and pagination handling.** The top-tier plan processes multiple URLs in one job and follows pagination automatically, returning null values for any field it can't find rather than failing the whole batch — useful when scraping a directory where not every listing has every field populated.

**Direct API access.** Every plan appears to include API access to the same `scrapeWebSite` endpoint the dashboard uses, per the published documentation — worth confirming whether it's gated by tier when you sign up, since that isn't broken out on the pricing page.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo founders and freelancers** doing periodic competitive-price checks or lead-list building get the most value from the $27 base plan — 250 URLs/month covers a modest recurring job with no developer needed.
- **Small marketing or growth teams** scraping dynamic sites (JS-rendered pricing pages, infinite-scroll listings) will want the $47 Pro plan for JS-wait and proxy support; the base plan will silently miss content there.
- **Agencies running large, recurring catalog scrapes** — price-monitoring across hundreds of competitor SKUs — are the target for the $87 Bulk plan, though 1,000 URLs/month is still modest next to dedicated scraping infrastructure platforms.
- **Developers building scraping into a pipeline** can skip the dashboard and call the API directly, using it as a lightweight extraction backend rather than a point-and-click tool.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Plain-language schema generation removes the need to hand-write selectors | No published refund policy |
| API access lets developers skip the UI entirely | Free trial length/URL cap isn't disclosed upfront |
| JS-wait and proxy support on paid tiers handle dynamic pages | Proxy pool size, geography, and rotation details aren't published |
| Three export formats (CSV, JSON, plain text) cover most downstream use cases | No annual billing discount advertised |
| Bulk plan handles pagination and multi-URL jobs in one run | URL-based pricing can be misleading for pagination-heavy jobs |
| Low entry price relative to enterprise scraping platforms | No named company/founder info published for trust-checking |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Webscrape AI's site doesn't list any native integrations with Zapier, Google Sheets, Slack, or similar automation tools — if you need scraped data to land automatically in a spreadsheet or trigger a downstream workflow, you'd build that connection yourself via the API and CSV/JSON exports, or route it through a general-purpose automation tool that calls REST APIs. There's no browser extension either; everything runs through the dashboard or the API. For a team already living in Zapier or Make, that's an extra integration step competitors with native connectors (Apify's actor store, Bright Data's dataset integrations) don't require.

## Where it's a strong fit

Webscrape AI earns its price tag for people who need structured data out of a handful of recurring targets — a competitor's pricing page, a directory listing, a set of product pages — without wanting to learn Python or maintain a scraper that breaks every time a site's HTML changes. The plain-language schema approach genuinely lowers the barrier compared to selector-based no-code tools, and API access even on lower tiers means it can grow from a dashboard job into an automated pipeline without switching products. It's also a reasonable way to test whether AI-driven scraping fits your workflow before committing to a heavier platform — the $27 entry tier is cheap enough to try against a real use case for a month.

## Where to think twice

If your team needs enterprise-grade compliance documentation, detailed proxy network specs, or a published SLA, skip this one — none of that is published on Webscrape AI's site, and you'd have to get those answers from support before committing budget. Teams in regulated industries that need to document a data-collection vendor's security posture will likely find the lack of public detail a blocker on its own.

If you need a genuinely free tool with no time-limited trial, look elsewhere — there's no free-forever plan, only a trial of unstated length. And if your needs involve very large volumes (tens of thousands of URLs a month) or resistant anti-bot targets, the URL caps and unspecified proxy quality suggest a dedicated infrastructure-grade scraper (Bright Data, Apify, ScraperAPI) is the safer bet — Webscrape AI reads as built for moderate, recurring jobs rather than heavy-duty crawling.

Finally, because the schema is AI-generated from your plain-language description, double-check the fields it infers before running a job at scale — an AI misreading "price" as a shipping cost on a messy page is the kind of silent extraction error easy to miss until you're auditing output.

## Bottom line

Webscrape AI does one thing well: it turns a URL and a plain-English request into structured data without requiring scraper code, and the tiered JS-wait, proxy, and bulk features scale reasonably across the $27–$87/month range. What holds it back from a stronger recommendation is transparency — no published refund policy, vague trial terms, and no detail on proxy infrastructure or company background make it a tool to test cautiously before trusting it with anything business-critical. For light, recurring extraction tasks, it's a fair no-code option; for compliance-sensitive or high-volume scraping, look further up the market.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Webscrape AI free?**
No. There's a free trial advertised on the homepage, but Webscrape AI doesn't publish a permanent free tier — paid plans start at $27/month for 250 URLs.

**How does Webscrape AI's free trial work?**
The vendor advertises a free trial, but the exact duration and URL allowance aren't published on its pricing or documentation pages as of this review — confirm the specifics during signup before assuming a set number of test scrapes.

**Does Webscrape AI need coding knowledge?**
No. The core workflow is entering a URL and describing what data you want in plain language; the AI generates the extraction schema for you. Developers can also call the API directly if they want programmatic control.

**Can Webscrape AI handle JavaScript-heavy websites?**
Yes, but only on the Pro ($47/month) and Bulk ($87/month) plans, which include JavaScript-wait handling and support for browsing instructions like clicking, scrolling, and filling forms. The base $27 plan doesn't include this, so it may miss content on dynamic pages.

**What export formats does Webscrape AI support?**
CSV, JSON, and plain text, according to the tool's published documentation.

**Does Webscrape AI have an API?**
Yes — the documented endpoint is `api.webscrapeai.com/scrapeWebSite`, which accepts your API key, target URL, a plain-language extraction command, and a schema of fields to return.

**Is Webscrape AI legal to use?**
Legality depends on the target site's terms of service, the data collected, and your jurisdiction — Webscrape AI's own FAQ raises the question but doesn't answer it. Evaluate per-site and, for business-critical use, check with legal counsel rather than assume the tool clears that for you.

**Does Webscrape AI have a refund policy?**
Not published on the site as of this review. If a refund matters to your decision, ask support before subscribing, particularly before paying for the Bulk plan.

**What are the alternatives to Webscrape AI?**
Depending on your needs: Apify and Bright Data for large-scale, infrastructure-grade scraping; Octoparse and ParseHub for click-based no-code scraping; ScraperAPI for a developer-first proxy-and-API approach. Compare current pricing on each vendor's site, since this space moves quickly.
