title: Beacons Review 2026: Pricing, AI Features and Verdict
excerpt: Beacons bundles a link-in-bio page, store, media kit, and AI assistant for creators. Here's the real pricing, features, and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Beacons worth using for a link-in-bio page?

Beacons is worth trying if you want more than a static links page — it bundles a store, email marketing, auto-updating media kits, and an AI assistant called Beam into one free dashboard, then charges 9% on sales until you upgrade. It's a strong fit for creators actively monetizing an audience; it's overkill if you just need a simple links list.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (Free Forever plan); Creator Plus is $30/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — free plan with no time limit, but a 9% fee on store sales |
| **Best for** | Creators selling digital products, courses, or brand deals who need a link page, store, and media kit in one place |
| **Standout feature** | Auto-updating media kit that pulls live follower/engagement stats for brand pitches |

## What Beacons actually is

Beacons is a creator business platform built by Beacons AI Inc. Underneath the familiar "link in bio" landing page, it packages a storefront for digital products, courses, and merch, an email/DM marketing suite, an auto-updating media kit generator for brand pitches, income tracking, and an AI layer called **Beam** that the company describes as a "teammate" for content strategy, growth analysis, brand outreach, and rate negotiation. It's positioned less as a single-purpose link tool and more as a lightweight back office for solo creators who don't want to stitch together five separate apps.

The company says it serves more than 10 million creators, and its customer list includes musicians and streamers with large followings — which matters less for evaluating the product than the fact that it's clearly built with monetization, not just link-sharing, as the primary use case. That's the core difference from a pure link-in-bio tool: Beacons wants to be where the sale, the pitch, and the email list all live too.

## Pricing

Beacons runs a two-tier structure: a genuinely free plan, and a single paid upgrade.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| **Free Forever** | $0 | Customizable link-in-bio page, Smart Reply auto-DMs, built-in store (with a 9% fee on sales), auto-updating media kits, courses with video hosting, 5 email automations |
| **Creator Plus** | $30/month | Everything in Free, plus 0% seller fees, unlimited daily AI credits, unlimited email sends, unlimited memberships, Buy Now Pay Later support, and a free custom domain |

The free plan isn't a crippled trial — it includes the store, the media kit, and basic email automation, which is more than most free link-in-bio tools offer. The catch is the 9% transaction fee on anything you sell through the built-in store, which adds up fast for creators doing meaningful volume. Creator Plus removes that fee entirely, so the $30/month effectively pays for itself once you're selling more than a few hundred dollars a month through the platform, on top of unlocking unlimited AI credits and email sends.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tool pricing and free-tier terms move quickly, so confirm current numbers on Beacons' own pricing page before committing.

## Core features walkthrough

**Link-in-bio page.** The base layer is a customizable landing page for your Instagram/TikTok/YouTube bio link, with blocks for individual links, embedded products, social icons, and email opt-ins. It's competitive with Linktree and Stan Store on flexibility, though the free plan carries Beacons branding unless you upgrade.

**Built-in store.** Rather than linking out to Shopify or Gumroad, Beacons lets creators sell digital downloads, courses (with hosted video), memberships, and physical merch directly from the same dashboard the link page lives in. On the free plan every sale carries a 9% platform fee; Creator Plus drops that to 0%, which is the single biggest reason a growing creator upgrades.

**Auto-updating media kits.** This is the feature that differentiates Beacons most from a plain link tool. It generates a shareable one-pager pulling in current follower counts and engagement stats across connected platforms, meant to be sent straight to brands during sponsorship pitches instead of a manually updated PDF or slide deck that goes stale within weeks.

**Email and DM marketing.** The free plan includes 5 email automations; Creator Plus unlocks unlimited sends and unlimited memberships, plus "Smart Reply" auto-DM handling on social platforms — useful for creators fielding repetitive comment/DM questions about pricing or where to buy.

**Beam (AI assistant).** Beacons markets Beam as an AI teammate for trend discovery, content planning, market-rate calculations for brand deals, growth-strategy analysis, and link-in-bio page generation. Deal-tracking and negotiation automation are listed by the company as still rolling out rather than fully live, so treat that end of Beam as a work in progress rather than a finished feature — worth confirming current scope directly with Beacons before relying on it for actual rate negotiation.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators just starting out**: the free plan is genuinely usable — store, media kit, and basic email tools included — making it a reasonable first stop before paying for anything.
- **Creators actively selling digital products or courses**: Creator Plus's 0% fee and unlimited memberships make sense once monthly sales volume outweighs the $30/month cost of avoiding the 9% cut.
- **Creators pitching brand sponsorships regularly**: the auto-updating media kit is the clearest differentiator here — it saves the repetitive work of manually refreshing a pitch deck every time a follower count changes.
- **Teams or agencies managing multiple creator accounts**: Beacons is built around a single creator's dashboard, not multi-seat team management, so larger operations may find it thinner than dedicated creator-commerce or CRM tools built for that scale.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Free plan includes a real store, media kit, and email tools, not just a link page | 9% seller fee on the free plan can be expensive at volume |
| Auto-updating media kit saves real time on brand pitches | Beam's deal-tracking/negotiation features are still rolling out, per the company |
| Single $30/month upgrade removes fees and unlocks unlimited AI credits, cleaner than tiered pricing ladders | Free-plan pages carry Beacons branding |
| Combines link page, store, email, and media kit in one dashboard, reducing tool-switching | Not built for multi-seat teams or agencies managing many creators |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Beacons is largely a self-contained platform rather than an integration hub — its value proposition is replacing separate tools (link page + store + email + media kit) with one dashboard, not plugging into an existing stack. It connects to the social platforms creators already use (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, etc.) to pull follower and engagement data into media kits and to power Smart Reply auto-DMs. Creator Plus adds a free custom domain and Buy Now Pay Later checkout support for store purchases. For anything beyond that — Zapier-style automation, third-party CRM sync, or API access — check Beacons' current help documentation, since the company doesn't prominently market a public API or broad third-party app marketplace the way some larger e-commerce platforms do.

## Where it's a strong fit

Beacons earns its keep for creators who are past the "just need a links page" stage and into actively monetizing: selling a course, running a membership, or regularly pitching brands for sponsorships. The free plan is a low-risk way to test that workflow, and the jump to Creator Plus is a single clear decision (remove the 9% fee, get unlimited AI credits and email sends) rather than a maze of feature-gated tiers. If your brand-deal pipeline is a recurring part of your income, the auto-updating media kit alone can justify trying the platform.

## Where to think twice

If you only need a static, no-frills link-in-bio page and never plan to sell anything through it, Beacons' store and monetization features are unused weight — a simpler free tool without a seller fee entirely might serve you better. If your store sales volume is already large, run the math on the 9% free-plan fee versus $30/month before assuming Creator Plus is automatically cheaper; at low volume, staying on Free and eating the fee can still come out ahead. Skip it if you need multi-seat team access or agency-level account management, since Beacons is built around a single creator's dashboard. And if you're relying on Beam for hands-off brand-deal negotiation specifically, verify current functionality first — the company itself frames that part of the AI assistant as still in progress rather than a finished capability.

## The bottom line

Beacons is a genuinely useful consolidation play for creators who are monetizing an audience, not just linking one. The free plan is more capable than most competitors' free tiers, the media kit feature solves a real recurring pain point around brand pitching, and the single $30/month upgrade is easy to reason about compared to platforms with five confusing pricing tiers. It's not the right tool if all you want is a plain links page, and the AI "teammate" positioning around Beam is still catching up to its marketing — but as an all-in-one creator back office, it's worth the free trial.

## FAQ

**Is Beacons actually free?**
Yes — the Free Forever plan has no time limit and includes the link-in-bio page, store, media kit, and 5 email automations. The trade-off is a 9% fee on anything sold through the built-in store.

**What does Creator Plus cost and what does it remove?**
Creator Plus is $30/month and removes the 9% seller fee entirely (0% fees), while also unlocking unlimited daily AI credits, unlimited email sends, unlimited memberships, Buy Now Pay Later checkout, and a free custom domain.

**What is Beam?**
Beam is Beacons' AI assistant, described by the company as handling content strategy, trend discovery, growth analysis, brand-outreach help, and market-rate calculations for sponsorship deals. Deal-tracking automation is still rolling out according to Beacons, so confirm current scope before relying on it for active negotiations.

**Does Beacons replace Shopify or a course platform?**
For creators selling digital products, memberships, or hosted-video courses at a small-to-mid scale, yes — the built-in store and course hosting cover that without a separate platform. Larger physical-product catalogs or complex inventory needs are still better served by dedicated e-commerce platforms.

**How does the media kit feature work?**
It auto-generates a shareable page pulling current follower and engagement stats from your connected social accounts, meant to be sent directly to brands for sponsorship pitches instead of a manually maintained deck.

**Is Beacons good for beginners?**
Yes — the dashboard doesn't require technical setup, and the free plan is capable enough to build a real page, list a product, and start collecting emails without paying anything upfront.

**What are the main alternatives to Beacons?**
Linktree and Stan Store are the closest link-in-bio-plus-commerce competitors; creators who only need a plain links page without selling tools might prefer a simpler, fee-free link tool instead.

**Does Beacons offer team or multi-account access?**
The platform is built around a single creator's dashboard rather than multi-seat team management, so agencies handling several creator accounts may find it thinner than dedicated creator-management tools.

title: Rephrasely Review 2026: Paraphrasing Pricing and Verdict
excerpt: Is Rephrasely worth it? An honest look at its 18 paraphrasing modes, $4.99/mo pricing, and where it falls short in 2026.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Rephrasely worth paying for in 2026?

Rephrasely is a browser-based AI writing suite built around paraphrasing, with translation, an AI text composer, grammar checking, plagiarism detection, and AI-content detection bundled into the same subscription. It's a reasonable pick if you paraphrase or reword text often, but the free tier is a 3-day trial rather than a permanent free plan, so casual users who paraphrase a sentence once a month may not get much long-term value.

### At a glance

| | Rephrasely |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $4.99/month (billed annually at $59.88) |
| **Free tier/trial** | 3-day free trial of all features (no permanent free plan) |
| **Best for** | Writers, students, and marketers who paraphrase or rewrite text regularly |
| **Standout feature** | 18 paraphrasing modes plus bundled translation, plagiarism check, and AI detection in one subscription |

Rephrasely is made by Rephrase Media and sits in the same category as tools like QuillBot and Wordtune, positioning itself as a paraphrase-first suite rather than a general-purpose chatbot. It doesn't publish which underlying language model(s) power its rewriting engine, so treat "AI-powered" as the vendor's framing rather than a specific model claim.

## What Rephrasely actually is

At its core, Rephrasely takes a block of text (up to 5,000 characters per submission) and rewrites it in one of several tones or styles — what it calls "writing modes." Beyond paraphrasing, the platform bundles a handful of adjacent tools under one login: an AI composer that expands keywords into paragraphs, a translator covering 100+ languages, a plagiarism checker spanning 50+ languages, a grammar checker, an AI content detector, and citation generation.

That bundling is the main pitch: instead of paying separately for a paraphraser, a translator, and a plagiarism checker, Rephrasely folds them into one subscription. Whether that's a genuine saving depends on how many of those tools you'd actually use.

## Rephrasely pricing

Rephrasely doesn't offer an always-free plan — new users get a 3-day trial with access to the full feature set, and after that a paid subscription is required to keep using the paraphraser beyond its free-mode limits.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly | $12.99/month | Unlimited paraphrasing, translation, AI composer, grammar checks, plagiarism detection, citation generation, AI detection |
| Annual | $4.99/month ($59.88 billed once a year) | Same feature set as Monthly, marketed as the "best value" tier |
| Prepay credits | $5 for 60K words, $10 for 120K words, $15 for 180K words | Pay-as-you-go word credits instead of a recurring subscription |
| Free trial | $0 for 3 days | Full feature access for evaluation before committing |

Outside of the paid tiers, Rephrasely's paraphraser also exposes 12 writing modes at no cost even after the trial ends (with 6 additional premium modes gated behind a subscription), based on the mode breakdown published on its site. That's a meaningful detail if all you need is basic paraphrasing rather than the full suite — you may never need to pay at all, depending on which modes you rely on.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — always confirm current figures on Rephrasely's own pricing page before subscribing, since AI-tool pricing shifts frequently.

## Core features worth knowing about

**18 paraphrasing modes.** Rephrasely's site lists 12 free and 6 premium rewriting modes, covering things like summarizing, simplifying, and shortening sentences in addition to standard paraphrasing. Having that many distinct modes in one tool is unusual — most competitors ship five or six presets (formal, casual, fluency, etc.) rather than nearly twenty.

**AI Composer.** Rather than only rewriting existing text, Rephrasely can generate new paragraphs from a handful of input keywords. This is aimed at drafting from scratch — outlines, intros, filler paragraphs — rather than polishing something you've already written.

**Bundled plagiarism and AI-content detection.** Because both checks live in the same account as the paraphraser, you can draft, rewrite, and then check the output for originality and AI-detectability without leaving the tool. Rephrasely states its plagiarism checker covers 50+ languages; that figure comes from the vendor and wasn't independently verified.

**100+ language translation.** The translator is a secondary feature rather than the headline one, but it's included at no extra cost across every paid tier, which is a real convenience if you occasionally need quick translations alongside rewriting work.

**Grammar checking and citation generation.** Both are fairly standard add-ons, but bundling them means a student or content writer could plausibly do first-draft generation, paraphrasing, grammar cleanup, and citation formatting in one workflow instead of four separate apps.

## Who Rephrasely is actually for

- **Students rewriting research notes or checking originality** — paraphrasing, plagiarism detection, and citation generation in one subscription covers most of a research workflow, though it's still on the student to use paraphrasing responsibly.
- **Content writers and marketers who rework existing copy** — the 18 modes and word-credit option suit people who paraphrase in bursts, such as repurposing one article into several variants.
- **Non-native English writers who also need quick translation** — translation across 100+ languages is included in every paid tier.
- **Heavy daily users publishing at scale** — the Annual plan at $4.99/month is far more economical than Monthly for identical features.
- **One-off or occasional users** — the prepay credit packs ($5–$15) avoid a recurring subscription entirely.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Wide range of writing modes (18 total) for varied rewriting needs | No permanent free plan — only a 3-day trial |
| Bundles translation, plagiarism check, AI detection, and citations in one subscription | Underlying AI model isn't publicly disclosed, so output quality is harder to benchmark against named-model competitors |
| Flexible pricing — subscription or pay-as-you-go word credits | 5,000-character input limit per submission means long documents need to be split into chunks |
| Annual plan is meaningfully cheaper per month than Monthly | Monthly plan is comparatively expensive at $12.99 for what's still a niche writing tool |
| 12 modes remain free to use even outside the trial | No browser extension advertised, unlike several direct competitors |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Rephrasely is primarily a web app — there's no indication of a Zapier integration, public API, or desktop app, and no browser extension is advertised the way competing paraphrasers (QuillBot, Grammarly) ship one. If integrations or an API matter to your workflow, confirm current availability directly on Rephrasely's site, since this is the kind of feature vendors add without much announcement.

## Where Rephrasely is a strong fit

- You want one login for paraphrasing, translation, plagiarism checking, and AI detection instead of separate subscriptions for each.
- You paraphrase in short, frequent bursts and want a low-commitment pay-as-you-go option via word credits.
- You need more paraphrase-style variety than a typical five-mode tool offers — 18 modes gives you room to match tone more precisely.
- You're a student or researcher who wants citation generation alongside rewriting in the same workflow.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a genuinely free, ongoing tool** — Rephrasely's free access is capped at a 3-day trial, so if your budget is zero long-term, a tool with a permanent (even if limited) free tier will serve you better.
- **If you need a browser extension for in-place rewriting** — Rephrasely appears to be a standalone web app, unlike some competitors that let you rewrite text inline on any website.
- **If you work with long documents in single passes** — the 5,000-character input cap means longer pieces have to be split up manually, which adds friction for book chapters, long reports, or full articles.
- **If you need enterprise features like SSO, team seats, or an audit trail** — nothing on Rephrasely's pricing page suggests team or enterprise tiers exist; it reads as a solo/individual-user product.
- **If model transparency matters to you** — Rephrasely doesn't name the model(s) behind its engine, so you can't compare output quality against a known baseline the way you could with a tool built explicitly on GPT or Claude.

## The bottom line

Rephrasely earns its place as a paraphrase-first suite rather than a general AI writing assistant — its strength is the breadth of rewriting modes and the fact that translation, plagiarism checking, and AI detection all live under one account instead of four separate subscriptions. The Annual plan at $4.99/month is genuinely cheap for what's bundled in, and the prepay credit option suits anyone who doesn't want a recurring charge. The catches are a trial-only free tier, a modest input limit, and no disclosed underlying model to benchmark against. If your workflow involves repeatedly rewording text — SEO variants, student assignments, repurposed marketing copy — it's worth the trial. If you need a permanently free tool, a browser extension, or enterprise features, it's not the right match.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Rephrasely free to use?**
Not permanently. New accounts get a 3-day free trial with full feature access; after that, continued use requires a Monthly ($12.99) or Annual ($4.99/month, billed $59.88/year) subscription, or a prepay word-credit pack starting at $5 for 60,000 words. Rephrasely does list 12 of its 18 paraphrasing modes as free even outside the trial.

**How many writing modes does Rephrasely offer?**
The site lists 18 total paraphrasing modes — 12 free and 6 premium — covering standard paraphrasing as well as summarizing, simplifying, and shortening text.

**Does Rephrasely check for plagiarism and AI-generated content?**
Yes, both are bundled into paid plans. The plagiarism checker is stated to cover 50+ languages, and AI content detection is included too, though neither has published, independently verified accuracy figures — treat detection results as a signal, not a definitive judgment.

**What's the input limit per submission?**
Rephrasely's input box accepts up to 5,000 characters per submission, so longer documents need to be pasted in sections.

**How does Rephrasely handle my data and privacy?**
Rephrasely doesn't publish a detailed, independently verifiable breakdown of data retention or training-use policies beyond a standard privacy policy. If you're pasting sensitive text into any paraphrasing tool, check the current privacy policy on Rephrasely's site before use.

**What are the main alternatives to Rephrasely?**
QuillBot and Wordtune are the closest direct competitors in the paraphrasing space, each with their own free-tier structures and browser extensions. If your priority is specifically detecting or humanizing AI-generated text rather than paraphrasing, tools built for that purpose — see our [Humanize AI review](/blog/humanize-ai-review) and [Winston AI review](/blog/winston-ai-review) — are worth comparing separately.

**Is Rephrasely beginner-friendly?**
Yes — the interface is a straightforward paste-and-rewrite workflow with mode selection, and no setup, integration, or technical configuration is required to get started.

**Can I cancel the Annual plan and switch to prepay credits?**
Rephrasely offers both subscription and pay-as-you-go options, but cancellation and switching mechanics (proration, refunds) should be confirmed with Rephrasely's support or terms of service before committing.

For more AI and software picks, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Invideo AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is Invideo's agentic AI video editor worth the credit-based pricing? A hands-on look at plans, features and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Invideo worth it for AI video creation?

Invideo AI is worth it if you want an editor that turns a text prompt or raw footage into a finished video through AI agents rather than manual timeline work — it's strong for creators and small teams making short-form and marketing video at volume, but its credit-based pricing gets expensive fast for heavy 4K or long-form use.

### At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $9/seat/month (Basic, billed annually) |
| Free tier/trial | No standing free plan on the current pricing page — confirm on invideo.io before signing up |
| Best for | Solo creators and small teams producing short-form, social and marketing video |
| Standout feature | Agentic editing — describe an edit in plain language and an AI agent executes it on the timeline |

## What Invideo actually is

Invideo is an AI-powered video creation and editing platform built by Invideo, a company that has been in the online video-editing space since well before the current wave of generative AI tools. The product has shifted from a template-driven editor into what it now calls an "agentic video editor" — instead of only handling manual cuts, you type an instruction like "add captions to this clip and trim the dead air at the start," and an AI agent applies the change directly on a multitrack timeline that behaves a lot like Premiere Pro.

Under the hood, Invideo doesn't build its own foundation video-generation model. It routes text-to-video requests through third-party models — the current lineup includes Seedance (2.0 and 2.5), Google's Veo 3.1, Kling AI, and Sora 2 — meaning the visual quality of AI-generated clips depends on whichever underlying model you pick, not on Invideo itself. Invideo's own layer is the orchestration: the agent system, timeline editor, footage-analysis tools, and the workflow stitching AI generation, voiceover, captions and stock assets into one export.

## Pricing

Invideo's current plans use a shared "credits" system rather than flat per-video pricing, and — as of this writing — billing on the public pricing page is annual-only for all three tiers.

| Plan | Price | Credits | Seats included | Notable limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $9/seat/month, billed annually | 190 credits/seat/month | 5 | Limited AI agent access (Lite tier only); no access to the newer Seedance 2.5 model; 10 GB storage |
| Pro | $25/seat/month, billed annually | 1,000 credits/seat/month | 10 | Full agent access (Lite, Pro, Ultra tiers); all Seedance models up to 1080p/4K; 30 GB storage |
| Ultra | $60/seat/month, billed annually | 3,000 credits/seat/month | 20 | Full agent and model access, lowest per-credit cost; 80 GB storage |

Credits are consumed per generation rather than per export — for example, roughly 30 credits for a 5-second Seedance 2.0 Fast clip, or about 2.5 credits for a single AI-generated image, per Invideo's own credit-usage figures. Unused credits don't roll over month to month, so a light-use month effectively wastes part of what you paid for. There's no publicly listed monthly (non-annual) billing option on the plans above, and the current pricing page doesn't advertise a standing free plan — some free trial credits or a limited daily-generation allowance have appeared in Invideo's promotions before, so check the live signup flow rather than assuming a free tier exists.

Pricing, credit allotments and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI video tools update pricing and model access frequently, so confirm current numbers on Invideo's own pricing page before subscribing.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

- **Agent-based editing.** Direct an AI agent to handle specific jobs — cinematography-style shot selection, color grading, sound design and basic music composition — through natural-language instructions on a real multitrack editor.
- **Multi-model text-to-video.** Choose between Seedance, Veo 3.1, Kling and Sora 2 per project, which matters because different models handle motion, faces and text-in-video differently.
- **Footage analysis and search.** An AI agent "watches" uploaded clips and logs their content, so you can find a moment by describing it instead of scrubbing manually — useful once a project has more than a few source files.
- **Batch editing.** A caption style, color grade or trim rule can be applied across multiple clips at once rather than repeating the same edit clip by clip.
- **Extras bundled in.** AI avatars, text-to-speech, voice cloning and face-swap tools are included, cutting down on separate point tools for a single marketing video.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and freelancers** making short-form social content likely fit on Basic or Pro, depending on how many AI video generations they need monthly — 190 credits on Basic covers a handful of short AI clips plus editing work, while Pro's 1,000 credits gives real room to experiment with multiple models.
- **Small marketing teams** producing a steady stream of ad or promo video will find Pro's full agent access and multi-model support the more realistic starting point, since Basic's "Lite" agent tier and lack of the newer Seedance 2.5 model are real constraints once output quality matters.
- **Agencies and high-volume production teams** are the target for Ultra, where the lower cost-per-credit and 20 included seats make sense if you're burning through generations across multiple client projects at once.
- **Anyone wanting a quick one-off video** should think twice before committing to an annual plan — with no confirmed standing free tier, testing the workflow on a real (even if small) project before buying is the safer move.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Genuine agentic workflow — natural-language edits on a real timeline, not just a template swapper | Credit system makes true cost hard to predict until you've used it for a month |
| Access to multiple leading text-to-video models in one place | Output quality varies with whichever underlying model you pick |
| Bundled avatars, voice cloning, TTS and face-swap reduce need for separate tools | Unused credits don't roll over, so light months cost more per generation |
| Batch editing and AI footage search save time on multi-clip projects | Annual-only billing is a bigger up-front commitment than monthly SaaS pricing |
| Familiar multitrack timeline for anyone who's used Premiere-style editors | No clearly advertised standing free plan to test the full workflow risk-free |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Invideo is primarily a self-contained web app, not a platform built around a wide third-party integration ecosystem. It pulls in premium stock footage libraries directly (allotments scale with plan, from 45 items on Basic to 180 on Ultra), and its main "integrations" are the AI models it licenses — Seedance, Veo, Kling and Sora — rather than Zapier-style connectors. If your process depends on deep API access or plugging generation into a marketing-automation stack, confirm on Invideo's own site whether an API/webhook option exists for your plan, since that's not detailed on the public pricing page.

## Where it's a strong fit

Invideo makes the most sense if your main bottleneck is turning raw ideas or footage into a finished short video fast, and you're comfortable directing an AI agent rather than hand-cutting every frame yourself. Teams making a steady volume of social ads, product explainers or short marketing clips get real value from switching generation models per project instead of being locked to one vendor's output style. The footage-search and batch-editing features pay off once you're managing more than a handful of source clips per project — that's where "describe what you want" beats manual scrubbing.

## Where to think twice

Skip Invideo, or start with a very small commitment, if you need a fully free tool to test with zero financial risk — the pricing page doesn't list a standing free plan, and annual-only billing means a wrong first pick costs more to walk back than a monthly SaaS subscription would. It's also not the right choice if your workflow depends on one consistent, predictable visual style across every clip: because output quality shifts with whichever underlying model (Seedance, Veo, Kling, Sora) you select, consistency across a large batch of AI-generated shots takes more manual quality control than a single-model tool would. Teams needing strict enterprise compliance guarantees, heavy API/webhook automation, or offline/on-prem editing should verify those specifics directly with Invideo's sales team, since none of that is spelled out on the consumer-facing pricing page. And because credits don't roll over, sporadic or seasonal users may pay for capacity they don't use most months.

## The bottom line

Invideo has moved past being "another template video maker" — the agent-driven editing and multi-model access make it one of the more capable AI video tools for people who want to direct a video with instructions rather than click through every cut manually. The trade-off is a credit-based, annual-only pricing structure that takes real usage before you know if a plan fits your output volume, and output quality that varies depending on which AI model you pick per generation. If you're a creator or small team producing short-form video regularly, it's worth testing against your actual workload before committing to a year; if you need a free, no-commitment starting point or one visually consistent AI model across every project, weigh those limits first.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Invideo actually free to use?**
The current public pricing page lists paid Basic, Pro and Ultra plans only, with no standing free tier advertised. Invideo has offered limited free credits or trial promotions in the past, so check the live signup page for any current trial offer before assuming a permanent free plan exists.

**How does Invideo's credit system work?**
Each plan includes a monthly credit allotment (190 on Basic, 1,000 on Pro, 3,000 on Ultra per seat) that's consumed by AI generations — video clips cost more credits than a single AI image, and unused credits expire at the end of the billing month rather than carrying over.

**Which AI video models does Invideo use?**
Invideo routes generation requests through third-party models including Seedance (2.0 and 2.5), Google's Veo 3.1, Kling AI and Sora 2, rather than a single in-house model — which plan you're on determines which of these you can access.

**Is Invideo good for beginners?**
The agent-based, describe-what-you-want workflow lowers the barrier versus a traditional timeline editor, but the credit system and multiple model options add a layer of decision-making a first-time creator won't find in a simpler template tool.

**Can I cancel Invideo mid-year if I'm on annual billing?**
Cancellation and refund terms aren't detailed on the public pricing page — confirm the specific policy for annual plans directly with Invideo support before subscribing.

**How does Invideo compare to a template-based video maker?**
Template tools are faster for straightforward, formulaic videos, while Invideo's agentic approach suits projects needing custom footage analysis, multi-clip batch edits, or a choice of AI models — at the cost of a steeper learning curve and less predictable per-project pricing.

**Does Invideo store or use my uploaded footage for training?**
Invideo's specific data-handling and privacy terms for uploaded footage should be confirmed in its official privacy policy rather than assumed, since generative AI platforms vary widely on this point.

**Are there cheaper AI video alternatives if credits don't fit my budget?**
Yes — several AI video tools use flat per-export or simpler subscription pricing instead of a shared credit pool; if predictable monthly cost matters more than multi-model access, compare Invideo's plans against flat-rate competitors before committing annually. Check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current verified offers on video and creative software.

title: Uizard Review 2026: AI UI/UX Design Tool Pricing
excerpt: Uizard turns prompts, screenshots, and sketches into editable UI prototypes with AI. Here's what it costs and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Uizard good for UI/UX design?

Uizard is a solid pick if you need to turn an idea into a clickable, editable app or web mockup fast, especially without a trained designer on hand. It's not a replacement for Figma-level pixel control, but for prompt-to-prototype speed, screenshot-to-mockup conversion, and quick stakeholder buy-in, it does the job well at a low price.

**At a glance**

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (limited); Pro from $12/month billed annually |
| Free tier / trial | Yes — 2 projects, 10 templates, 3 AI generations/month, no card required |
| Best for | Founders, PMs, and non-designers who need fast, editable UI prototypes |
| Standout feature | Autodesigner 2.0 — full multi-screen prototype from a text prompt |

Uizard is a browser-based design tool built by Uizard Technologies that uses AI to generate and edit app and web interface mockups. Instead of starting from a blank canvas, you can describe a product in a sentence, upload a screenshot of an app you like, or scan a hand-drawn wireframe, and Uizard turns any of those into an editable, multi-screen design you can then drag around like a normal design file. The company doesn't publish which underlying models power Autodesigner, so treat "AI-generated" as Uizard's own framing rather than a specific named model.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0/month | 2 projects, 10 templates, 3 AI generations/month, Autodesigner 1.5, unlimited viewers/commenters |
| Pro | $12/month (billed annually) | 500 AI generations/month, Autodesigner 2.0, up to 100 projects, private projects, developer handoff (React CSS), full template library |
| Business | $39/month (billed annually) | 5,000 AI generations/month, faster generation, custom brand kit, unlimited projects, priority support |
| Enterprise | Custom | Unlimited AI generations, unlimited teams, design system setup, AI data SLA, dedicated onboarding |

The Pro and Business prices above are the annual-billing rates; Uizard, like most SaaS design tools, charges more on a month-to-month plan, so check the live pricing page before committing if you want to pay monthly. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI tool pricing shifts often, so confirm current numbers on Uizard's own pricing page before you buy.

The free plan is genuinely usable for testing the workflow, not just a watered-down demo — you get real projects and real AI generations, just capped low (3 a month). That's enough to try Autodesigner once or twice and decide if the output quality matches what you need before paying anything.

### Core features that actually matter

**Autodesigner 2.0.** This is the headline feature: type a description of the app or site you want ("a fitness tracking app with a dashboard, workout log, and profile screen") and Uizard generates a multi-screen prototype with populated UI components, not just blank boxes. It's the fastest way to get from zero to something clickable, and it's meaningfully improved over the older Autodesigner 1.5 engine still used on the free tier — Uizard itself flags 2.0 as the newer, better version, which is a signal that free-tier output may look noticeably rougher than what you see in Pro-tier marketing screenshots.

**Screenshot Scanner.** Upload a screenshot of an existing app or website and Uizard converts it into an editable mockup with real layers, components, and text you can modify. This is genuinely useful for competitive teardown work — grabbing a screen from a competitor's app to use as a starting point for your own redesign — though the fidelity of the conversion depends heavily on how clean the source screenshot is.

**Wireframe Scanner.** Photograph or scan a hand-drawn wireframe and it becomes a digital low-fidelity design. Handy in early-stage brainstorming sessions where a team sketches on a whiteboard and wants a shareable digital version without redrawing everything from scratch.

**Design Assistant.** A set of AI-assisted editing tools bundled into the canvas for things like adjusting layout, rewriting UI copy, and suggesting component variations, so you're not stuck manually nudging every element after the initial generation.

**Theme Generator.** Swaps the visual theme (colors, typography, styling) of an existing project in one action, which is useful for quickly producing two or three visual directions to show a stakeholder without rebuilding the layout each time.

### Who it's actually for

- **Solo founders and non-designers**: the Free or Pro plan covers this well. You don't need design training to get from idea to a prototype you can put in front of users or investors, and the 100-project cap on Pro is generous for a single person's workload.
- **Small product teams**: Pro's developer handoff (React CSS export) and private projects make it workable for a startup team of two to five people moving fast, though 500 AI generations/month can run out quickly if multiple people are iterating heavily.
- **Agencies and larger product orgs**: Business plan's 5,000 generations, custom brand kit, and priority support fit teams producing client deliverables regularly. Uizard doesn't publish a seat limit for Business, so agencies should confirm collaborator/seat terms directly before assuming unlimited team size.
- **Enterprises (15+ users)**: Uizard explicitly positions Enterprise at this size, with unlimited generations, design system setup, and an AI data SLA — the SLA matters if your legal or security team needs contractual guarantees about how prompt data is handled.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely fast prompt-to-prototype workflow, even for non-designers | Not a full replacement for Figma-level precision editing |
| Free tier includes real AI generations, not just a locked demo | AI-generated layouts often need manual cleanup for production use |
| Screenshot and wireframe scanning are useful, differentiated features | Monthly AI generation caps can feel tight once you're iterating seriously |
| Developer handoff (React CSS) built into Pro, not gated to Enterprise | Underlying AI model(s) aren't publicly disclosed |
| Clear, published pricing with an annual discount | No offline/desktop app — browser-only |

### Integrations and ecosystem

Uizard's main technical hook for developers is its React CSS handoff on the Pro plan and above, which exports design specs in a format closer to what a front-end developer can drop into a codebase than a typical static design export. Beyond that, Uizard is primarily a standalone web app rather than a tool built around a wide plugin or Zapier-style integration ecosystem — it doesn't market itself the way Figma or Framer do around a large third-party plugin marketplace. If deep integration with your existing design-to-dev pipeline (Storybook, design tokens, etc.) is a hard requirement, confirm current export options on Uizard's site rather than assuming parity with more established design tools.

### Where it's a strong fit

Uizard earns its keep in the earliest stages of a product: turning a rough idea, a sketch, or a competitor's screenshot into something you can click through and react to. If your bottleneck is getting from "we should build an app that does X" to a shareable mockup within an afternoon, Uizard's Autodesigner and scanning tools solve that specific problem better than starting from a blank Figma canvas. It's also a reasonable low-cost option for teams that need developer handoff without paying for a heavier enterprise design-ops platform.

### Where to think twice

If you need pixel-perfect, production-grade UI design with fine-grained control over every spacing and interaction detail, Uizard's AI-generated layouts will likely need real cleanup in a more precise tool before they ship — it's a prototyping accelerator, not a finishing tool. If your team is already deep in Figma with an established component library and plugin workflow, switching tools just for Uizard's AI generation may not be worth the disruption; you're better off treating it as a separate ideation step. If you need a fully free, unlimited tool, Uizard's free tier caps out fast at three AI generations a month. And if your organization requires strict data residency, on-prem deployment, or SOC 2-level compliance guarantees baked into every tier (not just Enterprise), you'll want to confirm Uizard's current compliance documentation directly rather than assume it matches Free or Pro plan terms.

### Bottom line

Uizard is a genuinely useful shortcut for the "blank canvas" problem in UI/UX design — describe what you want, sketch it, or screenshot something similar, and get an editable starting point in minutes. It won't replace a skilled designer working in Figma for a polished production interface, but for founders, PMs, and small teams who need to move from concept to clickable prototype quickly and cheaply, it's a reasonable and affordably priced tool, with the free plan being generous enough to actually judge fit before paying.

For teams also evaluating AI-assisted website builders rather than app/UI prototyping specifically, our [Framer AI review](/blog/framer-ai-review) covers a tool aimed more at marketing sites and live web pages than product UI mockups — worth comparing if you're not sure which category fits your project.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Uizard free to use?**
Yes. The Free plan includes 2 projects, 10 templates, and 3 AI generations per month using the older Autodesigner 1.5 engine, with no credit card required to start.

**How much does Uizard Pro cost?**
Pro is $12/month when billed annually, and includes 500 AI generations/month, the newer Autodesigner 2.0 engine, up to 100 projects, and React CSS developer handoff.

**What AI model powers Uizard's Autodesigner?**
Uizard doesn't publicly disclose the specific underlying model(s) behind Autodesigner 1.5 or 2.0. Treat "AI-generated" claims as Uizard's own product description rather than a named, verifiable model.

**Can Uizard convert a screenshot into an editable design?**
Yes, via its Screenshot Scanner feature, which turns an uploaded app or website screenshot into an editable mockup with separated layers and components, though conversion fidelity depends on the source image quality.

**Does Uizard export code for developers?**
Pro plan and above includes developer handoff with React CSS export, which is closer to usable front-end code than a typical static design spec.

**Is Uizard good for beginners with no design experience?**
Yes — it's one of its core selling points. The prompt-based Autodesigner and template library are built so non-designers can produce a presentable prototype without design training.

**What's a realistic alternative to Uizard?**
Figma remains the standard for precision, production-grade UI design with a mature plugin ecosystem, while Framer AI leans more toward AI-assisted live website building rather than app UI prototyping. Which one fits depends on whether you need a rough concept fast (Uizard) or a polished, production-ready result (Figma) or a live marketing site (Framer).

**Does Uizard have an enterprise plan with compliance guarantees?**
Yes, Uizard's Enterprise tier (aimed at organizations with 15+ users) adds unlimited AI generations, design system setup, and what Uizard calls an "AI data SLA" — confirm the specifics of that SLA directly with Uizard's sales team if compliance is a hard requirement.
