title: CustomGPT.ai Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: CustomGPT.ai review covering pricing tiers, RAG accuracy features, file-format support, and who this AI agent builder actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is CustomGPT.ai worth it?

CustomGPT.ai is worth it for businesses that need a RAG-based chatbot trained on large, messy document libraries and want strong anti-hallucination safeguards with citations. It's a weak fit for solo creators or anyone wanting a cheap way to test AI chatbots, since plans start at $99/month with no free tier — only a 7-day trial that requires a credit card.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $99/month (Standard plan, $89/month billed annually) |
| Free tier | No — 7-day free trial only, credit card required |
| Best for | Mid-size to enterprise teams that need an accurate AI agent trained on large, varied document sets |
| Standout feature | Ingests 1,400+ file formats and cites sources on every answer, with third-party-verified anti-hallucination claims |

CustomGPT.ai is a no-code platform for building AI agents trained on a business's own content, using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground answers in uploaded documents rather than a general-purpose model's training data. It was founded in 2023 by Alden Do Rosario and is built by CustomGPT Inc., based in Needham, Massachusetts. The company says it now serves more than 10,000 organizations, including MIT, the University of Virginia, and Adobe among its named customers.

Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability described below were accurate as of this post's publish date and can shift — AI tool pricing moves fast, so confirm current numbers on [CustomGPT.ai's pricing page](https://customgpt.ai/pricing/) before buying.

### What CustomGPT.ai actually is

Unlike a general chatbot wrapper, CustomGPT.ai positions itself specifically around RAG accuracy. You upload or connect content — PDFs, spreadsheets, websites, help centers, CRMs — and the platform builds a retrieval index that grounds every chatbot response in that material. The vendor states the platform can ingest more than 1,400 file formats and connect to 100+ integrations, including Google Drive, HubSpot, Shopify, WordPress, and Notion. Under the hood, CustomGPT.ai lets you choose which underlying LLM powers a given agent, with support for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Cohere models rather than locking you into one vendor's model.

CustomGPT.ai doesn't have a matching store entry on SmartFare yet, so the figures below come from the vendor's own pricing and product pages.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | $99/month ($89/month billed annually) | 10 agents, 1,000 queries/month, 5,000 documents per agent, 60M words of storage, 3 team seats, RAG API access |
| Premium | $499/month ($449/month billed annually) | 25 agents, 5,000 queries/month, 20,000 documents per agent, 300M words of storage, 5 team seats, auto-sync website content, white-label branding removal |
| Enterprise | Custom | Everything in Premium, plus forward-deployed engineers, custom agent development, a dedicated account team, flexible data/query/seat limits, RBAC, SSO, a signed DPA, and white-glove onboarding |

Every tier includes multi-language support (the vendor cites 90+ languages), multi-format document training, the platform's anti-hallucination technology, source citations on responses, and SOC 2 Type II compliance with GDPR support. There's no perpetual free tier — new users get a 7-day free trial with full access to their chosen plan's features, but a credit card is required up front and billing starts automatically once the trial ends unless you cancel.

That pricing structure puts CustomGPT.ai well above lighter-weight competitors like Chatbase, which starts near $40/month with a limited but genuinely free tier. CustomGPT.ai isn't aiming at that price-sensitive, self-serve segment — it's positioned for teams willing to pay for accuracy tooling at scale.

### Core features that actually differentiate it

**Anti-hallucination and citations.** Every response includes citations linking back to the source document or page it drew from, and the vendor states CustomGPT.ai has been independently ranked "#1 for anti-hallucination technology" in third-party testing. That's a vendor claim worth verifying against your own use case rather than taking at face value, but the citation behavior itself is a real, checkable feature — you can click through and confirm an answer is grounded in the right source.

**Massive format and integration coverage.** Supporting 1,400+ file formats is a meaningfully larger net than most competitors cast, which matters if your knowledge base is spread across legacy PDFs, spreadsheets, scanned documents, and modern CMS exports. Combined with 100+ native integrations (Google Drive, HubSpot, Shopify, WordPress, Notion, and more), teams with fragmented content sources can consolidate training data without manual reformatting.

**Model choice.** Rather than building on a single proprietary model, CustomGPT.ai lets you pick which LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, or Cohere) powers a given agent. This is useful if your organization already has a model preference for cost, compliance, or performance reasons, or if you want to A/B test response quality across providers for the same knowledge base.

**Auto-sync for live content.** On the Premium tier and above, website content stays synced automatically, so an agent trained on your help center or product docs reflects edits without a manual re-upload — useful for teams that update documentation frequently and don't want a stale bot answering with outdated info.

**Enterprise security posture.** SOC 2 Type II compliance and GDPR support ship on every plan, with the vendor stating no customer data is used to train underlying models. Enterprise adds RBAC and SSO, which matters for larger teams that need access controls beyond "everyone shares one login."

### Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and small businesses testing the waters** — this is not the plan for you. At $99/month minimum with no ongoing free tier, CustomGPT.ai is priced well past casual experimentation. A cheaper tool with a real free tier is a better starting point.
- **Support and knowledge teams at mid-size companies** — the Standard plan's 10 agents and 5,000 documents per agent cover most single-department deployments (support, sales enablement, internal knowledge base) without needing Premium's higher ceilings.
- **Marketing and content-heavy teams with large, messy archives** — the 1,400+ format support and auto-sync features on Premium suit teams whose source material spans PDFs, wikis, and a live website that changes often.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** — SSO, RBAC, a signed DPA, and dedicated onboarding on the Enterprise tier make this a realistic option for regulated industries or large IT organizations that need procurement-grade security guarantees, not just a marketing checkbox.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Broad file-format and integration support (1,400+ formats, 100+ integrations) | No free tier — only a 7-day trial that requires a credit card |
| Citations on every answer make outputs auditable | Entry price ($99/month) is well above lighter chatbot builders |
| Choice of underlying LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere) | Query caps (1,000/month on Standard) can be tight for high-traffic support use |
| SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance on every plan | Premium's jump to $499/month is steep if you outgrow Standard's limits |
| Auto-sync keeps website-trained agents current (Premium+) | Enterprise pricing isn't published, so budgeting requires a sales call |

### Integrations and ecosystem

CustomGPT.ai connects to 100+ third-party tools, with named integrations including Google Drive, HubSpot, Shopify, WordPress, and Notion, alongside a RAG API on every paid tier for teams that want to embed the agent into their own product rather than using the hosted widget. API access starting at the Standard tier (not gated to Enterprise, as some competitors do) is a genuine advantage for developers building custom front-ends around the retrieval engine.

### Where it's a strong fit

CustomGPT.ai earns its price at organizations where a wrong or unsupported chatbot answer carries real cost — customer support at scale, internal knowledge tools for large teams, or anything customer-facing where a hallucinated answer damages trust. The citation-on-every-response behavior gives reviewers and end users a way to check the bot's work, which is rare among competitors that just print an answer with no traceable source. Teams with large, format-diverse document libraries will also appreciate not having to manually convert files before training an agent.

### Where to think twice

If you need a fully free way to try an AI chatbot builder before committing budget, look elsewhere — CustomGPT.ai's 7-day trial requires a credit card and converts to paid billing automatically. If your business is small enough that 1,000 queries a month is plentiful and you don't need SOC 2/enterprise-grade compliance, cheaper tools will cover the same ground for a fraction of the cost. And if you need heavy customization of the chat widget's conversational flow (rather than just Q&A grounded in documents), a dedicated conversational-AI platform built for flow design may fit better than a RAG-first tool like this one.

### Bottom line

CustomGPT.ai is built for teams that need an AI agent to be provably accurate against a large, varied knowledge base, and it backs that positioning with real features — broad format support, per-answer citations, model choice, and enterprise-grade compliance — rather than just marketing copy. The tradeoff is price: there's no meaningful free tier, and the jump from Standard to Premium is steep if your usage outgrows 1,000 monthly queries. For a support or knowledge team at a company that can absorb $99–$499/month and needs auditable, source-cited answers, it's a legitimate choice. For anyone testing AI chatbots on a shoestring budget, start with a tool that has a genuine free plan and revisit CustomGPT.ai once accuracy and compliance actually matter to your use case.

## FAQ

**Does CustomGPT.ai have a free plan?**
No. It offers a 7-day free trial with full access to your chosen plan's features, but you need to enter a credit card at signup and billing starts automatically once the trial ends unless you cancel.

**How much does CustomGPT.ai cost?**
Plans start at $99/month (Standard, or $89/month billed annually), rising to $499/month for Premium, with custom pricing for Enterprise. Confirm current pricing on the [official pricing page](https://customgpt.ai/pricing/), since AI tool pricing changes frequently.

**What file formats can I train an agent on?**
The vendor states support for more than 1,400 file formats, plus 100+ integrations with tools like Google Drive, HubSpot, Shopify, WordPress, and Notion for pulling content in directly rather than manual uploads.

**Is CustomGPT.ai accurate, or does it hallucinate like other chatbots?**
CustomGPT.ai says it has been independently ranked as a top performer for anti-hallucination technology, and every response includes citations to the source material it was generated from. That said, "anti-hallucination technology" is a vendor claim — treat it as a strong signal worth testing against your own documents rather than an absolute guarantee, since no RAG system is immune to occasional misattribution.

**Which AI models does it use?**
You can choose the underlying LLM per agent, with support for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Cohere models, rather than being locked into a single provider.

**Is my data used to train the underlying AI models?**
The vendor states customer data is not used to train underlying models, and the platform carries SOC 2 Type II compliance with GDPR support on every plan. Confirm current data-handling terms in CustomGPT.ai's own privacy documentation before uploading sensitive material.

**Is CustomGPT.ai beginner-friendly?**
Yes for setup — the vendor says a working agent trained on your content can be live in about two minutes with no coding required. The pricing and plan structure, however, assume a business buyer rather than a casual individual user.

**What are good alternatives to CustomGPT.ai?**
If you want a cheaper multi-channel support bot with a real free tier, [Chatbase](/blog/chatbase-review) is a lighter-weight option that deploys to chat, email, voice, Slack, and WhatsApp starting around $40/month. CustomGPT.ai instead trades that lower entry price for deeper document-format support and enterprise compliance features.

Browse more picks in [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: ChatGPT Writer Review 2026: Pricing, Features, Verdict
excerpt: ChatGPT Writer (now Jetwriter AI) drafts Gmail and LinkedIn replies inline. Here's pricing, features, and whether it's worth it.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## ChatGPT Writer Review 2026: Is This Gmail Extension Worth It?

ChatGPT Writer is a third-party browser extension (now rebranded to Jetwriter AI) that drafts emails, replies and other on-page text directly inside Gmail, Outlook, LinkedIn and similar sites. It's built on top of GPT, Claude and Gemini models rather than being an OpenAI product itself, and it's worth it mainly for people who send high volumes of email replies and want drafts without leaving their inbox.

It's important to be precise about naming here, because this is genuinely confusing: **ChatGPT Writer is not made by OpenAI.** It's a separate, independent browser extension that uses AI models (including GPT models) to help write email replies and other on-page text. OpenAI's own ChatGPT is a completely different product, and we've reviewed it separately if that's what you're actually looking for. This article covers the extension formerly called ChatGPT Writer, which as of 2026 has rebranded to **Jetwriter AI** (the old chatgptwriter.ai domain now redirects to jetwriter.ai). We're using the more widely-searched original name because that's still how most people find it, but the product you'll actually sign up for displays the Jetwriter name.

### At a glance

| | ChatGPT Writer (Jetwriter AI) |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (15 responses/month); paid plans from $14/month billed annually |
| Free tier | 15 regular AI responses/month, unlimited on free after upgrade tiers vary |
| Best for | Gmail-heavy users, customer support reps, sales/outreach teams |
| Standout feature | In-page Gmail auto-draft replies without switching tabs |

## What ChatGPT Writer / Jetwriter AI Actually Is

The extension installs into Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera or Vivaldi (Safari and Firefox support is listed as "coming soon" as of this writing) and adds an AI icon to the compose windows of supported sites — most notably Gmail, but also Outlook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp Web, Slack, Freshdesk, Zendesk and Zoho. Click it, describe what you want to say (or let it read the email you're replying to and suggest a response), and it drafts text inline that you can edit before sending.

Under the hood, the tool routes requests to more than one AI model — the vendor states it lets users switch between GPT-5, Claude and Gemini depending on the task and plan tier, rather than being locked to a single model provider. That's a meaningful difference from installing a raw ChatGPT bookmarklet: the extension handles reading the email thread's context, matching your writing tone, and inserting output back into the compose box, which a general-purpose chatbot tab doesn't do on its own.

The pitch is speed inside existing workflows — the tool is designed so a support rep, recruiter, or busy inbox-owner never has to alt-tab to a chatbot, copy a reply, then paste it back into Gmail.

## Pricing

Pricing, free-tier limits and feature availability below were accurate as of this post's publish date (2026-09-19) per the vendor's own pricing page, but AI tool pricing and feature sets change often — confirm current numbers on the [official Jetwriter AI pricing page](https://jetwriter.ai/pricing) before subscribing.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 15 regular AI responses/month, browser extension + web app, voice input, live web access, file attachments |
| Elite | $18/mo (or $14/mo billed annually at $168/year) | Unlimited regular AI responses, ~1,000 advanced-model responses/month, 50 Gmail auto-draft replies/day, priority support |
| Ultra | $39/mo (or $29/mo billed annually at $349/year) | Unlimited regular AI responses, ~2,500 advanced-model responses/month, 70 Gmail auto-draft replies/day, priority support |

Both paid tiers bill month-to-month with no lock-in — the vendor states plans are "cancel anytime." The free plan is genuinely usable for light, occasional email drafting (15 responses a month works out to roughly half a reply a day), but anyone drafting daily will bump into that ceiling quickly and need to weigh Elite against just using a general chatbot manually.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Gmail auto-draft replies.** This is the extension's headline feature and the reason most people install it. Open a received email in Gmail, click the extension icon, and it reads the thread and proposes a reply matched to context — you can nudge tone (formal, casual, brief) before inserting it into the compose box. The daily cap (50 on Elite, 70 on Ultra) is generous for individual use but worth watching if you're doing high-volume outbound.

**Multi-site coverage beyond email.** Unlike tools scoped only to Gmail, this extension also works inside LinkedIn messaging, WhatsApp Web, Slack, and support-desk tools like Zendesk, Freshdesk and Zoho. For a customer support agent fielding tickets across multiple channels, that consistency matters more than raw output quality on any single platform.

**Model switching (GPT-5 / Claude / Gemini).** Rather than being tied to one vendor's model, paid plans let you pick which underlying model handles a given draft. In practice this mostly matters for edge cases — one model handling a delicate customer complaint better than another — and most users will rarely change the default.

**Live web access and document chat.** The extension can pull in current information from the web when drafting (useful for anything time-sensitive) and can reference an uploaded document while composing, which is handy for support replies that need to quote a policy or spec sheet.

**Voice input.** You can dictate the gist of a reply rather than typing a prompt, which speeds things up further on mobile-adjacent workflows or for users who find speaking faster than typing a request.

## Who It's Actually For

**Solo users and freelancers** replying to a moderate volume of client emails will likely be fine on the free tier or a low-cost Elite subscription — the value is entirely in not breaking flow to open a separate chatbot tab.

**Customer support and sales teams** working across Zendesk, Freshdesk, LinkedIn and email simultaneously get the most out of this over a plain ChatGPT subscription, because the extension's whole value proposition is inline drafting across those specific tools rather than a general-purpose chat window.

**Recruiters and outreach-heavy roles** benefit from the LinkedIn and Gmail combination specifically, since a large share of their daily writing happens in exactly those two places.

**Enterprises needing compliance guarantees, audit logs, or admin-level seat management** should look elsewhere or contact the vendor directly before rolling this out — nothing on the public pricing page indicates dedicated enterprise/SSO tooling the way larger writing-assistant platforms (like Grammarly Business) offer.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Drafts inline in Gmail/Outlook/LinkedIn without tab-switching | Free tier caps at just 15 responses/month |
| Multi-model support (GPT-5, Claude, Gemini) on paid plans | Brand confusion — many searchers assume it's an official OpenAI product, and it isn't |
| Broad integration list (Slack, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Zoho, WhatsApp Web) | Safari and Firefox not yet supported |
| Lightweight extension (vendor states under 1MB) | No published enterprise/team-seat pricing tier |
| No long-term contract — cancel anytime on paid plans | Daily Gmail auto-draft cap (50–70/day) can bind for high-volume senders |

## Integrations and Ecosystem

The extension's integration list is its main differentiator from a plain chatbot: Gmail, Outlook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp Web, Slack, Freshdesk, Zendesk and Zoho are all supported directly inside their native web interfaces. There's no public Zapier listing or open API on the marketing site as of this writing — confirm directly with the vendor if workflow-automation triggers are a dealbreaker.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

If most of your writing workload lives inside Gmail, LinkedIn messaging, or a support-ticket queue, and you want AI-assisted drafts without breaking your normal workflow to open a separate AI chat window, this extension does exactly that job well. The free tier is a reasonable way to trial it before committing to a paid plan, and the annual pricing on Elite ($14/month effective) is competitive against paying for a general ChatGPT Plus subscription and manually copy-pasting between tabs.

## Where to Think Twice

**If you need a fully free, unlimited tool**, the 15-responses-a-month free cap will feel restrictive fast — daily email volume for most professionals blows past that within the first week or two of a month.

**If your team needs enterprise compliance features** — SOC 2 documentation, SSO, centralized admin billing, audit trails — there's nothing on the public site indicating those exist yet; you'd need to reach out to the vendor directly and get it in writing before rolling this out at a company with strict procurement requirements.

**If you're specifically looking for OpenAI's own ChatGPT product**, this isn't it — you want the actual chatgpt.com product, which we cover in a separate review.

**If you need offline or on-premises use**, this is a cloud-connected browser extension with no offline mode; every draft round-trips to the vendor's servers and the underlying model APIs.

## The Bottom Line

ChatGPT Writer — now operating as Jetwriter AI — solves a narrow but real problem: getting AI-drafted replies directly into Gmail, LinkedIn, and support-desk tools without leaving the page. It's not a general-purpose chatbot substitute, and it isn't affiliated with OpenAI despite the name overlap that still drives most of its search traffic. For anyone whose day is genuinely dominated by inbox and DM replies, the $14–$29/month range (billed annually) is a fair price for staying in flow; for anyone who just wants a capable AI assistant for general writing and research, a standalone chatbot subscription will cover more ground for similar money.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is ChatGPT Writer made by OpenAI?**
No. It's an independent third-party browser extension built on top of multiple AI models (including GPT models), not an OpenAI product. OpenAI's own product is ChatGPT at chatgpt.com.

**What happened to the name "ChatGPT Writer"?**
The product rebranded to Jetwriter AI; the original chatgptwriter.ai domain now redirects to jetwriter.ai, though many users and search results still reference the older name.

**Is there a free version?**
Yes — the free tier includes 15 regular AI responses per month along with the browser extension, web app, voice input, and file attachments, but it excludes access to advanced AI models.

**Which browsers does it support?**
Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi are supported. Safari and Firefox are listed by the vendor as coming soon, not currently available.

**Does it work with Outlook and LinkedIn, or just Gmail?**
It works across Gmail, Outlook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp Web, Slack, Freshdesk, Zendesk and Zoho, though Gmail auto-draft replies are the feature most heavily marketed.

**How much does the paid plan cost?**
Elite starts at $18/month (or $14/month billed annually at $168/year), and Ultra starts at $39/month (or $29/month billed annually at $349/year). Both include unlimited regular-model responses and a capped allotment of advanced-model responses.

**Is my email data private?**
The vendor doesn't publish detailed data-handling documentation on its marketing pages beyond general privacy-policy links, so if data privacy is a hard requirement for your organization, request their privacy policy and any compliance documentation directly before adopting it for sensitive correspondence.

**What's a good alternative if I just want a general AI assistant, not an inbox-specific extension?**
OpenAI's own ChatGPT is the more general-purpose option if your writing needs extend well beyond email/LinkedIn/support replies — see our full [ChatGPT review](/blog/chatgpt-review) for pricing and feature details on that separate product.

For more AI and software tool coverage and active discount codes, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Kin AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Kin AI pairs guided journaling with memory-sharing AI advisors. Here's what it costs, how it works, and who it's actually built for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Kin AI worth it?

Kin AI is a mobile journaling and personal-advisor app that pairs guided reflection with a set of specialized AI "advisors" who share memory across conversations. It's a solid pick if you want journaling with continuity and pattern-spotting, but the free tier is limited and the subscription pricing (up to roughly $44/month for the top tier) is steep for a journaling app.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (limited); paid tiers from around $20/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — core journaling and some advisors free, no card required |
| **Best for** | Solo users wanting continuity-based journaling with AI reflection |
| **Standout feature** | Shared memory across five specialized AI advisors |

## What Kin AI actually is

Kin is built by Kin ApS (listed on the App Store under seller Cap TechCo ApS), and it bills itself as "AI that actually knows you" rather than a generic chatbot. The pitch is continuity: instead of starting a fresh conversation every time, Kin retains what you've told it — about your job, your relationships, your goals — and uses that history to shape future conversations, journal prompts, and advice.

The product doesn't publicly disclose which underlying language model(s) power its advisors. That's fairly typical for consumer AI-companion apps, which frequently route requests through third-party model providers behind the scenes, but it does mean you can't verify accuracy or reasoning quality against a known model's track record. If that matters to you, it's worth asking Kin's support team directly before committing to a paid plan.

Structurally, Kin is organized around five things:

- **Advisory Board** — five specialized AI personas covering Work & Productivity, Relationships, Values & Meaning, Body & Energy, and Social Confidence, all drawing on the same shared memory of you
- **Journal** — guided, prompted journaling ("Help me process how I'm feeling about work today") rather than a blank page, with the app surfacing patterns across entries over time
- **Sessions** — longer, structured guided conversations that build on prior history instead of resetting each time
- **Voice** — spoken conversation mode, for talking through a reflection instead of typing it
- **Insights** — proactive pattern detection, e.g. flagging recurring emotional themes or connecting a current situation to a past one

## Pricing

According to its App Store listing, Kin runs on a freemium in-app-purchase model with three paid tiers, billed monthly, quarterly, or annually:

| Plan | Monthly | Quarterly | Annual | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | — | — | Core journaling and limited access to some advisors |
| Premium | ~$20/mo | ~$39/quarter | ~$189/yr | Full advisor board, expanded memory/sessions |
| Standard | ~$21.99/mo | ~$44.99/quarter | ~$169.99/yr | Similar tier positioning, alternate billing structure |
| Pro | ~$43.99/mo | ~$89.99/quarter | ~$339.99/yr | Highest usage limits, priority features |

A caveat worth flagging plainly: Kin doesn't publish a dedicated pricing page on its website — these figures come from the app's in-app purchase listing, and the naming/ordering of "Premium" vs. "Standard" isn't fully self-consistent in how Apple surfaces it, which suggests the tiers may be A/B tested or region-dependent. Don't take the numbers above as final; confirm exact current pricing inside the app before subscribing, since in-app-purchase pricing on both app stores changes more often and more quietly than a web pricing page would. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can shift without notice.

There's no web/desktop subscription checkout — Kin sells exclusively through Apple's and (presumably) Google's in-app purchase systems, which also means your subscription is managed through your phone's app store account, not a Kin-run billing portal.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Shared memory across advisors.** The five advisor personas aren't siloed — a detail you mention to the "Relationships" advisor can inform what the "Work & Productivity" advisor says later. This is the app's main technical bet: that continuity produces better advice than a stateless chatbot restarting from zero each session.

**Guided, prompted journaling.** Rather than a blank text box, Kin nudges you with specific prompts tied to your history ("this connects to what you said last week about..."). For people who stall out staring at an empty page, this is a meaningfully different experience than a plain journaling app like Day One.

**Voice mode.** Talking through a reflection out loud, rather than typing, lowers the friction for daily use — this is a common differentiator among AI companion apps versus static journaling tools.

**On-device-first storage.** Kin's privacy notice states that "most of your content — such as conversations, journal entries, and memory — stays locally on your device," with health data imported from Apple Health or Android Health Connect also kept on-device by default. For a journaling app handling sensitive personal reflection, that's a meaningfully different architecture than a pure cloud-sync competitor.

**Insights/pattern detection.** The app claims to surface recurring emotional patterns and connect current entries to past ones automatically, rather than requiring you to scroll back through old entries yourself.

## Who it's actually for

- **Daily journalers who want structure** — if you've tried journaling apps before and abandoned them because a blank page is intimidating, Kin's prompted format and continuity may keep you coming back more consistently than a plain notebook-style app.
- **People wanting a low-stakes reflective sounding board** — the Advisory Board format is aimed at everyday reflection (work stress, relationship friction, motivation), not clinical mental-health support.
- **Privacy-conscious users** — the on-device-first storage model and explicit "we do not sell your AI inputs" and "we do not use your data for advertisement" commitments matter if you'd otherwise avoid AI journaling tools over data concerns.
- **Not a fit for** anyone needing licensed therapy or crisis support — Kin is explicitly a self-reflection tool, not a substitute for a mental health professional.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Shared memory across advisors creates real continuity | No public web pricing page — figures only surface inside the app |
| On-device-first storage with explicit no-ad-training data commitments | Underlying AI model(s) not publicly disclosed |
| Guided prompts lower the barrier to consistent journaling | Paid tiers ($20–$44/mo) are expensive relative to plain journaling apps |
| Voice mode adds a lower-friction input option | Free tier is limited to "some" advisors, not clearly itemized |
| Strong App Store rating (4.8 stars) with a real install base | Mobile-only — no desktop or web app for daily use |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Kin is a standalone mobile app (iOS confirmed via its App Store listing; an Android build is referenced in company materials but wasn't independently verified here) with health-data import from Apple Health and Android Health Connect. There's no published public API, no browser extension, and no Zapier/Slack-style integrations — this is a closed, consumer-facing app rather than a platform meant to plug into other workflows. If you need an AI tool that connects into a broader stack (calendar, task manager, CRM), Kin isn't built for that; it's a self-contained personal-reflection app.

## Where it's a strong fit

Kin makes the most sense if your goal is a private, continuity-aware journal you'll actually open daily — the prompted format and cross-session memory solve the "blank page" problem that kills most journaling habits within a few weeks. The on-device-first privacy posture is also a genuine differentiator if you've been wary of putting personal reflections into a cloud-based AI chatbot.

## Where to think twice

Skip Kin if you need a fully free tool — the meaningful features (full advisor access, expanded memory, voice sessions) sit behind a subscription that runs comparably to Netflix or more per month. Skip it too if you want transparency into which AI model is generating your advice, since that isn't disclosed publicly. And skip it if you're looking for licensed mental-health support — Kin is a reflection and journaling companion, not therapy, and it doesn't claim otherwise. Finally, if you work primarily at a desktop, the mobile-only design will be a real friction point.

## The bottom line

Kin AI is a genuinely different take on journaling — shared memory across specialized advisors and an on-device-first privacy model set it apart from both plain journaling apps and generic AI chatbots repurposed for reflection. The free tier is enough to test whether the format clicks for you, but the jump to a paid plan is pricier than most journaling-specific tools, and the lack of a public pricing page or model disclosure means you're trusting the app store listing and the company's own claims more than you would with a fully transparent SaaS product. If daily, structured reflection with real continuity is what you're after, and the price doesn't bother you, it's worth the trial. If you just want a private place to write without a subscription, a plain journaling app will do the job for less.

## FAQ

**Is Kin AI free?**
Core journaling and access to some advisors are free with no card required. Full access to the Advisory Board, expanded memory, and voice sessions require a paid subscription.

**How much does Kin AI cost?**
Based on its App Store listing, paid tiers range from roughly $20/month up to about $44/month for the top Pro tier, with cheaper effective rates if you pay quarterly or annually. Confirm current pricing inside the app, since in-app purchase pricing isn't published on Kin's website and can change.

**What AI model powers Kin?**
Kin doesn't publicly disclose which underlying language model(s) it uses. If that's important to your decision, contact their support team directly before subscribing.

**Does Kin AI store my data privately?**
Kin's privacy notice states that most content — conversations, journal entries, and memory — stays on-device by default, and the company states it does not sell AI inputs or use data for advertising. No independent security audit or certification (like SOC 2) is publicly referenced, however.

**Is Kin AI a replacement for therapy?**
No. Kin is a self-reflection and journaling companion, not a licensed mental health service, and shouldn't be used as a substitute for professional care.

**Is there an Android version of Kin AI?**
An Android release is referenced in company materials, but this review independently verified only the iOS App Store listing. Check the Google Play Store directly to confirm current Android availability.

**What's the main alternative to Kin AI?**
Plain journaling apps (e.g. Day One) offer lower-cost, non-AI journaling; general-purpose AI chatbots can also be used for reflective conversation, but lack Kin's persistent, structured memory across dedicated advisor personas.

**Can I cancel my Kin AI subscription anytime?**
Since subscriptions are sold through Apple's (and likely Google's) in-app purchase systems rather than a Kin-run billing portal, cancellation is managed through your phone's app store account settings, not inside Kin itself.

Kin AI doesn't currently have a dedicated coupon page on this site — check back, or browse other [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers on AI tools.

title: Durable AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Durable pairs AI website generation with a built-in CRM, bookings and invoicing. Here is what it costs and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Durable a good AI website builder?

Durable is best for solo operators and small service businesses (contractors, salons, consultants) who want a live website, CRM and basic booking/invoicing tools set up in minutes, not for designers who want pixel-level control. It generates a full site from a business description, then bundles lead capture, invoicing and AI copy tools around it, starting free with a Durable-branded subdomain.

### At a glance

| | Durable |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (subdomain site); $22/mo on annual billing for a custom domain |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — permanent free plan, capped at 10 CRM contacts, 5 images/month, 10 AI chat messages/month |
| Best for | Solo service businesses needing a fast site + CRM, not a design-first build |
| Standout feature | Bundles website, CRM, invoicing, and lead/blog "agents" into one AI-generated package |

Durable is a Vancouver-based startup that positions itself less as a website builder and more as an "AI business builder" — the website is the entry point, but the product is a small bundle of business-ops tools wrapped around it. You type in a business name, industry and location, and Durable generates a complete site — copy, stock imagery, layout, sections like services and testimonials — in under a minute. From there you're editing inside its own drag-block editor, not a freeform canvas.

Durable doesn't publish which underlying language or image model powers its generation, and there's no public technical documentation naming a specific AI vendor. Treat any claim about "which AI" is under the hood as unconfirmed until Durable states it directly.

## Pricing: what Durable actually costs

Durable runs three tiers. Pricing below reflects the published monthly-billed rate and the discounted rate you get by committing to annual billing (Durable says annual billing saves roughly 15%).

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0/month | Website on a durable.site subdomain, unlimited AI-generated pages, unlimited traffic, CRM (up to 10 contacts), 5 images/month, 10 AI chat messages/month, blog writer agent (2 posts/month), lead agent (2/month), basic support |
| Launch | ~$25/month billed monthly, ~$22/month billed annually | Everything in Free, plus a free custom domain, advanced SEO/GEO tools with weekly visibility ranking, unlimited bookings synced to a calendar, automated lead replies, 50 images/month, 1,000 AI chat messages/month, blog writer agent (10 posts/month), lead agent (20/month), priority support |
| Grow | ~$49/month billed monthly, ~$41/month billed annually | Everything in Launch, plus a 1:1 onboarding call, unlimited team members, 500 images/month, unlimited AI chat, blog writer agent (32 posts/month), lead agent (100/month), daily AI ranking tracking |

A few things worth flagging on pricing. The Free plan's website only lives on a Durable subdomain (`yourbusiness.durable.site`) — you need Launch or above to point a real domain at it, though Durable includes the domain itself free up to a stated value (around $20) rather than charging separately for registration. Every tier also caps AI-generated images, chat replies and auto-written blog posts per month, which matters if you're leaning on the blog writer agent as a main content engine — 10 posts a month on Launch sounds generous until you compare it to a dedicated writing tool with no monthly ceiling.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability reflect what was published on Durable's site as of this post's date and can change — always confirm current numbers on [Durable's official pricing page](https://durable.com/pricing) before subscribing.

## Core features that actually differentiate Durable

**Instant site generation from a business description.** This is Durable's headline move — answer a handful of prompts (business type, name, location, tone) and it assembles a multi-page site with copy, images and structure already filled in. You're not starting from a blank canvas or a template gallery; you're starting from an almost-finished draft you then edit down.

**A built-in CRM and lead pipeline.** Most AI site builders stop at the website. Durable attaches a lightweight CRM to every plan (10 contacts free, unlimited on paid tiers) so leads captured through site forms flow straight into a contact list you can follow up from, rather than needing to wire up a separate tool like HubSpot or a Google Sheet.

**"Agents" for recurring content and lead work.** The blog writer agent and lead agent automate ongoing tasks rather than one-time generation — the blog agent drafts new posts on a schedule, and the lead agent auto-responds to and qualifies incoming leads. Both are capped monthly (2 posts/2 leads free, up to 32/100 on Grow); test performance on the free plan before trusting them for client-facing replies.

**Bookings, invoicing and payments bundled in.** Paid plans sync bookings to a calendar and support taking payments, which matters for the service-business audience Durable is clearly built for (a plumber, tutor or photographer who needs "get found, get booked, get paid" in one place, not three subscriptions).

**AI image studio for on-brand visuals.** Instead of generic template stock photos, Durable's image tools generate logos and marketing graphics tied to the business's stated branding — useful for a solo founder with no design budget, though output quality varies by industry and prompt.

## Who Durable is actually for

- **Solo service-business owners** (contractors, personal trainers, local consultants) who need a professional-looking site plus basic lead tracking live today, and don't want to stitch together a website tool, a CRM and a booking tool separately — the Launch plan is built almost exactly for this person.
- **Very early-stage founders testing an idea** who just need a page to validate a concept — the Free plan covers that without a credit card, as long as a Durable subdomain is acceptable short-term.
- **Small teams that want one dashboard for site + leads** rather than best-in-class tools for each — Grow adds unlimited team seats and daily ranking tracking, aimed at a small crew running the business's online presence together.
- **Not a fit for design-led brands or agencies.** If you need precise control over layout, custom code, or a portfolio-grade visual identity, Durable's block editor is noticeably more constrained than a design-first tool — see the Framer AI comparison below.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Generates a usable, structured site in under a minute from a short prompt | Editor is template/block-based, not a freeform design canvas |
| CRM, bookings, invoicing and lead agent bundled instead of separate subscriptions | Free plan's contacts (10), images (5/month) and AI chat (10/month) caps are tight |
| Free plan has no time limit, just feature caps | Custom domain and most automation require a paid plan |
| Pricing undercuts stitching together a site builder + CRM + booking tool separately | No named underlying AI model — hard to independently judge output quality claims |
| Blog and lead "agents" automate recurring work, not just one-time generation | Monthly caps on AI images/chat/blog posts on every tier, including Grow |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Durable is intentionally more closed than an open platform like WordPress or Framer — it doesn't offer a public plugin marketplace or app store. Its ecosystem is native: the CRM, booking calendar, invoicing/payments, and AI content agents live inside Durable rather than as add-ons. There's no publicly documented Zapier integration or open API on its pricing/features pages, so confirm current integration support directly with Durable support if your workflow depends on it.

## Where Durable is a strong fit

- You're a solo service provider who needs "online today" more than a custom design.
- You want leads, bookings and invoicing handled by the same tool that hosts your site, instead of juggling three logins.
- You're comfortable with AI-generated copy and images as a starting draft you'll lightly edit, not a finished, hand-crafted brand.
- Budget matters more than design flexibility — Launch at roughly $22–25/month undercuts paying separately for a site builder, a CRM and a booking tool.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a fully free, unrestricted tool** — Durable's free tier is real but capped tightly enough (10 contacts, 5 images, 10 AI chats a month) that most working businesses will outgrow it within weeks.
- **If your brand needs a custom, design-heavy look** — the block-based editor won't get you the freeform layout control that Framer AI or a hand-coded site would.
- **If you need enterprise compliance or a large team workflow** — Durable's plans top out at "unlimited team members" on Grow with no visible SOC 2/enterprise security page, so teams with formal compliance requirements should verify directly with Durable's support before adopting it for anything beyond a small business site.
- **If you want a portfolio, agency, or content-heavy publication site** — Durable's structure (services, bookings, leads) is clearly optimized for local/service businesses, not blogs, media sites or creative portfolios.
- **If you need guaranteed API/Zapier connectivity today** — confirm current integration support first; it isn't clearly documented as of this review.

## Bottom line

Durable's real pitch isn't "AI writes your website" — plenty of tools do that now. It's that the website comes pre-wired to a CRM, a booking calendar and basic invoicing, aimed at a solo service business that would otherwise need three separate subscriptions to get the same result. That focus is also its limit: if you want design freedom, a content-heavy site, or deep third-party integrations, Durable's block editor and closed ecosystem will feel restrictive fast. For "I need a site and a way to track leads, live by tonight," it's a genuinely efficient shortcut; for anything more ambitious, compare it against a design-first AI builder instead.

## FAQ

**Is Durable free to use?**

Yes. Durable's Free plan has no time limit, but it restricts you to a Durable subdomain, 10 CRM contacts, 5 AI images a month and 10 AI chat messages a month. A custom domain and most automation features require the Launch plan or above.

**How much does Durable cost per month?**

Launch is roughly $22/month billed annually (about $25/month billed monthly), and Grow is roughly $41/month annually (about $49/month monthly), based on Durable's published pricing at the time of writing. Confirm current rates on Durable's pricing page since AI tool pricing changes often.

**What AI model powers Durable's website generation?**

Durable doesn't publicly name the underlying language or image model in its marketing or pricing pages, so this should be treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed.

**Can I use my own domain on Durable's free plan?**

No — pointing a custom domain at your site requires the Launch plan or higher, which includes the domain free up to a stated value rather than charging separately for registration.

**Is Durable good for beginners with no design experience?**

Yes, that's its core audience — you answer prompts about your business and get a structured site without needing to make layout decisions from scratch. The tradeoff is less control than a freeform design tool would offer.

**Does Durable handle customer data and privacy responsibly?**

Durable's CRM stores customer contact details you collect through your site, so review Durable's own privacy policy and terms directly for how that data is handled, retained and secured — this review doesn't substitute for reading their current policy.

**What's the difference between Durable and Framer AI or Dora AI?**

Durable is built around business operations — CRM, bookings, invoicing and lead automation wrapped around an AI-generated site — aimed at local service businesses. Framer AI focuses on a full design canvas for teams that want precise visual control, and Dora AI leans toward interactive 3D/animation-heavy sites. Read our [Framer AI review](/blog/framer-ai-review) for the design-first comparison.

**Are there alternatives to Durable worth considering?**

If you need deeper design control, Framer AI or Dora AI are closer to what a design-conscious founder or agency would want; if you need a pure content-management/blog-first site, a traditional CMS may fit better than any AI business builder. Browse more [AI & software deals](/category/software) to compare options.

title: MajorGen Review 2026: AI Resume Builder Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Is MajorGen's AI resume and cover letter generator worth it? Real pricing, ATS claims, and honest limitations for job seekers.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## MajorGen Review 2026: Is This AI Resume Builder Worth It?

MajorGen is an AI resume and cover letter generator that turns a job description plus your existing resume or LinkedIn profile into a tailored, ATS-formatted document in under a minute. It's a reasonable pick for high-volume job applications, with paid tiers priced low ($3–$5/month), though the "AI-detects-everything" marketing claims deserve some skepticism.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (unlimited resumes on the Free plan) |
| **Paid tiers** | Basic $3/month, Pro $5/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — no credit card required |
| **Best for** | Active job seekers applying to many roles quickly |
| **Standout feature** | Job-description-to-resume tailoring in under a minute |

## What MajorGen actually is

MajorGen is built by Workergen and positions itself as a job-application accelerator rather than a general-purpose resume template site. The workflow is simple: paste a job description, add your background by uploading an existing resume or pointing it at your LinkedIn profile URL, and the tool generates a resume (and, separately, a cover letter) matched to that specific posting. MajorGen's marketing copy claims the output achieves a "98% ATS score" and generates in under 30 seconds — these are the vendor's own figures, not independently verified numbers, and "ATS score" isn't a standardized industry metric, so treat it as a directional claim rather than a guarantee that any given applicant tracking system will rank your resume highly.

The pitch is squarely aimed at people running a high-volume job search: instead of hand-editing one master resume for every application, you regenerate a tailored version per posting and manage the results from a dashboard. That's a genuinely different use case from a typical resume-builder-with-templates product, worth keeping in mind when judging whether the pricing and feature set fit you.

There's no public information about which underlying language model MajorGen runs on — the site doesn't disclose this. If that matters to you, it's worth asking MajorGen's support directly before committing.

## Pricing

MajorGen's own landing page markets a "credit-based, no subscriptions, credits never expire" model, but the actual in-app pricing page (app.majorgen.com/pricing) lists three tiers billed monthly rather than a pay-per-credit system. That's a discrepancy worth flagging: the top-level marketing page and the live pricing page don't fully agree on the billing model, so confirm the current structure on the pricing page before you pay.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0/month | Unlimited resumes and cover letters, standard templates |
| Basic | $3/month | Everything in Free, plus document downloads and a prompt editor |
| Pro | $5/month | Everything in Basic, plus a WYSIWYG (visual) editor and multiple candidate profiles |

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — always check MajorGen's current pricing page before subscribing, since AI tool pricing and feature sets move fast, and this one already shows some inconsistency between its own pages.

At $3–$5 a month, MajorGen is priced well under most dedicated resume-builder subscriptions (many of which run $15–$40/month), which is arguably its biggest selling point regardless of which billing model is currently live.

## Core features walkthrough

**Job-description-driven tailoring.** The core mechanic — paste a job posting, get a resume mapped to it — is what separates MajorGen from a static resume template tool. Instead of you manually rewriting bullet points to mirror a job listing's language, the AI handles the rewording pass.

**LinkedIn import.** You can seed your profile by pasting a LinkedIn URL instead of uploading a resume file, which lowers the barrier for first-time users who don't have a polished resume ready to upload.

**Multiple profiles (Pro).** The Pro tier supports creating more than one candidate profile, which is useful if you're job-hunting across genuinely different roles or industries (say, a hybrid marketing/data background) where a single master profile doesn't cover the range.

**WYSIWYG and prompt editors.** Basic unlocks a prompt-based editor for adjusting generated text; Pro adds a visual (WYSIWYG) editor for direct formatting control. This tiering is a reasonable way to separate casual users from people who want to fine-tune layout.

**Dashboard for bulk applications.** Generated resumes and cover letters live in a central dashboard, which matters more than it sounds like it should once you're tracking a dozen-plus tailored versions across different applications.

## Who it's actually for

- **Active job seekers applying to many roles per week** get the most value — the tailoring workflow is built for volume, and the Free tier's "unlimited resumes and cover letters" claim (if accurate at signup) removes the cost barrier for testing it out.
- **First-time resume writers** who don't already have a document to start from can use the LinkedIn import path instead of building from scratch, though they should still expect to proofread and adjust the output rather than trust it blind.
- **Career changers managing more than one professional identity** are the clearest case for upgrading to Pro, since multiple profiles let you keep, say, a technical resume and a management-track resume separate without overwriting one another.
- **Job seekers who want deep design control over layout and typography** may find MajorGen's templates limiting compared to dedicated resume-design tools — the emphasis here is speed and ATS formatting, not visual customization.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Low-cost paid tiers ($3–$5/month) vs. most resume-builder competitors | Pricing model description is inconsistent between MajorGen's marketing page and its live pricing page |
| Fast, job-description-specific tailoring workflow | "98% ATS score" and generation-speed claims are vendor-stated, not independently verified |
| LinkedIn import lowers the barrier to entry | No published information on the underlying AI model |
| Free tier available with no credit card required | Limited public documentation on data handling/privacy specifics |
| Multiple profile support on Pro for career changers | Template variety and design customization appear more limited than dedicated resume builders |

## Integrations and ecosystem

MajorGen's public-facing integration surface is narrow: it accepts a LinkedIn profile URL as an input source and lets you upload an existing resume file, but there's no publicly documented API, Zapier connector, browser extension, or job-board integration (e.g. auto-apply through Indeed or LinkedIn Easy Apply). If you're expecting an end-to-end automated application pipeline — auto-fill and submit, not just generate — that's not currently part of the product. Anyone weighing MajorGen against tools that do offer job-board auto-apply should treat that as a genuine gap.

## Where it's a strong fit

MajorGen makes sense if your bottleneck in job hunting is the manual grind of rewriting a resume for every posting. The core workflow — job description in, tailored resume out — directly targets that friction, and the low monthly cost means the downside of trying it is small. It's also a reasonable on-ramp for someone without a polished resume, since starting from a LinkedIn profile removes the blank-page problem.

## Where to think twice

Be cautious about a few things before relying on MajorGen as your only resume tool. Don't take the "98% ATS score" figure as a guarantee — ATS compatibility depends on the specific system a given employer uses, and no vendor's internal metric substitutes for actually reading the output and confirming it reads naturally and accurately reflects your experience. The pricing-model inconsistency between MajorGen's marketing page (credit-based) and its live pricing page (subscription tiers) is worth resolving with their support before you commit, especially if you're expecting a pay-once, credits-never-expire arrangement and instead get billed monthly. If you need heavy design customization — distinctive layouts, custom typography, multi-column creative resumes — a dedicated resume-design tool will likely serve you better than an ATS-first generator like this one. And if strict data-handling transparency matters to you (a clearly published policy on how uploaded resumes and LinkedIn data are stored or used), verify that directly with MajorGen before uploading sensitive career history, since it isn't laid out clearly on the public marketing pages.

## Bottom line

MajorGen solves a specific, real problem — the tedium of re-tailoring a resume for every job application — at a price low enough that trying it costs almost nothing. The Free tier and $3–$5 paid plans undercut most resume-builder competitors by a wide margin, and the LinkedIn-import and job-description-matching workflow is genuinely useful for anyone applying at volume. The catches are around trust and polish: the marketing claims (ATS score, generation speed, and even the billing model itself) aren't fully consistent or independently verifiable, so this is a tool to test with a critical eye and a proofreading pass, not to treat as a fire-and-forget resume machine. For high-volume applicants on a budget, it's worth trying the free tier before deciding whether Basic or Pro earns a spot in your job search toolkit.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is MajorGen free to use?**
Yes — MajorGen offers a Free plan with unlimited resumes and cover letters using standard templates, and no credit card is required to sign up. Paid tiers (Basic at $3/month, Pro at $5/month) add downloading, a prompt editor, a visual editor, and multiple profiles.

**Does MajorGen charge a subscription or use credits?**
MajorGen's marketing page describes a credit-based, no-subscription, credits-never-expire model, but its live pricing page lists monthly subscription tiers (Free/Basic/Pro). This is inconsistent — confirm the current billing structure directly on MajorGen's pricing page before you sign up for a paid plan.

**How does MajorGen tailor a resume to a job posting?**
You paste the job description into MajorGen and provide your background either by uploading an existing resume or linking your LinkedIn profile. The AI generates a resume (and separately, a cover letter) that maps your experience to the language and requirements in that specific posting.

**Can I trust MajorGen's "98% ATS score" claim?**
Treat it as a vendor-stated figure, not an independently verified benchmark. ATS compatibility varies by the specific applicant tracking system an employer uses, and there's no universal, standardized "ATS score" across the industry — so this number describes MajorGen's own internal testing rather than a guarantee for any particular job application.

**Does MajorGen have an API or integrate with job boards?**
Not based on publicly available information. MajorGen accepts a LinkedIn URL or resume upload as input, but there's no documented API, browser extension, or job-board auto-apply integration.

**Is MajorGen good for beginners with no existing resume?**
Yes — the LinkedIn import option is designed for exactly that case, letting you generate a first draft from your LinkedIn profile rather than starting from a blank document. You should still review and edit the output before submitting it to employers.

**What's the difference between the Basic and Pro plans?**
Basic ($3/month) adds document downloads and a prompt-based editor over the Free tier. Pro ($5/month) adds a WYSIWYG visual editor and support for multiple candidate profiles, useful if you're applying across more than one type of role.

**Who makes MajorGen?**
MajorGen is built by Workergen.

For more AI and software deals, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: TextCortex Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is TextCortex worth it? Our review covers its browser-extension writing tool, multi-model access, pricing tiers, and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is TextCortex worth it in 2026?

TextCortex is worth it if you want one AI writing layer that follows you across 30,000+ websites and apps via a browser extension, rather than a single standalone editor. It's less compelling if you specifically want a dedicated long-form writing studio like Jasper, since TextCortex now positions itself more broadly as an enterprise AI agent platform.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free; Premium from $23.99/user/month |
| Free tier / trial | Free plan with limited generations, plus a 14-day free trial of Premium |
| Best for | Teams that write across many web apps (email, CRM, docs, social) and want AI everywhere |
| Standout feature | Browser extension (Zeno) that injects AI writing/rewriting into 30,000+ sites |

TextCortex started as an AI writing assistant and browser extension for marketers, sales teams, and content creators. Over the past couple of years it has broadened its pitch to "enterprise AI infrastructure" — a hub for deploying AI agents, connecting company knowledge, and giving every employee model access without needing a dozen separate AI subscriptions. The writing extension is still the most tangible, day-to-day part of the product for most individual users, even as the company leans harder into agent building and workflow automation for larger teams.

The tool works through a Chrome/Edge browser extension plus a web app. The extension, internally branded as "Zeno," sits in text fields across the browser — Gmail, LinkedIn, Notion, Google Docs, CRMs, support ticketing tools — and lets you generate, rewrite, shorten, expand, or translate text without switching tabs. The web app adds a chat interface, document editor, knowledge base uploads, and (on paid plans) access to multiple third-party AI models rather than a single proprietary one.

### Pricing

TextCortex uses a three-tier structure: a permanently free plan, a paid Premium plan billed per user, and a custom Enterprise plan.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0/month | Core AI writing features, knowledge base access, up to 50 MB file storage, custom agent creation, limited generations |
| Premium | From $23.99/user/month | Everything in Free, access to all major AI models, higher/unlimited generation credits depending on tier, up to 10 GB file storage, AI image generation |
| Enterprise | Custom pricing | Everything in Premium, SSO/SCIM/SAML, dedicated deployment, centralized billing, priority support |

The Premium plan is sold in a few different credit tiers (TextCortex's pricing page lists several stepped options rather than one flat number), and pricing is quoted per user, excluding VAT. A 14-day free trial gives you a higher generation allowance than the free plan so you can test the paid features before committing a card.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tool vendors adjust credit allowances and tiers often, so confirm current numbers on [TextCortex's official pricing page](https://textcortex.com/pricing) before subscribing.

### Core features that actually differentiate it

**The browser extension is the product.** Most AI writing tools live in one app; TextCortex's biggest selling point is that it goes wherever you already type. Vendor materials describe compatibility with over 30,000 apps and sites through the extension, so instead of copy-pasting into ChatGPT and back, you can trigger a rewrite or continuation directly inside a Gmail draft, a Salesforce note, or a Zendesk reply.

**Model-agnostic access.** Rather than locking you into one underlying model, paid TextCortex plans give access to multiple major AI models through a single subscription. This matters if you've noticed that different models handle different tasks (brainstorming versus precise editing versus code-adjacent text) with different quality, and don't want separate subscriptions to switch between them.

**Knowledge bases and agents.** You can upload documents (up to the plan's storage limit) so the AI can reference your own style guides, product docs, or past content when generating new text. On top of that, TextCortex lets you build custom "agents" — configured personas or workflows with specific instructions, skills, and connectors — without writing code, and trigger them by @mentioning them in chat.

**AI image generation.** Premium plans bundle image generation alongside the text tools, useful for quick social graphics or blog headers without a separate subscription to an image generator.

**Templates and tone controls.** Like most AI writing tools, TextCortex ships pre-built templates (emails, product descriptions, social posts, ad copy) and lets you set a target tone or reading level, which speeds up repetitive writing tasks more than a blank-prompt chat window does.

### Who it's actually for

- **Solo marketers and customer-facing reps** who spend their day writing inside other tools (email, CRM, LinkedIn) benefit most from the extension-first approach — the free plan or a single Premium seat covers this well.
- **Small content and support teams** that want shared knowledge bases so AI-generated replies stay on-brand will find the knowledge base and agent features worth the per-seat Premium cost.
- **Agencies and larger teams** juggling multiple AI models for different clients may like not paying for separate ChatGPT, Claude, and other subscriptions per seat, since Premium bundles access to several.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** (SSO, SCIM, SAML, dedicated deployment) are the target of the Enterprise tier — but you'll need to contact sales for pricing and won't find self-serve numbers published.
- **Writers who want one deep, structured long-form editor** (think a novel manuscript or a heavily templated content calendar) may be better served by a dedicated long-form tool, since TextCortex's strength is breadth of reach rather than a single polished writing studio.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Works inside 30,000+ sites and apps via browser extension, not just one editor | Premium pricing is tiered by credit allowance, which can be confusing to compare against flat-rate competitors |
| Access to multiple AI models under one subscription | Free plan generation limits are fairly restrictive for daily heavy use |
| Knowledge base + custom agents let you tailor output to your own content | Enterprise pricing isn't published — you have to talk to sales |
| Free plan exists with no credit card required to start | Company's shift toward "enterprise AI agent platform" positioning means some marketing content is less focused on individual writers than it used to be |
| Built-in AI image generation on paid plans | Extension-based workflow depends on browser compatibility (primarily Chrome/Edge) rather than native desktop apps |

### Integrations and ecosystem

TextCortex's main integration surface is the browser extension itself, which functions as a lightweight integration into any site with a text field rather than a list of named app integrations. Beyond that, the platform lists native connectors for common workplace tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams, plus API access for teams that want to build the AI capabilities into their own internal tools rather than using the extension or web app directly. If you need a very specific named integration (a particular CRM or help desk, for example), check the current integrations list on TextCortex's site, since coverage changes as the product evolves.

### Where it's a strong fit

TextCortex is a strong fit if your writing work is scattered across many different web tools rather than concentrated in one editor. Sales reps drafting outreach in a CRM, support agents replying in a ticketing system, and marketers posting across social platforms all benefit from having AI assistance appear in the same window they're already working in, instead of needing to tab over to a chatbot and copy the result back.

It's also a reasonable pick for teams that want to consolidate AI model spend — if you're currently paying for more than one AI chatbot subscription just to compare outputs, a plan that bundles access to several major models under one seat price can work out cheaper.

### Where to think twice

Skip TextCortex if you need a fully free, unlimited writing tool — the free plan's generation limits will feel tight for daily professional use, and the real functionality sits behind the Premium tier. If your team specifically needs enterprise compliance features like SSO, SCIM, or SAML, know upfront that pricing for that tier isn't published, so you'll need a sales conversation before you can budget for it. And if you want a single, deeply structured long-form writing environment (a dedicated novel or long-report workspace with heavy revision history and structure tools), a purpose-built long-form editor will likely serve you better than a tool whose core strength is breadth across many small text fields rather than depth in one big document.

Also worth flagging: as with any AI writing tool, output still needs a human editorial pass. TextCortex doesn't publish independently verified accuracy or hallucination-rate figures, so treat generated claims, statistics, or quotes as drafts to fact-check rather than finished copy.

### Bottom line

TextCortex earns its keep by showing up where you already write instead of asking you to change your workflow to fit it. For individuals and small teams who live in Gmail, a CRM, or social platforms all day, the extension-first approach and bundled multi-model access are genuinely useful, and the free plan is a low-risk way to try it. Larger organizations weighing it against a dedicated long-form writing tool or a single-model chatbot subscription should map their actual use case — breadth across many apps versus depth in one editor — before picking a plan, and enterprise buyers should get an Enterprise quote early since it's not self-serve.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is TextCortex free to use?**
Yes, TextCortex offers a permanently free plan with core AI writing features, though generation limits are lower than on paid plans. A 14-day free trial of Premium is also available if you want to test the higher-limit paid features first.

**How much does TextCortex Premium cost?**
Premium starts at $23.99 per user per month (excluding VAT), with several credit-tier options available at that price point and above depending on how many AI generations you need monthly. Confirm the current tiers on TextCortex's pricing page, since credit allowances can change.

**Does TextCortex offer enterprise pricing?**
Yes. The Enterprise plan is custom-priced and adds SSO, SCIM, SAML, dedicated deployment, centralized billing, and priority support. You need to contact TextCortex's sales team for a quote.

**What makes TextCortex different from ChatGPT or a single-model AI writer?**
TextCortex's browser extension works inside thousands of other websites and apps, so you can generate and rewrite text directly inside the tool you're already using (email, CRM, docs) instead of switching to a separate chat window. Premium plans also bundle access to multiple AI models rather than one.

**Is TextCortex good for beginners?**
Yes — the templates, tone settings, and browser-extension shortcuts are built to require minimal prompting skill, which makes it approachable for people who aren't used to writing detailed AI prompts.

**How does TextCortex handle data privacy?**
TextCortex states it maintains GDPR-compliant infrastructure with ISO and SOC 2 certification, and describes a "zero data training" policy on its enterprise materials. Review its current privacy policy directly before relying on those claims for a procurement decision.

**What are the main alternatives to TextCortex?**
Common alternatives include Jasper (deeper long-form content workflows), Copy.ai (marketing copy templates and workflow automation), and Writingmate AI (credit-based access to a wide range of models) — see our [Writingmate AI review](/blog/writingmate-ai-review) for a comparison point if multi-model access is your priority.

**Can I cancel TextCortex Premium at any time?**
TextCortex bills Premium per user on a recurring basis; as with most SaaS subscriptions you should be able to cancel to avoid renewal, but confirm the exact cancellation and refund terms on the account/billing settings or TextCortex's terms page before subscribing, since specifics can vary by plan and region.
