**AI Meeting Assistant.** Automatic transcription and note generation across meeting platforms, supporting 16 languages. It produces a summary and pulls out action items without a visible bot in the call, since capture happens at the system level on your own device.

**Accent conversion.** An unusual feature for this category: Krisp can adjust a speaker's accent in real time or normalize how someone else's accent sounds to you, pitched as reducing miscommunication on international calls. Usage is capped by time-per-day on lower plans (1 hour/day on Core, 4 hours/day speaker-side on Advanced) rather than unlimited.

**Voice isolation (VIVA 2.5).** A newer capability that separates a target speaker's voice from overlapping background voices more aggressively than standard noise cancellation, aimed at crowded environments.

**Custom vocabulary.** Workspaces can add up to 750 custom terms, useful for company jargon or product names that generic transcription engines routinely mangle.

## Who it's actually for

- **Remote or hybrid individual contributors** on back-to-back calls from noisy environments — the Core plan's noise cancellation and note-taking justify the price alone.
- **Sales and customer success teams** — the Advanced plan's Salesforce/ConnectWise integration and manager view route meeting notes straight into a CRM pipeline.
- **Contact centers and BPOs** — Call Center AI is a distinct product with agent- and customer-side noise cancellation and after-call summaries, priced per agent.
- **Developers building voice products** — the Voice AI SDK exposes Krisp's noise-cancellation and voice-isolation models for embedding elsewhere, though pricing is entirely quote-based.
- **Regulated organizations** — the Enterprise tier's HIPAA option and on-device private transcription target healthcare, legal, and finance teams that can't send call audio to third-party servers by default.

Casual users who take the occasional video call and don't need transcription probably don't need Krisp — many video platforms now ship basic free noise suppression, and that may be enough.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Works across almost any app, not locked to one video platform | No permanently free tier, only a 7-day trial |
| No visible "bot" joining your calls to transcribe | Accent conversion and other features are time-capped on paid plans |
| Separate, purpose-built product for call centers | Enterprise and Call Center Advanced require a sales conversation |
| On-device processing option at the Enterprise tier | Underlying AI model details aren't disclosed |
| Custom vocabulary support for company terms | Annual billing needed to reach the lower per-seat prices |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Krisp connects with the tools most teams already use: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex, Slack, Discord, Salesforce, HubSpot, and Zapier, plus mobile apps for iOS/Android and a Chrome extension. Because the core noise-cancellation layer operates at the OS audio level rather than as a platform-specific plugin, it's less dependent on any single video vendor keeping an integration current. The Voice AI SDK is the path for developers building Krisp's audio processing into a custom application.

## Where it's a strong fit

Krisp earns its keep for anyone whose calls are regularly undermined by background noise — open offices, shared apartments, coffee shops, unreliable headsets. Only the person running Krisp needs it installed, unlike tools that require every participant to opt in. For sales teams and call centers, cleaner audio plus automatic summaries and CRM integration solves two problems with one subscription.

## Where to think twice

Krisp is a paid tool at every meaningfully useful tier — no free-forever plan, only a 7-day trial, so if you need a genuinely free option long-term, look elsewhere or lean on your video platform's built-in noise suppression. Accent conversion is capped by daily usage minutes on cheaper plans, so heavy users will need Advanced or Enterprise. Krisp doesn't publish the model architecture behind its transcription and note generation, so if your organization needs that documented for compliance, get it in writing from sales rather than relying on the public site. And if you need full on-premises or offline processing rather than the on-device option offered only at Enterprise, confirm that requirement with Krisp directly before committing budget.

## Bottom line

Krisp is a mature audio tool that has evolved past "just noise cancellation" into a broader meeting-productivity platform, and its app-agnostic approach to noise removal and transcription is a real differentiator versus bot-based competitors. It's not cheap past the trial, and some newer features still carry usage caps on paid plans. For remote workers, sales teams, and call centers dealing with genuinely noisy call environments, it's a solid buy; for someone who just wants free built-in noise suppression on the occasional video call, it's more tool than you need.

## FAQ

**Is Krisp free?**
Krisp offers a 7-day free trial with no credit card required. There's no permanent free tier for the full feature set — after the trial you need a paid Core, Advanced, or Enterprise plan.

**How much does Krisp cost?**
Meeting AI Core starts at $8/user/month billed annually ($16/month billed monthly). Advanced runs $15/user/month annually ($30/month billed monthly). Enterprise and Call Center AI Advanced are custom-quoted. Call Center AI Core starts at $15/agent/month billed annually.

**Does Krisp record or transcribe my meetings without other participants knowing?**
The AI Meeting Assistant captures and transcribes audio from meetings you're part of; unlike bot-based transcription tools it doesn't add a visible bot to the call roster, but check your organization's and local laws' requirements around notifying participants that a call is being recorded.

**What platforms does Krisp work with?**
Krisp works system-wide across most apps using your computer's audio, including Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex, Slack, and Discord, plus iOS/Android apps and a Chrome extension.

**Is Krisp good for call centers specifically?**
Yes — Krisp has a separate Call Center AI line (CC Core and CC Advanced) for contact centers, with agent- and customer-side noise cancellation, voice isolation, after-call summaries, and speech analytics, priced per agent.

**Does Krisp support languages other than English?**
Transcription supports 16 languages according to Krisp, and accent conversion targets cross-accent communication rather than translation, though voice translation is offered in Call Center AI Advanced and the developer SDK tiers.

**What AI model does Krisp use?**
Krisp doesn't publicly disclose the model architecture behind its noise cancellation, transcription, or note generation — it describes these as proprietary technology, branding its newer voice-isolation model "VIVA 2.5." Ask their sales team directly if you need this documented for compliance.

**Is there a cheaper or fully free Krisp alternative?**
Your video platform's built-in noise suppression is usually free but less capable, and dedicated transcription tools may focus purely on notes without the system-wide audio cleanup Krisp specializes in. Compare feature-for-feature before switching, since "cheaper" often means losing that cross-app noise cancellation.

For more AI and software deals, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: MyShell Review 2026: AI Agent Builder Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: MyShell lets you build AI chatbots and agents for free, plus paid AI art tools. Here's what it costs, who it's for, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is MyShell worth using to build an AI chatbot or agent?

MyShell is a free platform for building, chatting with, and publishing AI characters and agents without code, plus a separate paid product, MyShell Art, for AI image and video generation. It suits hobbyist creators and Telegram bot builders, less so teams needing enterprise support or predictable SLAs.

### At a glance

| | MyShell |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (core agent platform) |
| Paid add-on | MyShell Art from $7.49/mo (billed yearly) |
| Free tier | Yes — browse, chat with, and build agents at no cost |
| Best for | Solo creators, hobbyists, Telegram bot builders |
| Standout feature | No-code agent builder (Classic, Pro Config, ShellAgent modes) with an in-app "AIpp Store" for discovery |

## What MyShell actually is

MyShell describes itself as a decentralized AI consumer layer — a platform where anyone can create, share, and (in theory) monetize AI agents, rather than being limited to whatever a single closed-source chatbot vendor ships. It was backed early by crypto-native investors including Binance Labs and OKX, and runs alongside a native token, $SHELL, used for creator-incentive and governance mechanics through MyShell DAO.

That crypto backbone is worth flagging up front. MyShell isn't just "another Character.AI" — it's part chatbot builder, part app store for AI agents, and part token economy. If you only care about building and chatting with bots, ignore the token entirely and use the platform for free; if you're a creator hoping to eventually earn from a popular bot, the token and DAO mechanics matter more.

MyShell doesn't lock you into one LLM. Its documentation states creators can wire agents to closed-source models (GPT, Claude, Gemini), open-source models (Llama, Mixtral, and others), and MyShell's own in-house models tuned for role-play. Which model a public bot uses isn't always obvious from the chat UI, so check the agent's config or build your own if model choice matters.

Separately, MyShell has pushed into AI image and video generation under the **MyShell Art** brand, which now sits behind its own subscription and, as of this review, is effectively the front door at `app.myshell.ai` (which currently redirects visitors into the Art product). The original agent-builder experience is still there, one click further in via the Workshop.

## Pricing

MyShell's core functionality — browsing the agent store, chatting with existing bots, and building your own agent with the no-code Classic mode — carries no listed price. There's no published "Shells" or credit-cost table for agent usage in MyShell's documentation at time of writing, so for heavy usage (a high-traffic Telegram bot, say), confirm current rate limits and usage costs directly in the app before committing.

Where MyShell does have transparent pricing is **MyShell Art**:

| Plan | Monthly (billed yearly) | Monthly (billed monthly) | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | $7.49/mo | $9.99/mo | 30 daily energy (roughly 15 images), ad-free, lite priority render queue, high-resolution exports |
| Pro | $49.99/mo | $69.99/mo | 120 daily energy (roughly 60 images), ad-free, maximum priority render queue, watermark-free images, access to featured models (the vendor names Nano Banana Pro and Sora 2 as examples) |

The jump from Basic to Pro is steep — roughly 5–7x the price for 4x the daily energy — so Pro is really priced for people who need the priority queue and watermark removal, not just more volume. MyShell Art subscriptions are billed by a Singapore-registered entity (TensorMatrix Pte. Ltd.), worth knowing before you hand over card details. At the time of this review, MyShell's billing page also noted PayPal payments were temporarily unavailable while it updated billing infrastructure, so double-check your preferred payment method first.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability described here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly for AI tools — always confirm current numbers on MyShell's own site before subscribing.

## Core features walkthrough

**No-code agent builder with three skill tiers.** MyShell splits agent creation into Classic Mode (natural-language prompting and pre-built widgets for beginners), Pro Config Mode (JSON-based state-machine configuration for developers), and ShellAgent Mode (a visual, drag-and-connect interface for multi-step logic without hand-writing JSON). That range is unusual — most no-code bot builders offer one skill level, forcing you to stay basic or graduate to a separate developer product.

**A widget library, not just a prompt box.** MyShell states its platform includes over 1,000 modular widgets covering image generation, voice synthesis, and task-specific tools, which creators wire into an agent's logic by "drawing lines between blocks." An agent can do more than answer text questions — it can trigger image generation, voice output, or other workflow steps within one conversation.

**One-click Telegram deployment.** Any agent built in MyShell can reportedly connect to Telegram in minutes using a BotFather token, supporting one-on-one and group conversations with prompt updates syncing in near real time — a lower-friction path than building a bot integration from scratch.

**An "AIpp Store" for discovery.** MyShell hosts thousands of user-published agents across browsable categories — role-play characters, utility tools, meme generators, trading/analytics agents, and more — functioning like an app marketplace rather than a typical SaaS dashboard. Most users start by remixing an existing public agent instead of a blank canvas.

**MyShell Art for visual generation.** Though positioned as a separate product, MyShell Art is accessible from the same account and turns a single uploaded photo into stylized portraits, filters, or short videos across what the vendor describes as 200-plus styles, without writing an image prompt. It's the most polished piece of the ecosystem and clearly where recent product investment has gone.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and hobbyists** experimenting with character bots or companion-style agents get the free Classic Mode builder and public agent store as an easy entry point — no credit card, no coding.
- **Telegram community builders** who want a bot with personality (moderation, FAQ answering, roleplay, meme generation) get a fast path to deployment via BotFather.
- **Developers who want programmatic control** have Pro Config Mode and ShellAgent Mode, though docs are thinner than dedicated developer platforms — read our [Dynamiq review](/blog/dynamiq-review) if clearer developer docs matter more than no-code speed.
- **Casual creators wanting AI portraits or short video clips** are better served going straight to MyShell Art's Basic plan.
- **Businesses needing a support chatbot with SLAs and compliance documentation** should look elsewhere — our [Droxy AI review](/blog/droxy-ai-review) or [Chatbase review](/blog/chatbase-review) cover purpose-built support chatbots instead.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Free to browse, chat with, and build agents | No published pricing/credit table for core agent usage |
| Three creation modes span beginner to developer skill levels | Crypto/token layer ($SHELL, DAO) adds complexity most bot builders don't need |
| Fast, documented Telegram deployment path | Model transparency varies — not always obvious which LLM a public agent runs on |
| Large public library of remixable agents to learn from | Product focus has visibly shifted toward MyShell Art recently |
| MyShell Art pricing is clear and published | Pro Art tier is a steep jump from Basic for ~4x the daily generation allowance |

## Integrations and ecosystem

MyShell's most concrete integration is **Telegram**, via a BotFather token connection the vendor says takes about five minutes. Agents can also be exported as JSON, allowing them to be moved outside MyShell's Workshop, though this targets developers comfortable with agent state configs, not a plug-and-play integration. Beyond Telegram, MyShell doesn't publicly document Zapier, Slack, or Discord integrations the way many competitors do — confirm current support directly if a specific integration is a dealbreaker.

## Where it's a strong fit

MyShell works well if you want to build or chat with AI characters for free, ship a personality-driven bot to a Telegram community quickly, or generate stylized AI portraits/videos without prompt-engineering skill. The no-code builder lowers the barrier for non-developers, and the public agent store gives newcomers something to learn from rather than a blank page.

## Where to think twice

Skip MyShell if you need a business-grade support chatbot with clear SLAs, admin/team seat management, and compliance documentation (SOC 2, GDPR data processing agreements) — MyShell doesn't market itself or publish pricing around that use case. Also think twice if predictable pricing matters to you: the core platform's usage limits and any credit costs aren't published the way a typical SaaS pricing page lays them out, so you're relying on trial-and-error rather than a rate card. And if you're uncomfortable with a crypto token and DAO governance layered into a product's business model, that's structural to MyShell's creator economy, not an optional add-on.

## Bottom line

MyShell is one of the more ambitious no-code agent builders around, mainly because it doesn't stop at chatbots — it pairs a flexible three-tier agent builder with Telegram deployment, a public agent marketplace, and a growing AI art product, all reachable from one free account. The trade-off is a platform split between two identities: a community-driven agent-creation tool and an increasingly art-focused consumer app, with a crypto-token layer underneath both. For a hobbyist who wants to build and ship a character bot for free, it's hard to beat. For a business that needs predictable pricing and support-grade reliability, it's the wrong tool — the dedicated chatbot builders reviewed elsewhere on this site are a better start.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is MyShell free to use?**
Yes. Browsing the public agent store, chatting with existing agents, and building your own agent in Classic Mode don't carry a listed price. MyShell Art, the separate image/video generation product, is where paid subscription tiers apply.

**How much does MyShell Art cost?**
As of this review, Basic is $7.49/month billed yearly ($9.99/month billed monthly) with 30 daily energy (roughly 15 images), and Pro is $49.99/month billed yearly ($69.99/month billed monthly) with 120 daily energy (roughly 60 images), a priority render queue, and watermark-free exports. Confirm current pricing on MyShell's own site.

**What models does MyShell support?**
Its documentation states creators can build agents on closed-source models (GPT, Claude, Gemini), open-source models (Llama, Mixtral, and others), and MyShell's own in-house models tuned for role-play. Which model a specific public agent uses isn't always displayed in the chat interface.

**Can I deploy a MyShell agent to Telegram?**
Yes, via a BotFather token connection the vendor says takes about five minutes to set up, supporting both direct messages and group chats.

**Does MyShell have a customer support / business chatbot plan?**
Not really. There's no published enterprise tier, SLA, or admin/seat structure comparable to dedicated support platforms. Our [Chatbase review](/blog/chatbase-review) and [Droxy AI review](/blog/droxy-ai-review) cover tools built for that use case.

**What's the $SHELL token used for?**
MyShell ties $SHELL to creator incentives and governance through the MyShell DAO — creators of popular agents can eventually be rewarded through the token economy. You don't need to touch the token to build or use a free agent.

**Is there a MyShell coupon or discount code?**
MyShell doesn't currently have a dedicated coupon page on this site. Check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers on other AI tools.

title: Wonderchat Review 2026: Is This AI Chatbot Worth It?
excerpt: Wonderchat review covering resolution-based pricing, citation-grounded answers, multi-channel deployment, and who this AI chatbot builder actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Wonderchat Review 2026: Is This AI Chatbot Worth It?

Wonderchat is a good fit if you want a citation-focused support agent that trains on your existing help center and docs and deploys across web, WhatsApp, and SMS in minutes — but its plans are priced and billed around resolutions, not seats, and the useful tiers start well above what solo builders typically pay for Chatbase or Chaindesk.

### At a glance

| | Details |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (10 resolutions/month); paid plans from $124/month (billed yearly) |
| Free tier / trial | Yes — free plan plus a 7-day trial on paid plans |
| Best for | Support teams that want source-cited answers and multi-channel deployment (web, WhatsApp, SMS) |
| Standout feature | Built-in QA agent that flags weak bot answers for one-click fixes |

## What Wonderchat Actually Is

Wonderchat is an AI support and lead-qualification agent builder. You point it at a help center, documentation site, webpages, or a batch of past support tickets, and it trains a chatbot that answers customer questions with citations back to the source material rather than free-floating generated text. The company doesn't publish which underlying language model or models power the agent, so if that matters for your compliance or vendor-risk process, that's a detail to confirm directly with Wonderchat's sales team rather than assume.

The pitch is less "chatbot for a website" and more "support agent that replaces or triages the first line of a help desk." Wonderchat's own marketing claims a 70%+ resolution rate across the 500+ teams it says use the product, and cites one customer deflecting 92% of repetitive tickets. Those are Wonderchat's own reported figures rather than independently audited numbers, so treat them as directional, not a guarantee for your specific content or support volume.

## Pricing

Wonderchat's pricing is built around monthly "resolutions" (successfully answered conversations) and "credits" (a broader usage unit that also covers things like re-training and voice minutes), not a flat per-seat fee. That's a meaningfully different model from tools like Chatbase, which price mostly on message credits per plan, or Chaindesk, which leans on a simpler agent-count structure.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0/month | ~10 resolutions/month, 20 credits, 50 webpages stored, 1 AI agent, embeddable widget, human handover, basic integrations |
| Basic | $124/month (billed yearly) | ~1,000 resolutions/month, 5,000 credits/month, 1,000 webpages/agent, 2 AI agents, 3 team seats, 2 chat workflows, self-improving agents |
| Scale (most popular) | $417/month (billed yearly) | ~5,000 resolutions/month, 25,000 credits/month, 2,500 webpages/agent, 4 AI agents, advanced analytics, voice agent, helpdesk integrations |
| Enterprise | From $1,499/month (custom) | Custom resolutions and storage, bulk message discounts, SOC 2 & HIPAA compliance, SSO, custom integrations, SMS agent, priority support |

Both the Basic and Scale prices above are the yearly-billed rate — Wonderchat advertises roughly a 17% discount for paying annually, meaning the monthly-billed sticker price on both plans runs noticeably higher. There's also a pay-as-you-go add-on: an extra 1,000 message credits costs $29.99 as a one-time purchase from inside the dashboard, useful if you occasionally spike past your plan's monthly allotment without wanting to upgrade tiers outright.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on Wonderchat's own pricing page before buying, since AI tool pricing moves fast.

No store entry for Wonderchat exists on this site yet, so there's no coupon code to apply here — check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers on other AI tools in the meantime.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Multi-source training.** Wonderchat can ingest help center articles, product documentation, arbitrary webpages, and historical support tickets in one training pass. Pulling in past tickets specifically is less common among competitors, and it matters if your best answers already live in resolved conversations rather than a formal knowledge base.

**Answer citation and grounding.** Every response is designed to point back to the source document it drew from — the core differentiator Wonderchat leans on in its own messaging. The company frames its pricing as "cheaper because of how we price, not a weaker model," arguing answers "stay grounded and cited." That's a vendor claim worth testing against your own content before trusting it at scale.

**QA agent for weak answers.** The Scale and Enterprise tiers include an automated QA layer that reviews the bot's own conversations and flags weak or low-confidence answers for a human to fix with one click, rather than requiring a manual audit of transcripts. This is the kind of ongoing-maintenance feature that separates "launch and forget" chatbot tools from ones meant to actually improve over months of real traffic.

**Multi-channel deployment.** Beyond the standard embeddable website widget, Wonderchat deploys the same trained agent to mobile apps, WhatsApp, and SMS, plus a voice agent option starting on the Scale plan. Teams that get support requests across channels — not just on-site chat — get a single trained knowledge base instead of maintaining separate bots per channel.

**Inline lead capture.** The agent can collect contact details mid-conversation without redirecting the visitor to a separate form, then sync that data into a CRM. For teams running Wonderchat as much for pre-sales qualification as for support deflection, this avoids the drop-off that a "fill out this form" handoff typically causes.

## Who It's Actually For

- **Solo builders and very small teams**: The free plan (10 resolutions/month) is really a proof-of-concept tier, not something to run production support on. If your monthly conversation volume is low and budget is the top priority, cheaper single-purpose chatbot builders will likely serve you better than jumping straight to Wonderchat's $124/month Basic plan.
- **Growing support teams (10–50 people)**: The Basic and Scale plans, with 3+ team seats, self-improving agents, and (on Scale) advanced analytics and a voice agent, are aimed squarely here. This is where Wonderchat's resolution-based pricing and QA-agent workflow are most likely to pay for themselves against the cost of a human agent handling the same ticket volume.
- **Regulated or enterprise support orgs**: The Enterprise tier's SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance options, SSO, and custom integrations are built for healthcare, finance, or other teams that can't consider a vendor without those certifications in place — but that tier starts at $1,499/month and requires a custom quote, so it's not a casual signup.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Trains on tickets, docs, and webpages in one setup | No public disclosure of which AI model(s) power responses |
| Citation-grounded answers reduce made-up responses | Paid plans are billed yearly by default; monthly billing costs more |
| Multi-channel deployment (web, app, WhatsApp, SMS, voice) | Voice agent locked behind the $417/month Scale plan |
| Built-in QA agent flags weak answers automatically | Free plan's 10 resolutions/month is too low for real production use |
| SOC 2 Type 2 certified, HIPAA option on Enterprise | Enterprise compliance features require a custom quote, no listed price |
| 7-day trial on every paid plan | Resolution/credit-based pricing is harder to estimate upfront than flat per-seat pricing |

## Integrations and Ecosystem

Wonderchat's site describes integrations with help desk platforms and CRMs for syncing captured leads and tickets, alongside native deployment to WhatsApp and SMS. It doesn't list a public API reference or a Zapier app on its marketing pages the way some competitors do, so if your workflow depends on a specific connector or custom API access, verify that directly with Wonderchat support before committing to a paid plan.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

Wonderchat makes the most sense for support teams that already have a built-out knowledge base (docs, help center, or ticket history) and want a bot that cites its sources rather than paraphrasing freely. The QA agent workflow is also a genuine differentiator for teams running a chatbot for months, not weeks — most competitors leave transcript review to you.

## Where to Think Twice

Skip Wonderchat if you need a fully free tool to run indefinitely — the free plan's 10-resolution cap makes it a demo, not a support channel. Teams on a tight monthly budget should also compare the effective monthly-billed price, since Wonderchat's headline numbers assume annual payment upfront. If you specifically need a documented API or a Zapier integration built into the product, confirm availability first, since neither is clearly advertised. And if model transparency is a requirement for your AI vendor review, Wonderchat's lack of public disclosure on which language model it runs could be a blocker.

## Bottom Line

Wonderchat is a solid pick for support teams that want a chatbot trained across docs, tickets, and webpages, with citation-backed answers and a genuinely useful QA workflow for catching bad responses before customers complain about them. It's less appealing for solo operators or budget-constrained teams, since the free tier is too limited for real use and the paid tiers jump quickly toward team-plan pricing that assumes annual billing. If you're comparing it against [Chatbase](/blog/chatbase-review) or [Chaindesk](/blog/chaindesk-review), weigh Wonderchat's resolution-based pricing and multi-channel voice/SMS deployment against those tools' simpler per-seat or per-agent pricing before deciding.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Wonderchat free to use?**
Yes, there's a free plan that includes about 10 resolutions per month, 20 credits, 1 AI agent, and up to 50 stored webpages. It's suitable for testing the product, not for running production support volume.

**How much does Wonderchat cost?**
Paid plans start at $124/month for the Basic tier (billed yearly), scale to $417/month for the Scale tier, and go to a custom quote starting around $1,499/month for Enterprise. Monthly billing (without the annual commitment) costs more than the yearly rates listed here.

**What counts as a "resolution" in Wonderchat's pricing?**
A resolution is a conversation the AI agent successfully answers on its own, distinct from "credits," a broader usage unit that also covers retraining and voice-agent minutes. Confirm exact current definitions on Wonderchat's pricing page, since usage-based terms like this can change.

**What can Wonderchat train on?**
Help center articles, product documentation, arbitrary webpages, and past support ticket history. Training on historical tickets is a less common option among competing chatbot builders.

**Does Wonderchat support channels beyond a website widget?**
Yes — it deploys to mobile apps, WhatsApp, and SMS, and adds a voice agent option starting on the Scale plan.

**Is Wonderchat suitable for regulated industries like healthcare?**
The Enterprise plan offers SOC 2 Type 2 certification and a HIPAA compliance option, along with SSO. Confirm the specifics of any compliance requirement directly with Wonderchat's sales team before signing.

**How does Wonderchat compare to Chatbase or Chaindesk?**
Wonderchat differentiates on citation-grounded answers, a built-in QA agent for catching weak responses, and native voice/SMS deployment, while pricing is structured around monthly resolutions rather than a flat per-seat fee. See the [Chatbase review](/blog/chatbase-review) or [Chaindesk review](/blog/chaindesk-review) on this site for a direct look at how those tools price and structure their plans instead.

**Is there a mobile app or is Wonderchat website-only?**
Wonderchat deploys trained agents into mobile apps as one of its supported channels, alongside the website widget, WhatsApp, and SMS — it isn't limited to a browser-based widget.

title: Wope Review 2026: SEO Research Platform Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Wope is an AI-assisted SEO platform for rank tracking, keyword and backlink research. Here's its pricing, features, and who it actually suits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Wope worth using for SEO research and rank tracking?

Wope is an AI-assisted SEO research platform built around rank tracking, keyword research, and backlink analysis, priced from $27/month with a 14-day unlimited trial. It's a solid fit for agencies and marketers who want a faster, less cluttered alternative to legacy SEO suites, but its research-credit model means heavy users on lower tiers can burn through allowances quickly.

### At a glance

| | Wope |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $27/month (Basic plan) |
| Free tier / trial | 14-day unlimited trial, no credit card required |
| Best for | SEO agencies, startups, and marketers who want fast keyword/backlink research and daily rank tracking |
| Standout feature | Daily rank tracking with keyword alerts, cannibalization detection, and an Excel-like table interface |

## What Wope actually is

Wope calls itself a "new-generation SEO research platform" and, from what's publicly documented, it's built as a leaner, faster alternative to the decade-old SEO suites most agencies already know (think Ahrefs, Semrush, or Moz), with an emphasis on speed of setup and a spreadsheet-like interface rather than a sprawling menu of disconnected modules. The company is registered in Middletown, Delaware, and markets itself squarely at SEO agencies, in-house marketing teams, and startups that need to track rankings and research competitors without a steep onboarding curve.

The product leans on AI in two specific places, according to its own marketing: project creation (it claims new tracking projects can be set up in about 60 seconds using AI to auto-populate keywords and settings) and an AI content assistant that helps generate content ideas alongside competitor research. Wope doesn't publish which underlying language model powers these features, so treat "AI-powered" here as an assistive layer on top of its core research tools rather than a generative-writing product in its own right — if you're looking for a full AI writer, Wope isn't built to replace one.

Where Wope spends most engineering effort, based on its own feature pages, is the research and tracking layer: keyword finding, competitor keyword overlap, ranked-keyword tracking with historical trend data, backlink profile analysis, and daily rank tracking across desktop and mobile.

## Pricing

Wope prices its plans by seat count and monthly research credits rather than by domains tracked, which is a different model from most competitors. Each credit reportedly returns up to 100 results, so how far a plan stretches depends heavily on how granular your research queries are.

| Plan | Price | Users | Research credits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | $27/month | Unlimited | 500 credits |
| Starter | $55/month | 3 | 1,000 credits |
| Growth | $137/month | 5 | 2,500 credits |
| Elite | $275/month | 7 | 5,000 credits |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom |

All published plans include email and live support, and Wope advertises a 24-hour support team across every tier. Every plan can be upgraded or downgraded at any time, and the 14-day free trial covers the Basic plan's full feature set with no card required up front.

One quirk worth flagging: the Basic plan allows unlimited users but caps research credits at 500 — meaning a small team could in theory share one Basic seat pool, but they'd exhaust the credit allowance fast if several people are running research queries independently. Starter, Growth, and Elite instead cap user seats while scaling credits, which is the more conventional agency-pricing pattern.

Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on [Wope's official pricing page](https://wope.com/pricing) before buying, since SaaS pricing tiers shift often.

## Core features walkthrough

**Daily rank tracking.** Wope tracks keyword positions daily for both desktop and mobile, with built-in alerts for ranking swings and automatic detection of keyword cannibalization — where two pages on the same site compete for the same query, quietly diluting both. This is the feature Wope leans on hardest in its own marketing, and it's the one most likely to differentiate day-to-day usage from a generic keyword tool.

**Keyword and competitor research.** The platform includes a keyword finder, a "shared SEO keywords" tool that surfaces overlapping keywords between your site and a competitor's, and ranked-keyword tracking that pulls search volume, click-through rate estimates, historical trend lines, and keyword intent. That intent data matters for prioritizing which keywords are worth chasing versus which ones look attractive on volume alone but convert poorly.

**Backlink analysis.** Wope lets you inspect a site's backlink sources, review anchor-text distribution, and assess linking-domain authority — the standard link-building research trio, presented in the same spreadsheet-style interface as the rest of the tool rather than a separate module with its own UI conventions to learn.

**Fast project setup.** Wope advertises project creation in around 60 seconds, using AI to help scaffold a new tracking project (domain, keyword list, competitor set) rather than requiring manual configuration of every field. For agencies spinning up tracking for a new client, this is a meaningful time saver over tools where onboarding a new project takes 20+ manual steps.

**Data-export and workflow tools.** Pagespeed analysis flags performance issues that can affect rankings, an Excel-like table experience is used throughout instead of fixed dashboard widgets, charts can be exported or copied directly to clipboard, and CSV import is supported for bringing in external data. Together these read like a product built by people who were frustrated with copy-pasting numbers out of rigid SEO-suite dashboards into spreadsheets for client reporting.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo consultants and freelancers** — the Basic plan's unlimited-user, 500-credit structure works fine for a single person running rank tracking and periodic keyword research for a handful of client sites, as long as query volume stays modest.
- **Small SEO agencies** — Starter or Growth gives a small team (3–5 people) enough seats and credit headroom to split research work across multiple client accounts without hitting caps every week.
- **Larger in-house marketing teams or bigger agencies** — Elite's 7 seats and 5,000 credits suit teams running research across many domains simultaneously, though it's worth budgeting for the jump from $137 to $275/month.
- **Enterprises with compliance or custom-seat needs** — the custom Enterprise tier is the route for organizations that need seat counts, credit allowances, or contract terms beyond what the published plans offer.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Fast, spreadsheet-style interface that's quick to learn | Credit-based pricing can run out fast for high-query-volume research |
| Daily rank tracking with cannibalization detection built in | No published transparency on which AI model powers its "AI" features |
| 14-day unlimited trial with no credit card required | No free-forever tier — trial ends and a paid plan is required to keep using it |
| Unlimited users on the entry Basic plan | Basic plan's shared credit pool doesn't scale well once more than one or two people actively query it |
| CSV import/export and clipboard-friendly charts for reporting | Feature set is narrower than legacy all-in-one suites (no dedicated AI writer, no ads-research module documented) |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Wope's own materials emphasize CSV import and export as the primary way data moves in and out of the platform. Wope doesn't publicly document a formal API, a Zapier integration, or native Slack/Google Sheets connectors on the pages reviewed for this piece — confirm current availability directly with Wope's support team before subscribing if a live API or webhook integration is a requirement.

## Where it's a strong fit

Wope makes sense if you want an SEO research tool that doesn't require a week of onboarding to use productively — the spreadsheet-style tables and fast project setup are genuinely aimed at people who'd rather start tracking rankings today than configure dashboards for three days first. Agencies juggling several small client accounts will likely appreciate the unlimited-seat Basic tier and the CSV export options for client reporting. If daily rank tracking with cannibalization alerts is your main ask, Wope covers that ground directly rather than as an afterthought bolted onto a keyword-research tool.

## Where to think twice

Model the credit usage carefully before committing. Frequent, high-volume keyword or backlink queries across many domains can burn through 500–2,500 credits faster than expected, and jumping a tier for more credits also multiplies the price. Skip Wope, or at least run the trial before committing annually, if:

- You need a genuinely free tool with no paid ceiling — Wope's trial is time-limited, not a permanent free plan.
- Your workflow depends on API access or native integrations (Slack, Zapier, Google Data Studio) that aren't clearly documented as available.
- You want an all-in-one suite that also handles PPC/ads research, site audits at scale, or a full AI content writer in the same subscription — Wope's public feature set is centered on rank tracking, keyword research, and backlinks, not a broader marketing-suite scope.
- Your team needs enterprise compliance documentation (SOC 2, GDPR data-processing addenda) confirmed up front — verify this directly with Wope's sales team rather than assuming it based on the Enterprise tier's existence.

## Bottom line

Wope is a focused, fast-feeling SEO research tool rather than an attempt to be everything at once. Its rank tracking, keyword overlap research, and backlink analysis are well covered for the price, and the unlimited-user Basic plan is a genuinely unusual value at $27/month for a solo operator or small team with light research needs. The trade-off is the credit system — it rewards light, deliberate querying and can feel restrictive for teams that treat SEO research as a high-volume daily habit. Run the 14-day trial against your actual query patterns before picking a tier; that's the only way to know whether 500 or 2,500 credits covers a real month of work.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Wope free to use?**
No, but it offers a 14-day unlimited trial of the Basic plan, no credit card required. After that, a paid subscription starting at $27/month is required.

**What does a "research credit" get you?**
Wope states each credit returns up to 100 results from a research query, though usage can vary by query type — confirm current details on Wope's pricing page before choosing a plan.

**How is Wope different from Ahrefs or Semrush?**
Wope is a newer, narrower platform focused on rank tracking, keyword research, and backlinks, with a faster setup and spreadsheet-style UI, priced on a seat-plus-credit model rather than flat domain limits. Established suites cover more modules (site audits, PPC research) but cost more and take longer to learn.

**Does Wope include an AI writer?**
Not as a standalone product. It includes an AI content assistant for content ideas and competitor research, but it isn't marketed as a full long-form writing tool.

**Can multiple people use one Wope account?**
Yes — Basic allows unlimited users on one account sharing a 500-credit pool. Higher tiers cap seats but scale up credits instead.

**Does Wope offer an enterprise plan?**
Yes, a custom Enterprise tier for larger organizations; pricing and terms are negotiated directly with its sales team.

**Is Wope good for beginners?**
The spreadsheet-style interface and fast project setup lower the learning curve compared with denser SEO suites, though core concepts like cannibalization and backlink authority still require some background to act on usefully.

**What happens to my data if I cancel?**
Wope doesn't publish detailed retention terms on the pages reviewed here — export your data via CSV before cancelling, and confirm retention policy with support if it matters for your workflow.

Looking for more AI-powered software picks? Browse [AI & software deals](/category/software) for other tool reviews and coupons.

title: Accio Review 2026: AI Sourcing Agent Pricing & Features
excerpt: Accio review: an AI sourcing agent from Alibaba for ecommerce product research and supplier discovery. Pricing, features, and who it fits best.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Accio Worth Using for Product Sourcing in 2026?

Accio is an AI agent platform built by Alibaba.com for ecommerce sourcing, market research, and store operations, connecting directly to Alibaba's supplier network and trade data. It's a solid pick if you already source from Alibaba and want an AI layer on top of research, negotiation, and listing tasks, but its usefulness drops fast for sellers who source elsewhere.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (7-day onboarding allowance), then from $19.9/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — free plan with limited daily credits after onboarding |
| **Best for** | Ecommerce sellers, Alibaba-based sourcing, dropshippers, Amazon/Shopify/TikTok Shop merchants |
| **Standout feature** | Direct pull from Alibaba's supplier and trade data inside an agentic workflow |

Accio is built and operated by Alibaba.com, positioned as "an agentic business team" rather than a single-purpose chatbot. It runs as a desktop app, a web portal, and a mobile companion app, and it can read local files, run terminal commands, control a browser, and call outside APIs to complete multi-step tasks instead of just answering questions. That's the core pitch: you give it a goal ("find three suppliers for a private-label yoga mat under $4 landed cost"), and it works through the steps — market scan, supplier shortlist, price comparison — rather than handing you a single response you then have to act on yourself.

Alibaba doesn't publish which underlying language models power Accio's "advanced" vs. "base" tiers, and the site is vague on this point beyond describing a system that "leverages multiple AI models working collaboratively." Treat that framing as Alibaba's own description rather than a verified technical spec — there's no public model card or architecture doc to confirm it against.

### Pricing

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability below were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly for AI tools — always confirm current numbers on Accio's own [pricing page](https://www.accio.com/pricing) before subscribing.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 7-day onboarding allowance with bonus credits, access to higher-quality models for up to 30 requests per 3 hours during onboarding, then reverts to a base daily credit allowance |
| Pro | $19.9/month (15% off on annual billing) | 4,000 membership credits/month, 50 advanced-model uses per 3 hours, 30 daily credits — pitched as "for everyday tasks" |
| Elite | $99/month (15% off on annual billing) | 20,000 membership credits/month, 150 advanced-model uses per 3 hours, 50 daily credits — pitched as "for heavy, complex work" |
| Ultra | $199/month (15% off on annual billing) | 40,000 membership credits/month, unlimited high-quality model use, 100 daily credits — pitched as "for high-volume operations" |

Two things worth flagging before you subscribe. First, Accio runs on a credit system layered under the monthly price, and how fast a given task burns credits (a quick supplier lookup vs. a multi-step market analysis with browser automation) isn't clearly documented — budget for testing this on the Free or Pro tier before committing to Elite or Ultra. Second, the jump from Pro to Elite is a 5x price increase for roughly 5x the credits, which suggests Accio expects serious usage to land on its middle-to-top tiers rather than the entry plan.

### Core features walkthrough

**Market and trend scanning.** Accio says it scans Reddit, TikTok, and Amazon to surface trending products and category "winners," then can turn that into a shortlist of things worth sourcing. This is the feature that separates it from a plain sourcing directory — it's trying to answer "what should I sell" before "who do I buy it from."

**Direct supplier sourcing via Alibaba.** Because Accio is an Alibaba.com product, it has native access to Alibaba's supplier and trade data rather than scraping it. For sellers who already buy through Alibaba, that's a real edge over a general-purpose AI agent bolting on web search — you get supplier comparisons, MOQs, and pricing pulled from the same backend Alibaba's own marketplace runs on.

**Task automation with tool access.** Accio can read local files, run terminal commands, control a browser session, and call external APIs, backed by what Alibaba describes as 200+ automation tools and domain-specific workflows. In practice this means it can go beyond chat — e.g., logging into a connected store dashboard to pull sales data, or filling out a supplier inquiry form — with a sandboxed environment that requires user approval for sensitive actions.

**Marketplace integrations.** The platform connects with Shopify, Amazon, and TikTok Shop, which is the trio most relevant to the dropshipping and private-label crowd. That's a narrower integration list than a general automation tool like Zapier would offer, but it's directly matched to the ecommerce use case Accio is built for.

**Benchmark claim.** Alibaba states Accio completed a 107-task commerce benchmark at "over 50% lower cost" than using OpenAI Codex or Anthropic's Claude directly for the same tasks. This is Alibaba's own claim from its marketing material, not an independently verified or third-party-audited benchmark, so treat it as a vendor comparison rather than an established fact.

### Who it's actually for

- **Alibaba-first sellers and dropshippers**: the clearest fit. If you're already sourcing through Alibaba, Accio's native data access and supplier-comparison workflows save real research time, and the Free or Pro tier is enough to start.
- **Amazon/Shopify/TikTok Shop sellers doing product research**: the trend-scanning and market-analysis features are useful for finding what to list next, even if you don't buy through Alibaba for everything — though you'll want the Elite tier if you're running this daily across many SKUs.
- **Solopreneurs and side-hustlers testing product ideas**: the free onboarding window and Pro tier's $19.9/month price point make it cheap enough to trial against a single product idea before scaling spend.
- **Supply chain managers and procurement teams**: Accio's automation and negotiation-adjacent tooling can offload repetitive supplier outreach and comparison work, though larger teams should check whether Accio's browser/terminal automation fits their existing security policies before rolling it out company-wide.
- **Sellers who don't source from Alibaba at all**: a weaker fit — you're paying for a platform whose core data advantage (Alibaba's own trade data) doesn't apply to your supply chain.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Native Alibaba supplier and trade data access | Underlying AI models aren't publicly documented |
| Handles multi-step agentic tasks, not just chat answers | Credit-consumption rates per task type are unclear |
| Free onboarding tier to test before paying | Big price jump from Pro ($19.9) to Elite ($99) |
| Desktop, web, and mobile access | Narrower marketplace integrations (Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop only) |
| Trend-scanning across Reddit, TikTok, and Amazon | Less useful if you don't source through Alibaba |
| Sandbox approval flow for sensitive automated actions | Benchmark performance claims are vendor-reported, not independently audited |

### Integrations and ecosystem

Accio's documented integrations center on ecommerce: Shopify, Amazon, and TikTok Shop for store-side operations, plus its underlying tie-in to Alibaba.com's own supplier and trade database. Alibaba also references market-intelligence data resembling tools like Jungle Scout as an input to its trend analysis, though it's not clear whether this is a direct data partnership or Accio's own comparable analysis. There's no public mention of a Zapier connector, open API for third-party developers, or Slack/Teams integration as of this writing — if your workflow depends on connecting an AI agent into a broader automation stack beyond ecommerce platforms, verify current integration support directly with Accio before assuming it's there.

### Where it's a strong fit

Accio earns its keep for sellers whose sourcing already runs through Alibaba — the direct data access removes a layer of manual cross-referencing that a general AI chatbot simply can't replicate without scraping or guesswork. It's also a reasonable entry point for someone testing a new product idea end-to-end: scanning for trends, shortlisting suppliers, and comparing pricing in one tool instead of juggling a spreadsheet, a supplier directory, and a separate AI assistant.

The agentic task execution (reading files, running commands, controlling a browser) is genuinely more capable than a chat-only tool if your workflow involves repetitive multi-step research, and the free tier is enough to judge whether that's actually useful for your specific sourcing pattern before paying.

### Where to think twice

If you need clarity on exactly which AI models are answering your queries — for compliance, data-handling, or simple curiosity reasons — Accio's public materials don't spell that out, and you'd need to ask Alibaba directly or dig into their terms of service.

If your sourcing doesn't touch Alibaba at all (say, you buy exclusively from domestic manufacturers or a closed supplier network), a chunk of Accio's core advantage disappears and you're better served by a general-purpose research or automation AI tool matched to your actual supply chain.

If you need a fully free tool for ongoing use, Accio isn't it — the free plan is explicitly an onboarding allowance that reverts to a limited daily credit pool, not a permanent free tier suited to regular work.

If your team requires SOC 2 or similar enterprise compliance documentation before adopting a new automation tool with browser and terminal access, that paperwork isn't published on Accio's marketing site — get it from Alibaba's enterprise sales team before rolling this out to a team account.

If you need offline or on-premises use, Accio is cloud-based across all three of its access points (desktop, web, mobile), so this isn't the tool for locked-down offline environments.

### Bottom line

Accio is a genuinely differentiated AI sourcing tool because of who built it — Alibaba's own supplier and trade data baked into an agentic workflow is hard for a third-party AI wrapper to match. For sellers already buying through Alibaba, or evaluating a Shopify/Amazon/TikTok Shop product line from scratch, it's worth the free trial and probably the $19.9/month Pro tier. For everyone else, the value proposition narrows considerably, and the credit-based pricing means it's worth testing your actual task volume against a real budget before jumping to Elite or Ultra.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is Accio free to use?**
There's a free plan with a 7-day onboarding allowance and bonus credits, including temporary access to higher-quality models. After onboarding, it reverts to a smaller base daily credit allowance rather than staying at the onboarding level indefinitely.

**How much does Accio cost?**
Paid plans start at $19.9/month for the Pro tier (4,000 monthly credits), scaling to $99/month for Elite and $199/month for Ultra. All three offer roughly 15% savings on annual billing.

**Does Accio only work with Alibaba suppliers?**
Its core sourcing data advantage comes from Alibaba's own trade and supplier network, but the platform also does trend and market research across Amazon, Reddit, and TikTok, and connects to Shopify, Amazon, and TikTok Shop for store operations — so it's not exclusively an Alibaba-sourcing tool, even though that's where it's strongest.

**What AI models does Accio use?**
Alibaba describes Accio as running on "multiple AI models working collaboratively" but doesn't publish a specific model list or architecture breakdown publicly. If model provenance matters to your use case, confirm directly with Alibaba/Accio support.

**Is Accio beginner-friendly?**
The web and mobile apps are built for non-technical use (chat-style task requests), while the desktop app's file/terminal/browser automation features assume more comfort with connecting local tools. Most sourcing and research tasks don't require any technical setup.

**How does Accio handle data privacy?**
Alibaba states Accio includes "enterprise-grade security backed by Alibaba's infrastructure" and a sandboxed environment that requires user approval before it takes sensitive automated actions. Specific data retention and privacy policy details should be reviewed on Accio's official terms and privacy pages before connecting store or financial data.

**What are good alternatives to Accio?**
General AI research agents (for sellers not sourcing through Alibaba), dedicated product-research tools like Jungle Scout for Amazon-specific trend data, or working directly through Alibaba.com's standard marketplace search without the AI agent layer are all reasonable alternatives depending on which part of Accio's workflow you actually need.

**Is there an Accio coupon or discount code?**
Accio doesn't currently have a dedicated coupon page on this site. Check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers on other AI and ecommerce tools.

title: Unspam Email Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Unspam Email checks spam scores, blacklists, and inbox placement before you send. Here's what it costs, who it's for, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Unspam Email worth using to check your emails for spam triggers?

Unspam is an email deliverability testing tool that scores a campaign's spam risk, checks it against real blacklists, and previews how it renders across dozens of inboxes before you hit send. It's a solid pick for marketers and small teams who send regularly and want a fast way to catch authentication and content problems, though its per-test pricing structure takes some getting used to.

### At a glance

| | Unspam Email |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (no account needed) |
| Free tier | Yes — 3 spam tests, 2 inbox placements, 1 device preview with no signup; more on the free account plan |
| Best for | Email marketers, agencies, and SaaS teams sending regular campaigns or transactional email |
| Standout feature | Inbox placement testing across Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo combined with SPF/DKIM/DMARC/BIMI authentication checks in one report |

## What Unspam Email actually is

Unspam is a web-based email testing platform built specifically to answer one question before a campaign goes out: will this land in the inbox, or in spam? Rather than guessing at "spam trigger words" the way older checker tools do, it runs a fuller deliverability audit — checking your sending domain's authentication records, testing against major blacklists, simulating rendering across dozens of email clients, and reporting an overall spam score.

The site doesn't publicly name a parent company or founding team on its marketing pages, so if that matters for your vendor-vetting process, it's worth asking their support team directly. What is documented is the product itself: a dashboard where you send a test email (or paste a draft) and get back a structured report covering content, authentication, and inbox placement.

This puts Unspam in the same general category as tools like Mail-Tester or GlockApps, but its pricing model — pay by test rather than a flat monthly fee — and its bundled AI heatmap and accessibility checks set it apart.

## Pricing

Unspam prices around test volume rather than a simple "Basic/Pro/Enterprise" ladder, which is worth understanding before you commit.

| Plan | Price | Monthly allowance | Notable inclusions |
|---|---|---|---|
| No account | $0, no signup | Resets monthly | 3 spam tests, 2 inbox placements, 1 device preview, 3 screenshots, 1 heatmap; results kept 24 hours |
| Free account | $0/month | 21 tests/month combined allowance (5 spam tests, 3 inbox placements, 3 device previews, 5 screenshots, 5 heatmaps) | Results kept 14 days, unlimited sender accounts, DMARC monitoring, AI assistant, full API and MCP server access |
| Custom | Per-test pricing, volume discounts | Flexible — buy the specific test types you need | Results kept 3 years, unlimited sender accounts, top-up credits that don't expire |

A few things stand out here. Even the free tier gives you API access and an AI assistant — features some competitors lock behind a paywall. And the paid tier isn't a flat subscription; it's closer to a credit system where you buy the mix of spam tests, inbox placements, and heatmaps your team actually uses, with better per-test rates at higher volume. Unspam doesn't publish flat per-test dollar amounts on its marketing pages, so if predictable monthly billing matters, confirm the exact custom-plan rate for your expected volume on their pricing page before committing.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — always verify current numbers on Unspam's own pricing page before budgeting around them, since AI and deliverability tools tend to adjust limits frequently.

## Core features walkthrough

**Spam scoring.** Every test returns a 0–100 score built from authentication status, sender reputation, and content analysis, rather than a simple pass/fail flag. That composite approach is more useful than older-style "spam word" checkers, since a clean subject line with broken DKIM will still tank deliverability.

**Blacklist checking.** Unspam checks your sending IP and domain against major blacklists including Spamhaus, SpamCop, and Barracuda. This matters because a domain can have perfect email copy and still land in spam if it's flagged on a blacklist from a prior sender or shared IP issue — something a pure content checker would never catch.

**Inbox placement testing.** This is arguably the feature that separates Unspam from a basic spam-word scanner. It tests actual placement across Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, and other major providers, so you can see, for example, that a campaign clears Outlook fine but is landing in Gmail's promotions or spam tab.

**Email previews and AI heatmap.** The tool renders your email across 50+ clients and devices in both light and dark mode, catching layout breakage before subscribers do. The AI heatmap adds a predicted attention map showing where a reader's eyes are likely to go first — useful for checking that your call-to-action isn't buried below a giant hero image.

**Authentication and accessibility checks.** Unspam verifies SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI, and reverse DNS in one pass, plus runs a WCAG accessibility check on the rendered email — a feature most spam checkers skip entirely, and one that matters more each year as accessibility compliance becomes a real legal consideration for larger senders.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo marketers and freelancers** testing occasional campaigns can lean entirely on the no-account or free tier — the monthly allowance of spam tests and inbox placements covers a handful of sends without ever entering a card number.
- **Agencies and in-house marketing teams** running weekly or biweekly campaigns for multiple clients or brands will likely outgrow the free allowance fast and want the custom plan, where the per-test discounts at volume and the 3-year result retention (useful for client reporting) start to pay for themselves.
- **SaaS and product teams sending transactional email** — password resets, receipts, onboarding sequences — benefit most from the DMARC monitoring and authentication checks, since transactional email deliverability failures are often invisible until a support ticket comes in.
- **Developers and ops teams** who want deliverability testing wired into a CI/CD pipeline or internal tool can use the full API and MCP server access, which Unspam includes even on its free tier — a notable outlier compared to competitors that gate API access behind paid plans.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely useful free tier with no credit card required | Custom plan pricing isn't published as flat numbers — you have to confirm rates for your volume |
| Combines content, authentication, blacklist, and inbox-placement checks in one report | Test allowances (even on paid custom plans) mean heavy senders need to budget carefully around volume |
| API and MCP server access included even on the free plan | No named company/team on the marketing site, which some enterprise buyers will want clarified before signing |
| Accessibility (WCAG) and AI heatmap checks most competitors don't offer | Results retention on free tiers is short (24 hours to 14 days) unless you're on a paid plan |
| Unlimited sender accounts even on the free plan | Best value only becomes clear once you know your monthly test volume, which takes some trial and error |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Unspam offers a full API on every plan, including the free one, which is unusual for this category — most spam-testing tools reserve API access for paid tiers. It also lists MCP (Model Context Protocol) server access across all plans, letting it be wired directly into AI coding assistants and agent workflows, so a marketing-ops team can trigger spam checks as part of an automated send pipeline rather than through the web dashboard alone. The site doesn't list dedicated native integrations with specific email service providers (Mailchimp, Klaviyo, HubSpot, etc.), so if a direct ESP integration matters, confirm current support with Unspam directly.

## Where it's a strong fit

Unspam works well for teams that send email regularly enough to justify checking deliverability before every campaign, not just when something breaks. The combination of inbox placement testing, blacklist monitoring, and authentication checks in a single report saves the time of manually checking SPF/DKIM records, running a separate blacklist lookup, and eyeballing rendering in different clients. Agencies managing multiple client domains will likely get the most value, since the per-test volume discounts and multi-year result retention on the custom plan suit repeated, high-volume testing better than a flat subscription would.

## Where to think twice

If you need a fully free, unlimited tool with no test caps, Unspam isn't it — even the free plan's 21 monthly tests will run out fast for a team sending several campaigns a week, and you'll need to move to the metered custom plan. If your organization requires clear vendor transparency (a named company, security/compliance documentation, SOC 2 or similar) before adopting a tool, the marketing site doesn't surface that up front, so ask their support team before rolling it into a regulated workflow. And if you only send the occasional one-off email and don't need inbox placement or blacklist monitoring, a simpler free spam-word checker might be enough.

## Bottom line

Unspam earns its place for anyone who sends email often enough that a spam-folder landing actually costs them money — agencies, SaaS teams, and marketers running regular campaigns. The free tier is generous enough to try seriously before paying anything, and the combination of inbox placement testing, blacklist checks, and authentication verification in one dashboard beats piecing together several free tools separately. The main thing to sort out up front is your expected monthly test volume, since that determines whether the free plan is enough or you need custom, metered pricing.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Unspam Email free to use?**
Yes. You can run a handful of spam tests with no account and no card at all, and a free account adds a larger monthly allowance (21 tests total, split across spam tests, inbox placements, and other checks) along with API access.

**Does Unspam check blacklists as well as spam-trigger content?**
Yes. It checks your sending domain and IP against major blacklists like Spamhaus, SpamCop, and Barracuda, in addition to analyzing your email's content, authentication records, and rendering.

**How is Unspam's pricing structured?**
Instead of a flat monthly subscription, paid usage is billed per test on a custom plan with volume discounts, and unused top-up credits don't expire. Exact per-test rates aren't published publicly, so confirm current numbers for your expected volume directly with Unspam.

**Does Unspam offer an API?**
Yes, and unusually, full API access (plus MCP server access for AI-agent workflows) is included even on the free plan, not just paid tiers.

**How long are test results stored?**
Results are kept 24 hours with no account, 14 days on the free plan, and up to 3 years on the custom plan — worth factoring in if you need long-term deliverability records for client reporting.

**Is Unspam Email beginner-friendly?**
The core spam test is simple to run (send a test email and read the score), but interpreting authentication and blacklist results may take some familiarity with SPF/DKIM/DMARC basics if you're new to email deliverability.

**What data does Unspam access when I test an email?**
It needs the content of the test email and your sending domain's DNS/authentication records to generate a report. Check Unspam's own privacy policy for full data-handling details, since the marketing pages don't spell them out.

**Are there alternatives to Unspam Email?**
Yes — Mail-Tester and GlockApps cover similar spam-scoring and inbox-placement territory, though feature sets and pricing models differ, so compare your must-haves (like API access or accessibility checks) before choosing.

For more AI and software deals, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: CodeDesign.ai Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: CodeDesign.ai builds AI-generated websites you can export as real React or HTML code. Here's the pricing, features, and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is CodeDesign.ai Worth Using?

CodeDesign.ai is an AI website builder that generates a working site from a text prompt and then lets you export the underlying React or HTML code, so you aren't locked into its hosting the way you are with most drag-and-drop AI builders. It's a solid pick if you want a fast first draft with an exit ramp to real code; less so if you want the polished design-tool feel of Framer.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free plan (3 projects, subdomain hosting); paid plans required for a custom domain and code export |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — free plan available, plus a 7-day money-back guarantee on paid plans |
| **Best for** | Founders, freelancers and small teams who want an AI-generated site with an option to export clean code |
| **Standout feature** | One-click export to React or HTML, so the generated site isn't stuck on CodeDesign's own hosting |

CodeDesign.ai doesn't have a store listing on Smart Fare yet, so there's no coupon code to apply here — everything below is based on the vendor's own site and pricing page as of this writing.

## What CodeDesign.ai actually is

CodeDesign.ai is built by CodeDesign, Inc., a US-based company, and positions itself as an AI website builder aimed at people who want to go from a plain-language description to a live site without hiring a developer. Under the hood, it uses OpenAI's models to generate layout, copy and structure from a prompt, and the vendor states it runs under OpenAI's zero data retention policy so prompt data isn't used to train OpenAI's models. Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2+, and payments run through Stripe — standard stuff, but worth confirming if you're evaluating this for a client with its own compliance requirements.

The part that separates it from most of the "type a prompt, get a website" category is code ownership. Instead of keeping the generated site trapped inside a proprietary editor, CodeDesign.ai lets you export the entire project as clean React or HTML code. That means you can hand the export to a developer, drop it into your own hosting, or keep a portable backup instead of being permanently tied to CodeDesign's servers. Framer AI and Dora AI, by contrast, keep your site living inside their own design canvas with no comparable full-code export, and Durable focuses less on code ownership and more on bundling a CRM, invoicing and appointment booking around the generated site.

## Pricing

CodeDesign.ai's public pricing page doesn't publish a full breakdown of every tier — instead it emphasizes a free plan and an annual-billing discount. Here's what's confirmed from the vendor's own site:

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Up to 3 projects, hosted on a CodeDesign subdomain |
| Paid (monthly) | Not publicly itemized on the pricing page | Custom domain, code export, and the full feature set — confirm current tier pricing on the official pricing page before buying |
| Paid (annual) | 20% off monthly rate, plus a free domain | Same features as monthly, billed yearly |
| Lifetime deal (promotional) | Seen as low as $79 (list $194) during promotions | One-time payment tied to a specific promo; availability and terms vary |

All paid plans carry a 7-day money-back guarantee and can be canceled at any time, per the vendor. Because CodeDesign.ai doesn't lay out itemized tier names and per-seat limits the way some competitors do, treat any specific dollar figure above the free plan as something to double-check on [CodeDesign.ai's official pricing page](https://codedesign.ai/pricing) before you commit.

Pricing, free-tier limits and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI website builder pricing and feature sets move fast, and lifetime-deal promotions in particular tend to be temporary.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Code export to React or HTML.** This is the headline feature. Once you're happy with the AI-generated site, you can export the whole project as standard code rather than being stuck maintaining it inside CodeDesign's builder forever. For anyone who's been burned by a website builder that later changed its pricing or shut down a feature, this is the practical reason to pick CodeDesign.ai over a closed-garden competitor.

**Dual editing modes.** You can keep iterating through an AI chat interface ("make the hero section darker, add a pricing table") or switch to a visual drag-and-drop editor for pixel-level control. This hybrid approach means you're not fully dependent on the AI getting it right in one pass — you can always drop into manual editing when a prompt doesn't produce what you wanted.

**Built-in growth tools.** SEO audits, analytics and appointment scheduling ship with the platform rather than requiring separate subscriptions or plugins, according to CodeDesign.ai's own site. That's useful for a solo operator who doesn't want to stitch together several tools just to get basic traffic insight and a booking form.

**WordPress integration and a large template library.** CodeDesign.ai states it offers over 1,000 templates spanning 18+ industries (SaaS, healthcare, real estate, restaurants, and more), plus a WordPress integration for teams with existing content workflows. That's a wider net than a design-first tool like Framer AI, which leans more toward fewer, higher-polish starting points.

**Domain and hosting bundled in.** You can buy a domain from inside CodeDesign.ai across what the vendor says is 400+ extensions, with free SSL included, so a non-technical founder can go from prompt to a live, secured, custom-domain site without leaving the platform — unless they choose to export and self-host instead.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo founders and freelancers testing an idea** — the free plan (3 projects, subdomain hosting) is enough to validate a concept or build a portfolio site without paying anything upfront.
- **Small businesses that want a self-serve site with add-on tools** — the bundled SEO audits, analytics and scheduling reduce the number of separate subscriptions a small operator needs to run their site.
- **Agencies or freelance developers who want a fast first draft, then full code control** — the React/HTML export lets you generate a structural starting point in minutes, then hand it to a developer instead of building from a blank repo.
- **Teams already using WordPress** — the integration means CodeDesign.ai can slot into an existing content workflow rather than replacing it.

It's a weaker fit for teams whose primary requirement is best-in-class visual design control (Framer AI's canvas-based editor is more mature for that) or teams that want a CRM and invoicing baked in from day one (that's Durable's focus).

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Exports to real React or HTML code — no permanent lock-in | Pricing page doesn't clearly itemize every paid tier's price and limits |
| Free plan available with no credit card required for basic use | Visual polish and design flexibility trail dedicated design-first tools like Framer AI |
| Large template library across many industries | Lifetime-deal pricing seen in promotions may not reflect standard ongoing cost |
| Built-in SEO, analytics and scheduling reduce the need for extra tools | AI-generated first drafts, like most AI builders, often need manual cleanup for brand-specific nuance |
| WordPress integration for teams with existing content workflows | Third-party review volume on sites like Trustpilot is currently limited, making outside verification of satisfaction claims harder |

## Integrations and ecosystem

CodeDesign.ai's most notable "integration" is really an export path rather than a plugin marketplace: shipping your project out as React or HTML code means it can, in principle, connect to whatever stack a developer wants to build around it once exported. Beyond that, the platform documents a WordPress integration, in-platform domain purchasing (400+ extensions per the vendor), and Stripe for payment processing on the account side. It does not appear to offer a public API or native Zapier/Slack connectors the way some competitor tools do — if native automation hooks are a requirement, confirm current integration support directly with CodeDesign.ai before subscribing.

## Where it's a strong fit

CodeDesign.ai earns its keep when you want to move fast without giving up the option to take the code elsewhere later.
