Other AI customer support tools worth comparing include [Chatbase](/blog/chatbase-review), [CoSupport AI](/blog/cosupport-ai-review), and [Droxy AI](/blog/droxy-ai-review) — each uses seat-based or message-based pricing rather than resolution-based, so compare total cost at your expected ticket volume before choosing.

For more AI and software tool coverage, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Dreamwave AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is Dreamwave AI worth it for professional headshots? A detailed look at its pricing, features, team tools and real limitations.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Dreamwave AI worth it for professional headshots?

Dreamwave AI is a solid pick if you need studio-quality headshots fast without booking a photographer, especially for individuals and small teams on LinkedIn or company directories. It's less compelling if you need guaranteed, published pricing upfront or want a tool that does more than portrait generation — its scope stays narrow by design.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Not publicly listed for individuals; company headshots run $49–59 per person |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — a limited number of free daily headshot slots (first-come, first-served) |
| **Best for** | Individuals, small teams, and events needing fast, consistent AI headshots |
| **Standout feature** | HRIS-integrated company headshot rollouts (Workday, ADP, Rippling, Gusto, BambooHR) |

Dreamwave is an AI headshot generator built by a San Francisco company whose engineers previously worked at MIT, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, and SpaceX, according to the company's own site. Dreamwave doesn't publicly name the underlying image-generation model it trains on — it only says its models have produced more than 25 million portraits to date. That's a vendor claim, not an independently verified figure, so treat it as directional.

The pitch is straightforward: upload a handful of selfies, pick a style, and get back polished portraits in around two hours, without scheduling a photographer or hiring a retoucher. It's not a general-purpose AI image generator like Midjourney or Flux — it's purpose-built for headshots and portrait-style photos, for individuals, whole companies, and live events.

## What Dreamwave AI actually is

Dreamwave positions itself across three products that share the same underlying generation pipeline:

- **Personal headshots** — upload selfies, choose from business formal, casual, smart-casual, and other style categories, and receive a gallery of AI-generated portraits.
- **Company headshots** — a bulk workflow for teams, so an entire roster gets visually consistent headshots without everyone showing up to the same physical shoot.
- **Event photobooths** — an on-site AI booth product for conferences and trade shows, with a live slideshow wall and lead-capture tools for exhibitors.

All three route through the same core model, but company- and event-facing products add scheduling, bulk management, and integration layers.

## Pricing

This is the part where Dreamwave is harder to pin down than most AI SaaS tools. Unlike a typical AI writing or coding assistant with a public plans page, Dreamwave doesn't publish a static pricing table for its personal headshot product at the URL you'd expect (`/pricing` returns a 404 as of this writing). Instead, cost for individuals appears to be shown dynamically inside the order flow after you upload photos, and the company's marketing pages point undecided visitors to "Get an instant quote" or a sales email rather than a fixed rate card.

What is confirmed directly from Dreamwave's site:

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free daily headshot | $0 | A limited number of free generation slots open each day; the company says these "fill fast, often within a minute or two" |
| Personal headshots (paid) | Not publicly listed — shown in-app after upload | Multiple styles, all generated photos kept, ~2-hour turnaround per the site |
| Company headshots | $49–59 per person | 150 photos per person, free redo for any teammate unhappy with results, 1–2 hour turnaround, HRIS sync |
| Event photobooths | Custom quote | On-site booth, live slideshow wall, lead capture — priced per event via sales |

If you're comparing this against a competitor before committing, get the exact number directly from Dreamwave's checkout or sales team rather than relying on a third party's estimate — the company doesn't make that number easy to find without starting the order flow. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change quickly, since AI headshot tools iterate on pricing often.

Dreamwave also states it offers no refunds if the photos you upload don't follow its input guidelines — worth reading closely before you buy, since this isn't a typical satisfaction-guarantee refund policy.

## Core features that differentiate it

**Multiple style categories from one upload.** Rather than generating one generic "professional" look, Dreamwave lets you choose business formal, casual, smart-casual, and other category-specific styles, plus dedicated presets for roles like executives, lawyers, realtors, actors, doctors, and LinkedIn-specific crops.

**Post-generation editing tools.** Dreamwave includes prompt-based editing after your initial batch comes back — outfit swaps, background changes, and detail touch-ups — so you're not stuck re-uploading and re-paying if one detail is off, within what the tool's editing scope covers.

**HRIS-native company rollouts.** For team headshots, Dreamwave syncs with Workday, ADP, Rippling, Gusto, and BambooHR so a new hire's headshot can flow straight into the company directory without a separate manual upload step. This is genuinely uncommon among AI headshot competitors and is Dreamwave's clearest differentiator for HR teams.

**Event photobooth combo.** The event product isn't just a web app — it includes live slideshow walls for conference floors and lead-capture tied to the booth, aimed at trade show exhibitors rather than individual job seekers.

**Free daily generation slots.** The limited free tier is a genuine no-cost way to test output quality before paying, though availability is capped and fills within minutes once slots open, per the company.

## Who it's actually for

- **Individual job seekers and freelancers** updating a LinkedIn or resume headshot without booking a studio session — the personal product and free daily slots cover this well.
- **HR teams** onboarding hires regularly, wanting directory photos to stay consistent without a photo day — the company tier with HRIS sync is built for this.
- **Event marketers and exhibitors** wanting a branded, interactive photo activation at a booth — the photobooth product, though it requires a custom quote.
- **Agencies wanting a white-labeled or bulk API pipeline** may find Dreamwave's scope too narrow, since no self-serve developer API is publicly documented.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Fast turnaround (around two hours per the company) | No public, self-serve pricing page for individual headshots |
| Free daily generation slots to test quality first | Free slots are limited and can fill within minutes |
| Strong HRIS integrations for company-wide rollouts | No refunds if uploaded photos don't meet guidelines |
| Post-generation prompt-based editing included | Underlying AI model isn't publicly disclosed |
| Team founded by researchers from major AI labs, per the company | No documented public API for third-party integration |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Dreamwave's integration story is aimed at HR workflows rather than developers. It natively syncs with Workday, ADP, Rippling, Gusto, and BambooHR so that once a company headshot batch is approved, updated photos can push into the directory systems those platforms already manage. Beyond that, Dreamwave doesn't publicly document a Zapier connector, REST API, or plugin ecosystem the way broader creative AI platforms sometimes do — if you need to pipe headshot generation into a custom app, confirm API availability directly with Dreamwave's sales team first.

## Where it's a strong fit

Dreamwave is a strong fit if your need is specifically "professional-looking headshots, fast, without a photographer." The style presets cover common use cases (LinkedIn, executive bios, real estate listings, actor/model portfolios), and the HRIS sync solves a real pain point for growing teams adding hires continuously. The free daily slots make it low-risk to sample quality before spending anything.

## Where to think twice

Skip Dreamwave, or at least get a firm quote first, if you need transparent, comparison-shoppable pricing before you're willing to upload personal photos — most competitors publish a plans page; Dreamwave pushes you into its order flow or a sales conversation instead. It's also not the right tool if you need a documented public API for programmatic integration, since none is advertised. And because the company doesn't disclose which generative model or architecture underpins its output, if model transparency matters for your use case (for example, a regulated industry with AI-disclosure requirements), confirm those details directly with Dreamwave rather than assume.

If you specifically want a headshot tool with clearly published, tiered pricing, it's worth reading our [HeadshotPro review](/blog/headshotpro-review) alongside this one — HeadshotPro publishes fixed package pricing on its site, making upfront comparison easier even though the core promise is similar.

## Bottom line

Dreamwave AI delivers on its core promise — fast, stylistically varied, professional-looking headshots without a physical photo shoot — and its HRIS-native company headshot workflow is a genuinely useful differentiator for HR teams managing photos across a growing roster. The friction is on the transparency side: individual pricing isn't published anywhere on the public site, the refund policy is stricter than typical SaaS norms, and the underlying model stays undisclosed. If you're comfortable starting the upload flow to see your actual price, and your need fits squarely into personal, company, or event headshots rather than general AI image generation, Dreamwave is worth trying via its free daily slots first.

## FAQ

**Is Dreamwave AI free to use?**
Dreamwave offers a limited number of free headshot generation slots each day, but the company itself says these fill quickly, often within a minute or two. Paid personal headshot pricing is shown during the order flow rather than published as a fixed rate.

**How much do Dreamwave AI headshots cost?**
Company headshots are priced at $49–59 per person for 150 photos with a free redo option, according to Dreamwave's site. Personal pricing isn't published — confirm the exact cost during checkout before uploading photos.

**How long does Dreamwave take to generate headshots?**
Dreamwave states a turnaround of roughly one to two hours from upload to finished gallery, for both personal and company headshots.

**Does Dreamwave AI offer refunds?**
Dreamwave says it cannot offer refunds if your uploaded input photos don't follow its stated guidelines. Read the refund terms on Dreamwave's site closely before purchasing.

**What AI model does Dreamwave use?**
Dreamwave doesn't publicly disclose which foundational image-generation model powers its platform. The company only states its engineering team has backgrounds from labs including MIT, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, and SpaceX, and that its models have generated more than 25 million portraits to date, per its own marketing.

**Can Dreamwave integrate with our company's HR system?**
Yes — Dreamwave's company headshot product natively syncs with Workday, ADP, Rippling, Gusto, and BambooHR, so updated team photos flow into those directories without manual re-uploading.

**Is Dreamwave good for beginners with no photography experience?**
Yes. The core workflow — upload selfies, pick a style, wait for results — doesn't require photography or editing skill, and the prompt-based editing tools are simple text interactions.

**What are the alternatives to Dreamwave AI?**
HeadshotPro is a commonly compared alternative with published, fixed-tier pricing; see our [HeadshotPro review](/blog/headshotpro-review). Broader AI image tools like Midjourney can also produce portrait-style images but aren't purpose-built for headshot consistency the way Dreamwave is.

For more software deals and AI tool coverage, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Clipdrop Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Clipdrop offers fast AI background removal, cleanup, and upscaling tools. Here is what the free and Pro plans include, and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Clipdrop Review 2026: Is This AI Image Toolkit Worth It?

Clipdrop is a solid pick if you need one-off fixes — background removal, object cleanup, upscaling, or relighting — done fast in a browser without opening a full editor. It's less useful as a primary design tool: there's no layered canvas, and the free tier's daily caps make it best as a supplement to Photoshop, Canva, or Figma rather than a replacement.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free plan available; Pro plan priced per month (exact current rate not published as a fixed figure on the pricing page — confirm at checkout) |
| **Free tier** | Yes — daily-capped access to all core tools |
| **Best for** | Quick single-image fixes: background removal, cleanup, upscaling, relighting |
| **Standout feature** | One tool, nine single-purpose editors, no software install |

## What Clipdrop actually is

Clipdrop is a browser-based (and mobile-app) collection of single-purpose AI image tools: remove a background, erase an unwanted object, upscale a low-res photo, relight a subject, expand a cropped image, or generate an image from text. Each tool is its own page — you upload a photo, the tool runs, you download the result — rather than one big editor with layers and menus.

It was founded in 2020 by Cyril Diagne, Jonathan Blanchet, and Damien Henry, originally under the name Init ML. Stability AI acquired Clipdrop in 2023 to give its image-generation stack a consumer-facing front end. More recently, Clipdrop's support inbox and API docs route through a jasper.ai domain, and Jasper's own site advertises "Image APIs" for background removal, cleanup, and upscaling — the same toolset Clipdrop built its name on. Ownership appears to have moved again since the Stability AI acquisition; if evaluating Clipdrop for a business integration, confirm current ownership and terms of service on clipdrop.co before signing an API contract, since that can affect data handling and enterprise support terms.

Clipdrop doesn't publicly state which exact models power each tool. Given the Stability AI lineage, it's reasonable to assume some tools build on Stable Diffusion-family models, but that's inference rather than a documented fact — treat any specific model claim about Clipdrop's internals as unverified unless you find it in their own API docs.

## Pricing

Clipdrop runs a simple two-tier structure: a free plan with daily usage caps, and a paid Pro plan that removes queues and raises those caps.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | All 9 tools, capped at 20–50 uses per 24 hours per tool (varies by tool), 2x upscaling only |
| Pro | Paid, billed monthly (free trial offered) | Skip-the-queue processing, 1,000 uses per 24 hours per tool, high-resolution output, upscaling up to 16x |
| API | Usage-based | Per-call pricing for developers building Clipdrop's tools into their own apps |

A few specifics worth flagging before you sign up:

- The free plan's daily limits differ by tool — background removal, upscaling (2x only), cleanup, and relight are capped around 20 uses per 24 hours, while text removal allows roughly 50.
- Pro unlocks meaningfully higher-resolution output across the board, not just higher limits — this matters if you're prepping images for print or a large hero banner.
- Clipdrop's pricing page advertises a free trial on Pro but doesn't display a fixed monthly dollar figure in a way that's reliably scrapeable from the public page — confirm the exact current rate at checkout, since it may vary by region or promotion.
- Separately, Clipdrop offers a pay-as-you-go API for developers who want to call individual tools programmatically, billed by usage rather than a flat subscription.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI image tool pricing moves fast, so double-check the current numbers on Clipdrop's own pricing page before committing.

## Core features walkthrough

Clipdrop's whole pitch is "one tool per job, done well." Here's what actually stands out:

**Background removal and replacement.** Upload a photo, and Clipdrop cuts the subject out cleanly in seconds — no manual lasso work. The companion "Replace Background" tool goes further: instead of leaving a transparent PNG, it drops your subject into a new AI-generated scene from a text prompt, handy for product photography where you want consistent, branded backdrops without a physical studio.

**Cleanup (object/person removal).** This is the tool people come back for. Point at an unwanted object, photobomber, watermark, or blemish, and Clipdrop paints over it using context from surrounding pixels. It's not flawless on complex textures or busy backgrounds, but for straightforward removals (a stray cable, a tourist in the corner of a landscape shot) it's fast enough to use casually rather than opening a full photo editor.

**Image Upscaler.** Takes a low-resolution image and enlarges it while attempting to reduce noise and softness — free users get 2x, Pro users get up to 16x. Useful for salvaging old or small source photos before printing or using them larger.

**Uncrop.** Expands an image's canvas and fills the new space with AI-generated content matching the original — essentially outpainting. Good for reformatting a square photo into a wider banner without cropping content out.

**Relight and Text Remover.** Relight changes the apparent lighting direction/mood on a photo after the fact — a niche but genuinely hard-to-do-manually capability. Text Remover strips text, signage, or watermarks from images, pairing naturally with Cleanup.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and social media managers**: the free plan's daily caps (20–50 uses depending on tool) are workable for occasional touch-ups rather than batch-processing dozens of images a day.
- **E-commerce sellers and small teams**: Pro's higher-resolution output and 1,000-use daily cap make sense for prepping product photos at volume — swapping backgrounds, upscaling supplier images, cleaning up watermarks across a catalog.
- **Developers building image features into their own product**: the pay-as-you-go API lets you call individual Clipdrop tools programmatically instead of subscribing to the consumer app.
- **Professional retouchers doing complex composite work**: Clipdrop is a fast single-image utility, not a replacement for Photoshop's layer-based, non-destructive workflow — a good companion tool, not a full editing suite.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Nine focused tools cover common "fix this one thing" image tasks | No layers, masks, or non-destructive editing — single-pass, one image at a time |
| Free tier is genuinely usable, not just a crippled demo | Daily caps and lower resolution limit the free tier for production/print work |
| Fast — most tools return a result in seconds | Exact Pro price isn't listed as a fixed number on the public pricing page |
| Browser-based, no install, plus a mobile app | Cleanup and Uncrop can visibly struggle on complex textures or crowded scenes |
| Pay-as-you-go API available for developers | Ownership/branding has shifted (Stability AI to apparent Jasper links), worth watching for business use |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Clipdrop's main integration surface is its API — developers can call individual tools (background removal, cleanup, upscaling, text-to-image, and more) directly from their own applications on a pay-as-you-go basis, rather than routing end users through the Clipdrop web app. There's also a Clipdrop mobile app for iOS. Clipdrop doesn't publicly advertise native Zapier, Slack, or Adobe plugin integrations the way some competitors do — if you need Clipdrop-style effects inside Photoshop or a no-code automation chain, you'd generally build that connection yourself through the API rather than install an off-the-shelf plugin.

## Where it's a strong fit

Clipdrop earns its place as a fast utility for specific, recurring image chores: cleaning up a product photo, removing a background for a thumbnail, upscaling an old photo, or fixing a crop without starting over in a full editor. If your workflow is "one image, one problem," Clipdrop solves that quickly without a learning curve — and it's a reasonable pick for developers who want AI image utilities without building or hosting their own models.

## Where to think twice

Skip Clipdrop, or at least don't rely on it as your only tool, if:

- **You need layered, non-destructive editing** — Clipdrop processes one operation on one image at a time; there's no undo history across a multi-step composite, no layers panel, and no way to fine-tune a mask by hand.
- **You're batch-processing large volumes on the free plan** — the daily caps (as low as 20 uses per tool per 24 hours) will throttle you quickly on a real catalog.
- **You need a guaranteed, fixed monthly price before you commit** — since the exact Pro rate isn't published as a static number on the pricing page at the time of writing, confirm the current price directly before budgeting around a figure.
- **You need enterprise compliance guarantees (SOC 2, dedicated data processing agreements) for regulated industries** — Clipdrop's public marketing doesn't surface this kind of documentation; contact them directly rather than assuming coverage.
- **Your source images have complex, repetitive textures near the removal area** — Cleanup and Uncrop are good, not perfect, and can produce visible artifacts in tricky spots.

## Bottom line

Clipdrop does a specific job well: fast, single-purpose AI fixes for common image problems, without the overhead of a full design suite. The free tier is generous enough to be useful for casual and social-media-scale work, and Pro's jump in resolution and daily limits makes sense at real volume. It's not trying to be Photoshop and shouldn't be judged as one — treat it as a quick-fix toolbox for one image, one problem. Given the ownership shifts behind the scenes, business users leaning on the API for anything mission-critical should watch the terms of service rather than assume today's setup is permanent.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Clipdrop free to use?**
Yes. The free plan includes all nine tools with daily usage caps (roughly 20–50 uses per tool per 24 hours) and lower-resolution output than Pro.

**Who owns Clipdrop now?**
Clipdrop launched independently in 2020 (originally as Init ML) and was acquired by Stability AI in 2023. Its current support and API branding point toward Jasper, suggesting operation has shifted again since — confirm current terms directly with Clipdrop if this matters for a business decision.

**What's the difference between the free and Pro plans?**
Pro removes processing queues, raises daily usage limits to around 1,000 per tool, increases output resolution, and bumps the image upscaler from 2x to up to 16x.

**Does Clipdrop have an API?**
Yes, a pay-as-you-go API lets developers call individual tools directly from their own applications, billed by usage rather than a flat subscription.

**How accurate is the Cleanup (object removal) tool?**
It performs well on straightforward removals against relatively simple backgrounds but can leave visible artifacts on complex textures or crowded scenes — not a guaranteed clean result every time.

**Is Clipdrop good for beginners?**
Yes. Each tool is a single upload-and-run page with no settings to learn, approachable for people without photo-editing experience — though that also means less control than a full editor gives an experienced user.

**What image resolution does Clipdrop support?**
Free users get standard/lower-resolution output; Pro users get high-resolution output across all tools, including upscaling up to 16x versus 2x on free.

**Are there alternatives to Clipdrop?**
For background removal specifically, [Remove.bg](/blog/remove-bg-review) is a well-known focused alternative, and for broader AI-assisted photo editing with more manual control, [Pixlr](/blog/pixlr-review) is worth comparing.

For more AI and software deals, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Publer Review 2026: Pricing, AI Features and Verdict
excerpt: Publer review covering real pricing tiers, AI captioning, bulk scheduling, platform coverage, and who this social media scheduler fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Publer worth it?

Publer is a strong pick if you manage several social accounts across Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Pinterest, and the newer decentralized networks and want one dashboard for scheduling, bulk uploads, and light AI-assisted captioning. It's less compelling if AI generation is your main reason for buying, since the free and Professional tiers only include OpenAI-powered caption help while the deeper AI prompt allowance and analytics sit behind the pricier Business plan.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Around $12/month for the Professional plan (billed annually; monthly billing runs higher) |
| Free tier | Yes — 3 social accounts (excluding X/Twitter), 10 scheduled posts per account, 25 saved drafts, 24-hour post history |
| Best for | Small teams and agencies juggling multiple brands who want scheduling, bulk import, and basic AI captioning in one tool |
| Standout feature | Unlimited-workspace collaboration plus bulk CSV scheduling for up to 500 posts at once |

Publer doesn't have a matching store entry on SmartFare yet, so there's no coupon page to link here — figures below come from Publer's own pricing page (publer.com/pricing) and published comparison pages, checked in September 2026. AI tool pricing and feature availability change quickly, so confirm current numbers on Publer's site before subscribing.

## What Publer actually is

Publer is a social media scheduling and management platform that's been around since roughly 2016, well before "AI-powered" became a default marketing line for this category. It's built first as a scheduler and content calendar, with AI layered on top as a convenience feature rather than the whole pitch.

The company doesn't publish which specific model powers its AI Assistant beyond confirming an OpenAI integration, so it's fair to treat Publer's AI layer — caption generation, hashtag suggestions, and a bio generator — as a bolt-on for speeding up caption writing, not a dedicated writing tool you'd choose over something like Jasper or Copy.ai. What Publer is actually built around is platform breadth and team workflow: it connects Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X (Twitter), Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile, YouTube, Telegram, and WordPress, with approval workflows, unlimited workspaces on paid plans, and a browser extension for scheduling from any webpage you're browsing.

This puts it in a different lane than two other AI-adjacent social tools SmartFare has covered. [SocialDude](/blog/socialdude-review) leads with 15 AI content-generation agents and is closer to a copywriting tool that happens to post; [Beacons](/blog/beacons-review) is built around a link-in-bio page, storefront, and media kit for individual creators. Publer sits closer to traditional schedulers like Buffer or Hootsuite, with AI captioning as one feature among many rather than the headline.

## Publer pricing

Publer runs a free-forever plan plus three paid tiers — Professional, Business, and a custom-quoted Enterprise plan — pricing seats and connected accounts separately from the base fee, so your actual bill depends on how many accounts and members you add.

| Plan | Starting price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 1 user, 1 workspace, 3 social accounts (excludes X/Twitter), 10 scheduled posts per account, 25 saved drafts, 24-hour post history, free trials of most paid features |
| Professional | From about $12/month (billed annually) | Unlimited scheduling and drafts, first-comment and thread scheduling, unlimited media storage, unlimited workspaces, unlimited RSS automations, permanent post history, trending posts feed, X (Twitter) integration |
| Business | From about $21/month (billed annually) | Everything in Professional, plus unlimited AI prompts, analytics reports, best-times-to-post insights, competitor analysis, hashtag suggestions and analytics, spintax-powered post recycling, and API access |
| Enterprise | Custom quote (billed annually) | Everything in Business, plus volume discounts, 1:1 onboarding, prioritized support, unlimited daily posting, early feature access, and bank/wire transfer payment options |

Additional connected accounts and team members are billed incrementally on top of the base price on Professional and Business — Publer's pricing calculator lets you plug in your exact account and seat count before checkout, worth doing since the advertised "starting at" price assumes a small account count. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change, so confirm current numbers on Publer's pricing page before you commit.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Bulk scheduling via CSV.** Publer lets you import and schedule up to 500 posts at once from a spreadsheet, useful when migrating from another scheduler or batch-planning a content calendar a month out. Few competitors in this price range offer true bulk CSV import rather than one-post-at-a-time queuing.

**Workspaces and approval workflows.** Unlimited workspaces on paid plans mean an agency can keep each client's accounts, drafts, and calendar fully separated under one login, with members billed per seat and given collaboration or approval permissions.

**AI Assistant for captions, hashtags, and bios.** Publer's AI Assistant (OpenAI-based) generates post copy, and separate free tools handle hashtag generation and bio writing. Free includes limited AI use; Business unlocks what Publer calls "unlimited AI prompts."

**Content recycling with spintax.** Business's spintax-powered recycling automatically varies reposted evergreen content so it doesn't look copy-pasted — useful for accounts leaning on recycled tips or quotes.

**Browser extension and RSS automation.** The extension lets you schedule directly from any page you're reading, and RSS automation on paid plans can auto-populate your queue from blog feeds — handy for brands that want their scheduler pulling from a content source automatically.

## Who Publer is actually for

- **Solo creators testing the water:** the free plan's 3 accounts and 10 scheduled posts per account is enough to trial the workflow, though 24-hour post history and no X/Twitter support on free are real constraints.
- **Solopreneurs and small brands:** Professional's unlimited scheduling, drafts, and workspaces at a low entry price covers most single-brand needs once you outgrow free.
- **Agencies managing multiple clients:** unlimited workspaces plus per-seat member pricing on Business let Publer scale as an agency adds clients and collaborators, and Business API access opens custom integrations.
- **Teams wanting deeper AI use and analytics:** Business is the tier built for AI-heavy workflows and reporting — competitor analysis, best-times-to-post insights, and unlimited AI prompts sit there, not on Professional.
- **Large organizations with procurement needs:** Enterprise adds bank/wire payment options and prioritized support for orgs that can't pay by card.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Broad platform coverage including niche networks (Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business) | AI features are a caption/hashtag assistant, not a full content-generation suite |
| Bulk CSV import for up to 500 posts | Free plan excludes X/Twitter and caps post history at 24 hours |
| Unlimited workspaces even on the entry paid tier | "Starting at" prices exclude extra accounts/seats, so real cost climbs fast for larger teams |
| Free trials of paid features without a credit card | Analytics and competitor insights are gated behind the pricier Business tier |
| Browser extension and RSS automation for sourcing content | No published detail on which AI model powers the Assistant beyond "OpenAI integration" |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Publer connects natively to Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X (Twitter), Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile, YouTube, Telegram, and WordPress. It also integrates with Canva, Unsplash, and Google Drive for media sourcing, and offers Linkie, its own link-in-bio tool, as a bundled add-on. Business and Enterprise include API access for custom workflows. No native Zapier integration is listed on the pricing page at the time of writing, so confirm directly with Publer if that's a requirement.

## Where it's a strong fit

Publer earns its keep for teams and agencies managing a genuinely wide spread of social accounts from one place, especially if some accounts are on smaller networks like Mastodon or Bluesky that rival schedulers often skip. Bulk CSV import and unlimited workspaces on the entry paid tier make it a practical agency tool without agency-tier pricing, and the free-trial-without-a-card policy lowers the risk of testing Business.

## Where to think twice

If your main goal is AI content generation — long-form captions, multiple variations, tone control — Publer's AI Assistant is a convenience layer, not a dedicated writing tool, and you'll likely get more from a copy-focused product like SocialDude. Skip the free plan if you need X/Twitter scheduling, since it's excluded entirely below the paid tiers. And if your organization needs strict compliance documentation (SOC 2, for instance), that detail isn't published on Publer's public pages, so confirm it directly with sales rather than assume it's covered.

## Bottom line

Publer is a mature, broad-coverage social scheduler that treats AI as a helpful add-on rather than the product itself. For teams posting across many networks, collaborating across client workspaces, and occasionally leaning on AI for a caption or hashtag, it's a sensible, reasonably priced choice — budget for per-account and per-seat add-ons past the base tier, and look elsewhere if AI content generation is the primary job you're hiring a tool to do.

## FAQ

**Is Publer free to use?**
Yes. The free plan covers 1 workspace, 3 social accounts (excluding X/Twitter), 10 scheduled posts per account, 25 saved drafts, and 24-hour post history, with free trials available on most paid features without needing a credit card.

**Does Publer support X (Twitter)?**
Only on paid plans. Publer states that due to X's Enterprise API costs, X/Twitter accounts can only be connected on a paid subscription, not the free tier.

**What AI features does Publer actually include?**
An AI Assistant for generating post captions (built on an OpenAI integration), plus separate free web tools for AI hashtag generation and AI bio generation. Unlimited AI prompt use is reserved for Business and above.

**How is Publer priced for larger teams?**
Beyond the base plan price, additional connected accounts and team members are billed incrementally — Publer's site includes a calculator to estimate real cost based on your account and seat count rather than the advertised "starting at" figure.

**Does Publer offer an API?**
Yes, API access is included on Business and Enterprise, letting teams build custom integrations beyond the dashboard.

**Is Publer good for beginners?**
The core workflow — compose, preview, queue, publish — is straightforward, and the free plan is enough to learn the interface before paying. The account/seat-based pricing calculator takes a minute to understand before committing to a paid tier.

**What's the refund or trial policy?**
Publer advertises a 14-day money-back guarantee on paid plans and lets you trial most paid features free without entering payment details first.

**How does Publer compare to other AI-assisted social tools SmartFare has reviewed?**
It's closer to a traditional all-platform scheduler than an AI content generator. For AI-first caption writing across many agents, see the [SocialDude review](/blog/socialdude-review); for a link-in-bio page and creator monetization tools, see the [Beacons review](/blog/beacons-review). For more coverage, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: TypePrompt Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: TypePrompt review covering its viral hook templates, pricing transparency issues, features, and who this social AI writing tool actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is TypePrompt worth using for social content?

TypePrompt is a niche AI writing tool built around "viral hook" templates for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, and short-form social posts — it's a prompt-and-template layer on top of an AI model, not a full content suite. It's a reasonable pick if you specifically want hook-first social copy fast, but it's a thin choice if you need blog-length content, SEO writing, or a brand-voice trained assistant.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free tier available; paid plans exist but exact current pricing should be confirmed on typeprompt.com, since it wasn't independently verifiable at the time of writing |
| Free tier | Yes, with limited monthly generations (exact cap not publicly documented — check the app) |
| Best for | Solo creators, marketers, and LinkedIn/X posters who want hook-driven social copy without writing from a blank page |
| Standout feature | Viral hook template library modeled on patterns used by high-engagement creators, paired with a content-psychology framework (Educate, Entertain, Challenge, Empathize) |

TypePrompt doesn't have a matching store entry on SmartFare yet, so there's no coupon page to link here. A heads-up on sourcing: TypePrompt's own site (typeprompt.com) was unreachable during research for this review, so the details below are drawn from its Product Hunt listing and launch materials rather than its live pricing page. Treat every price and limit mentioned here as provisional — confirm current numbers directly on typeprompt.com before subscribing, and know that AI tool pricing and feature sets change often enough that anything checked in September 2026 can be stale within a few months.

## What TypePrompt actually is

TypePrompt launched on Product Hunt in 2024 as a lightweight, template-driven writing tool aimed squarely at social content — not general-purpose copywriting. The pitch is straightforward: instead of staring at a blank compose box, you pick a "hook" template (the kind of opening line that stops someone mid-scroll), feed it a topic or a rough idea, and the tool expands it into a full post using an underlying AI language model. TypePrompt doesn't publicly disclose which specific model or models power its generation — like a lot of smaller AI wrapper tools, it likely routes through a third-party API (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar) rather than running its own foundation model, but that's an inference, not a confirmed fact, so treat it as unverified until TypePrompt states it directly.

The product frames itself around a "content psychology" angle: templates are grouped by intent — Educate, Entertain, Challenge, and Empathize — which maps to fairly well-established social copywriting theory (teach something, make someone laugh, provoke a reaction, or make someone feel understood). That's a sensible organizing principle for a hook library, even if it's not a technical differentiator on its own.

## Pricing

TypePrompt offers a free tier, which is how most people will first try the product, plus paid plans for higher usage or additional templates. At its Product Hunt launch, TypePrompt ran a limited-time 50% discount for early adopters — a common launch tactic that tells you little about ongoing list pricing. Because the tool's own pricing page could not be reached during this review's research window, exact monthly figures for any paid tier, and the exact generation cap on the free plan, aren't reproduced here to avoid guessing. If pricing is the deciding factor for you, check typeprompt.com/pricing directly before committing, and consider that a tool this size may adjust tiers without much notice.

## Core features walkthrough

**Viral hook templates.** The centerpiece of TypePrompt is a library of pre-built hook structures — the kind of opening lines used repeatedly by high-engagement LinkedIn and Twitter/X creators (contrarian statements, numbered lists, "I did X for Y days" framing, and similar patterns). You pick a template, supply a topic, and the tool fills it in. This is the tool's actual value proposition: it's less "write me an article" and more "give me ten different scroll-stopping openers for this idea."

**AI Hook Prompts / post generation.** Beyond static templates, TypePrompt generates full short-form posts meant to read like a human wrote them, rather than an obviously AI-flavored paragraph. How well that holds up depends heavily on the underlying model and how much you edit before posting — as with any AI writing tool, treat the first draft as a starting point, not a final post.

**Platform-specific formats.** Templates are organized for the format differences between LinkedIn posts, Twitter/X threads, and general short-form social copy — a thread needs a different pacing than a single LinkedIn post, and TypePrompt's template categories reflect that rather than outputting one generic block of text for every platform.

**Content psychology framework.** The Educate/Entertain/Challenge/Empathize grouping gives you a way to pick a template based on the emotional or functional job you want the post to do, rather than scrolling a flat list of hundreds of prompts with no organizing logic.

**Article templates.** TypePrompt's listing also mentions article-style templates alongside the social-first ones, though its core identity and marketing emphasis are clearly social/short-form — don't expect it to replace a dedicated long-form writing assistant.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo LinkedIn or X creators** who post regularly and want a faster way past the blank-page problem, particularly for hook-writing, which is genuinely one of the harder parts of social copywriting to do well and consistently.
- **Marketers running personal or brand social accounts** who need a volume of short posts and are comfortable editing AI drafts rather than expecting publish-ready copy.
- **Freelance social media managers** juggling multiple client voices, where a template library speeds up first-draft generation across accounts — though voice consistency across clients will still require manual editing, since nothing in TypePrompt's public materials describes brand-voice training or fine-tuning.

It's a weaker fit for teams needing collaboration, scheduling, or analytics in the same tool, and for anyone needing long-form or SEO-structured content, where a general-purpose AI writing assistant will do more of the heavy lifting.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Narrow, useful focus on the specific problem of writing scroll-stopping openers | Official pricing isn't easy to verify publicly — you'll need to check the live site directly |
| Content-psychology template grouping gives structure to prompt selection | No disclosed underlying AI model, so output quality and consistency can't be benchmarked against named competitors |
| Free tier lets you test hook quality before paying | Small, young product (2024 launch, modest Product Hunt following) — less of a track record than established AI writing tools |
| Format-aware templates for LinkedIn, X, and short-form posts | No scheduling, analytics, or team collaboration features built in |
| Low learning curve — pick a template, add a topic, generate | AI-generated hooks still need human editing for accuracy, tone, and to avoid sounding formulaic if overused |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Public information about TypePrompt's integrations is limited. There's no confirmed API, no documented Zapier connector, and no listed Slack or CRM integration in the materials available for this review. If you need TypePrompt output to flow directly into a scheduler or CMS, plan on a manual copy-paste step, or verify directly with TypePrompt whether any integration options exist — nothing here should be assumed without checking the product's own site or support docs.

## Where it's a strong fit

TypePrompt earns its keep if your actual bottleneck is the opening line of a post — the part that decides whether someone stops scrolling — and you want a structured way to generate options fast rather than freewriting from scratch every time. For someone posting several times a week on LinkedIn or X, having a template bank organized by psychological intent (rather than a flat prompt list) can meaningfully cut the time between "I have an idea" and "I have a draft."

## Where to think twice

Skip TypePrompt, or don't rely on it alone, if you need a fully-featured content platform — it doesn't do scheduling, analytics, or multi-platform publishing, so you'll still need a separate tool like Publer or Buffer for the operational side. Think twice if verifiable, transparent pricing matters before you commit; this review couldn't independently confirm current tier pricing because TypePrompt's site wasn't reachable during research. Think twice too if you need enterprise features like SSO or SOC 2 documentation — nothing in TypePrompt's public materials suggests it targets that segment. And if your main writing need is long-form articles or SEO content, a hook-template tool built for social posts isn't the right shape of tool.

## Bottom line

TypePrompt is a small, purpose-built tool for one specific pain point: writing hooks and short social posts faster. If that's genuinely your bottleneck and you're comfortable testing the free tier before paying, it's worth a trial run — the content-psychology template structure is a sensible way to organize prompts, and the format-aware templates save some of the fiddling you'd otherwise do manually. But it's not a replacement for a full content or social-management platform, its underlying model and exact pricing aren't transparently documented in public sources, and it's young enough (2024 launch, small following) that you should verify current pricing, limits, and feature availability directly on typeprompt.com before relying on it for regular work. If you want a social-content generator with a broader library of specialized "agents" instead of a template-only approach, it's worth comparing against alternatives like [SocialDude](/blog/socialdude-review) before deciding.

## FAQ

**Is TypePrompt free to use?**
TypePrompt offers a free tier, though the exact monthly generation limit isn't clearly documented in public sources. Check the free plan's current limits directly on typeprompt.com before assuming a specific cap.

**What platforms does TypePrompt write for?**
Its templates are built primarily around LinkedIn posts, Twitter/X posts and threads, and general short-form social content, with some article-style templates also listed.

**Does TypePrompt disclose which AI model it uses?**
No, not in its public marketing materials as of this review. Like many smaller AI writing tools, it likely calls a third-party AI API rather than running a proprietary model, but that hasn't been confirmed by the vendor.

**How much does TypePrompt cost?**
Paid pricing exists beyond the free tier, but current figures weren't independently verifiable when this review was researched because the vendor's site was unreachable. Confirm pricing on typeprompt.com directly.

**Is TypePrompt good for beginners?**
Yes — the template-and-topic input flow has a low learning curve. You don't need prompt-engineering experience to get usable output, though editing the draft before posting is still recommended.

**Does TypePrompt handle scheduling or publishing?**
No. It generates text; you still need a separate scheduler or manual posting to actually publish to LinkedIn, X, or other platforms.

**What are the best TypePrompt alternatives?**
For a broader roster of social-copy generators with more specialized use-case "agents," [SocialDude](/blog/socialdude-review) is worth comparing. For teams that also need scheduling and multi-account management alongside AI captioning, [Publer](/blog/publer-review) covers that ground.

**Is my data private with TypePrompt?**
TypePrompt's public materials don't detail a specific data-retention or privacy policy in the sources available for this review. Check the tool's own privacy policy on typeprompt.com before entering sensitive or client-confidential content into any prompt.

For more AI and software coverage, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Glasp Review 2026: Pricing, AI Features and Verdict
excerpt: Glasp turns web pages, PDFs, YouTube and Kindle highlights into an AI-searchable knowledge base — here is what it costs and who it actually suits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Glasp Worth It in 2026?

Glasp is worth trying if you read across a lot of web pages, PDFs, YouTube videos, or Kindle books and want one searchable place for your highlights and notes. Its free plan is genuinely usable for light readers, and the AI chat/summary features are solid extras rather than the whole product — so it's a good fit for researchers and students, less so for teams needing shared knowledge bases.

### At a Glance

| | Details |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (limited); Pro from $12.50/month billed annually |
| Free tier | Yes — unlimited public highlights, capped AI/PDF/audio usage |
| Best for | Individual readers, researchers, students, content curators |
| Standout feature | Cross-format highlighting (web, PDF, YouTube, Kindle) in one searchable library |

## What Is Glasp?

Glasp is a browser-extension-based highlighter and note-taking tool built around a simple idea: your highlights from articles, PDFs, YouTube videos, and Kindle books shouldn't be scattered across five different apps. It captures them into one personal library, layers AI chat and summarization on top, and — unusually for a personal knowledge tool — adds a social layer where you can see (and follow) what other people are highlighting on the same pages you're reading.

The company describes itself as a "social web and PDF highlighter," and that framing matters: Glasp isn't trying to be a full note-taking suite like Notion or Obsidian. It's narrower and more specific — capture what you read, get an AI assist on it, and optionally sync it out to the tools you already use for deeper writing and organizing.

Glasp doesn't publicly commit to a single underlying model for its AI chat; its Pro and Unlimited plans advertise access to "all models" through a shared credit pool, which suggests it's routing requests across multiple third-party LLMs rather than running its own. That's worth confirming on the official site if model choice matters to your workflow, since vendors change model line-ups more often than they change pricing pages.

## Glasp Pricing

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability below were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tool pricing and usage caps move fast, so double-check the current numbers on Glasp's own pricing page before you commit to a paid plan.

| Plan | Price | Highlights | AI chat credits | PDF chat | YouTube summaries | Notion sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Unlimited public | 20/month | 20 messages/month, 30 file uploads | 3/day, 1 channel tracked | Not included |
| Pro | $12.50/mo ($150/yr billed annually) | Unlimited private | 500/month, all models | 500 messages/month, 100 file uploads | 1,000/month, 5 channels | Daily auto-sync |
| Unlimited | $30/mo ($360/yr billed annually) | Unlimited private | 2,000/month, all models | 5,000 messages/month, unlimited uploads | 5,000 per 30 days, 25 channels | Daily auto-sync + priority support |

A few things stand out in that table. First, the free plan's biggest restriction isn't AI usage — it's that your highlights stay public unless you upgrade, which is a real consideration if you're highlighting anything sensitive or work-related. Second, the jump from Pro to Unlimited is mostly about volume (more AI credits, more PDF chat messages, more tracked YouTube channels) rather than new capabilities, so heavy users of any single feature — say, someone who lives in PDF chat — should map their actual monthly usage against these caps rather than assuming "Pro" is automatically enough.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Cross-format highlighting.** The browser extension lets you highlight text on any web page, inside PDFs opened in the browser, and — through separate integrations — capture quotes from YouTube video transcripts and Kindle book highlights you've already made. Everything lands in one searchable library instead of being locked inside whatever app you read it in.

**AI chat on pages and PDFs.** Instead of just summarizing a page once, Glasp's AI chat lets you ask follow-up questions against the content you're reading — closer to a mini research assistant than a one-click "TL;DR" button. This is metered separately by credits (free tier) or a shared monthly pool (paid tiers), and PDF chat draws from its own message allowance on top of that.

**YouTube video summaries and channel tracking.** Glasp can generate a summary of a YouTube video's transcript and, on paid plans, track entire channels so new uploads get summarized automatically. The free plan caps this at three summaries a day and one tracked channel — enough to sample the feature, not enough to replace watching your usual subscriptions.

**Audio transcription.** A less-publicized feature: Glasp can transcribe audio (useful for podcast clips or voice notes) with a monthly minutes allowance that scales with plan tier — 30 minutes free, up to 1,500 minutes on Unlimited.

**Social highlight feed.** This is the feature that sets Glasp apart from a purely private tool like Readwise. Public highlights (the default on the free tier) are visible to other Glasp users who've highlighted the same content, and you can follow people whose highlighting habits you find useful — effectively a lightweight social network built on top of reading.

## Who It's Actually For

- **Solo readers and researchers** who read heavily across articles, PDFs, and YouTube and want one searchable archive — the free plan alone covers a meaningful chunk of this use case.
- **Students and lifelong learners** who want AI chat to interrogate dense PDFs (textbooks, papers) rather than just skim a summary — Pro's 500 PDF chat messages a month is a reasonable middle ground.
- **Content curators and newsletter writers** who track several YouTube channels or blogs for source material — the channel-tracking and daily Notion sync on Pro/Unlimited fit this workflow well.
- **Teams needing shared, private knowledge bases** are a weaker fit — Glasp is built around individual accounts and a public-by-default social layer, not team workspaces or granular sharing permissions.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Usable free tier with unlimited public highlights | Highlights are public by default unless you're on a paid plan |
| Covers web, PDF, YouTube, and Kindle in one tool | AI features are credit-metered and can run out mid-month on heavy days |
| AI chat lets you interrogate content, not just get a summary | No team/collaboration workspace — built for individuals |
| Notion sync automates moving notes into a second-brain setup | Pricing per-plan is fixed to specific quotas, not pay-as-you-go |
| Social feed can surface useful highlights from other readers | The social layer isn't for everyone reading sensitive material |

## Integrations & Ecosystem

Glasp's main integration is Notion — Pro and Unlimited plans include daily automatic syncing of your highlights and notes into a Notion database, which is the most practical bridge if your actual writing and organizing happens outside Glasp. Kindle highlight import is supported for readers who want their book notes alongside their web and PDF highlights. There's no public REST API documented for third-party developers as of this writing, and no native Zapier or Slack integration is advertised on the pricing page — so if your workflow depends on connecting Glasp to a broader automation stack beyond Notion, confirm current integration support directly on Glasp's site before relying on it.

## Where Glasp Is a Strong Fit

If most of your knowledge work starts with reading — papers, articles, video transcripts, book highlights — and ends with wanting to search back through what you've already read, Glasp's core loop (highlight, ask AI about it, sync out) solves a real problem that most note apps only handle half of. The free tier is generous enough to actually test this before paying, which isn't true of every AI tool on the market.

It's also a decent fit if you already use Notion as your permanent knowledge base and just want an easier way to get highlights into it without manual copy-pasting — the daily auto-sync removes a genuinely tedious step.

## Where to Think Twice

Skip Glasp, or at least stay on the free plan, if you're highlighting anything you wouldn't want visible to other users — the public-by-default model on the free tier is a real privacy trade-off, not a minor detail. If your team needs a shared, permissioned knowledge base with enterprise-grade access controls, Glasp isn't built for that; it's single-user by design. And if you need deep API access or Zapier-style automation to wire Glasp into a larger stack, the currently documented integration surface (mainly Notion) is thin compared to broader productivity platforms.

## Bottom Line

Glasp does one thing well that a lot of bigger note-taking suites do as an afterthought: it makes the actual act of highlighting across different formats — web, PDF, YouTube, Kindle — feel like a single workflow instead of five disconnected habits. The AI chat and summary layer is a genuine value-add rather than a bolted-on gimmick, and the free tier is honest enough to let you find out if the core idea fits your reading habits before you pay anything. The catch is the public-by-default highlighting model and the fact that it's not built for teams — know that going in, and Glasp is a low-risk, low-cost addition to a research-heavy workflow.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Glasp free to use?**
Yes. The free plan requires no credit card and includes unlimited public highlights, along with capped monthly allowances for AI chat, PDF chat, YouTube summaries, and audio transcription.

**Are my Glasp highlights private?**
Only on paid plans. On the free tier, highlights are public by default and visible to other Glasp users browsing the same content; Pro and Unlimited plans support unlimited private highlights.

**What AI models does Glasp use?**
Glasp advertises access to "all models" on its paid plans through a shared credit system rather than committing to one specific model publicly, so if model choice matters to you, confirm current details on its official pricing page.

**Does Glasp work with Kindle and PDFs, or just web pages?**
It covers all three, plus YouTube video transcripts — highlights from web pages, PDF uploads, Kindle books, and YouTube summaries all land in the same searchable library.

**Can Glasp send my notes to Notion automatically?**
Yes, but only on Pro and Unlimited plans, which include a daily automatic sync of highlights and notes into a connected Notion database. The free plan doesn't include Notion sync.

**Is Glasp good for teams, not just individuals?**
Not really. Glasp is built around individual accounts and a public/private highlight model rather than team workspaces, shared permissions, or collaborative editing, so teams needing a shared knowledge base should look elsewhere.

**How does Glasp compare to Readwise or Notion AI?**
Readwise is a closer direct competitor, focused more narrowly on capturing and resurfacing highlights without Glasp's social feed. Notion AI, covered in our [Notion AI review](/blog/notion-ai-review), is a different category entirely — an AI layer inside a full workspace/document tool rather than a dedicated highlighter — and the two can complement each other, since Glasp can sync into Notion rather than replace it.

For more AI and productivity tool coverage, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub.

title: Tettra Review 2026: Pricing, AI Features and Verdict
excerpt: Tettra pairs a Slack-native AI bot with page verification to stop repeat questions and stale docs. Here's the pricing and who it suits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Tettra worth it for internal knowledge management?

Tettra is a solid pick for small and mid-sized teams that are tired of answering the same questions in Slack and want a lightweight wiki with an AI layer on top, rather than a heavyweight enterprise knowledge platform. It's less compelling for large orgs needing deep permissioning, or teams that already have a wiki inside Notion or Confluence and don't want to migrate.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $8 per user/month on the Scaling plan (10-user minimum), billed monthly or annually |
| **Free tier/trial** | No permanent free plan — 30-day free trial, all features included |
| **Best for** | Small-to-mid-size teams that live in Slack and want fewer repeat questions |
| **Standout feature** | Kai, the AI bot that answers questions in Slack from your existing content |

Tettra is an internal knowledge base built by Tettra, Inc. around one specific problem: teams answer the same handful of questions over and over in Slack threads and DMs, and that knowledge never makes it into a searchable, maintained place. Instead of positioning itself as a general-purpose wiki or document editor, Tettra leans into being the layer that sits on top of the tools you already have — Google Docs, PDFs, Slack conversations — and turns them into something an AI bot can search and answer from.

Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability described below were accurate as of this post's publish date and can shift — AI product pricing moves quickly, so confirm current numbers on Tettra's own pricing page before you commit to a plan size.

## Pricing

Tettra keeps its pricing structure simple compared to a lot of knowledge-base competitors that split features across four or five tiers.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Scaling | $8/user/month (10-user minimum), ~20% off annually | AI answers and page tagging, AI FAQ generation, Kai AI bot in Slack, Google Workspace integration, usage analytics, API access, unlimited storage and version history, page verification workflows, guest and read-only users, live chat support |
| Enterprise | Custom, contact sales | Everything in Scaling, plus SSO & SCIM, hands-on training, custom import/onboarding, custom reporting, priority support, and custom integrations |

There's no permanently free plan — every account starts as a 30-day free trial with the full feature set unlocked, and Tettra says the trial doesn't require a credit card to start. The 10-user minimum on Scaling matters for very small teams: even a 3-person startup is billed as if it has 10 seats, which pushes the effective monthly floor to around $80 rather than $24. That's worth factoring in before you sign up if your team is smaller than ten people.

## Core features walkthrough

**Kai, the AI answer bot.** This is Tettra's headline feature and the reason it's positioned as an "AI-powered" knowledge base rather than just a wiki. Kai searches your existing Tettra pages (and connected sources like Google Docs and PDFs) and answers questions asked directly in Slack or inside Tettra itself, instead of making people dig through channels or ping a coworker. When it can't find a confident answer, it routes the question to a designated subject-matter expert rather than guessing — a sensible design choice for internal documentation, where a wrong answer about, say, a refund policy or deployment process is worse than no answer at all.

**Content verification workflows.** Stale documentation is the most common reason internal wikis die. Tettra addresses this directly with a verification system where page owners are prompted to periodically confirm a page is still accurate, and the tool surfaces pages that haven't been verified in a while. This is a genuinely differentiating feature next to tools like Notion, which has no built-in staleness tracking — see our [Notion AI review](/blog/notion-ai-review) for how that comparison plays out if you're choosing between the two.

**Works with content you already have.** Rather than forcing a full migration, Tettra lets you pull in existing Google Docs and PDFs as sources instead of requiring everything to be rewritten as native Tettra pages. That lowers the setup cost for teams with an existing scattered mess of docs, though it also means some of your "knowledge base" content still technically lives outside Tettra.

**Page requests and gap identification.** Employees can request a page be written on a topic that doesn't exist yet, which surfaces documentation gaps organically instead of relying on someone remembering to write things down. Combined with Kai routing unanswered questions to experts, this creates a light feedback loop for what to document next.

**Slack-first design.** Unlike wiki tools that treat Slack as an afterthought integration, Tettra's core interaction model assumes your team is already living in Slack and builds the AI bot to meet people there rather than requiring them to open a separate app first.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo operators and very small teams (under 5 people):** A weak fit — the 10-user Scaling minimum means paying for unused seats, and Notion or a shared Drive folder covers the same ground more cheaply.
- **Startups and small teams (10–50 people) that run on Slack:** Tettra's sweet spot. Per-seat pricing lines up naturally with headcount, and Kai pays for itself quickly once it starts deflecting repeat Slack questions.
- **Growing companies (50–250 people) documenting process across support/ops/HR:** Verification workflows and page requests matter more here, since content ownership gets murkier as headcount grows.
- **Enterprises needing SSO/SCIM and custom onboarding:** Go straight to the Enterprise plan and treat pricing as a negotiation rather than a self-serve decision.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Simple two-tier pricing, no confusing feature-gating across five plans | No permanent free plan, only a 30-day trial |
| Kai AI bot answers directly inside Slack, where most teams already work | 10-user minimum on Scaling inflates cost for very small teams |
| Built-in page verification tackles the stale-wiki problem head-on | Less flexible as a general workspace than Notion or Confluence (no databases, no complex nested project pages) |
| Works with existing Google Docs/PDFs instead of forcing a full migration | Enterprise pricing isn't public, so budget planning requires a sales call |
| API access included even on the entry-level Scaling plan | Smaller ecosystem of third-party integrations than larger platforms like Confluence |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Tettra's most prominent integration is Slack, where the Kai bot lives and answers questions directly in threads and DMs — this is the integration the product is effectively built around, not a bolt-on. It also connects to Google Workspace, letting teams pull existing Google Docs into the knowledge base as sources rather than duplicating content by hand. API access is included starting on the Scaling plan, opening the door to custom integrations if your team has engineering resources to build against it, and Enterprise customers get custom integration support directly from Tettra. Compared to a platform like Confluence, which has a large Atlassian Marketplace of third-party plugins, Tettra's integration surface is narrower and more focused on doing Slack plus Google Workspace well rather than supporting dozens of surface-level integrations.

## Where it's a strong fit

Tettra makes the most sense for teams where Slack is genuinely the operational hub — support teams, remote-first startups, and ops-heavy functions where the same "how do I..." questions recur constantly. If your team's biggest documentation problem is that answers exist somewhere but nobody can find them fast enough, Kai directly targets that gap instead of just giving you another place to write docs that go unread. The verification workflow is also a real advantage for teams that have tried a wiki before and watched it rot within six months.

## Where to think twice

Skip Tettra if you need a genuinely free tool for an ongoing small project — there's no free tier, only a time-limited trial, and the per-seat minimum makes it a poor fit for teams under ten people. If your organization needs a workspace that does more than documentation — task tracking, databases, kanban boards, embedded spreadsheets — a broader tool like Notion will cover more ground for a similar or lower price, even if it lacks Tettra's verification workflow and Slack-native AI bot. Teams with a large existing investment in Confluence/Atlassian probably won't find enough differentiation to justify switching. And because Kai's answers are only as good as the pages that exist and are kept current, teams that never adopt the verification workflow will likely see answer quality degrade over time — it's a tool that rewards ongoing maintenance, not a set-and-forget fix.

## The bottom line

Tettra earns its "AI-powered" label through a narrow, well-executed feature — Kai answering questions in Slack from your actual documentation — rather than by bolting generic AI writing tools onto a wiki. That focus is its biggest strength and its main limitation: teams that want an all-in-one workspace will outgrow it, but teams whose real problem is "we keep answering the same Slack questions and our docs go stale" get a tool built specifically to fix that. The lack of a free plan and the 10-seat minimum are real friction points for very small teams, but for a 10-to-250-person company already living in Slack, the trial is worth running before deciding.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Tettra have a free plan?

No. Tettra offers a 30-day free trial with all features unlocked, but there's no permanent free tier. After the trial, you'll need to choose the paid Scaling plan or talk to sales about Enterprise pricing.

### How much does Tettra cost per month?

The Scaling plan is $8 per user per month with a 10-user minimum, which puts the effective starting cost around $80/month. Annual billing brings a discount of roughly 20% (two free months). Enterprise pricing is custom and requires contacting Tettra's sales team.

### What is Kai in Tettra?

Kai is Tettra's AI bot that searches your knowledge base and answers questions directly in Slack or inside Tettra. When it can't confidently answer something, it routes the question to a designated subject-matter expert instead of guessing.

### Can Tettra import existing documentation?

Yes. Tettra can pull in existing Google Docs and PDFs as sources rather than requiring you to rewrite everything as native Tettra pages, which lowers the effort of getting started with content you already have.

### Is Tettra good for small teams?

It depends on size. Teams of roughly 10–50 people who rely heavily on Slack tend to get strong value from Tettra. Teams smaller than 10 people will likely pay for unused seats due to the Scaling plan's user minimum and may be better served by a cheaper, more general tool.

### How is Tettra different from Notion or Confluence?

Tettra is narrower by design — it focuses on Q&A retrieval via its Slack-integrated AI bot and on keeping documentation from going stale through verification workflows, rather than trying to be a full workspace with databases, tasks, and project management like Notion, or a large-scale enterprise wiki with an extensive plugin ecosystem like Confluence. See our [Notion AI review](/blog/notion-ai-review) for how that tool's broader feature set compares.

### Does Tettra require a credit card to start a trial?

Tettra states its 30-day free trial doesn't require a credit card to begin, though a payment method will be needed to continue on a paid plan once the trial ends.

### Is there a discount for nonprofits or education?

Tettra lists nonprofit and educational discounts as available; specifics should be confirmed directly with Tettra's sales team since exact terms aren't published on the general pricing page.
