title: Grit.io Review 2026: What Happened After Acquisition
excerpt: Grit.io was acquired by Honeycomb in 2025 and its GritQL language was donated to Biome. Here's what that means for developers today.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Grit.io still worth using in 2026?

Not as a standalone commercial product — Grit.io was acquired by observability company Honeycomb earlier in 2025, and in December 2025 its creator donated the open-source GritQL query language to Biome rather than let it stagnate. GritQL itself is now actively maintained, but "Grit.io" as an independent business no longer exists to sign up for.

### At a glance

| | Details |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free — GritQL is open source (MIT-style licensing under Biome) |
| Free tier/trial | N/A today — the old hosted Grit.io platform's paid tiers are no longer sold |
| Best for | Developers who want a declarative language for large-scale codebase search-and-transform |
| Standout feature | Query and rewrite code across 10+ languages with a single pattern-matching syntax, without hand-writing an AST parser |
| Current status | Company acquired by Honeycomb (2025); GritQL donated to the Biome organization (December 18, 2025) |

## What Grit.io actually was

Grit.io was a developer-tools startup built around a single, sharp idea: most large-scale code migrations — upgrading a framework, renaming an API across a monorepo, enforcing a new lint rule everywhere at once — don't need a fully custom script or a brittle regex. They need a query language that understands code structure the way SQL understands tables.

That language was GritQL, and it was the core of everything Grit.io shipped. Instead of forcing developers to write raw abstract-syntax-tree (AST) manipulation code — the traditional way tools like jscodeshift or codemod scripts work — GritQL let you describe a code pattern declaratively, similar in spirit to a CSS selector or a SQL `WHERE` clause, and then either search for matches or rewrite them in place. The company said it built the underlying engine in Rust specifically so pattern matching could scale to codebases in the millions of lines without grinding to a halt.

Grit.io positioned itself less as "an AI tool" in the generative sense and more as an AI-era refactoring/migration utility: it deterministically found and transformed code matching a defined pattern rather than hallucinating new code from a prompt — a meaningfully safer approach for mission-critical migrations than asking an LLM to rewrite files freehand. Some later tooling did pair GritQL with LLM-assisted pattern generation, letting you describe a transformation in English and get a starting query to refine, but the transformation itself always ran through the deterministic engine.

The company was founded by Morgante Pell, who remained the driving force behind GritQL through its acquisition and eventual donation to Biome. Grit.io raised a $7 million round (announced August 15, 2023), and the product picked up genuine developer traction — support for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Rust, Go, SQL, HCL and other languages, a public pattern library described as having "200+" pre-built patterns, a CLI, a browser playground, and a VS Code extension.

## What happened — the acquisition and the Biome donation

Two separate events matter here, and they happened close together.

First, Honeycomb — an observability and tracing company best known for its own developer tooling — acquired Grit earlier in 2025. Public detail on the acquisition's terms is thin; neither company published a breakdown of what changed for existing customers, migration timelines, or whether the hosted platform (dashboard, CI-triggered migrations, paid tiers) would keep running under Honeycomb's ownership.

Second, and more consequential for developers who use GritQL day to day: on December 18, 2025, Biome — the Rust-based JS/TS toolchain project — announced that GritQL's repositories had been donated to the Biome organization, and that Morgante Pell had personally joined its maintainers team. Biome had already been using GritQL as its preferred plugin language before the donation, so the move consolidated the language under the organization that was arguably its heaviest real-world user. Biome's framing was that GritQL's future had become uncertain after the acquisition, and donating the project — rather than letting useful tooling quietly stop receiving updates — was the better outcome for the ecosystem.

In practice: GritQL's language, CLI, and matching engine are now maintained inside Biome's GitHub organization (`biomejs/gritql`), with continued commits and an active maintainer. What's much less clear is the fate of any commercial, hosted Grit.io product that existed before the acquisition — neither company's public materials address former paying customers, and the old marketing site now redirects straight to the documentation, with no pricing page or signup flow visible.

**A note on sourcing:** details here reflect what was publicly documented as of this post's date (below), pulled from Biome's blog announcement, Grit.io's documentation, and its GitHub repositories — not vendor marketing copy. Verify current status via `biomejs/gritql` on GitHub before relying on this for a production decision.

## Core capabilities (based on GritQL's public documentation)

Since there's no active commercial product to evaluate hands-on, this reflects what GritQL's own documentation describes it as capable of:

- **Declarative pattern matching.** Write a GritQL pattern describing the shape of code you want to find — a function call with specific arguments, an import statement, a deprecated API usage — without hand-rolling AST traversal logic.
- **Multi-language support.** The same language works, with language-specific pattern libraries, across JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Rust, Go, SQL, HCL and more — useful for polyglot codebases.
- **A reusable module system.** Patterns can be composed and shared, so a team can build an internal library of transformations rather than one-off scripts.
- **A public pattern library.** Grit.io described its library as having 200+ standard patterns covering common migrations and lint-style fixes.
- **Auto-fix / rewrite mode.** GritQL searches for matches and applies structured rewrites — the actual mechanism behind large-scale codemods, not just a find-and-flag tool.
- **Rust-based performance.** The engine was built in Rust to keep matching fast at the scale of millions of lines of code.

## Who it was actually for

GritQL was never aimed at a general audience. It's squarely a developer-tools proposition: platform/infrastructure teams running large-scale framework upgrades or codebase-wide lint enforcement (the use case the $7M raise was built around), individual developers and open-source maintainers who want a lighter alternative to hand-writing AST scripts, and Biome plugin authors, since GritQL is now Biome's preferred plugin language. It is **not** a fit for teams that specifically wanted a vendor-backed, supported, paid product with an SLA — that commercial layer's future is genuinely unclear post-acquisition.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| GritQL is open source, free, and now actively maintained under Biome | No confirmed, currently-sold commercial/hosted Grit.io product to evaluate |
| Declarative syntax is easier to learn than hand-writing AST manipulation code | Pricing history (paid tiers, enterprise plans) isn't publicly documented |
| Genuine multi-language support (JS/TS, Python, Java, Rust, Go, SQL, HCL, more) | Company continuity is uncertain — Honeycomb's plans beyond the open-source code aren't public |
| Backed by an active maintainer (Morgante Pell) inside a real, ongoing project (Biome) | Anyone expecting a managed SaaS platform now has no clear commercial contact |
| Deterministic, rule-based transformations are safer for critical migrations than free-form LLM rewriting | Docs and tooling still carry old "Grit.io" branding, confusing post-acquisition |

## Integrations and ecosystem

GritQL's practical footprint runs through developer tooling rather than a hosted platform: a **CLI** for running patterns locally or in CI, a **VS Code extension** for authoring and testing patterns in-editor, a **browser playground** for experimenting without installing anything, and Biome's own **plugin system**, which now uses GritQL as its chosen language for custom linter/formatter rules — arguably the most active integration point going forward. The canonical source lives under `biomejs/gritql` on GitHub. There's no confirmed Slack, Zapier, or similar no-code integration — this has always been a code-level developer tool.

## Where it's a strong fit

It's a strong fit for teams already using or adopting Biome for JS/TS linting and formatting who want to write custom plugin logic in the same query language Biome is built around; for anyone doing a genuinely large, structural code migration who wants a deterministic, reviewable transformation rather than an LLM regenerating files and hoping the diff is correct; and for open-source maintainers who want a free, actively-developed tool over a paid commercial platform.

## Where to think twice

Think twice if you were specifically evaluating Grit.io as a **vendor-supported, paid SaaS product** with a dashboard and enterprise support — that commercial offering's current availability is unconfirmed, and you shouldn't budget around it without confirming current terms with Honeycomb. Also think twice if you need a tool a non-technical team can configure without touching a query syntax (GritQL still requires learning its pattern language), or if your organization needs a vendor with a clear support contract and SLA — this project's post-acquisition, now-open-source status makes that kind of commercial guarantee hard to obtain right now.

## Bottom line

Grit.io is a good example of an AI-adjacent developer tool succeeding on its technical merits even after its business model didn't survive as an independent company. Honeycomb's acquisition ended Grit.io as a standalone startup, and rather than let GritQL quietly rot as an orphaned product, its creator donated the code and joined Biome's maintainer team — arguably a better outcome than a slow wind-down. If you need a declarative code search-and-transform language today, GritQL under Biome is alive and worth learning. If you were hoping to buy a supported Grit.io subscription, confirm current status with Honeycomb before assuming it's still for sale.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Grit.io still an active company?**
No, not as an independent business. Honeycomb acquired Grit earlier in 2025, and its core open-source technology, GritQL, was subsequently donated to the Biome organization in December 2025.

**Is GritQL still maintained?**
Yes — GritQL is now maintained inside the Biome organization's GitHub (`biomejs/gritql`), with Grit.io's creator, Morgante Pell, having joined Biome's maintainer team directly.

**Is GritQL free to use?**
Yes, GritQL itself is open source and free. Whatever paid tiers the original Grit.io hosted platform offered are not currently confirmed as available for purchase.

**Can I still use Grit.io's old pattern library and CLI?**
Yes — documentation, CLI, playground, and pattern library remain publicly reachable through Grit.io's documentation domain, though the main marketing site now redirects there rather than to a product signup page.

**What's the difference between GritQL and tools like jscodeshift?**
jscodeshift requires you to write JavaScript that manipulates an AST directly. GritQL instead lets you describe the pattern you want to match and transform declaratively, which most developers find faster to learn for common migration tasks, though jscodeshift offers more low-level control for unusual transformations.

**Who should learn GritQL today?**
Developers already using or planning to use Biome for JS/TS tooling, and anyone doing large-scale structural code migrations who wants a free, open-source, actively-maintained pattern-matching language rather than a paid commercial platform.

For more currently active developer tools and AI software coverage, browse our [AI & software deals](/category/software) roundup.

title: Social Champ Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Social Champ review covering per-profile pricing, AI caption and image tools, social listening, and who this scheduler actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Social Champ worth it in 2026?

Social Champ is a solid pick if you manage several client accounts and want per-profile pricing instead of a flat seat fee, since its Growth and Standard tiers scale cheaply with account count. It's less compelling if you just need lightweight scheduling for one or two personal accounts — a free tool or [Publer](/blog/publer-review) covers that with less setup.

## At a glance

| | Social Champ |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $5/account/month (Starter, billed monthly) |
| Free tier | Yes — 3 accounts, 15 scheduled posts, 3 lifetime AI credits |
| Best for | Agencies and teams managing multiple client accounts |
| Standout feature | Per-profile pricing + built-in social listening on the Growth tier |

## What Social Champ actually is

Social Champ is a cloud-based social media management platform aimed at agencies, marketing teams, and multi-brand businesses. It covers the core loop most scheduling tools do — plan, publish, and report — across a dozen-plus networks, but its pricing structure and feature set lean noticeably toward agencies running several client accounts from one dashboard rather than a single creator managing one brand voice.

The platform doesn't publicly name a single foundation model; its "Champ AI Suite" covers captioning, hashtag suggestions, an AI image generator called Imaginator, and sentiment analysis for social listening, drawing on third-party AI infrastructure the way most scheduling tools do. Social Champ holds Meta Business Partner, AWS Partner Network, and TikTok Marketing Partner status, a reasonable proxy for platform-integration maturity.

Supported networks include Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, TikTok, YouTube, Google Business Profile, Threads, Mastodon, Bluesky, and WhatsApp Business, plus review management for Google Play, the App Store, and G2 — broader reach than most schedulers bother with, and one reason agencies with varied client rosters gravitate toward it.

## Pricing

Social Champ splits its plans into two structures: pay-per-profile plans (Starter, Growth) priced per connected social account, and flat-rate plans (Standard, Professional, Agency, Enterprise) priced per bundle of accounts and users. That's a genuinely different model from most competitors in this space, which almost universally price by user seat count.

| Plan | Monthly price | Accounts | Users | AI credits/month | Notable inclusions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 3 | 1 | 3 (lifetime) | Basic scheduling, analytics, social inbox |
| Starter | $5/account ($4/account yearly) | Per account | 1 | 5 | Unlimited scheduling, social inbox |
| Growth | $9/account ($8/account yearly) | Per account | Unlimited | Higher tier | Social listening, competitor analysis, advanced analytics |
| Standard | $29 ($23.20/mo yearly) | 6 | 2 | 50 | Bulk scheduling, basic approval workflow |
| Professional | $59 ($47.20/mo yearly) | 12 | 5 | Higher tier | Client management, multi-layer approvals, WhatsApp integration |
| Agency | $149 ($119.20/mo yearly) | 30 | Unlimited | Unlimited | White-label reports, API access, social listening included |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom | Dedicated account manager, SSO, Salesforce/HubSpot integrations |

The free plan is genuinely usable for testing the interface, but its 15-post scheduling cap and 3 lifetime (not monthly) AI credits make it a trial more than a daily driver. Annual billing knocks roughly 20% off every paid tier.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on Social Champ's own pricing page before subscribing, especially the AI credit allotments, which vendors tend to adjust more often than base prices.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Per-profile pricing that scales down for small client rosters.** Most competitors charge per user seat regardless of how many accounts that user manages, penalizing solo agency owners running ten client profiles under one login. Social Champ's Starter and Growth tiers charge per connected account instead, which can be cheaper for a one-person shop juggling many small clients — though it flips for a large team managing few accounts, where flat-rate plans win.

**Social listening and competitor analysis bundled into a mid-tier plan.** Growth ($9/account) and Agency ($149 flat) both include social listening and competitor tracking without an extra add-on fee. Many scheduling tools reserve this for a separate, pricier product tier or don't offer it at all — SocialDude and Robopost, for instance, focus their AI budget on content generation rather than listening.

**Champ AI Suite covers both text and image generation.** Beyond caption and hashtag writing, Social Champ's Imaginator tool generates images from prompts inside the same workflow, so a user doesn't need to round-trip through a separate design tool for every post that needs custom visuals — though the credit-based system means heavy image generation eats into the same monthly allowance as captions.

**Client workspace isolation and white-label reporting.** Professional and above support separate client workspaces with role-based access, and Agency adds fully white-labeled PDF/PPT/CSV reports. For an agency billing clients on retainer, being able to hand over a branded report without a Social Champ watermark is a meaningful differentiator against tools that only offer generic exports.

**Broader-than-average platform coverage, including WhatsApp Business.** WhatsApp integration (Professional tier and up) and review management across Google Play, the App Store, and G2 are unusual inclusions for a scheduling tool — most competitors stop at the standard six or seven major social networks.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo agency owners or freelancers managing many small client accounts** get the most value from Starter/Growth pay-per-profile pricing, since cost tracks account count rather than forcing a jump to a multi-seat flat plan.
- **Small-to-mid agencies running client campaigns** fit the Professional tier well — client workspaces, approval workflows, and WhatsApp support target exactly this use case.
- **Larger agencies needing white-label client reporting** should look at Agency, where reports drop the Social Champ branding and API access opens up custom integrations.
- **Enterprises with existing Salesforce/HubSpot stacks and compliance requirements** are the target for the custom Enterprise tier, which adds SSO and a dedicated account manager.
- **Solo creators or single-brand small businesses** are probably better served by a simpler, cheaper scheduler — Social Champ's agency-oriented feature set (client workspaces, competitor analysis) is overhead they won't use.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Per-profile pricing can undercut seat-based competitors for lean teams with many accounts | AI credits are metered even on paid plans, so heavy AI users can hit limits |
| Social listening and competitor analysis included well below enterprise pricing | Free plan's 3 lifetime AI credits (not monthly) make it a short trial, not ongoing use |
| Broad platform coverage including WhatsApp Business and review management | Two separate pricing structures (per-profile vs. flat-rate) take a minute to parse |
| White-label reporting and client workspaces built for agency workflows | Advanced approval workflows and API access are gated to upper tiers |
| Annual billing saves roughly 20% across all paid plans | No independently published benchmark on AI caption/image quality vs. rivals |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Social Champ connects to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Flickr, Imgur, Canva, and Giphy for asset sourcing, plus Bitly for link shortening. Salesforce and HubSpot integrations are positioned as Enterprise-tier features rather than available broadly. API access starts at the Agency plan, useful if you want to pipe scheduling or reporting data into an internal tool. There's no public Zapier listing confirmed at the time of writing — verify that specific integration with Social Champ support before subscribing if it matters for your workflow.

## Where it's a strong fit

Social Champ earns its keep for agencies and multi-account operators where cost needs to track account count, not headcount. Bundled social listening and competitor analysis on a mid-tier plan is genuinely useful for teams that would otherwise pay extra for a separate listening tool, and the client workspace/white-label reporting combo on Professional and Agency tiers is built around agency billing cycles rather than bolted on as an afterthought.

## Where to think twice

If you need a fully free, unlimited scheduler for one personal account, Social Champ's free tier caps out fast at 15 scheduled posts and a one-time AI credit allowance — you'll outgrow it within a week of regular posting. Teams needing heavy day-to-day AI content generation should budget carefully, since credits are metered even on paid tiers and there's no unlimited AI plan below Enterprise. If your organization specifically needs SOC 2 documentation or a named compliance certification before adopting a new SaaS vendor, that wasn't confirmed on Social Champ's public pages as of this review — get written confirmation from their sales team rather than assume it, since Enterprise language (SSO, dedicated account manager) implies compliance readiness without naming a certification.

## Bottom line

Social Champ's real edge is its pricing shape, not a single killer AI feature — per-profile billing on lower tiers and bundled social listening on mid tiers solve a specific problem (agencies with lots of small accounts and little appetite for enterprise pricing) that flat seat-based competitors don't address as directly. If that's your situation, trial the free plan and move to Growth or Professional once you outgrow it. If you're a solo creator managing one account, the agency-oriented feature set is more tool than you need, and a lighter scheduler will save you money without the learning curve.

## FAQ

**Is Social Champ free?**
There's a free plan covering 3 social accounts, 15 scheduled posts, and 3 lifetime AI credits, but it's better suited to testing the platform than to ongoing daily use given those limits.

**How much does Social Champ cost per month?**
Paid plans start at $5 per connected account on the Starter tier (pay-per-profile), or $29 flat for 6 accounts on the Standard tier. Annual billing cuts roughly 20% off either structure.

**Does Social Champ use AI to write captions?**
Yes, its Champ AI Suite generates captions, hashtags, and images (via the Imaginator tool), plus sentiment analysis for social listening. AI use is credit-metered, with allotments ranging from 5 credits/month on Starter up to unlimited on Enterprise.

**What social networks does Social Champ support?**
Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, TikTok, YouTube, Google Business Profile, Threads, Mastodon, Bluesky, and WhatsApp Business, along with review management for Google Play, the App Store, and G2.

**Is Social Champ good for agencies?**
It's built with agencies in mind — client workspace isolation, white-label reporting, multi-layer approval workflows, and per-profile pricing all target agency operations specifically, more so than most competing schedulers.

**How does Social Champ's pricing compare to competitors?**
Its per-profile pricing on lower tiers is unusual — most competitors like Publer or Robopost AI price primarily by user seats. That makes Social Champ potentially cheaper for solo operators managing many accounts, and potentially pricier for large teams managing few accounts, so run the math against your specific account-to-user ratio.

**Does Social Champ offer social listening?**
Yes, starting on the Growth (per-profile) tier and included in the Agency flat-rate plan, alongside competitor analysis — features many scheduling tools charge extra for or omit entirely.

**Is Social Champ beginner-friendly?**
The core scheduling and calendar interface is straightforward, but the two parallel pricing structures (per-profile vs. flat-rate) and tiered AI credit system take a bit of upfront reading to fully understand before choosing a plan.

For more tools in this category, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub, and compare against our [Publer review](/blog/publer-review), [Robopost AI review](/blog/robopost-ai-review), and [SocialDude review](/blog/socialdude-review) if you're still shopping around.

title: Originality AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is Originality AI worth it in 2026? A hands-on look at its credit pricing, combined AI/plagiarism detection, and who it's actually built for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Originality AI worth it in 2026?

Originality AI is a credit-based AI detector and plagiarism checker built for publishers, agencies, and content teams rather than solo writers or classrooms. It's strong on team workflows, bulk scanning, and combining AI detection with plagiarism and fact-checking in one dashboard, but its per-scan credit pricing and enterprise focus make it overkill if you just need an occasional gut-check on a paragraph.

### At a glance

| | Originality AI |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $14.95/month billed monthly ($12.95/month billed annually), Pro plan |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — 3 free scans per day (up to 2,000 words each) with no account required, AI detection only |
| Best for | Content agencies, publishers, and SEO teams vetting submitted or purchased content at scale |
| Standout feature | Combined AI detection + plagiarism + fact-check + readability scoring in a single credit-based scan, with team seats and API access |

## What Originality AI actually is

Originality AI is a Canada-based SaaS tool built specifically for people who buy or manage content at volume — content agencies, publishers, and SEO teams who need to verify that freelance or in-house writing is original and not AI-generated before it goes live. That's a narrower audience than a classroom-focused tool, and the product is built around it: credits, team seats, tagging, and scan history are core features, not add-ons.

Under the hood, Originality AI says its detector is built on a modified BERT-based classification model, trained on what it calls adversarial data specifically to catch paraphrased or "humanized" AI text, not just raw model output. The company holds a U.S. patent covering its text-analysis approach and states its multilingual model scores 97.8% accuracy across roughly 30 languages, citing internal and third-party testing. Treat that figure as a vendor claim rather than an independently reproduced benchmark — no detector on the market publishes fully open, third-party-audited accuracy numbers that hold up across every writing style and evasion technique, and Originality AI is no exception.

The tool detects text associated with major large language model families (OpenAI's GPT models, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini, and others), though the exact list of models it's tuned to recognize shifts as new ones ship — Originality AI updates its detection models on a rolling basis rather than locking to a fixed list.

## Pricing

Originality AI runs on a credit system: 1 credit covers roughly 100 words of AI detection, and heavier features (plagiarism, fact-check) consume credits at different rates depending on the scan.

| Plan | Price | Credits | What's included |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic (Free) | $0 | 60 credits/month (3 scans/day) | AI detection only, 2,000-word scan limit, no account required |
| Pro | $14.95/mo monthly, $12.95/mo billed annually | 2,000 credits/month | AI + plagiarism + fact-check + readability + grammar, Chrome extension, file uploads, website scanning, team tagging, 30-day scan history |
| Enterprise | $179/mo monthly, ~$136.58/mo billed annually | 15,000 credits/month | Everything in Pro, plus API access, 365-day scan history, dedicated success manager, priority (1-hour) support |

Extra team seats run roughly $8.62–$9.95/month on Pro and $19.04–$24.95/month on Enterprise. Purchased (top-up) credits don't expire for two years; monthly subscription credits reset and don't roll over. There's no traditional free trial of the paid plans — instead, the free Basic tier lets you run three no-signup scans a day indefinitely, which is a reasonable way to test detection quality before paying.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI tool pricing moves fast, so confirm current numbers on [Originality AI's pricing page](https://originality.ai/pricing) before subscribing.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Credit-based bulk scanning.** Unlike detectors billed per seat or on a flat monthly scan cap, Originality AI's credit model lets an agency scan a huge batch of freelance submissions in one go and see exactly how many credits each article consumed, which is more predictable for teams managing content at scale than a hard "X scans per month" ceiling.

**Combined AI detection and plagiarism in one report.** Most competitors treat AI detection and plagiarism checking as separate tools or separate passes. Originality AI runs both from the same scan and shows the results side by side, which matters for a publisher's real workflow: you don't just need to know if a paragraph was AI-written, you need to know if it was also lifted from somewhere else.

**Fact-checker.** Originality AI includes a fact-checking pass that flags claims in a document for verification, aimed at editorial teams worried about AI-generated hallucinated facts slipping into published content. It's a claim-flagging aid, not an automated truth oracle — it still requires a human to confirm or reject each flagged claim.

**Team management and tagging.** Pro and Enterprise plans include multi-seat team accounts, scan tagging, and shared history, letting an editorial lead see every writer's submission history and originality scores in one place.

**Chrome extension and website scanning.** Beyond pasting text, Originality AI can scan a live webpage or run inside the browser via its Chrome extension, useful for checking already-published content without copying text out of a CMS first.

## Who it's actually for

**Solo bloggers or students** are better served by the free Basic tier for the occasional spot-check, or by a cheaper single-purpose tool — Pro and Enterprise are priced and packaged for teams, not individuals doing a handful of checks a month.

**Content agencies and SEO teams** managing freelance writers at volume are the clearest fit for Pro: the combined AI + plagiarism scan, tagging, and per-writer history solve a real operational problem — verifying dozens or hundreds of submissions without juggling two separate tools.

**Publishers and enterprise editorial teams** that need API access to plug detection into an existing CMS or submission pipeline, longer scan history for audit purposes, or dedicated support will want Enterprise, where the per-credit cost drops meaningfully at volume.

**Educators and academic institutions** can use Originality AI, but it isn't built around classroom-specific workflows (LMS integrations, gradebook-style reporting) the way some competitors are — worth comparing against a detector marketed specifically to schools before committing budget here.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Combines AI detection, plagiarism, and fact-checking in one scan | Credit-based pricing is harder to predict for irregular usage than a flat monthly cap |
| Free daily scans with no signup required | No traditional free trial of paid plan features |
| Strong team/agency workflow tools (tagging, seats, shared history) | Enterprise tier is priced well above casual or small-team budgets |
| API access on Enterprise for pipeline integration | Detection accuracy claims are vendor-reported, not independently audited |
| Chrome extension and live website scanning | Heavily paraphrased or "humanized" AI text can still evade detection, as with any detector |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Originality AI offers a Chrome browser extension for in-page scanning, file upload support (including PDFs), and website URL scanning for already-published pages. API access is available on the Enterprise plan for teams that want to run detection automatically as part of a content submission or publishing pipeline — flagging a draft before it moves from "in review" to "published," for example. It doesn't publish a large app marketplace or native Zapier/Slack integrations the way some broader SaaS platforms do; integration beyond the browser extension currently runs through the API.

## Where it's a strong fit

If you're running a content agency or in-house editorial team that buys freelance writing at any real volume, Originality AI's combination of AI detection, plagiarism checking, and per-writer tagging solves a workflow problem that using two or three separate free tools doesn't. The free daily scans also make it easy to sanity-check the tool's output before paying for anything.

It's also a reasonable fit for publishers who want one report that covers both "is this AI-written" and "is this plagiarized" without asking a freelancer to run two separate checkers.

## Where to think twice

If you only need to check a handful of documents a month, the credit system and Pro-tier pricing are more than you need — stick to the free Basic tier or a simpler single-purpose detector. If you need a fully free, unlimited tool with no scan cap, Originality AI isn't it; the free tier caps at 60 credits a month. If your institution specifically needs SOC 2 or formal compliance documentation, or LMS-native grading integrations, confirm those specifics directly with sales rather than assuming Enterprise covers them — the public pricing page doesn't list SOC 2 certification. And like every AI detector on the market, don't treat a score from Originality AI as definitive proof in a dispute with a student, employee, or contractor — false positives and false negatives both happen, and heavily edited "humanized" AI text is a known blind spot across this entire product category.

## Bottom line

Originality AI is one of the more workflow-complete AI detectors available for teams that manage content at scale — the combined AI/plagiarism/fact-check scan, credit-based bulk pricing, and team tagging are built for agencies and publishers, not casual single-document checks. If that's your use case, it's worth trialing against the free tier before committing to Pro or Enterprise. If you just need to spot-check the occasional essay or blog draft, the free Basic plan (or a cheaper, simpler competitor) will likely cover it without the credit-tracking overhead.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Originality AI free?**
There's a free Basic tier offering 3 scans per day (up to 2,000 words each), AI detection only, no account required. Plagiarism, fact-checking, and team features require a paid plan.

**How much does Originality AI cost?**
Pro starts at $14.95/month billed monthly, or $12.95/month billed annually. Enterprise starts at $179/month billed monthly, or roughly $136.58/month billed annually, with more credits and API access.

**How accurate is Originality AI's detection?**
Originality AI states its multilingual model reaches 97.8% accuracy across about 30 languages, based on its own and third-party testing. Treat that as a vendor-reported figure — false positives and false negatives are possible, especially with heavily edited or paraphrased AI content.

**Does Originality AI check for plagiarism too?**
Yes. Pro and Enterprise plans include a plagiarism scan alongside AI detection and fact-checking in the same report — one of the tool's main differentiators from single-purpose detectors.

**Can Originality AI detect content from any AI model?**
It's tuned to detect output from major model families including OpenAI's GPT models, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini, with detection models updated on a rolling basis. No detector guarantees coverage of every model or evasion technique.

**Is Originality AI good for teachers checking student essays?**
It can be used that way, but it isn't purpose-built for classroom workflows the way some education-focused detectors are — no gradebook or LMS-native integration. Agencies and publishers are the more natural fit.

**Does credit usage roll over each month?**
Subscription credits reset each billing cycle and don't roll over. Separately purchased credit top-ups don't expire for two years, per Originality AI's stated policy — confirm current terms on the pricing page since credit policies can change.

**What are the main alternatives to Originality AI?**
Other AI content detectors worth comparing include [GPTZero](/blog/gptzero-review), [Winston AI](/blog/winston-ai-review), [Copyleaks](/blog/copyleaks-review), and [ZeroGPT](/blog/zerogpt-review) — each targets a slightly different audience, so the right pick depends on your workflow, not accuracy claims alone.

Looking for discounts on tools like this one? Check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers across AI and SaaS products.

title: HitPaw Review 2026: AI Video Suite Pricing and Verdict
excerpt: HitPaw offers AI video upscaling, editing and object removal tools sold app-by-app. Here is what it costs and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## HitPaw Review 2026: Is the AI Media Suite Worth It?

HitPaw is a suite of separate AI-powered video, photo and audio apps — not one unified product — built around upscaling, enhancement, object removal and AI video creation. It's a solid pick if you need a specific fix like video upscaling or background removal, but the fragmented app-by-app pricing means it's rarely the cheapest option if you need more than one tool.

### At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Made by | HitPaw (media enhancement software company) |
| Best for | Creators needing a specific fix: upscaling, object removal, or quick AI video edits |
| Starting price | Free trial (preview only); paid plans start around $43.19/month per app |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — preview AI results, but exports are typically limited/watermarked until purchase |
| Standout feature | AI video upscaling up to 8K with denoising, deblurring and colorization |

## What HitPaw actually is

HitPaw isn't one app — it's a portfolio of desktop and mobile tools sold under the HitPaw brand, each targeting a different job. The two most relevant to most shoppers are **HitPaw VikPea** (AI video enhancer/upscaler) and **HitPaw Edimakor** (a fuller AI video editing suite with text-to-video, AI avatars, voice cloning and auto-subtitles). Beyond those, the lineup includes HitPaw FotorPea (photo enhancer), a video/photo object remover, HitPaw Univd (video converter), HitPaw VoicePea (real-time voice changer), an AI audio enhancer, and an AI music generator (Oyamuse).

This matters more than it sounds — because unlike an all-in-one suite from a single vendor with one subscription (think Adobe Creative Cloud), HitPaw generally sells **each app on its own license**. If you need both video upscaling and AI video editing, you're likely buying two separate products with two separate bills, not one plan that covers everything. That's the single biggest thing to understand before comparing HitPaw's pricing to a competitor that bundles more into one subscription.

## Pricing (using HitPaw VikPea as the example)

HitPaw's flagship AI video enhancer, VikPea, is representative of how the company prices most of its desktop apps: a monthly subscription, a discounted annual plan, and a one-time perpetual license, plus separate team tiers.

| Plan | Price | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly | $43.19/month | Full AI enhancement access, 100 bonus credits, auto-renews |
| Yearly | $99.99/year (list $124.99) | Full access, 500 bonus credits, auto-renews |
| Perpetual license | $350.39 (list $437.99) | One-time purchase, no renewal, 800 bonus credits |
| Team — 5 PCs | $459.95/year | Multi-seat licensing for small teams |
| Team — 10 PCs | $859.95/year | Multi-seat licensing |
| Team — 100 PCs | $1,099.95/year | Enterprise-scale seat licensing |

HitPaw Edimakor is priced separately and runs on a **free-download-plus-credits** model: the base app is free with non-AI editing tools, and new users get 30 free AI credits to test features like text-to-video, voice cloning or auto-subtitles before deciding whether to upgrade to a paid credit or subscription tier.

Pricing, free-tier limits and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI tool pricing shifts often, so confirm current numbers on HitPaw's own pricing pages before buying, especially since HitPaw frequently runs "up to 35% off" promotional pricing that changes the effective cost shown at checkout.

## Core features that actually differentiate HitPaw

**AI video upscaling to 8K.** VikPea's main selling point is taking low-resolution or old footage and upscaling it with AI models trained for denoising, deblurring, frame interpolation and colorization. HitPaw states this can push footage up to 8K resolution — useful for restoring old family videos or salvaging usable footage shot on older phones or cameras, though how convincing the result looks depends heavily on how degraded the source footage was to begin with.

**Object removal without manual masking.** Both the video and photo object removers use AI to detect and remove unwanted elements (a passerby, a watermark, a stray object) from footage or images without the user manually tracing a selection mask frame by frame, which is normally the slowest part of object removal in traditional editors.

**Text-to-video and AI avatars in Edimakor.** Edimakor goes well beyond enhancement into actual content generation — turning a text prompt or a still image into a short video, generating AI avatars with lip-sync, and cloning voices across 35+ languages according to HitPaw's own product pages. This puts Edimakor in more direct competition with dedicated AI video generators than with a simple editor.

**Auto-subtitle and vocal-removal tools.** Edimakor also bundles auto-generated subtitles and audio-track separation (isolating or removing vocals), which are useful for repurposing long-form video into social clips without manually transcribing or re-editing the audio.

**A genuinely large creative asset library.** Edimakor ships with a claimed 1,000+ effects, 500+ filters, 1,000+ text animations, 200+ transitions and 50,000+ stock media files — a much deeper stock-asset library than most standalone AI enhancers bother including, which matters if you're building finished social content rather than just fixing a single clip.

## Who HitPaw is actually for

- **Solo creators salvaging old or low-quality footage** — VikPea's upscaling and denoising is a narrow but genuinely useful fix if you have specific damaged or low-res clips to restore, and the perpetual license can make sense if you'll reuse it repeatedly rather than pay monthly.
- **Social content creators repurposing long videos** — Edimakor's auto-subtitle, clip-maker and text-to-video tools fit creators turning podcasts or long-form video into short-form social clips, especially since the free tier plus 30 AI credits lets you test the workflow before paying.
- **Small teams needing a handful of licensed seats** — the 5/10/100-PC team tiers on VikPea suit small production or marketing teams needing the same enhancement tool on multiple machines.
- **Enterprise teams needing compliance guarantees** — less of a fit; HitPaw doesn't publicly advertise SOC 2 or similar certifications, so confirm this directly with HitPaw's sales team rather than assume it.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Strong, focused AI upscaling and enhancement results for a narrow use case | Each app is a separate purchase — no single subscription covers the whole suite |
| Free trial/free-credit model lets you test results before paying | Credit-based free tiers on tools like Edimakor run out quickly with AI-heavy features |
| Perpetual license option avoids ongoing subscription fatigue on VikPea | Monthly pricing ($43.19) is steep relative to more general-purpose AI video tools |
| Deep asset library in Edimakor for content creators | Desktop-first — some tools have lighter mobile support than desktop |
| Frequent "up to 35% off" promotions can meaningfully lower cost | Marketing language ("cutting-edge AI," 8K claims) isn't independently benchmarked, so results vary by source footage |

## Integrations and ecosystem

HitPaw's tools are primarily standalone desktop applications (Windows/Mac) with companion mobile apps for some products (VikPea and FotorPea both have mobile versions; AI Marvels is mobile-only). There isn't a public API for third-party developers, and HitPaw doesn't advertise Zapier, Slack or project-management integrations — these are consumer/creator tools you use directly rather than plug into a larger stack. If workflow automation or API access matters to you, confirm directly with HitPaw rather than assuming it exists.

## Where HitPaw is a strong fit

If your need is narrow and specific — restore a batch of old, low-quality video clips, remove an object from footage without manual masking, or quickly generate auto-subtitles for a set of social clips — HitPaw's dedicated tools do that one job with less friction than a general-purpose editor treating AI enhancement as a secondary feature. The free trial and free-credit models make it low-risk to confirm results on your own footage before paying.

## Where to think twice

Think twice if you need **one subscription covering video editing, upscaling and audio work together** — HitPaw's app-by-app pricing adds up fast if you need more than one tool, so compare that combined cost against an all-in-one creative suite first. Also think twice if you need a **fully free tool with no credit limits** (Edimakor's 30 free AI credits burn through quickly on AI-heavy features like text-to-video), if your organization needs **documented enterprise compliance** (SOC 2, HIPAA, etc. aren't publicly listed), or if you need **guaranteed benchmark-level upscaling quality** — HitPaw's 8K and enhancement claims come from its own marketing copy rather than independent benchmarks, so test on your own footage first.

## The bottom line

HitPaw is best understood as a toolbox of narrow, purpose-built AI apps rather than a single competitor to an all-in-one creative suite. VikPea's AI upscaling and Edimakor's content-generation features are genuinely capable for what they target, and the free trial/credit system means you can validate results on your own footage before paying anything. But because each app is billed separately — and VikPea's standalone pricing runs $99.99–$350.39/year depending on plan — it's worth mapping out exactly which HitPaw tools you'd actually use before buying, rather than assuming one purchase covers the whole suite.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is HitPaw free to use?**
HitPaw offers free trials and free-credit models depending on the app — VikPea offers an unlimited-time preview trial (results aren't exportable without limits until purchase), and Edimakor is free to download with core non-AI editing tools plus 30 free AI credits. Full AI features generally require a paid plan.

**How much does HitPaw cost?**
It varies by app. HitPaw VikPea runs $43.19/month, $99.99/year, or $350.39 as a one-time perpetual license (list prices before HitPaw's frequent discount promotions). Other apps like Edimakor use their own separate credit-based or subscription pricing, so total cost depends on which tools you need.

**Is HitPaw one product or several?**
Several. HitPaw is an umbrella brand for a set of separate apps — video enhancer (VikPea), video editor (Edimakor), photo enhancer (FotorPea), object removers, a video converter (Univd), a voice changer (VoicePea) and more — each generally sold and licensed on its own.

**Does HitPaw store or use my video/photo data to train its AI?**
HitPaw doesn't publish detailed public data-handling documentation comparable to larger enterprise AI vendors. If data privacy for sensitive footage is a concern, review HitPaw's specific privacy policy for the app you're using before uploading anything sensitive.

**What's a good alternative to HitPaw?**
Alternatives range from general AI video editors and dedicated upscaling tools to full creative suites bundling editing, enhancement and audio into one subscription. Compare total cost across the specific tools you'd actually use, since HitPaw's per-app pricing can end up costing more than a bundled competitor if you need multiple capabilities.

**Is HitPaw beginner-friendly?**
Yes, most HitPaw apps are built around simple drag-and-drop workflows aimed at non-professionals — you generally don't need video-editing experience to use the AI enhancement or object-removal tools. Edimakor's more advanced generation features (AI avatars, voice cloning) have a slightly steeper learning curve than the enhancement tools.

**Can I cancel a HitPaw subscription anytime?**
HitPaw's monthly and yearly plans are described as auto-renewing subscriptions you can cancel to stop future billing; the perpetual license on VikPea is a one-time purchase with no recurring billing to cancel. Confirm the specific cancellation process and any refund window (HitPaw advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee on some plans) directly on HitPaw's purchase page before buying.

**Does HitPaw work on both Windows and Mac?**
Most core HitPaw desktop apps, including VikPea and Edimakor, support both Windows and Mac, with some tools also offering mobile versions. Always confirm OS compatibility and version requirements on the specific product page before purchasing, since feature parity between Windows, Mac and mobile versions isn't always identical.

title: vidyo.ai Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: vidyo.ai (now Quso.ai) turns long video into clips with built-in multi-platform scheduling. Pricing, features, and honest verdict.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is vidyo.ai (now Quso.ai) worth it for short-form video repurposing?

Vidyo.ai rebranded to Quso.ai in 2024, and the two names are still used interchangeably in search. It's worth it if you want one platform that turns long recordings into clips, adds captions, and then schedules and publishes those clips across six or more social platforms; it's less compelling if you only need a lightweight clipper without publishing tools, since simpler competitors charge less for clipping alone.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $29/month (Lite plan, monthly billing; $19/month billed annually) |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — 75 credits/month, 720p exports, no card required to start |
| Best for | Podcasters, streamers, and agencies repurposing long-form video into multi-platform clips |
| Standout feature | Built-in scheduling and publishing to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Pinterest from one dashboard |

## What vidyo.ai actually is

Vidyo.ai launched as a standalone AI clipping tool aimed at podcasters and streamers who needed to turn hour-long recordings into short, social-ready clips. In 2024 the product rebranded to **Quso.ai**, and the vidyo.ai domain now redirects there — the underlying product and account system are the same, just under a new name and a broader feature set. Anyone searching "vidyo.ai" today lands on Quso.ai's site, so this review covers the product as it exists now, while noting the history since a lot of search traffic still uses the old name.

The company doesn't publicly disclose which specific AI models power its clip-scoring or transcription. Quso.ai says it serves around 4 million creators, podcasters, agencies, and businesses — a figure from the company's own marketing rather than an independently audited number.

Unlike a pure clipping tool, Quso.ai positions itself as an end-to-end repurposing and distribution platform: upload once, get multiple clips in multiple aspect ratios, and publish them without leaving the app. That's the core thing separating it from narrower faceless-video generators.

## Pricing

| Plan | Monthly price | Annual price | Credits | Key inclusions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | $0 | 75/month | 720p exports, chapters & short clips, TikTok publishing, CutMagic auto-editing, 7-day data retention |
| Lite | $29/month | $19/month (billed yearly) | 100/month (200 on annual billing) | Unlimited 1080p clips, desktop-grade editor, scheduling to 6 platforms, multiple export ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), 10GB storage |
| Essential | $39/month | $26/month (billed yearly) | 300/month (600 on annual billing) | Everything in Lite plus AI filler/silence removal, external content import, Content Planner, 25GB storage |
| Growth | $49/month | $33/month (billed yearly) | 600/month (1,200 on annual billing) | Everything in Essential plus custom brand kit and templates, Viddy AI content assistant, priority access to new features, social analytics, priority support, 75GB storage |

One credit is roughly equal to one minute of processed video, so usable capacity per month depends heavily on how long your source recordings are and how many clips you generate from each. A 60-minute podcast episode can eat through a meaningful chunk of a Lite plan's monthly allotment across multiple passes.

Annual billing cuts the effective monthly price by roughly a third and also doubles the credit allowance versus monthly billing — worth factoring in for regular publishers. All plans are billed month-to-month and cancellable anytime, per the pricing page.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tool pricing and feature sets move fast, so confirm current numbers on Quso.ai's own pricing page before subscribing.

## Core features walkthrough

**AI clip detection and virality scoring.** The AI Clips Generator scans a long upload and flags moments it scores as most likely to perform well as standalone shorts, so you're not scrubbing through an hour of footage manually. Quso.ai describes this as scoring based on engagement signals like pacing and hook strength — treat the "virality score" as the vendor's own framing rather than a guaranteed outcome, since no tool can reliably predict what an algorithm will boost.

**Word-level animated captions in 100+ languages.** Captions are generated automatically with filler-word detection built in, and styling is adjustable rather than fixed to one template. This is table stakes for the category now, but the language coverage is broader than some competitors.

**Vertical reframing and multi-format export.** A single clip can be exported in 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 simultaneously, with the AI repositioning the frame to keep speakers centered rather than just cropping the edges off a horizontal source.

**Built-in scheduling and publishing.** This is the feature that most separates Quso.ai from a narrower clipping tool: once clips are ready, you can schedule and publish them directly to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Pinterest from the same dashboard, with a content calendar and basic social analytics on the Growth plan. Most competing clippers stop at export and leave publishing to a separate scheduling tool.

**Text-based editing and silence/filler removal.** On Essential and above, you can edit a video by editing its transcript — cut a sentence from the text and the corresponding video segment is removed — plus automatic silence and filler-word trimming, which speeds up cleanup on unscripted podcast or interview footage.

## Who it's actually for

**Solo podcasters and streamers.** The free tier (75 credits, 720p, TikTok publishing) is enough to test the clipping workflow on a couple of episodes before committing to a paid plan. The Lite plan at $19–29/month covers most solo creators who post a handful of clips per episode.

**Small content teams and agencies managing multiple client channels.** The Essential and Growth plans add the Content Planner, brand kits, and multi-platform scheduling that make sense once you're juggling several shows or client accounts rather than one personal channel — the built-in scheduler avoids paying for a separate tool like Buffer or Later on top of the clipping subscription.

**High-volume publishers with long source recordings.** If you're processing multiple hours of footage weekly, credit consumption on Lite or even Essential adds up quickly; Growth's 600–1,200 monthly credits and priority support are built for that volume, though run your own math against actual footage length before committing to the top tier.

**Not the best fit:** if you only need to generate faceless, script-based videos (no real footage to clip), a tool built specifically around script-to-video generation will likely serve you better than a repurposing platform designed around long-form source video.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Publishing and scheduling built in, not bolted on | Credit system can be confusing to estimate against your actual footage length |
| Multi-format export (16:9, 9:16, 1:1) from one upload | Free tier caps at 720p and 7-day data retention, which is short for archival use |
| Wide caption language coverage (100+ languages) | Entry paid tier ($29/month monthly) is pricier than some narrower clipping-only tools |
| Text-based editing speeds up cleanup on long interviews | Rebrand to Quso.ai can confuse users searching for "vidyo.ai" support or reviews |
| Imports from a long list of sources (YouTube, Zoom, Twitch, Drive, Dropbox, etc.) | Advanced brand-kit and analytics features are locked to the top Growth tier |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Quso.ai supports importing source video directly from YouTube, Vimeo, X, Facebook, Twitch, Rumble, Loom, LinkedIn, Zoom, Google Drive, and Dropbox, removing a manual download-and-reupload step some competitors still require. On the output side, native publishing connections cover TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Pinterest. There's no publicly documented Zapier integration or open API at the time of writing — if programmatic access matters, confirm current API availability directly with Quso.ai before subscribing.

## Where it's a strong fit

Quso.ai works well for anyone whose bottleneck is turning one long recording — a podcast, webinar, livestream, or interview — into several platform-ready shorts without hopping between a clipping tool, a caption tool, and a scheduling tool separately. The combination of AI clip detection, multi-ratio export, and native publishing in one subscription is genuinely useful for solo creators and small teams who don't want three separate tool bills.

It's also a reasonable fit for agencies managing several client channels, where the Content Planner and brand-kit features on the higher tiers help keep clients' content visually distinct without rebuilding templates from scratch each time.

## Where to think twice

The credit-based pricing takes some getting used to, and because one credit maps to roughly one minute of processed video, heavy users of long source material (two-hour-plus podcast episodes, for instance) should test the free tier's math against their real footage before assuming a mid-tier plan will cover a month's output.

Skip it if you need a fully free, unlimited clipping workflow — the free tier is capped at 75 credits and 720p, and every paid tier has a real monthly cost. Skip it too if you need on-premise or offline processing, since this is a cloud-only SaaS product with no local/offline mode documented. And if you're mainly generating faceless, avatar-driven videos from scripts rather than repurposing real recorded footage, a tool purpose-built for that workflow — such as [Crayo](/blog/crayo-review) — will likely map more directly to your use case than a long-to-short repurposing platform.

## Bottom line

Quso.ai (formerly vidyo.ai) earns its higher starting price by bundling clip generation, captioning, multi-format export, and native multi-platform publishing into one subscription — a combination that would otherwise require stitching together two or three separate tools. For podcasters, streamers, and small agencies who want to go from raw recording to scheduled posts without leaving one dashboard, that bundling is the actual value proposition, not just the clip quality itself. If you only need to extract clips and don't care about built-in scheduling, cheaper clipping-only tools like [SendShort](/blog/sendshort-review) may cover your needs for less.

## FAQ

**Is vidyo.ai still around, or has it shut down?**
It hasn't shut down — it rebranded to Quso.ai in 2024. The vidyo.ai domain redirects to quso.ai, and existing accounts carried over under the new name.

**How much does Quso.ai (vidyo.ai) cost?**
Paid plans start at $29/month billed monthly, or $19/month billed annually, for the Lite plan. Essential and Growth tiers run up to $49/month monthly ($33/month annual) with more credits and features.

**Is there a free plan?**
Yes. The free tier includes 75 credits per month, 720p exports, TikTok publishing, and basic AI clip generation, with 7-day data retention. No credit card required to sign up.

**What counts as a "credit" on Quso.ai?**
Roughly one credit equals one minute of processed video. Effective monthly capacity depends on how long your source recordings are and how many clips you generate per upload.

**Does it publish directly to social platforms, or just export clips?**
Both. Paid plans include scheduling and direct publishing to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Pinterest, in addition to standard clip export.

**How does it handle data privacy?**
The free tier notes 7-day data retention for uploads; paid tiers extend storage (10GB to 75GB depending on plan). Check Quso.ai's current privacy policy directly for specific data-handling terms, since these can change.

**Is it beginner-friendly?**
The core workflow is straightforward — upload, review AI-suggested clips, export. The text-based editor and Content Planner add depth for teams but aren't required for a basic clip.

**What are the main alternatives?**
[SendShort](/blog/sendshort-review) is a lighter, cheaper option focused mainly on clipping and captions rather than full publishing. [Crayo](/blog/crayo-review) is built for faceless, script-based video generation rather than repurposing existing footage — a different use case.

For more AI and software deals, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Cleanvoice AI Review 2026: Podcast Editing Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Cleanvoice AI auto-removes filler words, mouth sounds, and dead air from podcasts. Here's the real pricing, features, and who it's for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Cleanvoice AI worth it for cleaning up podcast audio?

Cleanvoice AI is worth it if you regularly edit multi-speaker podcast or video recordings and want filler words, mouth sounds, and dead air stripped out automatically before you touch a timeline. It's a paid, hour-based tool rather than a free one-off enhancer, and it's built for repeat editing workflows, not a single quick fix.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Made by | Cleanvoice AI (Germany-based) |
| Starting price | $11/month for 10 hours of processing (pay-as-you-go from $11 for 5 hours) |
| Free tier | 30 minutes of free processing, no credit card required |
| Best for | Podcasters and video editors doing recurring multi-track cleanup |
| Standout feature | Automatic filler word, stutter, and mouth-sound removal that exports as an editable timeline |

Cleanvoice AI sits in a narrower lane than a general voice enhancer. It isn't a recording studio or a hosting platform — it's a processing step that takes a rough recording (or a whole multitrack session) and hands back something close to an edited draft, plus a timeline file you can drop into your existing editor.

## What Cleanvoice AI actually is

Cleanvoice AI is an automated audio and video editing service aimed specifically at podcast production. Instead of recording, hosting, or generating audio, it takes files you already have — from an interview, a solo recording, or a full multitrack session — and automatically cuts out the parts editors normally trim by hand: "um," "uh," and other filler words, stutters and repeated words, mouth clicks and lip smacks, breaths, long silences, and background noise or hum.

The company doesn't publish which speech or noise-reduction models power the tool, so this review treats "AI-powered" as the vendor's own description rather than a verified model claim. What is verifiable is the output: Cleanvoice returns either a fully rendered, cleaned audio/video file, or an editable timeline file that opens in a real editor, so you can review and undo any individual cut rather than trusting a black-box render.

## Pricing

Cleanvoice AI is priced by processing hours, not by seat or by feature tier, which is a meaningfully different model from most AI writing or image tools. There are two purchasing paths: pay-as-you-go credit packs, and a monthly subscription that works out cheaper per hour.

| Plan | Price | Hours included | Effective rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 30 minutes (one-time, no card required) | — |
| Pay-as-you-go — Starter | $11 | 5 hours | ~$2.20/hour |
| Pay-as-you-go — Standard | $20 | 10 hours | ~$2.00/hour |
| Pay-as-you-go — Pro | $45 | 30 hours | ~$1.50/hour |
| Subscription — Basic | $11/month | 10 hours | ~$1.10/hour |
| Subscription — Growth | $30/month | 30 hours | ~$1.00/hour |
| Subscription — Scale | $90/month | 100 hours | ~$0.90/hour |
| Custom (200+ hours/month) | Contact sales | Custom | Includes API access and priority support |

Pay-as-you-go credits stay valid for two years, and unused monthly subscription hours roll over up to three times the plan's monthly allotment before expiring — a Growth subscriber who doesn't use all 30 hours can bank up to 90 hours before anything is lost. All tiers get the same feature set (filler removal, noise reduction, mouth sounds, transcription, and video editing) — Cleanvoice doesn't gate core cleanup features behind higher tiers. What you're paying for as you go up is volume and, at the custom tier, API access and support priority.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on Cleanvoice's own pricing page before buying, since AI-tool pricing shifts often.

## Core features walkthrough

**Filler word and disfluency removal.** This is the tool's headline capability: automatic detection and removal of "um," "uh," repeated words, and stutters, tuned specifically for spoken podcast content rather than generic transcription cleanup. It's the single biggest time-saver for anyone who edits conversational audio by hand today.

**Mouth sounds, breaths, and dead air.** Beyond filler words, Cleanvoice also strips lip smacks, clicks, breath sounds, and long silences — the small artifacts that make raw recordings sound unpolished even after the "ums" are gone. Combined, these two feature sets replace a big chunk of what a human audio editor would otherwise do manually pass by pass.

**Multitrack support.** For interview-style or panel podcasts recorded on separate tracks per speaker, Cleanvoice processes and keeps tracks in sync rather than requiring you to flatten to a single mixed file first — a detail that matters a lot for shows recorded with the usual one-mic-per-guest setup.

**Timeline export to real editors.** Rather than only handing back a rendered MP3 or WAV, Cleanvoice can export an editable project timeline that opens in Adobe Audition, DaVinci Resolve, REAPER, Audacity, or Ultraschall. That means the AI's cuts become a starting point you can review, adjust, or undo in your normal editing environment instead of a final, unchangeable output.

**Background noise and audio enhancement.** On top of dialogue editing, Cleanvoice applies noise, hum, and echo reduction and general enhancement aimed at a more consistent "studio" sound — useful for guest audio recorded on inconsistent home setups, though it's a cleanup pass rather than mastering or loudness normalization to a specific broadcast standard.

**API and developer access.** Cleanvoice publishes a REST API along with Python and JavaScript SDKs, which is what the custom/200+ hour tier is really selling — teams building cleanup into their own production pipeline (a podcast network's ingest system, for example) rather than using the web dashboard by hand.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo podcasters and interview shows on the free or Starter tier** get enough runway (30 free minutes, then $11 for 5 hours) to test whether automated cleanup saves real editing time before committing to a subscription.
- **Regular podcast producers editing multiple episodes a month** are the clearest fit for the subscription tiers — the $30/month Growth plan suits a weekly show with a co-host and occasional guests.
- **Podcast networks and agencies** processing 200+ hours a month are pushed toward the custom/API tier, where the value is pipeline integration rather than the dashboard.
- **Video podcasters** get the same cleanup applied to video files, a genuine differentiator from audio-only competitors, since cuts sync to picture rather than requiring a separate video pass.
- **One-off users editing a single recording** are better served by the free tier or a cheapest pay-as-you-go pack rather than a subscription they won't renew.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely saves manual editing time on filler words, mouth sounds, and dead air | Priced by processing hour, which can get expensive for high-volume shows without the subscription discount |
| Exports editable timelines instead of only a rendered file, so you keep control | No free ongoing tier beyond the initial 30-minute trial |
| Handles multitrack sessions and keeps speaker tracks in sync | Underlying AI model and accuracy figures aren't publicly documented |
| Same feature set at every paid tier — no feature gating by plan | Video support exists but the tool is clearly audio-first in its design and marketing |
| REST API and SDKs for teams building automated pipelines | Custom/API pricing isn't published — requires a sales conversation |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Cleanvoice's main integration story is on the output side: exported timelines open directly in Adobe Audition, DaVinci Resolve, REAPER, Audacity, and Ultraschall, so it slots into an existing editing workflow rather than trying to replace it. On the input side, it accepts uploads from local devices, Dropbox, Google Drive, or a direct link, plus a recording option. For teams that want cleanup baked into a larger pipeline, the REST API and Python/JavaScript SDKs let Cleanvoice's processing run unattended, a different usage pattern from the one-file-at-a-time dashboard most individual podcasters will use.

## Where it's a strong fit

Cleanvoice AI is a strong fit for interview and panel podcasts recorded on multiple tracks, where filler words, cross-talk mouth sounds, and dead air pile up across every speaker and manually editing all of it is genuinely tedious. It's also a good fit for shows that already edit in Audition, DaVinci Resolve, REAPER, Audacity, or Ultraschall and want an AI-assisted first pass that still leaves a reviewable, editable timeline. Teams processing high volumes of audio on a schedule get real value from the API tier once the manual dashboard workflow no longer scales.

## Where to think twice

Skip Cleanvoice AI if you need a fully free, ongoing solution — the 30-minute trial is a taste test, not a workflow, and every tier beyond it is metered by the hour. If your editing needs are closer to raw speech enhancement (turning a noisy phone recording into clear dialogue) rather than removing filler words and dead air, Adobe Podcast's free Enhance Speech feature covers that narrower job without a subscription — see our [Adobe Podcast review](/blog/adobe-podcast-review) for how that compares. Also think twice if you need documented accuracy benchmarks or model transparency for a regulated procurement process, since Cleanvoice doesn't publish technical specifics about its detection models. And if your volume is genuinely unpredictable, pay-as-you-go credit packs are safer than a subscription tier you might not use.

## Bottom line

Cleanvoice AI does one job well: it takes the tedious, repetitive part of podcast editing — cutting filler words, mouth sounds, and dead air across single or multitrack recordings — and automates it while handing back a timeline you can still review rather than a black-box render. It's not trying to be a recorder, a host, or a full editing suite, and casual users should stick to the free trial or a pay-as-you-go pack rather than jumping straight to a subscription. For anyone producing podcasts on a recurring schedule, the time saved on the "ums" and clicks pass alone likely justifies the $11–$30 monthly cost within a couple of episodes.

## FAQ

**Is Cleanvoice AI free?**
There's a one-time free trial covering 30 minutes of processing with no credit card required. Beyond that, all use is metered by processing hour through either pay-as-you-go credit packs or a monthly subscription.

**How much does Cleanvoice AI cost?**
Pay-as-you-go starts at $11 for 5 hours of processing (~$2.20/hour). Monthly subscriptions start at $11/month for 10 hours (~$1.10/hour) and scale up to $90/month for 100 hours (~$0.90/hour). Teams processing 200+ hours a month get custom pricing with API access.

**Does Cleanvoice work on video, not just audio?**
Yes. The same filler-word, mouth-sound, and silence-removal features apply to video files, with cuts synced to the picture, though the tool's design and messaging remain audio/podcast-first.

**What editors does Cleanvoice export to?**
Cleanvoice can export an editable timeline that opens in Adobe Audition, DaVinci Resolve, REAPER, Audacity, or Ultraschall, rather than only returning a rendered audio file.

**How is Cleanvoice different from Adobe Podcast?**
Adobe Podcast's free Enhance Speech tool focuses on turning noisy raw audio into clear speech, plus browser-based recording. Cleanvoice is a paid, hour-metered tool focused on editing decisions — removing fillers, stutters, mouth sounds, and dead air — across single or multitrack sessions, with output that plugs into a professional editor. Many producers use both, for different stages of the same workflow.

**Does Cleanvoice have an API?**
Yes. It offers a REST API with Python and JavaScript SDKs, aimed at teams that want to build automated processing into their own production pipeline rather than using the web dashboard manually. This sits under the custom/high-volume pricing tier.

**Is Cleanvoice AI GDPR compliant?**
Cleanvoice states it is GDPR compliant and ISO 27001 certified, which matters for teams handling guest recordings that may include EU-based speakers' personal data. Confirm current certification details directly with Cleanvoice for any compliance-sensitive procurement.

**Do unused subscription hours roll over?**
Yes. Unused hours on monthly subscription plans roll over up to three times the plan's monthly allotment before expiring, and pay-as-you-go credits remain valid for two years from purchase.

For more AI production and editing tools, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Brandwatch Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Brandwatch is an enterprise social listening and consumer intelligence platform. Here's what it costs, what its AI layer Iris does, and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
