title: Saga AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is Saga still worth using in 2026? A hands-on look at pricing, AI backlinking, and how it stacks up as a faster Notion alternative.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Saga AI Review 2026: Is This Notion Alternative Worth It?

Saga is a lightweight, AI-native note-taking and knowledge base app built for small teams who find Notion too heavy. It's still an active, independently run product in 2026 — not discontinued — with a free plan for up to three people and paid tiers starting around $6-8 per member per month. It's best for fast personal notes and small-team docs, not complex databases.

## At a glance

| | Saga |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (up to 3 members) |
| Paid plan | Standard, roughly $6-8/member/month depending on billing cycle |
| Free tier limits | 3 members, ~5,000 AI words/month, 250 MB storage, 1 integration |
| Best for | Solo writers and small teams wanting fast notes + light task tracking |
| Standout feature | AI-generated backlinks that surface related notes automatically |

## What Saga actually is

Saga is a web and desktop app for notes, docs, and lightweight task management, made by a small startup (also called Saga, saga.so) that positions itself as a faster, less cluttered alternative to Notion. It launched out of beta as "Saga 1.0" in late 2024 and has kept shipping updates since — the company says it has around 60,000 users, with logos like Slack, Dataiku, and Deloitte listed as customers on its marketing site, which is worth reading as "some employees at these companies use it" rather than a company-wide rollout.

The product doesn't publicly commit to a single foundation model — its marketing copy just says Saga AI runs on "the latest AI models" for writing and search, which in practice has meant swapping between mainstream large language models as the team judges them to perform better.

Unlike Rewind AI, which built its product around continuously recording your screen and got acquired into Limitless in 2024 (a shift covered in this site's [Rewind AI review](/blog/rewind-ai-review)), Saga has stayed a straightforward, opt-in notes app. You type or paste content in; nothing runs in the background capturing your activity.

## Pricing

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability below were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI note-taking tools adjust free-tier caps and AI word allowances often, so confirm current numbers on Saga's own pricing page before committing.

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Unlimited pages/tasks, up to 3 workspace members, ~5,000 Saga AI words/month, 7-day version history, 1 integration, 250 MB storage |
| Standard | ~$6-8 per member/month | Unlimited members, unlimited Saga AI (subject to a fair-use policy), unlimited version history, both integrations, admin permissions, 5 GB storage |
| Business | ~$12 per member/month (listed as "coming soon" on Saga's site as of research) | AI search across connected tools and the web, advanced permissions, unlimited integrations, 100 GB storage |
| Enterprise | Custom, billed annually | Dedicated support, onboarding/training |

Two things worth flagging. First, Saga's site has shown slightly different Standard-tier figures ($6 vs. $8 per member/month) depending on billing cycle — check the toggle on checkout rather than trusting the first number shown. Second, "unlimited Saga AI" on paid plans is capped by an unpublished fair-use policy, so heavy AI users should test the free tier's 5,000-word limit first to gauge usage.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**AI-suggested backlinks.** Saga's headline feature is that it reads what you're writing and surfaces related pages automatically, without you manually typing `[[link]]` syntax the way Obsidian or Notion require. For anyone who has a knowledge base with dozens of overlapping notes and never bothers going back to cross-link them, this is the single biggest time-saver in the product.

**Live blocks.** You can embed a block from one page into another, and it stays synced — edit the source once, and every page referencing it updates. This is a genuinely useful pattern for teams that maintain one canonical doc (a glossary, a pricing table, an onboarding checklist) referenced from many other pages, and it avoids the classic problem of five different stale copies of the same paragraph floating around a workspace.

**Tasks and Kanban views baked into notes.** Rather than a separate project-management module, Saga lets any page double as a task list or board. It's not a replacement for a dedicated tool like Asana or Linear on complex projects, but for a two-to-five-person team that just wants "notes plus a lightweight to-do board" in one place, it removes the need for a second app entirely.

**Fast, local-feeling search.** Reviewers and users consistently point to Saga's search as noticeably snappier than Notion's, particularly once a workspace has a few hundred pages — Notion's search has been a long-running complaint among its power users, and Saga was built partly as a direct answer to that pain point.

**Side-by-side page viewing.** You can open two pages next to each other in the same window, which sounds minor but matters a lot for research-heavy writing (drafting a doc while referencing source notes) and is something Notion still handles awkwardly with its tab system.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo writers and researchers** — the free plan's unlimited pages and reasonable AI word allowance cover most individual note-taking needs without a subscription.
- **Small teams (3-15 people)** — the Standard plan's flat unlimited-AI structure and low per-seat price make it a realistic Notion swap for a startup or agency team that doesn't need Notion's databases, relations, or formula fields.
- **Teams that lean on integrations across many tools** — hold off. Saga currently only connects to Google Drive and Linear; the "search across tools and the web" capability is gated behind the not-yet-generally-available Business tier.
- **Enterprises needing compliance guarantees** — Saga's enterprise tier exists but the company doesn't publish SOC 2 or similar certification details on its marketing pages the way larger competitors do, so IT/security teams should ask directly before rolling it out beyond a pilot group.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely fast, uncluttered interface compared to Notion | No public database/relation features for structured data |
| AI backlinking works without manual tagging effort | Business tier (cross-tool AI search) is still "coming soon" |
| Generous free tier for individuals and tiny teams | Only two integrations (Google Drive, Linear) at time of writing |
| Flat per-seat pricing with unlimited AI use on Standard | No published SOC 2/ISO certification details for enterprise buyers |
| Desktop apps for macOS and Windows | Smaller ecosystem of templates/plugins than Notion or Obsidian |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Saga's integration list is deliberately narrow: Google Drive for embedding and referencing files, and Linear for connecting engineering issue tracking to notes. There's no public API documented on Saga's site as of this review, and no Zapier or native Slack integration listed — if your workflow depends on connecting a notes tool to a dozen other services, this is the clearest gap versus Notion, which has a mature API and third-party ecosystem. Saga's Business tier promises broader "search across tools and the web," but since it's still listed as upcoming, teams needing deep integrations today should treat Saga as standalone rather than a hub.

## Where it's a strong fit

Saga works well if your actual daily habit is writing and organizing notes, not building relational databases. Teams migrating off a scattered mix of Google Docs and Slack messages, who want one fast place to write meeting notes, project briefs, and a lightweight task board, tend to get value quickly because the learning curve is short — there's very little setup ceremony compared to designing a Notion workspace from scratch.

It's also a reasonable pick for anyone who has tried Notion and specifically bounced off its search speed or its page-loading lag on large workspaces, since that's the exact complaint Saga was built to address.

## Where to think twice

Skip Saga if you need structured databases — inventory trackers, CRMs built from tables with formulas and relations, or anything resembling a lightweight Airtable use case. Saga's page model is closer to a wiki/notes app than a database tool, and it doesn't hide that limitation.

Skip it too if your team needs a large integration surface (dozens of connected apps via Zapier or a documented public API), formal compliance documentation for procurement (SOC 2, HIPAA, etc.) available today rather than "ask sales," or if you specifically want an offline-first, local-file tool — Saga is cloud-based, unlike file-based alternatives such as Obsidian.

And if your organization is already deep into Notion with custom databases and integrations built out, the switching cost likely isn't worth it just for faster search and nicer backlinks — those gains matter most to teams starting fresh.

## Bottom line

Saga is a well-executed, focused notes app that delivers on its core pitch: faster and less cluttered than Notion, with AI backlinking that actually saves manual effort instead of being a bolted-on chatbot. It's not trying to be an all-in-one workspace, and that focus is both its strength and its ceiling — teams that need databases, a broad integration ecosystem, or enterprise compliance paperwork will outgrow it quickly. For a solo user or a small team that mostly wants a fast place to write and lightly organize work, it's a legitimately good, reasonably priced option worth trialing on the free plan before committing to a paid seat.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Saga free to use?**
Yes. The free plan supports unlimited pages and tasks for up to three workspace members, with roughly 5,000 words of Saga AI usage per month. It doesn't require a credit card to start.

**How much does Saga cost per user?**
The Standard plan runs roughly $6-8 per member per month depending on billing cycle (monthly vs. annual), with unlimited AI use subject to a fair-use policy. Confirm the exact current number on Saga's pricing page, since it's shown slight variation across the site.

**Is Saga still being developed, or was it shut down?**
Saga is still an active, independently operated product as of this review — it is not discontinued or acquired. It launched its "1.0" release out of beta in late 2024 and has continued shipping feature updates since, including expanding its AI capabilities.

**What AI model powers Saga AI?**
Saga doesn't publicly commit to one specific model; its marketing describes using "the latest AI models" for writing assistance and search, which in practice means the underlying model can change as the team updates the product.

**Does Saga integrate with other tools?**
Currently it connects to Google Drive and Linear. A broader "AI search across tools and the web" capability is listed under the Business plan, which was still marked "coming soon" at the time of this review.

**Is Saga a good Notion alternative?**
For notes, docs, and light task tracking, yes — many users switch specifically for faster search and a cleaner interface. If you rely on Notion's databases, relations, or formulas, Saga doesn't currently replace that functionality.

**Does Saga have desktop apps?**
Yes, Saga offers native desktop apps for macOS and Windows in addition to its web app.

**Is Saga suitable for enterprise use?**
Saga lists an Enterprise tier with custom pricing and dedicated onboarding, but doesn't publish detailed compliance certifications (like SOC 2) on its site, so larger organizations with strict procurement requirements should confirm those details directly with Saga's sales team before rolling it out widely.

For more AI and software picks, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software), and if you're comparing knowledge-base tools, see our [Notion AI review](/blog/notion-ai-review) for how the two compare on database features and AI depth.

title: Sharly AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Sharly AI review 2026: pricing, free-tier limits, multi-document comparison, citation features, and honest pros/cons of this AI document research tool.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Sharly AI Review 2026: Is This Document Chat Tool Worth It?

Sharly AI is a document research assistant that summarizes, compares, and cites content across PDFs, spreadsheets, Word files, Notion pages, and links. It's a solid pick for researchers and small teams who need multi-document comparison and formatted citations, but its free tier is tighter than some single-PDF chat tools, and per-seat team pricing adds up quickly.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $12.50/month (Pro, billed yearly) |
| Free tier | Yes — 10 documents/month, 50 messages/month |
| Best for | Researchers, analysts, and small teams comparing multiple documents |
| Standout feature | Cross-document comparison with formatted citations (APA/MLA/Chicago) |

Made by VOX AI Inc., Sharly AI markets itself less as a "chat with your PDF" novelty and more as a document research platform — the pitch is "summarize, verify, and collaborate" rather than just Q&A on a single file. That framing matters when you're deciding whether it's the right tool for you, because it's built around comparing several documents at once and producing citations you can drop straight into a paper or report, not just answering quick questions about one upload.

This site has already covered a few tools in the same category — [ChatPDF](/blog/chatpdf-review), [CelestialPDF](/blog/celestialpdf-review), and [FileGPT](/blog/filegpt-review) — and it's worth being upfront about where Sharly actually differs rather than repeating a generic "chat with your documents" pitch. ChatPDF and FileGPT are largely single-document Q&A tools with a simple upload-and-ask flow; Sharly's differentiators are multi-file/multi-format comparison, citation formatting built into the workflow, and team-oriented features like shared workspaces, annotations, and audit logs that the single-document tools generally don't offer.

No matching store entry exists for Sharly AI in this site's coupon catalog at the time of writing, so there's no coupon-page link here — pricing below comes directly from Sharly's own pricing page.

## What Sharly AI Actually Is

Sharly AI positions itself as a document intelligence tool rather than a narrow "PDF chatbot." You upload or link a document — or several — and the tool extracts summaries, answers questions with inline citations pointing back to the source text, and lets you compare data points across files side by side. Sharly says it's used by more than 2 million researchers and teams across academic, analyst, product, and compliance roles, though that figure comes from the vendor's own marketing copy and isn't independently verifiable, so treat it as a claim rather than a fact.

Supported formats include PDF, XLSX, DOCX, PPTX, Google Docs, Notion pages, and web links — a noticeably broader input list than most PDF-only chat tools, which is the main reason teams juggling mixed file types tend to land on Sharly over a single-format competitor.

## Pricing

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 10 documents/month, 50 messages/month, 5 uploads/day, basic summaries and AI answers, limited OCR, limited inline citations |
| Pro | $12.50/month (billed yearly) | Unlimited documents, 1,000 messages/month, unlimited uploads, higher-quality reasoning answers, citation format switcher, no training on your data |
| Team | $24/month per seat (billed yearly, up to 100 seats) | Everything in Pro, plus shared workspaces, team annotations, knowledge retention, semantic data extraction, analytics, and citation history |
| Business | Custom pricing (per seat, billed yearly) | Unlimited seats, admin dashboard, role-based access, version history, audit logs, SSO/SAML, private deployment options, dedicated support |

Sharly's pricing page indicates yearly billing carries roughly a 20% discount versus paying month to month, and it notes monthly billing is available on request rather than being a default checkout option — worth confirming directly with Sharly if annual commitment isn't something you want.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — AI tools iterate quickly on both plans and limits, so it's worth double-checking current numbers on [Sharly's pricing page](https://www.sharly.ai/pricing) before subscribing.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Multi-document comparison.** Rather than restricting you to one file per session, Sharly lets you load multiple documents and ask questions that span across them — useful for comparing quarterly reports, contract versions, or a batch of research papers where you need one consolidated answer instead of checking each file separately.

**Citation generation.** Answers come with source-backed citations, and Pro and above let you switch between APA, MLA, and Chicago formats. For students and analysts who need sourced claims in a finished paper, this saves manually tracking down page numbers and formatting references by hand.

**Broad format support.** PDF is table stakes for this category, but Sharly also handles DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, Google Docs, Notion pages, and raw links — a real advantage if your research pulls from spreadsheets and slide decks alongside PDFs.

**Team collaboration.** Team and Business tiers add shared workspaces, inline annotations, and knowledge retention across a group, so teammates can build on each other's document analysis instead of starting from scratch each time.

**Enterprise security controls.** The Business tier adds role-based permissions, version history, audit logs, and SSO/SAML — compliance checklist items that most lightweight PDF chat tools don't offer.

## Who It's Actually For

- **Solo researchers and students** — the Free tier's 10 documents and 50 messages a month is workable for occasional use, but anyone doing regular literature reviews will likely bump into the monthly cap fast and want Pro for the citation formatting alone.
- **Analysts and consultants** — Pro's unlimited documents and 1,000 messages/month, plus the citation switcher, fit people regularly producing cited reports or comparing multiple source documents for a single deliverable.
- **Small teams (2-100 people)** — Team tier's per-seat pricing and shared workspaces make sense for research, compliance, or product teams that need a shared knowledge base rather than everyone working in isolated sessions.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** — Business tier's SSO, audit logs, and private deployment options target organizations where security sign-off is a prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Handles more file formats than most document-chat competitors (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, Notion, links) | Free tier's 50 messages/month is noticeably tighter than some single-PDF-focused competitors |
| Built-in citation formatting (APA/MLA/Chicago) saves manual reference work | Team pricing is per-seat and can scale expensive for larger groups fast |
| Multi-document comparison in a single session | Monthly billing isn't the default — yearly commitment gets the advertised price |
| Team/Business tiers add real compliance features (SSO, audit logs, RBAC) | Business tier pricing isn't published — requires a sales conversation |
| "No training on your data" stated on Pro and above | OCR and citation quality are explicitly limited on the free tier |

## Integrations and Ecosystem

Sharly's ecosystem leans toward document-source integrations rather than broad third-party app connections: it pulls directly from Google Docs and Notion in addition to standard file uploads, and accepts web links as a document source. There's no indication on Sharly's site of a public API, Zapier connector, or Slack app at the time of writing — if workflow automation into other tools is a requirement for your team, that's worth confirming directly with Sharly before committing to a paid plan, since it isn't something the vendor advertises.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

Sharly is a strong fit if you regularly work across multiple documents in different formats and need citations that are actually usable in a finished report, rather than a quick answer to a one-off question. Teams that need a shared workspace where colleagues can annotate and build on each other's research — instead of running separate sessions — also get real value from the Team tier's collaboration features. And organizations that need compliance boxes checked (SSO, audit logs, private deployment) before a tool gets approved will find the Business tier addresses those requirements directly, which most lightweight PDF chat tools don't attempt to cover.

## Where to Think Twice

If you need a fully free tool for regular use, Sharly's 50-messages-a-month cap will likely feel restrictive faster than competitors built around lighter single-PDF use — it's designed to convert you to Pro, not to be a permanent free option. If your budget is tight, $24/month per seat adds up quickly for teams beyond a handful of people, and Business-tier pricing isn't published at all, so a larger rollout requires a sales call rather than self-serve checkout. If you need API access or pre-built integrations into tools like Slack or Zapier, Sharly doesn't publicly advertise those, so it may not fit an automation-heavy stack. And treat AI-generated summaries and citations as a starting point, not a final answer — as with any LLM-based tool, hallucinated or misattributed citations are a known risk category worth spot-checking against the source document.

## The Bottom Line

Sharly AI earns its place in the document-chat category by doing more than chat with a single PDF — the multi-format support, cross-document comparison, and built-in citation formatting are genuinely useful for research-heavy work, and the Team and Business tiers add collaboration and compliance features that make it viable for organizations, not just individuals. The free tier is workable for light, occasional use, but anyone doing this regularly will want Pro fairly quickly, and teams should budget carefully around the per-seat pricing before scaling up. If your workflow centers on comparing multiple documents and producing properly cited output, Sharly is worth trialing on the free tier before committing to a paid plan.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Sharly AI free to use?**
Yes, there's a free tier with 10 documents and 50 messages per month, along with a 5-documents-per-day upload cap. It's enough for occasional use but tight for regular research work.

**How much does Sharly AI Pro cost?**
Pro is $12.50/month when billed yearly, which includes unlimited documents, 1,000 messages/month, and citation format switching between APA, MLA, and Chicago.

**What file types does Sharly AI support?**
PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, Google Docs, Notion pages, and web links — a broader range than most PDF-only chat tools in this category.

**Does Sharly AI train on my documents?**
Sharly states that Pro and above plans don't use your data to train their models. Confirm the exact data-handling terms in Sharly's current privacy policy before uploading sensitive documents, since specifics can change.

**Is Sharly AI good for teams?**
Yes — the Team tier ($24/month per seat, billed yearly) adds shared workspaces, annotations, and knowledge retention, and Business adds SSO, audit logs, and role-based access for larger, compliance-conscious organizations.

**How does Sharly AI compare to ChatPDF?**
[ChatPDF](/blog/chatpdf-review) is built around simple single-PDF Q&A, while Sharly supports multiple file formats, multi-document comparison, and formatted citations — better suited to research work that spans several sources rather than quick lookups in one file.

**Does Sharly AI have a mobile app?**
Sharly's website doesn't advertise a dedicated mobile app; it's positioned as a web-based platform accessible through app.sharly.ai. Confirm current platform availability directly on Sharly's site if mobile access matters for your workflow.

**Is Sharly AI beginner-friendly?**
The core upload-and-ask workflow is straightforward for anyone familiar with document chat tools, but getting full value from citation formatting and multi-document comparison involves a bit more of a learning curve than a bare-bones single-PDF tool.

For more AI and software deals, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Dorik Review 2026: AI Website Builder Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Dorik pairs AI website generation with a white-label CMS agencies can resell. Here's what it costs and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Dorik a good AI website builder?

Dorik is a solid pick if you want an AI-generated site with a genuinely no-code drag-and-drop editor and a white-label CMS you can resell to clients, but it has no permanent free plan — only a 7-day trial — and its third-party integrations are thin outside of Airtable. It suits small businesses, freelancers and agencies more than designers who need pixel-level control.

### At a glance

| | Dorik |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $29/mo (Personal, billed monthly) or $20.75/mo billed annually |
| Free tier/trial | 7-day free trial on any plan, no permanent free plan |
| Best for | Small businesses, freelancers, and agencies wanting AI-generated sites plus a white-label CMS |
| Standout feature | Full white-label dashboard so agencies can rebrand and resell Dorik to their own clients |

Dorik is a website builder that leans on AI at the front end of the process — you describe your business in a prompt and it generates a starting site, copy and imagery — but everything after that happens in a conventional no-code, drag-and-drop editor built from more than 250 pre-built UI blocks and 110-plus templates. That combination (AI first draft, manual block editor after) puts it in a different lane from tools like Framer AI or Dora AI, which lean harder on AI-assisted layout adjustments throughout editing, not just at generation time.

Dorik doesn't publish which language or image model powers its AI generation features, so treat "AI website generation" as a starting-point tool rather than a fully autonomous design engine — expect to spend real time in the block editor afterward, same as with most AI site builders at this price point.

## Pricing: what Dorik actually costs

Dorik runs four plans, each available monthly, annually, over two years (via discount codes), or as a one-time lifetime purchase — an option most competitors in this category don't offer at all.

| Plan | Monthly | Annual (per mo) | Lifetime | Custom domains | Pages | Collaborators |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Personal | $29 | $20.75 | $249 one-time | 1 | 25 | 0 |
| Business | $59 | $41.50 | $599 one-time | 3 | Unlimited | 10 |
| Agency | $99 | $79 | Custom (contact sales) | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |

All three plans include AI website generation, unlimited storage and bandwidth, custom fields, a white-label dashboard, and code export. The gap between Personal and Business is mostly about scale — page count, collaborators and domain count — rather than a different feature set, which is worth noting if you're a solo user who just wants more than one custom domain: you'd have to jump a full tier to get it.

There's no permanent free plan. Dorik offers a 7-day free trial with full access to whatever plan you select, no credit card required to start. That's shorter than some competitors, so have your content and structure roughly ready before starting the clock rather than noodling on a free tier for weeks the way you could with Durable or Wix.

Pricing, free-trial terms and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — AI website builder pricing moves quickly, so confirm current figures on [Dorik's pricing page](https://dorik.com/pricing) before subscribing.

## Core features walkthrough

**AI website generation from a prompt.** You describe your business — type, name, industry, tone — and Dorik generates a first-draft site: layout, section structure, placeholder copy and stock imagery pulled to match. It's a faster starting point than a blank template, but it's explicitly a draft; expect to rewrite most of the copy and swap a chunk of the imagery.

**A genuine drag-and-drop block editor.** After generation, you're not stuck re-prompting to move things around — Dorik hands you a visual editor with 250+ pre-built blocks (hero sections, pricing tables, testimonial grids, forms) that you can drag, reorder, restyle and duplicate directly. This is the biggest practical difference from AI-first builders that keep funneling every change back through a prompt.

**White-label CMS and dashboard.** This is Dorik's clearest differentiator versus Durable, Framer AI, Dora AI and CodeDesign.ai. On paid plans, agencies can rebrand the entire dashboard — logo, domain, styling — and resell Dorik-built sites to their own clients under their own brand, with client billing tools built in. None of the other AI website builders already covered on this site offer white-labeling as a standard feature.

**Built-in CMS and blogging.** Personal plans get up to 200 blog posts; Business and Agency plans get unlimited posts and pages. The CMS supports custom fields, so you can structure content types beyond a standard blog (think portfolio items, case studies, product listings) without needing a separate database tool.

**Airtable integration.** Dorik connects directly to Airtable so you can pull structured data — a product catalog, a team directory, an event list — into your site and have it update when the Airtable base changes. It's a genuinely useful feature for content-heavy or catalog-style sites, but it's also close to the only named third-party integration Dorik publishes; there's no prominent Zapier, Stripe or Mailchimp integration listed on its marketing pages.

## Who Dorik is actually for

- **Solo freelancers and small businesses** on the Personal plan get a workable AI-generated site with one custom domain, 25 pages and unlimited storage — enough for a portfolio, a local service business, or a small content site, as long as you don't need collaborators.
- **Growing teams and small agencies** fit the Business plan, where unlimited pages, 10 collaborators and three custom domains open the door to managing a handful of client sites from one account, still under Dorik's own branding.
- **Agencies reselling websites to clients** are the clearest fit for the Agency plan — unlimited collaborators, unlimited domains, and the white-label dashboard mean you can put your own logo on the tool and bill clients for a service that's actually running on Dorik's infrastructure.
- **Designers who want pixel-perfect, code-level control** are better served elsewhere — Dorik's editor is block-based, not a freeform canvas, so highly custom layouts will run into more friction than they would in Framer AI.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Drag-and-drop editor with 250+ blocks gives real post-generation control | No permanent free plan — only a 7-day trial |
| White-label dashboard and client billing built into Business/Agency plans | Underlying AI model isn't disclosed |
| Lifetime purchase option avoids recurring fees entirely | Personal plan allows zero collaborators |
| Unlimited storage and bandwidth on every plan | Documented third-party integrations are thin beyond Airtable |
| Code export gives some portability if you outgrow the platform | Jump from Personal to Business (unlimited pages/domains) is a steep $30/mo increase |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Dorik's integration story is narrower than most AI website builders in this category. Its most notable named integration is Airtable, for pulling live structured data into a site. Beyond that, Dorik markets its CMS, SEO tools and analytics as built-in rather than routed through third-party plugins — simpler to set up, but limiting if your workflow depends on tools like Zapier, HubSpot or a dedicated email platform. Code export on every plan is the practical workaround: export and self-host if you need a connection Dorik doesn't natively support, though that means leaving its hosting and white-label features behind. Check [Dorik's help center](https://help.dorik.com) for the current, complete integration list before committing.

## Where Dorik is a strong fit

- You're an agency or freelancer who wants to resell websites under your own brand without building a CMS from scratch — the white-label dashboard and client billing tools solve a real operational problem.
- You want an AI head start on a site but plan to do real hands-on editing afterward — the block editor is capable enough to carry that work.
- You'd rather pay once than forever — the lifetime plans on Personal ($249) and Business ($599) are priced to pay for themselves within roughly a year versus the monthly rate, if you're confident you'll stick with the platform.
- You need a content-driven site backed by structured data and Airtable is already part of your workflow.

## Where to think twice

- **If you need a fully free tool to test before paying anything** — Dorik's 7-day trial is workable but short, and there's no free-forever tier the way Durable offers.
- **If your team relies on a specific third-party integration stack** (Zapier, Stripe, a CRM) — Dorik's publicly documented integrations are limited, and you may need to rely on code export and manual embeds instead.
- **If you want the AI to keep adjusting layout throughout editing**, not just at the first draft — Dorik's AI role is front-loaded at generation; ongoing edits are manual, block-based work, closer to a traditional builder than to Framer AI's more continuous AI-editing approach.
- **If you're a single collaborator who might eventually need a teammate** — the Personal plan's zero-collaborator limit means any team growth forces an immediate upgrade to Business.

## Bottom line

Dorik earns its place among AI website builders less because its generation engine is unusually advanced — it isn't disclosed and functions like most prompt-to-draft tools — and more because of what happens after generation: a real drag-and-drop editor, a white-label CMS agencies can resell, and lifetime pricing options that most competitors don't offer at all. If you're a freelancer or small agency that wants to build and bill client sites under your own brand, Dorik's combination of features is hard to match elsewhere in this roundup of tools. If you just want the fastest possible AI-generated site with no ongoing edits and a permanent free tier, Durable is the better starting point instead.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Dorik have a free plan?**
No. Dorik offers a 7-day free trial with full access to your chosen plan, but there's no permanent free tier. You'll need to commit to a paid plan (or the lifetime option) once the trial ends to keep your site live.

**What's the cheapest way to use Dorik long-term?**
The Personal lifetime plan, a one-time $249 payment, works out cheaper than roughly a year of monthly billing and removes recurring costs entirely — though it caps you at one custom domain, 25 pages and zero collaborators.

**Can agencies white-label Dorik for clients?**
Yes. Business and Agency plans include a white-label dashboard that lets agencies rebrand the platform with their own logo and domain, plus built-in client billing tools, so you can resell websites without clients ever seeing the Dorik name.

**What AI model does Dorik use to generate websites?**
Dorik doesn't publicly disclose which language or image model powers its website generation feature. Treat the AI-generated site as a strong starting draft rather than a fully autonomous design output.

**Does Dorik support Zapier or Stripe integrations?**
Dorik's publicly documented integrations are limited — Airtable is the most prominently featured one. Zapier, Stripe and similar tools aren't clearly listed on its marketing pages, so check [Dorik's help center](https://help.dorik.com) directly if a specific integration is a dealbreaker for you.

**Is Dorik good for beginners with no coding experience?**
Yes. The AI-generated starting point plus a visual drag-and-drop block editor is designed for non-technical users, and code export is available if you eventually want a developer to take over.

**How does Dorik compare to Durable, Framer AI or Dora AI?**
Dorik's biggest edge is its white-label CMS for agencies, which none of those three offer as a standard feature. Durable bundles a CRM and invoicing tools around the site for solo service businesses; Framer AI and Dora AI lean harder into AI-assisted design throughout editing, not just at generation. Read our [Durable AI review](/blog/durable-ai-review), [Framer AI review](/blog/framer-ai-review) or [Dora AI review](/blog/dora-ai-review) for more detail.

**Can I export my Dorik site if I want to leave the platform?**
Yes, code export is included on every plan, giving you a path off the platform if you outgrow its hosting or integration limits — though you'd lose the white-label CMS and hosting benefits by doing so.

title: MarketMuse Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: MarketMuse builds site-wide topic clusters and content briefs instead of scoring single articles. Here's its pricing, features, and best fit.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is MarketMuse worth it for content strategy and SEO in 2026?

MarketMuse is an AI content strategy platform built around topic modeling rather than single-article optimization — it maps your entire content inventory against a topic's competitive landscape, scores personalized ranking difficulty, and generates briefs and strategy documents. It suits editorial and content-marketing teams planning at the site level; it's the wrong tool if you just want a quick per-article SERP score or exact self-serve pricing upfront.

### At a glance

| | MarketMuse |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Not published; paid plans (Optimize, Research, Strategy) are quoted via a sales demo |
| Free tier / trial | Free plan with 10 queries/month and access to Topic Navigator, Keywords, SERP tools, and Site Heatmap; no content briefs on the free tier |
| Best for | Content strategists and editorial teams planning topic clusters and site-wide content inventories |
| Standout feature | Personalized topic-authority and difficulty scoring built on patented topic modeling, not generic keyword-difficulty metrics |

## What MarketMuse actually is

MarketMuse is made by MarketMuse, Inc., a Boston-based company founded by SEOs and content strategists who wanted a faster way to figure out what to write and what to fix, before generative AI made "content tools" a crowded category. It predates most of today's AI-writing wave — its core engine has been built around topic modeling and semantic analysis since well before ChatGPT existed, and that shows in how it's structured: organized around *topics* and *content inventories*, not a single blank-page editor.

That's the biggest thing separating MarketMuse from tools like [Surfer SEO](/blog/surfer-seo-review) or [Outranking](/blog/outranking-review). Surfer's whole workflow centers on one article at a time — write a draft, score it against the current SERP, adjust headings and terms until the score climbs. MarketMuse starts a step earlier: it crawls your site, classifies existing pages into topic clusters, flags where you're thin or missing coverage entirely, and only then generates briefs for the pieces worth writing or rewriting. If Surfer answers "how do I make this one post rank," MarketMuse answers "what should our content team be working on this quarter."

MarketMuse says its topic modeling is patented and built on proprietary data rather than the TF-IDF or basic keyword-clustering approaches some competitors lean on. That's a vendor claim worth noting as such — not independently auditable from the outside — but the practical effect for a user is a difficulty score personalized to your domain's existing authority for a topic, rather than a flat, competitor-agnostic number.

## Pricing

MarketMuse doesn't publish exact dollar figures for its paid tiers on its current pricing page — Optimize, Research, and Strategy are all gated behind a "book a demo" call, which is a meaningfully different sales motion than the self-serve, published pricing you'll find on Surfer SEO or most AI-writing tools. That opacity is itself worth flagging for anyone comparing options on a budget: you can't line up MarketMuse's price against a competitor's without talking to sales first.

| Plan | Users | Tracked topics | Content briefs | Strategy docs | Queries/month |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 1 | None | None | None | 10 |
| Optimize | 1 | 100 | 5/month (Article Briefs only) | 1/month | 100 |
| Research | 3 | 1,000 | 10/month (Article Briefs) | 3/month | Unlimited |
| Strategy | 5 | 10,000 | 20/month (all 9 brief types) | 5/month | Unlimited |

Every paid tier is currently limited to a single site inventory per account — so an agency running content for multiple client domains needs to weigh whether one workspace covers its needs, or whether it needs multiple subscriptions or an enterprise conversation.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability described here were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — MarketMuse doesn't publish self-serve pricing, so confirm current numbers directly with their sales team before budgeting.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**Topic Navigator and content clustering.** Instead of a keyword list, MarketMuse organizes a subject into a topic model — parent topics, subtopics, and semantic relationships — and maps existing content onto it. This is what makes it a planning tool first, an optimization tool second.

**Personalized difficulty scoring.** Rather than a generic 0–100 keyword-difficulty number pulled from backlink data, MarketMuse's score factors in your own site's existing topical authority. A topic that's hard for a brand-new site can score comparatively easy for a domain with strong coverage nearby.

**Content inventory and gap analysis.** MarketMuse crawls a connected domain and continuously classifies every page into its topic model, surfacing which pages are strong, thin, or missing entirely — on a schedule, not a one-off manual crawl.

**Content briefs (multiple types).** The Strategy plan unlocks all nine brief formats; lower tiers are capped to standard article briefs. Briefs cover topic and question coverage, competitive analysis, and recommended structure — what a writer actually works from.

**Strategy documents.** Site-level deliverables — executive summaries, competitive overviews, cluster breakdowns — built for stakeholder conversations rather than a single writer, a format most competing AI-SEO tools don't really have an equivalent for.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo bloggers and small sites** are better served by the free tier for occasional research, or a cheaper self-serve tool for regular briefs — Optimize's 5 briefs/month is thin for anyone publishing weekly.
- **In-house content teams at mid-sized companies** are the clearest fit for Research or Strategy — the tracked-topic ceiling (1,000–10,000) and multi-user seats support an ongoing editorial calendar, not a one-off audit.
- **Agencies managing several client sites** will hit the single-site-inventory-per-plan limit fast; budget for multiple subscriptions or an enterprise conversation, and raise that on the demo call rather than assuming pricing scales linearly.
- **Teams that already own a SERP-optimization tool** (like Surfer or Outranking) might use MarketMuse upstream of it — MarketMuse decides what to write, the other tool scores the draft once it's written.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Site-wide topic modeling and content inventory, not just per-article scoring | No published self-serve pricing — every paid tier requires a sales demo |
| Personalized difficulty scores based on your own domain's existing authority | Free tier has no content briefs at all, so real evaluation needs a paid trial or demo |
| Strategy documents useful for stakeholder/leadership planning conversations | Single site inventory per account on every tier, limiting for multi-client agencies |
| Long track record in topic modeling predating the current generative-AI tool wave | Learning curve — the topic-cluster workflow takes longer to learn than a single "paste keyword, get score" tool |
| Multiple content-brief formats (up to nine types on the top tier) | Lower tiers cap you to article briefs only, withholding other brief types until Strategy |

## Integrations and ecosystem

MarketMuse's product pages emphasize the web app and its brief/inventory/strategy outputs rather than a large public integration marketplace — it doesn't list a Zapier app or a broad native integration catalog the way general marketing suites do. If API access or CMS integrations (WordPress, Google Docs export, etc.) matter to your workflow, confirm current availability and which plan tier includes them directly with MarketMuse before subscribing, since this detail shifts between tiers and isn't reliably documented publicly.

## Where it's a strong fit

MarketMuse earns its keep on sites with an existing content library that needs a systematic audit — a blog with a few hundred posts and no clear sense of which topics are covered well, which are thin, and which are missing entirely. The topic-cluster view turns that mess into an actual prioritized list, and the personalized difficulty scoring means the priorities reflect the site's real starting position rather than a generic keyword-difficulty number that ignores what you've already built.

It's also a reasonable fit for content teams that need to justify a strategy to non-SEO stakeholders — the strategy documents are built for that conversation in a way a raw content-editor score isn't.

## Where to think twice

If you need a fully free tool, or even one with transparent self-serve pricing, MarketMuse isn't it — every paid plan is quoted through a sales call, adding friction for a solo creator just comparing a shortlist. If your workflow is really "optimize this one article against the current SERP," a lighter, cheaper tool built for that specific job will get you there faster. And if you manage content for multiple separate client sites, the one-inventory-per-plan structure means paying for multiple subscriptions or negotiating an enterprise deal rather than scaling a single plan up.

## Bottom line

MarketMuse is a planning-first content strategy tool, not a drop-in replacement for a per-article SERP optimizer. Its topic modeling and personalized difficulty scoring genuinely do something different from the score-your-draft category that dominates AI SEO tools right now, and that's most valuable to teams managing an existing content library who need to decide what to build next, not just polish what's already drafted. The catch is that you can't evaluate the actual cost without a sales conversation, and the free tier won't get you far enough to judge the brief quality yourself — budget time for a demo before committing.

## FAQ

**Does MarketMuse have a free plan?**
Yes. It includes 10 queries per month and access to the Topic Navigator, Keywords, SERP tools, and Site Heatmap, but not content briefs or tracked topics — those require a paid plan.

**How much does MarketMuse cost?**
MarketMuse doesn't publish dollar pricing for Optimize, Research, or Strategy; all three require booking a demo with sales for a quote. Confirm current pricing directly with MarketMuse before budgeting.

**How is MarketMuse different from Surfer SEO?**
Surfer optimizes a single piece of content against the current SERP for one keyword. MarketMuse works a step earlier, mapping your whole site into topic clusters and generating a prioritized content plan before you write anything. Some teams use both — MarketMuse for planning, Surfer for the final pass. See our [Surfer SEO review](/blog/surfer-seo-review).

**Does MarketMuse write content for me?**
Its core strength is planning and briefing rather than drafting. If you need AI-assisted first drafts, check what's currently included in each tier or pair it with a dedicated AI writer, since generative features can vary by plan.

**Is MarketMuse good for beginners?**
It has a real learning curve. The topic-cluster workflow takes longer to grasp than a "paste a keyword, get a score" tool, and the free tier doesn't unlock content briefs to let a beginner see the full output before paying.

**What's a realistic alternative to MarketMuse?**
For per-article SERP scoring, [Surfer SEO](/blog/surfer-seo-review) is more direct and self-serve-priced. For AI content generation with SEO guidance, [AISEO](/blog/aiseo-review) or [Outranking](/blog/outranking-review) are worth comparing. For rank tracking and technical research, [Wope](/blog/wope-review) covers different ground.

**Does MarketMuse support agencies managing multiple client sites?**
Every current plan is limited to a single site inventory, so agencies with several client domains typically need multiple subscriptions or an enterprise arrangement — worth raising on the sales call rather than assuming it scales automatically.

**Is MarketMuse's data proprietary or third-party?**
MarketMuse states it relies on proprietary data and patented topic modeling rather than commodity keyword-difficulty data. That's a vendor claim about methodology, not an independently verifiable benchmark, but it's the stated basis for why its difficulty scores differ from generic tools.

For more AI and SEO software coverage, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Unbounce Review 2026: AI Landing Pages, Pricing, Verdict
excerpt: Unbounce review covering Smart Traffic AI, Smart Copy, pricing tiers, pros and cons, and who its AI landing page builder actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Unbounce worth it for building landing pages?

Unbounce is a solid pick if you run paid campaigns and need to launch and A/B test landing pages fast without pulling in a developer. Its AI features (Smart Copy, Smart Traffic) add real value at the mid-tier plans, but the entry Starter plan is thin, and pricing climbs quickly once you need multiple users or higher traffic.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | $22/month (Starter, billed annually) |
| **Free trial** | 14 days, no credit card required |
| **Best for** | Marketers and agencies running paid-traffic landing pages |
| **Standout feature** | Smart Traffic — AI-based visitor routing between page variants |

Unbounce has been around since 2009, long before "AI landing page builder" was a category anyone searched for, and that history shows in how the product is built. It's not a from-scratch AI generator like some newer entrants — it's a mature drag-and-drop builder that has layered AI features (Smart Copy for writing, Smart Traffic for optimization, and an MCP server for AI-assistant control) on top of a conversion-focused core. That combination is worth understanding before you commit to a plan, because the AI parts are genuinely useful but aren't the whole story.

## What Unbounce actually is

Unbounce, part of Vendasta's marketing stack since its 2024 acquisition, is a standalone landing page and conversion platform. You build pages with a drag-and-drop editor (or start from one of 100+ templates), host them on Unbounce's own subdomains or a connected custom domain, and route paid or organic traffic to them without touching your main website's CMS.

The AI layer sits on top of that builder rather than replacing it. Smart Copy is a built-in writing assistant for expanding rough notes into full paragraphs, rewriting existing copy, summarizing longer sections, and suggesting the next sentence as you write — closer to a copywriting co-pilot embedded in the page editor than a general chat assistant. Smart Traffic is the more distinctive feature: once a page has enough visitors, it uses machine learning to route new visitors to whichever page variant is statistically most likely to convert for their attributes (location, device, browser, time of day), rather than waiting for a full A/B test to reach significance the old-fashioned way. Unbounce states Smart Traffic delivers an average 30% conversion lift — a vendor claim worth testing on your own traffic rather than taking as a guarantee.

## Unbounce pricing

Unbounce runs a five-tier structure, with the top two tiers being where most of the AI optimization features actually unlock.

| Plan | Price (billed annually) | Traffic limit | Users | Key inclusions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $22/mo | 500 visitors | 1 | 5 pages, drag-and-drop builder, lead gen forms |
| Build | $74/mo | 20,000 visitors | — | Unlimited pages, AI copywriting, popups/sticky bars, 1,000+ integrations |
| Experiment | $112/mo | 30,000 visitors | 3 | Unlimited A/B testing, 2 root domains, dynamic text replacement |
| Optimize | $187/mo | 50,000 visitors | 5 | Smart Traffic (AI routing), 3 root domains, advanced scheduling |
| Concierge / Agency | Custom | Custom | Custom | Dedicated support, higher limits, agency tooling |

Monthly (non-annual) billing runs noticeably higher — $29, $99, $149, and $249 for the same four self-serve tiers. Every plan includes unlimited conversions, unlimited subdomains, free hosting, and the template library; what changes as you move up is page count, traffic volume, user count, root domain connections, and which AI features are switched on.

That last point matters: Smart Traffic, the headline AI optimization feature, is gated to the Optimize plan and above. If you're on Starter or Build hoping for AI-driven conversion routing, you won't get it — you'll get Smart Copy for writing, but not the traffic-routing intelligence. Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — confirm current numbers on Unbounce's own pricing page before buying.

## Core features that actually matter

**Drag-and-drop builder with 100+ templates.** The editor is the foundation everything else sits on — no code required to ship a page. For marketers who need speed over pixel-perfect custom design, this is the main draw.

**Smart Copy (AI writing assistant).** Built into the page editor, it handles four jobs: expanding a bullet point into full copy, rewriting a paragraph in a different tone, summarizing long blocks, and suggesting how a sentence should continue. It's aimed at copy iteration inside the builder, not long-form content — don't expect it to replace a dedicated writing tool for blog posts or emails.

**Smart Traffic (AI conversion routing).** This is Unbounce's most defensible differentiator versus generic page builders. Instead of a static A/B test that needs to run to statistical significance before you act on it, Smart Traffic starts learning from visitor attributes almost immediately and dynamically sends each new visitor to whichever variant model predicts will convert best for them. It's only available on Optimize and above, and it needs real traffic volume to be useful — a page getting a handful of visitors a day won't generate enough signal for the model to learn from.

**Dynamic text replacement and unlimited A/B testing.** Available from the Experiment tier up, this lets a single landing page automatically swap headline or copy text based on the search query or UTM parameter that brought the visitor in — useful for running dozens of ad variants against one page template.

**MCP server access.** A newer addition across all plans, this lets you build, test, and manage Unbounce pages from AI assistants you already use via prompts — an early but notable move toward AI-assistant-driven page management.

## Who Unbounce is actually for

- **Solo marketers and small businesses** — Starter or Build covers basic page-building and copy help without needing Smart Traffic's traffic volume.
- **Growth teams running continuous PPC or paid social campaigns** — Experiment or Optimize makes sense once you're regularly testing offer variants and have traffic to make Smart Traffic worthwhile.
- **Agencies managing pages for multiple clients** — the Concierge/Agency tier and multi-domain support on higher plans are built for this, though pricing needs a sales conversation.
- **Teams needing tight CMS integration with an existing website** — Unbounce pages live on their own subdomains/domains by design; if you need pages deeply embedded in an existing site's CMS, this isn't built for that.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Mature, reliable drag-and-drop builder with a large template library | Smart Traffic (the standout AI feature) is locked to the top two plans |
| Smart Traffic can meaningfully lift conversions once traffic volume is sufficient | Starter plan's 500-visitor cap is very tight for anyone running real paid traffic |
| 1,000+ native integrations plus Zapier-style connections | Pricing rises steeply from Build to Optimize for AI features |
| MCP server support for AI-assistant-driven page management | Smart Copy is a writing assistant for page copy, not a full content tool |
| No coding required to launch and iterate on pages | Multi-user access is capped even on mid-tier plans, which can be limiting for larger teams |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Unbounce lists over 1,000 integrations starting at the Build plan, covering the usual marketing stack — email platforms, CRMs, analytics, ad platforms, and webinar tools — plus native connections for lead notification and form routing. It also supports custom scripts (Build tier and up) for teams that want to inject tracking or personalization code beyond what the native integrations cover. The newer MCP server support is worth watching: it signals Unbounce is positioning itself for a workflow where marketers manage pages through AI assistants and prompts, though this is early-stage and best treated as a bonus rather than a primary workflow today.

## Where it's a strong fit

Unbounce fits best for teams already running paid acquisition — Google Ads, Meta ads, paid social — who need to spin up and iterate on landing pages quickly without engineering support. If you're regularly testing different offers or audiences and have enough traffic per page to make statistical optimization meaningful, Smart Traffic and dynamic text replacement genuinely pay for themselves in saved testing time. Agencies managing several client accounts also get real value from the multi-domain, multi-user structure on higher tiers.

## Where to think twice

Skip Unbounce, or at least the Starter plan, if your traffic volume is low — a 500-visitor cap makes the entry tier impractical for most active campaigns, and you won't see much benefit from AI routing without enough visitors to train it on. If you need a fully free landing page tool, Unbounce isn't it; the trial is 14 days and then you're paying. Teams needing deep CMS integration with an existing website will find Unbounce's subdomain-first structure a mismatch. And if budget is the primary constraint, the jump from Build ($74/mo) to Optimize ($187/mo) just to unlock Smart Traffic is a real cost to weigh against simpler A/B testing tools.

## The bottom line

Unbounce earns its long track record in the landing page space — the builder is dependable, the template library is large, and Smart Traffic is one of the more genuinely useful applications of AI in this category because it solves a real problem (slow, manual A/B test cycles) rather than bolting AI onto a feature that didn't need it. The catch is that the feature people actually want Unbounce for sits behind the Optimize plan, and the gap between that and the affordable Starter tier is steep. If you're running consistent, meaningful traffic to paid landing pages and can justify $150–250/month, Unbounce is a strong, low-risk choice. If you're a solo operator testing an idea with low traffic, the value weakens considerably, and a lighter, cheaper builder might serve you better until your traffic grows into what Unbounce is built for.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Unbounce have a free plan?**
No. Unbounce offers a 14-day free trial with no credit card required, but there's no permanent free tier — after the trial you need to choose a paid plan starting at $22/month (annual billing).

**What's the cheapest way to use Unbounce's AI features?**
Smart Copy (AI writing assistance) is available starting on the Build plan ($74/month annual). Smart Traffic, the AI-based conversion routing feature, requires the Optimize plan ($187/month annual) or higher.

**How accurate is Unbounce's 30% conversion lift claim for Smart Traffic?**
That figure comes from Unbounce's own marketing materials as a stated average across its customer base, not an independently verified benchmark. Results depend heavily on your traffic volume and existing page performance — treat it as a directional claim to test on your own data, not a guarantee.

**Can I use Unbounce with my existing website?**
Yes, pages can run on a connected custom domain rather than only an Unbounce subdomain, but they're managed separately from your main site's CMS — it's a standalone landing page tool, not a website builder extension.

**Is Unbounce good for beginners with no design experience?**
The drag-and-drop builder and templates are designed for non-technical marketers, and Smart Copy helps with page copy without a dedicated copywriter. There's still a learning curve around setting up A/B tests and reading Smart Traffic data correctly.

**How does Unbounce handle data and privacy?**
Unbounce is a hosted SaaS platform, so visitor and lead data collected through your pages is processed and stored on its infrastructure. Review Unbounce's own privacy documentation for specifics relevant to your region (e.g., GDPR) before collecting sensitive visitor data.

**What are the main alternatives to Unbounce?**
Common alternatives include Instapage, Leadpages, and landing-page features built into broader marketing platforms like HubSpot. The right choice depends on whether you need Unbounce's specific strength — AI-driven traffic routing at scale — or a simpler, cheaper page builder for lower-volume campaigns.

Ready to launch your own landing pages? Check current Unbounce plans on its official site, and browse more [AI & software deals](/category/software) for tools worth pairing with your next campaign.

title: Ocoya Review 2026: Pricing, AI Features and Verdict
excerpt: Ocoya review covering pricing tiers, AI content generation, platform coverage, MCP/API access, and who this AI social tool actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Ocoya worth it?

Ocoya is worth it if you want AI content generation and social scheduling bundled into one subscription instead of paying separately for a caption tool and a scheduler — and if you're comfortable paying agency-style prices ($29–$199/month) for that convenience. It's a weaker fit if you just need simple, low-cost scheduling, since there's no free plan and cheaper rivals cover the same platform list.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $29/month (Starter plan, billed monthly; annual billing works out to 2 months free) |
| Free tier | No free plan — 7-day free trial with full feature access on all plans |
| Best for | Small teams and agencies that want AI-generated captions, images, and hashtags built into the scheduling workflow |
| Standout feature | Ocoya can be operated through AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Perplexity) via Model Context Protocol, not just its own dashboard |

Ocoya doesn't have a matching store entry on SmartFare yet, so there's no coupon page to link here. The figures and features below come from Ocoya's own pricing and product pages, checked in September 2026. AI tool pricing and feature limits shift often, so confirm current numbers on ocoya.com before subscribing.

## What Ocoya actually is

Ocoya is a social media management platform built by UAB Ocoya, an EU-based company. It pitches itself less as "another Buffer clone" and more as a stand-in for hiring a social media agency — its own marketing draws a direct comparison between the $29/month entry price and a typical $2,500–$5,000 monthly agency retainer. Whether that comparison holds up depends on how much hands-on strategy work you need versus scheduling and drafting, but it signals who Ocoya is chasing: solo operators and small teams who'd otherwise outsource content production.

The platform doesn't publish which specific model powers its AI features, so treat "AI-generated" claims as Ocoya's own description rather than a specified model version. Ocoya also says it serves several hundred thousand customers — a figure from its own marketing copy, not independently verifiable, so treat it as directional rather than audited.

SmartFare has already reviewed several tools in this category — [Robopost AI](/blog/robopost-ai-review), [Publer](/blog/publer-review), [SocialDude](/blog/socialdude-review), [Social Champ](/blog/social-champ-review), and [Beacons](/blog/beacons-review). Ocoya's clearest point of difference is leaning harder into AI content generation as the core product rather than a bolt-on caption assistant, and it's the only one of the group offering agent-based control through Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants via MCP and a REST API.

## Ocoya pricing

| Plan | Price (monthly billing) | Users | Social profiles | AI credits/month |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $29/month | 1 | 5 | 300 |
| Team | $79/month | 5 | 20 | 1,500 |
| Agency | $199/month | 20 | 100 | 5,000 |
| Enterprise | Custom pricing | Custom | Custom | Custom |

Annual billing works out to roughly two months free versus paying monthly — the standard SaaS discount pattern rather than anything Ocoya-specific. There's no perpetual free tier — every plan starts as a 7-day free trial with full feature access, then converts to a paid subscription unless you cancel first.

The AI credit system is the detail most likely to catch new users off guard. Credits are consumed by AI actions — generating captions, images, or hashtag sets — and they refresh monthly rather than rolling over, so a heavy content month can burn through your allotment before the cycle resets. Ocoya doesn't publish a fixed exchange rate (e.g., "1 credit = 1 caption"), so the practical number of posts you can AI-generate per month is worth testing during the trial.

Pricing, free-trial terms, and feature availability were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current figures on Ocoya's own pricing page before committing to a plan.

## Core features walkthrough

**AI content generation as the default workflow.** Rather than writing a caption and having AI clean it up, Ocoya generates the full post — caption, matching visual, and hashtags — from a single prompt. It also supports turning one idea into a multi-post campaign, closer to a content-calendar assistant than a simple caption rewriter.

**Brand Kit system.** You describe your brand voice and visual identity once, and Ocoya applies it across generated captions and images going forward. This matters more for teams generating high volumes of AI content, since it cuts down on the "this doesn't sound like us" editing pass that generic AI writing tools tend to need.

**Broad platform coverage, including niche networks.** Ocoya publishes to Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Facebook, YouTube Shorts, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Discord, Mastodon, Dribbble, Kick, Twitch, Whop, DEV.to, WordPress, Tumblr, and Google Business Profile — a wider net than most competitors, with developer- and streamer-leaning platforms (DEV.to, Twitch, Kick, Discord) suggesting it's chasing creator and community-management use cases beyond standard brand marketing.

**AI-assistant control via MCP.** Ocoya can be operated through Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Perplexity using the Model Context Protocol, alongside a standard REST API. In practice, a user or developer can ask an AI assistant to draft and schedule posts without opening the Ocoya dashboard at all — a workflow none of the other schedulers SmartFare has reviewed currently offer.

**Social inbox and workflow automation.** DMs, comments, and mentions across connected networks funnel into one inbox, and a visual automation builder can trigger scheduled replies or posting rules. This puts Ocoya closer to a lightweight social CRM than a pure scheduling tool, though engagement/inbox tools like this are common across the category (Social Champ and Publer both offer versions of it) rather than unique to Ocoya.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and freelancers:** the Starter plan (1 user, 5 profiles, 300 AI credits) covers a single-person operation managing a handful of brand or client accounts, though $29/month is steep if you're not actually using the AI generation features — a plain scheduler would be cheaper.
- **Small marketing teams:** the Team plan (5 users, 20 profiles, 1,500 credits) fits an in-house team managing several brands or client accounts who want shared access and a shared brand kit.
- **Agencies:** the Agency plan (20 users, 100 profiles, 5,000 credits) is built for agencies juggling many client accounts, and the per-profile/per-user math starts to look more competitive against hiring additional junior content staff.
- **Developers and AI-power-users:** the MCP/API access is a genuine differentiator if you want to fold social publishing into an existing AI assistant or internal tooling workflow rather than using Ocoya's dashboard directly.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| AI generates full posts (caption + image + hashtags), not just caption text | No free plan — only a 7-day trial before you must subscribe |
| Wide platform coverage including niche networks (Bluesky, Mastodon, Kick, Twitch, DEV.to) | AI credit system adds a usage cap and learning curve on top of normal plan limits |
| MCP/API access lets AI assistants operate the platform directly | Entry price ($29/mo) is higher than budget schedulers like Robopost ($9/mo) or SocialDude |
| Brand Kit keeps AI output consistent across a team | Underlying AI/image models aren't publicly specified |
| Social inbox and automation reduce the need for separate engagement tools | Customer-count and cost-savings claims come from Ocoya's own marketing, not third-party audits |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Ocoya's most notable integration is WooCommerce, which can auto-schedule posts for new products added to a store — useful for e-commerce brands that don't want to manually promote every new SKU. Beyond that, the REST API and MCP support are the bigger story: they let Ocoya function as a backend service that AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT can call directly, rather than requiring a human to log into a separate dashboard. There's no public mention of native Zapier or Shopify integrations on Ocoya's marketing pages, so verify support directly with Ocoya before subscribing if either is a must-have.

## Where it's a strong fit

Ocoya makes the most sense for teams that want to generate content with AI as part of their daily workflow, not just schedule content someone already wrote. If you're regularly short on caption ideas, need on-brand visuals fast, or manage a WooCommerce store and want new products auto-promoted, the bundled workflow saves time compared to stitching together a separate AI writer, image generator, and scheduler. The platform coverage is also a strong fit if you publish to smaller networks (Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads, Kick) some competitors treat as afterthoughts.

## Where to think twice

Skip Ocoya if you need a fully free scheduling tool — every plan requires payment after the 7-day trial, and $29/month is a real commitment for a solo creator who just wants to queue posts without AI generation. It's also not the right pick if your team needs enterprise compliance documentation (SOC 2, detailed data-processing agreements) spelled out publicly, since Ocoya's marketing pages don't surface that detail — ask directly if it's a requirement. If you specifically need Zapier or Shopify connections that Ocoya doesn't clearly advertise, confirm availability before subscribing. And because the AI credit system caps monthly generation, heavy AI users on lower tiers may need to upgrade sooner than the plan's headline credit count suggests.

## Bottom line

Ocoya earns its higher price by doing more than scheduling — AI content generation, brand-kit consistency, and AI-assistant integration via MCP put it in a different category from budget schedulers that just queue up posts you've already written. If that AI-first workflow is what you're after, and agency-adjacent prices don't scare you off, Ocoya is a reasonable pick, particularly for agencies managing multiple client accounts. If you just need reliable, low-cost scheduling, cheaper tools in this space will get you there without the AI credit math.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Ocoya have a free plan?**
No. It offers a 7-day free trial with full feature access, but there's no permanent free tier — you need a paid subscription after the trial.

**How much does Ocoya cost?**
Plans run from $29/month (Starter, 1 user, 5 profiles) to $199/month (Agency, 20 users, 100 profiles), with a custom Enterprise tier above that. Annual billing works out to about two months free versus paying monthly.

**What are Ocoya's AI credits, and what happens if I run out?**
Credits are consumed each time you generate captions, images, or hashtags. They refresh monthly and don't roll over, so exhausting your allotment typically means upgrading or waiting for the next refresh.

**Which social networks does Ocoya support?**
Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Facebook, YouTube Shorts, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Discord, Mastodon, Dribbble, Kick, Twitch, Whop, DEV.to, WordPress, Tumblr, and Google Business Profile.

**Can I use Ocoya through ChatGPT or Claude instead of its own dashboard?**
Yes, via Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Perplexity, plus a REST API, so an AI assistant can draft and schedule posts without you opening the Ocoya app.

**Is Ocoya good for beginners?**
The scheduling interface is comparable to other dashboards, but the AI credit system and brand-kit setup add a learning curve. Beginners who just want to queue posts may find the setup more than they need.

**How does Ocoya compare to Robopost or Publer?**
Ocoya is priced higher and leans further into AI content generation as the primary workflow, while [Robopost](/blog/robopost-ai-review) and [Publer](/blog/publer-review) are closer to traditional schedulers with AI features layered on at lower entry prices.

**Does Ocoya work for e-commerce brands?**
Its WooCommerce integration, which auto-schedules posts for newly added products, fits WooCommerce stores well. There's no clearly advertised native Shopify integration, so Shopify merchants should confirm support directly.
