And because Jasper is LLM-agnostic rather than built on one named, well-documented model, teams with strict requirements around exactly which model processes their data should confirm the specifics directly with Jasper's sales team before signing a contract.

## Bottom line

Jasper isn't the cheapest or the simplest way to get AI-written content — it's the one built for teams that need that content to consistently sound like the same brand, at volume, across channels. If that's your actual problem, the Brand Voice and campaign-agent system justify the price. If you just want fast, decent AI drafts for yourself, Jasper is more infrastructure than you need, and a lighter tool will save you money without costing you much quality.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Jasper have a free plan?**
No. Jasper offers a 7-day free trial on paid plans but no permanent free tier, which puts it behind some competitors that offer ongoing limited free usage.

**How much does Jasper cost per month?**
Pro starts at $69/month billed monthly, or $59/month if billed annually. Business pricing isn't published — it requires a sales conversation and carries a 12-month minimum commitment.

**What AI model does Jasper use?**
Jasper describes itself as LLM-agnostic, meaning it can route content generation across multiple underlying language models rather than committing to a single named model. It doesn't publicly specify which models power which features.

**Is Jasper good for beginners?**
It's usable by beginners, but the value of features like Brand Voice, Knowledge assets, and Agent Builder comes from setup work — importing brand guidelines, defining audiences — that a first-time user without a team or existing brand assets may not need or benefit from immediately.

**Does Jasper offer an API?**
Yes, but only on the Business plan. Pro users work through Jasper's own editor and browser extension rather than a direct API integration.

**How does Jasper handle data privacy?**
Jasper publishes enterprise governance controls (SSO, SCIM, role-based permissions) on its Business tier for compliance needs. For exact data-handling and retention terms, check Jasper's current privacy policy directly, since these can change independently of pricing.

**What's the difference between Jasper's Pro and Business plans?**
Pro is a single seat with limited Brand Voices, Knowledge assets, and Audiences, plus core agents and image generation. Business removes those caps, adds API access, the Agent Builder, Jasper Grid, and enterprise admin/security controls, but requires a custom quote and a 12-month commitment.

**Are there good alternatives to Jasper?**
Yes — depending on what you need, tools like Copy.ai and Writesonic cover overlapping ground in general AI marketing copy, often at lower entry prices, while [Hoppy Copy](/blog/hoppy-copy-review) focuses specifically on email marketing copy rather than a full campaign platform. Which fits best depends on whether brand-voice governance across a team is your priority or you mainly need faster individual drafts.

Looking for savings on Jasper or other AI marketing tools? Check [AI & software deals](/category/software) for current offers.

title: Descript Review 2026: Text-Based Editing and Pricing
excerpt: Descript lets you edit podcasts and video by editing a transcript. Here's a hands-on look at pricing, AI features, and who it's actually for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Descript Worth It in 2026?

Descript is worth it if you edit podcasts or talking-head video and want to cut, rearrange, and clean up audio by editing a text transcript instead of dragging waveforms on a timeline. It's less suited to complex multi-camera or motion-graphics-heavy video work, where a traditional NLE still wins.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free; paid plans from $16/month (billed annually) |
| **Free tier/trial** | Yes — 60 media minutes/month, 720p exports with watermark |
| **Best for** | Podcasters, YouTubers, course creators, marketing teams editing narrated video |
| **Standout feature** | Text-based editing — delete a word in the transcript, and it cuts the clip |

Descript is made by Descript, Inc., a San Francisco company originally founded by Andrew Mason (of Groupon fame) and a team of ex-Google and Y Combinator engineers. It isn't built on one named foundation model — Descript licenses and combines several third-party and proprietary AI systems for transcription, voice cloning ("Overdub"), filler-word removal, and its "Underlord" AI editing assistant, without publicly naming every model behind each feature.

## What Descript Actually Is

At its core, Descript treats audio and video like a Word document. You record or import a file, Descript auto-transcribes it, and from there you edit by cutting, retyping, or moving text in the transcript panel — the underlying media follows automatically. That's a genuinely different editing model from timeline-based tools, and it's the reason Descript built a following among podcasters and video creators who'd rather not scrub a waveform to find "the third um in the second sentence."

On top of that transcript-editing core, Descript layers a growing set of AI features: Studio Sound (noise/room-tone cleanup), filler-word removal, Overdub (AI voice cloning to fix a flubbed line without re-recording), AI-generated B-roll and video from text prompts, multilingual translation and dubbing, and Underlord — an AI assistant that executes multi-step editing instructions from a chat-style prompt.

## Descript Pricing

Descript's pricing structure is unusually granular — it caps by "media hours" (how much raw footage you can process per month) and separately meters "AI credits" (consumed by AI-heavy features like Overdub, Studio Sound, and video generation), which is worth understanding before you pick a tier.

| Plan | Monthly billing | Annual billing | Media hours/month | AI credits/month | Export quality |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | $0 | 1 hour (60 min) | 100 (one-time) | 720p, watermarked |
| Hobbyist | $24/mo | $16/mo | 10 hours | 400 | 1080p, no watermark |
| Creator | $35/mo | $24/mo | 30 hours | 800 | 4K, no watermark |
| Business | $65/mo | $50/mo | 40 hours | 1,500 | 4K, no watermark |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom | 4K, no watermark |

The free plan is usable for trying text-based editing on a short episode, but the 60-minutes-a-month cap and watermarked exports make it a trial rather than a workable tier for regular publishing. Hobbyist is the entry point for solo podcasters; Creator (Descript's "most popular" tier) is where most working YouTubers and course creators land, since it unlocks 4K exports and the fuller Underlord toolset. Business adds brand-kit tools, 30+ language dubbing, custom AI avatars, and SLA-backed support for teams producing video at volume. Enterprise adds SSO/SCIM and SOC 2 Type II compliance for procurement-heavy organizations.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current numbers on Descript's official pricing page before buying.

## Core Features Walkthrough

**Text-based editing.** This is the feature that defines Descript. Record or upload audio/video, get an automatic transcript, then edit by selecting and deleting words the way you'd edit a document — delete a sentence and the corresponding video/audio segment is cut from the timeline. It's dramatically faster than scrubbing for rough cuts on dialogue-heavy content, and Descript still keeps a conventional multitrack timeline underneath for fine-tuning transitions, B-roll, and audio levels.

**Studio Sound and filler-word removal.** One click applies noise reduction, EQ, and room-tone smoothing to raw audio, and a separate pass can strip filler words ("um," "uh," repeated false starts) directly from the transcript-driven edit. For podcasters recording in imperfect environments, this replaces a meaningful chunk of manual audio cleanup.

**Overdub (AI voice cloning).** After training a voice model on your own recorded speech, you can type new text and have Descript generate audio in your cloned voice to patch a flubbed line without re-recording. Descript states Overdub requires consent-based voice training and restricts cloning other people's voices without their permission — a sensible guardrail given the misuse potential of voice cloning tools generally.

**Underlord AI assistant.** A chat-style AI editor that can execute editing instructions across the project — tightening pauses, generating rough cuts from a prompt, or summarizing long recordings. How well it performs depends on how clearly you describe what you want, and like any AI assistant it can misjudge intent on ambiguous instructions.

**Translation and AI dubbing.** Business-tier and above can translate and dub a video into 30-plus languages using AI-generated voice tracks — a meaningfully differentiated feature at this price point, though quality varies by language pair and speaker accent.

## Who Descript Is Actually For

- **Solo podcasters** publishing weekly episodes fit comfortably on Hobbyist — 10 media hours a month covers most one-person shows, and Studio Sound plus filler-word removal cut post-production time significantly.
- **YouTubers and course creators** producing longer or more frequent video will outgrow Hobbyist's 1080p cap quickly; Creator's 4K exports and larger AI-credit pool are the realistic starting point.
- **Marketing and content teams** producing branded video at volume, especially across languages, are the target for Business — brand kits, dubbing, and SLA support matter more there than for a solo creator.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** (SSO, SOC 2 Type II) need the custom Enterprise tier; nothing below it offers those controls.
- **Complex multi-camera productions or motion graphics** aren't Descript's strength — heavy visual post-production is usually better paired with Descript for the rough cut and a dedicated NLE like Premiere or DaVinci Resolve for finishing.

## Pros and Cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Text-based editing is a genuine time-saver for dialogue-heavy content | Media-hours and AI-credit caps on every paid tier can run out mid-project for heavy users |
| Studio Sound and filler-word removal handle audio cleanup most editors do manually | Not built for multi-camera, motion-graphics-heavy, or highly visual editing |
| Overdub and AI dubbing are differentiated, not just marketing copy on top of a generic editor | Overdub voice cloning requires upfront training time and carries the general caveats of any AI voice tool |
| Free tier lets you test the core workflow before paying | Free tier's 60-minute/month cap and watermark make it impractical for regular publishing |
| Underlord AI assistant can automate multi-step edits from a prompt | AI-assisted cuts still need a human review pass — it won't always guess editorial intent correctly |

## Integrations and Ecosystem

Descript supports direct export/publish integrations to platforms like YouTube and Spotify for Podcasters from within the app, along with standard export formats (MP4, WAV, SRT/VTT captions) that work with any downstream editor or publishing tool. It doesn't have as broad a third-party plugin or Zapier ecosystem as some general-purpose SaaS tools — its integration story is mostly about being a strong hub for the record-transcribe-edit-publish workflow rather than a node plugging into dozens of other apps. There's no public, self-serve developer API at the time of writing; teams needing that should confirm directly with Descript sales.

## Where It's a Strong Fit

Descript earns its place for anyone whose editing work is fundamentally about spoken content — podcast episodes, interview-based video, course lectures, or talking-head YouTube content. If most of your editing time is spent cutting dead air, removing filler words, and rearranging what someone said rather than building visual sequences, text-based editing genuinely changes how fast that work goes.

## Where to Think Twice

If your work leans heavily on multi-camera coverage, color grading, or motion graphics, Descript's timeline is a secondary tool at best — you'll likely still want Premiere, Final Cut, or DaVinci Resolve for finishing. If you need a genuinely free, uncapped tool, the 60-minutes-a-month ceiling and watermark rule out the free tier for regular use. And if your organization needs SOC 2/SSO compliance from day one, only the custom Enterprise tier covers that — don't assume Business includes it.

## Bottom Line

Descript is one of the few AI editing tools where the core workflow — not just a bolted-on AI feature — is genuinely different from a conventional editor, and for spoken-word content that translates into real time saved. Its dual caps on media hours and AI credits take some getting used to, and heavy users will likely need Creator or Business rather than the cheaper entry tier. It's not a replacement for a full NLE on visually complex projects, but for podcasters, interview-based YouTubers, and course creators it's one of the more genuinely useful applications of AI in editing today.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Descript free to use?**
Yes, Descript has a free plan with 60 media minutes per month, 100 one-time AI credits, and 720p exports with a watermark. It's enough to try the text-based editing workflow but too limited for regular publishing.

**How much does Descript cost per month?**
Paid plans start at $16/month (Hobbyist, billed annually; $24/month billed monthly) and go up to $50/month (Business, billed annually; $65/month billed monthly), with a custom-priced Enterprise tier above that.

**What's the difference between "media hours" and "AI credits" in Descript's pricing?**
Media hours cap how much raw audio/video you can import and process each month. AI credits are a separate pool consumed by AI-heavy features like Overdub, Studio Sound, and video generation — running out of either limits what you can do until the next cycle or a top-up.

**Does Descript store or use my recordings to train AI models?**
Descript states Overdub voice cloning requires the speaker's own consent and training data, and restricts cloning other people's voices without permission. For specific data-retention and training-use policies, check Descript's current privacy policy directly, since these details can change.

**Is Descript beginner-friendly?**
Yes — the transcript-editing model is arguably easier to pick up than a timeline-based NLE for people who've never edited video before, since "editing" mostly means deleting and rearranging text.

**What are the main alternatives to Descript?**
For general AI video editing, [CapCut AI](/blog/capcut-ai-review) and [VEED.IO](/blog/veed-io-review) are common alternatives. For podcast-only audio cleanup, see [Cleanvoice AI](/blog/cleanvoice-ai-review), [Adobe Podcast](/blog/adobe-podcast-review), and [Podcastle](/blog/podcastle-review).

**Can I use Descript for video, or is it audio-only?**
Both — Descript handles audio-only podcast editing and video editing (screen recordings, webcam capture) through the same transcript-based interface, with a multitrack timeline underneath for finer visual edits.

For more AI editing and productivity tool coverage, see our [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub.

title: Vocol AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Vocol AI transcribes meetings in English, Chinese and Japanese with pay-per-minute pricing. Here's an honest look at cost and fit.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Vocol AI Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict

Vocol AI is a meeting and voice transcription tool from Aiello that turns recordings into searchable transcripts, summaries and action items, with a notable edge in Chinese and Japanese transcription accuracy alongside English. It runs on a pay-per-minute "V-points" system rather than flat unlimited seats, which suits light-to-moderate users more than heavy daily recorders.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Starting price** | Free (200 V-points on signup); paid plans from $11/month |
| **Free tier/trial** | 200 V-points (~200 minutes of transcription), no credit card required |
| **Best for** | Multilingual teams, especially Chinese/Japanese/English meetings and interviews |
| **Standout feature** | Multilingual transcription accuracy tuned for Asian languages, plus a shared "Highlight Hub" for clips and comments |

## What Vocol AI actually is

Vocol AI is built by Aiello, a conversational-AI company, and it positions itself less as a generic "AI notetaker" and more as a voice-to-insight platform for meetings, interviews, podcasts, and online courses. You upload or record audio, and Vocol AI transcribes it, generates a summary, extracts action items, and lets teammates comment on specific timestamps.

The company doesn't publish which underlying transcription/LLM models it uses, so treat model-specific accuracy claims as vendor statements rather than independently verified benchmarks. What is verifiable is the positioning: Vocol AI specifically calls out stronger accuracy for English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, and Japanese compared with general-purpose English-first transcription tools — a genuinely different lane from most Western AI meeting assistants, which tend to treat non-English languages as an afterthought.

## Pricing

Vocol AI uses a currency called "V-points," where roughly 1 V-point equals 1 minute of transcription. That's a meaningfully different model from the flat monthly-minutes-included plans you'll find with Otter.ai or Fireflies.ai, and it changes how you should think about cost: you're buying transcription capacity, not a seat.

| Plan | Price | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 200 V-points on signup (~200 minutes), 3,000 minutes of baseline storage |
| Individual — Starter | $11/month | 720 V-points/month |
| Individual — Plus | $25/month | 1,920 V-points/month |
| Individual — Pro | $46/month | 3,840 V-points/month |
| Pay-as-you-go | $16 / $36 / $66 | 450 / 1,200 / 2,400 V-points, no subscription |

Annual billing brings a discount over monthly pricing on the subscription tiers (Vocol AI advertises savings in the neighborhood of a quarter off, but confirm the exact percentage at checkout since promotional rates shift). All tiers include automatic transcription, AI summaries, action-item extraction, speaker identification, and basic collaboration tools — the paid tiers just buy you more transcription minutes and storage headroom, not a materially different feature set.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this review's publish date (September 2026) and can change — always confirm current numbers on Vocol AI's own pricing page before committing to a plan, particularly the V-points allocation per tier and any storage caps.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**1. Multilingual transcription tuned for Asian languages.** This is the headline differentiator. Where most AI meeting tools are optimized primarily for English and treat other languages as a bolt-on, Vocol AI markets itself specifically around higher accuracy for English, Chinese, and Japanese speech — useful if your team runs bilingual or trilingual meetings, interviews, or classes.

**2. Highlight Hub.** Instead of a single meeting summary buried in a folder, Vocol AI centralizes shareable highlights, timestamped comments, and "best practice" clips across recordings. This is closer to a lightweight knowledge base for recurring meeting insights than a one-off recap email.

**3. Action item extraction.** The AI scans transcripts for concrete tasks and deliverables and surfaces them separately from the general summary, so you're not re-reading a wall of text to find what you're actually on the hook for.

**4. Usage analytics.** Vocol AI includes topic word clouds and collaboration/data-usage metrics — a feature set aimed more at teams tracking how meetings are actually used across an organization than at an individual who just wants a quick recap.

**5. Broad content types, not just live meetings.** Because it's built around "voice collaboration" generally, Vocol AI handles interviews, podcasts, and recorded lectures as naturally as it does live video calls, with keyword search across the whole transcript library.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo users and freelancers** who need occasional transcription (interviews, calls, lecture recordings) will likely stay comfortable inside the free tier's 200 V-points or the $11/month Starter plan, since pay-per-minute pricing keeps costs proportional to actual usage.
- **Multilingual small teams**, especially those operating across English, Chinese, and Japanese, get the clearest advantage here versus English-only competitors — this is the use case Vocol AI is built around.
- **Content creators and researchers** working with interviews or podcast raw audio benefit from the Highlight Hub and keyword search across a growing transcript library.
- **Heavy daily meeting users** on Western, English-only teams should think harder about the V-points model — someone recording 5+ hours of meetings a day will burn through minutes quickly, and a flat unlimited-minutes competitor may work out cheaper.
- **Enterprises needing deep integrations** across a wide calendar/CRM/video-conferencing stack will find Vocol AI's integration list thinner than established competitors (see below).

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely stronger multilingual support for Chinese/Japanese/English than most English-first tools | Integration list is noticeably shorter than Otter.ai or Fireflies.ai — Microsoft Teams is supported, but broader Zoom/Google Meet automation is more limited |
| Pay-as-you-go pricing means light users aren't paying for unused seat minutes | V-points model gets harder to predict at high usage volumes compared with flat unlimited plans |
| Highlight Hub gives teams a shared, searchable home for meeting clips, not just one-off summaries | Smaller company/community than category leaders, so third-party reviews and community support content are sparser |
| Handles interviews, podcasts, and lectures, not just live meetings | Underlying transcription/AI model isn't publicly disclosed, so accuracy claims can't be independently benchmarked |
| Usable free tier (200 V-points, no card required) to test real accuracy on your own audio | Annual discount percentage and storage-cap specifics require checking at checkout — not fully transparent up front |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Vocol AI currently lists Microsoft Teams as its primary automatic-recording integration, with additional conferencing-platform connections marked "coming soon" as of this review. That's a shorter integration roadmap than Fireflies.ai, which connects broadly across Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Slack, HubSpot, Salesforce, and Notion, or Otter.ai, which layers in calendar auto-join and CRM-adjacent workflows for its business tiers. If your workflow depends on automatic recording across Zoom and Google Meet without manual uploads, verify current integration coverage directly on Vocol AI's site before subscribing.

There's no indication of a public API for developers at the time of writing, so teams looking to pipe transcripts into custom internal tools should confirm that capability exists before relying on it.

## Where Vocol AI is a strong fit

- Teams and individuals who regularly work across English and Chinese or Japanese and have struggled with accuracy on English-only transcription tools
- Researchers, journalists, and podcasters who want a searchable library of interview transcripts rather than a meeting-specific tool
- Anyone who wants to pay only for the minutes they actually transcribe instead of a flat monthly seat, especially light or occasional users
- Teams that want a shared "highlights" space for meeting takeaways rather than scattered individual summary emails

## Where to think twice

- **If you need deep, automatic integration across Zoom, Google Meet, and a CRM stack**, Vocol AI's current integration coverage (mainly Microsoft Teams, with more "coming soon") is thinner than Fireflies.ai or Otter.ai's business tiers — skip Vocol AI if that automation is non-negotiable for your workflow.
- **If your team records meetings constantly, several hours a day, every day**, the pay-per-minute V-points model can get expensive or unpredictable compared with a flat unlimited-minutes plan elsewhere.
- **If you need enterprise compliance credentials (SOC 2, HIPAA, etc.) confirmed in writing**, Vocol AI doesn't prominently publish this information — enterprises with strict compliance requirements should get written confirmation from Vocol AI's sales team before committing, rather than assuming parity with larger competitors.
- **If you want a fully free, unlimited tool**, Vocol AI's free tier is capped at 200 V-points, not unlimited — it's a trial-sized allowance, not a permanently usable free plan for regular use.
- **If independent, third-party accuracy benchmarks matter to your decision**, Vocol AI's transcription model isn't publicly named, and there's less independent review coverage of it than category leaders, so you're relying more on your own free-tier test than on established third-party data.

## Bottom line

Vocol AI earns its place by doing one thing that most AI meeting tools genuinely underserve: solid transcription for Chinese, Japanese, and English speech in the same platform, with a shared Highlight Hub that goes beyond a single summary email. If your meetings, interviews, or lecture recordings regularly involve those languages, it's worth running your own audio through the 200-point free tier before committing. If you're an English-only team that needs wall-to-wall Zoom/Google Meet/CRM automation and unlimited daily recording, though, Vocol AI's thinner integration list and metered pricing make Fireflies.ai, Otter.ai, or Bluedot a more natural fit — see our [Fireflies.ai review](/blog/fireflies-ai-review) and [Bluedot review](/blog/bluedot-review) for how those compare.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Vocol AI free?**
There's a free tier with 200 V-points (roughly 200 minutes of transcription) on signup, no credit card required. It's a trial allowance rather than an unlimited ongoing free plan.

**How does the V-points pricing system work?**
Roughly 1 V-point equals 1 minute of transcription. Buy points via a monthly subscription (720/1,920/3,840 points at $11/$25/$46) or one-time pay-as-you-go packages ($16 for 450 points, up to $66 for 2,400 points), so cost scales with actual usage.

**What languages does Vocol AI support best?**
Vocol AI markets stronger accuracy for English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, and Japanese versus general English-first tools. Confirm current language coverage on their site for other languages.

**Does Vocol AI integrate with Zoom and Google Meet?**
Microsoft Teams is the primary automatic-recording integration listed, with additional platforms marked "coming soon." Verify current integration status before assuming full Zoom/Google Meet automation.

**Is Vocol AI good for podcasters and journalists, not just meetings?**
Yes — it handles interviews, podcasts, and recorded lectures alongside live meetings, with keyword search across your transcript library.

**How does Vocol AI compare to Otter.ai or Fireflies.ai?**
Vocol AI's edge is multilingual accuracy (especially Chinese/Japanese) and pay-per-minute pricing for light users. Otter.ai and Fireflies.ai have broader integration ecosystems and flat unlimited-minute plans better suited to heavy daily meeting users.

**Does Vocol AI have an enterprise plan?**
Published pricing centers on individual and pay-as-you-go tiers. Teams needing compliance documentation or volume pricing should contact Vocol AI's sales team directly.

**Is Vocol AI beginner-friendly?**
Yes — uploading or recording audio and getting a transcript, summary, and action items back requires no setup beyond creating an account.

For more AI and productivity software deals, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Looka Review 2026: AI Logo Maker Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: Looka builds polished vector logos and brand kits fast, but every download costs money. Here's what each pricing tier actually includes.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Looka Review 2026: Is the AI Logo Maker Worth Paying For?

Looka is worth it if you want a genuinely professional-looking logo and a matching brand kit without hiring a designer, and you're fine paying a one-time fee or annual subscription to download the files. It won't replace a human designer for a complex rebrand, but for a new business that needs usable assets fast, it delivers more polish than most AI logo tools in its price range.

### At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $20 one-time for a single low-res logo file (Basic package) |
| Free tier/trial | Design and preview logos for free; payment required to download any usable file |
| Best for | New businesses, solo founders, and side projects that need a logo plus basic brand assets fast |
| Standout feature | Brand Kit subscription bundles 300+ ready-made social, business card, and letterhead templates around your logo |

Looka (formerly Logojoy) has been around since 2016 and says it has served more than 5 million users, which makes it one of the longer-running names in AI logo generation — older than most of the GPT-wrapper logo tools that showed up after 2022. It's built by a Toronto-based team and runs on a proprietary design algorithm rather than a general-purpose image model like Midjourney or DALL-E, which is part of why its output tends to look more like a "real" vector logo and less like AI art with letters in it.

### What Looka actually is

You start by picking your company name, industry, and a handful of style preferences (colors, symbols you like, fonts). Looka's engine generates an initial batch of logo concepts — the vendor says around 24 to start, expandable to roughly 100 as you refine your preferences — built from a library of vector icons, curated color palettes, and font pairings rather than freeform AI generation. That distinction matters: because the underlying assets are structured vector elements, not pixel-generated art, the final files are clean, scalable, and editable in Looka's own editor, which is not always true of image-model-based logo generators.

Once you pick a direction, you land in a logo editor where you can swap icons, adjust layout, change colors, and fine-tune typography before you pay anything. The catch — shared by nearly every tool in this category — is that you can't download a usable file until you buy a package.

### Pricing

Looka sells three main logo packages plus two subscription tiers for ongoing brand assets. Here's how they break down:

| Plan | Price | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $20 one-time | A single logo file in low resolution (JPG/PNG); limited practical use beyond quick previews |
| Premium | $65 one-time | High-resolution files in multiple formats (PNG, PDF, SVG), transparent background, full ownership rights, and unlimited design changes in the editor |
| Brand Kit | $96/year | Everything in Premium, plus 300+ branded design files — social media templates, business cards, letterheads, email signatures, and a brand style guide |
| Brand Kit + Website | $129/year | Everything in Brand Kit plus an AI-generated website built around your new brand |

There's no permanently free tier — you can design and preview for free, but every download requires a purchase. Looka offers a 7-day refund window, though it only applies if you haven't downloaded any of the purchased assets yet, so test the waters before you grab your files if a refund matters to you.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current figures on Looka's own pricing page before you buy, since AI tool pricing moves fast.

### Core features that actually differentiate Looka

- **Vector-based generation, not raw AI art.** Because Looka builds logos from curated vector icons and fonts rather than generating pixels from a prompt, you get crisp, infinitely scalable output — useful for everything from a favicon to a storefront sign — without the warped text or asymmetry that plagues prompt-based logo generators.
- **Brand Kit asset library.** The Brand Kit subscription is the real differentiator versus one-time logo generators: 300+ templates auto-populated with your logo, colors, and fonts mean you leave with a usable social media kit and business card set, not just a PNG.
- **Built-in editor with real design control.** You're not stuck accepting whatever the AI produces — you can swap fonts, recolor, reposition, and layer icons manually, which gives more hands-on control than tools that only let you regenerate and hope for something better.
- **AI website builder add-on.** The top-tier Brand Kit + Website plan generates a starter site pre-populated with your branding, which is a meaningful time-saver if you need an online presence alongside a logo and don't want to start from a blank page in a separate website builder.
- **Trademark and legal check.** Looka runs a basic trademark screening step during the design process to flag potential conflicts before you commit to a mark — a detail most budget logo generators skip entirely.

### Who Looka is actually for

- **Solo founders and pre-revenue startups**: the $65 Premium package gets you a fully-owned, high-res logo for less than most freelancers charge for a first draft — reasonable if a logo alone is all you need right now.
- **Small businesses launching across multiple channels**: the $96/year Brand Kit pays for itself quickly if you're setting up social profiles, business cards, and a pitch deck at once, since you'd otherwise recreate all of that manually in Canva.
- **Founders who also need a starter website**: the $129/year Brand Kit + Website tier is worth it only if you don't already have a site — otherwise you're paying for a website builder you won't use.
- **Agencies and repeat users**: Looka has no dedicated agency/white-label tier, so freelancers designing logos for multiple clients will likely find per-project pricing adds up faster than a flat subscription tool would.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Clean, editable vector output instead of AI-art-style logos | No permanently free tier — every download costs money |
| Named, transparent pricing tiers you can see before you commit | Refund window closes the moment you download a file |
| Brand Kit bundles real usable assets, not just a logo | Post-purchase edits are more limited than editing from scratch |
| Trademark conflict screening built into the flow | No agency/white-label plan for designers handling multiple clients |
| 5M+ users and a long operating history (since 2016) | Symbol and icon library, while large, isn't infinite — distinct designs get harder to guarantee as usage scales |

### Integrations and ecosystem

Looka isn't a platform with a broad API or Zapier/Slack-style integrations — it's a self-contained design and asset-generation tool. The main "integration" is the built-in AI website builder on the top plan, which pulls your brand assets directly into a hosted site rather than exporting to an external website platform. For everything else, you're exporting standard file formats (SVG, PNG, PDF) and importing them manually elsewhere, same as with most logo generators.

### Where Looka is a strong fit

Looka earns its price when you need a professional-looking mark fast and don't have budget for a freelancer or agency. The vector-based approach holds up at business-card size and billboard size alike, and the Brand Kit turns a single logo purchase into a full starter identity system — colors, fonts, templates — without extra design work. If you're launching something this month and need it to look credible online by Friday, Looka's editor-plus-templates combo gets you there faster than assembling the same assets by hand.

### Where to think twice

Looka is not the right call if you need a completely free tool — there's no way around paying for a download, even for the cheapest single-file option. It's also not built for teams needing brand governance features, multi-user collaboration, or an agency/reseller pricing structure; freelancers generating logos for many clients will likely find the per-logo cost model gets expensive compared to a flat-fee tool built for that workflow. And because generation runs on a proprietary vector-matching system rather than a state-of-the-art image model, don't expect the wildly original, illustrative logo concepts you might get from prompting a general AI image generator directly — Looka optimizes for clean and usable over experimental.

If originality above all else is the priority, a human designer or an open-ended AI image tool will get you further than Looka's curated-library approach, which by design produces logos that share DNA with other Looka users' marks.

### Bottom line

Looka is a dependable, well-established choice for founders who need a real, usable logo and brand kit without a design budget — the vector output and Brand Kit templates justify the price better than most competitors in this category, even if the pricing model (pay-per-download, no permanent free tier) is a minor friction point. Compare it against [our LogoAI review](/blog/logoai-review) if you want to weigh a competitor with murkier upfront pricing, or start with [Namelix](/blog/namelix-review) first if you haven't locked in a business name yet — its free logo previews pair naturally with a tool like Looka once you're ready to commit and download final files.

### FAQ

**Is Looka actually free to use?**
You can design and preview logos for free, including trying different colors, fonts, and icons in the editor. Downloading any usable file — even a single low-res image — requires buying at least the $20 Basic package.

**What's the cheapest way to get a usable Looka logo?**
The $65 Premium package is the realistic minimum if you want full ownership rights, high-resolution files, and multiple formats (PNG, SVG, PDF). The $20 Basic tier only gives you one low-resolution file, which is of limited practical use for print or a website header.

**Does Looka offer a subscription or is it a one-time purchase?**
Both. The logo packages (Basic, Premium) are one-time purchases. The Brand Kit and Brand Kit + Website tiers are annual subscriptions ($96/year and $129/year respectively) that include ongoing access to the template library and website hosting.

**Can I get a refund if I don't like my Looka logo?**
Looka offers a 7-day refund window, but it only applies if you haven't downloaded any purchased files yet. Once you download an asset, you generally forfeit refund eligibility, so review everything carefully before downloading.

**How does Looka's AI compare to prompt-based tools like Midjourney for logos?**
Looka doesn't generate images from an open text prompt the way Midjourney or DALL-E do. It assembles logos from a structured library of vector icons, fonts, and layouts based on your stated preferences, which produces cleaner, more scalable results but less experimental or illustrative designs than a general AI image model.

**Is Looka good for beginners with no design experience?**
Yes — that's really its core audience. The guided flow (pick style preferences, choose from generated concepts, fine-tune in the editor) doesn't require any design background, and the trademark screening step adds a layer of reassurance that a total beginner wouldn't think to check for themselves.

**Does Looka handle trademark registration?**
No. Looka runs a basic trademark conflict check during design to flag potential issues, but it does not file trademarks or provide legal services. If you need an actual trademark, you'll still need a lawyer or a filing service.

**What are the main alternatives to Looka?**
[LogoAI](/blog/logoai-review) and Namelix/Brandmark (see [our Namelix review](/blog/namelix-review)) are the closest AI-driven competitors, along with Canva's logo maker for a more general-purpose, free-first design tool. Looka's edge over most of them is its named, transparent pricing tiers and the depth of its Brand Kit template library.

For more AI and software tool coverage, browse [AI & software deals](/category/software).

title: Copy.ai Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Copy.ai's GTM AI platform tested: Workflows, Agents, pricing tiers, and who it actually fits versus a plain AI writing tool.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Copy.ai worth it for sales and marketing teams?

Copy.ai has grown from a copywriting template tool into a full GTM AI platform for sales, marketing, and revenue operations — built around Workflows, Agents, and Chat rather than simple text generation. It's a strong fit for teams that want to automate multi-step research and outreach processes, but it's priced and built for teams, not solo writers on a budget.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $29/month (Chat plan), or $24/month billed annually; team plans start at $1,000/month |
| Free tier/trial | No self-serve free plan or published free trial for Chat/Workflows; Copy.ai does offer separate free single-purpose tools (see below) |
| Best for | Sales, marketing, and RevOps teams automating research, outreach, and content workflows across a CRM |
| Standout feature | Workflows + Agents that chain prospecting research, enrichment, and content generation into one automated process |

This review covers Copy.ai's core paid platform — Chat, Workflows, Agents, and Tables. Copy.ai also publishes standalone free tools on its marketing site, covered separately in our [Product Description Generator review](/blog/product-description-generator-review). This article is about the broader product people actually pay for.

## What Copy.ai actually is

Copy.ai is built by CopyAI, Inc. and markets itself as an AI-native go-to-market platform rather than a writing assistant. The pitch has shifted: where it started as a template-driven blog and ad-copy generator, it now positions around unifying sales, marketing, and operations work — prospecting research, inbound lead processing, deal coaching, account-based marketing content, localization, and CRM enrichment — inside one system.

The platform is model-agnostic. Copy.ai states it gives users access to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Perplexity models depending on the workflow, rather than running on a single proprietary model. That matters if you're comparing output quality against a single-model tool like ChatGPT — Copy.ai's job is less about generating the best possible sentence and more about orchestrating research, data pulls, and content generation into a repeatable process.

Five components make up the current product:

- **Chat** — a conversational interface for one-off tasks, similar in spirit to ChatGPT but pointed at company data and brand voice.
- **Workflows** — multi-step automations that chain research, enrichment, and content actions together (e.g., "pull a company's recent funding news, summarize it, draft a personalized outbound email").
- **Agents** — targeted automations meant to run with guardrails, for tasks like lead qualification or account research at scale.
- **Tables** — a spreadsheet-like interface for consolidating data from different sources so workflows can act on it.
- **Infobase** and **Brand Voice** — a centralized knowledge base and a tone/style layer so generated content stays consistent across a team.

## Pricing

Copy.ai's pricing structure is built around seats and workflow credits, not simple per-user word limits. As of this post's date, published self-serve pricing looks like this:

| Plan | Price | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| Chat | $29/mo billed monthly, or $24/mo billed annually ($288/yr) | 5 seats, unlimited words in Chat, unlimited chat projects, access to OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini models |
| Growth | $1,000/mo (billed annually, $12,000/yr) | 75 seats, unlimited words in Chat, 20,000 workflow credits/month |
| Expansion | $2,000/mo (billed annually, $24,000/yr) | 150 seats, unlimited words in Chat, 45,000 workflow credits/month |
| Scale | $3,000/mo (billed annually, $36,000/yr) | 200 seats, unlimited words in Chat, 75,000 workflow credits/month |
| Enterprise | Custom (contact sales) | Guided implementation, API access, 20+ tech integrations, unlimited customizable workflows, dedicated support, enterprise-grade security |

The entry-level Chat plan is inexpensive relative to the team tiers, but it doesn't include Workflows credits — it's essentially a shared-seat chat product. Real automation value (Workflows, Agents, Tables) only opens up at Growth and above, a jump that puts Copy.ai firmly in team/company budget territory. Copy.ai does not publish a self-serve free trial for Chat or Workflows; testing the automation layer before committing likely means a Growth-tier sales demo.

Pricing and plan inclusions were accurate as of this post's date (September 2026) per Copy.ai's published pricing page, but AI tool pricing changes often — confirm current numbers on [copy.ai/pricing](https://www.copy.ai/pricing) before signing up.

## Core features walkthrough

**Workflows** are the platform's centerpiece. Rather than writing one prompt and getting one output, you assemble a sequence of "Actions" — data pulls, summarization steps, content drafts — into a repeatable process a non-technical team member can trigger. A common example: pull a target account's recent news or job postings, summarize the relevant signal, and draft a personalized first-touch email, all in one run.

**Agents** extend Workflows into more autonomous territory — tasks meant to run with less step-by-step human triggering, aimed at ongoing lead qualification or account monitoring. Copy.ai frames these as built with "appropriate safeguards," though as with any agentic AI feature, expect to review outputs closely early on rather than trust them unsupervised.

**Tables** function as a lightweight, spreadsheet-style data layer workflows can read from and write to — a working area between a CRM and Copy.ai's automations without custom integrations for every workflow.

**Brand Voice and Infobase** address consistency, a real pain point with AI content at scale. Feeding the platform a company's tone, terminology, and reference material keeps output from Chat, Workflows, and Agents aligned across a team, rather than sounding different every time someone new runs a prompt.

## Who Copy.ai is actually for

- **Solo creators and freelance writers** — Chat alone ($29/mo, 5 seats) works for lightweight one-off writing, but you're paying team pricing for a single-user chat tool with no Workflows access. Cheaper single-purpose AI writing tools likely serve solo use cases better.
- **Small marketing teams** — Chat's 5 seats cover day-to-day writing needs, though without workflow automation you're mostly using Copy.ai as a shared ChatGPT alternative rather than the differentiated GTM platform it markets itself as.
- **Sales and RevOps teams at growth-stage companies** — this is where the pitch lands. Growth tier and above unlock Workflows, Agents, and CRM-connected automation for prospecting research, lead enrichment, and personalized outreach at volume.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** — SOC 2, GDPR, and SSO compliance, plus dedicated support and API access, sit behind the custom Enterprise tier. Named customers like Siemens, Lenovo, and ServiceNow (per Copy.ai's own marketing) suggest it scales that far, though these are vendor-reported case studies, not independently audited results.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Deep CRM and sales-tool integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Outreach) | No published free trial or free plan for the core Chat/Workflows product |
| Model-agnostic access to OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Perplexity | Real automation value (Workflows/Agents) doesn't unlock until the $1,000/mo Growth tier |
| Workflows and Agents automate multi-step research-to-content processes, not just single prompts | Entry Chat plan is priced for a 5-seat team, awkward for true solo users |
| Brand Voice and Infobase help keep AI output consistent across a whole team | Steep learning curve to build effective multi-step Workflows versus a simple chat prompt |
| SOC 2, GDPR, SSO compliance for enterprise buyers | Enterprise pricing is opaque — requires a sales call, no published figures |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Copy.ai states support for 2,000+ integrations, with explicit mentions of Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, and Outreach. API access is an Enterprise-tier feature, not available on self-serve plans — Growth and Expansion teams route custom automations through the Workflows/Actions builder instead. There's no public mention of a Zapier app or standalone no-code connector, so teams outside Copy.ai's named integration set should confirm compatibility first.

## Where it's a strong fit

Copy.ai earns its "GTM platform" label for sales and marketing teams that already have a CRM and want to automate the research-heavy, repetitive parts of outbound — account research, lead enrichment, personalized first-touch messaging — without hiring more SDRs to do it manually. The combination of Workflows, CRM integrations, and Brand Voice consistency is a genuinely different pitch from a plain AI writing assistant, aimed squarely at RevOps and marketing ops teams who think in processes, not single documents. Teams already paying for Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, or Outreach get the most leverage here.

## Where to think twice

If you need a fully free tool, Copy.ai's paid platform isn't it — there's no self-serve free plan for Chat or Workflows, only the separate free single-purpose tools on its marketing site (narrower use cases; see the linked review above). If your budget tops out around $20–30/month total, this isn't priced for you beyond the basic Chat tier, and even that plan is a shared chat interface, not the automation the brand is built around.

If you're a solo creator or freelancer, you're likely better served by a tool priced and scoped for individual use — Copy.ai's cheapest plan bundles 5 seats you probably won't use, and workflow automation doesn't make sense at solo scale. And if your team needs a documented, self-serve API on a mid-tier plan, know that API access is gated behind Enterprise — a sales conversation, not a dashboard-generated key.

Building effective Workflows and Agents also has a real learning curve versus typing a prompt into Chat. Teams without time to map out a process before automating it may find the simpler Chat interface is most of what they actually use, making the jump to Growth-tier pricing harder to justify.

## Bottom line

Copy.ai has repositioned itself from a copywriting template tool into a workflow automation platform for GTM teams, and CRM-connected Workflows and Agents are a real differentiator against plain AI writing assistants — but that value sits behind $1,000+/month team pricing with no published free trial to test it first. For a sales or marketing team already running Salesforce or HubSpot and looking to automate research-to-outreach at volume, it's worth evaluating seriously. For a solo writer or a budget-conscious team wanting straightforward AI writing help, a narrower, cheaper tool (or Copy.ai's own free single-purpose tools, like the one in our [Product Description Generator review](/blog/product-description-generator-review)) is a better starting point.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Copy.ai free?**
Not for the core Chat/Workflows/Agents platform — Copy.ai publishes no free plan or free trial for it. It does offer separate free single-purpose tools (a headline generator, product description generator, etc.) on its marketing site, free with no account required for light use.

**How much does Copy.ai cost?**
Chat starts at $29/month, or $24/month billed annually. Team plans with Workflows and Agents start at $1,000/month (Growth, billed annually), scaling to $2,000/month (Expansion) and $3,000/month (Scale). Enterprise pricing is custom.

**What AI models does Copy.ai use?**
Copy.ai states it's model-agnostic, giving users access to OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, and Perplexity models depending on plan and workflow, rather than running its own proprietary foundation model.

**Does Copy.ai integrate with my CRM?**
Copy.ai states support for 2,000+ integrations, with named connections to Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, and Outreach. API access for custom integrations is reserved for the Enterprise tier.

**Is Copy.ai good for solo writers or freelancers?**
It can work for light one-off writing through Chat, but the pricing (5 seats bundled at $29/month) and the platform's design center on team workflows and CRM automation, so solo users will likely find cheaper, more narrowly-scoped AI writing tools a better fit.

**How is Copy.ai different from ChatGPT?**
ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational AI. Copy.ai layers Workflows, Agents, Tables, and CRM integrations on top of multiple underlying models to automate multi-step sales and marketing processes, rather than functioning as a single chat window.

**Is Copy.ai secure enough for enterprise use?**
Copy.ai states its Enterprise tier is SOC 2, GDPR, and SSO compliant, with named customers including Siemens, Lenovo, and ServiceNow per its own marketing. Teams with strict compliance needs should verify current certifications directly with Copy.ai rather than relying solely on marketing copy.

**What's the difference between Copy.ai's paid platform and its free tools?**
The paid Chat/Workflows/Agents platform is a team-oriented GTM automation product starting at $29/month. title: Crypko Review 2026: What This Anime AI Generator Was
excerpt: Crypko was a GAN-powered AI anime character generator by Radius5. It's no longer reachable online — here's what it did and what happened.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Crypko still worth using in 2026?

No — Crypko is not operating as a live, sign-up-able product anymore. The AI anime character generator, built by the Japanese studio Radius5 on GAN (generative adversarial network) technology, does not resolve as a working website as of this review; the domain that hosted the tool no longer loads. This review covers what Crypko actually did, why it stood out in its category, and what happened to it.

## At a glance

| | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price (historical) | Free tier for basic generation and breeding; paid tiers layered on for higher-resolution exports and commercial use |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — Crypko let anyone generate and remix characters without paying, with usage caps on exports and resolution |
| Best for (historically) | Illustrators, VTuber creators, and anime fans wanting quick AI-generated character art and mashups, plus early NFT collectors |
| Standout feature | "Breeding" two AI-generated anime characters together to produce a new, visually blended character |
| Current status | Domain no longer resolves; treat it as discontinued unless you can verify otherwise on the developer's current channels |

If you're here because someone mentioned Crypko as a tool for anime avatars or VTuber reference art, the short version is: don't plan a workflow around it today. What follows is an honest account of what it was and why it mattered, since some coverage still treats it as an active recommendation.

## What Crypko actually was

Crypko was built by Radius5, a Tokyo-based company, and launched in the late 2010s as one of the first widely-used generative-adversarial-network (GAN) tools purpose-built for anime-style character portraits. This matters for context: Crypko predates the diffusion-model wave (Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, DALL-E 2) that most people now associate with "AI art." It was trained specifically on anime-character imagery rather than being a general-purpose image model, which is why its output looked distinctly more polished and consistent within that narrow style than early general-purpose GAN art tools did.

The headline feature, and the thing that made Crypko stand out from competitors like Artbreeder, was "breeding." Users could pick two existing AI-generated characters and combine their visual traits — hair color, eye shape, expression, outfit style — into a new character, in a process modeled loosely on genetic crossover. You could also fine-tune individual traits with sliders on a single character rather than breeding two together. Because the underlying model was a GAN trained on a consistent art style, results tended to look like they belonged to the same "universe" of characters, which is part of why VTuber creators and hobbyist illustrators used it for quick concept exploration.

Radius5 later layered a blockchain/NFT angle onto the product — the "Crypko" name itself nods at "crypto" — letting users mint generated characters as NFTs and, for a period, trade a CGT utility token tied to the platform. That pivot lined up with the broader 2021 NFT boom, and Crypko marketed itself as an NFT-character platform as much as a character generator for a stretch.

## Pricing — what it cost, and important caveats

Pricing details below reflect what Crypko published on its site and in third-party coverage before it became unreachable. Treat every figure as historical, not current — and note that any still-active tool mentioned in this article was checked as of this post's date, September 19, 2026, and its pricing can change.

| Tier | What it historically included |
| --- | --- |
| Free | Character generation, trait sliders, and breeding at limited resolution, with a cap on exports and no commercial usage rights |
| Paid credits/subscription | Higher-resolution exports, more generations, and (during the NFT era) minting fees for turning a character into a tradeable token |
| NFT marketplace fees | Standard marketplace-style transaction fees on buying, selling, or minting character NFTs, on top of blockchain gas costs |

Because Crypko blended a SaaS-style subscription model with a crypto-token/NFT layer, actual cost varied a lot depending on whether you just wanted art (cheap or free) or wanted to mint and trade characters (subject to token price swings and gas fees).

## Core features, as the product described them

Based on Crypko's own marketing and product pages from before the site went dark, these were the capabilities the product was built around:

- **AI character generation from scratch.** A single click produced a full anime-style character portrait — face, hair, expression — using the underlying GAN rather than a text prompt, unusual even at the time versus the prompt-driven tools that came later.
- **Breeding two characters into one.** The signature feature: select two generated characters and blend their visual DNA into a new, related-looking character, faster than generating from zero each time.
- **Trait sliders for fine control.** Users could nudge attributes — hair color, eye shape, expression — on an existing character without regenerating the whole portrait.
- **NFT minting and marketplace.** Generated characters could be minted as NFTs and listed for sale within Crypko's own marketplace, tied to the CGT token during that phase.
- **API access for developers.** Crypko let external apps, including some VTuber and game-adjacent tools, pull generated characters programmatically rather than only through the web interface.

## Who it was actually for

Crypko's audience split roughly into three groups, and none of them can rely on it today:

- **Anime hobbyists and VTuber creators** used it for quick concept art and avatar exploration when they didn't have (or couldn't afford) a human illustrator for every iteration.
- **Illustrators and concept artists** sometimes used breeding and trait sliders as a moodboard step before doing original work by hand — closer to a brainstorming tool than a final-art generator.
- **Early NFT collectors** were drawn in during the 2021 pivot, treating Crypko-minted characters as speculative collectibles rather than as an art tool.

If you fall into any of these groups today, look at what replaced this category rather than trying to track down Crypko itself.

## Pros and cons (historical)

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Distinctive, consistent anime art style from a purpose-trained GAN | Discontinued/unreachable — nothing here can be verified against a live product today |
| Breeding mechanic was a genuinely novel way to explore character variation | GAN output was far less flexible than modern prompt-driven diffusion models — no text-to-image control |
| Had a real free tier for casual generation | NFT/token pivot added cost and complexity unrelated to the core art tool |
| API access for developer integrations | Community and support channels appear inactive, so troubleshooting or account/data questions have nowhere to go |

## Integrations & ecosystem

Crypko's ecosystem centered on its own web app, a developer API for VTuber or game-adjacent tools, and — during its NFT phase — a marketplace and token (CGT) on a public blockchain. There was no real integration into mainstream creative tools like Photoshop or Procreate beyond what developers built themselves against the API. Compare that to today's anime-generation tools, many of which ship as Discord bots or Stable Diffusion checkpoints/LoRAs that slot directly into existing pipelines — Crypko's standalone-web-app model looks dated by that standard, aside from its current unavailability.

## Where to think twice

This matters more than usual here: as of this review, Crypko is not something you can realistically plan to use.

- **If you need a tool you can sign up for today** — skip it. The site does not currently resolve, and there's no indication of an active signup flow, support inbox, or updated roadmap.
- **If you need text-prompt control over output** — even when live, Crypko's GAN-based approach couldn't do the open-ended prompt-to-image generation that Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, or NovelAI's diffusion models can.
- **If you need commercial-use rights or licensing clarity** — with the service unreachable, there's no way to confirm what commercial terms still apply to past output; don't assume continuity of any license.
- **If you're chasing the NFT/token angle** — CGT and the marketplace were tied to the 2021 NFT cycle; treat any expectation of ongoing liquidity there as unverifiable.
- **If your workflow depends on official support** — with no confirmed active channel, don't budget time expecting a response.

## The bottom line

Crypko was a genuinely interesting, early example of anime-specific generative AI, and it earned real attention in its heyday for solving one problem well: generating a large volume of visually coherent character concepts without hiring an illustrator for every draft. Its breeding mechanic and tightly-trained GAN produced output that still holds up visually next to a lot of what came after it. But it belongs to a specific moment in AI-art history — pre-diffusion-model, then briefly caught up in the 2021 NFT wave. As of this review the site does not resolve, and there's no evidence of an active product to sign up for. If you found this article because you saw "Crypko" recommended somewhere, treat that recommendation as outdated and look instead at currently-maintained anime-focused generators — several Stable Diffusion-based anime checkpoints and dedicated character-generation apps have since picked up where GAN-era tools like this one left off. For broader AI tool coverage and current software deals, see [AI & software deals](/category/software).

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Crypko still online?**
As of this review, crypko.ai does not resolve as a working website, and there's no recent public update from Radius5 pointing to a relaunch. If you find it live again, treat the details in this article as historical rather than current.

**What company made Crypko?**
Crypko was developed by Radius5, a Tokyo-based company, which built it as a GAN-powered anime character generator and later layered on NFT and token (CGT) features during the 2021 NFT boom.

**What made Crypko different from other AI art generators?**
Its "breeding" feature — combining two AI-generated anime characters into a new blended one — was its signature mechanic, along with a GAN trained tightly enough on anime-style art that output looked consistent within that niche, unlike general-purpose image generators of the same era.

**Could you generate images from text prompts in Crypko?**
No. Crypko predated the mainstream diffusion-model wave (Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, DALL-E 2) and worked by generating and remixing characters through its GAN and trait sliders, not through open-ended text prompts.

**Was Crypko free to use?**
It historically offered a free tier for basic generation and breeding, with paid options for higher-resolution exports and, during its NFT phase, minting and marketplace fees. None of this can be verified against a live checkout today.

**What happened to Crypko's NFT marketplace and CGT token?**
Radius5 added an NFT marketplace and a CGT token around the 2021 NFT boom, letting users mint and trade generated characters. There's no current public information confirming either remains active, so treat any expectation of ongoing trading or liquidity as unverifiable.

**What should I use instead of Crypko today?**
Most creators now use diffusion-model-based tools — Stable Diffusion checkpoints and LoRAs fine-tuned on anime art, or dedicated character apps built on top of them — which offer text-prompt control GAN-era tools like Crypko never had. Check this site's [AI & software deals](/category/software) hub for current tool coverage.

**Is there an official statement confirming Crypko is discontinued?**
Not one independently verified for this review. What's confirmed is that the domain does not currently resolve. Treat Crypko's status as "apparently discontinued" rather than a confirmed, sourced shutdown, and verify directly with Radius5's current channels if this matters for your use case.

title: Synthesia Review 2026: AI Avatar Video Pricing & Features
excerpt: Synthesia turns scripts into AI avatar videos with 160+ language dubbing. Here's the pricing, features, and who it's actually built for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Synthesia worth it for AI avatar videos?

Synthesia is worth it if you need polished, on-brand training or explainer videos at scale without a camera crew — its 240+ stock avatars, 160+ languages, and AI dubbing make it a strong pick for corporate L&D and localization. It's less suited to creators wanting fast, punchy social clips, where HeyGen's cheaper entry tier fits better.

### At a glance

| | Synthesia |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Free (10 min/month); paid plans from $29/month |
| Free tier/trial | Yes — Basic plan, 10 minutes/month, no credit card required |
| Best for | Corporate training, product explainers, multilingual localization |
| Standout feature | AI dubbing with lip-sync across 160+ languages |

Synthesia is one of the original AI avatar video platforms, and it's built its reputation on corporate training and internal comms rather than social content. If you've watched a compliance training video, an onboarding module, or a product walkthrough at a mid-size company recently, there's a decent chance it was made in Synthesia. That's a different use case than what HeyGen — the other big name in this space, and already reviewed on this site — is optimized for, and the two are worth separating clearly rather than treating as interchangeable.

## What Synthesia actually is

Synthesia is a browser-based platform for turning a script into a talking-head video, using AI avatars instead of filming a real presenter. You type or paste text, pick an avatar and voice, choose a background/template, and Synthesia renders a video of that avatar speaking your script with lip-synced mouth movement and natural-looking gestures.

The company is UK-based and positions itself for enterprise learning-and-development, HR, and corporate communications teams rather than solo YouTubers. Synthesia doesn't publicly disclose the specific model architecture behind its avatar generation and voice synthesis, but it layers text-to-speech, lip-sync modeling, and avatar rendering into one pipeline.

A meaningful differentiator versus much of the AI-avatar field: Synthesia requires explicit, recorded consent from every real person whose likeness becomes a stock or personal avatar, and runs video moderation to restrict misuse. That's a direct response to deepfake concerns, and part of why the platform is comfortable selling into regulated industries.

## Pricing

Synthesia runs a freemium model with three self-serve tiers plus a custom Enterprise plan. Annual billing is meaningfully cheaper per month than paying monthly — up to 38% less, per the pricing page — but locks you into a yearly commitment and converts your monthly minute allowance into an annual pool.

| Plan | Price | Minutes | Avatars | What's included |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic (Free) | $0 | 10 min/month | 9 stock avatars | Commenting, 160+ languages/voices, no credit card needed |
| Starter | $29/mo (monthly) or $18/mo billed annually | 10 min/month or 120 min/year | 125+ stock avatars | Downloadable videos, AI Video Assistant, AI dubbing, logo removal, 1 editor + 3 guests |
| Creator | $89/mo (monthly) or $64/mo billed annually | 30 min/month or 360 min/year | 180+ stock avatars, 5 personal avatars | API access, multi-avatar scenes, interactive videos, branded video pages, priority support |
| Enterprise | Custom | Unlimited | 240+ stock avatars, unlimited personal avatars | SSO/SAML, SCORM export, live collaboration, 1-click translation to 80+ languages, dedicated CSM |

A few things worth flagging. The "minutes" figure is finished output minutes, not raw recording or editing time — a 3-minute training video eats 3 minutes of your monthly allowance regardless of how long you spent building it. The free plan caps out fast: 10 minutes a month trials the tool but won't run an actual content program. And API access, which matters for auto-generating videos from a CMS or LMS pipeline, only unlocks at Creator and above.

Pricing, free-tier limits, and feature availability above were accurate as of this post's publish date and are worth double-checking on [Synthesia's official pricing page](https://www.synthesia.io/pricing) before you buy, since AI video vendors adjust tiers often.

## Core features that actually differentiate it

**AI avatars with consent-verified likenesses.** Synthesia's stock avatar library (240+ on Enterprise) is built from real actors paid and recorded for this purpose, with contractual consent baked into how their likeness can be used and moderated. You can also build a personal avatar of yourself or a spokesperson from a short recorded sample, useful for keeping content on-brand without that person on camera every time a script changes.

**AI dubbing with lip-sync.** Arguably the single most useful feature for global teams. Feed Synthesia a script or existing video, and it can generate a dubbed version in another language where the avatar's mouth movements are resynced to the new audio, not just overdubbed. Synthesia states this covers 160+ languages, mattering most for companies distributing the same training across regional offices.

**Document and slide-to-video conversion.** The AI Video Assistant takes an existing PowerPoint deck, PDF, or URL and converts it into a scripted, scened video draft, saving the blank-page problem a lot of first-time AI video tools leave you with.

**AI Screen Recorder.** Records your screen, automatically transcribes narration, and trims dead air/pauses, producing a cleaner screen-capture video without manual editing — useful for software walkthroughs where you want a real screen plus a spoken explanation.

**Interactive and branded video delivery.** On Creator and above, videos can include clickable elements (quizzes, branching choices, CTAs) and be hosted on a branded video page rather than only downloaded as an MP4 — relevant for training programs that need to track completion.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators/freelancers** — free or Starter covers occasional explainer videos, but thin minutes and no API on Starter suit infrequent publishing only.
- **L&D, HR, and internal comms teams** — Synthesia's actual home turf. Creator/Enterprise tiers, multilingual dubbing, and SCORM export solve problems (constant re-recording when policies change, translating training across offices) a camera crew can't solve cheaply.
- **Product/customer education teams** — the AI Video Assistant and Screen Recorder let a PM turn a spec doc or live screen demo into a polished explainer without a production budget.
- **Enterprises with compliance requirements** — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 42001, GDPR compliance, plus SSO/SAML on Enterprise, suit regulated industries needing an audit trail on AI-generated content.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Consent-verified avatars and active moderation reduce deepfake/misuse risk | Free tier's 10 minutes/month is too thin for real use |
| Strong AI dubbing with lip-sync across 160+ languages | API access gated behind the $89/month Creator tier |
| Document/slide-to-video and screen-recording workflows save script-writing time | Avatars can still look slightly uncanny in wide shots or fast speech |
| SOC 2, ISO 42001, GDPR compliance suits regulated enterprises | Minutes are consumed by finished output, not editing time |
| SCORM export and LMS-friendly delivery for training teams | Annual billing needed to unlock the cheapest per-minute rate |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Synthesia offers API access on Creator and Enterprise plans for programmatic video generation, letting teams pipe scripted content from a CMS, LMS, or internal tool directly into rendered video. Enterprise adds SAML/SSO and live collaboration for teams editing scripts together in real time. Synthesia doesn't publish a large native app marketplace comparable to a Zapier directory — its integration story is API-first, aimed at development teams rather than no-code users. Confirm current integration support on [Synthesia's site](https://www.synthesia.io) if this is a hard requirement.

## Where it's a strong fit

Synthesia earns its price tag when you have recurring video needs that would otherwise mean re-booking a presenter every time content changes — compliance training that updates quarterly, product explainers needing a dozen language versions, or onboarding modules that need to stay current without a reshoot. The dubbing and lip-sync quality is a feature most competitors still don't match convincingly.

## Where to think twice

Skip Synthesia, or at least don't pay for it yet, if you need a fully free tool for ongoing content — 10 minutes a month won't sustain a real publishing schedule. If your priority is fast, high-volume social video with trendy templates, a creator-first tool (HeyGen included) will likely feel faster and cheaper per video. If you need offline or on-premise deployment, Synthesia is cloud-only. And if your team's output regularly exceeds Creator's 30-minute allowance, budget for Enterprise pricing (unpublished, requires a sales call) rather than assuming Creator scales indefinitely.

Accuracy is generally solid for scripted, controlled content, but unusual proper nouns or non-standard pronunciations sometimes need manual correction in the pronunciation editor — budget review time rather than assuming a first render is publish-ready.

## Bottom line

Synthesia is a mature, enterprise-leaning AI avatar video platform genuinely differentiated by its consent-verified avatar library, strong multilingual dubbing, and compliance posture — not just by having a talking-head generator, which most competitors now also have. For corporate training, localization, and product education teams with a recurring video need, the Creator or Enterprise tier is a reasonable trade against traditional production costs. Casual creators chasing high-frequency social content will find the minute allowances tight and pricier than tools built for that lighter workflow — HeyGen is worth comparing directly if that's your use case.

## FAQ

**Is Synthesia free to use?**
Yes, there's a free Basic plan with 10 minutes of video per month, 9 stock avatars, and no credit card required — enough to test the platform, not enough for a regular content schedule.

**How much does Synthesia cost per month?**
Paid plans start at $29/month (Starter, billed monthly) or as low as $18/month billed annually. Creator is $89/month monthly or $64/month billed annually. Enterprise pricing is custom.

**Does Synthesia offer a free trial on paid plans?**
Synthesia's site indicates a free trial is available with annual billing; confirm current trial terms on the [official pricing page](https://www.synthesia.io/pricing) since terms can change.

**How good is Synthesia's AI dubbing?**
Synthesia advertises dubbing across 160+ languages with lip-sync designed to match new audio to the avatar's mouth movements while preserving the original speaker's voice characteristics. Quality is generally strong for common languages, though technical terminology should always be reviewed.

**What happens to my data and video content on Synthesia?**
Synthesia states SOC 2 Type II, ISO 42001, and GDPR compliance. For specifics on data retention and ownership, check Synthesia's current privacy policy and terms directly.

**Is Synthesia beginner-friendly?**
Yes — the browser-based editor, templates, and AI Video Assistant let someone with no editing background produce a finished video in one sitting. The learning curve is mostly in refining scripts, not mastering editing tools.

**What are the main alternatives to Synthesia?**
HeyGen is the most direct competitor, generally positioned as faster and cheaper for social/short-form content — see our [HeyGen review](/blog/heygen-review). Colossyan and D-ID are other options in the training/explainer video category.

**Can I use my own face as an avatar in Synthesia?**
Yes, personal avatars are available starting on Creator (5 included), created from a recorded sample of the real person with explicit consent, per Synthesia's stated policy.
